module.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
module.blurb: Tencent Holdings Limited is a Chinese multinational conglomerate and technology giant, best known for its social media platform WeChat and online games. It also provides cloud services, fintech, and digital content. Tencent is one of the world's largest internet companies by market capitalization and a dominant player in China's tech ecosystem.

module.name: Nomura Holdings, Inc.
module.blurb: Nomura Holdings is Japan's largest investment bank and brokerage firm, providing a broad range of financial services including retail brokerage, asset management, wholesale banking, and investment banking. Founded in 1925 and headquartered in Tokyo, it operates across Asia, Europe, and the Americas, serving individual investors, corporations, financial institutions, and governments. Nomura is widely regarded as the preeminent Japanese securities house and competes globally with major Western investment banks in fixed income, equities, and advisory services.

module.name: SoftBank Group Corp.

It is best known for its Vision Fund, which has stakes in companies like Arm, Alibaba, and various AI startups. The company operates as a global investment firm, focusing on transformative technologies and long-term value creation.

module.name: Airbnb, Inc.
module.blurb: Airbnb, Inc. operates a global online marketplace for lodging and travel experiences, connecting hosts with guests. Founded in 2008, the company has disrupted the traditional hospitality industry by enabling individuals to rent out their properties or offer unique activities. As of 2025, Airbnb is one of the largest travel platforms in the world, with a market capitalization exceeding $80 billion.

module.name: Applied Materials, Inc.
module.blurb: Applied Materials is the world's largest semiconductor equipment company by revenue, supplying deposition, etch, ion implantation, and metrology tools used in chip fabrication at every major foundry and memory manufacturer. Unlike ASML (which focuses on lithography), Applied Materials covers the broadest range of wafer processing steps — most chips manufactured anywhere pass through multiple Applied Materials tools. The company also supplies solar and display manufacturing equipment. Its services business (AGS) provides recurring revenue through parts, upgrades, and maintenance contracts.
module.recent: Applied Materials has benefited from sustained semiconductor equipment investment across logic (TSMC, Samsung, Intel), DRAM, and NAND capacity expansions. Forward P/E of ~27.3x on 27.1% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.01 — right at the conventional fair-value boundary. Revenue for FY2025 exceeded $28 billion. U.S. export restrictions on advanced equipment to China have created some demand uncertainty but also pushed customers to accelerate domestic tool installations.

module.blurb: Amkor Technology is the largest Western-headquartered OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) provider, packaging finished silicon dies into the chips that power AI accelerators, smartphones, and automotive systems. The company is investing heavily in advanced packaging technologies — 2.5D, 3D stacking, and flip-chip — and is building a major domestic facility in Peoria, Arizona as part of the U.S. semiconductor reshoring effort.
module.recent: Q1 2026 revenue hit $1.685 billion (+27% YoY), with management guiding that its AI packaging portfolio would triple in the second half of 2026. Capex for 2026 is set at approximately $2.75 billion, reflecting the Peoria buildout.

module.name: Ares Management Corporation
module.blurb: Ares Management Corporation is a global alternative asset manager operating through Direct Lending, Private Equity, and other segments. It provides financing solutions to small-to-medium sized companies and specializes in growth capital, middle market, mezzanine, distressed, and growth buyouts across sectors such as healthcare, services, energy, industrials, and consumer. The firm primarily invests in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, taking majority, minority, and shared-control positions. As of May 2026, Ares Management has a market capitalization of approximately $40.6 billion and manages over $5.9 billion in revenue.

module.name: ASML Holding N.V.
module.blurb: ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company and the sole manufacturer of EUV (extreme ultraviolet) lithography machines — the tools required to print the finest circuit features on leading-edge chips at 5nm and below. Every AI accelerator, high-bandwidth memory chip, and advanced logic die manufactured at TSMC, Samsung, or Intel passes through ASML optics. The company's monopoly position emerged after decades of public-private R&D investment in partnership with European governments and chipmakers.
module.recent: ASML reported €32.7 billion in total net sales for full-year 2025, up roughly 16% year-on-year, with net income of €9.6 billion and a gross margin of 52.8%. Year-end backlog stood at €38.8 billion. Q4 2025 saw record total net sales of €9.7 billion, including revenue recognized for the first High-NA EUV systems — the next-generation machines required for 2nm nodes and below. TSMC accounts for an estimated 40% of EUV tool deliveries. ASML guides to €34–39 billion for 2026 and €44–60 billion by 2030 as High-NA adoption widens. In December 2025 Huawei and Chinese startup SiCarrier confirmed a functional EUV light source using an alternative plasma architecture, but analysts place production-ready Chinese competition no earlier than 2028–2030.

module.name: ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: ASE Technology is the world's largest OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) company, responsible for packaging and testing chips after they leave the foundry wafer fab. Chip packaging — the process of cutting wafers into individual dies, mounting them in substrates, and connecting them to the outside world — is increasingly strategic as advanced packaging (chiplets, CoWoS, SoIC) becomes essential for AI accelerators that exceed the reticle size limits of individual dies. ASE's CoWoS-compatible packaging capacity has become a key bottleneck in NVIDIA Blackwell GPU supply chains. ASE is headquartered in Kaohsiung, Taiwan.
module.recent: ASE has benefited from surging demand for advanced packaging from AI chip supply chains. NVIDIA's Blackwell GPUs require CoWoS advanced packaging, a significant portion of which flows through ASE and its competitor SPIL (a subsidiary). Forward P/E of ~47.4x on 39.7% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.19. Revenue growth is driven by advanced packaging volumes rather than legacy wire-bond assembly.

module.name: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd.
module.blurb: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. is a leading global alternative asset manager with over $900 billion in assets under management. The company invests across real assets, including real estate, infrastructure, renewable power, private equity, and credit. It is known for its long-term, value-oriented investment approach and operates through a global network of offices.

module.name: Cipher Digital Inc. (formerly Cipher Mining Inc.)

The company now holds 600 megawatts of contracted HPC capacity. Q1 2026 bitcoin mining revenue was $34.8 million while the company absorbed a wider net loss of $114.3 million as it funds the HPC build-out. Stock rose roughly 300% over the trailing twelve months through mid-2025 before the HPC pivot announcement triggered a near-term sell-off on dilution concerns.

The company is expanding capacity in Thailand and building a major new Texas facility.

module.name: Coinbase Global, Inc.

It provides a primary financial account for consumers, a brokerage platform for institutions, and a suite of products for developers to build onchain. module.name: Salesforce, Inc.
module.blurb: Salesforce is a leading cloud-based software company specializing in customer relationship management (CRM) solutions. It offers a suite of enterprise applications for sales, service, marketing, analytics, and artificial intelligence. The company has been pivoting to position itself as an AI agent company, integrating generative AI into its platform. Salesforce is a major player in the enterprise software market, competing with the likes of Microsoft and Oracle.

module.name: Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc.
module.blurb: Eos Energy manufactures zinc-bromide long-duration battery storage systems using its proprietary Znyth chemistry. Unlike lithium-ion batteries (typically two hours of discharge), Eos's Z3 modules support four to sixteen-plus hours of storage with no degradation penalty — a profile suited to grid-scale renewable energy firming and data-centre backup. The company received a $305 million DOE loan guarantee in November 2024 to build two manufacturing lines in Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania.
module.recent: Eos guided full-year 2025 revenue of $150M–$190M (vs ~$16M in 2024), targeting a major production ramp in Q4 2025. Analysts project $477M in 2026 revenue and $1B in 2027. Four manufacturing lines combined are expected to produce over 8 GWh of annual capacity by 2026. A new Z3 battery architecture was launched to improve simplicity, safety, and AI-enabled grid controls. The company is positioning zinc-bromide storage as a complement to AI data-centre power demand.

module.name: Fluence Energy, Inc.
module.blurb: Fluence Energy is a global market leader in energy storage products and services, and digital applications for renewables and storage. The company provides turnkey energy storage systems, software, and services to optimize renewable energy integration and grid stability. With a strong presence in the Americas, Europe, and Asia, Fluence is positioned as a key player in the transition to clean energy.

The stock has been volatile in the past month amid broader market shifts in the clean energy sector. Investors are focused on the company's guidance and project pipeline for the upcoming quarters.

module.name: GE Vernova Inc.
module.blurb: GE Vernova is the power and energy spinoff of General Electric, separated as an independent NYSE-listed company in April 2024. The company operates three segments: Power (gas turbines, steam turbines, grid services), Wind (onshore and offshore turbines), and Electrification (grid software, power conversion, high-voltage equipment). It is one of the few companies in the world capable of manufacturing heavy-duty gas turbines at scale, a competitive moat that has become highly significant as hyperscalers race to secure reliable power for AI data centres.
module.recent: GE Vernova reported Q1 2026 revenue of $9.34 billion and net income of $4.75 billion, driven by record AI-linked orders. Its total backlog reached $150 billion — described by management as 'sold out for years.' The stock rose from its April 2024 IPO price of approximately $165 to $1,099 as of early May 2026, a gain of roughly 565%, making it one of the best-performing large-cap equities of the AI infrastructure cycle. Gas turbine lead times have stretched into the early 2030s, cementing GEV's pricing power. In 2025 full-year revenue was $38.1 billion (+9%), with net income of $4.9 billion, up 215% year-on-year. Analysts maintain a consensus Buy rating but the average 12-month price target of $1,068 implies the stock has largely priced in near-term upside.

module.name: SPDR Gold Shares
module.blurb: SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), launched in November 2004 by State Street Global Advisors and the World Gold Council, is the world's largest gold-backed exchange-traded fund by assets under management. Each share represents approximately 0.0926 troy ounces of gold held in allocated vaults, providing investors with direct economic exposure to spot gold prices without the logistical burden of physical ownership. GLD is widely used as a safe-haven hedge against equity-market volatility, U.S. dollar weakness, and inflation expectations. Its 52-week range through May 2026 spans $291.78 to $509.70, reflecting gold's dramatic bull run as central bank demand and geopolitical uncertainty drove the metal to successive records. Expense ratio: 0.40% annually.

The fund had pulled back from a peak near $509 in January, logging a roughly 27% drawdown into a March trough, before partially recovering through April. By early May 2026 GLD was trading near $419. Gold's relative resilience during the equity turbulence of early 2026 reinforced its correlation-breaking role in diversified portfolios and drew comparisons with semiconductor equities to highlight divergent risk appetite.

module.name: Hims & Hers Health, Inc.
module.blurb: Hims & Hers Health is a telehealth platform that sells branded personal-care and prescription products — hair loss, erectile dysfunction, anxiety, skincare — through a direct-to-consumer subscription model. It became a high-profile case study in pharmaceutical compounding: during the years-long shortage of semaglutide (the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy), the company produced and sold cheaper copycat formulations legally permitted under FDA shortage rules, turning a niche clinical carve-out into a headline growth engine.
module.recent: The FDA declared semaglutide no longer in shortage in early 2025, effectively terminating the legal basis for Hims's compounded GLP-1 business and triggering a roughly 20% stock drop. The company pivoted: it entered a distribution agreement with Novo Nordisk to sell branded Ozempic directly through its platform (lower-margin but legitimate), acquired an Australian telehealth company, Eucalyptus, for $1.15 billion, and launched a testosterone-therapy product. An SEC investigation into its GLP-1 marketing practices was disclosed in early 2026. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $2.35 billion; the company guided to $2.7–$2.9 billion for 2026.

module.name: Infineon Technologies AG
module.blurb: Infineon Technologies is a global power-semiconductor leader headquartered in Munich, Germany, trading on US markets as an ADR (IFNNY). Its product lineup for AI server power delivery includes OptiMOS and CoolMOS MOSFETs, high-density quad-phase power modules (OptiMOS TDM2454xx, 280A in a 10x9mm footprint), XDP digital hot-swap and protection controllers for 48V AI racks, EiceDRIVER isolated gate drivers supporting SiC and GaN topologies, and high-voltage GaN reference designs for LLC converters running at 800V input. Infineon is a preferred power-silicon partner in NVIDIA's 800V HVDC reference architecture for next-generation AI data centres.
module.recent: Infineon closed FY2025 (ending September 2025) with revenue of €14.66 billion and significantly raised its AI power revenue target to approximately €1.5 billion in FY2026, citing rapidly rising AI infrastructure demand. Revenue for the quarter ending December 2025 was $4.26 billion, up 16.8% year-over-year. In Q1 FY2026 the company announced new HV GaN reference designs for AI server power architectures and expanded its XDP digital protection family with the XDP711-001 48V hot-swap controller. A new Smart Power Fab in Dresden is on track to open in summer 2026. FY2026 guidance calls for moderate total revenue growth, with AI power as the primary growth driver against softer automotive and industrial demand, and adjusted gross margin in the low-forties percent range.

module.name: Infineon Technologies AG
module.blurb: Infineon Technologies AG is a German semiconductor manufacturer that provides microelectronics solutions for automotive, industrial, and security applications. The company is a leading supplier of power semiconductors and microcontrollers, particularly for electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. Infineon operates globally with a strong market position in the automotive and industrial sectors.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Infineon's stock has shown moderate volatility amid broader market trends. The company released its Q1 fiscal 2025 earnings, reporting revenue of €3.4 billion, slightly above expectations, driven by strong demand in automotive and green energy segments. Analysts have maintained a positive outlook on the stock due to its exposure to electrification and decarbonization trends.

module.name: Jabil Inc.
module.blurb: Jabil Inc. is a global provider of engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain solutions, serving industries such as healthcare, automotive, aerospace, and consumer electronics. The company operates through three segments: Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living and Digital Commerce. With over 135,000 employees and a market cap of approximately $37.5 billion, Jabil is a key player in the electronic manufacturing services (EMS) sector.
module.recent: In the past month, Jabil's stock reached a 52-week high of $372.37 on May 6, 2026, driven by strong demand and positive analyst sentiment. The company reported robust revenue growth of 19% year-over-year to $32.67 billion, with net income up 67%. Analysts remain bullish, with a consensus 'Strong Buy' rating, though the average price target of $272.33 suggests potential downside from current levels.

module.name: The Coca-Cola Company
module.blurb: The Coca-Cola Company manufactures and sells nonalcoholic beverages worldwide, including sparkling soft drinks, water, sports drinks, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based beverages. It is one of the largest beverage companies globally, with a market capitalization of approximately $340 billion. The company's brand portfolio includes Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, and other well-known labels.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, KO stock closed at $79.23, up 0.96% on the day, with a 52-week range of $65.35–$82.00. The company reported strong earnings on April 28, 2026, with net income up 27% year-over-year to $13.70 billion and EPS of $3.18. Analysts maintain a Strong Buy consensus with a price target of $85.06.

module.blurb: Kratos builds unmanned aircraft, jet-powered drone targets, and satellite communications systems for the U.S. military. Its XQ-58 Valkyrie is a stealthy, low-cost autonomous aircraft designed as a 'loyal wingman' for manned fighters — capable of carrying sensors or weapons alongside F-35s. Kratos also dominates the aerial target drone market (simulating enemy missiles for live-fire training) through its UTAP-22 and BQM-167 platforms. The common retail shorthand '$KRATOS' is incorrect; the listed ticker is KTOS.
module.recent: In January 2026 the U.S. Marine Corps selected Kratos and Northrop Grumman to develop its first operational Collaborative Combat Aircraft, graduating the Valkyrie from experimental program to procurement. FY2026 revenue guidance is $1.595–$1.675 billion against FY2025 revenue of $1.35 billion, supported by a $1.57 billion backlog and a $13.7 billion qualified pipeline. Market cap stood at approximately $11.6 billion in early May 2026.

module.name: Centrus Energy Corp.
module.blurb: Centrus Energy Corp. is a leading supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry. The company provides enriched uranium, uranium hexafluoride, and related services to utilities and other customers globally. Centrus is also advancing its American Centrifuge technology to produce high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for next-generation reactors, positioning itself as a key player in the U.S. nuclear fuel supply chain.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Centrus Energy stock has seen increased volatility amid growing interest in nuclear energy as a clean power source. The company has been in the news for its role in developing HALEU fuel for advanced reactors, supported by U.S. government contracts. Price action has been positive, reflecting investor optimism about nuclear fuel demand.

module.blurb: Eli Lilly is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies by market capitalization, transformed in the 2020s by the commercial success of its GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist tirzepatide (Mounjaro for diabetes, Zepbound for obesity). Lilly also markets Verzenio (breast cancer), Jardiance (diabetes/heart failure), and Taltz (inflammatory disease).
module.recent: Lilly's next-generation triple agonist retatrutide — targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously — produced up to 28.7 percent average body weight loss in Phase 3 TRIUMPH trials and is on track for an NDA filing in late 2026 or early 2027, with potential approval in 2027–2028. Trailing-twelve-month revenue is approximately $45 billion against a roughly $700 billion market capitalization in early May 2026.

module.name: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE
module.blurb: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE is a German technology company that develops and manufactures laser-based solutions for the electronics, semiconductor, and medical technology industries. Its key growth areas include Advanced Semiconductor Packaging and LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) for glass processing. The company holds a strong market position in laser systems for PCB prototyping and micro-material processing.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, LPKF reported weaker Q1 2026 results with lower sales and a larger loss, but the stock surged as investors focused on its Advanced Semiconductor Packaging and LIDE growth potential. The share price reached a 52-week high of €29.90 on May 11, 2026, reflecting a year-to-date return of over 350%. The stock has since pulled back slightly, trading around €25.70 as of mid-May.

module.name: Lam Research Corporation
module.blurb: Lam Research is a leading semiconductor equipment company specialising in deposition (CVD, ALD) and etch systems — the tools that add and remove material layers during chip fabrication. Lam has particularly strong positioning in 3D NAND flash memory manufacturing, where its multi-layer deposition and etch tools are essential for building the hundreds of memory layers in modern NAND stacks. It also supplies critical tools for DRAM and advanced logic. Lam competes most directly with Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron, with each company holding dominant positions in different tool categories.
module.recent: Lam Research trades at a forward P/E of ~36.2x on 30.7% projected EPS growth (PEG 1.18). The company has benefited from the NAND memory capacity buildout and is positioned to grow as 3D NAND layer counts increase — requiring more of Lam's deposition cycles per wafer. Revenue exceeded $17 billion in FY2025. Export restrictions to China have created some headwinds but domestic and non-China customer spending has partially offset the impact.

module.name: Microchip Technology Incorporated
module.blurb: Microchip Technology is a leading supplier of 8/16/32-bit microcontrollers and analog semiconductors, with a deep power-management portfolio covering PMICs, LDO regulators, DC-DC controllers, gate drivers for MOSFETs and IGBTs, and SiC gate drivers under its mSiC brand. It is one of the largest suppliers of mixed-signal and connectivity ICs for industrial, automotive, aerospace, and data-centre applications. Its Digitally Enhanced Power Analog (DEPA) controllers and 600V gate driver families address the high-voltage side of AI server power delivery, while its broad PMIC lineup targets point-of-load regulation for FPGAs, MPUs, and ASICs in compute racks.
module.recent: Microchip reported Q3 FY2026 (quarter ending December 2025) net sales of $1.186 billion, up 15.6% year-over-year and beating guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.44 against a $0.39 consensus. CEO Steve Sanghi cited broad-based recovery across end markets, non-GAAP gross margins expanding from 52% to 60.5%, and strong bookings building into the March 2026 quarter. Q4 FY2026 guidance was set at $1.26 billion (midpoint), representing roughly 30% year-over-year growth, with EPS of $0.48–$0.52. The company also introduced a new 600V gate driver family and the MCP16701 PMIC targeting AI, high-performance computing, and data-centre applications in early 2026.

module.name: Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF
module.blurb: NANC is an exchange-traded fund launched in February 2023 by Unusual Whales (a financial-data firm known for tracking options flow and congressional trading activity) in partnership with Subversive Capital. The fund replicates the disclosed stock trades of Democratic members of Congress and their spouses, weighted and rebalanced according to publicly filed Periodic Transaction Reports. Its ticker is an explicit reference to Nancy Pelosi, whose trading disclosures have attracted outsized public attention. A companion fund, GOP, tracks Republican members' trades.
module.recent: As of early 2026, NANC holds approximately $258 million in assets under management and has returned roughly 74% since its February 2023 inception, outpacing both the S&P 500 and its GOP counterpart over the same period. The fund's portfolio is heavily weighted toward mega-cap technology names — Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet feature prominently — reflecting the actual disclosed trades of Democratic members. A structural lag exists: the mandatory 30-to-45-day reporting window means the fund buys disclosed positions after the fact, preventing it from fully replicating the returns of the members it tracks. Expense ratio: 0.75%.

module.name: onsemi (ON Semiconductor Corporation)
module.blurb: onsemi designs and manufactures intelligent power and sensing semiconductors, with a particular focus on silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs and modules under the EliteSiC brand, IGBT power modules, intelligent power modules (IPMs), and gate drivers. The company is a dominant SiC supplier to EV traction inverters and has been rapidly expanding into AI data-centre power delivery, supplying high-efficiency SiC and MOSFET solutions for GPU server power stages. Onsemi claims to be the first vendor to scale vertical GaN production, with 700V and 1,200V devices addressing AI server PSU and rack-level power conversion.
module.recent: Onsemi reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.513 billion, above the guidance midpoint, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.64 versus the $0.61 consensus. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated AI data-centre revenue grew more than 30% sequentially and more than doubled year-over-year in Q1 2026, well ahead of the company's earlier guidance for high-teens growth. Q2 2026 revenue guidance was set at $1.535–$1.635 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $0.65–$0.77. Management reiterated an expectation that AI data-centre revenue will double year-over-year across all of 2026, supported by broader chip-vendor adoption of EliteSiC and new 900V SiC design wins with EV/ESS customers including Geely, NIO, and Sineng Electric.

module.name: One Stop Systems, Inc.
module.blurb: One Stop Systems designs and manufactures high-performance compute and storage solutions for edge applications, including artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles, and defense. The company specializes in ruggedized servers and storage systems for harsh environments. It serves customers in the aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, OSS stock has experienced volatility amid broader market trends. The company has not released major news or earnings, but investor sentiment has been influenced by developments in AI and edge computing. No significant price-moving catalysts have been reported.

module.name: Palo Alto Networks, Inc.
module.blurb: Palo Alto Networks is a global cybersecurity company offering a range of security solutions including network security, cloud security, and AI-driven threat protection. Its products include Prisma Access (SASE), Strata Cloud Manager, and Prisma AIRS for AI security. The company is a leader in the cybersecurity market, competing with firms like CrowdStrike and Fortinet.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, PANW stock closed at $183.68, down 0.16% on the day, with a 52-week range of $139.57 to $223.61. The company has a market cap of $148.96B and a forward PE of 50.84. No major news in the past 30 days was identified from the provided sources.

module.blurb: Photronics is one of the world's leading manufacturers of photomasks — the high-precision glass reticles used in semiconductor and flat panel display lithography to transfer circuit patterns onto silicon wafers. Operating eleven facilities across Asia, Europe, and North America, it serves virtually every major chipmaker. The business is structurally tied to node migration: each new process generation requires new mask sets.
module.recent: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $225 million (+6% YoY), with $588 million in cash, zero meaningful debt, and a $330 million capex plan to expand U.S. and Korean capacity.

module.name: Silicom Ltd.
module.blurb: Silicom is an Israeli supplier of high-performance networking hardware - smart NICs (network interface cards), FPGA-based accelerators, edge appliances and switch fabric components - sold mostly to OEMs that bake the boards into their own cybersecurity, SD-WAN, telecom and cloud-edge products. It is a classic small-cap design-win business: revenue depends on how many customer programs ramp into volume each year. Lod-headquartered, founded 1987.
module.recent: Q1 2026 revenue of $19.1m was up 33% year-over-year and ahead of guidance; Q2 was guided to $20-21m and full-year 2026 to $82-83m. The balance sheet ended Q1 with no debt and about $109m of working capital and marketable securities ($63m cash and equivalents, $63m inventory). Management has banked four design wins in the first four months of 2026 against a target of seven to nine for the year, including a tier-one cybersecurity edge system worth over $1m of 2026 orders and an inference-specific NIC under co-development with one of two large AI compute customers, with hyperscaler proof-of-concept deployments slated for H2 2026.

module.name: Snowflake Inc.
module.blurb: Snowflake Inc. provides a cloud-based data platform that enables organizations to consolidate data, build data applications, and share data products. Its platform includes the AI Data Cloud, which applies artificial intelligence to solve business problems. Snowflake serves industries such as financial services, healthcare, retail, and technology. The company is a leader in the cloud data warehousing market, competing with Amazon Redshift and Google BigQuery.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, SNOW closed at $139.74, down 1.39% on the day, with a market cap of $48.25B. The stock has a 52-week range of $118.30–$280.67 and is trading below its analyst price target of $248.62. Upcoming earnings are scheduled for May 27, 2026.

module.name: S&P Global Inc.
module.blurb: S&P Global Inc. is a leading provider of financial intelligence, credit ratings, benchmarks, and analytics. Its core divisions include S&P Global Ratings (one of the world's three major credit rating agencies), S&P Global Market Intelligence (data and research platforms), S&P Global Commodity Insights, and S&P Dow Jones Indices, which administers the S&P 500 and thousands of other indices. The company significantly expanded its scale through the 2022 merger with IHS Markit, reinforcing its position as a critical infrastructure provider for global capital markets.
module.recent: Shares fell approximately 4.15% on May 13, 2026, closing at $406.55 — a notable single-day decline that prompted coverage on MarketBeat asking why the stock dropped, though the specific catalyst is not detailed in available sources. Pre-market pricing on May 14 showed a modest recovery to $407.97, suggesting the sell-off may be stabilizing. Not enough public information from these sources to confirm the precise earnings or macro trigger behind the move.

module.name: TE Connectivity plc
module.blurb: TE Connectivity is one of the world's largest manufacturers of electrical connectors, sensors, and related components, serving transportation, industrial, energy, and data-communications markets. Often invisible to the end consumer, its products appear wherever electricity or data must cross a physical boundary reliably — from the high-voltage harness inside an electric vehicle to the subsea cable splice deep on the ocean floor.
module.recent: In February 2025 TE announced the acquisition of Richards Manufacturing, a maker of overhead and underground electrical distribution hardware, for approximately $2.3 billion — signalling an expansion into grid infrastructure beyond its traditional connector product lines. The company has also been investing in 800V and 1000V EV connector architectures, where content-per-vehicle is estimated to run roughly 30% above internal-combustion equivalents. A presence at DISTRIBUTECH 2026 underscores its grid-modernisation push.

module.name: Trilogy Metals Inc.
module.blurb: Trilogy Metals is a Canadian-headquartered base-metals explorer developing the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects (UKMP) in the remote Brooks Range of northwestern Alaska. Its flagship assets — the Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver deposit and the Bornite copper-cobalt deposit — sit within the Ambler Mining District, one of the world's largest undeveloped polymetallic regions. The company holds a 50% interest in Ambler Metals LLC (joint-ventured with South32), which controls 100% of UKMP. In September 2025 the U.S. Department of Defense acquired a 10% equity stake for approximately $35.6 million, citing the copper and cobalt content as strategic to defense supply chains.
module.recent: The DoD investment in October 2025 sent TMQ shares from roughly $2.17 to a 52-week high of $15.21 CAD. The stock has since pulled back sharply amid permitting uncertainty — the Ambler Access Road, a 211-mile industrial road required for any commercial mine, remains contentious and faces ongoing legal and regulatory challenges from Alaska Native communities. Despite the government's endorsement, no construction timeline has been set, and the company is pre-revenue.

module.name: Trio-Tech International
module.blurb: Trio-Tech International provides burn-in and reliability testing equipment and services for the back-end semiconductor manufacturing process. Burn-in testing stresses chips under elevated voltage and temperature to flush out early failures before they reach end users — a quality step used for memory, logic, and increasingly AI GPU silicon. The company also operates test service centres in Southeast Asia. It is an indirect beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout through the semiconductor testing supply chain rather than a photonics company per se.
module.recent: In March 2026, Trio-Tech secured a $5.3M order for burn-in boards for a next-generation AI GPU platform, signalling direct involvement in the GPU production supply chain. The stock gained approximately 421% over the trailing twelve months as of early May 2026, trading near $13.36. The gain reflects both the AI-hardware testing demand surge and the company's small-cap status, which magnifies price moves on modest volume increases.

module.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
module.blurb: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company is best known for its Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K, and Red Dead Redemption franchises. It operates through labels Rockstar Games and 2K, holding a dominant position in the premium console and PC gaming market.
module.recent: In the past month, Take-Two's stock rose about 12.66% as anticipation builds for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI launch. CEO Strauss Zelnick described the launch as both exciting and terrifying, citing higher development costs and intense investor expectations. A recent SEC filing also revealed Vanguard holds just over 7% of the company's stock.

module.name: Uber Technologies, Inc.
module.blurb: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications for ridesharing, food delivery, freight, and other mobility services across the US, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. Uber is a dominant player in the global ride-hailing and food delivery markets, with a market cap of approximately $161 billion as of May 2026.
module.recent: On May 6, 2026, Uber reported earnings that beat bookings estimates and announced Uber One reached 50 million members, sending the stock up 8.53% to $79.17. The stock has a 52-week range of $68.46 to $101.99 and a consensus analyst price target of $107.18.

module.name: Vicor Corporation
module.blurb: Vicor Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets modular power components and power systems for converting electrical power in electrically powered devices. The company offers a range of brick-format DC-DC converters, complementary components for AC line rectification and filtering, and input/output voltage products. Vicor serves customers in the United States, Europe, Asia Pacific, and internationally, and is known for its high-performance power management solutions.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, Vicor's stock closed at $280.34, up 5.39% on the day, with a 52-week range of $39.64 to $293.95. The company reported strong financials with revenue of $426.70M (up 15.6% year-over-year) and net income of $136.68M (up 490.6%). Analysts have a Strong Buy rating with a price target of $217.50, though the stock trades above that level.

module.name: Vishay Precision Group, Inc.
module.blurb: Vishay Precision Group is a manufacturer of precision sensors, force/torque measurement systems, and weighing instruments serving industrial, aerospace, and defense markets. The company specializes in high-accuracy measurement components including foil resistors and load cells used in demanding environments. VPG has carved out a niche as a supplier of precision parts to advanced manufacturing sectors, increasingly including robotics and automation. Its products are critical in applications where measurement accuracy is non-negotiable.
module.recent: VPG shares surged approximately 30% following a strong earnings beat that exceeded analyst expectations. The company announced deals to supply components to robot makers, with investor attention drawn to its exposure to AI infrastructure, data centers, and industrial robotics themes. The earnings result and new customer wins marked a significant near-term catalyst for the stock.

module.name: SenseTime Group Inc.
module.blurb: SenseTime Group Inc. is an investment holding company that researches, develops, and sells artificial intelligence software platforms, primarily in Mainland China and other regions. It is a leading AI software company focused on computer vision and deep learning, serving sectors such as smart city, finance, and autonomous driving. Despite its technological leadership, the company has faced profitability challenges, with negative earnings per share and net margins.
module.recent: Over the past 30 days, SenseTime's stock has traded between a 52-week low of 1.33 and high of 2.94, with a recent price around 2.09. The company reported a market cap of approximately HK$88 billion and a negative P/E ratio, reflecting ongoing losses. No major earnings or news catalysts were identified in the immediate period.

module.name: CASTECH Inc.
module.blurb: CASTECH Inc. is a Chinese company listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The company is primarily engaged in the research, development, production, and sale of optical crystals and related components. It serves various industries including laser, optical communication, and scientific research. CASTECH is recognized as a leading supplier in the global optical crystal market.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, CASTECH's stock price has shown moderate volatility, influenced by broader market trends in China's tech sector. No major earnings reports or significant news announcements have been released. The stock continues to trade in line with its historical averages.

module.name: Accelink Technologies Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: Accelink Technologies Co., Ltd. is a Chinese company specializing in the research, development, and manufacturing of optical communication devices and modules. The company provides key components for fiber-optic networks, including transceivers, amplifiers, and passive components, serving telecom and data center markets. It is a leading supplier in China's optical communication industry and competes globally with other optoelectronic firms.
module.recent: Not enough public information

module.name: NAURA Technology Group Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: NAURA Technology Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese semiconductor equipment manufacturer specializing in etching, deposition, and cleaning equipment. The company is a key domestic supplier to China's semiconductor fabrication industry, benefiting from the country's push for self-sufficiency in chip manufacturing. It holds a leading market position in China for several semiconductor equipment categories.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, NAURA has been highlighted in multiple analyst reports as a top pick in the Chinese semiconductor sector. UBS and Morgan Stanley have included the stock in their preferred lists for Chinese and APAC markets, citing strong demand for wafer fabrication equipment and China's focus on domestic chip production. The stock has seen positive momentum amid these endorsements.

module.name: LB Group Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: LB Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese company primarily engaged in the production and sale of titanium dioxide and other chemical products. It is one of the leading titanium dioxide manufacturers in China, with a strong market position in the domestic and international markets. The company also produces iron oxide pigments and other related products. LB Group focuses on technological innovation and capacity expansion to maintain its competitive edge.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, LB Group's stock has shown moderate volatility amid broader market trends. No major earnings releases or significant corporate announcements have been reported. The stock price has been influenced by fluctuations in raw material costs and demand for titanium dioxide.

module.name: Hyundai Motor Company
module.blurb: Hyundai Motor Company is a South Korean multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Seoul. It is the world's third-largest automaker by sales, producing a wide range of vehicles from sedans and SUVs to electric and hydrogen fuel cell cars. The company also operates through subsidiaries like Kia and Genesis, and has a strong presence in global markets including North America, Europe, and Asia.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Hyundai Motor's stock has shown moderate volatility amid broader market trends. The company announced plans to expand its electric vehicle lineup and invest in new production facilities. Analysts have noted positive momentum from strong sales in North America and Europe, though concerns about global supply chain disruptions persist.

module.name: Geely Automobile Holdings Limited
module.blurb: Geely Automobile Holdings Limited is one of China's largest privately-owned automobile manufacturers, producing and selling passenger vehicles under the Geely, Lynk & Co, and Galaxy brands, among others. The company is the listed vehicle-manufacturing arm of Zhejiang Geely Holding Group, which also controls stakes in Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, and the Smart brand (via a joint venture with Mercedes-Benz). Geely has aggressively expanded into new-energy vehicles (NEVs), competing in both the domestic Chinese market and select international markets. Its scale and brand portfolio make it a bellwether for China's auto industry transition toward electrification.
module.recent: On May 13, 2026, Daiwa lowered its target price on Geely Auto (00175) to HKD 23.7, contributing to a sharp single-day decline of approximately 5.2% to HK$21.38. The stock has remained under pressure, trading around HK$21.26 as of May 14, 2026. A block trade of roughly 2.35 million shares (HK$52.78 million) was recorded on April 27, 2026, signaling continued institutional activity in the name.

module.name: Knowledge Atlas Tech Joint Stock
module.blurb: Knowledge Atlas Tech Joint Stock is a technology company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company focuses on providing knowledge-based technology solutions. It has shown significant price volatility since its listing, with strong grey market performance and subsequent upward momentum.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, the stock has surged from around HK$820 to over HK$1,018, driven by positive momentum and a UBS initiation with a target of HK$1,160. The stock continues to trade actively with notable block trades and hot stock status.

module.name: ASMPT Limited
module.blurb: ASMPT Limited is a leading global supplier of semiconductor and electronics assembly equipment, providing solutions for the packaging and assembly of integrated circuits and electronic components. The company operates in the technology sector, specifically within the semiconductors industry, and has a market capitalization of approximately $73.8 billion. With a strong presence in Asia, ASMPT serves major semiconductor manufacturers and electronics assemblers worldwide.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, ASMPT's stock has shown positive momentum, trading around HK$176.9 as of early May 2026, up 1.9% on the day. Notable block trades occurred in late April, including a 915k share transaction worth HK$91.05 million. Analysts at UBS and Macquarie have raised their price targets to HK$141 and HK$133 respectively, reflecting optimism about the company's growth prospects.

module.name: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation
module.blurb: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) is an investment holding company that engages in the manufacture, testing, and sale of integrated circuit wafers and compound semiconductors. It serves customers in the United States, China, and Eurasia, offering foundry services, design and IP support, and photomask manufacturing. As one of the leading semiconductor foundries globally, SMIC plays a critical role in the semiconductor supply chain, particularly in China. The company has a market capitalization of approximately HKD 733 billion and employs nearly 20,000 people.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, SMIC's stock price has risen significantly, trading around HKD 77.70 as of May 7, 2026, up 3.81% on the day. The stock has a 52-week range of HKD 38.65 to HKD 93.50, with a year-to-date gain of about 65.5%. Upcoming earnings are scheduled for May 14, 2026, and analysts have raised price targets, with BOCI lifting its target to HKD 83.6.

module.name: BYD Company Limited
module.blurb: BYD Company Limited is a Shenzhen-based conglomerate founded in 1994 that operates across two primary segments: new energy vehicles (NEVs) and related products, and mobile handset components and assembly services. It is one of the world's largest manufacturers of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, selling across China, Europe, Southeast Asia, and other international markets. BYD also remains a major supplier of lithium-ion batteries to the consumer electronics industry, with a global workforce of approximately 869,600 employees and a Hong Kong-listed market capitalization near HKD 976 billion.
module.recent: BYD reported earnings on April 28, 2026, posting trailing-twelve-month revenue of approximately HKD 891–902 billion and net income of HKD 30.98 billion (EPS: HKD 3.40), reflecting notable year-over-year pressure on margins. The stock has declined roughly 25.6% over the past year, trading at HKD 98.15 as of May 14, 2026 — well below its 52-week high of HKD 159.27 reached in May 2025 and hovering above the 52-week low of HKD 88.50 set in February 2026. Forward PE of approximately 19x suggests analysts expect earnings recovery, though near-term sentiment remains cautious amid global EV pricing competition.

module.name: Saudi Arabian Mining Company (Maaden)
module.blurb: Saudi Arabian Mining Company (Maaden) is the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's national mining champion, founded in 1997 and headquartered in Riyadh. It operates across four business units — Phosphate, Aluminium, Base Metals & New Minerals, and other segments — mining gold, phosphate rock, bauxite, kaolin, magnesite, copper, and zinc. With a market capitalization exceeding 250 billion SAR, Maaden is one of the largest mining and metals companies in the Middle East and sells into markets spanning India, Europe, the Americas, Africa, and the broader GCC.
module.recent: Maaden reported Q1 2026 earnings on May 2, 2026, posting EPS of 0.42 SAR on revenue of 8.79 billion SAR. The stock has gained roughly 26% over the past year but pulled back about 7% over the past month, trading near 64 SAR as of May 14, 2026. Full-year trailing net income of 7.43 billion SAR represents a 116% year-over-year increase, reflecting strong commodity pricing and operational leverage.

module.name: Xiaomi Corporation

module.blurb: Alpha Architect 1-3 Month Box ETF seeks to replicate T-bill equivalent returns through box spreads — a four-legged options strategy (long call, short put at one strike; long put, short call at a higher strike) that eliminates market-directional risk and produces a synthetic risk-free rate. The fund does not hold actual Treasury bills. Under IRC Section 1256, gains from the strategy receive 60/40 treatment (60% long-term, 40% short-term capital gains) rather than being taxed as ordinary income, as T-bill interest would be. For investors in top federal brackets, the tax advantage can be substantial.
module.recent: The strategy's tax treatment is contested: IRC Section 1258 (the anti-conversion statute) may allow the IRS to recharacterize gains as ordinary income. As of mid-2026, the IRS has not acted against the fund, which has approximately $11 billion in assets at a 0.19% expense ratio. BOXX is state-tax-disadvantaged relative to T-bill ETFs, whose interest is state-exempt; investors in high-tax states should weigh this carefully.

module.name: KLA Corporation
module.blurb: KLA Corporation is the global leader in process control and yield management equipment for semiconductor manufacturing — the tools that inspect wafers and detect defects at every stage of chip fabrication. As process nodes shrink and pattern complexity increases, process control becomes more critical: a single undetected defect layer can ruin an entire wafer lot. KLA's near-monopoly in wafer inspection and metrology gives it unusually stable revenue even during equipment spending downturns, as chipmakers cannot defer defect inspection without catastrophic yield losses. KLA also supplies equipment for PCB, LED, and solar manufacturing.

KLA's recurring service revenue (parts, software) provides a stable base around which equipment revenue cycles.

module.name: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE

Glass substrates processed with LIDE can carry both electrical interconnects and optical waveguides in the same package — a property directly relevant to co-packaged optics (CPO) architectures. Beyond reactors, the company is developing a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel processing facility as well as fuel transportation and nuclear consulting businesses. With only 36 employees and no revenue as of its latest filings, NNE is firmly in early-stage development, targeting the emerging market for distributed and off-grid nuclear power.

After a 72% surge through January, silver crashed to near $63.90 by February 6 following Trump's nomination of hawkish Fed chair candidate Kevin Warsh and CME margin hikes. By mid-February spot silver had recovered to the low-to-mid $80s range (approximately $82.49 on February 12, 2026). By early April 2026 silver had climbed back above $70 per ounce. SLV closely tracks these moves. The structural backdrop — five consecutive years of market deficits, depleted LBMA and COMEX inventories, and strong industrial demand from solar and AI power infrastructure — remains intact but has not produced a sustained delivery crisis.

module.name: NuScale Power Corporation

Founded in 2007 and headquartered in the United States, the company provides end-to-end services including regulatory licensing support, design and engineering, construction guidance, and operator training. NuScale holds the distinction of being the first SMR design to receive NRC design approval in the U.S., positioning it as a first-mover in the emerging commercial SMR market. module.name: Synopsys, Inc.
module.blurb: Synopsys is the market leader in EDA (electronic design automation) — the software toolchains used by chip designers to design, simulate, verify, and synthesise integrated circuits before they are sent to a foundry for fabrication. Without EDA tools, modern chip design at sub-10nm nodes is effectively impossible. Synopsys also sells silicon intellectual property (IP) — pre-designed circuit blocks like USB controllers and PCIe interfaces that chip designers license and integrate. Its duopoly with Cadence Design Systems gives both companies enormous pricing power and sticky customer relationships.
module.recent: Synopsys is in the process of acquiring Ansys, a simulation software company, in a deal valued at approximately $35 billion. Forward P/E of ~28x on 18.3% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.53 — modestly expensive relative to its growth rate but reflective of the structural indispensability of EDA tools in an era of accelerating chip complexity. AI-driven chip design is increasing demand for Synopsys tools as companies attempt more complex designs on tighter schedules.

module.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF

module.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF

module.name: Global X Uranium ETF
module.blurb: The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) tracks the Solactive Global Uranium & Nuclear Components Total Return Index, a broad-market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark spanning roughly fifty companies across the nuclear fuel cycle: uranium mining, milling, refining, enrichment, and reactor-equipment manufacturing. Launched in 2010, URA is the largest and most liquid pure-uranium-exposure ETF by assets, with approximately $5 billion in AUM as of 2025. Its expense ratio is 0.69%. The fund's largest holding is Cameco Corporation at roughly 23% of assets, followed by Oklo Inc. Class A (a small modular reactor developer) at ~11% — an unusual position for a 'miner' ETF that reflects URA's willingness to include the broader nuclear technology value chain. Other top holdings include Uranium Energy Corp., NexGen Energy, and Centrus Energy. URA is widely used as a reference benchmark for the uranium sector and is the underlying vehicle that the now-closed Defiance 2x leveraged ETF (URAX) sought to double.

module.name: Direxion Daily Uranium Industry Bull 2X ETF
module.blurb: The Direxion Daily Uranium Industry Bull 2X ETF (URAA) seeks daily investment results of 200% of the performance of the Solactive United States Uranium and Nuclear Energy ETF Select Index. Launched June 26, 2024 and managed by Rafferty Asset Management, URAA is the primary surviving 2x leveraged uranium vehicle after Defiance's URAX closed in April 2025. AUM is approximately $48 million as of April 2026. Like all leveraged ETFs, URAA resets its exposure daily, which creates volatility decay — a compounding drag that erodes returns for holders who maintain positions across volatile days even if the underlying index trends upward. The fund is designed for short-term tactical trading, not buy-and-hold investing. The predecessor URAX (Defiance Daily Target 2x Long Uranium ETF, tracking URA) launched May 2024 and closed April 16, 2025, its final share price near $7.94 versus a 52-week high of $21.09.

module.name: Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF
module.blurb: The Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF (URNJ) tracks the Nasdaq Sprott Junior Uranium Miners Index and targets early-stage and development-phase uranium companies — the segment commonly called junior miners or explorers. It holds approximately 35 fairly evenly weighted positions, which provides modest diversification within a universe that is by definition high-risk. Expense ratio is 0.80%, the highest in the Sprott uranium ETF family. The fund pays a dividend yield of approximately 2.25%. Energy Fuels (UUUU) is the largest single holding at over 14% of the portfolio. Junior miners offer the highest potential operating leverage to spot prices — development-stage companies can reprice dramatically when uranium spot prices rise — but also the highest idiosyncratic risk: permitting failures, financing gaps, and the 10–15-year lead time from discovery to production mean that even well-resourced juniors regularly disappoint.

The fund underperformed both URNM and URA on a one-year trailing basis through November 2025.

module.name: Sprott Uranium Miners ETF

Its expense ratio is 0.75%. A structurally distinctive feature is an approximately 11% allocation to the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (SRUUF / U.UN), giving holders simultaneous exposure to mining equity and physical uranium in trust — effectively a hybrid miner-plus-commodity vehicle. URNM is more concentrated than URA, with higher sensitivity to uranium spot prices and lower exposure to utilities or reactor-equipment firms. It pays a dividend yield of approximately 1.69%. The fund is managed by Sprott Asset Management and is part of a broader uranium-focused product suite that also includes URNJ (junior miners) and the Physical Uranium Trust itself.

module.name: Energy Fuels Inc.

The company explores, develops, and operates uranium mines alongside the White Mesa Mill in Utah—the only conventional uranium mill in the United States capable of processing uranium ore and alternative feedstocks. Energy Fuels is also advancing REE separation at the mill, producing oxides from monazite sands to reduce U.S. reliance on Chinese REE supplies. Its vertically integrated model, spanning mining to milling, provides a competitive edge as domestic uranium production gains priority on national security grounds.

module.name: 5N Plus Inc.
module.blurb: 5N Plus Inc. (TSX: VNP) is a Montreal-based producer of ultra-high-purity specialty semiconductors and performance materials, operating in two segments. Specialty Semiconductors manufactures compound semiconductor wafers, epitaxial substrates, and advanced materials — principally from tellurium, germanium, indium, gallium, bismuth, and selenium — for applications in space solar cells, defence infrared sensors, and compound semiconductor devices. Performance Materials supplies bismuth and other high-purity metals for pharmaceutical, industrial, and energy applications. The company's German subsidiary, AZUR SPACE, is one of the world's leading manufacturers of space-grade multi-junction solar cells for satellite programmes, with production capacity expanded roughly 30% in 2025 and a further 25% expansion planned for the second half of 2026. 5N Plus appeared as a named competitor in Coherent Corp.'s 2022 10-K filing when shares traded near C$0.92; by mid-2026 the stock had reached C$35–36, a gain of roughly 38x.
module.recent: Full-year 2025 results featured 35% revenue growth and 73% higher Adjusted EBITDA, following record 2024 results (revenue up 19% to $289M, EBITDA up 39% to $53M). In February 2026 the company announced another 25% expansion of AZUR SPACE solar-cell capacity. The 52-week range as of May 2026 is C$5.12–C$36.40, with the stock having outperformed the TSX Composite by roughly 342 percentage points over the prior twelve months. The analyst consensus is Buy, with a target near C$37.65.

module.blurb: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF tracks the S&P 500 Index, a market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark of the five hundred largest U.S.-listed companies. It is among the largest ETFs in the world by assets and carries an expense ratio of 0.03%, reflecting Vanguard's mutual-ownership structure. VOO is a foundational holding for passive investors seeking broad domestic equity exposure at minimal cost.
module.recent: AUM stood at approximately $927 billion as of May 2026, with top holdings led by Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Berkshire Hathaway, Tesla, Broadcom, and JPMorgan Chase.

module.name: Volkswagen AG
module.blurb: Volkswagen AG is a German multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Wolfsburg, Germany. It designs, manufactures, and sells passenger and commercial vehicles, as well as related parts and services, under brands including Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Škoda, and SEAT. As one of the world's largest automakers, Volkswagen is a key player in the global automotive industry, with a significant market position in Europe, China, and the Americas.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Volkswagen's stock traded in a range of approximately €85 to €110, with a 52-week high of €110.20 reached in December 2025. Recent news includes Citi's analysis suggesting a defense pivot could revive the struggling company, and Volkswagen's push into driver-assist EVs without Nvidia. The stock has been volatile amid broader European market movements and ongoing industry challenges.

module.name: Vishay Intertechnology, Inc.
module.blurb: Vishay is one of the world's largest manufacturers of discrete semiconductors (MOSFETs, diodes, rectifiers) and passive electronic components (resistors, inductors, capacitors), making it a two-sided play on the AI server power-plumbing build-out. On the passive side, its vPolyTan polymer tantalum capacitors and IHLE inductors are design-in components for Nvidia Blackwell GB200 server power-supply units. On the semiconductor side, Vishay's PowerPAK MOSFETs, DrMOS integrated power stages, VRPower buck regulators, and SiC Schottky diodes populate the voltage-regulation and power-conversion circuitry of AI racks. The company is executing a multi-year capacity expansion centred on a new 12-inch wafer fab.
module.recent: Vishay reported Q4 2025 revenue of $800.9 million, up 1.3% sequentially, with full-year 2025 revenue of $3.07 billion. The Q4 book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.20 overall (1.27 for semiconductors, 1.13 for passives), and ending backlog reached 4.9 months — the strongest demand signal in several quarters. Management attributed growth partly to confirmed design wins in Nvidia GB200 AI servers across both MOSFET and vPolyTan capacitor lines. Q1 2026 guidance was $800–$830 million with 2026 CapEx of $400–$440 million, the majority directed to the 12-inch fab in what management called the peak of the five-year expansion. The CEO described the company as ready to accelerate on factory utilisation and margin recovery in 2026.

module.name: Vistra Corp.
module.blurb: Vistra is the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating approximately 44,000 megawatts of total capacity including 24,000 MW of natural-gas generation, 6,400 MW of nuclear, and substantial coal and battery storage assets. It is the second-largest nuclear operator in the U.S. behind Constellation Energy. Vistra operates primarily in restructured, deregulated power markets including ERCOT (Texas), PJM (Mid-Atlantic/Midwest), ISO-NE, MISO, and CAISO — markets where electricity prices clear at the margin and where data-center load growth has dramatically tightened supply/demand balances.
module.recent: Vistra issued 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8 to $7.6 billion — roughly $1 billion above its 2025 range — anchored by three 20-year power-purchase agreements with Meta covering 2.6 gigawatts of nuclear output that lock in contracted cash flows through the 2050s. The company acquired 5.5 GW of dispatchable gas assets via a $4.7 billion Cogentrix deal, strengthening its position in PJM and ISO-NE where data-center load growth is most acute. Gas turbine equipment lead times stretching into the early 2030s make Vistra's existing gas fleet increasingly difficult to replicate, supporting a structural re-rating argument. The stock sold off approximately 25% from its highs in early 2026, which some analysts characterized as a buying opportunity given the contracted earnings profile.

module.blurb: Vanguard Total International Stock ETF tracks the FTSE Global All Cap ex US Index, providing broad exposure to thousands of stocks across both developed and emerging markets outside the United States. At an expense ratio of 0.05%, it is one of the cheapest instruments for international diversification.
module.recent: AUM was approximately $144 billion as of May 2026, with top holdings led by Novo Nordisk, ASML, Samsung Electronics, Nestlé, Shell, Toyota, LVMH, AstraZeneca, HSBC, and Roche. The fund's trailing price-to-earnings ratio (around 14 as of mid-2026) makes it a notable valuation counterweight to higher-multiple U.S. equity funds.

module.name: Warner Music Group Corp.
module.blurb: Warner Music Group Corp. is a global music entertainment company operating in recorded music and music publishing. It is one of the three major record labels, alongside Universal Music Group and Sony Music Entertainment. The company owns a vast catalog of recordings and songs, and works with artists across all genres. WMG generates revenue through streaming, physical sales, licensing, and artist services.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Warner Music Group announced a strategic investment, though details are limited. The stock has been trading near its 52-week range, with analysts providing mixed ratings. No major earnings or price-moving catalysts have been reported in the immediate period.

module.name: Walmart Inc.
module.blurb: Walmart Inc. is a multinational retail corporation that operates a chain of hypermarkets, discount department stores, and grocery stores. It is the world's largest company by revenue and the largest private employer. Walmart also runs Sam's Club retail warehouses and has expanded into e-commerce, advertising, and supply chain services.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Walmart stock has seen mixed performance amid shareholder proposals to reduce the Walton family's voting power. The company announced a $350 million investment in a new milk processing facility in Texas and formed a 'Human Intelligence Team' to boost beauty sales. Analysts remain focused on Walmart's ad growth and competitive positioning against Costco and Amazon.

module.name: Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
module.blurb: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is an omni-channel specialty retailer of home products, including cookware, home furnishings, and decor, operating brands such as Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, West Elm, and Rejuvenation. Founded in 1956, the company has a strong direct-to-consumer and e-commerce presence, with a market cap of approximately $22 billion. It competes in the specialty retail sector, focusing on premium home goods and furniture.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, WSM closed at $186.47, up 3.44% on the day, with a 52-week range of $147.39–$222.00. The stock has gained 25.2% year-to-date, supported by strong earnings and analyst optimism. The next earnings report is scheduled for May 22, 2026, with a consensus price target of $209.71.

module.name: TeraWulf Inc.
module.blurb: TeraWulf is a power-infrastructure company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has pivoted toward high-performance computing (HPC) and AI data-centre hosting. It operates the Lake Mariner facility in New York and the Nautilus Cryptomine joint venture in Pennsylvania, with a focus on nuclear- and hydro-powered compute capacity — a differentiator in an era of AI-driven power scarcity.
module.recent: By early 2026, more than 50% of TeraWulf's revenue derived from HPC hosting, up from approximately zero two years prior, anchored by multi-year contracts with Core42 and Fluidstack. In April 2026, the company raised over $900 million in a common-stock offering to fund Lake Mariner HPC build-out phase 3 and retire convertible debt. The stock moved from a 52-week low near $3.18 to a high of roughly $19.31, a gain of approximately 507% over the trailing twelve months, though at a price-to-book ratio far above industry norms.

module.name: X-Energy, Inc.
module.blurb: X-Energy, Inc. is a nuclear reactor technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Rockville, Maryland. Its flagship product is the Xe-100, a small modular reactor (SMR) designed to generate 80 megawatts of electric power or 200 megawatts of thermal output. The company also manufactures TRISO-X fuel, a high-assay low-enriched uranium pebble fuel designed for advanced reactors. With 889 employees and a market capitalization of approximately $12.2 billion, X-Energy is one of the leading pure-play SMR developers in the United States.
module.recent: X-Energy completed its IPO on April 24, 2026, making it one of the most closely watched nuclear energy listings of the year. The stock has traded in a range of roughly $29.45–$37.10 since its debut, closing at $30.99 on May 13, 2026 — a decline of 2.36% on the day, with pre-market weakness continuing into May 14. The company's next earnings report is scheduled for May 30, 2026; trailing twelve-month revenue stands at $94.26 million (+12.2% year-over-year) against a net loss of $389.78 million.

module.name: ExxonMobil Corporation
module.blurb: ExxonMobil is the largest U.S. integrated oil-and-gas company by market capitalization, operating across upstream exploration and production, downstream refining, chemicals, and an expanding LNG business. Its advantaged asset portfolio — anchored by record Guyana production exceeding 900,000 barrels per day and growing Permian volumes — has made it the go-to large-cap expression of the oil supermajor trade. The company targets $20 billion in structural cost savings by 2030 and has delivered 43 consecutive years of annual dividend growth.
module.recent: In Q1 2026, ExxonMobil posted adjusted EPS of $1.16, beating consensus by 15% — the largest positive surprise in at least four consecutive quarters — on record Guyana output and $0.6 billion in structural cost reductions. GAAP net income was depressed by $3.9 billion in mark-to-market derivative timing effects that are expected to reverse in subsequent quarters. The Golden Pass LNG terminal loaded its first export cargo in April 2026. Management maintained full-year capex guidance at $27-29 billion and a $20 billion share buyback program. The stock is up sharply year-to-date, buoyed by Brent crude near $130/barrel following the Strait of Hormuz crisis.

module.name: Xperi Inc.
module.blurb: Xperi Inc. is a media and entertainment technology company that develops and licenses software powering the consumer viewing experience. Its flagship offerings include Pay-TV user experience solutions, the TiVo electronic program guide, integrated DVR/VOD navigation, and universal search and content-discovery tools that work across linear and streaming sources. Serving pay-TV operators and device manufacturers worldwide, Xperi licenses its platform to embed its software in televisions, set-top boxes, and connected-device ecosystems. With roughly 1,460 employees and trailing-twelve-month revenue near $448 million, the company occupies a niche middleware position between content providers and the living-room screen.
module.recent: Xperi reported its most recent quarterly results on May 6, 2026; the stock subsequently climbed to a fresh 52-week high of $8.50 on May 13, closing at $8.21 (+2.50% on the day) with elevated volume of ~1.27 million shares. The analyst consensus sits at Strong Buy with a price target of $11.67, implying roughly 42% upside from current levels. Revenue remains under modest pressure (–8.3% year-over-year on a trailing basis) and the company continues to run at a net loss, but a forward P/E of 8.68 suggests the market is pricing in a meaningful profitability improvement.

module.name: XPeng Inc.
module.blurb: XPeng Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and markets smart electric vehicles (EVs) in China. Its product lineup includes sedans (P7, P7i, Next P7), SUVs (G9, G6, G7), an MPV (X9), and the MONA M03 hatchback. The company competes in the rapidly growing Chinese EV market, focusing on advanced technology and autonomous driving features.
module.recent: As of May 8, 2026, XPEV closed at $15.62, with a market cap of $14.93B and revenue growth of 87.7% year-over-year. The stock is down 24.5% year-to-date and trades near its 52-week low of $15.38. Analysts give a Buy rating with a price target of $23.08, implying 47.76% upside.

module.name: Zeta Global Holdings Corp.
module.blurb: Zeta Global operates what it calls an AI marketing cloud — a data and software platform that helps large brands identify, acquire, and retain customers across digital channels. Founded in 2007 by John Sculley (former Apple CEO) and David Steinberg, it aggregates consumer data from hundreds of sources into a proprietary database of roughly 235 million individuals in the US, which it uses to power targeted advertising and personalization at scale.
module.recent: Full-year 2025 revenue reached $1.305 billion (+30% year-over-year), the company's 18th consecutive quarter of beating and raising guidance. Net revenue retention — a measure of how much existing customers grow their spending — stood at a record 120%, suggesting strong upsell momentum. In March 2026, Zeta launched Athena, an agentic AI product that moves beyond analytics to autonomous marketing execution. The company raised its 2026 revenue midpoint guidance to $1.785 billion (+37%). KeyBanc upgraded to Overweight; average analyst price target circa $28.

module.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
module.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
module.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

module.name: NVIDIA Corporation
module.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
module.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

module.name: Microsoft Corporation
module.blurb: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
module.recent: As of early May 2026, MSFT trades near $413 — down approximately 25.6% from its July 31, 2025 all-time high of $555.45 and -15.7% YTD — after touching a March 28 correction low of $356.07. The drawdown carried the stock briefly below its 200-week moving average for the first time in roughly 13 years (prior touches: 2009, 2018, 2020, 2022). Revenue grew 18% YoY with Azure +40%, while annualized AI revenue reached approximately $37 billion; calendar-2026 capex is projected near $190 billion and free cash flow contracted -22% YoY. Forward P/E is approximately 24.4.

module.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
module.blurb: Meta Platforms, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads — collectively the largest social-media ecosystem in the world by monthly active users. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue through digital advertising, using detailed behavioural data to target ads across its platforms. After a painful 2022 in which shares fell roughly 65% amid a revenue slowdown and ballooning metaverse losses, Meta executed a dramatic turnaround by cutting costs, boosting margins, and rapidly integrating AI-driven ad ranking tools (Advantage+) that demonstrably improved advertiser returns. CEO Mark Zuckerberg declared 2023 a 'Year of Efficiency' and the company followed through. By late 2025 Meta was simultaneously the most profitable it had ever been and the most aggressive in AI infrastructure spending, committing up to $65 billion in capex for 2025 and raising that figure to as much as $145 billion for 2026.
module.recent: Meta reached an all-time high near $796 per share in September 2025. The stock declined approximately 24–28% from that peak through April 2026, with the primary investor concern being the scale of the 2026 capital-expenditure commitment — up to $145 billion — and uncertainty about whether AI-driven revenue would materialise at the pace required to justify it. Quarterly earnings remained strong through the period, but multiple compression drove share-price weakness.

module.name: Apple Inc.
module.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
module.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

module.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
module.blurb: Amazon operates the world's largest e-commerce marketplace and the leading cloud infrastructure platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS generates the majority of Amazon's operating profit despite representing a minority of total revenue. The company also has significant positions in digital advertising, streaming (Prime Video), and logistics infrastructure.
