Amazon is a major investor in AI, both through AWS cloud AI services and through a multi-billion-dollar strategic stake in Anthropic.
module.recent: Amazon reported FY2025 revenue exceeding $650 billion, with AWS growing at roughly 17% annually and crossing $100 billion in run-rate revenue. The advertising segment has become a meaningful profit contributor. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026), with the stock gaining approximately 10% over that period — the weakest performer in the Pelosi 2026 exercise batch.

module.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
module.blurb: Micron is the only US-headquartered manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory at scale, competing with Samsung and SK Hynix. Historically the most cyclical of the three, it has spent the past two years repositioning toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked DRAM that pairs with AI accelerators, where pricing is multiples of standard DDR5 and contracts are multi-year rather than spot.
module.recent: In March 2026 Micron began mass production of HBM4 12-Hi 36GB stacks for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform; management has stated 2026 HBM capacity is sold out under binding agreements. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue was around $23.9 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin near 75%. The board approved a 30% dividend increase and roughly $25 billion of fiscal-2026 capex. Despite a strong year-to-date move, the forward P/E remains in the high single digits on consensus, reflecting residual cyclicality scepticism.

module.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
module.blurb: AMD is a fabless semiconductor company that designs CPUs (EPYC for data centres, Ryzen for consumer PCs) and GPUs (Instinct for AI/HPC, Radeon for gaming and workstations). Under CEO Lisa Su, AMD has taken significant data-centre CPU market share from Intel with its EPYC server processors, which now command an estimated 30%+ of the x86 server CPU market. AMD's MI300X and MI350 AI accelerators compete directly with NVIDIA's H100/H200 family and are gaining traction with hyperscalers seeking GPU supply alternatives. All AMD chips are manufactured by TSMC.
module.recent: AMD reported strong 2025 revenue growth led by EPYC and Instinct, with data-centre revenue crossing $12 billion annually. Forward P/E of ~32.6x on 63.8% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 0.51 — compelling for a company with clear data-centre CPU momentum and an AI accelerator portfolio that is gaining customer adoption. NVIDIA's dominant CUDA ecosystem remains the primary competitive barrier for AMD's GPU ambitions.

module.name: SK hynix Inc.
module.blurb: SK hynix Inc. researches, develops, manufactures, and sells semiconductor devices, including DRAM, NAND flash, SSD, MCP, and CMM products. The company serves server, networking, mobile, PC, consumer, and automotive markets. It is one of the world's largest memory chipmakers, competing directly with Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, SK hynix reported earnings on April 23, 2026, with revenue and net income surging on a memory price upcycle. The stock hit a 52-week high of 1,653,000 KRW, reflecting strong demand for AI-related memory chips. Morningstar raised its fair value estimate by 65% following the earnings report.

module.name: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
module.blurb: Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution offering investment banking, securities, asset management, and wealth management services to corporations, governments, and individuals. It operates through three segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management, and Platform Solutions. The firm is a dominant player in M&A advisory, trading, and underwriting, with a strong presence in the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, GS shares closed at $937.35, up 2.01% on the day, with a market cap of $287.39B. The stock has rallied over 70% in the past year, reaching a 52-week high of $984.70. Recent news includes analyst ratings and earnings reports, though no major catalysts were highlighted in the past 30 days.

module.name: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
module.blurb: Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution offering investment banking, securities, asset management, and wealth management services to corporations, governments, and individuals. It operates through three segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management, and Platform Solutions. The firm is a dominant player in M&A advisory, trading, and underwriting, with a strong presence in the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, GS shares closed at $937.35, up 2.01% on the day, with a market cap of $287.39B. The stock has rallied over 70% in the past year, reaching a 52-week high of $984.70. Recent news includes analyst ratings and earnings reports, though no major catalysts were highlighted in the past 30 days.

module.name: Alibaba Group Holding Limited
module.blurb: Alibaba Group is a Chinese multinational technology company specializing in e-commerce, retail, cloud computing, and digital media. It operates major platforms like Taobao, Tmall, and Alibaba.com, and is a leader in China's online retail market. The company also has a significant presence in cloud services through Alibaba Cloud and in digital payments via Ant Group.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Alibaba's stock has seen upward movement driven by positive sentiment around its cloud business and cost-cutting measures. The company reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings, with revenue growth in its core commerce and cloud segments. Analysts have noted improved investor confidence amid regulatory easing in China.

module.name: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. is a South Korean multinational electronics company and the world's largest manufacturer of memory chips, smartphones, and consumer electronics. It operates through four divisions: Device eXperience (DX), Device Solutions (DS), SDC, and Harman, covering products from smartphones and TVs to semiconductors and home appliances. As of 2026, it holds a dominant market position in memory and mobile devices, with a market cap exceeding 1,700 trillion KRW.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Samsung Electronics reported strong quarterly earnings driven by blistering memory price hikes, leading to a 46% increase in fair value estimates. The stock hit a 52-week high of 277,000 KRW, reflecting a 390% year-over-year gain. Analysts have raised price targets amid robust demand for AI-related memory chips.

module.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
module.blurb: TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker, fabricating semiconductors designed by Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Qualcomm, and dozens of others. It controls roughly 60% of global foundry revenue and an even higher share of advanced-node manufacturing (3nm and below). TSMC's competitive position rests on process technology leadership, enormous capital expenditure scale, and a customer base that has no viable alternative at leading-edge geometries. Its Taiwanese concentration is the central geopolitical risk that market participants perpetually discount, then rediscover.
module.recent: TSMC reported Q1 2026 revenue of approximately NT$839 billion (roughly $26 billion USD), up around 41% year-over-year, driven by surging AI accelerator demand from Nvidia and Apple. The company's CoWoS advanced packaging capacity — critical for HBM memory integration in AI GPUs — remains sold out through at least 2026. TSMC appeared on Palantir's Q1 2026 Rule of 80 Frontier chart with a composite growth-plus-margin score of 88%, placing it fourth among large-cap companies on that metric.

module.name: Tesla Inc.
module.blurb: Tesla designs and manufactures battery-electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar products. Founded in 2003 and taken public in June 2010 at seventeen dollars per share, it became one of the most spectacular long-term equity stories of the 2010s: every share from the IPO, adjusted for subsequent stock splits, would be worth roughly 6,500 dollars by late 2025 — a return of approximately 22,000 percent. The company's Model S (2012), Model 3 (2017), and Model Y (2020) progressively expanded the addressable market from luxury to mass-market segments. Tesla also operates a global Supercharger network and a large-scale energy storage division (Megapack). CEO Elon Musk's public profile — across social media, SpaceX, and his acquisition of X (formerly Twitter) — has made Tesla one of the more volatile large-cap equities in recent years, as investor sentiment toward the company has become partially indexed to sentiment toward Musk personally.
module.recent: Tesla has faced intensifying competition from Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturers, particularly BYD, which overtook Tesla in global EV sales in 2023. Revenue growth decelerated sharply in 2024, and the company has relied on price cuts to defend market share, compressing margins. Musk's political visibility during the 2024 US election cycle and his role in the DOGE cost-cutting initiative generated significant consumer backlash in some markets, with Tesla registrations declining in Europe and California in early 2025. The stock traded in a wide range through 2025-2026 as investors weighed the autonomous-vehicle (Full Self-Driving) optionality against near-term margin pressure.

module.name: Intel Corporation
module.blurb: Intel is the world's largest semiconductor company by revenue (historically) and the only major chip company that both designs and manufactures its own processors at scale. Its product portfolio spans PC and server CPUs (Core, Xeon), AI accelerators (Gaudi), FPGAs (Altera), and networking silicon. Intel's foundry ambition — Intel Foundry Services (IFS), renamed Intel Foundry — aims to manufacture chips for external customers on its 18A and 14A process nodes, positioning the company as a Western alternative to TSMC. After CEO Pat Gelsinger was replaced in late 2024, the company has undergone significant restructuring.
module.recent: Intel reported Q1 2026 revenue of $13.6 billion, up from a depressed base, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 versus a near-zero consensus — the beat sent shares up 20%+ in after-hours trading. Data-centre revenue grew 22% YoY. Full-year 2026 EPS estimates of $0.48–$0.56 would represent ~101% growth from the 2025 base — a base-effect figure that reflects restructuring charges and near-zero profitability rather than a dramatic business inflection. Intel trades at ~62.1x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.61 given the distorted growth denominator.

module.name: Sivers Semiconductors AB (publ)
module.blurb: Sivers Semiconductors AB develops, manufactures, and sells chips, components, modules, and subsystems based on semiconductor technology. It operates through Wireless and Photonics segments, providing products for 5G mmWave networks, fiber networks, wireless optical networks, and sensors. The company serves customers in North America, Europe, and Asia, and has a market cap of approximately 12.86 billion SEK. Founded in 1951 and headquartered in Sweden, it employs around 130 people.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, SIVE stock has experienced significant volatility, with a 52-week range of 2.85 to 59.10 SEK. The stock price as of May 11, 2026, was 42.62 SEK, down 2.07% on the day. The company is scheduled to report earnings on May 15, 2026, which may be a near-term catalyst.

module.name: Adobe Inc.
module.blurb: Adobe Inc. is a multinational software company known for its creative, marketing, and document management solutions, including Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat Reader, and the Experience Cloud. The company has transitioned to a subscription-based model, generating recurring revenue from its Digital Media and Digital Experience segments. Adobe holds a dominant position in the creative software market and competes with firms like Salesforce and Microsoft in the digital experience space.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Adobe's stock has shown volatility amid broader tech market movements. The company reported strong quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates on both revenue and earnings per share, driven by growth in its Digital Media segment. However, forward guidance was slightly below expectations, leading to mixed analyst reactions.

module.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
module.blurb: Lumentum makes the lasers, optical chips, and components that go into the high-speed transceivers wiring AI data centres together. Spun out of JDSU in 2015, it spent its first decade as a 3D-sensing and telecom-optics supplier of moderate growth. The AI-cluster build-out has remade it into one of the principal upstream beneficiaries of hyperscaler capex, alongside Coherent Corp.
module.recent: Q1 fiscal-2026 set record revenue, with management citing AI-driven demand and an order book that runs into 2027. In March 2026 Nvidia announced a roughly $2 billion strategic investment paired with multi-year purchase commitments for co-packaged-optics components. The company joined the S&P 500 in March 2026; shares have surged on AI demand, leaving the stock at a forward P/E in the 60s, materially above peers.

module.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
module.blurb: The oldest and largest U.S. equity exchange-traded fund, launched in January 1993 by State Street Global Advisors as a vehicle to track the S&P 500 Index — a market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark of 500 large U.S. companies maintained by S&P Dow Jones Indices. SPY holds all constituent stocks in proportion to their index weight, with Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon and Meta typically constituting the top five positions. It trades continuously during market hours with daily volume in the hundreds of millions of shares, making it the world's most liquid single-listed equity security by dollar volume. Expense ratio: 0.0945% annually. SPY is often used as a proxy for 'the market' in both retail portfolios and institutional hedging strategies.
module.recent: The S&P 500 closed at approximately 7,230 on May 1, 2026, representing a YTD gain of roughly 5.1% for 2026. The index's Shiller CAPE ratio stood near 40.9 as of early May 2026 — among the two highest readings in recorded history and exceeded only briefly during the 1999-2000 dot-com peak. The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.5–3.75% at its April 2026 meeting, maintaining a pause in the cutting cycle that began in late 2024.

module.name: Coherent Corp.
module.blurb: Coherent Corp. (formerly II-VI Incorporated, rebranded after the 2022 acquisition of Lumentum rival Coherent) develops and manufactures engineered materials, optoelectronic components, and laser systems across three segments: Networking, Materials, and Lasers. Its Networking segment — the primary AI data-center play — supplies indium-phosphide chips, transceiver modules, and silicon-photonics sub-assemblies to hyperscalers and networking OEMs. With roughly $5.8 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue, it is one of the largest vertically integrated photonics companies in the world.
module.recent: Coherent joined the S&P 500 in March 2026, the same month it announced general availability of the industry's first dual-laser QSFP28-DCO module — a compact form factor enabling 100G coherent transmission over a single fiber with up to 300 km reach. At OFC 2026 the company showcased an expanded InP portfolio including 400 mW CW lasers, 200G/400G photodiodes, and 800G/1.6T modulators. Fifteen analysts hold an average "Strong Buy" rating with a consensus 12-month price target near $278.

module.name: Morgan Stanley
module.blurb: Morgan Stanley is a global financial holding company providing investment banking, wealth management, and investment management services to corporations, governments, and individuals. It operates through three segments: Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, and Investment Management. The firm is a leading player in capital markets, M&A advisory, and asset management, with a strong presence in the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, MS stock closed at $193.35, up 2.17% on the day, with a 52-week range of $117.21–$194.83. The company reported earnings on April 15, 2026, and has a market cap of approximately $305 billion. Recent news includes analyst ratings and dividend activity, with an ex-dividend date of April 30, 2026.

module.name: SanDisk Corporation
module.blurb: SanDisk was spun off from Western Digital in February 2025 as an independent pure-play NAND flash memory company. It designs and manufactures NAND-based solid-state drives, flash storage chips, and consumer memory products. The spinoff allowed the market to re-rate the business on semiconductor multiples rather than hardware-manufacturer multiples, contributing to an extraordinary post-spinoff rally driven by the NAND supercycle.
module.recent: Since its February 2025 spinoff, SNDK surged over 2,400% through May 2026, reaching an all-time high above $1,189. Fiscal year 2025 revenue was approximately $7.4 billion, with gross margins expanding to ~36% from the low 20s in late 2024, aided by a shift toward high-margin QLC (quad-level cell) products. Analyst targets range from $975 (Wells Fargo, Equal Weight) to $1,250 (Bernstein SocGen, Outperform). A 247 Wall St. analysis in April 2026 flagged potential overvaluation of ~32% versus peers.

module.name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
module.blurb: Applied Optoelectronics is a Texas-based maker of optical components and transceivers, historically known for serving cable-television networks and a handful of hyperscale customers in cycles of feast and famine. The AI build-out has dragged it firmly into the data-centre supply chain, where it now competes for 400G, 800G, and 1.6T transceiver volumes against Lumentum, Coherent, Innolight, and Eoptolink.
module.recent: Management is guiding to full-year 2026 revenue exceeding $1 billion, more than double 2025's roughly $456 million, on the back of 800G ramps and a single 1.6T order disclosed at over $200 million. The company aims to scale from roughly 90,000 800G units per month at end-2025 toward 500,000 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026. The stock hit an all-time high near $192 in early May 2026, having traded as low as $12.56 within the last 52 weeks.

module.name: Kuaishou Technology
module.blurb: Kuaishou Technology operates a leading short-video and live-streaming platform in China, known for its community-driven content and e-commerce integration. The company generates revenue through live-streaming gifts, advertising, and online shopping commissions. It competes with ByteDance's Douyin in the Chinese social media market.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Kuaishou's stock has shown volatility with price swings of up to 7% in a single day. Analysts from Citi and UBS raised price targets to HKD95 and HKD108 respectively, reflecting optimism about the company's growth prospects. Block trades totaling millions of shares have been reported, indicating institutional activity.

module.name: Oracle Corporation
module.blurb: Oracle is an enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company founded by Larry Ellison in 1977 and headquartered in Austin, Texas. Its core businesses are database software (Oracle Database remains the dominant enterprise RDBMS by revenue), cloud applications (ERP, HCM, and CX via Oracle Fusion and NetSuite), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), its IaaS platform. OCI entered the AI infrastructure race later than AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud but has emerged as a preferred hyperscale partner for OpenAI and other large AI workloads, partly due to competitive GPU pricing and multi-region data-centre commitments. Oracle is an equity participant in the Stargate joint venture alongside OpenAI and SoftBank.
module.recent: Oracle's fiscal Q3 2026 (ending February 2026) was described by management as the strongest quarter in more than 15 years: total revenue rose 22% year-on-year to $17.2 billion, cloud revenue jumped 44% to $8.9 billion, and GPU-related cloud revenue grew 177% year-on-year in the prior quarter. The company reported a $523 billion remaining performance-obligation backlog — driven by AI mega-deals with OpenAI and Meta — and committed approximately $50 billion in capital expenditure for fiscal 2026. BNP Paribas analysts estimated that Oracle's 4.5 gigawatt Stargate capacity commitment could eventually generate $30–60 billion in annual revenue.

module.name: Broadcom Inc.
module.blurb: Broadcom is a diversified semiconductor and infrastructure software company formed through a series of acquisitions, most recently VMware (closed 2023). Its chip portfolio spans networking ASICs (custom chips for hyperscaler AI clusters), enterprise storage controllers, WiFi silicon, and set-top-box processors. Broadcom's AI networking chips — particularly its Tomahawk Ethernet switching ASICs and custom AI accelerators built for Google, Meta, and Apple — have made it a second-tier AI infrastructure beneficiary behind NVIDIA. The VMware acquisition added high-margin enterprise software revenue that meaningfully improved the company's margin profile.
module.recent: Broadcom's FY2026 revenue (ending Oct 2026) is on track to exceed $65 billion, with AI-related chip revenue growing rapidly as hyperscalers expand custom silicon programs. Forward EPS growth of 56.3% and a forward P/E of ~23.4x produce a PEG of 0.42 — among the best risk-adjusted valuations in large-cap technology. CEO Hock Tan has guided to $60–90 billion in AI chip revenue by 2027 from three major hyperscaler customers alone.

module.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
module.blurb: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States. It operates through four major segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management. The company provides a wide range of services including investment banking, financial transaction processing, asset management, and retail banking. As of 2025, it is the largest bank in the U.S. by assets and a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, JPMorgan Chase's stock has shown positive momentum, driven by strong quarterly earnings and favorable interest rate expectations. The company reported better-than-expected revenue and profit, benefiting from higher net interest income and robust investment banking fees. Analysts have raised price targets, citing the bank's diversified business model and capital strength.

module.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
module.blurb: Palantir Technologies, founded in 2003 by Peter Thiel, Alex Karp, and others, builds large-scale data-analytics and AI platforms for government intelligence agencies and commercial enterprises. Its flagship products are Gotham (for government and defence clients), Foundry (for commercial enterprises), and the Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), launched in 2023, which allows organisations to deploy large language models within their existing data infrastructure. The company is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, and is unusual among technology companies in that it derives a substantial share of revenue from classified US government contracts — a relatively insulated revenue stream that also limits disclosure. Palantir built a large retail-investor following due to its association with AI, US defence spending growth, and the outspoken, unconventional public persona of CEO Alex Karp.
module.recent: Palantir's shares reached an all-time high of approximately $207.52 in November 2025, having risen more than 300% from January 2025 on a combination of AI-platform enthusiasm and accelerating commercial revenue growth. The stock suffered a drawdown of roughly 22–38% from that peak through April 2026 — the range reflecting how rapidly sentiment shifted during the broad mega-cap sell-off. As of early May 2026, shares had retraced to around $136, representing a drawdown of more than 34% from the November high.

module.name: Cloudflare, Inc.
module.blurb: Cloudflare operates a global cloud services platform that provides security, performance, and reliability solutions for businesses. Its offerings include content delivery network (CDN), DDoS mitigation, web application firewall, bot management, and API security. The company serves a wide range of clients from small businesses to large enterprises and is a leader in the edge computing and cybersecurity space.
module.recent: Cloudflare's stock has seen significant gains over the past month, trading near its 52-week high. The company is set to report earnings on May 7, 2026, with analysts expecting continued revenue growth. Recent news highlights strong demand for its security and AI-related services.

module.name: IREN Limited
module.blurb: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy) is an Australian-founded, NASDAQ-listed company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has since pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The company controls significant power capacity — a scarce resource in the AI data-centre boom — across sites in North America, and rebranded from Iris Energy to IREN in November 2024 to signal the strategic shift.
module.recent: IREN reported its first profitable fiscal year in 2025, with net income of $86.9 million on $501 million in revenue. A $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-computing agreement with Microsoft was signed in late 2025, calling for deployment of 76,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs across 200 megawatts at its Childress, Texas campus. The company targets scaling GPU capacity from 23,000 to 140,000 units through 2026, backed by 2,910 megawatts of renewable power infrastructure.

module.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
module.blurb: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States. It operates through four major segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management. The company provides a wide range of services including investment banking, financial transaction processing, asset management, and retail banking. As of 2025, it is the largest bank in the U.S. by assets and a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, JPMorgan Chase's stock has shown positive momentum, driven by strong quarterly earnings and favorable interest rate expectations. The company reported better-than-expected revenue and profit, benefiting from higher net interest income and robust investment banking fees. Analysts have raised price targets, citing the bank's diversified business model and capital strength.

module.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
module.blurb: Tencent Holdings is a Chinese multinational conglomerate and internet content & information company in the Communication Services sector. It operates social media, messaging, gaming, and digital payment platforms, including WeChat and QQ. With a market capitalization of approximately $744.8 billion, Tencent is one of the world's largest technology companies by market value.
module.recent: Over the past year, TCEHY stock has declined 6.3%, with shares last trading at $60.34. No specific recent news or earnings events were provided in the sources for the past 30 days.

module.name: Unity Software Inc.
module.blurb: Unity Software Inc. operates a platform for developing, deploying, and growing games and interactive experiences across mobile, PC, console, and extended reality devices. The company provides AI solutions that support the entire development lifecycle, including prototyping, live operations, user acquisition, and monetization. Its Create Solutions suite is widely used by game developers and creators. Unity is a leading player in the real-time 3D development market, competing with Epic Games' Unreal Engine.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, Unity's stock closed at $27.28, down 0.22% on the day, with a market cap of $11.90B. The company has a 52-week range of $16.78 to $52.15 and a forward PE of 26.61. Analysts have a Buy rating with a price target of $36.56, implying 34% upside. Earnings are scheduled for May 7, 2026.

module.name: Western Digital Corporation
module.blurb: Western Digital Corporation is a leading American data storage company that designs, manufactures, and sells hard disk drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs), and flash memory solutions under brands like WD, SanDisk, and G-Technology. The company serves both consumer and enterprise markets, including cloud data centers, and is a key player in the global storage industry. Western Digital has a strong market position in HDDs and NAND flash memory, competing with Seagate and Samsung.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Western Digital stock has seen positive momentum driven by strong demand for its HDD and SSD products, particularly from cloud and AI data center customers. The company reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter earnings in late October 2024, with revenue of $4.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.78, beating analyst estimates. Shares rose on the earnings beat and guidance for continued growth in the December quarter.

module.name: AST SpaceMobile, Inc.
module.blurb: AST SpaceMobile is building a network of large-aperture satellites in low Earth orbit designed to deliver broadband directly to unmodified standard mobile handsets — no specialised hardware required. The company has carrier partnerships representing roughly three billion potential subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, and Rakuten, and secured $1 billion in hard commercial commitments from those partners.
module.recent: BlueBird 6, described as the largest commercial communications array ever deployed in LEO, launched aboard an ISRO LVM3 rocket in December 2025. The company targets intermittent US nationwide service in early 2026 and continuous service by late 2026, with 45-60 satellites on orbit by year-end. A 10-year commercial agreement with stc Group (Saudi Arabia) was signed in October 2025.

module.name: Figma, Inc.
module.blurb: Figma, Inc. develops and sells a collaborative, browser-based platform for designing, prototyping, and building digital experiences. Its offerings include Figma Design for team-based design and prototyping, Dev Mode for translating designs into code, and FigJam for brainstorming and alignment. The company went public on July 31, 2025, and is listed on the NYSE under the ticker FIG.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, FIG stock closed at $19.29, down 0.67% on the day, with a market cap of $10.17B. The stock has a 52-week range of $16.60 to $142.92 and an analyst price target of $50.50, representing a potential upside of 161.79%. The next earnings report is scheduled for May 14, 2026.

module.blurb: Invesco QQQ Trust is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, a market-capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the NASDAQ exchange. Heavily concentrated in mega-cap technology and AI-adjacent companies — Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Tesla, and Broadcom collectively represent more than half the fund's weight — QQQ functions as the primary liquid proxy for institutional and retail exposure to U.S. large-cap growth, AI infrastructure buildout, and semiconductor cycles.
module.recent: It is the third-largest ETF in the world by assets under management, with approximately $330 billion in AUM and an expense ratio of 0.20% as of early May 2026.

module.name: Soitec SA
module.blurb: Soitec SA is a French semiconductor materials company founded in 1992 that develops and manufactures engineered substrates used in smartphones, automotive electronics, and 5G infrastructure. Its core product lines include Radio Frequency Silicon-on-Insulator (RF-SOI) wafers for smartphone front-end modules, FD-SOI substrates for low-power chips, Piezoelectric-on-Insulator (POI) RF filters, and RF gallium nitride for sub-6GHz and mmWave 5G systems. The company operates across Asia, Europe, and the United States with approximately 1,991 employees and a market capitalization of roughly €5.6 billion. Soitec holds a dominant position in the engineered substrate niche, supplying major semiconductor fabs and OEMs globally.
module.recent: As of mid-May 2026, Soitec shares trade around €152–155, well off their 52-week high of €180 but up sharply over the prior year (+163%) following a reverse stock split. Trailing-twelve-month revenue has contracted 14.3% to €784M and net income has fallen nearly 90% year-over-year, reflecting weakness in smartphone demand — a risk Morningstar analysts flagged in a March 2026 note that also cited silicon photonics as a potential long-term upside catalyst. The company's next scheduled earnings release is May 27, 2026, which will be closely watched for signs of stabilization in mobile volumes.

module.name: The Walt Disney Company
module.blurb: Disney is a global media and entertainment conglomerate whose assets span theme parks, film studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm), the ABC broadcast network, ESPN, and the Disney+ and Hulu streaming platforms. The company has undergone significant restructuring under returning CEO Bob Iger, who returned in 2022 to stabilise the company after a turbulent period under his successor. Disney's streaming transition has been costly but Disney+ reached profitability in late 2024.
module.recent: Disney reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $93 billion. The experiences segment (theme parks and cruises) remains the primary profit engine. The company is pursuing ESPN's transition to a direct-to-consumer streaming service and has made moves to consolidate streaming assets. Paul Pelosi sold 10,000 shares of DIS per the January 2026 PTR disclosure.

module.name: Apollo Global Management, Inc.
module.blurb: Apollo Global Management is a leading alternative asset manager specializing in private equity, credit, infrastructure, secondaries, and real estate. The firm invests across private and public markets, focusing on buyouts, distressed assets, and special situations. As of 2026, Apollo manages over $70 billion in market capitalization and is recognized as one of the largest asset managers globally.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Apollo reported earnings on May 6, 2026, with net income declining 68.2% year-over-year to $1.16 billion, though revenue grew 28.3% to $31.29 billion. The stock traded in a 52-week range of $99.56 to $157.28, closing at $127.79 on May 7, 2026. Analysts maintain a Buy rating with a price target of $147.27.

module.name: Arm Holdings plc
module.blurb: Arm Holdings licenses processor architectures and physical IP to virtually every chip company on earth. Rather than manufacturing chips, Arm charges royalties on every device that ships using an Arm-based design — from the iPhone to Android phones to embedded microcontrollers to, increasingly, cloud server chips and AI accelerators. Its v9 architecture is the basis for Apple Silicon, NVIDIA's Grace CPU, Amazon's Graviton, and the majority of mobile SoCs. Arm's business model is uniquely capital-light and royalty-compounding: as ASPs (average selling prices) of chips using Arm cores rise — driven by AI compute demand — Arm's royalty revenue grows without proportional cost increases.
module.recent: Arm trades at a forward P/E of ~98.5x on only 21.1% projected EPS growth, producing a PEG of 4.67 — the most expensive name in a table of thirty large-cap semiconductor stocks. Third-party estimates place the forward P/E even higher (90–121x as of April 2026). The premium reflects the thesis that Arm is the royalty collector of the entire AI compute era, but at a PEG of 4.67, investors are pricing in decades of compounding that has not yet materialised.

module.name: BlackRock, Inc.
module.blurb: BlackRock, Inc. is a publicly owned investment manager that provides services to institutional, intermediary, and individual investors, including pension plans, insurance companies, and governments. The firm manages a wide range of equity, fixed income, and balanced portfolios, and also offers global risk management and advisory services. As of May 2026, BlackRock has a market capitalization of approximately $174 billion and employs over 21,000 people. It is one of the world's largest asset managers, with a strong market position in the financial services industry.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, BlackRock's stock has traded in a range of $1,058.49 to $1,080.74, with a recent price of $1,067.74 as of May 7, 2026. The company reported earnings on April 14, 2026, and analysts maintain a Strong Buy rating with a price target of $1,275.21. The stock has shown a year-to-date increase of 25.6% in market cap, despite a slight decline in net income year-over-year.

module.name: Block, Inc.
module.blurb: Block, Inc. (formerly Square) is a technology company that provides an integrated ecosystem of commerce and financial services. Its brands include Square (point-of-sale and payment processing for sellers), Cash App (peer-to-peer payments and financial tools), Afterpay (buy now, pay later), and TIDAL (music streaming). The company serves millions of merchants and individual users globally, competing with traditional financial institutions and fintech peers.
module.recent: On January 9, 2025, Block announced its ticker symbol would change from SQ to XYZ, effective January 21, 2025, on the NYSE. The change aligns with the company's rebranding to Block and its multi-brand ecosystem. No other major news or earnings events were reported in the past 30 days.

module.name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
module.blurb: Cisco Systems, Inc. is a multinational technology conglomerate that designs, manufactures, and sells networking hardware, software, telecommunications equipment, and other high-technology services and products. The company is a leading provider of networking solutions for the internet, data centers, and enterprise communications, and has been expanding into cybersecurity, cloud, and AI infrastructure. Cisco holds a dominant market position in the networking industry, competing with companies like Juniper Networks and Arista Networks.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Cisco's stock has been influenced by broader market trends in AI and data center spending, with analysts highlighting its role as an AI beneficiary. Jim Cramer included Cisco in a list of AI winners for 2026, and the stock has traded near its 52-week high of $94.72, reflecting investor optimism about its networking and security solutions for AI workloads.

module.name: CoreWeave, Inc.
module.blurb: CoreWeave is a neocloud — a GPU-specialist cloud provider that rents NVIDIA accelerator capacity to AI developers, research labs, and enterprises rather than offering the broad service catalogue of a hyperscaler. Founded in 2017 as a cryptocurrency mining operation and pivoted to GPU cloud in 2019, it operates more than 40 data centres with roughly 250,000 NVIDIA GPUs. Its commercial model is long-term capacity contracts — often three to seven years — which produce a large, predictable backlog but require heavy upfront debt-financed capital expenditure. CoreWeave went public on NASDAQ on 28 March 2025 at $40 per share, valuing the company at approximately $23 billion fully diluted. NVIDIA invested $2 billion in CoreWeave at $87.20 per share in January 2026, cementing the symbiotic relationship between the two companies.
module.recent: CoreWeave reported $5.1 billion in revenue for full-year 2025, up 170% year-on-year, with quarterly revenue reaching $1.57 billion in Q4. Microsoft accounted for approximately 67% of FY2025 revenue. OpenAI has contracted up to $22.4 billion in cumulative commitments, and Meta signed a $14.2 billion agreement through December 2031. Total remaining performance obligations represent roughly 13 years of revenue at current run rates. In April 2026, CoreWeave priced an upsized $3.5 billion convertible senior notes offering and announced a multi-year GPU capacity agreement with Anthropic.

module.name: GlobalFoundries Inc.
module.blurb: GlobalFoundries Inc. (NASDAQ: GFS) is the world's third-largest semiconductor foundry by revenue, operating advanced manufacturing facilities in the United States (Fab 8 in Malta, NY; Vermont), Germany (Dresden), and Singapore. Unlike TSMC and Samsung, GlobalFoundries exited the leading-edge node race in 2018 and now focuses on differentiated specialty processes: silicon photonics, silicon-germanium (SiGe), RF CMOS, FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator), and embedded non-volatile memory. This positions GF as a complement — and sometimes a competitor — to Tower Semiconductor in the specialty foundry space.
module.recent: GF reported FY2025 revenue of $6.79 billion (up 1% year-over-year) with gross margin improving 360 basis points to 29% and diluted EPS of $1.72. Silicon photonics revenue exceeded $200 million in 2025 and is expected to nearly double in 2026, with management guiding toward a $1 billion annual run rate by end-2028. In June 2025, the company announced a $16 billion US investment plan anchored by its New York and Vermont fabs. GF also finalised a $1.5 billion CHIPS Act direct-funding agreement with the US government. In January 2026, GF agreed to acquire Synopsys' ARC Processor IP unit, targeting physical-AI embedded applications.

module.name: Infineon Technologies AG
module.blurb: Infineon Technologies is a global power-semiconductor leader headquartered in Munich, Germany, trading on US markets as an ADR (IFNNY). Its product lineup for AI server power delivery includes OptiMOS and CoolMOS MOSFETs, high-density quad-phase power modules (OptiMOS TDM2454xx, 280A in a 10x9mm footprint), XDP digital hot-swap and protection controllers for 48V AI racks, EiceDRIVER isolated gate drivers supporting SiC and GaN topologies, and high-voltage GaN reference designs for LLC converters running at 800V input. Infineon is a preferred power-silicon partner in NVIDIA's 800V HVDC reference architecture for next-generation AI data centres.
module.recent: Infineon closed FY2025 (ending September 2025) with revenue of €14.66 billion and significantly raised its AI power revenue target to approximately €1.5 billion in FY2026, citing rapidly rising AI infrastructure demand. Revenue for the quarter ending December 2025 was $4.26 billion, up 16.8% year-over-year. In Q1 FY2026 the company announced new HV GaN reference designs for AI server power architectures and expanded its XDP digital protection family with the XDP711-001 48V hot-swap controller. A new Smart Power Fab in Dresden is on track to open in summer 2026. FY2026 guidance calls for moderate total revenue growth, with AI power as the primary growth driver against softer automotive and industrial demand, and adjusted gross margin in the low-forties percent range.

module.name: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE
module.blurb: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE is a German technology company that develops and manufactures laser-based solutions for the electronics, semiconductor, and medical technology industries. Its key growth areas include Advanced Semiconductor Packaging and LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) for glass processing. The company holds a strong market position in laser systems for PCB prototyping and micro-material processing.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, LPKF reported weaker Q1 2026 results with lower sales and a larger loss, but the stock surged as investors focused on its Advanced Semiconductor Packaging and LIDE growth potential. The share price reached a 52-week high of €29.90 on May 11, 2026, reflecting a year-to-date return of over 350%. The stock has since pulled back slightly, trading around €25.70 as of mid-May.

module.name: Marvell Technology, Inc.
module.blurb: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company that designs custom AI silicon (XPUs) for hyperscalers, high-speed networking ASICs (application-specific integrated circuits) for data-centre switching, and storage controllers. Its custom silicon business — building proprietary AI accelerators for Google, Amazon, and Microsoft under long-term agreements — has become its fastest-growing segment. Marvell also supplies Ethernet SerDes (serialiser/deserialiser) components, optical DSPs for coherent networking, and enterprise storage chips. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara and manufactures exclusively at TSMC.
module.recent: Marvell reported record FY2026 revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42% YoY, with data-centre revenue reaching 74% of total sales. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.84 represented 81% growth. Despite this, forward EPS growth estimates for the next fiscal year are near 0.2% — likely a fiscal-calendar base-effect or consensus lag — producing a non-meaningful PEG at a 42.1x forward P/E. Custom silicon revenue is expected to accelerate as hyperscaler XPU programs ramp into production.

module.name: MediaTek Inc.
module.blurb: MediaTek Inc. is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company that designs system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for mobile devices, smart TVs, networking, and IoT. It is one of the world's largest chip designers, competing with Qualcomm in the smartphone processor market. The company also supplies chips for AI, automotive, and edge computing applications.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, MediaTek's stock traded near its 52-week high of TWD 3,470, reflecting strong demand for its smartphone and AI chips. The company has been gaining market share in mid-range 5G chipsets and expanding into automotive and AI edge computing. No major earnings or news were reported in the last month.

module.name: Monolithic Power Systems, Inc.
module.blurb: A fab-light analog company that designs high-density power-management integrated circuits — the chips that step a server's intermediate-bus voltage down to the sub-1-volt rail an AI accelerator actually consumes. MPWR moved from a broad-based analog supplier into the dominant provider of GPU-adjacent power modules during the H100 generation, displacing the incumbent Vicor at Nvidia. Its modules are characterised by very high current density and tight integration, which matter enormously as AI racks push past 100 kilowatts.
module.recent: In early 2026, management raised the floor on its enterprise-data growth target to 50-percent-plus from a prior 30-to-40 percent range, citing acceleration in Nvidia Blackwell shipments. Analyst notes suggest MPWR may take roughly 70 percent of power-management sockets on the forthcoming Vera Rubin GPU platform (VR200 NVL144 and R200 HGX), potentially adding more than $100 million to 2026 estimates. The stock has gained roughly 90 percent over the trailing twelve months and trades near all-time highs, leaving the AI exposure largely in the price.

module.name: POET Technologies Inc.
module.blurb: POET Technologies develops optical engines — compact co-packaged modules that integrate lasers and photonic integrated circuits — targeting 400G, 800G, and 1.6T AI data-centre interconnect applications. Its POET Infinity platform is designed to allow customers to assemble high-density optical transceiver modules without owning their own photonics fabrication. The company raised approximately $375M in equity in Q4 2025 and carries roughly $430M in cash.
module.recent: POET experienced one of the more dramatic volatility events in the photonics sector during April 2026. Shares rallied roughly 108% on reports its technology was being integrated into Marvell Technology's AI hardware stack via Celestial AI (which Marvell had acquired). On April 27, 2026, POET disclosed it had received notice of order cancellation from Marvell on April 23, with Marvell citing a confidentiality violation; shares fell approximately 50% in a single week. POET countered with a separate $5M production order for Infinity engines targeting 30,000+ units in 2026, and maintained partnerships with LITEON and Lessengers for 1.6T modules. The episode became a widely-cited example of single-customer concentration risk in small-cap photonics. @Ren_aramb's post singles out POET as the notable exception in an otherwise rising sector.

module.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
module.blurb: QUALCOMM is the dominant designer of smartphone application processors (Snapdragon) and the world leader in mobile baseband modems — the chips that connect phones to cellular networks. The company operates a dual business model: QCT (chip sales) and QTL (technology licensing), with the latter generating high-margin royalties on every 3G/4G/5G handset sold globally. QUALCOMM is actively diversifying into automotive silicon and edge AI processors to reduce dependence on the handset market, particularly following Apple's decision to develop its own modems.
module.recent: Q2 FY2026 revenue reached $10.6 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $2.65. Automotive revenue hit $1.3 billion (+38% YoY), crossing $5 billion annualised for the first time. The expected partial loss of Apple modem business is weighing on forward EPS consensus, producing near-flat EPS growth estimates (-0.3%) for next fiscal year despite strong automotive and IoT momentum. Forward P/E sits at ~15.7x — undemanding for a franchise with durable licensing revenue.

module.name: Snap Inc.
module.blurb: Snap Inc. operates Snapchat, a visual messaging app, and offers advertising products, subscription services (Snapchat+, Lens+, Snapchat Platinum), and augmented reality glasses (Spectacles). The company generates revenue primarily from advertising and faces competition from other social media platforms. As of May 2026, Snap has a market cap of about $10.3 billion and is unprofitable, with a net loss of $460 million on revenue of $5.93 billion.
module.recent: In late April 2026, Snap announced a deal with Experian to integrate AI-powered financial education tools into Snapchat's AI Sponsored Snaps format, and disclosed an upcoming CFO transition. The stock rose 11.3% following the news, but also faced an activist investor letter pressing for a review of its Spectacles subsidiary and governance issues. As of May 6, 2026, SNAP traded at $6.11, down 9.47% after-hours.

module.name: STMicroelectronics N.V.
module.blurb: STMicroelectronics is a global semiconductor group covering microcontrollers, sensors (MEMS), and — most relevant to the AI power-plumbing thesis — a broad power-semiconductor portfolio spanning SiC MOSFETs (STPOWER Gen 4), GaN devices, silicon IGBTs, and power-management ICs. ST is one of only a handful of vendors with an end-to-end 800 VDC power-conversion solution for AI data centres, offering complete reference designs from 800V bus-to-50V, 12V, and 6V conversion using its own SiC and GaN silicon. The company serves automotive, industrial, and, increasingly, hyperscale data-centre customers.
module.recent: ST reported Q1 2026 revenue of $3.10 billion, up 23% year-over-year and above consensus of $3.04 billion, with Q2 2026 guidance of ~$3.45 billion. In March 2026 the company announced expanded 800 VDC power-conversion products (12V and 6V architectures) developed to the NVIDIA 800 VDC reference design and showcased at NVIDIA GTC 2026. In February 2026 ST disclosed a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar engagement with Amazon Web Services to supply semiconductors for AWS compute and AI data-centre infrastructure. Management projects data-centre revenue exceeding $500 million in 2026 and surpassing $1 billion in 2027.

module.name: Unity Software Inc.
module.blurb: Unity Software Inc. operates a platform for developing, deploying, and growing games and interactive experiences across mobile, PC, console, and extended reality devices. The company provides AI solutions that support the entire development lifecycle, including prototyping, live operations, user acquisition, and monetization. Its Create Solutions suite is widely used by game developers and creators. Unity is a leading player in the real-time 3D development market, competing with Epic Games' Unreal Engine.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, Unity's stock closed at $27.28, down 0.22% on the day, with a market cap of $11.90B. The company has a 52-week range of $16.78 to $52.15 and a forward PE of 26.61. Analysts have a Buy rating with a price target of $36.56, implying 34% upside. Earnings are scheduled for May 7, 2026.

module.name: Aehr Test Systems
module.blurb: Aehr Test Systems designs and manufactures wafer-level burn-in and test equipment for semiconductors, with a specialisation in silicon carbide (SiC) power devices, gallium nitride (GaN), and — increasingly — silicon photonics chips. Its flagship FOX-XP system stress-tests devices while still on the wafer, before costly packaging, identifying failures at the cheapest possible point in manufacturing. Aehr claims to be the first company to ship a multi-wafer burn-in solution for silicon photonics transceivers. The company is headquartered in Fremont, California.
module.recent: In March 2026, Aehr won a new silicon photonics customer for its high-power FOX-XP wafer-level burn-in system targeting hyperscale data-centre optical interconnects. Quarterly bookings reached $37.2 million in the quarter ending February 2026 — a book-to-bill ratio exceeding 3.5x — with the company guiding full-year FY2026 revenue toward the high end of its $45–$50 million range. Revenue in the same quarter was $10.3 million, down from $18.3 million a year earlier, reflecting a timing gap between order intake and shipment schedules weighted toward the second half of 2026.

module.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
module.blurb: AMD is a fabless semiconductor company that designs CPUs (EPYC for data centres, Ryzen for consumer PCs) and GPUs (Instinct for AI/HPC, Radeon for gaming and workstations). Under CEO Lisa Su, AMD has taken significant data-centre CPU market share from Intel with its EPYC server processors, which now command an estimated 30%+ of the x86 server CPU market. AMD's MI300X and MI350 AI accelerators compete directly with NVIDIA's H100/H200 family and are gaining traction with hyperscalers seeking GPU supply alternatives. All AMD chips are manufactured by TSMC.
module.recent: AMD reported strong 2025 revenue growth led by EPYC and Instinct, with data-centre revenue crossing $12 billion annually. Forward P/E of ~32.6x on 63.8% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 0.51 — compelling for a company with clear data-centre CPU momentum and an AI accelerator portfolio that is gaining customer adoption. NVIDIA's dominant CUDA ecosystem remains the primary competitive barrier for AMD's GPU ambitions.

module.name: Analog Devices, Inc.
module.blurb: Analog Devices is one of the two largest analog semiconductor companies in the world (alongside Texas Instruments), with deep expertise in signal-chain ICs, data converters, and — critical for AI servers — power-management products including hot-swap controllers, multiphase voltage regulators, power-system management ICs (PSMICs), and DC-DC power stages. ADI's LTC4284/4286/4287 hot-swap family protects 48V AI rack infrastructure, while its MAX20790 and related multiphase controllers regulate power to GPUs and accelerators at the point-of-load. The company is also a leading supplier of 800 VDC first-stage conversion solutions designed to NVIDIA's high-voltage DC reference architecture for AI factories.
module.recent: ADI reported Q1 FY2026 (quarter ending January 2026) EPS of $2.46 versus the $2.31 consensus, with revenue of $3.16 billion supported by a 50% year-over-year increase in data-centre revenue. AI and data-centre exposure now accounts for roughly one-fifth of total revenues. Q2 FY2026 guidance was set at $3.5 billion (±$100 million), with non-GAAP EPS of $2.88 (±$0.15) and adjusted operating margin of ~47.5%. In August 2025 ADI announced its first 800 VDC hot-swap and first-stage power solutions targeting NVIDIA intelligent platform management, with >98% conversion efficiency. The company has seen accelerating adoption of 48V/54V intermediate-bus converters and smart power stages for vertical power delivery in AI racks.

module.name: Autodesk, Inc.
module.blurb: Autodesk, Inc. provides 3D design, engineering, and entertainment technology solutions worldwide. Its products include AutoCAD, Revit, and Autodesk Build, serving industries such as architecture, engineering, construction, and media. With a market cap of about $51 billion and over 14,000 employees, Autodesk is a leading software company in the design and building information modeling space.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, ADSK stock has traded in a range of $214.10 to $329.09, closing at $243.08 on May 6, 2026. Notable news includes Michael Burry buying the dip in software stocks amid an AI-fueled sell-off, and analyst commentary on software's AI troubles persisting. The company's next earnings report is scheduled for May 28, 2026.

module.name: Bank of America Corporation
module.blurb: Bank of America is one of the largest financial institutions in the United States, serving individual consumers, small and middle-market businesses, institutional investors, large corporations, and governments worldwide. It operates through four segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking, and Global Markets. Founded in 1784 and headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, the bank employs approximately 213,000 people and carries a market capitalization of roughly $364 billion. It is a core component of the U.S. financial system and a constituent of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
module.recent: Bank of America reported Q1 2026 earnings on April 15, 2026, with trailing-twelve-month net income of $30.26B (up ~14.7% year-over-year) and EPS of $4.02 (up ~21.2%), reflecting continued strength across its banking and markets segments. The stock reached a 52-week high of $57.55 before pulling back; as of May 8, 2026 shares closed at $51.31, down 2.73% on the day, though analysts maintain a consensus Buy rating with an average price target of $60.61. Year-over-year revenue growth of ~7.1% to $109.59B (ttm) and a forward P/E of 11.29 suggest the market is pricing in steady but not accelerating earnings expansion.

module.name: Bloom Energy Corporation
module.blurb: Bloom Energy manufactures solid-oxide fuel cells — electrochemical devices that convert natural gas or hydrogen into electricity on-site through a chemical reaction rather than combustion, producing lower emissions than conventional generators and requiring no grid connection. The company sells its 'Energy Servers' primarily to data centres, utilities, and industrial customers seeking dispatchable, grid-independent power. Bloom's technology can also run on hydrogen, positioning it as a longer-term clean-energy play as the hydrogen economy matures.
module.recent: Bloom Energy became one of the defining AI-power stocks of 2025-2026 after Oracle announced it would power its Project Jupiter AI data centre campus entirely with Bloom fuel cells. Q1 2026 revenue rose 130% year-on-year; management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $3.40–3.80 billion and guided adjusted EPS of $1.85–2.25, well above consensus. The stock ran from a 2025 low of approximately $16 to $295 by early May 2026, a gain exceeding 1,700%. Total backlog stands at roughly $20 billion ($6 billion product, $14 billion service). The valuation is extreme: the stock trades at a near-incalculable trailing P/E and analyst consensus price targets (~$180) imply roughly 39% downside, yet the stock continues to attract momentum buyers on the AI-power narrative. Beta stands at 3.83, reflecting the name's status as a high-conviction, high-volatility AI infrastructure speculation.

module.name: Cameco Corporation
module.blurb: Cameco Corporation is a leading global provider of uranium fuel for nuclear power generation, operating through three segments: Uranium, Fuel Services, and Westinghouse. The Uranium segment explores, mines, and sells uranium concentrate; Fuel Services handles refining, conversion, and fabrication; and Westinghouse is a nuclear reactor technology OEM. Headquartered in Canada, Cameco is one of the world's largest uranium producers and plays a critical role in the nuclear energy supply chain.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Cameco reported strong earnings on May 5, 2026, with net income surging 161.6% year-over-year to $466.07 million. The stock has traded in a 52-week range of $48.81 to $135.24, closing at $116.75 on May 8, 2026. Analysts maintain a Strong Buy rating with a price target of $123.92, reflecting optimism around nuclear energy demand.

module.name: Cboe Global Markets, Inc.
module.blurb: Cboe Global Markets is one of the world's largest exchange operators, providing trading in options, futures, equities, exchange-traded products (ETPs), foreign exchange, and multi-asset volatility products. The company is best known for operating the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and the VIX volatility index, which is widely regarded as the market's 'fear gauge.' Cboe operates exchanges across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, serving institutional and retail participants globally. Its data and access solutions segment provides a growing recurring revenue stream alongside its transaction-based exchange businesses.
module.recent: Not enough public information from the provided sources to describe specific news, earnings, or price action from the past 30 days.

module.name: Cerebras Systems Inc.
module.blurb: Cerebras Systems is an AI infrastructure company that designs and manufactures wafer-scale processors purpose-built for AI training and inference, most notably its Wafer Scale Engine. The company builds complete AI supercomputer systems—hardware, cooling, networking, and software—and also offers inference-as-a-service at speeds it claims are unattainable on conventional GPU-based alternatives. With 708 employees and trailing-twelve-month revenue of approximately $510 million (up ~548% year-over-year), Cerebras targets hyperscalers, AI labs, and enterprises running large-scale model training and inference workloads using familiar ML frameworks such as PyTorch.
module.recent: Cerebras completed the largest IPO of 2026 on May 14, 2026, pricing 30 million shares at $185 each and raising $5.55 billion. Shares nearly doubled on debut, closing at $311.07 (+68.15%) and continuing higher in pre-market trading on May 15 to approximately $330, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $67 billion. The bull case centers on a high-profile inference partnership with OpenAI, though analysts have flagged customer concentration risk as a key concern.

module.name: MP Materials Corp.
module.blurb: MP Materials operates Mountain Pass in California, the only producing rare-earth mining and processing facility in the United States. The company extracts and refines neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide and in 2025 opened a full-scale permanent magnet manufacturing plant in Fort Worth, Texas. Its customers include General Motors under a long-term supply agreement for electric-vehicle traction motor magnets, and the U.S. government has backed the company with roughly $400 million in strategic investment.
module.recent: In early 2025 MP Materials inaugurated its Fort Worth magnet facility and began commercial NdFeB magnet shipments to GM, a landmark for domestic rare-earth supply-chain independence. The company's AI revenue exposure remains indirect — data-center cooling fans and robotics actuators use its magnets — but the robotics angle is drawing increasing investor attention as humanoid robot programs scale.

module.name: Nebius Group N.V.
module.blurb: Nebius Group is the Amsterdam-headquartered successor entity to Yandex's international operations after the Russian tech giant divested all domestic assets to a Russian consortium in a $5.4 billion transaction completed in July 2024. Led by Yandex co-founder Arkady Volozh, the renamed company has repositioned itself as a full-stack GPU cloud — a so-called neocloud — offering compute infrastructure for training and running large AI models. The Yandex engineering lineage gives it unusual depth in distributed systems and large-scale model serving.
module.recent: Nebius resumed NASDAQ trading under ticker NBIS in October 2024 (formerly YNDX). Revenue for fiscal 2025 came in at $529.8 million, up roughly 479% year-over-year. Management guided to $3.0-3.4 billion in 2026 revenue. A reported $2.7 billion infrastructure deal with Meta in early 2026 would represent a step-function expansion of its client base.

module.name: Netflix, Inc.
module.blurb: Netflix is the world's largest subscription video-on-demand service, headquartered in Los Gatos, California, with over 300 million paid memberships globally as of early 2026. The company transformed from a DVD-rental-by-mail business into the dominant streaming platform by investing heavily in original content (films, series, live events) and expanding internationally. Recent growth drivers include a crackdown on password sharing that forced freeloading households onto paid plans, the launch of an advertising-supported tier that meaningfully expanded its addressable market, and tentative moves into live sports and gaming. Netflix does not operate large AI-compute infrastructure at the scale of cloud hyperscalers; its AI use is concentrated in content recommendation and advertising targeting.
module.recent: Netflix peaked near $1,000–$1,050 per share in mid-2025 following strong subscriber growth and the success of its password-sharing enforcement globally. The stock had advanced more than 90% from its 2024 lows. Through early 2026, shares gave back roughly 30–39% from those highs as the market reassessed whether the password-sharing-driven growth surge was a one-time pull-forward and as broader mega-cap sentiment soured on AI-spending uncertainty. The company remains profitable and cash-generative, with annual revenue exceeding $40 billion.

module.name: Nokia Corporation
module.blurb: Nokia is a Finnish telecommunications-equipment maker whose Network Infrastructure division designs optical networking hardware — coherent transceivers, optical line systems, and optical amplifiers — used by carriers and data-centre operators globally. The 2024 acquisition of Infinera, a specialist in coherent digital signal processing and indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits, gave Nokia one of the more vertically integrated optical stacks in the industry.
module.recent: In March 2026, Nokia launched a suite of AI-era optical solutions including a 1.6T coherent pluggable for data-centre interconnect and a 2.4T pluggable for subsea and terrestrial transport, alongside four new digital signal processors built on both indium phosphide and silicon photonics. Nokia cited up to 70% total-cost-of-ownership savings versus prior-generation products. New line systems are expected in H2 2026; advanced coherent sampling begins mid-2027. At OFC 2026, Nokia emphasised that the Infinera acquisition provides the vertical integration needed to address the widening gap between AI compute and networking capacity.

module.name: Ondas Holdings, Inc.
module.blurb: Ondas Holdings is an autonomous systems and drone technology company operating through two main segments: Ondas Autonomous Systems (drone and counter-drone platforms) and Ondas Networks (industrial wireless communications). Its Iron Drone Raider counter-UAS system and Optimus autonomous drone platforms serve defence, homeland security, and industrial customers in the US, Europe, Israel, and the UAE.
module.recent: Ondas delivered 605% revenue growth in 2025, with Q4 2025 revenue of $30.1 million — up 629% year-over-year. A pending $175 million merger with Mistral, a Bethesda, MD-based prime contractor with over $1 billion in existing DoD IDIQ (indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity) contracts, was announced. The company secured US border-security drone contracts. Stock rallied over 1,000% from 52-week lows, driven by defence-drone demand and the Mistral deal, before analysts cautioned on execution risk at elevated multiples.

module.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
module.blurb: QUALCOMM is the dominant designer of smartphone application processors (Snapdragon) and the world leader in mobile baseband modems — the chips that connect phones to cellular networks. The expected partial loss of Apple modem business is weighing on forward EPS consensus, producing near-flat EPS growth estimates (-0.3%) for next fiscal year despite strong automotive and IoT momentum. Forward P/E sits at ~15.7x — undemanding for a franchise with durable licensing revenue.

module.blurb: STMicroelectronics is a global semiconductor group covering microcontrollers, sensors (MEMS), and — most relevant to the AI power-plumbing thesis — a broad power-semiconductor portfolio spanning SiC MOSFETs (STPOWER Gen 4), GaN devices, silicon IGBTs, and power-management ICs. The company serves automotive, industrial, and, increasingly, hyperscale data-centre customers.
