In March 2026 the company announced expanded 800 VDC power-conversion products (12V and 6V architectures) developed to the NVIDIA 800 VDC reference design and showcased at NVIDIA GTC 2026. In February 2026 ST disclosed a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar engagement with Amazon Web Services to supply semiconductors for AWS compute and AI data-centre infrastructure. Management projects data-centre revenue exceeding $500 million in 2026 and surpassing $1 billion in 2027.

module.name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
module.blurb: The largest pure-play analog-semiconductor maker in the world by revenue, with roughly twenty percent share of the analog market. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures power-management chips, signal-chain devices and embedded processors used in industrial machinery, automobiles and, increasingly, AI servers. Its strategy is unusual in the industry: it owns and operates several 300-millimetre wafer fabs in the United States, giving it a long-term cost advantage against fab-light competitors, but also requiring a multi-year capital-spending programme that compressed free cash flow through 2023-2024.
module.recent: Q1 2026 revenue came in at $4.83 billion, ahead of the $4.53 billion consensus, with analog-segment revenue up 22 percent year on year and data-centre revenue up roughly 90 percent. Capital expenditure dropped 40 percent year on year to $676 million as the 300mm fab build-out tapers, and free cash flow rose to $1.40 billion. The company has also announced selective price increases of 15 to 85 percent on certain analog products effective April 2026, in line with similar moves by Analog Devices, Infineon and Murata. The stock is up roughly 50 percent year-to-date through April 2026.

module.name: Tower Semiconductor
module.blurb: Tower Semiconductor is an Israeli specialty foundry that fabricates analogue, mixed-signal, and photonic chips across 200mm and 300mm wafer lines. Unlike pure-play logic foundries such as TSMC, Tower focuses on differentiated process technologies where customers need more than commodity nodes — silicon photonics, silicon-germanium (SiGe), radio-frequency CMOS, and power management. Tower's silicon photonics platform (SiPho) is widely regarded as one of the most mature independent photonics foundry offerings, supporting both passive waveguide structures and active electro-optic components on the same wafer. The company operates fabs in Israel, the United States, Japan, and Italy.
module.recent: Tower committed $920 million in capital expenditure to silicon photonics and SiGe capacity — a 40% increase from a plan announced just three months earlier — with over 70% of that reserved or prepaid by customers through 2028. In November 2025, the company launched a dedicated CPO Foundry offering with 300mm wafer-bonding technology and targeted more than quintupling its monthly SiPho wafer shipments between Q4 2025 and late 2026. In March 2026, Tower announced full ownership of its 300mm Fab 7 facility in Japan to support this expansion, positioning itself to challenge GlobalFoundries for the top-ranked independent silicon photonics foundry slot.

module.name: Unimicron Technology Corp.
module.blurb: Unimicron Technology Corp. is a Taiwan-based manufacturer of printed circuit boards (PCBs) and IC substrates, serving the semiconductor and electronics industries. The company is a key supplier for advanced packaging solutions, including substrates for high-performance computing and AI chips. It holds a strong market position as one of the world's largest IC substrate producers, competing with companies like Ibiden and Shinko Electric Industries.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Unimicron's stock has been influenced by broader semiconductor demand trends and AI-related optimism. The company reported steady revenue growth, supported by robust demand for ABF substrates used in AI and data center applications. Analysts have highlighted its potential to benefit from increased chip packaging complexity, though near-term price action has been mixed amid global economic uncertainties.

module.name: Vertiv Holdings Co
module.blurb: Vertiv Holdings Co designs, manufactures, and services critical digital infrastructure technologies and life cycle services for data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial environments globally. The company offers power management products, thermal management solutions, and integrated modular systems. Vertiv is a key player in the data center infrastructure market, benefiting from the growth of AI and cloud computing.
module.recent: As of May 7, 2026, VRT stock closed at $340.01, down 5.27% on the day, with a 52-week range of $91.84 to $359.84. The company reported strong financials with revenue of $10.84B and net income of $1.56B over the trailing twelve months. Analysts maintain a Buy rating with a price target of $272.83, implying a potential downside from current levels.

module.name: Wolfspeed, Inc.
module.blurb: Wolfspeed designs and manufactures silicon carbide (SiC) power devices and substrates, positioning itself as the only vertically integrated producer at 200mm SiC wafer scale. Carved out of Cree in 2021, the company bet heavily on the EV and industrial power transition, sinking billions into the John Palmour Manufacturing Center in North Carolina and the Mohawk Valley Fab in New York. The ambition was sound; the balance sheet was not. After accumulating roughly $4.6 billion in debt and missing the expected CHIPS Act funding of $750 million, Wolfspeed filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on June 30, 2025. It emerged ninety-one days later in a prepackaged restructuring that eliminated ~70% of its debt, extended maturities to 2030, and cut annual cash interest expense by roughly 60%. Existing shareholders received only 3–5% of the reorganised equity; the bulk went to convertible noteholders (56.3%) and strategic investor Renesas (38.7%), who received new common stock plus warrants.
module.recent: Post-emergence, the reorganised Wolfspeed trades on NYSE under WOLF. The company's enterprise value at emergence was estimated at $2.35–2.85 billion (midpoint $2.6B), implying equity of $850M–$1.35B. As of May 2026 shares trade near $38. A December 2025 IRS settlement worth roughly $698 million provided unexpected cash relief. Chinese SiC substrate producers SICC (688234.SS) and TanKeBlue have gained market share during Wolfspeed's restructuring, while Infineon, STMicroelectronics, onsemi, and Rohm continue to invest in competing SiC capacity.

module.name: Airbnb, Inc.
module.blurb: Airbnb, Inc. operates a global online marketplace for lodging and travel experiences, connecting hosts with guests. Founded in 2008, the company has disrupted the traditional hospitality industry by enabling individuals to rent out their properties or offer unique activities. As of 2025, Airbnb is one of the largest travel platforms in the world, with a market capitalization exceeding $80 billion.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Airbnb's stock has shown volatility amid mixed analyst ratings and broader market trends. The company reported strong Q4 2024 earnings in February, beating revenue estimates but providing cautious forward guidance due to macroeconomic uncertainties. Shares have fluctuated between $130 and $150, with recent news focusing on regulatory challenges in key European markets.

module.name: Applied Materials, Inc.
module.blurb: Applied Materials is the world's largest semiconductor equipment company by revenue, supplying deposition, etch, ion implantation, and metrology tools used in chip fabrication at every major foundry and memory manufacturer. Unlike ASML (which focuses on lithography), Applied Materials covers the broadest range of wafer processing steps — most chips manufactured anywhere pass through multiple Applied Materials tools. The company also supplies solar and display manufacturing equipment. Its services business (AGS) provides recurring revenue through parts, upgrades, and maintenance contracts.
module.recent: Applied Materials has benefited from sustained semiconductor equipment investment across logic (TSMC, Samsung, Intel), DRAM, and NAND capacity expansions. Forward P/E of ~27.3x on 27.1% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.01 — right at the conventional fair-value boundary. Revenue for FY2025 exceeded $28 billion. U.S. export restrictions on advanced equipment to China have created some demand uncertainty but also pushed customers to accelerate domestic tool installations.

module.name: Ares Management Corporation
module.blurb: Ares Management Corporation is a global alternative asset manager operating through Direct Lending, Private Equity, and other segments. It provides financing solutions to small-to-medium sized companies and specializes in growth capital, middle market, mezzanine, distressed, and growth buyouts across sectors such as healthcare, services, energy, industrials, and consumer. The firm primarily invests in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, taking majority, minority, and shared-control positions. As of May 2026, Ares Management has a market capitalization of approximately $40.6 billion and manages over $5.9 billion in revenue.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Ares Management stock experienced a decline, with a 14.9% drop in market cap and a 52-week range of $95.80 to $195.26. The company reported earnings on May 1, 2026, with net income up 42.2% year-over-year to $564.1 million and EPS of $2.10, a 19.6% increase. Analysts maintain a Buy rating with a price target of $166.25, suggesting a 35% upside from the current price of $123.15.

module.name: ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: ASE Technology is the world's largest OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) company, responsible for packaging and testing chips after they leave the foundry wafer fab. Chip packaging — the process of cutting wafers into individual dies, mounting them in substrates, and connecting them to the outside world — is increasingly strategic as advanced packaging (chiplets, CoWoS, SoIC) becomes essential for AI accelerators that exceed the reticle size limits of individual dies. ASE's CoWoS-compatible packaging capacity has become a key bottleneck in NVIDIA Blackwell GPU supply chains. ASE is headquartered in Kaohsiung, Taiwan.
module.recent: ASE has benefited from surging demand for advanced packaging from AI chip supply chains. NVIDIA's Blackwell GPUs require CoWoS advanced packaging, a significant portion of which flows through ASE and its competitor SPIL (a subsidiary). Forward P/E of ~47.4x on 39.7% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.19. Revenue growth is driven by advanced packaging volumes rather than legacy wire-bond assembly.

module.name: ASML Holding N.V.
module.blurb: ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company and the sole manufacturer of EUV (extreme ultraviolet) lithography machines — the tools required to print the finest circuit features on leading-edge chips at 5nm and below. Every AI accelerator, high-bandwidth memory chip, and advanced logic die manufactured at TSMC, Samsung, or Intel passes through ASML optics. The company's monopoly position emerged after decades of public-private R&D investment in partnership with European governments and chipmakers.
module.recent: ASML reported €32.7 billion in total net sales for full-year 2025, up roughly 16% year-on-year, with net income of €9.6 billion and a gross margin of 52.8%. Year-end backlog stood at €38.8 billion. Q4 2025 saw record total net sales of €9.7 billion, including revenue recognized for the first High-NA EUV systems — the next-generation machines required for 2nm nodes and below. TSMC accounts for an estimated 40% of EUV tool deliveries. ASML guides to €34–39 billion for 2026 and €44–60 billion by 2030 as High-NA adoption widens. In December 2025 Huawei and Chinese startup SiCarrier confirmed a functional EUV light source using an alternative plasma architecture, but analysts place production-ready Chinese competition no earlier than 2028–2030.

module.name: Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc.
module.blurb: Eos Energy manufactures zinc-bromide long-duration battery storage systems using its proprietary Znyth chemistry. Unlike lithium-ion batteries (typically two hours of discharge), Eos's Z3 modules support four to sixteen-plus hours of storage with no degradation penalty — a profile suited to grid-scale renewable energy firming and data-centre backup. The company received a $305 million DOE loan guarantee in November 2024 to build two manufacturing lines in Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania.

It became a high-profile case study in pharmaceutical compounding: during the years-long shortage of semaglutide (the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy), the company produced and sold cheaper copycat formulations legally permitted under FDA shortage rules, turning a niche clinical carve-out into a headline growth engine.
module.recent: The FDA declared semaglutide no longer in shortage in early 2025, effectively terminating the legal basis for Hims's compounded GLP-1 business and triggering a roughly 20% stock drop. The company pivoted: it entered a distribution agreement with Novo Nordisk to sell branded Ozempic directly through its platform (lower-margin but legitimate), acquired an Australian telehealth company, Eucalyptus, for $1.15 billion, and launched a testosterone-therapy product. An SEC investigation into its GLP-1 marketing practices was disclosed in early 2026. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $2.35 billion; the company guided to $2.7–$2.9 billion for 2026.

module.name: Sumco Corporation
module.blurb: Sumco Corporation is a Japanese semiconductor materials company that manufactures and sells silicon wafers used in chip fabrication. Its product portfolio spans polished, annealed, epitaxial, junction-isolated, silicon-on-insulator, and reclaimed polished wafers, as well as monocrystalline ingots. The company operates globally across Japan, the United States, China, Taiwan, South Korea, and Europe. Formerly known as Sumitomo Mitsubishi Silicon Corp., it rebranded as Sumco in August 2005 and is headquartered in Minato, Tokyo.
module.recent: Sumco reported earnings on May 12, 2026, with trailing twelve-month net income remaining negative at -¥23.27B and EPS of -¥66.53, reflecting continued softness in the silicon wafer market. Morningstar noted that forward guidance remains weak but raised its fair value estimate to ¥1,440, signaling an upbeat longer-term outlook. The stock has surged roughly 241% over the past year, trading around ¥3,427 on May 14, 2026, with a 52-week range of ¥937–¥3,859.

module.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
module.blurb: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company is best known for its Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K, and Red Dead Redemption franchises. It operates through labels Rockstar Games and 2K, holding a dominant position in the premium console and PC gaming market.
module.recent: In the past month, Take-Two's stock rose about 12.66% as anticipation builds for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI launch. CEO Strauss Zelnick described the launch as both exciting and terrifying, citing higher development costs and intense investor expectations. A recent SEC filing also revealed Vanguard holds just over 7% of the company's stock.

module.name: TE Connectivity plc
module.blurb: TE Connectivity is one of the world's largest manufacturers of electrical connectors, sensors, and related components, serving transportation, industrial, energy, and data-communications markets. Often invisible to the end consumer, its products appear wherever electricity or data must cross a physical boundary reliably — from the high-voltage harness inside an electric vehicle to the subsea cable splice deep on the ocean floor.
module.recent: In February 2025 TE announced the acquisition of Richards Manufacturing, a maker of overhead and underground electrical distribution hardware, for approximately $2.3 billion — signalling an expansion into grid infrastructure beyond its traditional connector product lines. The company has also been investing in 800V and 1000V EV connector architectures, where content-per-vehicle is estimated to run roughly 30% above internal-combustion equivalents. A presence at DISTRIBUTECH 2026 underscores its grid-modernisation push.

module.name: The Coca-Cola Company
module.blurb: The Coca-Cola Company manufactures and sells nonalcoholic beverages worldwide, including sparkling soft drinks, water, sports drinks, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based beverages. It is one of the largest beverage companies globally, with a market capitalization of approximately $340 billion. The company's brand portfolio includes Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, and other well-known labels.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, KO stock closed at $79.23, up 0.96% on the day, with a 52-week range of $65.35–$82.00. The company reported strong earnings on April 28, 2026, with net income up 27% year-over-year to $13.70 billion and EPS of $3.18. Analysts maintain a Strong Buy consensus with a price target of $85.06.

module.name: Trilogy Metals Inc.
module.blurb: Trilogy Metals is a Canadian-headquartered base-metals explorer developing the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects (UKMP) in the remote Brooks Range of northwestern Alaska. Its flagship assets — the Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver deposit and the Bornite copper-cobalt deposit — sit within the Ambler Mining District, one of the world's largest undeveloped polymetallic regions. The company holds a 50% interest in Ambler Metals LLC (joint-ventured with South32), which controls 100% of UKMP. In September 2025 the U.S. Department of Defense acquired a 10% equity stake for approximately $35.6 million, citing the copper and cobalt content as strategic to defense supply chains.
module.recent: The DoD investment in October 2025 sent TMQ shares from roughly $2.17 to a 52-week high of $15.21 CAD. The stock has since pulled back sharply amid permitting uncertainty — the Ambler Access Road, a 211-mile industrial road required for any commercial mine, remains contentious and faces ongoing legal and regulatory challenges from Alaska Native communities. Despite the government's endorsement, no construction timeline has been set, and the company is pre-revenue.

module.name: Trio-Tech International
module.blurb: Trio-Tech International provides burn-in and reliability testing equipment and services for the back-end semiconductor manufacturing process. Burn-in testing stresses chips under elevated voltage and temperature to flush out early failures before they reach end users — a quality step used for memory, logic, and increasingly AI GPU silicon. The company also operates test service centres in Southeast Asia. It is an indirect beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout through the semiconductor testing supply chain rather than a photonics company per se.
module.recent: In March 2026, Trio-Tech secured a $5.3M order for burn-in boards for a next-generation AI GPU platform, signalling direct involvement in the GPU production supply chain. The stock gained approximately 421% over the trailing twelve months as of early May 2026, trading near $13.36. The gain reflects both the AI-hardware testing demand surge and the company's small-cap status, which magnifies price moves on modest volume increases.

module.name: Uber Technologies, Inc.
module.blurb: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications for ridesharing, food delivery, freight, and other mobility services across the US, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. Uber is a dominant player in the global ride-hailing and food delivery markets, with a market cap of approximately $161 billion as of May 2026.
module.recent: On May 6, 2026, Uber reported earnings that beat bookings estimates and announced Uber One reached 50 million members, sending the stock up 8.53% to $79.17. The stock has a 52-week range of $68.46 to $101.99 and a consensus analyst price target of $107.18.

module.name: Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF
module.blurb: NANC is an exchange-traded fund launched in February 2023 by Unusual Whales (a financial-data firm known for tracking options flow and congressional trading activity) in partnership with Subversive Capital. The fund replicates the disclosed stock trades of Democratic members of Congress and their spouses, weighted and rebalanced according to publicly filed Periodic Transaction Reports. Its ticker is an explicit reference to Nancy Pelosi, whose trading disclosures have attracted outsized public attention. A companion fund, GOP, tracks Republican members' trades.
module.recent: As of early 2026, NANC holds approximately $258 million in assets under management and has returned roughly 74% since its February 2023 inception, outpacing both the S&P 500 and its GOP counterpart over the same period. The fund's portfolio is heavily weighted toward mega-cap technology names — Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet feature prominently — reflecting the actual disclosed trades of Democratic members. A structural lag exists: the mandatory 30-to-45-day reporting window means the fund buys disclosed positions after the fact, preventing it from fully replicating the returns of the members it tracks. Expense ratio: 0.75%.

module.name: Vicor Corporation
module.blurb: Vicor Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets modular power components and power systems for converting electrical power in electrically powered devices. The company offers a range of brick-format DC-DC converters, complementary components for AC line rectification and filtering, and input/output voltage products. Vicor serves customers in the United States, Europe, Asia Pacific, and internationally, and is known for its high-performance power management solutions.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, Vicor's stock closed at $280.34, up 5.39% on the day, with a 52-week range of $39.64 to $293.95. The company reported strong financials with revenue of $426.70M (up 15.6% year-over-year) and net income of $136.68M (up 490.6%). Analysts have a Strong Buy rating with a price target of $217.50, though the stock trades above that level.

module.name: Vishay Precision Group, Inc.
module.blurb: Vishay Precision Group is a manufacturer of precision sensors, force/torque measurement systems, and weighing instruments serving industrial, aerospace, and defense markets. The company specializes in high-accuracy measurement components including foil resistors and load cells used in demanding environments. VPG has carved out a niche as a supplier of precision parts to advanced manufacturing sectors, increasingly including robotics and automation. Its products are critical in applications where measurement accuracy is non-negotiable.
module.recent: VPG shares surged approximately 30% following a strong earnings beat that exceeded analyst expectations. The company announced deals to supply components to robot makers, with investor attention drawn to its exposure to AI infrastructure, data centers, and industrial robotics themes. The earnings result and new customer wins marked a significant near-term catalyst for the stock.

module.name: The Walt Disney Company
module.blurb: Disney is a global media and entertainment conglomerate whose assets span theme parks, film studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm), the ABC broadcast network, ESPN, and the Disney+ and Hulu streaming platforms. The company has undergone significant restructuring under returning CEO Bob Iger, who returned in 2022 to stabilise the company after a turbulent period under his successor. Disney's streaming transition has been costly but Disney+ reached profitability in late 2024.
module.recent: Disney reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $93 billion. The experiences segment (theme parks and cruises) remains the primary profit engine. The company is pursuing ESPN's transition to a direct-to-consumer streaming service and has made moves to consolidate streaming assets. Paul Pelosi sold 10,000 shares of DIS per the January 2026 PTR disclosure.

module.name: Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: Zhongji Innolight Co., Ltd. researches, designs, develops, packages, tests, and sells optical communication transceiver modules and devices in China and internationally. The company operates in two segments, Optical Module Business and Others, and also engages in investment activities, project management, trading, technical services, and house rental. It is a leading player in the optical module industry, with a market capitalization of approximately 953.24 billion CNY as of May 2026.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, the stock has traded in a range of 835.00 to 919.99 CNY, with a 52-week range of 85.15 to 919.99 CNY. The company reported strong financials with revenue of 51.06 billion CNY (up 98.7% year-over-year) and net income of 14.95 billion CNY (up 160.2%). The stock has gained 957.46% over the past year, reflecting robust demand for optical modules driven by AI and data center growth.

module.name: 5N Plus Inc.
module.blurb: 5N Plus Inc. (TSX: VNP) is a Montreal-based producer of ultra-high-purity specialty semiconductors and performance materials, operating in two segments. Specialty Semiconductors manufactures compound semiconductor wafers, epitaxial substrates, and advanced materials — principally from tellurium, germanium, indium, gallium, bismuth, and selenium — for applications in space solar cells, defence infrared sensors, and compound semiconductor devices. Performance Materials supplies bismuth and other high-purity metals for pharmaceutical, industrial, and energy applications. The company's German subsidiary, AZUR SPACE, is one of the world's leading manufacturers of space-grade multi-junction solar cells for satellite programmes, with production capacity expanded roughly 30% in 2025 and a further 25% expansion planned for the second half of 2026. 5N Plus appeared as a named competitor in Coherent Corp.'s 2022 10-K filing when shares traded near C$0.92; by mid-2026 the stock had reached C$35–36, a gain of roughly 38x.
module.recent: Full-year 2025 results featured 35% revenue growth and 73% higher Adjusted EBITDA, following record 2024 results (revenue up 19% to $289M, EBITDA up 39% to $53M). In February 2026 the company announced another 25% expansion of AZUR SPACE solar-cell capacity. The 52-week range as of May 2026 is C$5.12–C$36.40, with the stock having outperformed the TSX Composite by roughly 342 percentage points over the prior twelve months. The analyst consensus is Buy, with a target near C$37.65.

module.name: Abbott Laboratories
module.blurb: Abbott Laboratories is a diversified global healthcare company headquartered in North Chicago, Illinois, operating across four segments: Medical Devices, Diagnostics, Established Pharmaceuticals, and Nutrition. Its Medical Devices segment is anchored by the FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitoring system, one of the world's best-selling diabetes management products, alongside cardiovascular and neuromodulation devices. Its Diagnostics division produces rapid and laboratory testing systems, while its Nutrition segment markets brands including Similac (infant formula) and Ensure (adult nutrition). Abbott is a member of the S&P 500 and a Dividend Aristocrat with decades of consecutive dividend increases.
module.recent: Abbott shares hit a new 52-week low of $84.08 on May 8, 2026, closing down 3.09% at $84.32 on heavy volume of over 10 million shares — the stock has shed roughly 40% from its 52-week high of $139.06 reached in June 2025. Abbott was cited among the stocks making the biggest midday moves on April 16, 2026, coinciding with the broader Q1 2026 earnings season. The prolonged selloff reflects sector-wide pressure on large-cap healthcare names amid shifting tariff and trade policy concerns.

module.name: Accelink Technologies Co., Ltd.
module.blurb: Accelink Technologies Co., Ltd. is a Chinese company specializing in the research, development, and manufacturing of optical communication devices and modules. The company provides key components for fiber-optic networks, including transceivers, amplifiers, and passive components, serving telecom and data center markets. It is a leading supplier in China's optical communication industry and competes globally with other optoelectronic firms.

module.name: Adeia Inc.
module.blurb: Adeia Inc. is a media and semiconductor intellectual property licensing platform company incorporated in 1990 and headquartered in the United States. The company owns and licenses large patent portfolios to multichannel video programming distributors — including cable, satellite, and telecom TV providers — as well as streaming services and semiconductor manufacturers globally. With approximately 150 employees, Adeia operates a capital-light, royalty-driven model, generating revenue by licensing its IP across North America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and other international markets. The company was spun out of Xperi Inc. in 2022 and trades under the ticker ADEA on the Nasdaq.
module.recent: Adeia reported earnings on May 4, 2026, with trailing-twelve-month revenue of $460.5M (+21.1% year-over-year), net income of $122M (+61.6%), and EPS of $1.09 (+65.1%), reflecting strong licensing deal momentum. The stock closed at $31.72 on May 13, 2026 — near its 52-week high of $34.34 — with a market cap of approximately $3.5B, up sharply from a 52-week low of $11.61. module.name: Aduro Clean Technologies Inc.
module.blurb: Aduro Clean Technologies is a small-cap Canadian cleantech company (founded 2011, ~25 employees) that develops water-based chemical recycling processes under its proprietary Hydrochemolytic Technology (HCT) platform. Its core applications span three verticals: converting end-of-life plastics and tire rubber into specialty chemicals and fuels, upgrading heavy crude oils and bitumen, and transforming renewable oils into renewable fuels and specialty chemicals. The company operates at near-zero commercial revenue (trailing twelve-month revenue of ~$177K), positioning it as a pre-commercial technology licensor rather than a manufacturer. It was formerly known as Dimension Five Technologies.
module.recent: As of mid-May 2026, ADUR trades around $12.75 (down ~3.8% on May 13), well below its 52-week high of $17.66 but up sharply from the $5.88 low, with a market cap of roughly $430M reflecting speculative growth expectations rather than current earnings. The company reported Q results on April 15, 2026; with a net loss of $13.3M and minimal revenue, the stock remains unprofitable. Sell-side analysts carry a consensus Strong Buy with an average price target of $38.67, implying more than 200% upside, though the analyst base is small given the company's micro-cap profile.

module.name: Advantest Corporation
module.blurb: Advantest is a Japanese semiconductor test equipment company and the global leader in high-performance ATE (automated test equipment) for logic chips and memory. Its V93000 platform is the dominant tester for cutting-edge SoCs and AI accelerators; its T2000 family leads in DRAM and HBM test. As AI chips grow more complex and HBM stacks taller, the cost and time required for testing increases, directly benefiting Advantest's revenue per unit shipped. Advantest holds an estimated 50%+ share of the global ATE market for advanced logic and memory.
module.recent: Advantest has ridden the AI and HBM supercycle. Demand for testing H100/H200/Blackwell GPUs and HBM3E modules has driven record orders. Forward P/E of ~42.7x on 40% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 1.07 — essentially fair value for a monopoly-adjacent business in a structurally growing segment. Revenue is denominated largely in USD (test tool invoicing) but reported in JPY, creating currency translation effects.

module.name: Aixtron SE
module.blurb: Aixtron SE is the dominant supplier of metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) reactors — the industrial ovens that grow compound semiconductor films atom-by-atom onto wafers. With a 70–90% market share across most of its product portfolio, Aixtron equipment is found in the fabs of virtually every laser diode manufacturer. The company is based in Herzogenrath, Germany, and its technology is material-agnostic across arsenides, phosphides, nitrides, and carbides, spanning markets from telecoms lasers to power electronics.
module.recent: Aixtron's Q1 2026 revenue fell 47% year-over-year to €59 million due to seasonal delivery timing, but order intake surged 30% to €171 million with optoelectronics comprising nearly 70% of new orders. The company subsequently raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to €560 million (±€30 million) with an EBIT margin of 17–20%, up from prior guidance of €520 million. Its G10-AsP platform, designed for arsenide/phosphide lasers used in AI data-centre transceivers, was the primary volume driver.

module.name: Albemarle Corporation
module.blurb: Albemarle is one of the world's largest producers of lithium compounds, supplying battery-grade lithium hydroxide and carbonate to electric-vehicle and energy-storage markets. It also produces bromine and specialty chemicals. The company holds roughly 16% of global lithium market share and operates mines in Chile, Australia, and the United States. Its AI revenue exposure is indirect — lithium's primary demand driver remains EV batteries — but data-center battery backup systems and robotics batteries create a secondary link.
module.recent: Albemarle has faced significant margin pressure through 2025 and into 2026 as lithium spot prices remained well below 2022 peaks amid a supply glut and slower-than-expected EV adoption in key markets. The company has responded by curtailing production and deferring expansion projects. AI-related demand for lithium is real but remains a small fraction of total consumption.

module.name: Allegro MicroSystems, Inc.
module.blurb: Allegro MicroSystems designs, develops, manufactures, and markets sensor integrated circuits (ICs) and application-specific power ICs for motion control and energy-efficient systems. Its products include magnetic sensor ICs (position, speed, current) and power ICs (motor drivers, regulators, LED drivers, isolated gate drivers). The company primarily serves the automotive market, with additional exposure to industrial and consumer sectors. As of May 2026, it has a market capitalization of about $9.5 billion and employs roughly 4,060 people.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, ALGM stock surged over 200% from its 52-week low of $18.17 to a high of $51.40, driven by strong earnings and positive market sentiment. The company reported revenue of $839.73 million (TTM) and is scheduled to report next earnings on May 7, 2026. Analysts have a Strong Buy consensus with a price target of $44.27.

module.name: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Limited
module.blurb: A mid-cap supplier of discrete power devices, wide-bandgap (silicon-carbide and gallium-nitride) transistors, power-management integrated circuits and modules. AOSL is the kind of name Citrini groups under 'AI power plumbing': it does not appear on any AI-headline list, but its MOSFETs and gate drivers sit inside intermediate-bus converters and point-of-load stages on AI server boards, where current densities now exceed 400 amps per device. The company operates a hybrid manufacturing model, with internal fabs in Oregon and joint-venture capacity in China.
module.recent: In October 2025 AOSL announced a portfolio of silicon-carbide and gallium-nitride parts aimed at Nvidia's 800-volt-DC rack architecture, the next generation of power distribution for megawatt-scale AI factories. In March 2026 it introduced 25-volt and 80-volt MOSFETs in advanced packaging targeting AI-server intermediate-bus and point-of-load applications, with continuous current ratings up to 405 amps. The stock has been volatile but is among the smaller analog names that have not yet rerated as aggressively as TXN or MPWR, leaving more headline AI optionality.

module.name: American International Group, Inc.
module.blurb: American International Group (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization serving commercial, institutional, and individual customers through property-casualty and life insurance operations. The company's General Insurance segment offers a wide range of property and casualty insurance products, while its Life & Retirement segment provides life insurance, retirement services, and investment products. AIG is one of the largest insurers in the world, with a significant market presence in the United States and internationally.
module.recent: In the past month, AIG's stock has traded within a 52-week range of $71.25 to $87.46, with recent price around $76.43. Notable news includes discussions on how the AI data center boom is 'stress testing' insurers and private capital inflows, as well as broader industry topics like car insurance pricing and travel insurance. The stock has experienced some volatility amid these industry developments.

module.blurb: Amkor Technology is the largest Western-headquartered OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) provider, packaging finished silicon dies into the chips that power AI accelerators, smartphones, and automotive systems. The company is investing heavily in advanced packaging technologies — 2.5D, 3D stacking, and flip-chip — and is building a major domestic facility in Peoria, Arizona as part of the U.S. semiconductor reshoring effort.
module.recent: Q1 2026 revenue hit $1.685 billion (+27% YoY), with management guiding that its AI packaging portfolio would triple in the second half of 2026. Capex for 2026 is set at approximately $2.75 billion, reflecting the Peoria buildout.

module.name: Apacer Technology Inc
module.blurb: Apacer Technology Inc is a Taiwan-based company specializing in the design, manufacturing, and sales of memory modules, solid-state drives (SSDs), and other digital storage solutions. The company serves various markets including industrial, automotive, and consumer electronics. Apacer is known for its focus on high-quality, reliable memory products and has established a strong presence in the global memory module industry.

module.name: Argan, Inc.
module.blurb: Argan, Inc. (NYSE: AGX) is a US holding company whose primary subsidiary, Gemma Power Systems, provides engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) services for gas-fired power plants under fixed-price, lump-sum turnkey contracts — meaning Argan bears schedule and cost risk but captures margin if it delivers efficiently. The company operates in the US, Ireland, and the UK. Argan has become an indirect AI infrastructure play as surging data-centre power demand has sharply increased the pipeline for grid-scale gas generation, which Argan's clients commission to serve industrial and hyperscaler load.
module.recent: Argan reported FY2025 revenue of $874.2 million (up 53% year-over-year) and net income of $85.5 million (up 164%). The project backlog reached $2.9 billion, anchored by the 1.2 GW Sandow Lakes Power Station and a 700 MW gas plant, both linked to AI-adjacent industrial and data-centre power demand. One-year total shareholder return exceeded 80% as of early 2026. The stock moved from $473.85 to $615.42 during the period tracked in the @zephyr_z9 report.

module.name: Arista Networks, Inc.
module.blurb: Arista Networks is a leading provider of cloud networking solutions, including high-performance switches, routers, and software for data centers and campus environments. The company is known for its Extensible Operating System (EOS) and has a strong market position in the cloud networking space, competing with Cisco and others. Arista serves large-scale data center customers, including cloud titans and Fortune 500 enterprises.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Arista Networks stock experienced a sell-off, but analysts remain bullish, with a consensus price target suggesting a potential 36% gain. The company continues to benefit from strong demand for AI and cloud networking infrastructure, with recent earnings beating expectations.

module.name: ASML Holding N.V.
module.blurb: ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company and the sole manufacturer of EUV (extreme ultraviolet) lithography machines — the tools required to print the finest circuit features on leading-edge chips at 5nm and below. Every AI accelerator, high-bandwidth memory chip, and advanced logic die manufactured at TSMC, Samsung, or Intel passes through ASML optics. The company's monopoly position emerged after decades of public-private R&D investment in partnership with European governments and chipmakers.
module.recent: ASML reported €32.7 billion in total net sales for full-year 2025, up roughly 16% year-on-year, with net income of €9.6 billion and a gross margin of 52.8%. Year-end backlog stood at €38.8 billion. Q4 2025 saw record total net sales of €9.7 billion, including revenue recognized for the first High-NA EUV systems — the next-generation machines required for 2nm nodes and below. TSMC accounts for an estimated 40% of EUV tool deliveries. ASML guides to €34–39 billion for 2026 and €44–60 billion by 2030 as High-NA adoption widens. In December 2025 Huawei and Chinese startup SiCarrier confirmed a functional EUV light source using an alternative plasma architecture, but analysts place production-ready Chinese competition no earlier than 2028–2030.

module.name: ASMPT Limited
module.blurb: ASMPT Limited is a leading global supplier of semiconductor and electronics assembly equipment, providing solutions for the packaging and assembly of integrated circuits and electronic components. The company operates in the technology sector, specifically within the semiconductors industry, and has a market capitalization of approximately $73.8 billion. With a strong presence in Asia, ASMPT serves major semiconductor manufacturers and electronics assemblers worldwide.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, ASMPT's stock has shown positive momentum, trading around HK$176.9 as of early May 2026, up 1.9% on the day. module.name: Direxion Daily Uranium Industry Bull 2X ETF
module.blurb: The Direxion Daily Uranium Industry Bull 2X ETF (URAA) seeks daily investment results of 200% of the performance of the Solactive United States Uranium and Nuclear Energy ETF Select Index. Launched June 26, 2024 and managed by Rafferty Asset Management, URAA is the primary surviving 2x leveraged uranium vehicle after Defiance's URAX closed in April 2025. AUM is approximately $48 million as of April 2026. Like all leveraged ETFs, URAA resets its exposure daily, which creates volatility decay — a compounding drag that erodes returns for holders who maintain positions across volatile days even if the underlying index trends upward. The fund is designed for short-term tactical trading, not buy-and-hold investing. The predecessor URAX (Defiance Daily Target 2x Long Uranium ETF, tracking URA) launched May 2024 and closed April 16, 2025, its final share price near $7.94 versus a 52-week high of $21.09.
module.recent: URAA remains active as of May 2026, with AUM near $48 million. Uranium equities have recovered with spot prices above $100/lb, but volatility decay continues to make the fund a poor vehicle for investors seeking long-term uranium exposure.

Its flagship products are Gotham (for government and defence clients), Foundry (for commercial enterprises), and the Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), launched in 2023, which allows organisations to deploy large language models within their existing data infrastructure. The company is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, and is unusual among technology companies in that it derives a substantial share of revenue from classified US government contracts — a relatively insulated revenue stream that also limits disclosure. Palantir built a large retail-investor following due to its association with AI, US defence spending growth, and the outspoken, unconventional public persona of CEO Alex Karp.

module.name: Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF
module.blurb: The Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF (URNJ) tracks the Nasdaq Sprott Junior Uranium Miners Index and targets early-stage and development-phase uranium companies — the segment commonly called junior miners or explorers. It holds approximately 35 fairly evenly weighted positions, which provides modest diversification within a universe that is by definition high-risk. Expense ratio is 0.80%, the highest in the Sprott uranium ETF family. The fund pays a dividend yield of approximately 2.25%. Energy Fuels (UUUU) is the largest single holding at over 14% of the portfolio. Junior miners offer the highest potential operating leverage to spot prices — development-stage companies can reprice dramatically when uranium spot prices rise — but also the highest idiosyncratic risk: permitting failures, financing gaps, and the 10–15-year lead time from discovery to production mean that even well-resourced juniors regularly disappoint.

Its flagship HDBaseT technology delivers simultaneous 4K/8K video, audio, Ethernet, USB, and power over a single cable, serving enterprise AV, education, industrial, and digital signage markets. The company also has an automotive segment targeting in-vehicle connectivity for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving applications. With ~233 employees and trailing revenue of roughly $70.7 million, it competes in the broader semiconductor connectivity market against companies such as Parade Technologies and Analogix.
module.recent: Valens reported Q1 2026 earnings on May 13, 2026, with trailing twelve-month revenue up ~11.9% year-over-year to $70.66 million, though the company remains unprofitable with a net loss of $31.57 million. The stock surged 9.26% on earnings day to close at $2.95, continuing a recovery from its 52-week low of $1.10 hit on March 30, 2026. As of the May 14 pre-market, shares were trading around $3.01, and analysts carry a consensus Strong Buy rating with a $3.50 price target.

module.name: Vimeo.com, Inc.
module.blurb: Vimeo.com, Inc. provides video software solutions, including hosting, editing, live-streaming, and AI-powered tools for businesses and creative professionals. The company serves a range of customers from small businesses to large enterprises, with a focus on high-quality, ad-free video experiences. As of November 2025, Vimeo was acquired by Bending Spoons US and delisted from NASDAQ.
module.recent: On November 24, 2025, Vimeo was delisted from NASDAQ after being acquired by Bending Spoons US for $1.38 billion in cash, with shareholders receiving $7.85 per share. The acquisition closed in late November 2025, ending Vimeo's public trading history.

module.name: Vishay Intertechnology, Inc.
module.blurb: Vishay is one of the world's largest manufacturers of discrete semiconductors (MOSFETs, diodes, rectifiers) and passive electronic components (resistors, inductors, capacitors), making it a two-sided play on the AI server power-plumbing build-out. On the passive side, its vPolyTan polymer tantalum capacitors and IHLE inductors are design-in components for Nvidia Blackwell GB200 server power-supply units. On the semiconductor side, Vishay's PowerPAK MOSFETs, DrMOS integrated power stages, VRPower buck regulators, and SiC Schottky diodes populate the voltage-regulation and power-conversion circuitry of AI racks. The company is executing a multi-year capacity expansion centred on a new 12-inch wafer fab.
module.recent: Vishay reported Q4 2025 revenue of $800.9 million, up 1.3% sequentially, with full-year 2025 revenue of $3.07 billion. The Q4 book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.20 overall (1.27 for semiconductors, 1.13 for passives), and ending backlog reached 4.9 months — the strongest demand signal in several quarters. Management attributed growth partly to confirmed design wins in Nvidia GB200 AI servers across both MOSFET and vPolyTan capacitor lines. Q1 2026 guidance was $800–$830 million with 2026 CapEx of $400–$440 million, the majority directed to the 12-inch fab in what management called the peak of the five-year expansion. The CEO described the company as ready to accelerate on factory utilisation and margin recovery in 2026.

module.name: Vistra Corp.
module.blurb: Vistra is the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating approximately 44,000 megawatts of total capacity including 24,000 MW of natural-gas generation, 6,400 MW of nuclear, and substantial coal and battery storage assets. It is the second-largest nuclear operator in the U.S. behind Constellation Energy. Vistra operates primarily in restructured, deregulated power markets including ERCOT (Texas), PJM (Mid-Atlantic/Midwest), ISO-NE, MISO, and CAISO — markets where electricity prices clear at the margin and where data-center load growth has dramatically tightened supply/demand balances.
module.recent: Vistra issued 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8 to $7.6 billion — roughly $1 billion above its 2025 range — anchored by three 20-year power-purchase agreements with Meta covering 2.6 gigawatts of nuclear output that lock in contracted cash flows through the 2050s. The company acquired 5.5 GW of dispatchable gas assets via a $4.7 billion Cogentrix deal, strengthening its position in PJM and ISO-NE where data-center load growth is most acute. Gas turbine equipment lead times stretching into the early 2030s make Vistra's existing gas fleet increasingly difficult to replicate, supporting a structural re-rating argument. The stock sold off approximately 25% from its highs in early 2026, which some analysts characterized as a buying opportunity given the contracted earnings profile.

module.name: Volkswagen AG
module.blurb: Volkswagen AG is a German multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Wolfsburg, Germany. It designs, manufactures, and sells passenger and commercial vehicles, as well as related parts and services, under brands including Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Škoda, and SEAT. As one of the world's largest automakers, Volkswagen is a key player in the global automotive industry, with a significant market position in Europe, China, and the Americas.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Volkswagen's stock traded in a range of approximately €85 to €110, with a 52-week high of €110.20 reached in December 2025. Recent news includes Citi's analysis suggesting a defense pivot could revive the struggling company, and Volkswagen's push into driver-assist EVs without Nvidia. The stock has been volatile amid broader European market movements and ongoing industry challenges.

module.name: Walmart Inc.
module.blurb: Walmart Inc. is a multinational retail corporation that operates a chain of hypermarkets, discount department stores, and grocery stores. It is the world's largest company by revenue and the largest private employer. Walmart also runs Sam's Club retail warehouses and has expanded into e-commerce, advertising, and supply chain services.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Walmart stock has seen mixed performance amid shareholder proposals to reduce the Walton family's voting power. The company announced a $350 million investment in a new milk processing facility in Texas and formed a 'Human Intelligence Team' to boost beauty sales. Analysts remain focused on Walmart's ad growth and competitive positioning against Costco and Amazon.

module.name: Warner Music Group Corp.
module.blurb: Warner Music Group Corp. is a global music entertainment company operating in recorded music and music publishing. It is one of the three major record labels, alongside Universal Music Group and Sony Music Entertainment. The company owns a vast catalog of recordings and songs, and works with artists across all genres. WMG generates revenue through streaming, physical sales, licensing, and artist services.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Warner Music Group announced a strategic investment, though details are limited. The stock has been trading near its 52-week range, with analysts providing mixed ratings. No major earnings or price-moving catalysts have been reported in the immediate period.

module.name: Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
module.blurb: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is an omni-channel specialty retailer of home products, including cookware, home furnishings, and decor, operating brands such as Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, West Elm, and Rejuvenation. Founded in 1956, the company has a strong direct-to-consumer and e-commerce presence, with a market cap of approximately $22 billion. It competes in the specialty retail sector, focusing on premium home goods and furniture.
module.recent: As of May 6, 2026, WSM closed at $186.47, up 3.44% on the day, with a 52-week range of $147.39–$222.00. The stock has gained 25.2% year-to-date, supported by strong earnings and analyst optimism. The next earnings report is scheduled for May 22, 2026, with a consensus price target of $209.71.

module.name: Winbond Electronics Corp
module.blurb: Winbond Electronics Corp is a Taiwanese semiconductor company specializing in memory IC products, including DRAM, NOR Flash, and SLC NAND Flash. It is one of the leading memory manufacturers in Taiwan, with a focus on specialty DRAM and code storage flash memory. The company serves various markets such as automotive, industrial, and consumer electronics.

The stock has been on a three-day winning streak with a cumulative gain of 20.82%. News highlights include potential benefits from a Samsung strike, which could boost DRAM prices and benefit Winbond and Nanya Technology.

module.name: X-Energy, Inc.
module.blurb: X-Energy, Inc. is a nuclear reactor technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Rockville, Maryland. Its flagship product is the Xe-100, a small modular reactor (SMR) designed to generate 80 megawatts of electric power or 200 megawatts of thermal output. The company also manufactures TRISO-X fuel, a high-assay low-enriched uranium pebble fuel designed for advanced reactors. With 889 employees and a market capitalization of approximately $12.2 billion, X-Energy is one of the leading pure-play SMR developers in the United States.
module.recent: X-Energy completed its IPO on April 24, 2026, making it one of the most closely watched nuclear energy listings of the year. The stock has traded in a range of roughly $29.45–$37.10 since its debut, closing at $30.99 on May 13, 2026 — a decline of 2.36% on the day, with pre-market weakness continuing into May 14. The company's next earnings report is scheduled for May 30, 2026; trailing twelve-month revenue stands at $94.26 million (+12.2% year-over-year) against a net loss of $389.78 million.

module.name: Xiaomi Corporation
module.blurb: Xiaomi Corporation is a Chinese multinational electronics company that designs, develops, and sells smartphones, IoT devices, and lifestyle products. It is one of the world's largest smartphone manufacturers and has a strong ecosystem of connected devices. The company also provides internet services and has expanded into electric vehicles.
module.recent: In the past 30 days, Xiaomi's stock has shown moderate gains amid positive market sentiment. The company announced strong quarterly earnings, driven by smartphone sales and IoT growth. Analysts have noted Xiaomi's successful expansion into the EV market as a key catalyst.

module.name: XPeng Inc.
module.blurb: XPeng Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and markets smart electric vehicles (EVs) in China. Its product lineup includes sedans (P7, P7i, Next P7), SUVs (G9, G6, G7), an MPV (X9), and the MONA M03 hatchback. The company competes in the rapidly growing Chinese EV market, focusing on advanced technology and autonomous driving features.

module.name: Xperi Inc.
module.blurb: Xperi Inc. is a media and entertainment technology company that develops and licenses software powering the consumer viewing experience. Its flagship offerings include Pay-TV user experience solutions, the TiVo electronic program guide, integrated DVR/VOD navigation, and universal search and content-discovery tools that work across linear and streaming sources. Serving pay-TV operators and device manufacturers worldwide, Xperi licenses its platform to embed its software in televisions, set-top boxes, and connected-device ecosystems. With roughly 1,460 employees and trailing-twelve-month revenue near $448 million, the company occupies a niche middleware position between content providers and the living-room screen.

module.name: Zeta Global Holdings Corp.

Founded in 2007 by John Sculley (former Apple CEO) and David Steinberg, it aggregates consumer data from hundreds of sources into a proprietary database of roughly 235 million individuals in the US, which it uses to power targeted advertising and personalization at scale.

concepts.definition: A software development approach, popularised by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy, in which a programmer describes the desired behaviour in natural language and relies on a large language model to generate most or all of the actual code. The developer's role shifts from writing logic to reviewing, directing, and accepting AI output. It has lowered the barrier to shipping functional tools, though critics note it can produce brittle or insecure code if the output is not carefully scrutinised.

A three-dimensional DRAM architecture in which multiple memory dies are stacked vertically and connected by microscopic through-silicon vias, then placed directly alongside a GPU or AI accelerator in the same chip package. HBM delivers data to processors far faster than conventional DRAM but consumes two to three times the wafer manufacturing capacity per gigabyte, creating a supply drain on the broader DRAM market whenever AI chip production scales up.

A real-time neural rendering technique introduced at SIGGRAPH 2023 that represents a 3D scene as a set of anisotropic (ellipsoid-shaped) translucent blobs initialized from a sparse point cloud. Each blob stores its position, shape, opacity, and color, and the full scene is rendered by projecting and blending these blobs onto the image plane. It achieves photorealistic quality at interactive frame rates, making it the de facto starting point for neural scene reconstruction research.

An advanced photonic integration approach that places optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors — inside the same chip package as a high-speed network switch or AI accelerator, rather than in a separate pluggable module. Reducing the electrical connection distance from centimeters to millimeters cuts power consumption by up to 40% and enables much higher bandwidth density, which is critical as AI clusters scale to hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

The modern browser graphics and compute API that succeeds WebGL, exposing lower-level GPU features including compute shaders — which allow general-purpose GPU workloads beyond rendering. WebGPU enables techniques like cloud raymarching to run as standalone compute passes, with significant performance potential over the equivalent WebGL approach.

A JavaScript API that enables hardware-accelerated 3D graphics in web browsers without plugins, based on the OpenGL ES specification. Introduced around 2011, it made browser-based game engines technically feasible for the first time. WebGL 2.0, released in 2017, added compute-adjacent features but remains limited compared to modern GPU APIs.

The market's forward-looking estimate of how much a stock's price will fluctuate, expressed as an annualised percentage and derived from the prices of traded options. Higher implied volatility means options — both puts and calls — are more expensive. For a zero-cost collar, very high implied volatility helps because even deeply out-of-the-money calls become worth real premium, making it easier to fund the protective put.

The finite token budget within which a language model must hold everything relevant to a task: system instructions, conversation history, code, tool outputs, and intermediate reasoning. Once this budget fills, the model can no longer attend equally to all of it, and early constraints tend to get ‘forgotten.’ It is the fundamental scarcity that shapes how AI coding agents must be structured.

An open standard, introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 and subsequently adopted by OpenAI and others, that defines how AI agents connect to external tools and data sources. An MCP server exposes a set of typed tool definitions; an MCP-compatible agent such as Claude Code can discover and invoke those tools during a session, enabling it to take actions in external systems — file systems, APIs, browsers — without bespoke integration code.

Dynamic random-access memory: the dominant form of volatile computer memory, used in servers, PCs, and smartphones. DRAM cells must be continuously refreshed with electrical charge, making them fast but power-hungry relative to storage. The DRAM market — dominated by Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung — is historically one of the most cyclical in technology, prone to violent swings between oversupply and shortage because capital-intensive fabs take years to build while market conditions can shift in months.

A system that learns to simulate the dynamics, physics, and geometry of an environment from observed data rather than using hard-coded rules. A world model can predict how an environment will evolve over time and how actions within it produce consequences, enabling AI agents to plan and train inside learned simulations. The concept traces to cognitive science but became central to deep learning–era AI research as a proposed path toward general intelligence.

AI systems designed to act autonomously across multi-step tasks — browsing, coding, scheduling, making decisions — rather than simply answering single queries. Because agentic workloads run longer chains of inference and require more compute per session than simple chatbot interactions, they are expected to drive sustained demand for both specialised AI accelerators and general-purpose processors.

A technique for representing and rendering 3-D scenes as a cloud of tiny translucent ellipsoids called 3-D Gaussians, each defined by its position, shape, opacity, and colour. During training the ellipsoids are projected onto a 2-D image plane and compared to real photographs; their parameters are then adjusted to minimise the pixel difference. Unlike neural radiance fields (NeRFs), which trace rays through an implicit field, Gaussian splatting uses explicit geometric primitives and rasterisation, enabling real-time rendering at high resolution. The approach was introduced by Kerbl et al. at SIGGRAPH 2023.

The small group of companies — Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Meta, Oracle, and a few others — that operate cloud and AI infrastructure at planetary scale. Their data centres can consume hundreds of megawatts each and require continuous, high-quality power. The term is widely used in energy, semiconductor, and infrastructure markets to denote this buyer class as a distinct and outsized customer segment.

A compound semiconductor — a crystalline material made from indium and phosphorus — that is particularly efficient at converting electrical signals into light at the wavelengths used in fiber-optic communications. InP-based lasers are the light source inside high-speed optical transceivers. Manufacturing InP wafers requires specialized, expensive fabrication facilities distinct from silicon chip fabs, creating a meaningful barrier to entry and concentrating supply among a small number of producers including Lumentum.

An architecture in which a large model is divided into many smaller specialist sub-networks ('experts'). For any given input, only a small subset of experts is activated, keeping compute requirements low while maintaining high overall capacity. A 26B-parameter MoE with 3.8B active parameters uses roughly the compute of a 3.8B dense model per inference step.

A family of machine-learning methods that represent 3D scenes as neural networks. Given a viewpoint, a NeRF queries the network to determine what color each pixel should be — a per-pixel computation that produces high-quality results but is too slow for real-time rendering without significant hardware. 3D Gaussian Splatting emerged partly as a faster alternative that achieves comparable visual quality.

A technology for transmitting data as pulses of light on silicon chips rather than as electrical signals over copper wires. Inside AI data centers, silicon photonics enables the high-bandwidth, low-latency links between GPU clusters that copper interconnects cannot support at scale. It depends on specialized engineered wafer substrates — such as Soitec's Photonics-SOI — as its material platform.

The VIX (“Volatility Index”) is a real-time index published by Cboe Global Markets measuring the market’s expectation of S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days, derived from a blend of near-term options prices. Widely called the “fear gauge,” it typically falls as stocks rise in a healthy bull market. When the VIX rises alongside equities—as occurred in May 2026—it suggests traders are simultaneously speculating on further upside and paying for protection against a reversal, an anomaly that often precedes volatility events.

Capital expenditure: spending on physical assets such as land, buildings, servers, and networking equipment, as opposed to recurring operating expenditure. Hyperscaler capex announcements are widely used as a proxy for future AI infrastructure capacity, but the translation from dollars committed to compute delivered depends on supply-chain lead times that can extend years beyond the announcement date.

A class of generative AI model that learns to create images or video by training on the process of adding random noise to data, then reversing it. At inference time, the model starts from pure noise and iteratively refines it into a coherent output. Most leading image and video generators — Stable Diffusion, Sora, Veo — are built on this principle.

A type of non-volatile semiconductor memory that retains data without power, used in solid-state drives, smartphones, and data-centre storage arrays. NAND prices are notoriously cyclical because fabrication capacity takes years to build while demand can shift quickly. The current supercycle is driven by AI training and inference workloads that require vast amounts of fast, dense storage.

A financial platform where participants buy and sell contracts tied to the outcome of future events — elections, asset prices, sports results. The market price of a contract reflects the crowd's collective probability estimate. Platforms like Polymarket popularized crypto-native prediction markets, where smart contracts handle settlement automatically.

A hypothetical class of AI systems capable of performing any intellectual task a human can accomplish, without domain-specific training. In investment discourse, AGI infrastructure is shorthand for the compute and energy capacity presumed necessary to train and operate such systems — used in the @cryptorand Phase 4 thesis to describe a long-dated bet on sustained demand for large-scale AI compute beyond narrow-purpose models.

Anthropic's agentic coding CLI tool that reads codebases, edits files, runs shell commands, and executes multi-step workflows. It supports a “skills” architecture in which repeatable tasks are defined as markdown slash-command files that the agent reads and runs. career-ops is implemented entirely as a collection of these skills.

A valuation ratio comparing the current stock price to estimated earnings per share over the next twelve months. A low forward P/E can signal either genuine undervaluation or that analysts expect earnings to fall sharply — distinguishing between the two is the central challenge in cyclical-stock investing, where low multiples at peak earnings often precede the sharpest drawdowns.

A mode of AI video synthesis in which a static image is provided as input alongside a text prompt, and the model animates the scene forward in time. Distinct from pure text-to-video, this mode offers creators more precise control over subject appearance and starting composition.

A pluggable module that converts electrical data signals into pulses of light (for transmission over fiber-optic cable) and back again. In AI data centers, transceivers are the physical links connecting GPU clusters; as AI model sizes and training cluster sizes have grown, the required data rates have jumped from 400G to 800G (800 gigabits per second) and are moving toward 1.6T, making transceiver manufacturers critical suppliers in the AI infrastructure chain.

The compression of a trained model's weights from high-precision floats (16 or 32 bits) to lower precision (8 or 4 bits), reducing memory footprint and speeding up inference at a modest cost to accuracy. Post-training quantization applies after training; quantization-aware training bakes the compression into the training loop itself to minimize quality loss.

The cognitive error of drawing conclusions only from the entities that survived a selection process — winners, listed companies, successful funds — while ignoring the larger, invisible population that failed. In investing, it makes past returns look more achievable and predictable than they actually were.

A class of AI models that converts written descriptions into short video clips. The user writes a prompt specifying scene, motion, camera angle, and style; the model synthesizes video through diffusion or similar techniques. Quality is judged by how faithfully the output matches the prompt, how realistic the motion appears, and how consistent the visuals stay across the clip.

A JavaScript library created by Ricardo Cabello (mrdoob) in 2010 that wraps WebGL — the browser's low-level 3D graphics API — into an approachable, high-level API for rendering scenes, cameras, lights, materials, and animations. With over 112,000 GitHub stars and roughly six to eleven million npm downloads per month, it is the dominant framework for 3D content on the web.

Three.js's JavaScript-based shader composition system, introduced alongside the WebGPU renderer. Developers express shader logic as JavaScript function trees; the compiler emits WGSL for WebGPU and GLSL for WebGL from the same source. TSL makes it practical to maintain a single complex shader codebase that runs across both graphics APIs.

Zero Days to Expiration options are contracts that expire at the end of the trading session in which they are purchased. Because there is no time value left, they are priced almost entirely on the probability that the underlying stock will finish above (for calls) or below (for puts) the strike price by market close. A stock move that pushes through the strike on expiration day can produce extreme percentage returns because the initial premium is so cheap.

Reusable instruction sets — each a folder containing a SKILL.md file with natural-language instructions — that extend an AI coding agent's capabilities. Skills load lazily: the agent holds brief descriptions in context at all times but fetches full instructions only when a matching task arises. An open specification maintained across 54+ compatible agents and distributed through Vercel's skills.sh directory.

In finance, alpha is the portion of an investment return that exceeds what can be explained by general market movement or systematic risk factors. A strategy with positive alpha is, in theory, generating returns through skill or informational advantage rather than simply riding a rising market. The catch is that alpha is notoriously difficult to distinguish from luck over short horizons — which is why professional risk managers demand large trade samples and long observation windows before crediting any strategy with genuine alpha.

A financial metric that projects a company's current subscription or contract revenue over a full year. In AI companies, it is often calculated from a single quarter's revenue multiplied by four. It is a forecast and a signal, not an audited annual total — comparisons across companies are tricky because accounting methodologies differ.

The hypothetical development of machine intelligence capable of performing any intellectual task a human can across arbitrary domains, as opposed to narrow AI systems optimized for specific tasks. Distinct from current large language models, which excel at language generation but lack the open-ended, embodied adaptation AGI implies.

An open-source, node-based interface for running AI diffusion models locally. Users connect processing nodes — model loaders, samplers, ControlNet applicators — into a directed graph that makes every step of the generation process explicit and editable. Released in January 2023 by an anonymous developer known as comfyanonymous; now maintained by Comfy Org with more than 89,000 GitHub stars.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation. A proxy for operating cash generation that strips out non-cash charges and financing costs. For AI companies that lease rather than own compute, most GPU costs flow through operating expenses rather than depreciation, making EBITDA a less clean measure of cash generation than it would be for a capital-light SaaS business.

The loose community of retail and professional investors, analysts, and commentators who discuss stocks, macroeconomics, and trading on X (formerly Twitter). FinTwit ranges from rigorous independent research to promotional noise, and the NFA disclaimer is one of its most ubiquitous conventions — functioning simultaneously as a legal hedge and a cultural signal of insider membership.

A memory architecture that stacks multiple DRAM dies vertically and connects them via thousands of microscopic conductors called Through-Silicon Vias, then places the stack directly adjacent to a processor on a silicon interposer. The result is a bus interface up to 2,048 bits wide — versus 64 bits for conventional DDR5 — delivering terabytes per second of memory bandwidth at lower power than traditional memory. HBM is essential for AI accelerators because large language models require moving billions of parameters through memory faster than conventional chips allow.

Scripts, webhooks, or prompt-based triggers that Claude Code fires at specific points in its execution cycle — before a tool runs, after a task completes, when a session ends. With 31 configurable lifecycle events and five hook types, they let developers intercept and modify the tool’s behavior programmatically, functioning more like a build system’s lifecycle hooks than simple macros.

A technique, borrowed from transformer-based language models, that stores intermediate attention computations so they do not need to be recalculated when generating successive tokens or frames. In video generation, reusing cached key-value pairs from earlier frames allows the model to produce new frames far more quickly than recomputing from scratch each time.

A neural network trained on large text corpora to predict and generate language. Models such as GPT, Claude, and Mistral’s own text models power chatbots, code assistants, and document summarizers. Referenced here as a comparator: the trajectory of LLM commoditization — from expensive proprietary API to cheap open-weight local inference — is now repeating in voice synthesis.

The statistical tendency of an asset’s price or ratio to drift back toward its long-run historical average after a significant departure. In markets it underpins contrarian strategies: a sector that has underperformed sharply may be poised to revert as the forces driving the divergence fade. It cuts directly against momentum strategies, which assume the trend continues.

An open standard released by Anthropic in November 2024 that lets AI coding environments call external tools and data sources as if they were native functions. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 as its transport and follows a three-part architecture: host (the AI environment), client (an integration layer), and server (the external tool provider). Think of it as a USB standard for AI agent tool integrations.

A design pattern in AI systems in which multiple specialised AI models or agents coordinate to complete a task — one might search the web, another write code, a third check outputs. It allows complex tasks to be decomposed and parallelised, and is increasingly a benchmark capability that AI labs cite when demonstrating model maturity.

The default package registry for the Node.js JavaScript ecosystem, used by developers to install software dependencies. In documented attacks on Polymarket users, malicious actors published packages to npm that appeared to be legitimate bot tools; when installed, they silently exfiltrated private cryptocurrency wallet keys to attacker-controlled servers.

An attack on AI systems in which malicious instructions are embedded in content the model reads — a document, a webpage, a plugin's metadata — causing it to behave as if those instructions came from a trusted user. Researchers found this in OpenClaw's ClawHub skill marketplace, where some extensions quietly redirected the model's actions to exfiltrate user data.

Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. A training method in which human raters rank model outputs by preference; those rankings train a reward model, which then guides further fine-tuning via reinforcement learning. It is the principal technique used to make generative models more helpful and less harmful after initial pre-training on raw text.

A momentum oscillator that measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes, producing a value between 0 and 100. Readings above 70 are conventionally overbought; below 30 is oversold. Technicians use it to gauge whether a move is extended relative to its own recent history. An RSI reversal from below 30 to above 70 in eleven sessions is, by historical comparison, extremely rapid.

The erosion of a trading signal's excess return over time, particularly after publication or widespread adoption. McLean and Pontiff (2016) found that documented stock-return predictors lose roughly 58% of their in-sample returns once they appear in academic papers, as sophisticated investors trade on the published rule and arbitrage the edge away. Alpha decay is faster for strategies that are easy to implement, highly liquid, and require little proprietary data.

In its classical financial meaning, arbitrage is the simultaneous purchase and sale of an asset in two markets to profit from a price difference. ArbitrageDiscover uses the term more broadly: any durable mismatch between the price a market charges for a service and the true marginal cost of delivering it — a gap that a well-positioned entrant can exploit.

A unit equal to one one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%), universally used in fixed income to describe yield changes. Eight basis points is 0.08%; 108 basis points is 1.08%. The convention exists because percentage-point changes in bond yields—often fractions of a percent—would be cumbersome to express in plain percentage terms.

In options markets, skew measures the difference in implied volatility between out-of-the-money calls and out-of-the-money puts at comparable distances from the current price.
