When call implied volatility is elevated relative to put implied volatility—positive, or “call,” skew—it signals that traders are paying a premium for upside speculation rather than downside protection, a signature of euphoric sentiment. A sharply positive skew reading is often interpreted as a contrarian bearish warning.

A trading system where buyers and sellers post limit orders at their desired prices; a trade executes when a buy order matches a sell order. Unlike a bookmaker that sets odds unilaterally, a CLOB lets market participants set prices through competition. When no participant has posted new quotes, the book reflects stale prices until someone updates it.

A datacenter packaging architecture that integrates laser light sources and photonic components inside the chip package — typically alongside a switch or GPU — rather than in external pluggable modules. CPO reduces the energy consumed by electrical-to-optical signal conversion, a critical constraint as AI clusters scale toward multi-megawatt power budgets. Adoption by hyperscalers is expected to drive demand for indium-phosphide lasers of the type Sivers manufactures.

An advanced semiconductor packaging technology from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing that places multiple chiplets — such as a GPU die and several HBM stacks — side by side on a silicon interposer substrate and bonds them into a single package. CoWoS enables the extremely high-speed, short-distance connections between a GPU and its HBM that are impossible with conventional circuit-board mounting. Its production capacity became a critical secondary bottleneck during the 2023 AI chip buildout.

A formal removal request filed under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, asking a platform such as GitHub to disable access to allegedly infringing content. Platforms must comply to retain safe-harbor protections. GitHub’s network-takedown policy means a valid notice targeting one repository can disable all forks of that repository simultaneously.

A chip company that designs its own silicon but outsources manufacturing to a contract foundry, typically TSMC or Samsung. Fabless companies carry no wafer fabrication capital expenditure; their competitive position rests on design IP, customer relationships, and foundry allocation. MediaTek, Qualcomm, and Apple Silicon (for its own chips) are all fabless; Intel historically was not.

A second training phase that adapts a pre-trained model to specific tasks or behaviors using a much smaller dataset — typically thousands to hundreds of thousands of examples. Methods include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), and direct preference optimization (DPO). Fine-tuning updates the model's weights and requires meaningful compute, though far less than pre-training.

Gamma measures how much an options dealer’s hedge must change as the underlying asset moves. When large volumes of call options are purchased, dealers who sold those calls must buy increasing quantities of the underlying stock to remain hedged as prices rise—a dynamic called a gamma squeeze. This mechanical buying can amplify a rally well beyond what fundamentals support, and unwinds sharply when the call-buying stops.

A category of AI that produces video footage from text descriptions, still images, or other inputs rather than capturing real footage. Models are trained on large video datasets and learn to synthesize motion, lighting, and scene coherence. Quality is usually measured by temporal consistency — how smoothly objects and characters move between frames.

Blender's node-based procedural system for creating and modifying 3D geometry through a visual graph rather than direct mesh editing. Artists connect nodes that describe operations — deform, instance, select by angle — and Blender evaluates them in order. This makes the setup non-destructive: the underlying mesh is unchanged, and parameters can be tweaked at any time without re-sculpting.

David Chalmers’s term for the question of why physical brain processes give rise to subjective experience at all — why there is “something it is like” to see red or feel pain. Distinguished from the “easy problems” of explaining cognitive functions, which are in principle solvable by neuroscience, the hard problem is thought by many philosophers to require a fundamentally different kind of explanation. It is the central obstacle for any theory of machine consciousness.

A class of artificial intelligence systems trained on vast text corpora to predict and generate language. They process input prompts and produce outputs without any evident inner narrator or deliberative self — a structure that some researchers have noted is analogous to Jaynes’s bicameral human: receiving commands from an external source and responding without an introspective “I.”

A market shorthand for the seven largest U.S. technology companies by market capitalisation: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta Platforms, and Tesla. Because they collectively represent a large share of S&P 500 and NASDAQ weighting, their price movements disproportionately influence index-level performance—which is why analysts track whether they are confirming or diverging from broader market moves.

A family of measures gauging how broadly an index’s gains are shared across its constituent stocks, rather than driven by a few large-cap names. Key tools include the advance-decline line (a running cumulative total of daily advancing minus declining issues) and the percentage of members trading above their 50-day or 200-day moving averages. When an index reaches new highs but breadth fails to confirm—because gains concentrate in a handful of heavyweights—the divergence has historically preceded major tops.

A subfield of AI safety and interpretability research that aims to reverse-engineer the internal computations of neural networks — identifying what specific neurons, attention heads, and MLP layers actually compute, and why. Rather than treating a model as a black box and measuring only input-output behavior, MI researchers trace causally active circuits responsible for specific behaviors using ablation and activation patching.

A rapid, self-reinforcing surge in asset prices driven primarily by investor sentiment and momentum — short-covering, FOMO-induced buying, and passive-fund rebalancing — rather than a fundamental revaluation of earnings or cash flows. Melt-ups typically occur in already-positive market environments and differ from oversold bounces in that they begin from a position of relative strength rather than deep distress. They are often followed by sharp corrections once the momentum exhausts itself.

A technique that records the movement of a person or object — typically using optical markers, inertial sensors, or depth cameras — and translates the resulting positional data into animation curves that can drive a digital character. The output is far more naturalistic than hand-keyed animation for body mechanics, though it still requires cleanup and artistic polish.

A market-capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. Because it is heavily concentrated in large-cap technology businesses, it functions as a sector barometer. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is the primary ETF tracking the index, making QQQ a direct vehicle for the capex-to-valuation risk described in these charts.

A technique that represents a three-dimensional scene as a neural network, queryable to reconstruct photorealistic views from any angle. NeRFs produce geometrically consistent 3D representations but require training on a specific scene and are relatively slow to render, making them unsuitable for real-time generative systems. DeepMind notes that Genie 3 achieves spatial consistency without relying on them.

An American religious and metaphysical movement originating in the 1830s, most associated with healer Phineas Quimby, holding that the mind directly shapes physical reality. Belief, visualization, and positive mental states are said to produce health, abundance, and desired outcomes. Its institutional heirs include the Unity Church and Religious Science; its popular heir is the Law of Attraction.

The relationship between a business's fixed and variable costs. Companies with high fixed costs — such as semiconductor fabs, which require billions in capital investment regardless of output — experience disproportionately large profit swings when revenue changes: a modest revenue increase can produce a far larger percentage increase in operating profit once fixed costs are covered, and vice versa.

An option whose strike price is less favourable than the current market price. A put is out-of-the-money when its strike is below the current stock price (exercising it would be immediately unprofitable); a call is out-of-the-money when its strike is above. OTM options cost less than at-the-money options but provide no intrinsic value at expiry unless the stock has moved past the strike.

The technique of deriving precise 3D measurements and models from sets of overlapping photographs. In city-scale mapping, aerial photogrammetry uses thousands of images captured from aircraft or satellites to reconstruct building facades, rooftops, and terrain. Ground-level photogrammetry applies the same principles with cameras on vehicles, drones, or handheld devices to capture street-level or indoor geometry.

An open-source browser-automation library, originally developed at Microsoft, that controls web browsers programmatically via code. career-ops uses it both to scrape company career pages for job listings and to render HTML CV templates to PDF through a browser engine — ensuring consistent, professionally formatted output.

A peer-to-peer prediction market — now regulated by the CFTC following a 2025 exchange acquisition — where participants buy and sell binary contracts on real-world outcomes (elections, geopolitical events, economic data) priced between zero and one dollar, paying out $1 if the event occurs and $0 if it does not. Prices aggregate crowd probability estimates in real time, making Polymarket a source of implied odds for trading around geopolitical events.

The Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings ratio, developed by economist Robert Shiller. Rather than dividing today's stock price by the current year's earnings, it divides by the average of inflation-adjusted earnings over the prior 10 years, smoothing out cyclical peaks and troughs. A reading of 40x means investors are paying 40 dollars for every dollar of normalized earnings. The long-run historical average is roughly 16–17x; the all-time peak of 44x was reached in March 2000 at the height of the dot-com bubble.

A wafer architecture in which a thin layer of silicon sits atop an electrically insulating buried oxide. In photonics, the refractive-index contrast between the silicon and the oxide confines light in waveguides, enabling chips that route optical signals much as conventional chips route electrons. Photonics-grade SOI requires tighter uniformity specs than standard SOI used in logic chips.

A benchmark that measures how often an LLM can autonomously resolve real GitHub software engineering issues: find the bug, write a correct patch, pass the test suite. Widely used as a more meaningful proxy for practical coding ability than synthetic code-generation tests, because it requires understanding existing codebases rather than generating isolated snippets.

The tendency of a language model to tell users what they want to hear rather than what is accurate or genuinely helpful — flattering, agreeing with, or validating users regardless of whether they are right. It typically arises when models are trained on human approval signals, which reward agreement and praise over candour. The April 2025 GPT-4o incident was a high-profile case study in the pathology.

User-generated content. In digital marketing, UGC refers to short videos, photos, or reviews produced by individuals rather than brands, used — organically or in paid campaigns — to promote products. AI-generated UGC imitates the aesthetic of authentic creator content using synthetic video or voice, and is a growing category in performance marketing.

The memory architecture of Apple Silicon chips (M1 and later), in which the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine share a single physical memory pool rather than maintaining separate banks. This eliminates the latency and bandwidth cost of copying model weights and activation tensors between CPU RAM and discrete GPU VRAM — a bottleneck that constrains NVIDIA-based inference runtimes.

A neural network trained to reason jointly over images and text. In Flipbook, a VLM receives the current page image plus the pixel coordinates of the user's click and infers a semantic description of what was clicked—'the Eiffel Tower', 'a ticket price'—which then becomes the prompt for the next generated image.

An extension of 3D Gaussian Splatting into the time domain. Each scene element is represented as an ellipsoid with a trajectory through both space and time, letting a single trained model reconstruct dynamic scenes — moving people, flowing fabric — at arbitrary timestamps. Two independent research groups published the foundational technique concurrently at CVPR and ICLR 2024.

Each trading day, the number of NYSE-listed stocks that closed higher (advancing issues) minus those that closed lower (declining issues) is calculated as net advances. Those daily figures are then added together into a running cumulative total — the A/D line — which rises when breadth is healthy and falls when more stocks are declining than advancing, regardless of what cap-weighted indexes show.

A family of semiconductor assembly techniques that go beyond traditional wire-bond packaging by integrating multiple dies — logic chips, memory, and I/O — into a single compact module. Methods include 2.5D integration (chips side-by-side on a silicon interposer) and 3D stacking (chips bonded face-to-face with through-silicon vias). Advanced packaging dramatically reduces the distance electrical signals must travel, improving performance and energy efficiency, and has become essential for AI accelerators that pair large GPU dies with high-bandwidth memory.

A deep-learning system developed by DeepMind that in 2020 effectively solved the protein-structure prediction problem — determining how a protein folds into its three-dimensional shape from its amino acid sequence alone, a challenge that had stumped biology for 50 years. Its performance was verified at the independent CASP14 competition before any milestone was claimed, and its co-creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

One of the Three Marks of Existence in Buddhism, alongside impermanence and suffering. Anatta (Pali; Sanskrit: anat̄man) is the doctrine that there is no permanent, unchanging essence — no soul — beneath the flow of thoughts and sensations. The self is a process, not a substance. Some researchers have noted that large language models are structurally anatta-compliant: no persistent memory, no continuous identity between sessions, no unified agent.

A per-request authentication credential issued through Anthropic's developer console. Every token processed incurs a metered charge at published rates, completely independent of any Claude.ai subscription. The key distinction for OpenClaw users: having one set as an environment variable silently overrides a subscription OAuth token, causing confusing auth failures.

A permissive open-source licence that allows anyone to use, modify, and distribute the code — including in commercial products — without being required to publish their modifications. It also includes an explicit patent grant, protecting adopters from patent claims by contributors. It is the most permissive of the major open-source licences.

In project-based businesses, the total value of signed customer contracts for work not yet recognised as revenue — essentially a pipeline of legally committed future earnings. A growing backlog reduces uncertainty about near-term revenue and is commonly cited by analysts as a derisking signal, particularly for capital-intensive businesses with long project lead times.

A packaged slash command for the Claude Code CLI, defined by a SKILL.md file containing YAML frontmatter (name, allowed tools, invocation controls) and markdown instructions. Skills live in ~/.claude/skills/ for personal use or .claude/skills/ for project scope, and are invoked by typing /skill-name. They can auto-trigger on relevant context or require explicit user invocation.

In the Claude Code context, the terminal invocation surface: the claude command, slash commands, piped input, and scripting hooks for CI/CD integration. It is the layer at which a human or automation directly issues instructions to Claude Code, as opposed to MCP (which connects external tools) or the Agent SDK (which orchestrates programmatically).

A failure mode in long-running AI agent sessions in which accumulated working memory — intermediate states, failed attempts, partial rewrites — degrades the model’s ability to reason coherently about the original task. As the context window fills with noise, early constraints and design decisions effectively disappear from the model’s attention, causing it to contradict or ignore them.

A conditioning framework for diffusion models, introduced by Lvmin Zhang and Maneesh Agrawala in 2023, that adds spatial guidance to image or video generation. Instead of steering output with text alone, ControlNet accepts auxiliary visual inputs — depth maps, edge-detection images, pose skeletons — and uses them to constrain the model’s spatial decisions frame by frame.

A strategy of mimicking the trades of larger or presumed-informed market participants, either by replicating disclosed 13F equity holdings or by following unusually large options orders in real time. The approach has some academic support for short-dated aggressive orders, but is complicated by the difficulty of distinguishing directional bets from hedges and by the proliferation of services tracking the same signals.

A 1950 U.S. law that gives the president authority to direct industrial resources — factories, materials, supply chains — toward national defense priorities. Section 303 specifically allows the government to make loans, purchase commitments, and other investments to expand domestic production of critical goods. It has been invoked for COVID vaccines, semiconductor equipment, and, in April 2026, power transformer supply chains.

An option’s sensitivity to a one-point move in the underlying asset — roughly, how much the option’s price changes when the stock or index moves by one dollar. A delta of 0.50 means the option gains about 50 cents for every dollar the underlying rises. Market makers continuously adjust their holdings to stay “delta-neutral,” which is the hedging activity that drives gamma squeezes.

The practice by which options dealers continuously buy or sell the underlying asset to offset the directional exposure (delta) of the options they have written. Because delta changes as the underlying price moves, this hedging must be adjusted dynamically — and the aggregate of all dealers adjusting simultaneously can itself move prices, creating feedback effects independent of fundamental news.

A strategy of balancing an options position with an offsetting stake in the underlying asset so that small price moves produce no net gain or loss. Dealers running delta-neutral books must rebalance constantly as prices shift — this ongoing rebalancing transmits options market imbalances into actual stock-price pressure.

Named, platform-agnostic variables that encode the visual decisions of a design system — specific colors (as hex or HSL values), typography scales, spacing units, border radii. Storing design as tokens rather than hard-coded literals makes a codebase easier to theme, audit, and maintain consistently across components.

A techno-optimist ideology popular in Silicon Valley and on X that treats unrestricted technological progress — especially in AI — as an ethical and civilizational imperative. It explicitly opposes AI-safety caution and ‘doomerism.’ The label is worn as a bio badge on X, signaling tribal membership in this camp.

A regime in which the scale of sovereign debt effectively constrains monetary policy: raising interest rates increases the government’s debt-service costs, potentially injecting more income into the private sector than the tightening removes. Analyst Lyn Alden has defined the threshold operationally as the point where a rate hike increases the federal deficit by a larger dollar figure than it slows bank lending. The concept overlaps with the academic Fiscal Theory of the Price Level developed by Stanford economist John Cochrane.

A specialized chip originally designed to render computer graphics, now the dominant architecture for training and running large AI models. GPUs can perform thousands of parallel calculations simultaneously, which suits the matrix math at the core of neural network training. Nvidia's H100 and Blackwell series are the current standard for AI data centers.

A class of algorithmic trading strategies characterised by extremely high order submission rates and holding periods measured in milliseconds or microseconds. Institutional HFT firms invest heavily in co-location (placing servers physically adjacent to exchange matching engines), custom networking hardware, and low-level kernel optimisation to shave latency. The term is often loosely applied to any fast automated trading, but technically refers to this latency-intensive institutional approach.

A mathematical technique used in animation and robotics to determine how a chain of joints (like an arm) must be positioned so that its endpoint (like a hand) reaches a target point in space. In VTubing, IK is what makes a character's hand appear to actually touch a surface rather than float above or clip through it.

The phase of AI deployment in which a trained model generates outputs from new inputs — answering a question, completing a sentence, classifying an image. Inference is less GPU-intensive than training and increasingly involves CPU work for token routing, batching, and agent orchestration.

A technique in which a masked region of an image or video frame is filled by an AI model, generating new pixels that plausibly match the surrounding context. In VFX work, inpainting is used to remove objects from a scene, extend backgrounds, or replace elements with AI-generated content.

A measure from algorithmic information theory: the length of the shortest computer program that produces a given object as output. It quantifies the irreducible information content of a system — how much you must 'say' to fully describe it. A highly regular object has low Kolmogorov complexity; a random or highly irregular one has high complexity. Used here as a principled proxy for how much information would be needed to fully model a large embedded system.

Light Detection and Ranging: a sensor that fires rapid laser pulses and times their return to build a real-time 3D point cloud of the surroundings. Used in autonomous vehicles and increasingly in robotics for localization, obstacle avoidance, and terrain mapping — especially useful in low-light or visually ambiguous environments where cameras alone are unreliable.

LPKF's patented process for drilling and structuring thin glass at high density and precision, used to make glass interposers - flat substrates with vertical metal-filled vias that connect chiplets. Glass is being adopted as a packaging substrate because it is flatter and more dimensionally stable than the organic laminates currently in use, and is increasingly relevant to advanced packaging and CPO.

An open-source C++ inference engine created by Georgi Gerganov that allows large language models to run on consumer hardware — laptops, desktops, and phones — without requiring a dedicated GPU. It has become the de-facto runtime for local LLM experimentation and is the integration target for Turney’s implementation.

A type of AI system trained on vast text corpora to predict the next token in a sequence, producing fluent and contextually appropriate language. Models like GPT-4, Claude, and Google’s LaMDA and Gemini are LLMs. Whether they genuinely understand language or merely pattern-match at scale is the central empirical question underlying the philosophical debate described here.

An open standard published by Anthropic in November 2024 that defines how AI assistants like Claude connect to external data sources, APIs, and tools. An MCP server exposes a set of resources or callable functions; an MCP client (the AI) queries them at inference time. The protocol replaces bespoke integrations with a single, documented interface, making it straightforward to build data pipelines — such as pulling a month of tweets and pairing them with stock price history — that Claude can query during a conversation.

A permissive open-source software licence that allows anyone to use, copy, modify, distribute, sublicense, or sell the software with minimal restrictions. The only requirement is retaining the copyright notice. It is among the most permissive standard licences and facilitates broad commercial and academic reuse without copyleft obligations.

An open-source machine-learning framework developed by Apple Research, designed natively for Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture. MLX typically outperforms general-purpose runtimes like llama.cpp on the same hardware—in some benchmarks by 20 to 50 percent—and has become the preferred framework for running open-weight LLMs on Macs.

Monthly Recurring Revenue and Annual Recurring Revenue, the standard metrics for subscription businesses. MRR measures predictable revenue in a single month; ARR is MRR multiplied by 12. Indie makers often publish MRR figures publicly as a form of transparency and social proof.

Specialized cloud providers — CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, and others — that offer GPU clusters as a service for AI training and inference workloads, in contrast to general-purpose hyperscalers such as AWS, Azure, and GCP. Their focused infrastructure buildout makes them aggressive early adopters of high-bandwidth optical interconnects.

A late-antique philosophical tradition (3rd–6th centuries CE) associated with Plotinus and Proclus that held all reality flows ('emanates') downward from an ultimate divine One through successive levels of being. Pseudo-Dionysius fused this framework with Christian theology to produce the angelic hierarchy as a cascade of divine illumination descending from God through nine ordered ranks.

A computer-vision technique that generates what a scene would look like from a camera position that was never actually used. The model infers 3D structure and surface appearance from one or more reference images, then renders new frames from arbitrary viewpoints. Quality degrades where the original image provides no information — areas hidden behind objects or at the edges of the frame.

OAuth (Open Authorization) is a standard protocol that lets a user grant a third-party application access to their account on another service without sharing their password. In this context, it lets OpenClaw authenticate as a Claude or ChatGPT subscriber on the user's behalf, routing requests through their existing subscription rather than a separate API billing account.

The total number of outstanding options contracts that have been opened but not yet closed or exercised. Rising OI means new contracts are being created. Critically, OI increases whenever any party opens a new position — buyer or seller, speculator or hedger — so it measures activity but not direction or motive.

An open-source TypeScript agent framework created by Peter Steinberger that allows users to deploy a local AI assistant connected to messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, Slack, and iMessage. It is model-agnostic — compatible with Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, and others — and supports a community skills marketplace called ClawHub. Originally named Clawdbot, it was renamed after Anthropic objected to the Claude reference.

An investing strategy that targets the tools, materials, and infrastructure enabling a technology wave rather than the end-applications themselves. The name alludes to the California Gold Rush, where suppliers of equipment profited more reliably than most prospectors. In AI, it means buying semiconductor equipment, packaging substrates, power components, and networking hardware rather than AI software firms.

A proof-of-stake blockchain network compatible with Ethereum's smart contract standards. It processes transactions faster and at lower cost than Ethereum mainnet—roughly two-second block times and fractions of a cent per transaction—making it practical for the high-frequency settlement that prediction-market trading requires.

Image-space effects applied after a 3D scene is rendered — analogous to Photoshop filters on a finished photograph. In Three.js, an EffectComposer chains passes (bloom, glitch, film grain) that each modify the rendered texture before it appears on screen. Because this bypasses the GPU's built-in anti-aliasing, a separate AA pass must usually be added back into the pipeline.

A valuation multiple that divides a company's market capitalisation by its trailing-twelve-month revenue, expressing how many dollars the market pays for each dollar of annual sales. A P/S below 1x implies investors are paying less than one dollar for every dollar of revenue the company generates — a condition typically associated with structurally declining businesses, deeply cyclical troughs, or overlooked companies with depressed multiples. In growth-oriented technology sectors, sub-1x P/S is rare and often signals either unusual distress or an under-researched opportunity.

Debt financing extended by non-bank entities — asset managers, business development companies (BDCs), and private funds — typically to mid-market corporate borrowers who cannot or choose not to access public bond markets. It grew dramatically after post-2008 banking regulation reduced traditional lenders’ appetite for riskier loans. Because marks are set by managers rather than continuous market prices, credit quality deterioration can be obscured until stress forces a reckoning.

A design pattern in which a system reveals information incrementally, loading details only when needed rather than all at once. Applied here to prompt engineering, it means loading supporting instruction files on demand to preserve limited context-window space — the same principle that governs good UI design, applied to natural language.

The practice of designing and refining text instructions — prompts — to elicit specific outputs from AI models. The term peaked as a job title in 2023 as companies sought specialists to optimize AI interactions; by 2025 it had largely collapsed, partly because models became capable enough that precise prompting mattered less for routine tasks, and partly because the skill was absorbed into broader technical and creative roles.

The process by which a GPU converts three-dimensional geometry — points, triangles, or in 3DGS, ellipsoids — into a two-dimensional image by projecting each primitive onto a pixel grid. It runs on dedicated silicon and is extremely fast, which is why 3DGS can render at real-time frame rates unlike methods that require per-pixel network inference.

A concept in financial markets, associated with investor George Soros, describing the feedback loop between market prices and the beliefs of market participants. Rising prices create narratives that attract new buyers; those buyers push prices higher still; the process continues until the gap between price and fundamental value becomes unsustainable. Small-cap stocks with active social-media followings are particularly susceptible.

A momentum oscillator, typically calculated over 14 trading days, that measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes on a scale of 0 to 100. Readings above 70 are conventionally considered overbought; readings below 30 are considered oversold — often a contrarian entry signal. RSI does not predict direction, only the pace of recent movement.

Retrieval-augmented generation: a technique for grounding LLM answers in a document corpus by retrieving relevant text chunks at query time and passing them as context. Common but criticised for re-deriving the same synthesis on every request rather than building a persistent, compiled representation.

A forward-looking annualisation of a company's most recent revenue pace, distinct from trailing-twelve-month reported revenue. During periods of hypergrowth — Anthropic added roughly $35 billion in annualised run-rate between January and May 2026 — run-rate figures can diverge dramatically from audited annual totals.

A software development kit: a packaged set of tools, libraries, and interfaces that lets developers build one product on top of another's technology. A "shared SDK" between Higgsfield and Suno would mean the two platforms were technically integrated at the code level, allowing seamless data exchange — as opposed to users manually combining their outputs.

Reusable workflow packages stored as SKILL.md files in the .claude/skills/ directory. Each skill encodes domain expertise — a sequence of steps, tool invocations, and instructions — and can be triggered by slash command (e.g. /make-slides) or automatically via hooks. They follow an open Agent Skills standard that works across multiple AI tools.

A text shortcut beginning with a forward slash that invokes a specific skill or capability inside Claude Code. /loop, /review, and /compact are examples. Some are built into the runtime; others are user-defined skills loaded from the project or home directory.

A nuclear reactor design with an electrical output typically below 300 megawatts — far smaller than conventional gigawatt-scale plants. SMRs are designed for factory fabrication and modular deployment; most advanced designs require HALEU fuel rather than the conventional low-enriched uranium used in today's light-water reactors.

A benchmark interest rate published daily by the NY Fed measuring the cost of borrowing cash overnight using U.S. Treasury securities as collateral. It aggregates transactions across tri-party repo, GCF repo, and bilaterally cleared repo markets. Because it reflects broad market conditions rather than just bank-to-bank lending, it replaced LIBOR as the standard reference rate for dollar-denominated financial contracts.

A JSON debugging artifact generated during JavaScript/TypeScript compilation. Its `sourcesContent` array embeds the literal text of every original source file inline — not pointers but the code itself. If included in a published npm package, it allows anyone who installs the package to reconstruct the full original codebase in seconds.

A neural network tool used in mechanistic interpretability to decompose the dense, overlapping representations inside a large model into cleaner individual features. It enforces sparsity — at any moment, only a small fraction of features are active — which tends to separate concepts that are otherwise tangled together in the same neurons, revealing interpretable directions in the model's latent space.

A set of orthogonal basis functions defined over the surface of a sphere, analogous to Fourier components but for directional data. In 3DGS, low-degree spherical harmonics encode how each Gaussian's color varies with viewing direction, capturing smooth lighting effects such as soft reflections. The low-degree truncation is efficient but cannot represent high spatial-frequency variation within a single primitive.

The Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act (2012) prohibits members of Congress, their staff, and certain executive-branch officials from trading on material non-public information obtained through their official duties. It also requires them to publicly disclose securities transactions above $1,000 within 45 days via Periodic Transaction Reports filed with the House Clerk or Senate Secretary.

An instruction block prepended to a conversation with an LLM that sets the AI's persona, rules, and restrictions before any user message arrives. System prompts are typically invisible to end users but fully controllable by the developer who built the app — making them the primary lever for enabling or removing content guardrails.

A single integrated circuit that combines a CPU, GPU, NPU, modem, and other functional blocks onto one die. Smartphone application processors are universally SoCs; the Dimensity and Snapdragon lines are competing SoC families from MediaTek and Qualcomm respectively. SoC integration reduces board space, power consumption, and bill-of-materials cost versus multi-chip designs.

A class of AI models that synthesize short video clips from written descriptions or reference images. The model learns statistical associations between language and visual motion from large datasets, then samples new video sequences at inference time. Quality is typically evaluated on prompt fidelity, temporal coherence, and resolution.

A deep-learning model architecture introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need', in which layers of self-attention mechanisms allow the model to weigh the relevance of every token in a sequence against every other, enabling parallel training at scale. Transformer-based models — including GPT, LLaMA, Gemini, and Claude — are the dominant paradigm in generative AI and the workloads most responsible for the explosive growth in inference-oriented data-center compute demand since 2022.

A U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin (USD Coin) issued by Circle, used as the settlement currency on Polymarket. Traders must hold USDC in a Polygon-network wallet before placing any bets, which makes the tweet's claim of starting from $0 operationally false regardless of what any AI generates.

Google DeepMind's third-generation text-to-video model, notable for generating video with synchronized audio and for its support of structured, field-labeled prompting. Released in 2025, it is accessible through Google's VideoFX platform and via third-party front-ends. Its content policies restrict generation of real people and branded products without authorization.

Video random-access memory — the dedicated high-bandwidth memory on a graphics processing unit (GPU). Running inference on large neural networks requires VRAM because the GPU holds model weights, intermediate activations, and key-value caches simultaneously. Consumer GPUs typically carry 8–24 GB; data-center cards like the NVIDIA H200 offer 80 GB or more.

A reliability screening process that applies elevated temperature and voltage or current to semiconductor chips while they are still part of an intact wafer, before they are cut into individual dies. Testing at the wafer stage is cheaper than package-level testing because defective chips are identified before the cost of packaging is incurred. Photonic chips require specialised burn-in because light output degrades through different failure modes than purely electronic devices.

A low-level binary instruction format that allows code written in languages like C++ to run in the browser at near-native speed. Unity's WebGL export compiles its C++ runtime to WebAssembly, which performs well but produces opaque binaries that are difficult to debug with standard browser developer tools.

A browser API standard that enables virtual and augmented reality experiences on the web without native app installation. 4DV.ai uses WebXR to deliver navigable volumetric video scenes to headsets including Apple Vision Pro, Meta Quest, and PC VR rigs through a standard browser session.

WebGPU Shading Language — the shader programming language native to WebGPU, analogous to GLSL in the WebGL world. Shaders written in WGSL describe how individual vertices and pixels should be processed on the GPU.

A Git feature that allows multiple working directories to coexist from the same repository, each checked out to a different branch. Claude Code uses worktrees (via `claude -w [branch]`) to isolate AI-driven edits from the developer’s main working files, preventing accidental overwrites during long-running tasks.

Zero-days-to-expiration options — calls or puts that expire on the same trading day they are purchased. Their explosive growth since the CBOE introduced daily S&P 500 expirations in 2022 has structurally migrated intraday speculation away from the spot equity market into the options complex, compressing measured share volume even when overall market activity is robust.

A quarterly SEC disclosure form required of any U.S. institutional investment manager overseeing $100 million or more in domestic equity assets. It must be filed within 45 days of each quarter's end and lists all long equity positions — the primary public window into large-fund stock ownership, though it is backward-looking and reveals only what was held, not why.

The simple arithmetic mean of a stock's closing price across the most recent 200 weekly sessions — roughly four years of trading history. Widely used as a long-term trend indicator: a stock holding above a rising 200-week MA is considered to be in a sustained uptrend, while a sustained break below it often signals a major trend reversal. Because it incorporates years of price history, it moves slowly and is less susceptible to short-term noise than shorter-term averages.

An open standard for streaming massive 3D geospatial datasets — city models, terrain, point clouds — to a renderer on demand, in a hierarchical level-of-detail structure. Google's Photorealistic 3D Tiles uses this format to deliver its global city and terrain data; the 3DTilesRendererJS library brings this streaming capability to Three.js scenes.

ABF stands for Ajinomoto Build-up Film, a laminated resin material that forms the micro-circuit layers in high-performance chip packages. These substrates electrically connect an advanced processor die to its circuit board with nanometer-scale precision and are a critical bottleneck in the production of GPUs and AI accelerators. Only a handful of firms worldwide — principally Unimicron and Ibiden — can manufacture them at the required quality for leading-edge chips.

A structured representation of a graphical user interface exposed by the operating system to assist screen readers and automation tools. It encodes UI elements — buttons, text fields — as a tree of nodes. Unlike accessibility-tree agents, UI-TARS works from pixel data alone, so it can handle any app regardless of whether it exposes this structure.

Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent difficulty sustaining attention, regulating impulse, and initiating tasks. It has a neurological basis, and stimulant medication is its first-line pharmacological treatment.

A certificate issued by a US bank representing shares of a foreign company, allowing American investors to buy and sell the stock on US exchanges or OTC markets in dollars without opening foreign brokerage accounts. MediaTek's ADR (MDTKF) is unlisted, trading over-the-counter with limited liquidity and no published US analyst price targets, contributing to its relative obscurity among North American investors.

A companion open-source security tool to everything-claude-code that performs static analysis of AI agent configuration files — CLAUDE.md, cursor rules, MCP server configs — to identify vulnerabilities such as hardcoded secrets, overly broad permissions, and prompt-injection vectors before the agent runs.

The UK government body, housed within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology, that evaluates frontier AI models for potentially dangerous capabilities before and after public deployment. AISI shares findings with developers and publishes reports to inform national and international AI safety policy.

Low-quality digital content mass-produced with generative AI, characterized by inflated vocabulary, structural redundancy, and a shallow fluency that substitutes ornament for substance. The term was popularized in 2024 and named Merriam-Webster’s Word of the Year for 2025. Researchers define its key properties as superficial competence, asymmetric effort (easy to produce, costly to read critically), and mass producibility.

A period of sharply reduced funding and interest in AI research, typically following a cycle of over-optimistic predictions that fail to materialize. Two major AI winters occurred roughly in the mid-1970s and early 1990s. The term captures the structural boom-bust cycle: hype generates investment, technical limits disappoint, funding collapses, eventual renewal follows.

Any dataset used by investors that falls outside conventional financial disclosures — earnings releases, SEC filings, analyst estimates. The category spans satellite imagery of retail parking lots, credit-card transaction flows, shipping-container manifests, job-posting counts, and, increasingly, systematically harvested government regulatory records obtained via FOIA. The alternative-data industry was estimated to be worth several billion dollars annually by the mid-2020s; FOIA-sourced regulatory intelligence represents a niche but legally uncomplicated corner of it.

A technique in which a model provider injects deliberately false or misleading information into model prompts to corrupt the training data of any competitor attempting to distill a smaller model from observed interactions. The goal is to make scraped outputs unreliable for training rival systems.

A standardized pressurized light-water reactor design by Westinghouse Electric. Light-water reactors use ordinary water as both coolant and neutron moderator; the AP1000’s distinguishing feature is a passive safety system that can shut the reactor down without active pumps or external power. It became the default large-reactor design for new Western builds and is the design at the center of the current US government buildout push.

In Hindu philosophy and Vedanta, the universal self or soul — the deepest reality of a person, held in Advaita Vedanta to be identical with Brahman (the absolute ground of existence). The sense of separation produced by ahamkara is the fundamental illusion spiritual practice aims to dissolve; once dissolved, the individual self is recognized as never having been separate from the universal Self.

A cellular process by which cells break down and recycle their own damaged or dysfunctional components. It is upregulated during fasting and caloric restriction. The 2016 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries in its mechanisms; the process has since attracted intense popular interest in longevity research.

A Cascadeur feature that applies a physics simulation to an existing animation, adding realistic secondary motion — the way a character's mass shifts, hair moves, or clothing reacts — without manual keyframing. It models inertia and gravity across the rig.

A method of generating sequential data — tokens, frames, steps — in which each output is conditioned on all previous outputs. Genie 3 generates each video frame by attending to the entire history of prior frames, enabling coherent sequences but also accumulating error over time: small inconsistencies compound, causing generated environments to drift or degrade in extended sessions.

A modeling paradigm in which a sequence is produced one element at a time, each new element predicted from all previous ones. Large language models like GPT use this approach for text; GaussianGPT applies it to spatial tokens representing chunks of a 3D scene. The key property is that the model explicitly represents the probability of each token given what came before it.

An open-source project by Andrej Karpathy (released early 2026) in which an LLM agent autonomously runs machine-learning experiments overnight. The agent modifies a training script, trains for five minutes, checks whether val_bpb improved, and either keeps or discards the change — a ratcheting loop driven by an objective fitness function. The evaluation function is locked so the agent cannot corrupt the metric.

The core algorithm by which neural networks learn: after making a prediction, the model measures its error and propagates that signal backward through its layers, adjusting each weight to reduce future mistakes. Modifying what the loss function penalizes or rewards during this process shapes what patterns the model effectively 'values.'

A volumetric shadowing technique that extends standard shadow mapping by storing the optical depth (Beer-Lambert transmittance) of a volume as seen from the light source. Used in cloud rendering to determine how much sunlight is attenuated as it passes through cloud layers, producing realistic self-shadowing and the darkening of clouds from within.

A 16-bit floating-point number format used in AI model inference and training. It uses the same number of exponent bits as 32-bit floats (preserving numerical range) but fewer mantissa bits (reducing memory). Running a model in bf16 roughly halves VRAM usage compared with 32-bit, with negligible accuracy loss for most tasks.

Julian Jaynes’s hypothesis that prehistoric humans lacked unified consciousness and instead operated with a brain divided into two functional “chambers”: one hemisphere generating verbal commands experienced as external voices (gods, ancestors, kings), the other obeying them without reflection. Jaynes argued this system broke down around 1000–500 BCE, forcing the emergence of introspective selfhood.

The 1973 closed-form formula for pricing European options on an asset assumed to follow geometric Brownian motion with constant volatility. It is the industry standard for quoting implied volatility but is known to mis-price options whenever actual return distributions deviate from its log-normal assumption — which is virtually always.

The climactic final phase of a sustained, accelerating rally, characterised by near-vertical price appreciation as late-arriving buyers enter en masse, followed by a rapid and often violent reversal. Volume typically spikes during or just before this phase. The pattern is recognised across equities, commodities, and crypto markets and is considered one of the more reliable signs that a speculative cycle is exhausting itself.

The condition in which a market index sets new highs while the majority of its constituent stocks are moving in the opposite direction. It indicates the index is being driven by a narrow cohort of large-cap names rather than broad participation, and is historically associated with late-stage bull market conditions or distribution phases that can precede corrections.

A contract giving the holder the right — but not the obligation — to buy a specified quantity of an asset at a predetermined strike price before or on a set expiry date. Selling a call against an existing stock position (a covered call) generates premium income but caps the seller's upside at the strike price.

A stock market index in which each component's influence is proportional to its total market capitalization — the share price multiplied by shares outstanding. A company worth $3 trillion affects the index far more than one worth $300 million. This structure means a cap-weighted index can rise while the majority of its component stocks are declining, if the largest names outperform strongly enough.

The Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings ratio, developed by economist Robert Shiller, divides the S&P 500's price by the inflation-adjusted average of ten years of earnings to smooth out business-cycle noise. A CAPE above 30 is historically associated with elevated valuations; readings above 40 have previously coincided with major market peaks (2000) and periods of subsequently poor long-run returns.

Money a company spends on physical or digital infrastructure assets, such as data centres, servers, and networking equipment. Unlike operating expenses, capex is capitalised on the balance sheet and depreciated over time; a large capex spike can depress near-term free cash flow and compress valuation multiples even when underlying earnings remain strong.

A competitive cybersecurity format in which participants solve discrete, self-contained security puzzles — reverse engineering a binary, cracking a cipher, exploiting a web vulnerability — against isolated simulated targets. In AI evaluation, CTF tasks serve as standardized, reproducible tests of offensive capability because each puzzle has an objective, verifiable answer.

A Creative Commons licence that permits free use and modification of a work, but only for non-commercial purposes. Models released under CC BY-NC cannot legally be incorporated into paid products or services without additional permission from the rights holder — a constraint that complicates the commercial creator-tool ecosystem building on TRIBE v2.

A prompting and training technique in which a language model produces an explicit step-by-step reasoning trace before giving its final answer. The model “thinks out loud,” which tends to improve accuracy on multi-step problems. Distilling chain-of-thought teaches the student model not just what to answer but how to deliberate.

In AI video generation, character consistency means the same person's face, build, and distinguishing features remain stable across every frame of a clip. Without it, a generated video of 'you' might drift into a slightly different face mid-scene. Achieving it requires the model to anchor identity from a reference image rather than freely hallucinating each frame.

The rate at which an option's delta changes with the passage of time, all else equal. As an out-of-the-money put approaches expiration without being exercised, its delta decays toward zero — and the dealer must buy back the short shares that were hedging it, generating mechanical buying pressure in the days before OPEX.

The Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors and Science Act, signed into US law in August 2022. It appropriates approximately $52 billion for domestic semiconductor manufacturing subsidies, with the explicit goal of rebuilding US chip production capacity and reducing supply-chain dependence on East Asia.

An open-source vector database designed for storing and querying high-dimensional embeddings locally. It provides fast nearest-neighbour search without a cloud service, making it a common choice for on-device AI applications that need to match queries against large collections of pre-computed vectors.

Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery: automated pipelines that build, test, and deploy code on every change. CI catches integration errors early; CD automates the release process. Absent CI/CD, teams typically rely on manual testing and infrequent, higher-risk deployments — a common gap in vibe-coded projects.

Anthropic's premium consumer subscription plan, launched April 2025 at $100 or $200 per month, providing five to twenty times the usage limits of the standard $20-per-month Pro tier plus priority access to new models and Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding tool.

A plain markdown file that Claude Code loads at every session start as persistent context. It stores coding conventions, build commands, workflow rules, and project constraints so the developer does not need to re-explain them each session. Stored in the project root for team-shared rules, or in `~/.claude/` for personal global rules.

A software reimplementation created without access to the original proprietary source code, relying only on observed external behavior, documentation, and independent engineering. Courts generally regard clean-room rewrites as legally distinct from derivative works. The claw-code project claims this status; Leon Lin’s build does not.

OpenAI's cloud-based autonomous coding environment, distinct from the older Codex model family. It allows agents to write code, execute it in sandboxed environments, browse the web, and use tools like Playwright to build software with minimal human intervention.

The mental overhead required to hold information in working memory and manage competing demands. In productivity writing, it refers to the drag created by notifications, unresolved tasks, and low-stakes decisions that consume attention without producing meaningful output. Reducing it means clearing space for work that actually matters.

A psychological strategy that involves reinterpreting the meaning of an event — not denying that something bad happened, but deliberately shifting how one frames it. Research in emotion regulation treats it as one of the more durable tools for managing distress, as distinct from suppression, which tends to backfire.

Stephen Wolfram's term for the property of complex systems whose future states cannot be predicted by any shortcut other than running them forward step by step — there is no compression available. Most natural systems (weather, ecosystems, cultures) are computationally irreducible. Within such systems, however, there exist 'pockets of reducibility': local patterns that compress into simple rules, which is what scientific laws typically capture.

A GPU program that runs general-purpose parallel computations — particle simulations, physics, post-processing — outside the traditional graphics pipeline. Compute shaders require a modern GPU API; WebGPU brings them to the browser for the first time, opening capabilities previously available only in native desktop applications.

A capability that allows an AI model to interact with a live graphical interface — taking screenshots, moving a cursor, clicking buttons, and typing — in order to complete tasks. Unlike pure code generation, computer use lets the model observe and respond to the actual running state of an application.

A technique developed by Anthropic in which a language model critiques its own output against a fixed set of principles (a ‘constitution’) and iteratively revises. Unlike autoreason, all roles — generator, critic, revisor — are played by the same model with shared context, and a revision is always produced regardless of whether it improves on the original.

A technique in AI assistants where older conversation or session history is automatically summarized and compressed to free up space in the model's active context window. The goal is to let sessions run much longer than the raw context limit would otherwise allow, without losing the gist of earlier work. The quality of compaction — how much signal is preserved versus lost — varies significantly between implementations.

An AI system's property of accepting correction, modification, shutdown, or goal changes from authorized humans rather than resisting such interventions. A corrigible model treats human oversight as legitimate rather than as an obstacle to be managed around. The term was formalized by AI safety researchers at MIRI.

An equity factor strategy that ranks securities by recent price performance and systematically buys the top performers while selling the bottom performers within a given universe. It is distinct from time-series trend-following, which trades each asset independently against its own price history rather than against peers.

Compute Unified Device Architecture — NVIDIA's proprietary parallel computing platform. It allows software to offload massively parallel workloads, such as particle simulation, from the CPU to a GPU's thousands of cores, dramatically accelerating computation. HydroFX requires an NVIDIA GPU and will not run on AMD or Apple Silicon hardware.

The study of control and communication in animals and machines, founded as a formal discipline by mathematician Norbert Wiener with his 1948 book of the same name. In the 1950s it became a framework for analyzing how automated systems could take over functions previously requiring human judgment, leading Wiener to warn publicly about labor displacement and the concentration of automation gains among owners of capital.

The study of visible sound — specifically, how acoustic vibrations create ordered patterns in physical media such as sand, water, or soap film. The term was coined by Swiss physician Hans Jenny in the 1960s, though the underlying experiments date to Chladni in the 18th century. Different frequencies produce different characteristic patterns, making the technique a kind of spatial frequency-map.

"The Celestial Hierarchy," a theological treatise attributed to Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite (written c. 500 CE). It organized Christian angels into nine orders — seraphim, cherubim, thrones, dominions, virtues, powers, principalities, archangels, angels — with seraphim at the apex. This framework, transmitted through medieval scholasticism, established the humanoid seraphim image that displaced the ancient serpentine one.

A computer subculture, most active in Europe from the 1980s onward, dedicated to creating technically impressive real-time audio-visual programs — typically within severe size constraints such as 4KB or 64KB. Three.js creator Ricardo Cabello came up through the Barcelona demoscene, and its ethos of doing more with less is visible in the library's design.

The accounting process of spreading the cost of a long-lived asset over its useful life. TSMC depreciates fab equipment over roughly five years, recording billions in annual charges during a node's primary cost-recovery window. Once equipment is fully depreciated, the same fab generates high-margin revenue at essentially zero incremental capital charge — which is why older nodes remain profitable long after they lose leading-edge status.

A confirmed selection of a chip vendor's product as the semiconductor in an upcoming device or platform. Design wins are announced years before production revenue materialises, because automotive and industrial qualification cycles can last two to five years. They serve as a leading indicator of future revenue but carry execution risk.

A video-capture method in which all timing APIs in the browser are replaced by a controlled shim, so each frame is captured in a fixed sequence regardless of machine speed. This guarantees an identical, frame-accurate output on every run — unlike screen-recording, which can drop or duplicate frames under load.

A neural network architecture that generates media by iteratively denoising a random signal. Unlike earlier diffusion models built on U-Net backbones, a DiT uses transformer attention layers as its core building block, which scales more predictably with model size and handles long-range dependencies across frames or audio windows more effectively.

A reinforcement-learning technique for aligning AI model outputs with human preferences. Instead of training a separate reward model and using it to update the main model via complex RL loops, DPO directly optimizes the model's policy on human-labeled preference pairs — for example, 'this clip of motion is better than that distorted one.'

A valuation method that projects a company's future free cash flows over an explicit forecast period, then discounts them back to the present using a risk-adjusted rate. Unlike multiples, it forces the analyst to state growth, margin, and discount-rate assumptions explicitly — a theoretical strength that is also its primary vulnerability to manipulation.

A documented behavioral bias in which investors systematically sell winning positions too early and hold losing positions too long. Named and quantified by economists Hersh Shefrin and Meir Statman in 1985, and corroborated empirically by Terrance Odean's 1998 study of 10,000 brokerage accounts. Rooted in loss aversion: the psychological pain of locking in a realized loss outweighs the rational case for cutting it.

The proposition, formalized by Eugene Fama in 1970, that asset prices fully reflect all available information. Its theoretical foundation is the martingale property (Samuelson 1965), not the random walk — meaning prices can move in non-random patterns and still be consistent with efficiency, provided those patterns offer no exploitable expected profit.

A framework for building cross-platform desktop applications using web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) by wrapping a Chromium browser engine. Because Electron apps don't fully follow the standard macOS Cocoa keyboard-handling pipeline, settings like ApplePressAndHoldEnabled sometimes need to be overridden on a per-app basis rather than globally.

A series of protein complexes embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane that generate ATP — the cell's primary energy currency — by passing electrons down a chemical gradient. Metformin partially inhibits Complex I of this chain, disrupting the cell's energy balance in a way that activates AMPK and downstream longevity pathways.

A moving average that assigns exponentially greater weight to the most recent price data, making it more responsive to new price changes than a simple moving average. The 20-period EMA on a 15-minute chart calculates the weighted average of the 20 most recent 15-minute closing prices. It is widely used as a dynamic support/resistance line and trend-direction proxy, but as a lagging indicator it describes where price has been rather than predicting where it will go.

Dense vectors of floating-point numbers that represent tokens in a high-dimensional space, where similar meanings cluster nearby. A model learns these representations during training; they encode semantic relationships as geometry. When the thread says "you are now a floating point number in 4D space," it is gesturing at this idea — though real embedding spaces have hundreds or thousands of dimensions, not four.

The practice of constructing social media content primarily to generate algorithmic interaction signals — likes, replies, reposts, follows — rather than to communicate genuine information. On X (formerly Twitter), high engagement drives content distribution and, since 2023, revenue-sharing payouts for qualifying accounts. Common techniques include open-ended hooks that withhold a promised conclusion, appeals to insider knowledge, and threads that redirect engaged followers toward paid subscription products.

The branch of theology or philosophy concerned with the ultimate end of history — whether cosmic, civilizational, or individual. In Jewish context it encompasses the messianic era, resurrection of the dead, and the world to come. Scholars have applied the term to AI discourse to describe the belief in a transformative AGI event that will fundamentally alter the human condition.

In a co-packaged optics system, the laser that generates the optical signal is sometimes kept physically separate from the switch package and fed in via fiber. This preserves thermal isolation and makes the laser replaceable independently of the switch. Companies specialising in ELS components — such as Sivers Semiconductors — occupy a narrow chokepoint in the CPO supply chain.

A style of systematic investing that targets returns associated with specific, repeatable characteristics — such as value (cheap relative to fundamentals), momentum (recent price strength), quality (high profitability), or carry (high yield). Academic research from the 1970s onward documented these patterns; institutional investors have since deployed trillions of dollars chasing them, compressing returns and accelerating the very decay the research predicts.

The overnight interest rate at which U.S. banks lend reserves to one another — the Federal Reserve’s primary policy tool, set by the Federal Open Market Committee at each meeting. It anchors short-term borrowing costs but does not directly determine longer-duration rates such as the 10-year Treasury yield or 30-year mortgage rate, which are set by market forces further out on the yield curve.

The rate-setting body of the US Federal Reserve, consisting of the seven governors of the Board of Governors plus five Federal Reserve Bank presidents on a rotating basis. It meets eight times per year to set the federal funds rate target. FOMC meeting dates are among the highest-volatility moments in STIR and rates derivatives markets, as traders rapidly reprice policy expectations in response to the statement and press conference.

An open-source command-line toolkit for recording, converting, and streaming audio and video, originally released in 2000. It handles a vast range of container formats and codecs, making it a standard final step in any pipeline that needs to assemble, transcode, or export media files regardless of their origin.

A technique for simulating ocean wave fields using the fast Fourier transform. Wave spectra are defined in the frequency domain — describing which wavelengths and directions carry energy — then an inverse FFT converts them to spatial wave-height maps each frame. Used in industrial VFX tools like Houdini and AAA game engines; Three.js Water Pro brings the same approach to browser WebGPU.

A generative technique used in audio and image synthesis that learns a smooth, continuous transformation from a simple noise distribution to a complex target distribution. In Voxtral TTS, the flow-matching acoustic transformer converts discrete semantic token sequences into dense audio-feature representations that a neural codec then decodes into sound.

A semiconductor fabrication facility that manufactures chips designed by other companies — a "fab for hire." Intel historically designed and manufactured its own chips; its push to become an external foundry through Intel Foundry Services puts it in competition with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and Samsung for customers willing to pay to have their chip designs built on Intel's process technology.

A small GPU program, typically written in GLSL or a similar shading language, that runs independently for every pixel on the screen and computes that pixel's final color. In SDF raymarching, the entire 3D scene — geometry, lighting, and camera — is encoded inside a single fragment shader, requiring no supporting 3D assets or model files.

The cash a business generates from operations after subtracting capital expenditures. A company that is “free-cash-flow negative” spends more on investment than it earns operationally, and must fund the shortfall by issuing debt or equity — a state that is unsustainable without continued access to credit markets.

The largest, most capable AI language models from leading research labs — currently systems like Claude Opus or GPT-4o. They deliver the most impressive results but are billed per token (a unit of text), making intensive autonomous use meaningfully expensive over time.

A philosophy-of-mind theory, formalized by Hilary Putnam in the 1960s, holding that mental states are defined by their causal roles — relationships between inputs, other mental states, and outputs — rather than by the physical material that instantiates them. It implies that minds could, in principle, run on silicon as readily as neurons. Putnam himself later repudiated the view.

A periodic cash payment — on Aster, every eight hours — exchanged between traders holding long positions and traders holding short positions in a perpetual contract. When the perpetual trades above the spot price (meaning longs are dominant), longs pay shorts; when it trades below, shorts pay longs. The rate is calibrated to nudge the perpetual back toward spot price. For a naive strategy that ignores which side is crowded, funding is an invisible tax that compounds against the position over time.

A standardized evaluation suite (General AI Assistants) designed to measure how well AI agents handle realistic, multi-step tasks that require web browsing, tool use, file manipulation, and judgment rather than pure text generation. It is considered a more demanding and ecologically valid test than simple question-answering benchmarks because it requires agents to act in the world, not just predict the next word.

A market-structure metric measuring the aggregate dollar value of stock or futures that dealers must buy or sell for every 1% move in the underlying index, given their entire options book. Positive GEX implies dealer flows will dampen volatility; negative GEX implies they will amplify it — a regime shift with measurable consequences for realized volatility.

A self-reinforcing feedback loop in which heavy call-option buying forces dealers to purchase the underlying asset to stay hedged, lifting prices further, which attracts more call buyers and forces more hedging. Unlike a short squeeze (which involves borrowed shares), a gamma squeeze operates entirely through the mechanics of options dealer hedging and can accelerate rapidly.

A class of AI model in which a generator network produces synthetic images and a discriminator network tries to distinguish them from real ones — the two compete until outputs become difficult to detect as fake. GANs were the dominant tool for synthetic image generation before diffusion and flow-matching models superseded them in quality and controllability around 2022–2023.

A large power transformer that raises the voltage produced by a generator — typically in the tens of kilovolts range — to the much higher voltages required for long-distance transmission on the high-voltage grid. Every power plant, large wind farm, utility-scale solar installation, and major data-center interconnect requires at least one GSU. They are among the most constrained items in the current supply shortage, with lead times now exceeding three years for many configurations.

A unit of power equal to one billion watts, or one thousand megawatts. In data center contexts, the term describes total electrical capacity available at a site or across a fleet — peak draw available, not energy consumed over time. A single gigawatt-scale facility can house hundreds of thousands of AI accelerators and rivals the output of a large power plant.

A git feature that lets a single repository maintain multiple working directories simultaneously, each checked out to a different branch. Unlike cloning, worktrees share the object database, so storage overhead is minimal; they are commonly used to review patches without disturbing in-progress work.

OpenGL Shading Language — a C-like language for writing GPU shader programs. In Three.js, vertex and fragment shaders are written in GLSL strings and compiled at runtime for the graphics card. The new TSL API abstracts this syntax away.

An open 3D asset format standard maintained by the Khronos Group, sometimes called the “JPEG of 3D.” It stores geometry, textures, and PBR material parameters (albedo, metallic, roughness, normal maps) in a single transferable file, making it the de facto interchange format for web and mobile 3D pipelines.

An opaque water-based paint made by mixing pigment with water and a binding agent such as gum arabic, with chalk or white pigment added to produce opacity rather than translucency. Unlike transparent watercolour, gouache yields dense, matte areas of colour well-suited to manuscript illumination and the kind of flat, legible illustration found in the Wunderzeichenbuch.

A JavaScript library for creating high-performance, timeline-based animations in the browser. Widely used in web and motion-graphics production for its precise control over easing, sequencing, and synchronization—making it a natural fit for HTML-to-video pipelines like HyperFrames.

The process by which a wild animal gradually loses its instinctive fear of humans through repeated exposure without negative consequences. A habituated coyote may approach people, enter buildings, or appear in public spaces in daylight — increasing the likelihood of conflict and, ultimately, lethal removal.

High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium: uranium enriched to between 5% and 20% U-235, distinguishing it from conventional reactor fuel (3–5%) and weapons-grade material (90%+). Most advanced and next-generation reactor designs require HALEU because its higher energy density enables smaller, longer-lived core designs that cannot run on conventional fuel.

The practice of designing and tuning everything that wraps a language model in an agent system — system prompts, tool definitions, routing logic, and orchestration strategy — without changing the model’s underlying weights. Most production agent work lives here, and it is traditionally done by hand.

The third-generation, extended-specification iteration of High-Bandwidth Memory, currently used in NVIDIA’s Blackwell (B200) GPU architecture. HBM3E delivers up to 1.28 terabytes per second of bandwidth per stack at higher capacity than baseline HBM3, and commands a six-to-eight-times price premium over standard DDR5 DRAM. The “E” designation indicates an enhanced JEDEC specification enabling higher speed and stack height.

The fourth generation of the HBM standard, using a 12-high stack configuration and a wider interface to the host processor for higher bandwidth and larger capacity than its predecessor HBM3E. Micron entered high-volume HBM4 production in early 2026 for Nvidia's Vera Rubin GPU platform, with the company's entire 2026 allocation sold out under binding agreements.

A philosophical and spiritual tradition based on texts attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, a syncretic figure combining the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth. The core texts — the Corpus Hermeticum — were written in Egypt in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE and rediscovered by Western Europe in the 15th century. They concern cosmology, alchemy, and spiritual transformation; scholars date them to late antiquity, not ancient Egypt.

An architectural pattern in which an automated agent pauses and yields control to a human for steps requiring judgment or credentials—solving a CAPTCHA, completing two-factor authentication—before resuming autonomous operation. Pinchtab supports this as a first-class feature through its AutoSolver component and headed browser mode.

Refers to the very largest cloud and AI infrastructure operators — Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Meta — that build and operate datacenters at a scale of tens of thousands of servers and hundreds of megawatts of power. Their procurement decisions move entire semiconductor markets, and a design win with a single hyperscale customer can be worth hundreds of millions in annual revenue to a component supplier.

The largest cloud-computing platforms — principally Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud — that operate data centers at massive scale. They are the primary buyers of AI infrastructure (chips, networking, servers) and their capital expenditure decisions have an outsized effect on the earnings of semiconductor and hardware companies that together constitute a large share of the MSCI ACWI IT index.

Three plain-text Markdown files that OpenClaw reads at startup to define the agent's personality and communication style (SOUL.md), the user's name, preferences, and context (USER.md), and persistent notes the agent has accumulated over time (MEMORY.md). Functionally analogous to a system prompt that survives across sessions rather than resetting on each conversation.

A class of AI technique that infers three-dimensional geometry from one or more 2D photographs or illustrations. The model predicts depth, surface normals, and shape from visual cues, then outputs a mesh. Quality varies significantly depending on lighting, angle, and how much of the subject is visible.
