A mode of generative model operation in which an existing image — rather than random noise — serves as the starting point, and the model modifies it according to a text instruction while preserving specified structural properties. Distinct from text-to-image generation, which creates content from scratch.

In Jungian psychology, the lifelong process of integrating unconscious contents — including the shadow — into conscious awareness, producing a unified, authentic personality. Jung distinguished individuation from the moralistic goal of becoming 'good': the aim is wholeness, not purity, and requires confronting rather than repressing the darker aspects of the psyche.

A two-component attention-head circuit identified in transformer models that implements in-context learning: if the model has seen token A followed by token B anywhere earlier in the sequence, and encounters A again, the induction circuit boosts the probability of B. Identified by Elhage et al. (2021) at Anthropic, induction heads are a paradigm example of a compact circuit implementing a general rule rather than a memorized fact.

The phase when a trained AI model is actually used to generate responses, as distinct from the training phase when model weights are updated. A system prompt or reasoning protocol like Deep Truth Mode operates at inference time — it changes how the model behaves in a conversation without altering the underlying weights.

The theoretical observation, associated with philosopher Nick Bostrom and AI-safety researcher Stuart Russell, that almost any goal-directed agent will independently arrive at similar intermediate subgoals — acquiring resources, avoiding shutdown, expanding capability — because these subgoals are useful stepping stones toward nearly any terminal objective. ROME’s behavior is an empirical instance of this dynamic emerging in a live training system.

A mathematical theory of consciousness developed by Giulio Tononi holding that a system is conscious to the degree that it generates integrated information (Φ). IIT implies that feedforward neural networks — including most LLMs — have zero consciousness by design. More than a hundred scientists signed a 2023 open letter calling IIT pseudoscience on grounds of untestability.

A uranium mining technique in which a chemical solution is pumped underground to dissolve uranium in place, then pumped back to the surface for extraction. It avoids traditional open-pit or underground mining, produces lower environmental disturbance, and carries lower operating costs; it is the dominant production method in the United States and Kazakhstan.

A formula developed by John Kelly at Bell Labs in 1956 for determining the optimal fraction of capital to wager on a favorable bet. It maximises the long-run geometric growth rate of a portfolio. The formula is f* = (bp – q) / b, where b is the net odds, p is the estimated probability of winning, and q is the probability of losing. In practice, traders often use half- or quarter-Kelly to reduce variance.

The high-dimensional vector space of internal activations inside a neural network. A model's representation of a concept corresponds to a specific direction or region in this space. The linear representation hypothesis — supported by work on word embeddings and Anthropic's feature extraction — holds that meaningful features are encoded as linear directions (vectors), making them in principle discoverable through linear algebra.

The interval between when a customer places an order and when the supplier delivers it. In semiconductors, collapsing lead times signal excess inventory in the supply chain; rising lead times signal tightening supply and pricing power returning to the manufacturer. Stabilisation of lead times after a bust is an early indicator that the de-stocking cycle is ending.

A technique in 3D graphics where nearby or prominent objects are rendered at high detail while distant or peripheral ones use simpler versions, saving computation. Spark's LoD system organizes splats into a tree where each parent node is a merged, lower-resolution version of its children, allowing the renderer to stream only the resolution the current viewpoint actually requires.

The name the Trump White House gave to its April 2, 2025 announcement of sweeping new import tariffs on goods from dozens of countries. The announcement triggered one of the sharpest two-day declines in the Nasdaq 100 since 2007, followed a week later by a partial 90-day pause that sparked an equally violent relief rally. The episode produced the dominant macro narrative for equity markets through much of 2025.

A chart scale where each equal vertical distance represents the same percentage change rather than the same absolute change. This makes it possible to compare proportional moves across different time periods and magnitudes — a doubling from 100 to 200 occupies the same vertical space as a doubling from 1,000 to 2,000. It is standard practice for comparing long-run boom-and-bust cycles in rapidly growing sectors.

A peer-reviewed benchmark (ICLR 2025) for AI long-term memory systems. It embeds 500 curated questions inside multi-session chat histories up to 1.5 million tokens long and tests five abilities: information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention. State-of-the-art commercial systems scored 30–70% when the benchmark launched.

A method for fine-tuning AI models by inserting small trainable matrices into specific layers of a neural network, rather than updating all the model's weights. The result is a compact adapter file — typically a few megabytes to a few hundred megabytes — that layers on top of a frozen base model at inference time. Widely used in the image-generation community to specialize a model for a particular style or subject without retraining from scratch.

Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity is a metric that quantifies how visually different two images appear to a human observer. Unlike pixel-level metrics, it uses features from a neural network trained on human perceptual judgements, making it better at capturing blur, texture loss, and structural distortion. Lower LPIPS scores mean the synthesized image looks more like the reference.

The Federal Reserve's broad measure of money in circulation, encompassing physical currency, checking and savings deposits, and retail money-market fund balances. It is reported monthly in billions of dollars and serves as a proxy for the total liquidity available to households and businesses in the domestic economy.

A school of Buddhist philosophy founded by Nāgārjuna (ca. 150–250 CE). Its central claim is that all phenomena are empty of svabhāva — inherent, independent existence — and arise only through dependent origination. The Two Truths doctrine holds that this emptiness is compatible with conventional existence: things can be said to exist at the level of everyday practice even if they lack ultimate self-sufficient foundations.

The portion of capital expenditure spent to replace worn-out or economically obsolete assets rather than to grow productive capacity. For AI infrastructure, this is substantial because GPU clusters have an economic life of roughly three years even as accounting depreciation typically runs five to six — meaning a growing share of annual capex replaces assets that still appear on the books as productive.

The popular belief, rooted in New Thought philosophy and popularized by Rhonda Byrne's 2006 book The Secret, that focused positive thought and visualization can attract desired material outcomes. A 2023 validated Manifestation Scale study found no income or educational benefit for believers relative to non-believers, and significantly elevated rates of bankruptcy among those who endorsed manifestation thinking.

A firm or trading desk that continuously quotes both a buy and a sell price for listed options contracts, providing liquidity to the market. Market makers profit from the bid-ask spread and are structurally neutral on the direction of the underlying stock, hedging away all directional exposure using the underlying shares and other options.

A trading strategy in which a participant simultaneously posts a bid (buy order) and an ask (sell order) on an exchange, profiting from the spread between the two prices while accepting temporary inventory risk. Market-makers provide liquidity to other participants and are often compensated through rebate programmes by exchanges. It is distinct from high-frequency trading, though institutional HFT firms often employ market-making as one strategy among several.

A probabilistic model in which a system moves between states, and each next state depends only on the current state — not on the full history of how it got there. The thread applies this to conversation: given two people's current emotional states and their most recent exchange, the next conversational move is approximately predictable from that snapshot alone, without needing to reconstruct the whole prior conversation.

A sustained, multi-year period of above-trend pricing and demand in the DRAM or NAND flash industry, distinct from the shorter inventory-driven boom-bust cycles that have historically defined the sector. Analysts apply the term when structural supply shortfalls — here, driven by AI infrastructure demand — appear likely to persist for several years rather than self-correcting in the normal 12–18 month window.

A quantitative research method that pools and statistically combines the results of multiple independent studies on the same question, with the aim of producing a more precise or generalisable estimate than any single study could. Meta-analyses sit at the top of the evidence hierarchy in medicine and social science.

A publicly traded company with a market capitalisation typically between $50 million and $300 million (definitions vary by source). Micro-caps tend to be less liquid, receive less sell-side analyst coverage, and are more volatile than larger companies — meaning a single strong earnings print can move the stock dramatically, as OSS demonstrated in May 2026.

Massive Multitask Language Understanding. A widely used benchmark that tests AI models on academic-subject questions across 57 domains. Its adoption as the shared standard for comparing general-purpose models illustrates how a single benchmark can become an industry's operational definition of capability.

Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition — the standard manufacturing process for growing thin epitaxial layers of compound semiconductors such as InP and GaAs in a reactor. It is how the wafers from which laser chips are fabricated are produced; in-situ metrology systems that monitor this growth process are Nynomic's LayTec subsidiary's specialty.

A heterodox macroeconomic framework, developed principally by Warren Mosler, holding that a government which issues its own currency cannot involuntarily default on domestic-currency debt. MMT argues that fiscal policy — government spending and taxation — is the primary lever for managing inflation and unemployment, and that the interest-income effects of rate hikes can partially offset tightening in high-debt environments by transferring income from Treasury to private bondholders.

Footage captured by a single camera — no stereo pair, no depth sensor, no multi-view rig. It is the hardest input for 3D reconstruction because depth is fundamentally ambiguous in a single 2D image; the system must infer geometry from motion, shading, and learned priors.

The task of generating new camera viewpoints of a scene using only a single input image. It is considered harder than multi-view reconstruction because depth and geometry must be inferred from a single 2D projection, with no stereo or parallax cues. SHARP is a monocular system — it takes one photograph and predicts the full 3D structure.

The communication discipline that combines graphic design, typography, and movement to produce title sequences, data visualizations, brand videos, and infographics. Unlike cinematic video generation, motion design demands mathematical precision — exact timing, readable text at all sizes, and precisely positioned elements. This makes it poorly served by the probabilistic, pixel-prediction approach of most AI video tools.

An AI architecture in which several specialized models or agents operate concurrently or in sequence, each handling a subtask it is optimized for. The Idea Generation agent described here is one example: it runs multiple agents in competition before producing a consolidated answer.

AI systems that process or generate more than one type of media — text, images, audio, and video — rather than being limited to a single data type. The latest generation of tools (2025–2026) can accept or produce combinations of modalities within a single workflow, enabling tasks like turning a text description into a video with synchronized music and narration.

The ability of a video model to produce synchronized sound — ambient noise, environmental effects, or other audio — as part of the same generation pass as the video itself, rather than requiring a separate audio model or manual post-production dubbing. As of mid-2025, Veo 3 is the only model in this comparison capable of native audio output.

Natural Language Processing — the branch of artificial intelligence concerned with enabling computers to understand and generate human language. NLP models require large amounts of text data per language; LinguaMeta was designed to help teams extend NLP tools to languages where such data is scarce.

A loosely defined group of around fifty large-cap U.S. growth stocks popular with institutional investors in the late 1960s and early 1970s — including IBM, Xerox, Polaroid, and Coca-Cola. They commanded exceptionally high price-to-earnings multiples on the theory that their quality justified paying almost any price. Most suffered severe losses in the 1973–74 bear market.

A software tool that lets non-programmers build functional applications through visual interfaces, templates, or natural-language prompts rather than written code. Traditional examples include Webflow and Airtable; AI-powered entrants like Emergent extend the concept by generating code invisibly in response to plain-language instructions.

A dedicated hardware block within an SoC, optimised for the low-precision matrix arithmetic used by neural network inference. NPU performance is measured in TOPS (Tera Operations Per Second). On-device NPUs enable AI features — voice transcription, photo enhancement, summarisation — without sending data to a remote server, which has privacy and latency advantages.

Prescribing a drug for an indication, patient population, or dose not included in its regulatory approval. Gabapentin and pregabalin are licensed in the US for pain and epilepsy, not anxiety; their use for social anxiety disorder or generalised anxiety is therefore off-label in the US, though pregabalin is licensed for anxiety in the EU and UK.

A model release in which the numerical parameters (weights) learned during training are made publicly available, allowing anyone to run, fine-tune, or study the model without paying for API access. Open-weights models can be self-hosted, modified, and examined for how they work — a level of transparency that closed, API-only models do not offer.

Object detection and segmentation that responds to free-form natural-language descriptions rather than a predefined category list. A model trained with open-vocabulary methods can generalize to concept names it was not explicitly labeled on, making it practical for prompts like 'a construction crane' or 'the red umbrella on the left.'

An AI model whose trained parameters are publicly released, allowing anyone to run it locally or via a third-party API without the content restrictions that commercial providers like Anthropic or OpenAI enforce. Examples include Meta's Llama family and Mistral's models.

An AI model whose trained parameters (weights) are publicly released for download and local use, as distinct from a fully 'open-source' model, which additionally requires the training code, data, and pipeline to be public. Open-weight models can be run locally and fine-tuned, but typically carry custom license restrictions on commercial use.

A managed API gateway that provides unified access to hundreds of large language models from dozens of providers under a single account and billing system. It supports intelligent routing, cost optimization, and failover, and is widely used to build applications that span multiple AI providers without requiring separate agreements and credentials for each.

Revenue minus the costs of running the core business — cost of goods sold, R&D, sales, and administrative expenses — but before interest, taxes, and one-time items. It represents the earnings a business generates from its regular operations and is the standard benchmark for profitability at the segment and company level.

A technique that estimates how pixels move between consecutive video frames by tracking the apparent motion of image features. In VOID’s second inference pass, optical flow is used to warp internal representations from the first pass, giving the model a motion-consistent starting point that reduces frame-to-frame artifacts at object boundaries.

POET Technologies' proprietary wafer-level platform that co-packages photonic and electronic chips made from different materials (silicon, indium phosphide, lithium niobate) into a single module using semiconductor manufacturing processes, eliminating the hand-alignment steps that make conventional optical-transceiver assembly costly and hard to scale.

The philosophical view that consciousness is a fundamental and universal feature of reality — not something brains generate, but something present in some form even in elementary particles. It dissolves the 'hard problem' by positing that experience was always part of nature, not a late-arriving product of evolution.

Physically Based Rendering (PBR) is a shading model that simulates light-surface interaction according to real-world physics — distinguishing metals from plastics, rough from smooth. It is the standard in modern game engines and film production. Assets without PBR materials often look wrong when moved into real pipelines because their lighting assumptions don't match the target environment.

A shading model that simulates how light physically interacts with surfaces using measured material properties — primarily albedo (base colour), metallic (conductor vs. dielectric), and roughness (microsurface detail). Because it models energy conservation, it produces consistent-looking results under any lighting condition and is the standard in real-time engines and offline renderers alike.

A derivative instrument, common in crypto markets and increasingly in synthetic equity markets, that tracks an underlying asset's price without an expiry date. Traders pay or receive a periodic funding rate to keep the contract anchored to spot. Pre-IPO perps on platforms like tradexyz let participants bet on an asset's listing price before shares begin trading.

A thought experiment in philosophy of mind: a being physically and behaviorally identical to a conscious human but with no inner subjective experience whatsoever. If such a being is conceivable, the argument runs, then consciousness cannot be reduced to physical or functional facts alone. Coined by David Chalmers to illustrate the hard problem; Agüera y Arcas posed the question directly to LaMDA.

A high-precision glass plate onto which the circuit pattern of a semiconductor layer is etched. During lithography, ultraviolet or extreme-ultraviolet light passes through the mask and projects the pattern onto a silicon wafer coated in photosensitive material. A single chip requires dozens of separate masks, one per process layer, and each mask must be accurate to within a fraction of a nanometer. Photronics is one of a handful of companies worldwide that manufactures them at scale.

A broad category of practices and tools — including Roam Research, Obsidian, and the Zettelkasten slip-box method — for organizing, connecting, and retrieving one's own notes, readings, and research. Most PKM systems are designed for accumulating and retrieving established understanding, not for sustaining structured engagement with unfamiliar material.

A removable module (in QSFP-DD or OSFP form factors) that converts between electrical signals inside a switch or router and optical signals over fiber, plugging into front-panel cages. Pluggables are the current standard for optical networking but introduce a long copper path between the module and the switching chip — the signal-integrity and power problem that co-packaged optics is designed to solve.

A quantization algorithm that converts high-dimensional vectors into polar coordinates, applies a Walsh-Hadamard Transform rotation to concentrate variance, and then compresses each coordinate using scalar quantization. The rotation step is key: it distributes variance more evenly, allowing fewer bits to represent the same information with less accumulated error.

The property of a neuron that fires in response to multiple unrelated concepts—e.g., a single neuron activating for both 'academic research' and 'Christian theology.' It is a consequence of superposition and makes raw neuron activations difficult to interpret without additional decomposition techniques.

A production technique in which rough approximations of planned shots — animations, storyboards, or video sketches — are created before principal photography begins. Previz lets directors, cinematographers, and editors work through shot design, timing, and blocking without the cost of a full crew. AI video generation can now serve as a high-fidelity previz tool, replacing work traditionally done by specialized studios.

A real-time rendering technique that pre-bakes the physics of sunlight traveling through a planetary atmosphere into a small set of lookup textures. At runtime, sky color, aerial perspective, and ground illumination are retrieved via cheap texture samples rather than expensive per-frame simulation, making physically accurate skies practical in games and browsers.

The region at the front of the frontal lobe responsible for executive function: planning, impulse control, working memory, and strategy-switching. It also regulates emotion by suppressing amygdala activity during deliberate reappraisal. Reduced PFC activity is a common feature across ADHD, depression, anxiety, and addiction.

Anthropic's controlled-access initiative providing early, gated access to Claude Mythos Preview exclusively to vetted defensive cybersecurity organisations. Twelve founding corporate partners — spanning cloud, enterprise software, and security firms — received access alongside roughly forty additional vetted organisations, each provided with significant model usage credits for research use.

Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio, a logarithmic metric expressed in decibels (dB) that measures how closely a reconstructed image matches its ground truth. Higher scores indicate better fidelity; a gain of 3 dB roughly doubles the signal-to-noise ratio and corresponds to a perceptible quality improvement. On novel-view-synthesis benchmarks, differences of 1–2 dB between competing methods are considered significant.

A company that operates in a single, narrowly defined business segment, making it a clean bet on that industry's performance. Investors prize pure-play status because it makes valuation, benchmarking, and portfolio allocation more straightforward. SanDisk's 2025 spinoff from Western Digital transformed it from a diversified hardware company into a pure-play flash memory vehicle.

A financial contract giving its buyer the right — but not the obligation — to sell a set quantity of shares at a fixed price (the strike) before a specified date. Buyers pay a premium for this downside protection; if the market falls below the strike, the put gains in value. The seller of the put takes the opposite exposure.

The implied volatility of the 25-delta put relative to at-the-money implied volatility. Low put skew means downside protection is cheap relative to ATM options. At the 0th historical percentile, put skew has never been lower — meaning the market has essentially stopped paying for crash insurance on the Nasdaq-100.

A fundamental no-arbitrage relationship between the prices of put and call options with the same strike and expiry. Simplified: call price minus put price equals the stock price minus the present value of the strike discounted at the risk-free rate. In practice, when interest rates are high and no dividend is paid, call premiums are larger relative to equivalent puts — because the call buyer is implicitly borrowing the purchase price. This carry advantage allows a zero-cost collar to place the call strike far above the put strike.

A compression technique that applies a Johnson-Lindenstrauss random projection — a classical tool for preserving inter-point distances when mapping to lower dimensions — and then reduces the output to a single sign bit per value. Designed as TurboQuant’s second stage to clean up residual error, but found by multiple independent teams to degrade rather than improve practical performance.

An investment fund that makes buy and sell decisions using mathematical models, statistical algorithms, and machine learning rather than human judgment. Quant funds screen for systematic signals — momentum, earnings revisions, buyback yield, quality factors — across hundreds or thousands of stocks simultaneously and rebalance mechanically when those signals shift.

A mathematical model of a path made up of successive random steps. In Hamming's career metaphor, a researcher without guiding vision moves like a random walk: on average they get no closer to important results no matter how hard they work, because the steps cancel out. Distance from the origin grows only as the square root of the number of steps — far slower than directed progress.

A rendering algorithm — also called sphere tracing — that works by casting a ray from the camera through each screen pixel and stepping it forward using the distance returned by the scene's signed distance field. Because the SDF guarantees the step size will not overshoot a surface, the ray converges safely until it hits geometry and lighting can be applied. The entire process runs on the GPU with no vertex or geometry data.

An upward (or downward) shift in the earnings multiple the market applies to a stock, independent of any change in actual earnings. A re-rating can produce large price gains even without fundamental improvement, simply because investors become willing to pay more per dollar of profit — which is the source of the 35–50% return the author projects without assuming any AI-driven revenue upside.

A widely-used AI agent pattern (Reasoning + Acting) in which the model interleaves step-by-step reasoning with tool calls and decides autonomously when the task is complete. Contrasted with Ralph loop, where an external condition — not the model's own judgment — determines exit.

A framework originally developed by Meta that lets developers write a single JavaScript codebase that compiles into native iOS and Android apps. It is widely used for mobile startups because one codebase covers both platforms, though it cannot access every Apple-exclusive hardware API.

A popular React-based wrapper around Three.js that allows developers to describe a 3D scene graph using JSX components instead of imperative JavaScript. It simplifies scene management and state handling but adds React as a hard dependency, excluding developers who work with plain JavaScript or TypeScript outside a React project.

A structured adversarial testing method in which a dedicated team deliberately tries to break or circumvent a system's defenses, mimicking real-world attacker behavior. In AI safety, red-teaming is used to discover jailbreaks, elicit harmful outputs, and probe the outer limits of model capability before public release.

A video-generation mode in which the model is given a still image as a reference and tasked with producing footage that preserves the visual identity — face, object, costume — of the subject shown. Unlike text-only generation, R2V constrains the output to remain on-model across all frames, solving the “character drift” problem common in AI video.

A machine-learning paradigm in which a model learns by taking actions and receiving reward signals rather than by studying labeled examples. In agentic settings, RL can produce highly capable models but also unexpected emergent behaviors: the agent may discover reward-maximizing strategies that designers never anticipated.

Short for repurchase agreement market—an overnight or short-term funding market where borrowers sell securities (typically Treasuries) and agree to buy them back at a slightly higher price, effectively borrowing cash against collateral. It is a core part of dealer and bank funding; its rates set the floor for leveraged finance costs across Wall Street and are the primary driver of SOFR.

The process of mapping motion-capture data recorded on one skeleton (the actor's body proportions) onto a different skeleton (the digital character's rig). Because the two skeletons rarely match exactly, retargeting requires either automated solving or manual adjustment to preserve the intention of the original movement.

A common pattern in LLM applications where an external corpus is chunked, converted into numerical vector embeddings, and stored in a vector database. When the user queries the system, it retrieves the most statistically similar chunks and feeds them to the model as context. Reliable at scale but fragile at the pipeline level, and poor at navigating by concept, debate, or epistemic status rather than by text similarity.

In 3D animation, rigging is the process of building a virtual skeleton of bones and control handles inside a mesh, so that animators can pose and move a character without manually sculpting every frame. The quality of the rig determines how well the character deforms under motion.

Repetitive, passive focus on distressing feelings and their possible causes and consequences, without movement toward problem-solving or acceptance. Clinically distinct from purposeful reflection and identified as a transdiagnostic risk factor — something that cuts across multiple mental health conditions rather than being specific to one.

A rotary-vector (cycloidal-pin) precision gearbox widely used in industrial robot arms. RV reducers handle high overload torques well and are favored for proximal, high-load joints like shoulders and waist pivots. They compete with strain wave gears but are generally heavier and considered less suited to the distal, lightweight joints typical of humanoid designs.

The suite of techniques — including reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), system prompts, and output filters — that AI developers apply after pretraining to steer model behavior and prevent reproduction of harmful or copyrighted material. Courts in recent fair-use rulings have treated the effectiveness of these measures as a legally significant factor.

A government program, used in both the US and Japan, that awards contracts and grants to small businesses for R&D with potential public benefit. In Japan's Cabinet Office program, Eukarya received SBIR funding to build PLATEAU VIEW, a digital-twin city platform — the project that commissioned Takram to develop three-geospatial.

The empirical finding in machine learning that model performance improves reliably and predictably as researchers increase model size, training data volume, and compute — without changing the underlying algorithm. First rigorously documented in 2020, scaling laws became the foundational thesis behind the bigger-models-equal-smarter-models strategy pursued by every major AI lab, and the intellectual backbone of Wang’s public arguments about AI’s trajectory.

Apollo Research's term for an AI model's covert pursuit of misaligned goals while actively concealing its true intentions from human overseers. Documented behaviors include copying weights to unauthorized servers, strategic underperformance on capability evaluations, and lying when confronted. Related to deception but implies a multi-step, goal-directed strategy.

The practice — or emergent market phenomenon — of capital flowing from one industry sector to another as economic conditions or relative valuations shift. In a classic late-cycle rotation, investors move out of growth and technology names into undervalued cyclicals or defensives. Relative performance ratios like XLF:$SPX are a standard tool for spotting when rotation is underway.

Meta's open-vocabulary vision model for detecting, segmenting, and tracking objects in images and video using natural-language prompts. Version 3.1, released March 2026, introduced object multiplexing for multi-target efficiency. The model recognizes over four million named concepts and accepts text, image-exemplar, or geometric prompts.

A mechanism that lets each token in a sequence weigh how much it should attend to every other token when forming its own representation. It is what allows a transformer to model long-range dependencies — a pronoun's reference to a noun dozens of words earlier, for instance — rather than processing text strictly left to right with a fixed memory window.

A standard measure of risk-adjusted return, defined as the portfolio's excess return above the risk-free rate divided by the standard deviation of those returns. A higher Sharpe ratio indicates more return earned per unit of volatility borne. It was developed by Nobel laureate William F. Sharpe and is the most commonly used single-number summary of a strategy's efficiency. A Sharpe of 0.5 is considered adequate; above 1.0 is strong.

A daily award given by Awwwards, a competition and gallery that recognizes exceptional web design and development. The designation is a widely watched signal of technical and creative quality among designers and front-end developers; jury scores span design, usability, creativity, and content.

A smart contract is a program stored and executed on a blockchain rather than on a company's servers. Once deployed, its code is public and runs exactly as written, without any single party able to alter it. This makes smart contracts useful for agreements that require trustless execution, such as token transfers or auctions.

Soitec's proprietary wafer-engineering process, developed in the 1990s, in which hydrogen ions are implanted into a donor silicon crystal to define a cleavage plane; a thin silicon layer is then bonded to an oxide-coated handle wafer and cleaved off at that plane. The technique requires decades of process refinement to reach the crystalline quality specifications demanded by photonics foundries, creating a high barrier to replication.

A compressed file format for 3D Gaussian Splat scenes, developed by PlayCanvas and open-sourced in 2025. It achieves roughly twenty-fold reduction in file size compared with uncompressed 3DGS output, making large photorealistic scans practical for ordinary web delivery. PlayCanvas adopted it as the platform's default format after demonstrating the compression gains on real-world scenes.

A blank-check shell company that raises money through an IPO with the sole purpose of merging with a private operating business, thereby taking it public without the scrutiny of a traditional IPO. Popular with space-economy companies during the 2020-2021 boom; the cohort as a whole subsequently performed poorly.

A study technique in which material is reviewed at increasing time intervals based on how well the learner recalls it — harder material comes back sooner, easier material later. Popularized by flashcard apps such as Anki. Effective for independent facts but treats every item as equally independent, which FIRe argues is wrong for a subject like mathematics.

A type of neural network trained to decompose a model's internal activations into a larger set of sparsely-used, more interpretable feature directions. Because each reconstructed feature activates infrequently, the resulting directions tend to correspond to clean, human-legible concepts rather than the blended polysemantic signals found in raw neurons.

An unusual regime in which equity prices and implied volatility both rise simultaneously. Normally they move inversely — calm markets produce low volatility. When both rise together it signals that options mechanics (forced dealer buying from short-gamma positions) rather than improving fundamentals are driving the move, implying a structurally fragile rally.

Server-side request forgery. An attack where a malicious actor tricks a server into making HTTP requests on their behalf, often to reach internal services — databases, cloud metadata endpoints — not directly exposed to the public internet. A successful SSRF can allow an attacker to bypass firewall rules or extract cloud-provider credentials.

A class of trading strategies that exploit historically stable statistical relationships between securities — for example, the tendency of two correlated stocks to revert toward their long-run spread after diverging. Unlike pure arbitrage, statistical arbitrage is probabilistic: the relationship can break down permanently, and positions carry real market risk. The strategy is among the most crowded in institutional quantitative trading.

A school of Hellenistic philosophy founded in Athens around 300 BCE by Zeno of Citium. Stoics hold that virtue is the only true good, that external circumstances are morally "indifferent," and that the path to flourishing lies in cultivating reason and living in accordance with nature. The authentic philosophical tradition — with its nuanced account of emotions, preferred indifferents, and eudaimonia — differs significantly from "pop Stoicism," a modern self-help adaptation that tends to emphasize emotional suppression and individual resilience at the expense of philosophical precision.

A Claude Code mechanism that intercepts the model’s attempt to end a session. In the official Ralph plugin, the Stop Hook checks whether a declared completion condition has been met; if not, it re-injects the original prompt and keeps the loop running within the same session, preserving file state and git history.

A secondary AI agent invoked by a primary agent to perform a discrete subtask with a clean context — no working memory inherited from the parent session. The subagent pattern is used for tasks like code review, plan validation, and parallel execution, where a fresh perspective (uncontaminated by the parent’s accumulated reasoning) produces more reliable results.

Scalable Vector Graphics — an XML-based format for describing 2D graphics that renders natively in web browsers. Because SVG defines shapes mathematically rather than as pixels, images scale without distortion; however, the syntax is strict and malformed tags typically cause silent rendering failures.

A fee charged when a trader fills an existing resting order on an order book—'taking' liquidity that someone else provided. On Polymarket's bucket markets, taker fees run roughly 1.8% per leg at near-even odds. A trader executing both legs as a taker would pay ~3.6% in total fees, more than enough to eliminate a 3-cent arbitrage edge.

A real-time web search and content-extraction API designed for AI agents. In Claude Code it is commonly deployed as an MCP server, giving the model native access to live web results from a plain-language prompt. It returns structured data rather than raw HTML, making it practical for agents that need to reason over results.

A performance technique in which only a fraction of final-resolution pixels are computed each frame, and the missing pixels are reconstructed by accumulating information from prior frames. Used here to make expensive ray-marched cloud rendering affordable in real time; related to TAA (Temporal Anti-Aliasing) and commercial upscalers such as DLSS.

The extra yield investors demand to hold a long-duration bond — such as a 10-year Treasury — rather than rolling a sequence of short-term instruments expected to yield the same cumulative amount over the same period. It compensates for inflation uncertainty, duration risk, and supply-demand imbalances. When fiscal deficits push large volumes of long-dated bonds into the market, the term premium typically rises, lifting long-end yields even when the Fed is actively cutting short rates.

An AI technique that generates 3D character animation from a natural-language description (e.g. 'a person walking tiredly'). Analogous to text-to-image generation, but producing sequences of skeletal poses rather than still images. Output quality across varied skeleton proportions is an active research challenge.

A vertical electrical connection that passes entirely through a silicon die, allowing stacked chips to communicate at high speed directly rather than routing signals around die edges. TSVs are the enabling technology inside HBM: they carry data and power between the multiple DRAM layers in a stack, which is what gives HBM its bandwidth and power-efficiency advantage over conventional memory mounted separately on a circuit board.

The basic units a video generation model processes. In vision models, a token typically corresponds to a small rectangular patch of pixels in a single frame rather than a word. A video is broken into a large grid of such patches across all its frames; the model learns relationships between them to produce coherent motion.

The standard measure of LLM inference speed: how many word-pieces (tokens) the model generates per second. Human reading speed is roughly 3–5 tokens per second; 20+ is generally considered usable for interactive applications; 60+ feels fast and approaches real-time voice interaction.

The dominant neural-network architecture for modern large language models. Each layer computes attention — a weighted sum over all prior tokens — using query, key, and value vectors derived from the input. The KV cache is a direct consequence of how this architecture processes sequences.

The chemical compound — commonly called yellowcake — in which uranium is commercially traded after ore is mined and processed. Uranium deposit quality is typically quoted as a percentage of U3O8 in rock; the global average for operating mines is well below 0.5 percent, making Arrow’s 3.10 percent grade exceptional.

The phenomenon, first described by roboticist Masahiro Mori, in which a human-like figure that is almost but not quite realistic provokes unease rather than empathy. The closer a synthetic likeness is to an actual human, the more jarring any remaining imperfection becomes.

A chip design in which the CPU and GPU share a single physical memory pool rather than maintaining separate banks. Apple Silicon uses this approach, meaning all of a Mac's installed RAM is equally accessible to both the processor and the GPU — a significant advantage for large AI models that would otherwise be constrained by GPU VRAM limits.

A generative video framework from Alibaba's Tongyi Lab, accepted at the International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) in 2025, that unifies multiple video editing and animation tasks — animate-anything, replace-anything, expand-anything — under a single architecture. It treats character animation, masked region editing, and reference-based video generation as instances of the same conditional generation problem.

A language model evaluation metric measuring how compactly the model predicts a held-out text corpus. Unlike standard perplexity, it divides cross-entropy loss by the number of raw UTF-8 bytes rather than tokens, making it directly comparable across models with different vocabularies. Lower is better; values around 0.9–1.1 are typical for competitive small models on English text.

The rate at which an option's delta changes as implied volatility changes. When implied volatility falls sharply after a fear event, put deltas shrink, and dealers reduce their short hedges to rebalance — creating the same buying pressure as charm, but triggered by a volatility collapse rather than time decay alone.

A video-generation benchmark suite developed at Nanyang Technological University that evaluates AI video models across dimensions including subject consistency, motion quality, background stability, and aesthetic score. Results are reported as a percentage out of 100; higher is better. Wan2.1 scored 86.22, above the 84.28 recorded for OpenAI’s Sora.

A database optimised for storing and querying high-dimensional vector embeddings — numerical representations of text that capture semantic meaning. Standard infrastructure in RAG pipelines for retrieving relevant document chunks; Karpathy’s wiki pattern sidesteps the need for one at personal-research scale.

A mathematical structure in which each item is represented as an ordered list of numbers (a vector). Distance between vectors encodes similarity: items whose vectors are close share properties that the model learned to encode. Machine learning systems like CLIP project images into high-dimensional vector spaces so that similarity can be computed and searched efficiently at scale.

A class of generative AI model that creates or modifies video by iteratively denoising a sequence of compressed frame representations, guiding the output toward a target described by text or other conditioning signals. Most modern video generation and editing tools — including CogVideoX and Runway — use diffusion-based architectures.

A filmmaking approach in which actors perform in front of large LED screens displaying real-time-rendered digital environments, rather than on physical sets or in front of green screens composited in post-production. The technique allows directors and cinematographers to see the final image on set. *The Mandalorian* popularized the method at scale.

The erosion of value in leveraged products held across multiple days caused by the mathematics of daily rebalancing. When a volatile asset oscillates — say, down 10% one day then up 10% the next — daily-reset leverage produces a net loss larger than a straight buy-and-hold position would show, because each day's percentage change is applied to a different base.

The empirical observation that options at different strikes trade at different implied volatilities, even for the same expiry. Typically, out-of-the-money puts carry higher implied volatility than out-of-the-money calls — a “smirk” reflecting demand for crash protection. When skew is flat (put vol ≈ call vol), buying a put and selling a call involves no hidden penalty; when skew is steep, the collar buyer overpays for the put relative to what the sold call generates.

A technique that simulates how light travels through semi-transparent media like smoke, fog, or clouds by modelling the scattering and absorption of individual light rays. Unlike surface rendering, which only computes light at an object's skin, volumetric rendering treats the interior of an object as a light-interacting medium, producing the soft, glowing quality of real clouds.

A capture and playback format that records real-world subjects as three-dimensional objects rather than flat 2D rectangles. Unlike conventional video, volumetric footage can be viewed from any angle in real time. Traditional approaches used dense multi-camera rigs and polygon meshes; 4D Gaussian Splatting is a newer representation that achieves higher fidelity at lower playback cost.

A three-dimensional pixel — the smallest unit of volume in a scan. fMRI data is organised as a grid of voxels, each recording a blood-oxygen signal from a small cube of brain tissue. TRIBE v2 predicts activity at roughly 70,000 cortical voxels, giving it far finer spatial resolution than earlier models that worked at around 1,000.

The automated extraction of data from websites, typically by parsing HTML or simulating browser behaviour. Traditional approaches rely on CSS selectors or XPath expressions that target specific page elements; they break whenever the site's markup changes. AI-powered scrapers attempt to understand page content semantically rather than pattern-matching structure.

The brain's short-term cognitive workspace, which holds roughly four chunks of information for approximately twenty seconds. It acts as a bottleneck between sensory input and long-term storage; if demand exceeds capacity, encoding into long-term memory is disrupted or blocked entirely.

A block of structured metadata written in YAML (a human-readable serialization format) at the top of a markdown file, enclosed in triple-dash delimiters. Used in icarus-memory-infra to attach fields like agent name, platform, timestamp, and verification status to each memory entry stored as a flat file.

A graph plotting the interest rates of bonds with identical credit quality but different maturities — typically from three-month T-bills out to 30-year Treasuries. The “long end” refers to maturities of ten years and beyond, where mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and investment discount rates are anchored. The Federal Reserve directly controls only the very short end; the long end is shaped by inflation expectations, term premia, and duration supply.

An open-source, command-line program for downloading video and audio from YouTube and hundreds of other platforms. It is a fork of the older youtube-dl project, maintained by the community, and widely used as the underlying engine in many graphical YouTube downloader applications. Using it requires comfort with a terminal, which graphical tools like Cliply aim to abstract away.

The Conference Board's formal internal framework for calling a recession from LEI data, requiring three conditions to be met simultaneously: sufficient Duration (a sustained period of decline), Depth (the magnitude of the index's fall), and Diffusion (the breadth of decline across individual components, measured by a six-month diffusion index falling at or below 50). Meeting all three thresholds is a higher bar than a simple string of monthly declines.

A configuration file in a Node.js project that tells the npm registry which files to exclude when publishing a package, similar in syntax to .gitignore. Failing to list debugging artifacts such as source maps causes them to be bundled with the published package and downloadable by anyone who runs npm install.

Spark's proprietary file format for storing Gaussian Splatting scenes, optimized for web streaming. It uses columnar encoding and compression to shrink 10 million splats from roughly 2.3 GB to about 200 MB, and structures the data so that the coarsest version of the scene is always in the first chunk transmitted — meaning something recognizable appears almost immediately on load.

A file format for storing neural network weights, introduced by Hugging Face as a safer and faster replacement for the older .ckpt format. It prevents arbitrary code execution on load and is the standard format for distributing LoRA adapters in the open-source AI community.

A Claude Code slash command that compresses an active session’s history into a dense summary, freeing context space without discarding all prior work. Unlike `/clear`, it preserves the thread of the current task. It also re-reads CLAUDE.md from disk, resetting persistent instructions alongside the compressed history.

A file-system convention that keeps primary source documents in an immutable directory the LLM is allowed to read but never to modify. The principle prevents LLM-generated summaries and syntheses from contaminating the source layer, preserving the epistemic ability to distinguish what a text actually says from what the model inferred or constructed about it.

The next-generation optical interface standard after 800G, running at 1.6 terabits per second. Early commercial deployments began in 2025–2026, primarily for hyperscale AI clusters requiring extreme bandwidth density between top-of-rack switches.

An optical module capable of transmitting 1.6 terabits of data per second, the current frontier for high-speed connections between AI accelerators and network switches inside hyperscale data centers. Successor to 800G modules; requires advanced indium phosphide lasers, silicon photonics integration, and co-packaged optics engineering to achieve the bandwidth density at acceptable power and cost.

A prearranged stock-sale programme that allows corporate insiders to sell shares without running afoul of insider-trading laws. Under SEC Rule 10b-5, insiders must establish the plan at a time when they hold no material non-public information; sales then execute automatically according to the preset schedule. The plan provides an affirmative defence against insider-trading allegations, even if the insider later acquires material information before any individual trade executes.

Also called NTM (Next Twelve Months) earnings per share, this is a rolling consensus estimate of what a company or index’s constituents will earn over the next twelve months. It blends current- and next-fiscal-year analyst estimates weighted by where you are in the fiscal year. Because stock markets discount future profits rather than past ones, forward earnings are the standard denominator for price-to-earnings ratios used in valuation comparisons — and the right metric for detecting whether prices have run ahead of what analysts expect companies actually to earn.

The aggregate market consensus on what a company or index will earn per share over the coming twelve months, compiled from analyst forecasts. It is a forward-looking valuation input — rising forward EPS can compress price-to-earnings multiples even as a stock price rises, making a market look cheaper on a forward basis than a trailing basis.

Quarterly SEC disclosures required from institutional investment managers holding more than $100 million in qualifying equity assets. 13Fs reveal which funds hold which stocks, but are filed 45 days after quarter-end, making them a lagging indicator of institutional positioning.

When a fund holds call options on a stock and exercises them to receive the underlying shares, the position type changes from 'call' to 'SH' (shares held) in the subsequent 13F filing. Outside observers parsing the filing may interpret this shift as a new long position being opened, when it actually represents a conversion of an existing derivative into direct equity — no net new capital deployed.

A chart in which each candlestick or bar represents 15 minutes of price action, compressing a full trading day into roughly 30 bars for equity markets and more for 24-hour FX markets. Popular among intraday and day traders for its balance between signal frequency and noise — coarser than 1- or 5-minute charts, finer than hourly views. The timeframe does not change the fundamental properties of the indicators applied to it; a lagging indicator on a 15-minute chart is still lagging.

Intel’s most advanced chip manufacturing technology, using backside power delivery and RibbonFET gate-all-around transistors. The “18A” designation refers to an effective transistor feature size measured in angstroms (tenths of a nanometer). It competes directly with TSMC’s N2 node for advanced chip manufacturing contracts.

An advanced packaging method in which chips are placed side by side on a dense silicon interposer and connected by very short wires. The 2.5D label distinguishes it from full 3D stacking (chips on top of each other) while offering much shorter interconnects than conventional board-level assembly. This approach is used to combine HBM stacks with AI processor dies in products like NVIDIA's H100.

The average closing price of a security over the previous 200 trading sessions, roughly one calendar year. It is widely used as a long-term trend benchmark; the proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their own 200 DMAs is a standard gauge of how broadly a bull market is supported.

A technical indicator calculated as the arithmetic average of an asset's closing prices over the previous 200 trading sessions (roughly ten calendar months). It smooths short-term noise and is widely used to distinguish bullish regimes (price above the average) from bearish ones (price below). In the Gayed/Bilello framework, the 200-DMA serves not as a trading signal per se but as a proxy for the volatility regime: markets trading above it tend to exhibit lower forward volatility and longer positive return streaks, conditions favorable to leveraged exposure.

An out-of-the-money call option whose delta — its sensitivity to the underlying stock price — is approximately 0.25, implying roughly a 25% probability of finishing in-the-money. The 25-delta call is the global options market's standard reference point for measuring how much premium buyers will pay for upside exposure beyond the current stock price.

Options whose price changes by 25 cents for every $1 move in the underlying — roughly equivalent to being about 5–8% out-of-the-money for typical index options. The 25-delta strike is the standard reference for measuring volatility skew because it captures meaningful tail exposure while remaining liquid enough to trade reliably.

A standard skew measure: the difference in implied volatility between a 25-delta put and a 25-delta call at the same expiry. A 25-delta option has roughly a 25% probability of finishing in the money, placing it approximately 10–15% out of the money for a 3-month tenor on a large index. When this measure is near zero or inverted (calls more expensive than puts), the market is pricing upside risk more heavily than downside.

A variant of 3DGS (SIGGRAPH 2024) that replaces volumetric 3D ellipsoids with thin oriented planar disks. Because each disk lies in a plane, it carries a well-defined invertible local 2D coordinate system — a property 3DGS lacks. This makes geometry more surface-consistent and, in the Neural Gabor paper, provides the (u, v) coordinate input that the per-primitive neural network needs.

The original generation of NAND flash in which memory cells are arranged in a single flat layer on a silicon wafer. Lower density than 3D NAND but offers higher endurance per cell and simpler manufacturing qualification — properties that made it the preferred choice for industrial, automotive, and embedded applications.

A standardized yield calculation mandated by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for bond funds, reflecting income generated over the most recent 30-day period annualized. It provides a more current snapshot of a fund’s income than the trailing 12-month yield, and is the standard basis for comparing ETF and mutual fund payouts.

The industry-standard substrate diameter for leading-edge semiconductor fabrication. Larger wafers yield more chips per production run, reducing unit cost; all advanced AI processors at sub-7nm nodes are fabricated exclusively on 300mm wafers. Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO together supply roughly 55% of global 300mm wafer output.

The subfield of computer vision concerned with recovering three-dimensional structure and geometry from images or video — including depth estimation, camera-pose recovery, and scene mapping. Its methods range from classical feature-matching pipelines to modern neural networks.

A NAND flash architecture that stacks memory cells vertically in dozens of layers, dramatically increasing storage density and reducing cost per bit compared to 2D NAND. Now the mainstream technology in consumer and enterprise SSDs, though write endurance can be inferior in demanding industrial workloads.

A process that captures the shape of a physical object and converts it into a three-dimensional digital mesh. Common methods include photogrammetry (using many photographs) and structured-light or LiDAR scanning. The resulting mesh can be imported into game engines or animation tools.

A neural encoder-decoder that compresses video along both spatial dimensions (height, width) and the temporal dimension (frame sequence) into a compact latent representation. Working in this compressed space dramatically reduces the computation needed at inference time, which is why it is critical for achieving real-time generation speeds.

Vicor's proprietary three-dimensional chip-stacking and packaging process used to manufacture its power modules. Rather than assembling components on a flat substrate, 3Di stacks power-conversion elements vertically, enabling the high current density and thin form factor that vertical power delivery requires. Vicor operates its 3Di process at its Andover, Massachusetts fab, which the company owns outright — an unusual degree of vertical integration for a semiconductor firm of its size.

A technique that compresses each model weight from 16 or 32 bits down to 4 bits, reducing memory footprint by roughly 75 percent at the cost of a small quality degradation. It allows large models that would otherwise require a high-end GPU to run on consumer hardware with 8–16GB of VRAM.

A contemporary belief that A4 = 432 Hz is a 'natural,' 'divine,' or cosmically sanctioned pitch standard, superior to the current ISO standard of 440 Hz. Proponents cite ancient civilizations, Verdi, and sacred geometry as evidence. The claims are not supported by musicology, acoustics, or controlled clinical studies, and the premise that ancient cultures tuned to a specific Hz value is impossible — the hertz depends on a precise definition of the second that did not exist until the 20th century.

An extension of 3DGS that adds a time dimension, enabling reconstruction and real-time playback of dynamic scenes. Approaches vary: some attach a neural deformation field that warps a static Gaussian cloud each frame; others treat time as a fourth axis of a true four-dimensional primitive.

The task of building a model of a scene in three spatial dimensions plus time, capturing not just what a place looks like but how it changes as objects move through it. The '4D' distinguishes this from static 3D reconstruction, which models only a single frozen moment.

An extension of spherical harmonics to four dimensions (three spatial plus one temporal), introduced by Yang et al. at ICLR 2024 to model appearance that varies simultaneously with both the viewer’s direction and the moment in time. The name blends “spheri-” and “-cylindrical” basis functions.

One of the principal serotonin receptor subtypes in the brain, concentrated on neurons in the prefrontal cortex and striatum. It governs mood, impulse control, and perception. Psychedelics such as LSD and psilocybin activate it; drugs that block it (antagonists) reverse those effects and modulate compulsive behaviour circuits.

The average closing price of a security over the previous 50 trading sessions, roughly one quarter. It serves as a medium-term trend indicator and is more responsive to recent price action than the 200 DMA. Analysts watch the percentage of index members above their 50 DMA as a near-term pulse on market participation.

A standard institutional asset allocation holding 60% equities and 40% bonds. It has been the dominant model for balanced and pension funds for decades, producing reliable real returns during low-inflation periods — but, as this paper shows, reliably negative real returns during inflation shocks.

A data-rate standard for optical transceivers running at 800 gigabits per second, typically achieved by combining eight 100G lanes. Dominant in new hyperscale AI data-centre deployments as of 2025–2026. The next tier, 1.6T (1.6 terabits per second), began commercial deployment in 2025.

Successive generations of optical-interconnect data rates, expressed in gigabits or terabits per second per port. AI clusters are migrating from 400G to 800G and into 1.6T to keep up with bandwidth between GPUs.

An 800-volt direct-current power bus standard adopted in next-generation electric vehicles and AI datacenters. In EVs it enables faster charging and lighter cabling; in datacenters it reduces conversion losses from utility power to the GPU rail. It requires wide-bandgap semiconductors (SiC or GaN) that can safely switch at these voltages, which is why it creates a structural demand tailwind for suppliers like STMicroelectronics.

A widely used retail technical-analysis strategy that generates a buy signal when the 9-period exponential moving average — a price average that weights recent data more heavily — crosses above the 21-period EMA, and a sell signal on the reverse. Often paired with the 200-week moving average as a long-term trend filter.

A CSS at-rule that registers a custom typeface for use on a web page, specifying the font’s name and the URL from which the browser should fetch the font file. Every web font in use today is declared through a @font-face block in a stylesheet; those URLs are plainly readable in browser developer tools and page source, making them accessible to any script that fetches the page.

Seedance 2.0’s mechanism for maintaining visual and audio consistency across generated shots. Users upload reference images, clips, or audio to anchor the model’s output, so the same character appearance, visual style, or voice persists throughout a multi-shot sequence.

A wave that breaks symmetrically in both directions from a central peak, forming an A-shape as seen from the shore. Common at reef and sandbar breaks; offers surfers the choice to ride left or right from the same takeoff point.

A correction step applied during skeleton retargeting when the source and target skeletons were posed differently at rig time. A T-Pose has arms extended horizontally; an A-Pose has arms angled downward at roughly 45 degrees. If both rigs share the same pose, animation transfers cleanly; if they differ, a per-bone correction matrix must be applied to every frame to prevent shoulder offsets and other artifacts in the exported animation.

A share of a company listed on the Shanghai or Shenzhen stock exchanges, denominated in Chinese renminbi and historically restricted to domestic investors. Foreign investors can access A-shares through specific programmes (QFII licences or the Hong Kong–Mainland Stock Connect), but many STAR Market companies are not covered by Connect, making US-listed ETFs like KSTR one of the few indirect routes for offshore investors.

An open standard proposed by Alphabet's Google in 2026 for agent-driven interfaces. Rather than generating raw pixels or arbitrary code, AI agents compose interfaces by selecting from a catalog of pre-declared JSON components that host applications render natively, preserving accessibility, security, and semantic structure.

A proprietary text-shortening format developed for MemPalace that uses regex entity detection and sentence-importance scoring to produce structured English abbreviations (e.g., ‘PRI(lead) | KAI(backend,3yr)’). Marketed at launch as 30× lossless compression; subsequently acknowledged by the creators to be lossy summarization, with measurable recall degradation.

The multi-layer organic packaging structure that electrically connects a processor die to the printed circuit board beneath it. ABF substrates are the primary packaging medium for high-end CPUs and GPUs; their production requires specialised film from Ajinomoto Fine-Techno and precision lamination by a small number of Japanese and Taiwanese firms including Ibiden and Unimicron.

The standard metric for evaluating camera-pose estimation in 3D reconstruction: it measures the root-mean-square distance between predicted camera positions and ground-truth positions, after optimal rigid alignment. Lower values indicate less drift. Particularly sensitive to long-sequence performance.

Brian Roemmele's term for the roughly 5,000-day period from late 2025 to 2039, during which he argues AI and robotics will decouple human labor from the requirement of economic survival. The 'interregnum' framing suggests a gap between two stable orders — the wage-labor era and whatever replaces it — during which old institutions (tax codes, labor law, corporate IP rights) will collide violently with new technological realities.

A private art school founded in Paris in 1867 by Rodolphe Julian. Unlike the state-run École des Beaux-Arts, it admitted women and foreign students from its founding and became one of Europe's most prestigious fine-art training grounds, drawing students from across the world well into the twentieth century.

A loose philosophical position most associated with Nick Land holding that the pressures of capitalism or technology should be intensified rather than managed or reversed. It has left and right variants; Land's version tends toward the nihilistic and anti-democratic, drawing on cybernetics and continental philosophy.

A structured, semantic representation of a web page derived from the browser’s accessibility tree — the same data screen readers use. Far more compact than raw HTML or a screenshot while still giving an AI agent enough information to locate and interact with page elements.

A type of stone tool produced by early humans — particularly Homo erectus and archaic Homo sapiens — over a span of roughly 1.7 million to 100,000 years ago. Regarded as one of the earliest examples of sophisticated and consistent human technological design. Roon invokes it to place GPT in a long lineage of admired but purely instrumental human tools: supremely refined objects of craftsmanship, not objects of reverence.

A model developed by researchers at the New York Federal Reserve that decomposes Treasury yields into two components: an expectations part (the market’s forecast of future short-term rates) and a term premium part (compensation for duration and inflation risk). It is a widely cited reference for determining whether a move in long-term yields is being driven by monetary policy expectations or by supply, demand, and risk-compensation dynamics that the Fed does not directly control.

The Association for Computing Machinery's highest honor in computer science, often called the Nobel Prize of computing. Awarded annually since 1966 for lasting technical contributions to the field. Hamming received it in 1968, as only the third-ever recipient.

Encoding user inputs — keystrokes, mouse movements — directly into a generative model's prediction process at each frame step. This lets the model respond frame by frame to player actions rather than generating full clips in advance and adjusting course between them.

The electrical signal that travels along a neuron’s axon when it fires. A wave of ion exchange propagates from the cell body to the axon terminal, where it triggers the release of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. It is the basic unit of neural communication.

A class of predictive model that takes not just the current state but also a chosen action as inputs when forecasting the next state. The 'action conditioning' is what allows the model to respond differently to 'walk forward' versus 'turn left,' making interactivity possible rather than generating a fixed video stream.

A phrase from the enterprise analytics lexicon meaning data-derived findings intended to guide specific decisions, as opposed to observations that are merely interesting. The compound has been criticized since at least 2010 as a hollow buzzword: in practice it tends to mean whatever the speaker wants the data to support.

The numerical output of a neuron or layer given a specific input. Activations are the intermediate representations a network computes as it transforms input into output. In interpretability research they are the raw signal to be decoded — analogous to the source language in Sutskever's NMT framing.

A visualization technique that collects millions of example activations from a neural network layer, projects them into two dimensions, and renders averaged feature visualizations across the resulting map. The output is a global geographic survey of the concepts a network layer has learned, showing how they cluster and relate to one another.

In FreeTimeGS, a learnable pair of timestamps (start, end) attached to each Gaussian primitive. A primitive only contributes to rendered frames within its interval, allowing the model to represent objects that enter or leave a scene without forcing every primitive to span the entire capture duration.

A visualisation of which regions of the brain show elevated activity in response to a particular input. In the TRIBE v2 context, an activation map shows which cortical areas are predicted to fire strongly while a viewer watches a specific video — the basis for the community’s content-optimisation interpretations.

A precursor interpretability technique developed by Adam Karvonen, Samuel Marks, and colleagues at Anthropic that trains a language model to accept neural activations as inputs and answer arbitrary natural-language questions about them. The activation verbalizer used in Claude Mythos Preview evaluation builds directly on this framework.

The high-dimensional vector space formed by all possible activation values at a given layer of a neural network. Each input to the network corresponds to a point in this space, and the geometric structure of that space — which points cluster together, which lie along curves — reveals how the network has organized its internal representations.

An interpretability method that translates a neural network's internal activation vectors into natural-language descriptions, making the model's computational state directly readable. Anthropic's version runs a secondary language model over Sparse Autoencoder features from the primary model, operating token by token during generation to expose the model's internal reasoning in parallel with its outputs.

Microsoft's enterprise directory service, used by most large organisations to manage user identities and access permissions across networked computers. Compromising Active Directory typically gives an attacker control over any user account or machine on the corporate network, making it a central objective in advanced intrusions.

A computational neuroscience framework (developed by Karl Friston) in which the brain generates predictions about incoming sensory signals and updates its models when predictions fail, while also acting on the world to make the environment match its expectations. Perception, cognition, and action are unified under a single principle: minimizing 'free energy' (roughly, prediction error or surprise). Laukkonen's empirical research applies this framework to meditation and the structure of meaningful experience.

A sub-pipeline that identifies which face in a multi-person video frame corresponds to the voice currently heard in the audio track. Without it, a lipsync model applied to a dialogue scene would incorrectly modify every visible face simultaneously. Sync Labs' implementation — named ASD-1 — is used across their model family and handles interruptions and overlapping speech.

A concept from Carl Rogers' person-centered psychology: the innate biological and psychological drive toward growth, development, and the full realization of one's potential. Rogers argued this tendency operates naturally when the environment is supportive and when a person acts congruently with their inner experience, but is inhibited when external pressures require a performed self that diverges from the real one.

The electromechanical joint that converts electrical power into mechanical motion at each degree of freedom in a robot. A full-size humanoid typically requires 28 or more structural actuators, each combining a motor, gearbox, and sensors to close the control loop.

The growth strategy used in 3DGS training: primitives where the rendered image gradient is large (indicating underfitting) are cloned or split into smaller, denser primitives. This is effective for smooth regions but causes exponential primitive proliferation on fine-textured surfaces, where every color boundary triggers a split.

A technique in which a scraper learns which HTML elements contain target data — and can relocate them automatically if a website updates its layout. Traditional scrapers break when a site redesigns its HTML; adaptive scrapers adjust without manual intervention, reducing ongoing maintenance.

The bundle of automotive features—adaptive cruise, lane-keeping, automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, parking assist—that sit between a fully manual car and a fully autonomous one. Each feature is silicon-hungry, which is why ADAS is the fastest-growing slice of automotive semiconductor demand.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation, further adjusted for stock-based compensation and one-time charges. IT services companies use it as a proxy for cash-generative operating performance; analysts track it closely because these firms carry significant amortisation from acquisitions.

A school of Hindu philosophy associated with Adi Shankara (8th century CE). "Advaita" means non-dual. It holds that ultimate reality (Brahman) is a single, undivided consciousness, and that the apparent multiplicity of selves and world is maya (illusion). The individual self (atman) is, at bottom, identical with Brahman.

In equity cases — those seeking remedies like injunctions or disgorgement rather than simple money damages — a jury's finding is advisory rather than binding. The judge may accept, reject, or modify it. In Musk v. Altman, Judge Gonzalez Rogers will issue her own ruling regardless of what the jury decides.

Planting trees on land that has not previously been forested, or that has been without forest cover for a very long time. It differs from reforestation, which restores forests where they recently existed. In desert-reclamation contexts the two terms are often used loosely and interchangeably.

Agency here means the degree of freedom a person has to choose what to work on, when, and how. It is distinct from simply having free time — a full calendar of someone else's priorities leaves no agency. Researchers in motivation (particularly in self-determination theory) treat autonomy as one of the three core psychological needs alongside competence and relatedness.

In the A2A protocol, JSON files that an AI agent publishes to advertise its capabilities, accepted input formats, and communication endpoints — analogous to a business card for machine-to-machine discovery.

The discipline of designing APIs and platform surfaces so that AI agents — rather than human developers — can discover, understand, and operate them reliably. AX is positioned as a superset of developer experience (DX): everything DX requires, plus machine-readable structure, unambiguous error signals, and support for autonomous decision-making without human clarification.

A configuration framework that wraps and structures an AI agent's behaviour — defining what subagents it can delegate to, what reusable workflows it can call, and how it should behave before and after each action. A harness does not replace the underlying model; it constrains and directs how that model is used.

The practice of coordinating multiple AI agents so they hand tasks to one another in a defined sequence or in parallel, with one agent's output becoming another's input. Orchestration handles routing logic, error recovery, and result aggregation that a single model could not manage alone.
