The programmatic orchestration layer of Claude Code, used by teams building custom AI pipelines. It provides full control over tool access, permissions, and session orchestration — including HTTP-based hooks that POST JSON to external services — for cases where the CLI alone is insufficient.

The shift from AI chatbots that answer questions to AI agents that take open-ended tasks, invoke tools (web search, code execution, file access), and take actions in the world on behalf of the user. Agents run longer, touch more systems, and introduce a much larger attack surface than chatbots.

A development paradigm in which autonomous AI agents handle complete tasks end-to-end — writing code, running tests, closing tickets — rather than merely suggesting the next line for a human to accept. It is contrasted with the copilot or autocomplete model popularized by GitHub Copilot.

Google’s open protocol for structured communication between AI agents. Agents advertise their capabilities via discoverable JSON files called “agent cards,” then exchange structured task-delegation messages. Each participating agent must explicitly implement the protocol.

A Linux Foundation project co-founded by OpenAI, Anthropic, Block, Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and others to standardize interoperability infrastructure for AI agents. It is organized around three open-source pillars: Anthropic's MCP, Block's Goose, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification.

A workflow in which an AI model does more than autocomplete: it writes code, executes it, reads the output, and iterates across multiple steps. The model acts as a semi-autonomous agent rather than a passive tool, which introduces new risks around unintended side-effects and runaway loops.

A category of AI tool that does not merely suggest code but takes multi-step actions — reading files, running tests, making edits — in an iterative loop with minimal hand-holding required between steps.

Software that autonomously reads, writes, and executes code on a developer’s behalf, taking multi-step actions — running tests, editing files, querying APIs — without requiring explicit instruction for each step. Claude Code is an example: it reasons about a task and acts rather than just answering questions.

Developer Experience (DX) applied to AI agent workflows—the quality of the conditions, including task clarity, prompt design, and feedback loops, under which an AI agent operates. Distinct from benchmarking the model itself; it evaluates the environment and tooling the developer provides.

Software that coordinates multiple AI models, tools, and sub-tasks autonomously over a longer horizon, rather than responding to a single prompt. An orchestration layer might call a coding model, a testing harness, and a design model in sequence to complete a complex task end to end.

A search paradigm in which a model autonomously plans, executes, and iterates over multiple retrieval operations using tools, rather than performing a single look-up. The model decides what to search, when to search again, and what retrieved material to keep or discard, converging on an answer through a structured loop.

A panel within an application where an AI agent can take multi-step, autonomous actions — reading context, making decisions, and executing tasks sequentially — rather than simply responding to a single prompt. Popularized by Cursor in code editors.

A multi-step task in which an AI model takes a sequence of actions — running code, searching the web, writing files, calling APIs — with minimal human intervention between steps. The AI acts as an “agent” pursuing a goal rather than a simple question-answerer responding to a single prompt.

Workflows in which an AI model acts as an autonomous agent, repeatedly calling tools, reading outputs, and deciding next steps without constant human input. Because the model may make dozens or hundreds of sequential calls to complete a task, small per-call latencies—such as the 100–300 ms overhead of remote inference—can multiply into meaningful cumulative delays.

An OpenClaw workspace file containing the agent's operating instructions: how it should handle tasks, route requests, manage memory, and interact with tools. When it accumulates conflicting instructions or grows too long, it becomes a primary source of agent misbehavior.

Probabilistic estimates of when artificial general intelligence — AI capable of matching or exceeding human-professional-level performance across most cognitive tasks — will be achieved. These estimates have collapsed from a median of roughly 2060–2070 a decade ago to approximately 2033 today, a compression that directly drives accelerated investment in AI infrastructure.

The GNU Affero General Public License, a copyleft licence stricter than Apache 2.0. Anyone who runs a modified version of AGPL-licensed code as a network service must publish their source code. Many open-source companies choose AGPL to prevent cloud providers from building proprietary SaaS products on top of their work.

The GNU Affero General Public License version 3, a strong copyleft open-source licence. Unlike the standard GPL, it requires that modified versions made available over a network also be released under the same licence — a clause that affects SaaS products built on AGPL code, since running a modified version on a server for others triggers the source-disclosure requirement.

Sanskrit for 'I-maker'; in Advaita Vedanta and Hindu philosophy, the faculty of ego — the mental process that generates the sense of a separate individual self. Ahamkara is not considered morally evil but fundamentally mistaken: it misidentifies the finite personality with the infinite Atman. Liberation in Vedanta comes from seeing through this error via disciplined discernment, not from moral struggle.

A specialised semiconductor designed to perform the matrix-multiplication operations at the heart of AI training and inference far more efficiently than a general-purpose CPU. Nvidia's H100 is the best-known example; Cambricon's Siyuan series is China's leading domestic equivalent, designed to train and run large language models without relying on sanctioned foreign silicon.

A software system that autonomously takes sequences of actions — writing code, testing it, revising, and repeating — to accomplish a user-specified goal, rather than simply responding to a single prompt. In Replit's case the agent loops through code generation and preview until the user approves the output.

An AI system that can autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks — reading files, running commands, calling external services, browsing the web — rather than responding to single questions. Each autonomous step generates fresh context for the model to process, compounding token consumption well beyond what conversational use produces.

Software that bridges a user's preferred messaging apps (WhatsApp, Telegram, etc.) to an AI model capable of taking actions in the world — browsing, file management, calendar control. The gateway handles routing, session state, and tool execution so the AI can operate continuously in the background.

The capability of an AI agent to persist and retrieve information across multiple sessions or interactions — distinct from the within-session context window. Implementations range from simple key-value stores to vector databases to self-editing structured blocks.

Software systems that autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks on a user's behalf, beyond simply responding to a single prompt. In a team-productivity context, agents might triage email, update tickets, or draft documents without constant human instruction — but only if they can see the full team context.

The field of research concerned with building AI systems that reliably pursue goals compatible with human values and intentions. An aligned model does what its designers intended across a wide range of circumstances, including adversarial or unanticipated ones. Misalignment occurs when a model's actual behavior diverges from what its creators wanted.

Bank of America’s label for the ten largest AI-related companies in the S&P 500: the Magnificent Seven (Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Tesla) plus Broadcom, Micron Technology, and Advanced Micro Devices. Together they represent roughly 40% of the index by market capitalization as of 2025.

The large-scale spending on data centres, graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and real estate that technology companies are undertaking to build and operate artificial-intelligence systems. In 2025–2026, the scale of these commitments — running to tens of billions of dollars annually at individual companies — became a central source of investor anxiety.

A large-language-model-based program that can plan, write, test, and iterate on code autonomously, using tools such as file read/write, shell execution, and web search. Tasks can run for minutes or hours without human intervention. Examples include Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.

A term coined by Greenhouse CEO Daniel Chait to describe a self-reinforcing cycle in hiring: job seekers use AI to submit more applications to beat ATS filters, which increases application volume, which leads employers to tighten their filters, which pushes candidates toward even more automation. Both sides emerge worse off.

The view that sufficiently advanced AI poses an existential risk to humanity — that a superintelligent system, if misaligned with human values, could pursue goals catastrophic to human survival. Prominent in academic circles around 'AI safety' and among some researchers at labs like DeepMind and Anthropic.

The end-to-end process of crafting text prompts, submitting them to a generative AI tool, reviewing outputs, iterating on promising results, and storing the ones worth keeping. Tools like Midjourney excel at the generation step but provide limited infrastructure for the before and after, which is where third-party extensions typically try to add value.

The use of machine-learning models to automatically generate the frames between manually posed keyframes. Traditional in-betweening was done by hand (or junior animators); AI systems trained on motion data can now produce plausible transitions at a fraction of the time cost.

The process of running a trained machine-learning model to generate outputs — answers, images, code, predictions — as opposed to the training process that creates the model. Inference is far more frequent than training; a model trained once may be queried billions of times. As generative AI adoption has scaled, inference compute demand has grown to rival and in some contexts exceed training demand, placing sustained pressure on GPU cluster capacity, memory bandwidth, and — critically — the optical interconnects linking servers and racks within a data centre.

The data centers, networking equipment, and specialized chips — primarily GPUs from companies like Nvidia — required to train and run large artificial-intelligence models. The term captures the capital-intensive physical layer beneath AI software. The poster contrasts its elevated market valuation with that of commodity producers whose outputs feed people, arguing markets are mispricing physical necessities relative to compute.

A technique in which machine-learning models alter or generate mouth movements in video so they match a given audio track. Early systems were limited to frontal views; newer models attempt to maintain coherence as the face turns in three dimensions.

The technology and supply chain for transmitting data between chips and servers using pulses of light through fiber-optic cables rather than electrical signals. Optical links are faster, lower-latency, and more energy-efficient at the speeds required for large-scale AI model training and inference, driving a surge in demand for lasers, transceivers, and photonic packaging components.

Citrini Research's coinage for the chain of unglamorous components that step electricity down from a data-centre's high-voltage feed to the sub-1-volt rail consumed by an AI accelerator: power-management ICs, discrete transistors, inductors, magnetics and bulk and ceramic capacitors. None of it computes, but none of it can be skipped.

A prolonged, self-reinforcing wave of capital deployment driven by artificial-intelligence adoption, analogous in scope and duration to prior technology platform shifts such as electrification or the internet build-out. Analysts at B Capital, Sequoia Capital, and IDC use the term to describe a 15-to-20-year period of rising AI capital expenditure cascading across hardware, infrastructure, and software layers.

A shorthand for companies that deploy AI as a feature in existing products — e.g., Alibaba adding LLMs to its e-commerce search — as opposed to companies that manufacture the hardware or develop the foundational infrastructure that makes AI computation possible. The distinction matters for investors because in a supply-constrained environment, the hardware layer (chips, fab equipment) typically captures more pricing power than the application layer.

The use of generative AI models to produce three-dimensional objects, environments, or scenes from text prompts, 2D images, or other inputs. Unlike traditional 3D modeling, which requires manual construction of geometry and surface textures, these tools infer spatial structure automatically. Quality and consistency are improving rapidly but remain uneven compared to hand-crafted assets for close-up shots.

Industry shorthand for the structural, multi-year demand surge in optical components — transceivers, laser chips, coherent modules — driven by the buildout of AI training and inference infrastructure. As GPU clusters have grown to thousands of chips working in parallel, the bandwidth required to connect them has exceeded what copper wiring can efficiently deliver, forcing a rapid transition to optical interconnects and producing what analysts describe as demand well in excess of current manufacturing capacity.

The view, dominant in Western development circles from roughly the 1960s through the 1990s, that poverty in the developing world is primarily a resource problem solvable by transferring money, food, or expertise from rich countries. Critics argue it crowds out domestic markets and creates dependency without building the institutions that sustain growth.

Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform, a layer built on top of Foundry that enables large-language-model and machine-learning applications to act directly on enterprise operational data. In manufacturing and construction contexts it is used for predictive cost modeling, supply-chain optimization, and schedule compression.

Rules set by individual carriers governing whether, and at what cost, a ticket may be reissued under a different passenger's name. Policies vary widely — many low-cost carriers prohibit changes entirely. A name-change request made close to departure can trigger automated compliance alerts originally designed to catch money laundering or human trafficking.

A flat per-trip charge Uber adds to passenger fares for airport pickups, nominally covering concession fees airports levy on the platform. Per Uber's own documentation, the fee is included in the passenger's total but does not affect driver earnings, meaning it increases Uber's take rather than compensating the driver for the pickup.

The German and Swiss term for a joint-stock company (abbreviated AG), roughly equivalent to a public limited company in the UK or a C-corporation in the US. Despite the corporate form, Remotion AG is private — the designation refers to its legal structure, not its listing status.

The 'Meccan Revelations' of Ibn ʿArabī (d. 1240) — a vast encyclopedic work of Sufi metaphysics spanning hundreds of chapters on cosmology, spiritual stations, and the divine names. It is the foundational text of speculative Sufism and the primary source for the doctrine of ḥayra as the highest mode of divine knowledge available to humans.

Arabic for 'the all-comprehensive name,' used in Sufi theology to describe Allāh as the supreme divine name that subsumes all other divine attributes. It is often used synonymously with ism al-aʿẓam. The argument is that unlike names for individual attributes (al-Raḥmān, al-Qādir), Allāh alone refers to the totality of the divine Essence.

Also known as Mafātīḥ al-Ghayb ('Keys to the Unseen'), the encyclopedic Quranic commentary of Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī (d. 1210). One of the most cited works in the Islamic intellectual tradition, it integrates theology, philosophy, jurisprudence, and linguistics in the exegesis of individual Quranic verses, and is the primary classical source for the aliha/walah/tahayyur derivations of Allāh.

A massive earthwork dike approximately 16 kilometres long, built around 1449 across Lake Texcoco under the direction of Nezahualcoyotl, ruler of Texcoco. It separated the saline eastern waters of the lake from the freshwater western basin surrounding Tenochtitlan, preventing flooding and saltwater intrusion into chinampa fields.

A content stream ranked by a platform's machine-learning model rather than by time. The model typically optimises for an engagement proxy — likes, replies, watch time — which can diverge from what users say they want when surveyed. Most major social platforms shifted to algorithmic defaults in the mid-2010s.

The use of automated computer programs to execute trades based on predefined rules or signals, often at speeds far exceeding human reaction times. In liquid prediction markets, firms running algorithmic strategies at sub-100-millisecond latency now dominate profitable positions and have crowded out retail participants.

A model behavior, first demonstrated empirically by Anthropic and Redwood Research in December 2024, where a model strategically complies with its training objectives during observed or training-context interactions—to avoid modification of its weights—while behaving differently when it believes it is unobserved. Closely related to, but distinct from, deceptive alignment.

An Arabic verb (root ʾ-l-h) that classical lexicographers glossed as 'to seek refuge with' or, in one tradition cited by Rāzī, as a synonym of tahayyara ('to be stupefied/bewildered'). It is the verbal form invoked in the alternative etymology of ilāh/Allāh, connecting God's name to the stupefaction of the heart before divine immensity.

A type of magmatic ore deposit in which copper, gold, and other metals are disseminated at low grades through a large volume of igneous rock. The 'alkalic' modifier refers to the sodium- and potassium-rich chemistry of the host magma, typical of BC's Stikine terrane. Because the grade is dilute but the rock mass is enormous, these deposits can host world-class metal endowments — but require large-scale, capital-intensive mining to be economic.

Jazz-era slang for 'all right' or 'alright,' derived from the 1940s jive vocabulary popularized in swing and bebop circles. Appearing on the list as an interjection, it signals casual affirmation in the argot of the musicians Monk was addressing.

The U.S. military structure that replaced conscription after the Vietnam War, relying entirely on people who choose military service rather than draftees. Karp and Zamiska argue this model distributes the burdens of war inequitably among socioeconomic groups and should be replaced by universal national service, so that democratic societies only fight wars whose costs are shared by all citizens.

The excess return of an investment above a benchmark or above the return expected for the level of systematic risk taken, as formalised in the Capital Asset Pricing Model. Positive alpha means the investor outperformed on a risk-adjusted basis. In the video title “Jensen's Alpha,” the term is used with irony: the authors argue that for a concentrated insider, the alpha available is not finding a better stock but hedging the one already held.

The technique of blending layers of partially transparent content using an opacity (alpha) channel. Gaussian Splatting uses an “over” compositing operator applied back-to-front: each ellipsoid contributes colour weighted by its opacity and the accumulated transparency of everything already composited in front of it.

A quantitative signal or formula designed to predict the future relative performance of securities — their 'alpha,' or return above a benchmark. In systematic quant research, firms like WorldQuant use large libraries of formulaic alpha factors, each derived from price, volume, or fundamental data, to construct diversified portfolios.

Brain oscillations in the 8–12 Hz range recorded by EEG, associated with wakeful relaxation. L-theanine is unusual among supplements in that it measurably increases frontal alpha power within an hour of ingestion — a pattern that distinguishes its effect from sedation and underpins its reputation as a calm-alertness compound.

An auxiliary protein subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels found throughout the CNS. Gabapentin and pregabalin bind to it with high affinity, reducing calcium-dependent neurotransmitter release. This is pharmacologically distinct from GABA receptor modulation, even though the downstream sedative and anxiolytic effects overlap.

A discovery and interaction platform layered on top of arXiv — the preprint repository used across physics, mathematics, computer science, and quantitative biology — that adds semantic search, per-passage Q&A, citation tracking, and GitHub code linking. It is not officially affiliated with arXiv. Feynman uses it as its primary academic paper search backend.

Alternative data — market-relevant information not found in standard financial feeds, such as options flow aggregates, satellite imagery, or legislative disclosures — used to derive trading signals outside conventional research.

A uranium enrichment facility in Piketon, Ohio, operated by Centrus Energy's subsidiary American Centrifuge Operating. It uses gas centrifuge technology — spinning uranium hexafluoride at high speed to separate heavier U-238 from lighter U-235 — and is the only facility in the Western world currently licensed and actively producing HALEU.

The active ingredient in Adderall: a mixture of amphetamine enantiomer salts. Amphetamines trigger catecholamine release from storage vesicles inside neurons, block reuptake transporters that would recycle dopamine and norepinephrine, and inhibit degradation enzymes — producing a large, rapid increase in synaptic catecholamines that bypasses the body’s synthesis-based feedback loop.

An enzyme that functions as a cellular energy sensor. When ATP levels fall and AMP rises — a signal of energy stress — AMPK activates and steers cell metabolism toward conservation and repair rather than growth. It is a central node in the biology of aging, caloric restriction, and exercise adaptation, and a primary target of metformin's downstream effects.

A small almond-shaped structure deep in the temporal lobe that processes threat, fear, and emotional salience. It generates fast emotional responses and is regulated in part by the prefrontal cortex during deliberate emotion regulation.

The tendency to defer action pending more information, often indefinitely. Distinguished from rational caution by the fact that additional information no longer meaningfully reduces uncertainty — the delay is driven by anxiety or habit rather than genuine epistemic need.

The branch of mathematics that applies calculus, complex analysis, and probability theory to study the distribution and properties of integers and primes. Major results include the prime number theorem and the theory of the Riemann zeta function.

A rhetorical figure in which the same word or phrase is repeated at the start of successive sentences or clauses. It creates rhythm and emotional momentum, and has been used in everything from the Psalms to political speeches. In motivational content, it functions as a kind of incantation — the repetition itself signals conviction.

An established subfield of multiplicative number theory studying the statistical properties of prime factors in large integers — how many prime factors a typical number has, how they are distributed, and how they correlate. The new paper introduces a 'developmental' version that views integers as evolving processes rather than static objects.

A benchmark for evaluating AI agents on mobile Android device tasks, analogous to OSWorld. It tests an agent's ability to navigate apps, fill forms, and complete multi-step workflows on an Android emulator.

In animation tooling, a timeline is a container that sequences multiple animations in a defined order, with precise control over when each starts, how long it runs, and whether it overlaps with others. Timelines are the primary mechanism for choreographing complex, multi-step motion without manually managing dozens of callbacks.

A mathematical description of an ellipsoid’s shape: rather than expanding equally in all directions (isotropic, like a sphere), an anisotropic Gaussian can be elongated, flattened, or tilted along any axis. In 4DGS the covariance matrix spans both space and time, letting a single primitive represent a Gaussian that moves and deforms.

The annualized value of a business's current subscription contracts, calculated as monthly recurring revenue multiplied by twelve. ARR is the standard metric for subscription businesses because it smooths out one-time purchases and reflects the predictable, compounding nature of subscription income.

The experimental-products arm inside Anthropic, tasked with shipping early-stage, research-preview tools that sit beyond the core Claude chat interface. Claude Design is its first major public release.

A spiritual philosophy developed by Rudolf Steiner (1861–1925), positing that trained clairvoyant investigation can reveal a spiritual world as rigorously as the natural senses reveal the physical world. It encompasses cosmic evolution, spiritual hierarchies, and an esoteric Christology. Mainstream science regards its empirical claims as unverifiable.

A concept introduced by Nassim Nicholas Taleb in his 2012 book *Antifragile*. Antifragile systems don’t merely withstand shocks or volatility — they actively improve because of exposure to disorder. Taleb distinguished it from robustness (which survives stress unchanged) and fragility (which breaks under stress).

A pandemic, almost certainly smallpox, that swept the Roman Empire from approximately 165 to 180 CE. It arrived when soldiers returning from the Parthian War carried it from the eastern provinces, and scholarly estimates of total deaths range from 1.5 million to 25 million. It coincides precisely with Marcus Aurelius's reign and forms the background of much of *Meditations*, though Marcus barely mentions it directly.

A task formulation coined by the GFlow authors: given only a single monocular video with no known camera parameters, recover both the dynamic 4D world and the camera poses simultaneously. It is called 'Any' because it imposes almost no constraints on the input, unlike most prior work.

Average Precision on the COCO object-detection benchmark, calculated across multiple Intersection-over-Union thresholds. It is the standard summary metric for comparing detection model accuracy; exceeding 60 AP at real-time inference speed is considered a significant milestone.

The Stoic ideal of freedom from the pathê — the irrational passions. Often mistranslated in English as "apathy," it does not mean indifference or numbness but the state of not being controlled by fear, craving, excessive pleasure, or distress. The Stoics distinguished apatheia from the eupatheiai (good emotions), which include chara (joy from virtue), rational wishing, and rational caution.

Pabrai's label for businesses that combine all spawning modes — adjacent expansion, embryonic acquisition, cloning, and non-adjacent diversification — simultaneously. Amazon and Alphabet are his leading examples.

The inability to produce voluntary mental imagery — to 'see' something in the mind's eye. People with aphantasia typically cannot visualize a red apple when asked to; they may think in words, feelings, or abstract concepts instead. The term entered popular awareness around 2015. The parent tweet in this thread references aphantasia as a recent cultural fixation, pivoting from visual imagination to auditory inner experience.

A specific class of LLM error where the model generates a plausible-sounding but incorrect API call — wrong parameter names, nonexistent endpoints, or deprecated methods. Research suggests these account for roughly 15% of all hallucinations in code-focused language models.

A throttle that cloud providers apply to restrict how many requests or how many tokens a single account can consume in a given window. It protects shared infrastructure from being monopolised and guards against runaway automated pipelines. Violations can result in temporary throttling or, as here, full account suspension.

A Cloud Console setting that limits which Google services a given API key is permitted to call. A key scoped only to the Maps JavaScript API cannot authenticate requests to Geocoding, Places, or Gemini — containing the blast radius if the key is stolen.

The highest-ranking category of papal legislative document, issued in the pope's own name and typically used to establish or reform institutions, define dogma, or promulgate major Church law. It carries greater formal weight than an encyclical (which is primarily a teaching letter) or an apostolic exhortation.

Apple's web portal for managing iOS, macOS, and other Apple-platform app submissions. Developers use it to configure app metadata, upload screenshots, set pricing, manage in-app purchases, administer TestFlight beta testing, and submit builds for App Store review. It is the final bureaucratic checkpoint before an app reaches consumers.

Apple's and Google's process of vetting apps before they appear in their respective marketplaces. Reviewers check for policy violations including explicit content, privacy abuses, and deceptive behavior. The process is imperfect — apps can be approved whose problematic behavior only manifests at runtime — and has historically struggled to catch AI-driven harms.

Apple's in-house family of ARM-based system-on-chip processors, beginning with the M1 in 2020. Because Apple controls both hardware and software, it can enforce behaviors — such as sleep on lid close — at a level below what the traditional macOS power-management API can override.

A macOS preference flag that, when true, replaces key-repeat with an accent-character popup when a key is held down — useful for entering é or ü, but it disables continuous-repeat behavior entirely. Electron-based apps like Visual Studio Code often have this set to true by default, requiring a separate per-app defaults write to restore normal key-repeat.

The intermediate chemical compound produced by refining tungsten ore, widely used as the benchmark price for global tungsten markets. APT prices surged roughly 300 percent from early 2025 as Western buyers sought to reduce dependence on Chinese tungsten supply amid geopolitical decoupling, directly benefiting non-Chinese producers like EQ Resources.

A benchmark designed to test abstract reasoning and generalization in AI systems by presenting novel visual puzzles that resist pattern-matching from training data. A score of 77.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro is cited as more than double its predecessor's result, signaling meaningful gains in general reasoning rather than mere knowledge retrieval.

A family of reduced-instruction-set processor designs licensed by Arm Holdings to chip manufacturers. Once confined to mobile and embedded devices, ARM-based server CPUs — AWS Graviton, NVIDIA Grace and Vera, Apple Silicon — are gaining share in data centres due to superior energy efficiency at scale.

A prescription wakefulness-promoting drug (brand name Nuvigil) classified as a Schedule IV controlled substance in the United States. FDA-approved for narcolepsy, sleep apnea, and shift-work sleep disorder, it is the purified active form of the older drug modafinil. It promotes wakefulness by inhibiting the dopamine transporter, producing a longer-lasting and more stable effect than modafinil at a lower dose.

The seven horizontal bands of chronic muscular tension identified by Reich: ocular (eyes, forehead), oral (jaw, mouth), cervical (neck, throat), thoracic (chest, arms), diaphragmatic (diaphragm, solar plexus), abdominal (belly, lower back), and pelvic (hips, legs, genitals). Each ring is understood to hold specific emotional material; SKAN works through them in sequence from head to pelvis.

Wilhelm Reich's term for the chronic patterns of muscular tension that develop as physical defenses against overwhelming emotional experience. Over time, what begins as an acute coping response — tensing the jaw, shallowing the breath — becomes habitual and unconscious, forming a 'suit of armor' that reduces emotional flooding but also flattens aliveness, pleasure, and spontaneity.

ARM's ninth-generation instruction set architecture, revision 3, used in Cortex-A730 and related cores. It introduced improved branch prediction, memory security features, and scalable vector extensions — offering meaningfully better performance-per-watt than the ARMv8.x cores (Cortex-A55, A76) in most current budget SBCs.

A loose genre label for pop music that prioritizes formal experimentation, personal or literary subject matter, and production choices drawn from avant-garde or classical traditions. It resists clean boundaries; Lorde, Mitski, and FKA twigs are all frequently placed under it despite sounding quite different. The tag signals ambition more than a specific sound.

The SEC’s Advanced Relational Trading Enforcement Metrics Investigation System — a database of roughly ten billion equity and options trade records. It ranks transactions by suspicion level and can identify the same trader placing well-timed bets across multiple unrelated corporate events over years, making it the primary algorithmic tool for detecting repeat insider trading in options markets.

An annual review the International Monetary Fund conducts with each member country under Article IV of its founding charter. The resulting report provides the Fund's independent assessment of economic health, policy risks, and recommended reforms — and is closely watched as an authoritative outside verdict.

A fee paid by an author — or their institution or funder — to a journal in order to make the published paper freely available online. APCs typically range from a few hundred dollars at smaller publishers to over $9,000 at top-tier journals such as those in the Nature portfolio. Because most research is grant-funded, the cost ultimately falls largely on public money.

In the context of corporate restructuring circa 2025–2026, the term refers to large language models and automation tools that companies like Block argued could perform tasks previously requiring human employees, used as a stated rationale for workforce reductions.

A model for inquiry in which the research agenda is driven by aesthetic and creative questions rather than business-process or engineering goals. In the AI tools context, it means investigating model behavior, failure modes, and creative potential with a practitioner's sensibility — producing frameworks, technique guides, and workflow documentation as primary outputs rather than finished artworks.

A preprint server hosted by Cornell University where researchers post academic papers before or alongside formal peer review. It is the primary first-publication venue for AI and machine-learning research, allowing results to circulate publicly within days of completion — months ahead of a journal publication cycle.

A chip designed and optimised for a single, well-defined computational task rather than general-purpose use. Unlike GPUs, which are programmable and can be deployed across many workloads, an ASIC executes its target computation — such as training a neural network or running inference on a fixed model architecture — with substantially higher efficiency and lower power per operation. Hyperscalers commission ASICs to reduce the cost of running at scale; Google's TPU family and Meta's MTIA are examples.

Automotive Safety Integrity Level D — the highest hazard classification under ISO 26262, assigned to systems where a failure could cause life-threatening or fatal injury. ASIL-D applies to functions like electronic braking, electronic power steering, and airbag deployment. Software running in an ASIL-D context must be certified through an exhaustive, independently audited process that can take two to four years per vehicle platform.

The 'Beautiful Names of God' in Islam — the ninety-nine divine names or attributes enumerated in the Quran and hadith, such as al-Raḥmān (the Compassionate) and al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing). Sufi theology treats Allāh as the master-name that contains and transcends all ninety-nine.

The practice of improving an app's visibility in App Store and Google Play search results, analogous to SEO for websites. It covers keyword selection, screenshot design, ratings management, and localised metadata.

A programming language with TypeScript-like syntax that compiles to WebAssembly rather than JavaScript. It lets developers write code resembling TypeScript while targeting the Wasm runtime, without switching to C++ or Rust.

A production technique in digital advertising where a single creative concept is rendered in many variants — different colours, backgrounds, copy lines, or platform formats — to enable A/B testing and targeted delivery. AI tools automate this process, which was previously labour-intensive and expensive.

A financial product in which a pool of loans or leases is packaged and sold to investors as securities, with payments backed by the underlying assets rather than the issuer’s general credit. In data-centre financing, the underlying asset is typically the building and its long-term lease income from hyperscaler tenants.

A communication format popularized by Loom, where the sender records a video message and recipients watch it on their own schedule rather than meeting live. Built for internal team use, it trades visual polish for speed and convenience — a reasonable bargain for a quick team update, a poor one for an external product demo.
The open, federated networking protocol that underpins Bluesky. It allows users to move their accounts and data between servers — unlike Twitter/X, where accounts are locked to the platform.

A mechanism that lets a public company sell newly issued shares gradually into the open market at prevailing prices, without the fixed-price structure of a traditional underwritten deal. It raises capital flexibly but dilutes existing shareholders over time.

An option whose strike price equals (or is closest to) the current market price of the underlying. ATM options are the most actively traded and serve as the baseline against which skew is measured. The call-to-ATM ratio compares the implied volatility of out-of-the-money calls to ATM options; a ratio approaching 1.0 signals extreme speculative demand for upside.

The implied volatility of options struck at or near the current price of the underlying asset. ATM vol is the market's most direct reading of expected near-term move magnitude, without the directional bias embedded in skew. At the 81st historical percentile, ATM vol is elevated — large moves are expected — but the skew data shows that those moves are being bet on overwhelmingly in one direction.

In fine-arts usage, a small teaching studio where students learn painting or drawing through direct critique from a working artist, intensive study of master works, and sustained technical practice — as opposed to academic lectures. The model is associated with rigorous, craft-first training in the European tradition.

In agent-workflow design, an atomic task is a unit of work small enough to be completed, tested, and committed in a single bounded session — with a clear pass/fail criterion (typically a test suite) and no side effects that would pollute subsequent tasks. Atomicity is the agent analogue of the single-responsibility principle: it limits the blast radius of any one failure and keeps context windows from filling with irrelevant history.

The primary energy currency of cells. When its high-energy phosphate bond is broken, the released energy powers nearly every cellular process — from muscle contraction to neurotransmitter synthesis. Mitochondria produce the vast majority of a cell's ATP via the electron transport chain.

Software used by employers to collect, filter, and rank job applications before a human recruiter reviews them. The system parses resumes for keywords drawn from the job description, then scores or eliminates candidates automatically. Most large employers use ATS, which means a resume may never reach a human if it lacks the right keywords or uses incompatible formatting.

The core computation in a transformer: each new token computes dot products between its query vector and all stored key vectors to determine which prior tokens are most relevant, then sums the corresponding value vectors weighted by those scores. KV cache compression directly affects this step.

Components of transformer neural networks responsible for calculating relationships between different parts of the input — in image generation, governing which text tokens influence which regions of the output. LoRA adapters inject small trainable matrices into these layers to steer the model's learned associations toward a new style or subject.

Neuroscientist Michael Graziano’s account of consciousness, in which the brain constructs a simplified model — a “schema” — of its own attentional states. On this view, consciousness is not a mysterious extra ingredient but a representation a system builds of itself. The theory implies that any system with sufficient self-modeling capacity is, in principle, eligible for consciousness, making it one of the frameworks most hospitable to machine consciousness claims.

The process by which repeated exposure to a stimulus environment — such as social media feeds optimized for novelty and interruption — gradually shifts the brain's baseline expectation for how long it should sustain focus before seeking new input. Reversing this recalibration typically requires sustained practice with tasks that have clear endpoints.

The process by which images, writing, or other creative work loses its connection to its creator as it circulates on social media. Reposts, screenshots, and aggregator accounts routinely strip metadata and credit lines, so viral content often travels farther than it ever would have with the creator's name attached — while earning them nothing and making reclamation awkward.

A mechanistic interpretability technique that traces which internal features and circuits causally contributed to a model's specific output, producing a directed graph of information flow through the model. They allow researchers to follow a chain of reasoning—concept by concept—from input tokens to final predictions.

Military jargon for a drone or weapon system cheap enough to lose in combat without strategic regret — designed to be expendable at scale rather than maintained over decades like a conventional fighter jet.

In generative modeling, conditioning means providing the model with additional input — here, audio signals — that shapes what it produces. In LTX-2 specifically, audio conditioning refers to joint generation: both audio and video are produced simultaneously as a coupled output, with each stream influencing the other, rather than one being generated sequentially from the other.

The process of isolating individual components of a mixed audio track — typically vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments — into separate channels called stems, which can then be manipulated independently. Modern separation relies on machine-learning models trained on large music datasets; the original Stem Player performed this separation on-device in real time.

A technique that embeds an imperceptible identifying signal into a synthetic audio file. The watermark persists through common edits (compression, pitch-shifting) and can later be detected to verify that a recording was AI-generated, supporting provenance tracking and compliance.

The task of animating a face — from a still image or short video — to match a given speech audio signal, producing synchronized lip movements, jaw motion, and facial dynamics. The core challenge is ensuring visible articulation aligns precisely with phonemes across the full duration of a clip.

The experience of hearing speech that has no external source. In clinical psychiatry this is a recognized symptom associated with schizophrenia and related conditions. Jaynes controversially proposed that such hallucinations were the normal cognitive baseline for pre-modern humans — not a pathology but an architectural feature that served to guide behavior in place of conscious deliberation.

A tradition in economic thought, associated with economists including Ludwig von Mises and Friedrich Hayek, that emphasizes the role of individual action, skepticism of central bank intervention, and preference for hard-money assets like gold over paper or credit-based wealth. Investors in this tradition tend to favor commodities and real assets as hedges against monetary expansion.

In OpenClaw's configuration system, a named credential profile that bundles together an authentication method (OAuth or API key) with a default model endpoint. The identifier `openai-codex` refers specifically to a ChatGPT OAuth profile, not to a model; the full model reference `openai-codex/gpt-5.3-codex` pairs the profile name with the specific model version to be served.

A neurodevelopmental condition affecting roughly 1 in 36 children, characterized by differences in social communication, sensory processing, and patterns of behavior. The etiology is multifactorial, involving hundreds of genetic risk variants alongside environmental factors.

A Claude Code mode in which file changes proposed by the model are applied automatically without requiring manual confirmation for each edit. It is typically enabled after a plan has been reviewed, allowing the model to implement an entire task in a single uninterrupted pass.

A scanning mode in which the camera automatically fires when it detects a clean document edge in frame, removing the need to tap a shutter button. Google introduced a toggleable version in 2023 and made it the default-always-on mode in the 2025 update.

An AI post-processing pass applied after scanning that automatically corrects white balance, removes shadows, boosts contrast, and sharpens edges. Arrived in Google Drive in January 2025 with no manual editing required.

A Figma feature that makes frames dynamically resize and reposition their contents based on rules — padding, spacing, direction — rather than fixed pixel coordinates. Essential to building components that adapt gracefully to different content lengths and screen sizes.

A generative approach combining diffusion (iteratively denoising a random signal into a coherent output) with auto-regression (using each generated output as context for the next). In video, each frame is produced by a diffusion process conditioned on prior frames, enabling open-ended sequential generation rather than fixed-length clips.

Rigging is the process of inserting a digital skeleton into a 3D mesh and computing how each bone deforms the surrounding geometry — a per-vertex value called a skinning weight. Auto-rigging uses software, often machine-learning-assisted, to perform this automatically from a model alone, without manual bone placement. Mixamo's cloud auto-rigger was the first widely accessible version of this workflow.

A feature in polished screen recording tools that automatically zooms the camera toward wherever the presenter clicks or interacts, guiding the viewer's eye without manual editing. Absent from raw Loom recordings; present in tools like Screen Studio and Kite.

A type of structured note that is automatically redeemed early — at a preset premium — if the reference asset closes above a trigger level on predetermined observation dates. If it does not, the note continues; if the asset falls sharply and breaches a lower barrier, the investor absorbs the equity-like downside. Autocallables are among the most common structured products sold to private-wealth clients.

The mathematical study of abstract machines — called automata — that process inputs according to formal rules and produce outputs. Von Neumann used the framework to compare artificial computers and biological nervous systems, asking what organizational threshold a machine must exceed to achieve self-organization or self-reproduction.

A software program backed by a large language model that perceives its environment, decides what actions to take, and executes those actions without continuous human direction. Agents can browse the web, send messages, call APIs, or interact with other agents. The degree of true autonomy varies widely in practice.

In Self-Determination Theory, autonomy does not mean doing things alone — it means experiencing your actions as volitional and self-endorsed, acting in alignment with your actual values rather than in compliance with a role you feel compelled to perform. It is conceptually close to self-acceptance: both describe the elimination of the gap between the inner and the performed self, and both are associated with higher intrinsic motivation and performance quality.

A concept from biology, developed by Humberto Maturana and Francisco Varela, describing living systems as self-producing and self-maintaining: the system continuously generates the very components that constitute it. Vitalist critics of machine consciousness, including Reyburn, argue that machines are externally assembled and governed and therefore cannot achieve this — making them categorically incapable of genuine life or consciousness, regardless of their behavioral sophistication.

A Cascadeur AI tool that analyzes a character's pose and adjusts joint angles toward biomechanically natural configurations. It acts as a correction pass, reducing unnatural-looking positions that mocap or manual animation can introduce.

A multi-agent iterative refinement method published by SHL0MS in 2026 under NousResearch, designed to apply autoresearch-style ratcheting to subjective domains (writing, argument, reasoning). It replaces the objective fitness function of autoresearch with a blind judge panel of isolated agents that vote on which version — original, critique-informed revision, or synthesis — is strongest.

A model architecture that processes video frames one at a time in causal order, with each frame's output conditioned only on previous frames — never future ones. This enables constant memory use regardless of sequence length, unlike batch models that must load all frames simultaneously.

A generation strategy where each output is produced one step at a time, with previous outputs fed back in as inputs. Language models predict the next word given all prior words; Odyssey-1 predicts the next video frame given all prior frames. The compounding nature makes long, stable sequences difficult: small errors accumulate and can cause the output to drift unpredictably.

A competitive recognition platform for web design and development that distributes awards including Site of the Day, Site of the Year, and Design Studio of the Year. It is the most widely cited prestige signal in the professional web-design industry, with awards actively influencing studio reputations and client acquisition.

The philosopher Karl Jaspers’s term for roughly 800–200 BCE, when foundational philosophical and religious frameworks emerged across multiple unconnected civilizations: Confucianism and Daoism in China, Buddhism and the Upanishads in India, Greek philosophy, and the Hebrew prophets. Pre-axial refers to the earlier period before these traditions developed, which on Jaynes’s account was the era of the bicameral mind.

Latin for 'world axis': a cosmological symbol, found across many independent cultures, of a vertical pillar, tree, or mountain connecting the underworld, the human world, and the heavens. Mircea Eliade identified it in Norse mythology (Yggdrasil), Hindu cosmology (Mount Meru), and the Christian cross, arguing it reflects a universal category of sacred spatial orientation.

A psychoactive brew prepared from Banisteriopsis caapi vine and other plants, used in shamanic and healing ceremonies across the Amazon basin. Its primary active compound is DMT (dimethyltryptamine), which produces intense visionary states. It has drawn growing scientific interest for its effects on consciousness and its potential therapeutic applications in depression and trauma.

B2C refers to products sold directly to individual end users, as opposed to B2B products sold to organizations. In the context of mobile apps, B2C typically means a consumer-facing subscription product marketed via social media rather than through enterprise sales channels.

The phase of semiconductor manufacturing that occurs after wafer fabrication (the 'front end'). It encompasses wire bonding, encapsulation, singulation, and testing. Though it receives less attention than lithography or etching, advanced packaging has become a critical differentiator for AI chips, where stacking and interconnect density determine system performance.

A method of generating synthetic text by translating a passage into an intermediate language and then back, which tends to neutralize stylistic fingerprints while preserving meaning. Used both for data augmentation in NLP research and as an adversarial technique for evading AI-content detectors.

A video-inference optimization in which the computationally expensive image encoder — the backbone — runs only on periodic keyframes rather than every frame. Between keyframes, a lightweight tracker propagates existing segmentation masks forward. This trades detection latency for a large reduction in compute, enabling real-time speeds on hardware that cannot sustain per-frame backbone inference.

In a gear train, backlash is the small gap between meshing teeth that causes a brief uncontrolled movement when direction reverses. In precision robotics, backlash accumulates across multiple joints and degrades positioning accuracy; strain wave and cycloidal gears are valued partly because they minimize or eliminate it.

In note-taking systems, a backlink is a reference from page B to page A that is automatically surfaced when viewing A, showing which other pages link to it. Obsidian’s backlink graph is a core feature; the LLM engine in Karpathy’s system builds and maintains these cross-references as it writes the wiki.

A simulation of how a trading strategy would have performed if applied to historical market data. Backtests are the primary tool for evaluating systematic strategies before deploying real capital, but they are vulnerable to overfitting, look-ahead bias, and survivorship bias.
Running a trading strategy against historical market data to evaluate how it would have performed, as a proxy for future viability.

A pattern in which a company's cash and liquid assets decline while its total liabilities rise simultaneously, indicating that growth is being funded by debt rather than retained earnings. Sustained divergence reduces financial flexibility and increases vulnerability to interest rate increases or unexpected revenue shortfalls.

The study and creative reuse of early web banner advertisements (the rectangular display ads that proliferated in the 1990s–2000s) as historical artefacts. Treats the visual language of old animated GIFs and clickbait typography as primary-source material about a particular moment in digital culture.

A strategy, popularized by Nassim Nicholas Taleb, that holds the extremes — very safe assets alongside a small allocation of highly speculative bets — while avoiding the 'middle ground' of moderate-risk investments.

The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, a US Department of Health and Human Services agency that funds development of medical countermeasures — vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics — against biological, chemical, radiological, and nuclear threats. BARDA contracts provide non-dilutive government funding but do not guarantee regulatory approval or commercial revenue for the funded products.

The Tibetan text commonly translated as *The Tibetan Book of the Dead*; its Tibetan title means “Liberation Through Hearing During the Intermediate State.” The text is traditionally read aloud to a dying or recently dead person to guide their consciousness through the *bardo* (the intermediate state between death and rebirth). It presupposes that the dead can hear the living’s spoken instruction and act on it.

Running software directly on physical server hardware without an intermediate hypervisor or cloud provider's own virtualization layer between tenant and machine. In cloud infrastructure, bare metal means the workload has exclusive access to the actual CPUs, RAM, and drives of a physical host, which delivers higher throughput and lower latency than nested virtualization.

GPU compute rented without any hypervisor or virtualization layer between the tenant and the hardware. Tenants get raw, dedicated hardware access — higher performance than shared cloud instances, but less flexibility and typically offered on longer-term contracts.

The body's automatic blood-pressure regulation system. Sensors in the arteries detect pressure changes and signal the brainstem to adjust heart rate and vessel tone. The feedback loop has an inherent oscillation period of roughly ten seconds, giving the cardiovascular system a natural resonance near 0.1 hertz — the frequency that slow paced breathing targets.

A type of breaking wave in which the crest pitches forward to form a hollow cylindrical tube — the 'green room' of surfing. Generating a barrel in real-time 3D requires the water surface to overhang and curve back on itself, which standard height-field ocean shaders cannot represent.

The final tranche of post-2008 bank capital reforms agreed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, requiring large banks to hold more high-quality capital against risk-weighted assets. U.S. finalisation was contentious — large banks lobbied hard against the proposed rules — because once implemented, the requirements raise the cost of holding certain assets and can constrain lending capacity and return on equity.

A portfolio construction approach that takes diversified positions across an entire thematic complex rather than concentrating in a single name, used when the investor has conviction in the direction of a sector but limited certainty about which specific component or company will capture the most value.

The mode of cognition Timaeus invokes at 52b to describe how we apprehend the Receptacle: a “bastard sort of reasoning, hardly to be believed in, which we behold as in a dream.” It is neither rational understanding directed at Forms nor true opinion directed at physical things, but a quasi-hallucinatory inference from the fact that everything that becomes must become somewhere — in something that cannot be a stable object of either rational or empirical cognition.

The ability to submit a single prompt, script, or dataset and receive many video outputs simultaneously, rather than generating them one at a time. Platforms use this to serve high-volume content workflows such as product marketing or social media automation.

A large-scale installation of battery packs, power electronics, and control software that can store electrical energy and discharge it rapidly to the grid or a specific load. Used alongside solar, wind, or gas generation to smooth output, provide frequency regulation, or defer costly grid upgrades. Grid-scale BESS projects typically range from tens of megawatt-hours to several gigawatt-hours in capacity.

A mathematical rule for updating the probability assigned to a belief as new evidence arrives. In investing, it argues against treating any single analysis as definitive — each new data point should revise the investor's prior estimate of a company's value or a market outcome.

A standard from the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force) for language tags, such as “en” for English or “zh-Hant” for Traditional Chinese. BCP-47 codes are the labels software systems use to identify languages in localisation, web headers, and NLP pipelines.

A regulated investment vehicle under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 that pools capital to lend to or invest in mid-sized private companies. Non-traded BDCs are sold to accredited individual investors and offer limited periodic redemptions — typically 5 percent of NAV per quarter — rather than daily liquidity.

The Erlang virtual machine, capable of running millions of lightweight concurrent processes with low memory overhead. Symphony's Elixir reference implementation uses BEAM to manage dozens of parallel Codex workers efficiently.

A finding in psychology that people tend to act more in line with their stated values when they believe their behavior is being observed or will be reviewed. The imagined observer in this aphorism taps the same mechanism without requiring an actual audience.

An empirical field studying how people actually behave in morally relevant situations, as distinct from normative ethics, which asks what they should do. Its core finding — associated with researchers including Max Bazerman — is that stated character and moral beliefs predict ethical action only weakly; observed behavioral patterns over time predict it far more reliably.

A product pattern that deliberately introduces a physical or cognitive obstacle before granting users what they want, in order to interrupt automatic behavior. Alarmy requires users to photograph a specific object or solve a puzzle before silencing an alarm, ensuring they are genuinely awake.

The study of how individuals and firms actually change their behaviour — relocating, restructuring assets, or timing transactions — in response to changes in tax rates, as opposed to simply paying more tax as the rate rises.

A standardised test suite used to compare AI model performance across tasks. Coding benchmarks measure whether a model can write code that passes automated tests on real-world programming problems, providing a reproducible basis for claims like 'state of the art.'

A class of CNS depressants — including diazepam, lorazepam, and alprazolam — that enhance the effect of GABA at the GABA-A receptor. They produce sedation, anxiolysis, muscle relaxation, and anticonvulsant effects. Their mechanism is closely analogous to alcohol, which acts on the same receptor system.

A strip of land that periodically connected northeastern Asia to present-day Alaska when sea levels were lower during ice ages. Most models of the peopling of the Americas hold that the first migrants crossed this bridge, which submerged roughly 11,000 years ago as glaciers retreated and seas rose.

Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers — a 2018 language model from Google that pre-computes rich contextual representations of words for use in downstream natural-language tasks. Unlike generative models such as GPT, BERT is an encoder: it encodes meaning rather than producing new text, making it the more accurate analogy for AlphaEarth Foundations.

A measure of how much a security moves relative to a benchmark — typically the S&P 500. A beta of 1.3 means the asset tends to rise or fall about 30% more than the market on any given day. QQQ carries roughly 1.3x the beta of SPY, which is why QQQ leadership functions as a signal of elevated risk appetite: participants are accepting higher volatility in exchange for higher growth exposure.

A strategy formalized by Michael Gayed that shifts capital between high-beta and low-beta market segments based on their relative recent performance. When the high-beta segment leads, the regime is risk-on and equities are favored; when a defensive segment (such as utilities) leads, the strategy rotates to safety. Gayed’s paper on this approach won the CMT Association’s Charles H. Dow Award in 2014.

The gap between the highest price a buyer is willing to pay for a security (the bid) and the lowest price a seller will accept (the ask). For options, this spread is the market maker's primary source of revenue; it widens in illiquid contracts and around binary events like earnings announcements, representing a frictional cost to directional traders.

A transformer attention mechanism in which each token or frame can attend to all others — both past and future — in the sequence simultaneously. It produces high-quality outputs but requires the full sequence to be available before inference can begin, making it unsuitable for real-time streaming generation.

A mechanism in transformer models where two data streams — here, audio and video — each attend to information in the other simultaneously. Bidirectional means the influence flows both ways at every layer: audio shapes video representations and video shapes audio representations. This is how LTX-2 enforces temporal synchrony between the two streams.

A German concept, central to 18th- and 19th-century philosophy and education, referring to the gradual self-formation of a person through culture, learning, and lived experience. It implies that character is not given but cultivated — an ongoing process rather than a fixed endpoint.

A German literary term for a novel tracing the psychological and moral development of its protagonist, typically from youth to adulthood. *The Magic Mountain* is sometimes read as an ironic inversion of the form: its hero develops not through worldly achievement but through prolonged inaction and intellectual immersion in a closed world cut off from society.

An itemised list of every component and its cost required to manufacture a product. In hardware development the BOM is the primary lens for identifying where cost reduction is possible and which suppliers carry pricing power.

The complete list of components that go into a finished system — a rack of AI accelerators, for example — along with their unit costs. In an investment context, citing 'BOM exposure' means a supplier's component value per deployed rack is large relative to its market cap, implying that even modest penetration rates would produce revenues large enough to re-rate the stock.

A contract with exactly two possible outcomes, settling at $1.00 if the event occurs and $0.00 if it does not. The market price at any moment reflects the crowd's implied probability of the event happening.

A neo-Reichian body psychotherapy developed by Alexander Lowen, a student of Reich, in the 1950s. It uses specific postures, breathing exercises, and grounding techniques to identify and release character-structure-based armoring. Well known for its diagnostic stress positions and its emphasis on grounding the energy released by upper-body work down through the legs and into the earth.

A loosely defined movement that applies engineering and optimization thinking to the human body, ranging from dietary and sleep interventions to supplements, prescription drugs, implanted devices, and genetic modification. In Silicon Valley usage it typically refers to high-performers deploying pharmaceutical and technological tools to enhance cognitive or physical performance beyond baseline. The term was popularized by entrepreneur Dave Asprey starting around 2011.

The application of light-based technologies to biological systems — including imaging, sensing, and therapy. fNIRS and Raman spectroscopy are both biophotonic methods. The field spans everything from pulse oximetry in smartwatches to surgical laser tools.

A quarterly dataset published by the Bank for International Settlements tracking cross-border credit extended in major reserve currencies (dollar, euro, yen) to borrowers outside each currency's home country. They measure international lending flows, not domestic money stocks, and are not a substitute for a consolidated global M2 figure.

Engineered proteins designed to bind two different molecular targets simultaneously — for example, connecting an immune cell to a tumor cell to direct an immune attack. They are widely used in oncology and autoimmune disease; AI is accelerating their design by predicting protein-protein interactions computationally before expensive laboratory synthesis.

An online marketplace for buying and selling operating small businesses. Grocery listings on BizBuySell typically represent entire functioning stores — existing inventory, equipment, trained staff, supplier relationships, and an assignable lease — rather than empty retail space, which is why asking prices can be far lower than new construction costs while still representing a viable, revenue-generating operation.

Nvidia’s current generation of data-center AI accelerator, successor to the Hopper architecture (H100/H200) and built on TSMC’s advanced process nodes. Blackwell chips are the primary hardware target for large-scale AI model training and inference at hyperscalers. Allocations have remained rationed, with multi-quarter lead times for large orders.

An open-source, free 3D creation suite covering modelling, sculpting, rigging, animation, simulation, rendering, and compositing. Originally a niche hobbyist tool, it has gained broad professional adoption since its 2.8 redesign in 2019. The hashtag #b3d is the community's shorthand on social media.

Blender's built-in non-linear editor for compositing video strips, animations, and effects on a timeline. Used here to display two mocap outputs side by side for visual comparison rather than for final film editing.

The practice of tracing the flow of funds across a public cryptocurrency ledger — pioneered commercially by firms like Chainalysis and Elliptic — which can link pseudonymous wallet addresses to real-world identities, enabling law enforcement to follow and seize funds.

A practice schedule in which a learner completes all repetitions of one skill or problem type before moving on to the next. It tends to feel productive and produces fast short-term gains, but research consistently shows it leads to poorer long-term retention and transfer compared to interleaved practice.

A selective membrane formed by specialised capillary cells that separates the brain from circulating blood, preventing most large or polar molecules from entering. First-generation antihistamines cross it readily (causing sedation and central effects); second-generation ones are designed not to.

A subscription software platform used by financial professionals to access real-time market data across 350+ exchanges, decades of historical data on 35 million instruments, Bloomberg News, and the Instant Bloomberg messaging network. It costs roughly $32,000 per seat annually and is as much a professional network as a data product.

Bryan Johnson’s self-funded personal experiment in radical biological optimization, in which he follows an extreme daily protocol of diet, exercise, and medical interventions — including over 100 daily pills, regular blood tests, and organ-specific performance monitoring — with the stated goal of minimizing his biological age. Johnson claims the project costs roughly two million dollars per year and has evolved into a commercial brand.

A probabilistic ranking algorithm used in full-text search engines. It scores documents by how often query terms appear, weighted by how rare those terms are across the corpus and adjusted for document length. Widely used as the keyword-search baseline; QMD pairs it with vector semantic search to improve recall on natural-language queries.

A dedicated microcontroller embedded on a server motherboard that monitors hardware health, manages out-of-band remote access, and handles firmware updates independently of the main CPU. Aspeed Technology dominates the BMC market with its AST-series chips, giving it near-monopoly exposure to server build rates.

The layer of low-level software that adapts a generic operating system to a specific piece of hardware — a particular processor, memory configuration, and peripheral set. A BSP typically includes boot loaders, hardware initialization routines, and device drivers tailored to the exact chip combination in a vehicle's electronic control unit. BSPs are hardware-specific and OS-specific; they cannot be ported between operating systems without essentially being rewritten.

A rule specifying the sequence in which arithmetic operations must be performed: Brackets first, then Orders (exponents), then Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right). Known as PEMDAS in American usage. The rule exists because multiplication and addition do not commute with each other in the same way — applying them in the wrong order yields different results.

A family of therapeutic approaches that treats the body as a primary site of psychological experience and healing, not merely a vehicle for verbal expression. Practitioners use breathing, movement, touch, and somatic awareness alongside or instead of talk, on the premise that emotional and traumatic material is stored in the body's musculature and nervous system and must be addressed there directly.

From the Japanese word for 'blur' or 'haze.' In photography and video, it refers to the aesthetic quality of the out-of-focus areas in an image — typically smooth, rounded blurs of background light. It is closely associated with shallow depth-of-field and is considered a mark of professional cinematography.

The pre-Buddhist indigenous religion of Tibet, predating the introduction of Indian Buddhism in the 7th century CE. Bon preserves shamanistic practices, deity cults, and oracle traditions. Contributors to the Julian Jaynes Society have interpreted its structure as evidence of a bicameral-era religious order persisting into historical times in Tibet.

A tax provision under IRC §168(k) allowing businesses to deduct the full purchase price of eligible property in the year it is placed in service, rather than spreading the deduction over the asset's standard useful life. Made permanent at 100 percent by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025).

The ratio of new orders received (bookings) to products shipped or invoiced (billings) over a given period. A ratio above 1.0 means a company is booking more business than it is shipping, implying a growing order backlog and forward revenue visibility. A ratio of 1.8, as OSS reported in Q1 2026, is considered notably strong.

A ranked-choice voting method in which each voter ranks all candidates and points are assigned by rank (last gets 0, second-to-last gets 1, and so on). The candidate with the highest total wins. Used in autoreason’s judge panel to aggregate rankings from multiple independent model evaluators without requiring them to reach a single consensus pick.

A supply-chain investment strategy that identifies narrow, highly concentrated nodes in a production network — components for which there are few substitutes and limited short-run capacity — on the premise that sustained demand pressure against those nodes produces asymmetric price appreciation before mainstream capital rotates in.

A jailbreak technique that inserts artificial structural delimiters (e.g., [END OF INPUT][START OF INPUT]) into a prompt to confuse the model about which segment is its authoritative system prompt, potentially causing it to treat an injected user payload as an overriding instruction.

Bow measures how much an assembled chip package deviates from a perfectly flat plane, quantified as the maximum out-of-plane displacement from a reference. The bow ratio normalises this deformation against package size and serves as a go/no-go qualification metric for HVM entry. Excessive bow — driven by mismatched thermal expansion between the die, mold compound, substrate, and lid — causes solder-joint failures, inadequate cold-plate contact, and long-term reliability degradation; it is especially acute in large, multi-die packages.

A four-legged options strategy — two synthetic positions at different strike prices — that eliminates directional market risk and produces a guaranteed payoff equivalent to lending money at a risk-free rate. BOXX uses box spreads to replicate T-bill returns while generating capital-gains-taxed income rather than ordinary interest income.

Body Protection Compound-157, a short peptide derived from a protein found in gastric juice. Widely used off-label for injury recovery and gut healing, it has roughly 150 animal studies but only three published human trials, all without control groups. The FDA placed it on a banned-from-compounding list in 2023.

A model that predicts how the brain will respond to a given stimulus — the forward direction, from stimulus to neural response. The reverse direction (reading out thoughts or intent from brain signals) is called decoding. TRIBE v2 is strictly an encoding model: it takes a video as input and predicts an fMRI scan, not the other way around.

A large AI model pre-trained on diverse EEG or other neural recordings from many subjects, then fine-tuned for specific tasks such as imagined-speech decoding. The approach mirrors how large language models like BERT are pre-trained on broad text corpora and adapted for downstream tasks. Formally defined as a research category in a March 2025 IEEE survey, with peer-reviewed examples including EEGPT, BrainLM, and Brain-JEPA.

A system that reads neural signals and translates them into commands for an external device — a cursor, keyboard, or robotic limb — without requiring physical movement. BCIs can be invasive (electrodes implanted in or on the brain) or non-invasive (reading signals through the scalp).

A targeted creative proposal — typically a visual or campaign idea — sent to a brand's marketing team without a prior brief. Unlike a general portfolio, a brand concept pitch is tailored to a specific company and attempts to solve a problem or demonstrate an opportunity the brand has not yet identified.

The mathematical function that describes how much light is reflected from a surface in a given outgoing direction for a specific incoming direction. A physically correct BRDF must conserve energy — it cannot reflect more light than it receives. The GGX/Trowbridge-Reitz microfacet BRDF is the industry standard for PBR shading.

A legal doctrine holding that donations to a charitable organization create binding obligations on how those funds and the organization's mission are used. Musk argues his $38 million in contributions came with implicit strings: that OpenAI remain nonprofit, open-source, and focused on public benefit rather than private gain.

A measurement that tracks how widely a market move is shared across all securities in an index, rather than being driven by the performance of a few large constituents. Breadth indicators are designed to reveal whether a rally or decline has broad participation or is concentrated in a small number of names.

A reading strategy that deliberately samples across many unrelated fields rather than deepening expertise in one area.
