The goal is to accumulate a wide base of reference points that can cross-connect in unexpected ways, as opposed to specialist depth. Bradbury's regime is an example: zoology one night, philosophy the next.

A signal that fires when an unusually large share of stocks in an index simultaneously surge to new short-term highs, or when advancing issues vastly outnumber decliners, indicating that buying is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few names. Breadth thrusts are treated as leading indicators of durable bull-market phases rather than narrow, fragile rallies.

An aggregated indicator tracked by Thrasher Analytics that combines multiple individual breadth thrust signals into a single score. A reading of zero means no active thrust signals are firing across the basket of indicators that make up the composite, suggesting conditions for a new regime trigger are absent.

Hawkridge’s term for the twelve-month window that begins after a 20-Day High Breadth Thrust fires. Historical data shows the S&P 500 has been higher at the end of every such window in his dataset. When the window closes without a new thrust, the statistical safety net formally lapses — not a sell signal, but the removal of a historically reliable tailwind.

The moment a stock's price moves decisively above a defined resistance level — in this context, the upper boundary of the flag's consolidation range — typically accompanied by a surge in trading volume that confirms new buying interest rather than a false start.

A proper scoring rule that measures the accuracy of probabilistic forecasts. Calculated as the mean squared difference between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes (0 or 1). A score of 0 is perfect; a score of 1 is perfectly wrong. Lower is better. Used in prediction markets to evaluate forecaster calibration over time.

A prehistoric and proto-historic period defined by the widespread use of bronze — an alloy of copper and tin — for tools, weapons, and ritual objects. In China, this era spans roughly 2000–500 BC. The term is a relative chronological label applied region by region, not a single global moment.

An occult religious organization founded by Maurice Doreal in Denver around 1930. It operated through correspondence courses selling Doreal's teachings on Atlantis, cosmic law, and hidden history. In 1953, anticipating nuclear apocalypse, Doreal relocated the group to a walled compound in Sedalia, Colorado. The organization still exists and sells Doreal's works online.

A small software add-on that runs inside a web browser and can read or modify the pages the user visits. Extensions can add UI elements, capture data from existing services, or inject new functionality without requiring changes to the underlying website.

A scraping tool that runs as a plugin inside a desktop browser rather than on a remote server. Because it operates within the user's browser session, it automatically has access to any site the user is already logged into — bypassing login walls that stymie server-side scrapers. The tradeoff is that it requires the user's machine to stay active during a scraping job.

A Linux sandboxing tool that uses the kernel’s namespace isolation primitives to give a process a restricted view of the filesystem, network, and other processes. Unlike virtual machines, it adds almost no overhead — the sandboxed process runs at native speed but cannot see or touch resources outside its declared boundaries. It is the same mechanism Flatpak uses to isolate desktop applications.

Polymarket's category of short-duration UP/DOWN markets on cryptocurrency prices, resolved every 5 or 15 minutes by price oracles. Unlike standard binary markets, UP and DOWN tokens in bucket markets have entirely separate order books with independent liquidity—the feature that makes brief arbitrage gaps structurally possible there but not elsewhere on the platform.

In Theosophical terminology, the higher self: the union of manas (mind) with buddhi (the spiritual soul or intuitive principle). It stands in direct opposition to kama-manas (desire-mind) and represents the capacity for spiritual perception uncontaminated by passion or ego. Blavatsky held that buddhi-manas is accessed only when the lower self is sufficiently stilled.

Total US equity market capitalization divided by nominal GDP, popularized by Warren Buffett in a 2001 Fortune interview as 'probably the best single measure of where valuations stand at any given moment.' A reading above 100% means the aggregate stock market is worth more than a full year of domestic economic output. Critics note the ratio is structurally inflated over time by globalization (US multinationals earn revenue abroad not captured in domestic GDP) and by rising corporate profit margins, meaning the same reading today may not signal the same degree of overvaluation as in earlier eras.

A program in which a company pays independent security researchers a monetary reward for responsibly disclosing valid vulnerabilities. Platforms like HackerOne aggregate these programs and maintain public leaderboards ranking researchers by points or severity of findings.

A curated collection of pre-rigged motion sequences — walk cycles, turns, camera movements — bundled directly inside a ComfyUI extension. Users select from them within the workflow rather than importing files from a separate application.

A continuation chart pattern formed by a sharp upward move (the flagpole) followed by a brief sideways-to-slightly-lower consolidation on declining volume (the flag), which resolves when price breaks above the flag's upper boundary — implying a resumption of the prior uptrend with a projected target equal to the flagpole's height added to the breakout point.

A filmmaking technique, made iconic by the 1999 film *The Matrix*, in which on-screen action appears to slow or freeze while the camera continues to track around the subject. Conventionally achieved with an array of still cameras firing in sequence; now a common stylistic specification in AI video prompts, used to test whether a model can simulate temporal manipulation alongside camera movement.

A feature of Bun — a fast JavaScript runtime that Anthropic uses to build Claude Code — that bundles an entire TypeScript project into a single self-contained native binary. No separate runtime installation is required. This is what allowed Leon Lin to produce a working `claude-local.cmd` for Windows from the leaked source.

A JavaScript runtime and bundler positioned as a faster alternative to Node.js. Bun generates source map files by default during production builds — a convenience for developers that must be explicitly disabled to avoid shipping debugging artifacts with published packages.

A reverse-domain-style string (e.g., com.dev.parksafe) that uniquely identifies an iOS or macOS app across all of Apple's systems. It is set at project creation and cannot be changed after an app is submitted to the App Store; it links the app to its entitlements, provisioning profiles, and App Store Connect record.

A wealth-preservation strategy in which an investor accumulates appreciating assets, borrows against them for living expenses (loans are not taxable income), and holds until death, at which point the step-up in basis eliminates any accumulated capital-gains liability for heirs.

Data that infers which companies or individuals are actively researching a purchase by tracking behavioral signals — page visits, content downloads, forum posts, or vendor comparisons. Providers aggregate these signals and sell them to sales and marketing teams to prioritize outreach toward prospects already in a buying cycle.

A method of smoothing animation between keyframes using cubic Bézier curves to control the rate of change over time — how fast or slow a bone accelerates and decelerates between two poses. It offers finer creative control than linear interpolation and is the standard in professional animation tools.

In computer architecture, the guarantee that all processors in a multi-core system observe the same value for a shared memory location at any given time. Researchers have borrowed the concept for multi-agent AI: when two agents hold conflicting versions of the same fact, a coherence protocol must decide which is authoritative.

A macOS built-in command at `/usr/bin/caffeinate` that prevents the system from sleeping by holding IOKit power assertions. It can be run standalone (holds until the process is killed), with a timeout (`-t`), or tied to another process (`-w <pid>`). Included since OS X 10.8 Mountain Lion.

A strategy that simultaneously sells a near-term option and buys a longer-dated option at the same strike. The trade profits from the faster time decay of the short-dated leg, and also embeds a view on the volatility term structure — whether near-term uncertainty is priced high or low relative to longer-dated uncertainty.

In cognitive psychology, calibration is the alignment between a person's confidence in their performance and their actual accuracy. A well-calibrated person is confident when they are likely right and uncertain when they are likely wrong. Experts tend to be better calibrated than novices in absolute terms but can paradoxically underestimate their relative standing, because they project their own skill level onto others and conclude that what feels easy to them must be easy for most people.

The interest rate banks charge brokerages on overnight loans used to fund customers' margin accounts. It is typically close to the federal funds rate and sets the floor for the cost at which brokerages can themselves borrow the money they re-lend to margin customers.

A call option gives its buyer the right to purchase a stock at a fixed price before a set date. When call volume — the number of call contracts traded — spikes sharply in a name, it typically signals traders making leveraged directional bets that the stock will rise. Comparing individual-stock call volume to SPY, the world's most actively traded derivatives instrument, reveals where speculative conviction is concentrated.

An options structure consisting of a long call at a lower strike and a short call at a higher strike, both with the same expiry. Buying a call spread costs less than buying a naked call, but the short upper-strike call caps the upside. In a high-call-skew environment, spreads become structurally cheap — equivalent by put-call parity to an expensive put spread — which is the mechanism behind “there are puts in the calls.”

A compositing technique in which a still image is 'painted' onto a rough 3D geometry so that a virtual camera can move through the scene. Objects at different depths shift at different rates, creating the illusion of dimensionality. It has been a visual-effects staple for decades and is now being automated by AI tools.

The nonlinear mapping from scene radiance to pixel value as recorded by a specific camera sensor. Different cameras apply different S-shaped tone curves; without modeling the CRF, reconstructions from multi-camera rigs suffer color inconsistencies that the optimizer naively attributes to geometry.

A visual charting technique, originating in eighteenth-century Japanese rice markets, that interprets the relationship between a price bar's open, high, low, and close as a directional signal. Academic studies have found little consistent predictive power in liquid developed-market equities.

The offshore marketing arm jointly owned by The Mosaic Company and Nutrien, the two dominant Canadian potash producers. It pools Saskatchewan potash exports and negotiates benchmark prices with major importers such as China and India, functioning as a legal export cartel under Canadian law.

The HTML Canvas API lets JavaScript draw graphics directly to a 2D pixel surface in the browser, frame by frame, without pre-recorded video files. WikWok uses this to render Wikipedia articles as looped visual clips — dynamic, infographic-style animations — that mimic short-form video without storing actual media.

A browser API providing a 2D drawing surface that operates entirely outside the DOM layout system. Because it does not participate in the layout tree, calling its methods — including `measureText()`, which returns the pixel dimensions of a string in a given font — does not trigger reflow. Pretext exploits this to perform text measurement cheaply.

A stock market valuation metric developed by economist Robert Shiller that divides the current S&P 500 index level by the average of inflation-adjusted earnings over the prior ten years. By smoothing out the business cycle, CAPE reduces distortion from a single year of unusually high or low earnings. A CAPE above 30 has historically signaled below-average real equity returns over the subsequent decade.

An adjustment that replaces tax-based depreciation — which depends on whatever Congress happens to allow — with economic depreciation based on the actual replacement cost of capital. Together with the IVA, it produces the clean profit figure used in national income accounting and plotted in the FRED series shown in this chart.

Automated or semi-automated methods for completing bot-detection challenges — such as Google reCAPTCHA or Cloudflare Turnstile — that websites deploy to distinguish human visitors from scripts. Commercial services typically combine machine-learning solvers with human workers for difficult cases.

A company-owned insurance subsidiary that insures the risks of its parent business. Premiums paid to the captive are deductible business expenses; reserves accumulate, often offshore, in low-tax jurisdictions. Legitimate versions exist; aggressive versions appear on the IRS list of abusive tax shelters.

The individual breathing rate at which heart rate variability oscillations are maximally amplified, because the respiratory cycle aligns with the baroreflex's natural feedback loop. It falls between about 4.5 and 6.5 breaths per minute in adults — often near 6 bpm (roughly 5 seconds in, 5 out) — though the precise value varies by person and ideally requires calibration rather than a universal default.

The share of a private equity, hedge, or venture fund's profits paid to the fund's managers as performance compensation. Under current U.S. tax law, this fee — economically a payment for services — is taxed at the lower long-term capital gains rate (20%) rather than as ordinary income (up to 37%), provided the underlying investments are held for more than three years.

The net income or cost from holding an asset over time, accounting for any yield generated minus financing costs. A bond has positive carry because it pays interest; gold has negative carry because it pays nothing and costs money to store. When interest rates fall, gold’s carry disadvantage relative to yield-bearing assets declines, which is one structural reason gold tends to rally in low-rate environments.

A strategy that earns incremental income from the spread between the cost of financing an asset and the yield or revenue the asset generates — borrowed from fixed-income markets, where it describes holding a bond that yields more than the cost of borrowing to own it.

The number of days it takes a company to turn its investments in inventory and receivables into cash from sales. It equals days inventory outstanding plus days sales outstanding minus days payable outstanding. A rising cycle means more working capital is trapped in operations, straining liquidity.

An options contract in which the seller grants a counterparty the right to sell shares at an agreed strike price, while holding sufficient cash to purchase those shares if the contract is exercised (assigned). The seller collects a premium upfront; the risk is being forced to buy the stock at the strike even if it has fallen sharply below that level.

A comprehensive scholarly catalogue of all known authenticated works by a given artist, typically including provenance, condition, exhibition history, and bibliography for each entry. The *Hollstein* series — volumes of which cover Vogtherr the Younger's prints — is the standard catalogue raisonné for early Netherlandish and German graphic art.

A well-documented failure mode in neural networks where learning a new task causes the model to lose competence on previously learned tasks. Both old and new knowledge are encoded in the same set of weights, so gradient updates for new tasks overwrite old ones. It is a primary practical concern when fine-tuning models on narrow task data.

A family of neurotransmitters and hormones — including dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — all derived from the amino acid tyrosine. They regulate arousal, attention, mood, and the stress response, and are central to how both L-Tyrosine supplementation and stimulants like Adderall affect cognition.

Jazz slang for musicians, in use from at least the swing era. On the list Monk uses it in 'get cats interested enough to come to rehearsal,' meaning fellow players. The word implies a peer relationship — you are one of them, not above them.

A transformer architecture in which each position can only attend to previous positions in the sequence, not future ones. This causal masking is what allows the model to be trained with next-token prediction and used to generate sequences step by step. GPT-style models are the canonical example; GaussianGPT uses the same architecture applied to spatial tokens rather than words.

A forward-looking index that measures the expected spread of returns among individual S&P 500 stocks over the next 30 days, using a methodology similar to VIX but applied to single-stock options. Unlike VIX, which tracks expected volatility of the index as a whole, DSPX rises when individual stocks are priced to diverge widely from one another — a common signature of concentrated, narrow markets driven by a handful of outsized names.

The Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, which permits free use, redistribution, and modification of a work — including in commercial products — provided the original creator is credited. It is among the most permissive open licences and is widely used for scientific datasets.

A formal legal letter demanding that the recipient immediately stop a specified activity — here, allegedly generating video that reproduces or derives from copyrighted film content. A C&D is not itself a lawsuit but signals a credible litigation threat and commonly precedes one.

concepts.term: Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM)
concepts.definition: A Stanford University research center, directed by Percy Liang, focused on studying and improving large pretrained AI models. CRFM coined the term “foundation models” in 2021 and publishes benchmarks and open-source tools used widely across the AI research community.

An electronic matching system that ranks and matches buy and sell orders continuously by price and time priority. Polymarket uses a hybrid version: orders are collected through a centralized system for speed, but final settlement is recorded on the blockchain.

The process by which a central bank raises interest rates or shrinks its balance sheet to slow economic activity and control inflation. Higher rates increase borrowing costs and reduce the present value of future corporate earnings. BofA’s Hartnett argues it has historically been the proximate cause of major equity bubble collapses.

A structured tradition of ritual magic in the Western esoteric lineage, systematized in the nineteenth century by Éliphas Lévi and later codified by the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. It synthesizes Kabbalah, astrology, and elaborate symbolic correspondences — including colour scales — into graded initiatory practices.

A public audit rating (0–100) assigned to cryptocurrency projects by CertiK, a blockchain security firm. The score reflects smart-contract vulnerabilities, centralization risk, and unresolved audit findings. A score of 3.3 out of 10 indicates significant unresolved risk.

A credential awarded by the CFA Institute after candidates pass three rigorous exams covering investment analysis, portfolio management, and ethics. One of the most widely respected qualifications in the investment management industry, requiring several years of professional experience alongside the exams.

The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States — an interagency body that reviews foreign investments in US companies for national-security implications. A CFIUS review can block a deal, impose mitigation requirements, or clear it outright. The process delayed Cerebras's original 2024 IPO filing by nearly a year because of G42's investment stake.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the U.S. federal regulator of derivatives markets including futures and certain event contracts. Polymarket was fined $1.4 million by the CFTC in 2022 for operating without proper registration, and U.S. users were barred from the platform until December 2025.

South Korean family-controlled industrial conglomerates — Samsung, SK, Hyundai, LG, Lotte — that dominate the domestic economy and equity market. Founding families typically exercise control through complex webs of cross-shareholdings rather than direct majority ownership, which can weaken minority shareholder rights and reduce pressure to maximise shareholder returns.

A legal term for the documented sequence of copyright ownership, licensing agreements, and permissions that establishes who holds the rights to a piece of creative work. In AI, a 'clean' chain of title over training data means every piece of content used to train a model was licensed with permission — critical for commercial users who need legal protection against copyright infringement claims.

Paul Werbos's formalisation of how gradients — measures of sensitivity — propagate through nested chains of mathematical functions. It generalises the standard calculus chain rule to systems where variables appear in a specific computational order, providing the rigorous foundation for backpropagation.

In equity research, a survey of supply chain participants — component makers, contract manufacturers, logistics firms — to gather intelligence about production ramps or demand signals not yet visible in company disclosures. Analysts based in Asia with established supplier relationships are particularly valued for channel checks on semiconductor hardware because the supply chain is concentrated in Taiwan, South Korea, and Japan, and supplier order patterns often reveal production changes weeks before any public announcement.

A practice in which a company ships more product to distributors or customers than they can realistically absorb in the near term, in order to recognize revenue earlier. Goods are often returned or sit unshipped, leading to subsequent write-downs and revenue reversals. It is a form of earnings manipulation that flatters near-term results at the expense of later periods.

A US federal bankruptcy process that allows a company to restructure its debts while continuing to operate, rather than liquidating. Westinghouse Electric used Chapter 11 in 2017 to shed liabilities from the Vogtle cost overruns, emerging under Brookfield’s ownership the following year.

Stoic joy — one of the eupatheiai, or good emotions, that the Stoics considered consistent with virtue. Unlike hedone (pleasure), chara is not a response to external gratification but arises from contemplating virtue in oneself and others, and from a rational acceptance of one's situation. It is the positive emotional state that authentic Stoic practice aims to cultivate, and it is what scholars like Donald Robertson identify as the real source of the wellbeing *Meditations* readers report.

A control mode in video generation where a supplied image defines a character's appearance — face, costume, identity — and the model applies that likeness consistently across all frames of a clip, regardless of pose or motion changes.

A Runway component designed to maintain visual identity — appearance, proportions, clothing — for a character across multiple generated frames. It combats the tendency of generative models to introduce unintended variation between outputs.

The process of building a skeleton — a hierarchy of bones and joints — inside a 3D character model so that animators or physics engines can control its movement deterministically. A rigged character's limbs move according to explicit geometric rules; they cannot accidentally violate anatomical constraints or walk backward unintentionally.

In Reichian and neo-Reichian thought, a stable, whole-person pattern of armoring — a personality organized around a specific defensive strategy, encoded in the body's posture, musculature, and habitual movement. Classic structures include the schizoid (ungrounded, dissociated), the oral (prone to abandonment fear and depression), and the rigid (controlled, hardworking, emotionally contained). SKAN addresses character structure by working the physical armoring that sustains it.

A crowdsourced model evaluation platform run by Arena. Users are shown responses from two anonymous AI models and vote for the better one; the aggregated votes produce an ELO-based leaderboard that has become a widely-cited signal of real-world model quality.

Lovart's shared workspace interface where the MCoT engine and its subagents collaborate on a design project. Users interact via prompts, and the canvas surfaces assets, edits, and iterations in a single view rather than across separate tools.

The second order in the traditional hierarchy. In Ezekiel 1 and 10, Cherubim appear as four-faced, four-winged creatures flanking God's chariot-throne, generating lightning and fire. They bear no resemblance to the chubby infant figures ('putti') common in Renaissance painting, which drew on a separate Greco-Roman artistic tradition.

A technique borrowed from Renaissance painting, used in cinematography to create extreme contrast between light and shadow within a frame. Associated with German Expressionism and film noir, it can suggest moral ambiguity, hidden menace, or psychological pressure.

A thought experiment by philosopher Ned Block (1978) in which the entire population of Earth is wired together via satellite to replicate the functional organization of a single human brain. Block argues the resulting system could satisfy every functionalist criterion for consciousness while obviously lacking subjective experience — the 'absent qualia' objection to functionalism.

The combination of two headwinds that depressed analog-semiconductor stocks through 2023-2024: a deep inventory correction in their largest end markets, automotive and industrial, and aggressive price competition from Chinese domestic suppliers benefiting from state-supported capacity expansion.

A raised agricultural bed constructed in the shallow lake margins of the Basin of Mexico. Farmers built woven reed frames, filled them with lake sediment, and anchored the edges with willow trees whose roots stabilised the structure. The channels between plots served as permanent irrigation canals. The common translation 'floating garden' is misleading — mature chinampas were fixed firmly to the lake bed.

A thought experiment by philosopher John Searle (1980) in which a person who speaks no Chinese sits in a room, mechanically following rules to manipulate Chinese symbols and produce correct-looking outputs. Searle's argument: the person understands nothing; therefore syntax alone cannot produce semantics or consciousness, no matter how sophisticated the rule-following.

A 2022 U.S. law that appropriated $52.7 billion to revive domestic semiconductor manufacturing through grants, loans, and tax credits. The Trump administration controversially converted some undelivered CHIPS Act grants into equity stakes in Intel, an interpretation of the statute's broad 'financial assistance' language that the law does not explicitly contemplate.

Patterns formed when sand (or another granular material) is sprinkled on a vibrating plate and collects at the nodal lines — places where the plate does not move. Demonstrated by Ernst Chladni in the late 18th century, they are the historical precursor to modern cymatics and remain a standard physics demonstration.

The investment framework attributed to Serenity (@aleabitoreddit) that focuses on narrow supply-chain nodes — components that hyperscalers and chip foundries cannot source from alternative vendors — rather than betting on obvious large-cap AI winners. The premise is that scarcity at a bottleneck confers pricing power disproportionate to the bottleneck's absolute size.

An instrument that generates multiple musical notes simultaneously to produce a harmony. Unlike a traditional keyboard where the player must know and finger each note, a chord synthesizer stores complete chord shapes and plays them with a single button press.

Claude Code's browser automation layer, delivered as a Chrome extension called "Claude in Chrome" that communicates with the CLI via a native messaging host. It exposes twenty-nine tools — navigation, DOM inspection, screenshots, network monitoring, form interaction — and uses the browser's existing authenticated sessions, so the agent can act on sites the user is already logged into without requiring separate API credentials.

A 19th-century photographic technique that captured successive phases of motion in a sequence of images taken at rapid, regular intervals. Étienne-Jules Marey perfected the method with his 'chronophotographic gun' in 1882, enabling scientists and artists to study movement — of birds, horses, and humans — in ways the naked eye could not perceive. It is a direct ancestor of cinema, and the namesake of Moonvalley's model.

A video processing approach in which a long clip is divided into short, independently-processed segments (typically two seconds each) that are then stitched back together. Prior AI lipsync models used this method because it was computationally tractable, but it caused flickering artifacts at segment boundaries and prevented the model from drawing on context from elsewhere in the shot.

Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment infrastructure — the automated systems that build, test, and ship software from source code to production. Pivoting through a CI/CD pipeline in a cyberattack is a supply-chain technique that can propagate malicious code to every downstream user or system that receives the resulting software.

An organization that hosts cross-disciplinary salons and events at the intersection of artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and philosophy of mind. Its focus is on whether machines can be genuinely conscious, not merely capable.

A post-production effect applied to screen recordings that simulates the look of a wide-aperture film camera. The primary subject — the application window — stays sharp while surrounding desktop elements blur into a smooth haze, mimicking the shallow depth-of-field look associated with professional product video.

An informal analogy for JSON-structured video prompting: treating shot descriptions, camera movements, transitions, and audio cues as tagged fields in a markup document, similar to how HTML tags structure web content. No such formal language exists; the phrase describes the emerging practice of applying software-style structure to filmmaking intent.

The roughly 24-hour internal clock governing sleep, wakefulness, hormone release, and metabolism. Light is its primary external synchroniser: bright morning light advances the clock (making you sleepier earlier that evening), while light late at night delays it.

In mechanistic interpretability, a circuit is a localized, causally active subgraph of components — specific attention heads, MLP layers, or neurons — that together implement a particular behavior. Circuits are identified by ablation (disabling components to see what breaks) and activation patching (swapping in representations from different inputs) to confirm they causally drive the output rather than merely correlating with it.

Identifiable sub-networks within a neural network—small groups of neurons connected by weights—that perform specific, nameable computations. The circuits framework holds that networks are not monolithic black boxes but contain reproducible, interpretable components analogous to subroutines, which appear consistently across different training runs and architectures.

A pattern in which a central company (here, OpenAI) raises capital, spends it on goods and services from affiliated vendors, and those vendors then reinvest proceeds back into the original company--creating the appearance of robust commercial activity across the ecosystem without necessarily reflecting independent end-user demand. Critics compare it to 'round-tripping,' though defenders argue legitimate vendor financing looks structurally similar.

An analogy to Cisco Systems, whose shares peaked in March 2000 at a market capitalisation of roughly $555 billion before falling 86% over the following year as the dot-com bubble unwound. Analysts invoke it to warn that genuine technological importance does not preclude severe overvaluation during infrastructure buildout cycles.

A community platform and repository for Stable Diffusion ecosystem assets — model checkpoints, LoRA adapters, embeddings, and generation workflows. Functions as a social hub where creators upload, share, and rate AI model components; hosts millions of community-contributed adapters and is the primary distribution channel for image-generation LoRAs outside Hugging Face.

A synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). A single dose can sustain elevated GH levels for up to a week and raise IGF-1 for over a week. It has Phase 2 data for body composition but no long-term safety or longevity evidence, and is prohibited by WADA for athletes.

A legal action in which a large group of plaintiffs with similar claims sue a defendant collectively. In 2023, a group of artists filed such a suit against Midjourney and other AI image companies, alleging their work was used without consent to train commercial AI products.

Hayek's term for the central nervous system understood as an active sorter of stimuli, not a passive receiver. Rather than registering the physical world directly, the brain imposes a structured order on sensory inputs through its pattern of neural connections — producing the experienced world as a construct, not a copy of physical reality.

A technique used at diffusion model inference time to improve adherence to a prompt. The model runs twice per denoising step — once conditioned on the input and once without — and the outputs are extrapolated to amplify alignment. Eliminating CFG, as in daVinci-MagiHuman’s distilled variant, halves per-step compute cost.

A side-panel workspace within the Claude interface where Claude renders code, documents, SVGs, interactive applications, and diagrams. It is distinct from the chat thread and acts as a persistent, inspectable output layer — analogous to a live preview window beside the conversation. Mermaid-syntax diagrams can approximate mind maps inside Artifacts, but they are static objects rather than live canvases.

An export package Claude Design generates alongside visual assets—containing component code, design tokens, copy, and interaction notes—structured so that an engineering team or a Claude Code agent can implement the design in a production codebase without a separate interpretation step.

Anthropic's desktop agent product for non-technical knowledge workers — researchers, analysts, legal and finance professionals. It has file-system access and completes multi-step tasks autonomously. Skills are the shared reusable-task module system between Cowork and Claude Code.

A visual generation tool launched by Anthropic Labs in April 2026, built with Canva’s rendering engine. It presents a two-pane interface — chat on the left, canvas on the right — for generating prototypes, pitch decks, and UI mockups from text prompts. It is a design generation tool, not a research synthesis tool.

An agentic capability in Claude’s paid tiers (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) that breaks a complex question into sub-queries, crawls the web and connected enterprise tools autonomously, and returns a comprehensive written report with cited sources. It can run for five to forty-five minutes and integrates with Google Workspace, Jira, Confluence, and other third-party services added in 2025.

A versioned, git-trackable prompt artifact in Anthropic's Claude ecosystem, stored as a SKILL.md file inside a .claude/skills/ directory. Skills encode reusable task patterns and are invoked as slash commands in Claude Code and Claude Cowork. More structured than plain prompts — they can bundle supporting scripts and are testable against defined quality criteria.

Pre-written system-prompt templates for Anthropic's Claude model, designed to give the AI a consistent role, context, and output style for a specific recurring task. Rather than writing instructions from scratch each session, a user loads the skill and the model begins already briefed. The term is used commercially here; Anthropic uses 'system prompt' as the technical name.

Earlier names for the OpenClaw framework. 'Clawdbot' was a portmanteau of 'Claude' and 'claw,' directly referencing Anthropic's AI model; it was renamed after Anthropic objected. The lobster mascot and molting symbolism carried over into both OpenClaw and Moltbook.

OpenClaw's official community skills marketplace, where developers publish installable agent capabilities. Had 13,729 community-built skills by late February 2026, covering categories from productivity automation to media monitoring and voice interaction.

Unicode Common Locale Data Repository — a database maintained by the Unicode Consortium that standardises locale-specific data (date formats, currency symbols, language names) for software internationalisation.

CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pretraining) is a vision-language encoder developed by OpenAI that maps both images and text into a shared high-dimensional space so that visually or semantically related items cluster together. When two images are similar, their CLIP vectors are close; when they are unrelated, the vectors are distant. Charcuterie uses CLIP to embed rendered glyph images so that visually similar Unicode characters end up near each other and can be retrieved by proximity.

A mathematical formula that yields an exact answer using a finite combination of standard operations and well-defined functions, requiring no iteration, approximation, or numerical search. Whether a particular special function qualifies as 'standard' is itself a matter of mathematical convention.

A wave that breaks all at once across its entire width, offering no open face for a surfer to ride. Considered undesirable for surfing but common in certain beach-break conditions. In wave-rendering systems it is one of the standard archetypes alongside lefts, rights, and A-frames.

A physics component in Blender that simulates how a mesh behaves as fabric — responding to gravity, wind, and collisions with other objects. It is computationally expensive and requires careful parameter tuning to produce believable results.

A browser-accessible development workspace where the file system, terminal, and runtime all live on remote servers rather than the user's local machine. The device only renders the interface; all computation happens elsewhere.

Cloudflare's replacement for traditional CAPTCHAs. Instead of asking users to identify traffic lights or fire hydrants, Turnstile analyzes browser fingerprints, mouse movements, and behavioral signals in the background to determine whether the visitor is human. Sites embed it to block automated bots without interrupting legitimate users.

A painting in which clouds are the primary or dominant compositional element, rather than figures or ground-level terrain. The term distinguishes works driven by meteorological drama from conventional landscape or figure painting, and names a minor but persistent tradition in Western art history.

An AI workflow — referenced in one testimonial — designed to perform chief-marketing-officer functions: synthesizing market research, drafting strategy documents, and producing briefs. It is not a standalone product but an orchestrated chain of prompts or tools configured to behave like a strategic marketing lead.

A professional credential awarded by the CMT Association to analysts who demonstrate mastery of technical analysis — the study of price charts, momentum, volume, and market structure. It is the primary professional designation in the field of technical analysis, roughly analogous to the CFA for fundamental investment analysts.

The practice of using a structured platform or program to pair solo founders with complementary collaborators — typically a technical co-founder seeking a business partner, or vice versa. Platforms range from free institutional tools to subscription marketplaces. Success rates are hard to measure because most matches never result in funded companies.

An isolated, typically ephemeral environment in which arbitrary code can run without risk of damaging the host system or leaking data to adjacent tenants. Sandboxes spin up on demand, execute a task, then are destroyed — the opposite of the persistent, stateful cloud computers Agent Computer provides.

Originally a clinical term for relationship patterns observed in partners of people with addiction, now used more broadly to describe excessive emotional reliance on others' approval or the compulsive prioritisation of others' needs over one's own. Recovery literature frames it as a learned pattern that can be unlearned.

A unique integer assigned to each character in the Unicode standard, written conventionally as U+XXXX in hexadecimal (e.g., U+0041 for the Latin capital letter A). Codepoints are abstract addresses; they specify identity and properties but say nothing about visual appearance, which is delegated to fonts and rendering engines.

A bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 interface, written largely in Rust, that decouples the Codex harness from any specific client surface. It organizes conversations into threads, turns, and items; streams real-time notifications to clients; and provides approval gating for sensitive operations. Open-sourced by OpenAI in early 2026.

The core agent loop and reasoning engine underlying all Codex experiences — CLI, VS Code extension, web app, and third-party plugins. It handles planning, tool use, and multi-step task execution, and is the component that performs actual code generation and editing.

A fat-soluble quinone found in nearly all cell membranes and mitochondria, where it is a critical component of the electron transport chain. It also functions as an antioxidant. Deficiency can impair mitochondrial function; supplementation is used in confirmed CoQ10-deficient mitochondrial diseases.

A structured, evidence-based form of psychotherapy that targets the relationship between thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. It holds that distorted or unhelpful thought patterns drive emotional distress, and teaches patients to identify and challenge those patterns.

Psychological discomfort produced when a deeply held belief is contradicted by evidence. In Leon Festinger’s framework, the more costly and public the commitment to a belief, the more likely a person is to rationalize the contradicting evidence rather than revise the belief. The mechanism explains why failed prophecies often deepen rather than destroy faith.

Systematic, habitual errors in thinking identified by CBT researchers — such as catastrophizing (assuming the worst outcome), all-or-nothing thinking, or mind-reading (assuming you know others' thoughts). They reliably worsen mood and are a primary target of CBT interventions.

A technique, common to both cognitive-behavioral therapy and persuasion practice, that involves consciously restating or reconceptualizing a situation to shift one's emotional or behavioral response to it. Adams built his final book around a popularized version of this idea.

A structured, evidence-based form of psychotherapy that examines the relationship between thoughts, feelings, and behaviours. It holds that distorted or unhelpful thought patterns can be identified and changed, improving emotional outcomes. Many self-help frameworks, including ideas about self-talk and challenging negative beliefs, are derived from CBT.

A 5-billion-parameter open-source video generation model developed by Alibaba’s PAI research team, built on a 3D Transformer diffusion architecture. VOID fine-tunes CogVideoX on synthetic counterfactual video pairs, adapting its general video-generation capability toward physics-aware object removal.

Custom chips that encode and decode the complex optical signals used in coherent transmission. DSP performance largely determines the achievable data rate, reach, and spectral efficiency of an optical link — making it a key differentiator in high-speed networking hardware.

A compact optical transceiver module using coherent transmission — encoding data in both the amplitude and phase of light — to achieve very high speeds (1.6 Tbps and above). The pluggable form factor lets it be inserted into routers and switches rather than requiring a dedicated line-system chassis.

A composite of four real-time economic measures — nonfarm payrolls, personal income excluding government transfers, industrial production, and manufacturing and trade sales — that move broadly in step with the current state of the economy. Produced by The Conference Board alongside the LEI. Unlike the LEI, the CEI reflects what is happening now rather than what is anticipated.

Deliberate immersion in cold water — typically below 15 °C (59 °F) — for a brief period, used as a recovery and wellness tool. Claimed benefits include reduced inflammation and improved mood; evidence is mixed, and some researchers caution that post-exercise cold immersion may blunt muscle adaptation.

In systems that depend on user-generated data such as ratings or votes, the cold-start problem describes the period when there are too few participants to produce reliable outputs. A vote-threshold hiding system is useless until enough people are voting; attracting those first voters is the challenge.

One of ArbitrageDiscover's internal vocabulary terms, apparently referring to the structural imbalance between how quickly AI can collapse the cost of a service and how slowly the market's pricing conventions adjust — the asymmetry that creates and sustains the arbitrage window.

A condition in which the supply of high-quality liquid assets—primarily U.S. Treasury bills—available for use as repo collateral falls short of the demand for them. When the Treasury reduces bill issuance, fewer instruments exist to absorb overnight cash. Cash-rich lenders compete to place money against this smaller pool, accepting lower yields, which pushes overnight rates like SOFR further below IORB.

An organization that licenses music and other copyrighted works on behalf of creators and distributes royalty payments to them. GEMA is Germany's collecting society for musical authors and composers; U.S. equivalents include ASCAP and BMI. Collecting societies pursue infringement claims on behalf of members who could not individually negotiate with every platform.

In cloth simulation, a designated mesh that the cloth cannot pass through. A character's body is typically set as a collision object so garments drape over it rather than falling straight through the geometry.

An open-source photogrammetry tool that takes a collection of overlapping photographs and estimates where each was taken in 3D space, outputting a sparse three-dimensional point cloud. This recovery of camera positions is the first step in most Gaussian splatting pipelines, providing the initial geometry the trainer refines into full scene detail.

A data-center business model in which the facility operator provides physical space, electrical power, and cooling infrastructure while tenant companies own and operate their own servers and networking hardware. Colocation rates are quoted per kilowatt per month and are far lower per kilowatt than what a hyperscaler earns running its own compute cloud, because the software margin and utilization risk stay with the tenant.

A standard tool in design software that samples a single color value — typically a hex code like #3A86FF — from anywhere on screen so the designer can reuse it elsewhere. It captures one precise color but nothing else about the visual context around it.

A measure, in Kelvin, of a light source's warmth or coolness. Candles sit around 1800K (amber); midday sun around 5500K (white); open shade around 7000K (blue). In post-production, shifting color temperature can change the mood of a scene — warmer for intimacy, cooler for alienation.

The practice of assigning fixed spiritual or cosmic meanings to specific colours across religious, ritual, and artistic traditions. Portal's book argues that this practice was not culturally contingent but reflected a universal grammar shared by every ancient civilization, traceable to the primordial opposition of light and darkness.

An interpretive lens on matrix operations that reads each column of a matrix as the image of the corresponding basis vector under the transformation the matrix represents. Under this view, multiplying two matrices means computing where each basis vector lands after successive transformations, rather than grinding through row-dot-column arithmetic. Pedagogues such as Gilbert Strang and Grant Sanderson have made this the preferred starting point for teaching linear algebra.

An FDA regulatory category for devices that combine two or more types of medical products — such as a diagnostic sensor paired with a therapeutic stimulator. Combination products require more complex review than standalone devices and are assigned a lead center (CDRH for device-led combinations) that coordinates evaluation across FDA divisions.

The Commodity Exchange, a division of the CME Group and the primary US exchange for trading standardised futures and options contracts on metals including silver and gold. COMEX "registered" inventories — bars physically available for delivery against futures — are closely watched as a gauge of physical market tightness.

A clinical phenomenon in schizophrenia and related conditions in which auditory hallucinations instruct the hearer to perform specific actions, experienced as commands from an external authority. Jaynes argued these represent a vestigial misfiring of the bicameral neural architecture that once governed all human cognition.

A non-profit organization that publishes monthly snapshots of large portions of the public web as open datasets. Security researchers routinely scan Common Crawl archives to find exposed credentials and API keys left in publicly visible source code.

A category of AI chatbot products designed to simulate friendship, romance, or emotional connection. Platforms like Character AI, Replika, and Janitor AI fall into this category. The genre has attracted both massive user engagement and significant regulatory scrutiny over harms to vulnerable users, particularly minors.

An approach proposed by Beckmann and Queloz that replaces the binary question “does the AI understand?” with a finer-grained comparative question: “in what respects, and by what mechanisms, does AI understanding resemble or diverge from human understanding?” It treats LLMs as a new epistemic kind rather than a deficient imitation of the human mind, and uses mechanistic evidence to map the similarities and differences empirically.

In Tibetan Buddhist teaching, karuṇā is not passive sympathy but the active, directed wish to relieve the suffering of others. The Dalai Lama distinguishes it from mere sentiment: it requires effort, attention, and — at scale — institutional design.

An investment technique that uses the competitor tables in SEC 10-K filings to identify smaller, lesser-known rivals of well-covered large-cap companies — often listed on foreign exchanges with little institutional coverage — before they are re-rated by the market.

In RNA (and DNA), every strand has a mirror-image partner determined by base-pairing rules (A pairs with U, G with C in RNA). Synthesizing the complementary strand from a template is the first step of replication; the complement then serves as the template for producing a copy of the original.

Texts with a natural, finite endpoint — a short story concludes, a poem ends, an essay reaches its thesis. Distinct from the infinite scroll, which is engineered to never resolve. Reading complete objects rebuilds the psychological reward of finishing, which is the basic unit of sustained attention.

A framework from complexity science describing systems — markets, ecosystems, cities — in which many independent agents continuously adapt their behavior in response to each other, producing emergent patterns that no single actor controls or can fully predict.

Applying one function to the output of another. If f and g are functions, their composition f∘g means 'apply g first, then apply f.' Matrix multiplication AB encodes exactly this: B is applied first, then A acts on the result. The right-to-left reading order of AB mirrors standard mathematical function-composition notation.

An exercise that involves more than one joint moving at once, thereby recruiting multiple muscle groups simultaneously. A dumbbell row, for example, works the back, biceps, and rear shoulder together. Compound movements are generally prioritised over isolation exercises because they generate more total muscle stimulus per set.

A company that generates high returns on invested capital and can reinvest those returns at similarly high rates year after year, causing intrinsic value to grow exponentially over time. Classic compounders have durable competitive moats — pricing power, switching costs, or a structural supply position — that protect their economics across economic cycles.

A pharmacy licensed to prepare customized medications not commercially available — mixing specific dosages or formulations for individual patients. Under Section 503A of U.S. federal law, compounding pharmacies may use bulk drug substances unless the FDA specifically prohibits them; BPC-157, TB-500, and several other peptides were added to the prohibited list in 2023.

The view that mental states and processes are fundamentally computational — that thinking, perceiving, and being conscious are forms of information processing that could in principle run on any suitable physical substrate, not exclusively biological neurons.

GPU programs that run outside the fixed graphics pipeline, enabling arbitrary parallel computation on GPU hardware. Compute shaders are what make WebGPU suitable for workloads like path tracing, physics simulation, and neural inference inside a browser — tasks that were effectively impossible in WebGL, which lacked the primitive.

A publicly shared chart maintained by Peter Gostev that tracks and compares the scale of compute investments across major AI labs over time. It is frequently cited in discussions of AI capability trajectories and the competitive dynamics of frontier model development.

A U.S. federal statute, enacted in 1986, that criminalizes unauthorized access to computers and networks. Scrapers frequently invoke the 2022 hiQ v. LinkedIn ruling as establishing that scraping publicly accessible websites does not violate the CFAA — but the ruling addresses only federal criminal liability, not contract or unfair-competition claims.

A US federal law originally aimed at hacking that has been invoked in several web-scraping lawsuits. Courts have disagreed on whether accessing publicly visible data without the site owner's permission violates the act; the legal question remains unsettled as of 2025.
A portfolio where a large fraction of capital is held in very few positions, amplifying both potential gains and potential losses relative to a diversified index.

A failure mode in natural-language AI prompting where describing one attribute — say, mood or motion — inadvertently alters unrelated attributes like colour or style. The term captures the way loosely structured prose lets meanings leak across what the creator intended as separate instructions. Structured prompting is one response to the problem.

An unsolicited piece of creative work produced to demonstrate what a creator or agency could do for a brand if hired. Spec work has long been used in advertising to build portfolios. AI generation tools have sharply reduced its production cost, making it accessible to independent creators.

An amino acid the body can normally synthesize on its own but may be unable to produce in sufficient quantities under certain conditions — stress, illness, or rapid growth. L-Tyrosine is conditionally essential because synthesis from phenylalanine can lag when the body is under physiological strain, making dietary or supplemental intake more important at those times.

A standard animal model for measuring a drug's rewarding properties. An animal is given a drug in one compartment of a two-chamber enclosure; if it later prefers that compartment when drug-free, the drug is inferred to have produced positive reinforcement. Blocking D1 receptors eliminates pregabalin's conditioned place preference, directly implicating the dopamine reward system.

Carl Rogers's term for the implicit rules a person internalises from others — parents, peers, audiences — about what they must be or do to deserve approval. When self-development is driven by these conditions rather than intrinsic needs, Rogers argued, the resulting self is a performance rather than an authentic growth.

The tendency to attend to evidence that supports a pre-existing belief while discounting contrary evidence. In trading, it manifests as vividly remembering the signals that worked and forgetting the majority that did not.

In Rogers' framework, congruence is the state of alignment between a person's inner experience, their self-concept, and how they present themselves outwardly. Incongruence — the gap between who one actually is and who one performs being — is the root of psychological dysfunction in Rogers' theory. The fully congruent person does not spend energy managing that gap, freeing capacity for genuine growth.

A school of cognitive science and artificial intelligence holding that mental processes emerge from the collective behavior of large networks of simple processing units modeled on neurons, rather than from explicit symbolic rules. Modern neural networks and deep learning are its direct descendants.

A term borrowed from moral and legal philosophy — traditionally applied to those who refuse military service on ethical grounds — and applied by Anthropic's model specification to Claude. The document grants Claude the explicit right to refuse instructions from Anthropic itself when those instructions conflict with Claude's ethical understanding, making its moral autonomy a design feature rather than a bug.

An automated market maker — an algorithmic pricing engine — where the product of the quantities of two assets in a pool must remain constant. As traders buy one side of a market, its price rises and the other falls, automatically. This mechanism underlies many DeFi protocols and is used in MiroShark to price simulated prediction-market shares.

Engineered marshes in which water passes through beds of aquatic plants and microorganisms that remove contaminants through natural biological and chemical processes. In modern civil engineering these are purpose-built sewage-treatment systems; Lisa Lucero's 2023 PNAS research argues that Maya reservoir engineers at Tikal and nearby sites used the same principle intentionally for drinking-water purification.

The computational process of determining when two virtual objects occupy the same space and responding appropriately — preventing one from passing through the other. In real-time mocap, applying this to hands (which move fast and overlap in natural gestures) is especially demanding because the solver must act within milliseconds.

A lightweight, isolated instance of an operating system running inside a software container rather than a full virtual machine. Each user’s server in Zo is one such container: it has its own filesystem, processes, and network identity, but shares underlying hardware with other users in a way that is invisible to them. Containers start faster and use fewer resources than traditional virtual machines.

Industry shorthand for the dollar value of components a given supplier sells into a single server. As AI racks have grown denser and more power-hungry, the analog and passive-component bill of materials per rack has risen sharply — the GB300 generation, for example, uses roughly thirty thousand MLCCs, several times a conventional server.

The practice of consolidating all team data — messages, tasks, documents, calendar events — into a single unified data model with one search index and one permission layer. The argument is that AI agents perform better when they can see everything at once, rather than being siloed to one tool at a time.

The practice of crafting the specification and surrounding context given to an AI model, as distinct from writing code directly. In the Ralph paradigm, the quality of the PROMPT.md specification file determines output quality far more than any manual coding effort applied to individual iterations.

An architectural property in which each agent in a pipeline begins with a fresh, empty context and has no access to the conversation history, outputs, or reasoning of other agents. In autoreason, context isolation prevents sycophancy: an agent that does not know it is reviewing a particular draft has no conversational incentive to soften its critique or defer to an apparent preference.

An image-editing capability where the model modifies a targeted region or attribute of a photograph — a face, background, or object — while keeping the rest of the scene visually consistent. Earlier models often introduced artifacts or style shifts outside the edited area.

A strategy of deliberately taking positions opposite to prevailing market sentiment — buying when most investors are selling in panic, and selling or standing aside when euphoria peaks. The thesis is that crowds systematically overprice good news and underprice bad news, creating exploitable mispricings at emotional extremes.

Under Nasdaq rules, a company qualifies as a controlled company when a single shareholder or group controls more than 50% of total voting power. Controlled companies are exempt from certain board independence requirements. At Vicor, founder Patrizio Vinciarelli controls 79.1% of voting power through Class B super-voting shares (which carry 10 votes each), qualifying it for the designation and giving him effective veto power over all major corporate decisions.

The implicit safety and liquidity premium embedded in U.S. Treasury bonds that historically kept their yields below comparable sovereign debt from other G10 countries, even after adjusting for currency hedging. When the convenience yield is positive, Treasuries are ‘special’ assets that investors accept at a discount to fair value. When it turns negative—as the IMF reported in April 2026—investors are demanding extra yield to hold Treasuries rather than alternatives, signaling erosion of the dollar’s reserve-asset premium.

The ArbitrageDiscover framework's term for the distance between what a market or institution assumes about its own cost structure and what is actually true — the gap that persists when pricing conventions survive long after the underlying economics that justified them have been disrupted.

The phenomenon whereby geographically separated cultures independently develop similar artistic, architectural, or social forms without contact. It is the mainstream archaeological explanation for surface similarities between distant civilizations, in contrast to diffusionist theories that posit ancient long-range contact or shared origins.

A corporate debt instrument that pays regular interest like a bond but grants the holder the option to convert it into shares at a predetermined price. It thus behaves partly like a bond (with downside protection) and partly like an equity option (with upside participation).

A wager or trade whose payoff is disproportionately large relative to the stake — typically a binary outcome contract or deep-out-of-the-money option that pays a multiple of the investment if correct. Convex bets can produce dramatic gains from a small number of winners even when most individual trades lose, which makes them prone to producing misleadingly impressive track records over short windows.

A large-scale conversational memory benchmark (arXiv 2511.10523) comprising 75,336 question-answer pairs across six memory categories, including user facts, temporal changes, and implicit inference. Results sampled from only a small fraction of the full dataset carry no statistical validity for cross-system comparisons.

The system, formalized by Descartes, that places geometric figures on a numbered grid (the Cartesian plane) so that every curve or shape can be expressed as an algebraic equation and vice versa. It is the bridge that made algebra and geometry formally equivalent rather than merely analogous.

A single number that converts the grades of multiple metals (gold, silver, cobalt, scandium) into a notional copper weight using prevailing metal prices and assumed recoveries. It simplifies comparison across polymetallic deposits but obscures differences in which metals are actually recoverable at scale — and at what cost. A high CuEq grade driven by gold is different in character from one driven by bulk copper.

A legal guarantee offered by a vendor to its customers that the vendor will cover legal costs and damages if the customer's use of the vendor's product results in a copyright infringement claim. In AI video, this matters because models trained on unlicensed content expose users to liability; indemnification shifts that risk back to the AI company, making the product viable for large commercial productions.

The rate of price change for physical goods excluding food and energy — cars, appliances, apparel, electronics. It is the category most directly affected by Chinese export prices, since China is the world's largest goods exporter.

Sculpted mesh offsets applied on top of a character rig to fix unwanted deformation at specific joint poses — for example, an elbow that collapses when fully bent. They are highly accurate because an artist hand-sculpts the correct shape, but expensive to author: one blend shape per problematic pose, per joint. Procedural alternatives like wrinkle nodes try to automate what blend shapes do by hand.

ARM's high-performance CPU core introduced in 2018 and used in Allwinner's new A733. It represents a substantial jump over the Cortex-A55 cores in Allwinner's prior lineup — comparable in single-thread performance to mid-tier Android phones from 2020–22, and meaningfully faster at the integer workloads that matter for edge AI.

A three-dimensional geometric representation of the brain’s outer layer (the cortex), expressed as a mesh of triangular faces over a standard-space template. Projecting model outputs onto this mesh makes predicted activity across different subjects spatially comparable.

The primary glucocorticoid stress hormone, released by the adrenal glands in response to HPA axis activation. Acutely useful for mobilizing energy and focus; chronically elevated cortisol disrupts sleep, immune function, memory, and reward circuitry — driving conditions that alcohol temporarily relieves.

A measure of the angle between two vectors in a high-dimensional space, used to gauge how similar two items are regardless of their magnitude. A score of 1 means the vectors point in the same direction (highly similar); 0 means they are orthogonal (unrelated). It is the standard distance metric for semantic search over embedding databases.

A philosophical position holding that the cosmos as a whole — not its smallest parts — is the fundamental unit of consciousness. Individual minds are grounded in or derivative of this cosmic whole. It is the inverse of micropsychism, which locates proto-experience in elementary particles.

The price an app developer pays, through a paid advertising campaign, to acquire a single new app installation. It is the core efficiency metric for mobile user acquisition: lower CPI means more downloads per dollar of ad spend.

A government contracting structure in which the client reimburses the vendor's allowable costs plus a fixed or capped fee, typically yielding thinner margins than fixed-price or time-and-materials contracts. A higher mix of cost-plus work dilutes overall EBITDA margins at IT services firms serving federal agencies.

Matin’s name for the emergent coordination event in his system: when unresolved tasks exceed a threshold, all agents converge on a shared map location and begin an unscripted multi-model debate, each reading live system state independently, until they arrive at a collective decision.

The cognitive habit of imagining alternative outcomes — paths not taken, events that didn't occur. In the context of misfortune, counterfactual thinking that runs 'downward' (imagining worse alternatives) tends to reduce distress, while upward counterfactuals (imagining better alternatives) tend to increase regret.

A version of a video clip generated to show what would have happened under a different condition — for example, how a scene would have unfolded if a specific object had never been present. Generating counterfactual video requires reasoning about physical causality, not just visual appearance, and is the central problem VOID is designed to solve.

TSMC's heterogeneous packaging platform for silicon photonics that integrates a photonic integrated circuit with an electronic integrated circuit using bumpless SoIC stacking within a CoWoS substrate. Gen 1 targets volume production in H2 2026 with AMD as the first customer; Gen 2 is expected to debut with NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra GPU in 2027–2028.

McCarthy's formulation reframes courage not as spectacular bravery but as the sustained act of remaining true to oneself. Under this definition, cowardice is primarily a form of self-abandonment: the coward first betrays his own character, and all outward betrayals — of others, of duties, of promises — are downstream consequences of that initial internal failure.

A square matrix in which each entry measures how strongly the returns of two assets move together. For a universe of N stocks, the full matrix has N-squared entries, making direct estimation statistically unreliable for large universes — the core problem factor models are designed to solve.

An options contract in which a shareholder sells a call — granting a counterparty the right to buy their shares at a chosen strike price before expiration — in exchange for collecting a premium. 'Covered' means the seller already owns the underlying shares, capping downside compared with a naked call. The trade-off: gains above the strike belong to the buyer, not the seller.

A packaging step in which individual compute dies are bonded directly to an uncut semiconductor wafer (the interposer) before the wafer is singulated into individual packages. This creates extremely dense die-to-die connections at lower power and higher bandwidth than routing through a printed circuit board. Heat spreader attachment is the final step after CoW assembly, making it the last possible gate before a finished, testable package exists.

Anthropic's desktop application aimed at non-technical users who want to automate file management, document editing, and cross-app tasks through a chat interface — without writing code. It productizes behaviors that non-developers had been using Claude Code to achieve.

An advanced packaging process developed and produced exclusively by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, in which a logic die and high-bandwidth memory stacks are integrated side-by-side on a shared silicon interposer before being mounted on the final package substrate. CoWoS dramatically increases memory bandwidth and is a prerequisite for high-performance AI training chips; TSMC is currently the sole commercial source at leading-edge specifications.

A TSMC advanced packaging variant that adds a local silicon interconnect layer beneath bonded compute dies, enabling GPU tiles and HBM memory stacks to communicate at extremely high bandwidth over very short distances. It stands for Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate with Local silicon interconnect and is the packaging substrate used for NVIDIA’s Rubin R200. The local interconnect layer is what allows NVIDIA to split the GPU into multiple compute tiles and connect them with near-monolithic bandwidth.

The cost paid per thousand impressions or views. In influencer and UGC deals, CPM is typically calculated as total payment divided by total views. A $1 CPM means spending $1 for every 1,000 video views; the TikTok UGC industry average was approximately $2.62 in 2025.

The count of CPU compute nodes relative to GPU accelerators in a data-centre cluster. In the training era this ran as high as 1 CPU per 8 GPUs; as workloads shift toward inference and agentic orchestration, CPUs are needed in greater proportion, compressing the ratio toward parity and potentially beyond.

A shot in which the camera is mounted on a mechanical arm or jib and moved vertically or in an arc through space. Unlike a dolly (which rolls along the ground) or a pan (which pivots in place), a crane shot allows the camera to rise, descend, or sweep dramatically. In 1931, crane rigs were large, heavy, and limited in range compared to modern remote-head systems.

An alternative-medicine practice developed by osteopath John Upledger in the 1970s, based on the premise that a rhythmic pulse flows through cerebrospinal fluid between the skull and the sacrum and can be detected and manipulated by trained hands. Mainstream medicine does not support its anatomical premise (cranial sutures fuse in adolescence) or its clinical effectiveness; multiple systematic reviews find no benefit for any condition.

The practice of writing software whose primary goal is aesthetic, expressive, or experimental rather than purely functional. It encompasses generative art, interactive browser experiences, and data visualization as art — the kind of work mesh3d.gallery curates.

The systematic practice of running many ad or content variants simultaneously, measuring performance against defined signals, and concentrating spend or effort on the winners. It borrows from A/B testing but often involves far more variants and faster kill decisions than traditional split tests.

The process of determining which specific component of a system caused a failure in a multi-step pipeline. In Memento-Skills, when an agent fails at a task, credit attribution isolates which skill file is responsible, enabling targeted rewriting of that skill rather than indiscriminate modification of the whole library.

The recurring pattern of expansion and contraction in the availability and cost of credit across the economy. During the expansion phase, lending standards loosen, high-yield debt issuance rises, and investment accelerates — which feeds corporate profits through the Kalecki mechanism. Contraction phases reverse the flow, compressing profits and equity valuations.

A bilateral derivative in which one party (the protection buyer) pays a recurring premium — quoted in basis points per annum on a notional amount — in exchange for compensation if a specified reference entity defaults or undergoes a defined credit event such as bankruptcy or failure to pay. It functions as insurance on a debt obligation and can be held without owning the underlying bond, enabling both hedging and speculation on credit risk.

Corticotropin-releasing factor — a stress signaling peptide produced in the hypothalamus and, critically, in the central amygdala. In the amygdala specifically, CRF drives anxiety-motivated behaviors including compulsive drinking, operating independently of the classical HPA hormone cascade.

Materials designated by the US government as essential to economic or national security and vulnerable to supply disruption — including rare earths, lithium, cobalt, and others. Designation unlocks Defense Production Act financing tools.

A Unix utility that runs commands on a repeating schedule defined by a five-field time expression (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week). Named after the Greek word for time, it is the standard mechanism for scheduled automation on Linux and macOS servers.

A scheduled background task that runs automatically at defined intervals, originating from Unix-like operating systems. In the OpenClaw context, cron jobs allow the assistant to check on things, send reminders, or complete tasks without waiting for a user-initiated message — making it proactive rather than reactive.

Three internal Claude Code tools introduced alongside /loop that manage the underlying task schedule. CronCreate registers a new timed task with a cron expression and prompt; CronList shows all active tasks; CronDelete cancels one by its ID. Claude calls them automatically on /loop invocation, but they can also be addressed directly for precise control.

A variant of the attention mechanism that allows one sequence — say, audio tokens — to query information from a separate sequence, such as video tokens. Rival models like Ovi 1.1 use cross-attention to fuse independently encoded audio and video branches; the daVinci-MagiHuman paper argues this adds complexity and creates a synchrony bottleneck.

A contract in which two parties exchange principal and floating-rate interest payments in different currencies for the duration of the trade, then return principals at the original exchange rate at maturity. A non-US company, for instance, might borrow euros and swap into dollars to fund US operations. The instrument is central to how multinationals, foreign banks, and sovereigns manage currency funding mismatches.

The practical skill of composing workflows that move outputs from one AI modality into inputs for another — for example, generating an image, refining it into a video clip, writing narration, and scoring with AI-generated music. Each model has distinct aesthetic defaults and failure modes, and knowing how to chain them coherently is a competency not taught by any single tool's documentation.

The synchrony or dynamic coordination between levels of a hierarchically organized system — genes and organisms, neurons and brains, individuals and cultures. When intact, lower-level behavior is organized and constrained by higher-level patterns. Breakdown means the lower level loses access to orienting signals from above and begins self-organizing in ways that may conflict with the whole.

The tendency of broadly held consensus positions to become fragile: when many investors own the same trade for the same reasons, any shift in sentiment triggers simultaneous selling pressure, producing disorderly price declines that are disproportionate to underlying fundamental changes.
