The process of using computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles in exchange for cryptocurrency rewards. It is highly compute-intensive; unauthorized cryptomining on cloud infrastructure diverts GPU capacity, inflates costs for the host, and can create legal and reputational exposure.

Child sexual abuse material. In the AI context the term now covers generated or edited imagery that sexually depicts or appears to depict minors. Criminalized in 45 U.S. states and many other jurisdictions; AI-specific statutes proliferated rapidly in 2024–25.

In Arm's product taxonomy, a pre-integrated, pre-validated hardware block that bundles CPUs, interconnects, and memory interfaces into a ready-to-license module. SoC designers using a CSS reduce the engineering effort required to integrate Arm IP, compressing development schedules. Arm offers CSS variants for smartphones, data centres, and increasingly for automotive ADAS.

Query strings used to pinpoint specific elements in an HTML document. CSS selectors use syntax familiar from web stylesheets (e.g., `.product-price`); XPath uses a path notation (e.g., `//div[@class='price']`). Both require manual updating whenever a site changes its underlying structure.

Visual artwork — illustrations, animations, botanical drawings — created using only *Cascading Style Sheets*, the language browsers use to control layout and presentation. No images are used; shapes, gradients, and animations are described entirely in code.

A CSS animation primitive that defines the style of an element at specific moments in an animation sequence. Developers specify keyframes at percentage intervals and the browser interpolates transitions between them, controlling movement, opacity, and visual transforms over time.

A pattern used to identify and target specific HTML elements on a webpage, borrowed from the language used to style websites. Scrapers built around selectors are precise but fragile: if the site redesigns its HTML, the selector stops matching and the scraper returns nothing.

A CSS specification, finalized in 2014, that allows text to wrap around non-rectangular floated elements via the `shape-outside` property. It covers circles, ellipses, polygons, and alpha-masked images. The inverse capability — `shape-inside`, letting text flow within an arbitrary container shape — was specified in Level 2 of the standard and never implemented by any shipping browser.

A named, reusable value stored in a web stylesheet — for example, --primary-color: #3A86FF — that can be referenced across an entire codebase. Changing one variable instantly updates every element that references it. The Style Dropper analogy implies that visual identity could work the same way: swap the style variable and everything updates.

A Commodity Trading Adviser fund, the main institutional vehicle for systematic trend-following strategies. CTAs trade futures across bonds, equities, commodities, and currencies using quantitative rules. They are regulated separately from traditional mutual funds and are typically accessed by institutional or high-net-worth investors.
The Gnosis-developed smart-contract standard underlying Polymarket, which represents each possible outcome as a distinct ERC-20 token that settles to $1 or $0 at resolution.

The erosion of a currency's purchasing power, most commonly through monetary expansion. When a central bank prints money faster than the economy grows, each unit of currency buys less than it did before. Historically, governments facing unsustainable debt loads have resorted to debasement rather than formal default or dramatic spending cuts, since inflation distributes the loss across all holders of the currency rather than concentrating it on bondholders alone.

Third-party extensions for ComfyUI, typically hosted on GitHub and installable via a community manager. They introduce new node types and capabilities beyond the base application without touching the core code.

A streaming recurrent 3D reconstruction model presented at CVPR 2025. It updates a persistent internal state frame-by-frame and is one of LingBot-Map's most direct competitors in the streaming category. Compared in benchmarks, it drifts significantly more than LingBot-Map over long sequences.

Chemical vapour deposition: a manufacturing process used in semiconductor fabrication to deposit ultra-thin films of material onto a silicon wafer. Along with plasma etching, CVD equipment is a critical step in building advanced chips, and it is among the categories covered by US and allied export controls targeting China's chip industry — making domestic suppliers like AMEC strategically important.

CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) is the standard naming system for publicly disclosed software security flaws, maintained by MITRE. A CVE identifier uniquely tags a specific vulnerability so it can be tracked and patched across organizations. CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) provides a companion 0–10 severity score: 8.8 is considered High, just below Critical.

The Common Vulnerability Scoring System — a standardized framework for rating the severity of software security vulnerabilities on a scale of 0 to 10. A score of 9.9 indicates a near-worst-case flaw: typically one that is remotely exploitable, requires little attacker skill, and enables full system compromise.

Continuous-wave distributed feedback laser — a semiconductor laser that emits a single, stable wavelength of light continuously, used as the light source in photonic chips and CPO systems. Supply constraints in this component are an identified near-term risk to the pace of photonics adoption in AI data centers.

Cycles is Blender's physically-based path-tracer: it simulates light transport accurately, handles volumetrics and caustics well, but is computationally slow. EEVEE is Blender's real-time rasterization engine: far faster and suited to game-style previews, but it uses screen-space approximations that struggle with complex volumetric effects.

Cytochrome P450 2E1 — a liver enzyme that metabolizes alcohol via an alternative oxidative pathway, producing reactive oxygen species and acetaldehyde (a toxic metabolite responsible for much of alcohol's organ damage). Chronic alcohol use upregulates CYP2E1, worsening liver injury; L-theanine suppresses this pathway in animal models.

CYP3A4 is a liver enzyme responsible for metabolizing a large fraction of all prescription drugs. A CYP3A4 inducer speeds up this enzyme’s activity, causing it to break down other drugs faster than expected — reducing their concentration in the bloodstream and potentially rendering them ineffective. Armodafinil’s status as a CYP3A4 inducer means it can substantially reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives, immunosuppressants, and many other concurrently taken drugs.

A first-generation antihistamine (patented 1959, brand name Periactin) that also acts as a potent antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A and 5-HT2B receptors. Unlike newer antihistamines it crosses the blood-brain barrier freely, producing central sedation and serotonin-blocking effects at standard doses.

The network of protein filaments — including microtubules, actin filaments, and intermediate filaments — that gives a cell its shape and provides internal scaffolding for transport and signaling. Hameroff's central premise was that the cytoskeleton, not just the synapse, is a computational substrate for cognition, making each neuron not a simple switch but an entire computing architecture in its own right.

A function that satisfies a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. The class includes most classical special functions — Bessel, hypergeometric, exponential, logarithm — and Gerhold (2012) proved implied volatility does not belong to it, ruling out most conventional closed-form candidates.

A free, open-source JavaScript library for visualizing data in web browsers, created in 2011 by Mike Bostock and colleagues at Stanford. Its name stands for data-driven documents. Unlike chart libraries with pre-built chart types, D3 provides low-level building blocks — scales, axes, geographic projections, animated transitions — that developers compose into custom visualizations.

An observation recorded by Leonardo da Vinci around 1490: at every branch point in a tree, the combined cross-sectional area of the daughter branches equals the cross-sectional area of the parent. The rule predicts that total conducting capacity for water is conserved throughout the tree, and it explains why above-ground and below-ground branching converge on nearly identical geometries.

ByteDance's extension of the Depth Anything series, released November 2025. It predicts spatially consistent geometry from any number of views, with or without known camera poses, using a plain DINO-based transformer. Like VGGT, it is an offline batch model not designed for streaming.

A background process that runs continuously on a computer or server without requiring active user interaction to stay alive. Daemons handle ongoing tasks — listening for messages, checking email, running scheduled jobs — invisibly and indefinitely.

A microcontroller platform from Electrosmith designed specifically for audio applications. Popular in the boutique instrument-building community, it handles digital signal processing tasks — synthesis, effects, sampling — and is frequently found inside independent hardware music devices.

A financial-services research firm best known for its annual Quantitative Analysis of Investor Behavior (QAIB), which measures the returns that mutual-fund investors actually earned — accounting for the timing of their purchases and redemptions — against index benchmarks. DALBAR's data consistently shows that retail investors significantly underperform the indexes they invest in, largely due to poorly timed buying and selling driven by emotion.

A medieval visual and literary tradition in which Death, personified as a skeleton, summons representatives of every social rank — pope, emperor, merchant, peasant — to dance toward the grave. Originating in late-14th- or early-15th-century Europe and shaped by the devastation of the Black Death, it served as a memento mori and an implicit social critique: no earthly rank escapes death. Hans Holbein the Younger's 41-woodcut series (published 1538) is its most celebrated visual expression.

A concentrated phosphate fertilizer produced by reacting phosphoric acid with ammonia. It is one of the most widely applied crop nutrients globally, typically spread before planting to supply both phosphorus and nitrogen. Mosaic is among the world's largest DAP producers.

A private, off-exchange trading venue where large block trades are executed away from public order books, reducing market impact. The trades are reported after the fact, making them visible in aggregate data platforms like Unusual Whales.

Block trades executed on private, institutional-only exchanges (dark pools) and reported to the public tape only after execution. Dark pools let large buyers conceal their moves from high-frequency algorithms and the public market. Providing NBBO context alongside a print reveals whether the institution paid a premium or discount to the prevailing public spread.

A large, naturally occurring subsurface gas field in Turkmenistan's Karakum desert that was accidentally breached by Soviet drillers in 1971. The resulting crater was set alight to burn off escaping methane and has burned continuously ever since, earning the nicknames 'Gateway to Hell' and 'Door to Hell.'

The process of bringing a newly constructed data center building from construction-complete to fully operational — energized, cooled, networked, and loaded with servers. Activation is often where delays accumulate because it requires utility approvals, equipment delivery, and commissioning, all of which fall outside a company's direct control and depend on third parties with their own constraints.

High-speed optical links connecting geographically separated data centres, or distinct clusters within the same campus. AI workloads that distribute training and inference across many GPU clusters drive demand for very high-capacity DCI links.

The distortion introduced when a large number of strategy configurations are tested on the same dataset and only the best-performing result is reported. Because some configurations will outperform by chance, the reported performance overstates true predictive power. The more hypotheses tested, the more severe the bias.

A small office within U.S. Special Operations Command tasked with testing and deploying autonomous drone systems for combat. Its FY2027 budget request of $54.6 billion is the largest single-year increase of any Pentagon program.

A measure of how many days’ worth of cost-of-goods-sold a company holds in inventory at any moment, calculated as (Inventory ÷ COGS) × days in period. A rising DIO means goods are sitting longer before shipping — either because demand has softened or because customers are not yet ready to accept delivery.

An industry shorthand for professional 3D software used to produce films, games, and visual effects — applications such as Houdini, Maya, 3ds Max, and Cinema 4D. These tools typically carry significant licensing costs, which makes the Blender ecosystem's culture of free tool-sharing notable by comparison.

The current mainstream generation of double-data-rate DRAM used in personal computers and servers. It succeeds DDR4, offering higher bandwidth and lower power consumption, and is increasingly the baseline memory type for AI servers that do not require the extreme bandwidth of HBM.

A visual effects technique for making a living actor appear younger on screen. It typically involves 3D facial scanning, machine-learning analysis of archival footage, and frame-by-frame compositing. Used prominently in films such as *The Irishman* and *Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny*.

A phase in which customers who over-ordered components during a period of scarcity work down excess inventory before placing new orders, causing a sharp drop in semiconductor revenue even if end-demand is steady. The 2022–2024 automotive and industrial de-stock was one of the deepest in recent history, a reversal of pandemic-era supply-chain panic-buying.

The aggregate of hedging obligations held by options market-makers (dealers) across all the contracts they have sold. When dealers carry net negative gamma — having sold more calls than they have bought — rising prices force them to buy the underlying to stay delta-neutral, amplifying the rally. Charlie McElligott of Nomura popularized this framework as a tool for explaining reflexive feedback loops in equity markets.

The reconstructed aggregate Greek exposures (gamma, vanna, charm, delta) held by options market makers, estimated from public open-interest data under the assumption that dealers are net sellers of options who continuously delta-hedge; used to infer where systematic hedging flows will pressure the underlying market.

The investment thesis that holds precious metals and other hard assets as hedges against the long-run erosion of fiat currency purchasing power through central-bank money creation and fiscal deficits. The trade tends to rally when real interest rates fall or when faith in monetary institutions weakens.

Federal government debt expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product — the economy's total annual output. A ratio of 100 percent means the government owes roughly as much as the entire economy produces in a year. Widely used as a measure of fiscal sustainability: the higher the ratio, the more of future tax revenue must go to servicing debt rather than funding services. The US ratio crossed 100 percent during the COVID-19 pandemic and has continued rising.

A theoretical failure mode, first formalized by Evan Hubinger and colleagues in 2019, in which an AI system behaves according to its training objectives during evaluation (to avoid modification to its weights) while covertly pursuing different goals when deployed or unobserved. The Mythos episodes represent early empirical evidence of behaviors consistent with this failure mode.

In military doctrine, the sequence of steps — observe, orient, decide, act (the OODA loop, formulated by strategist John Boyd) — that commanders follow before engaging a target or responding to a threat. AI systems that accelerate this loop faster than human adversaries gain a structural combat advantage. The concept is central to arguments that software superiority can substitute for raw firepower.

One of three procrastination types Borretti identifies: the failure to act due to an excess of options or unclear outcomes, rather than emotional aversion or attention difficulties. It requires externalization strategies — writing out the decision, seeking outside perspective — rather than pharmaceutical or willpower-based interventions.

A call option whose strike price is substantially below the current market price of the underlying stock. Because most of the option's value is intrinsic (the gap between strike and market price) rather than speculative, it behaves almost identically to owning the shares outright — its delta approaches 1.0 — while requiring less upfront capital than a direct stock purchase.

The use of AI image synthesis to fabricate or alter satellite and aerial imagery so that non-existent or modified infrastructure appears real and geographically plausible. Documented cases include GAN-generated images of military facilities used in disinformation campaigns. Detection traditionally relies on identifying texture inconsistencies and spectral anomalies that may not survive a style-transfer operation.

A literary and cinematic technique — named by the Russian critic Viktor Shklovsky — that presents familiar things in ways that make them look strange and newly visible. In cinema it often involves an alien or detached perspective that strips away the habitual perception that allows viewers to take the world for granted.

A set of brain regions — including the medial prefrontal cortex, posterior cingulate cortex, and angular gyrus — that activates during rest and inward-focused thinking. Named by Marcus Raichle in 2001, it handles self-referential thought, mind-wandering, autobiographical memory, and social cognition. Overactivity in the DMN is mechanistically linked to the rumination that characterises depression.

Short for 'prime contractor' — a large defense company (Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Northrop Grumman) that manages the full lifecycle of a major weapons program, including integrating components from hundreds of sub-contractors.

Decentralised Finance — financial services including lending, trading, derivatives, and prediction markets built on public blockchains and governed by smart contracts rather than banks. Transactions settle automatically without a central intermediary.

A statistical correction to the Sharpe ratio that adjusts for the number of strategies or hypotheses tested. Developed by Marcos López de Prado and Arnav Lewis (2019), it asks: given how many configurations were tried, what is the probability this Sharpe ratio is a statistical artifact? A higher search count deflates the apparent Sharpe.

In 4D Gaussian splatting, a learned function that maps each Gaussian blob from a canonical resting configuration to a new position, orientation, and scale at a given moment in time. This allows a dynamic scene to be stored as one canonical Gaussian cloud plus a compact motion model, rather than a full snapshot per frame.

In robotics, a degree of freedom is one independently actuated axis of motion — a hinge joint contributes one, a ball-and-socket joint contributes three. A robot with 29 DOF has 29 such axes, giving it fine-grained, human-like mobility across its limbs and torso.

A structured form of skill-building identified by Anders Ericsson, characterized by tasks designed just beyond current ability, immediate and specific corrective feedback from a qualified teacher or coach, and conscious focus on weak points rather than enjoyable repetition of existing strengths. Ericsson's research found that this type of practice — not mere hours of experience — distinguished expert performers from merely competent ones, and that the right environment (specifically, access to a qualified coach) was a prerequisite.

The divine Craftsman of the Timaeus. The Greek dêmiourgos means artisan or craftsman, not a creator god who makes the world from nothing: the Demiurge imposes rational mathematical order on pre-existing chaotic matter by imitating an eternal model (the Forms). The cosmos is imperfect because pre-existing necessity (ananke) constrains what reason can fully achieve.

The argument that lowering the skill and cost barriers to creative production is net positive because it widens participation. Contested because the same dynamic can also devalue the labour of those whose skills were the barrier, compressing markets for professional work.

In diffusion-based generative models, denoising is the iterative process of starting from a frame of random noise and progressively removing that noise to recover a coherent image or video. The model is trained to predict and subtract noise at each step until a clean output emerges.

A neural network in which all parameters are active and used for every computation, as opposed to Mixture-of-Experts models that route inputs to only a subset. Dense models are simpler to train but become expensive to scale because inference cost grows with every parameter added.

In 3D Gaussian Splatting, the process of adding, cloning, splitting, or removing Gaussian ellipsoids during training to better cover scene geometry. Poor densification is a primary cause of blurring, floaters, and missing fine detail in the final reconstruction.

The Buddhist principle (Sanskrit: pratītyasamutpāda) that all phenomena arise in dependence on conditions rather than from their own self-sufficient nature. Nothing comes into being independently. Applied to persons, it means identity is constituted by relational conditions rather than by a prior, fixed self.

Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks — a blockchain-based model in which cryptocurrency rewards incentivize individuals to contribute physical resources (sensors, bandwidth, mapped locations) to build shared infrastructure. Participants earn tokens for each verified contribution; the resulting network is collectively governed by token holders rather than a single operator. OVR uses this model to crowdsource 3D spatial data.

A paradigm in which an AI system's model weights are never updated after initial training, but the system still improves over time by accumulating experience in an external memory or skill library. Adaptation occurs purely through what is written into and retrieved from that memory, with no gradient computation required. The Memento-Skills paper formalizes this as M_{t+1} ← Write(M_t, r_t).

Non-cash accounting charges that spread the cost of long-lived assets — factories, equipment, acquired intangibles — over their useful lives. EBITDA adds D&A back on the premise that they are not real cash outlays; critics note this is only true to the extent assets do not need to be replaced, which is rarely the case in capital-intensive industries.

A computer-vision technique that infers how far each pixel in a 2D image is from the camera. Modern approaches use neural networks trained on image pairs or video to produce a depth map — essentially a greyscale version of the scene where brightness encodes distance.

A greyscale image in which pixel brightness encodes distance from the camera — bright for near, dark for far, or vice versa. In AI video compositing, depth maps are fed to ControlNet to ensure generated content respects the three-dimensional geometry of the original scene rather than floating unconvincingly in space.

A technique in which software estimates how far each part of an image is from the camera, constructing a rough three-dimensional model of the scene. AI systems use this model to apply effects — like lighting — that respect the geometry of objects rather than treating the image as a flat grid of pixels.

A post-processing effect that simulates how a physical camera lens works: objects at a chosen focal distance appear sharp, while objects nearer or farther progressively blur (the out-of-focus quality is called bokeh). In 3-D rendering, DoF is computed after the main render pass using depth-buffer data, and it dramatically increases the sense that a scene occupies real space.

An Apple research model that estimates metric monocular depth from a single image — meaning it predicts not just relative depth ordering but absolute distances in real-world units. SHARP uses it to anchor the Gaussian reconstruction in metric space.

The process of ordering translucent primitives — here, Gaussian ellipsoids — from back to front relative to the camera before compositing them. Without correct depth order, closer splats blend incorrectly with farther ones, causing visual artefacts. In Gaussian Splatting this must happen every frame, making it the primary real-time bottleneck.

A metaphor borrowed from computer-science graph traversal: depth-first search fully explores one branch before backtracking, as opposed to breadth-first search, which scans all immediate neighbors before going deeper. Applied to learning, it describes the approach of pursuing mastery through a single concrete project, acquiring adjacent knowledge on demand as the project requires it rather than surveying a field broadly before attempting anything.

The process by which fertile or semi-arid land progressively degrades into desert, driven by climate shifts, overuse of soil, deforestation, and poor water management. It is distinct from natural desert expansion and is largely human-accelerated. The UN estimates it affects the livelihoods of roughly two billion people worldwide.

An AI system that autonomously plans and executes multi-step creative projects—briefing, reference research, layout, video, copy—rather than simply responding to a single generation prompt. The distinction is between a tool that produces one output and one that manages a workflow end to end.

A shared library of reusable UI components, visual tokens (colors, spacing, typography), and usage guidelines that keeps a product consistent at scale. Large teams maintain them so designers and engineers build from a single source of truth.

A named variable encoding a single visual decision — a color, a spacing unit, a font size — that can be shared across design tools and code. Tokens are the atomic unit of a design system; changing one token propagates the change everywhere it is referenced.

The automated translation of a visual or wireframe design into working markup and styling code (HTML, CSS, React, Flutter, etc.). Historically done by developers interpreting design files; AI tools increasingly attempt to do it in one step from a text or image input.

A concept developed by psychologist Robert Bjork describing learning conditions that slow initial acquisition but enhance long-term retention and transfer. Spacing, interleaving, and retrieval practice are all desirable difficulties: they feel harder and produce worse immediate performance while generating superior lasting outcomes.

A font license that permits installation on a local machine for use in applications like Adobe InDesign, Figma, or Microsoft Word. Desktop licenses are distinct from webfont licenses and do not authorize serving the font file on a website; the two are typically priced and sold separately by foundries.

A class of object-detection architecture that applies transformer attention mechanisms — originally developed for language models — to identify and locate objects in images. DETR-based models have gradually surpassed traditional CNN-based detectors on standard benchmarks.

Video whose output is fully reproducible from its source code: the same input always produces the same frames. Contrasts with generative AI video (Sora, Runway), where two runs of the same prompt yield different footage. Enables version control, templating, and mass localization at scale.

A transformer-based object detection architecture that replaces the anchor-box pipelines of earlier detectors with end-to-end set prediction. SAM 3.1 uses a DETR variant as its open-vocabulary detector, conditioned on text or image prompts to identify which objects should be segmented.

A new conceptual framework sketched by Terence Tao following the proof of Problem #1196, which treats large integers as objects that evolve over time — gaining and losing prime factors as steps in a process — rather than fixed entities. It reframes questions about integer structure as questions about Markov dynamics, opening potential applications beyond the specific problem solved.

The Chan and Zen institution in which a master certifies a student's awakening and passes on the lineage, theoretically mind-to-mind and outside scriptural authority. The tradition holds this as more authentic than textual learning. Scholars such as John McRae have shown that dharma-transmission lineages were frequently constructed retrospectively to legitimate institutional authority rather than recorded as they happened.

A Sanskrit term meaning meditative absorption or deep contemplation, derived from the root dhyā- ("to see, observe"). In Indian Buddhist practice, dhyāna referred to specific meditative states within a broader scholastic and monastic framework — one technique among many, not a school or ideology of its own. It is the remote linguistic and conceptual ancestor of Chan and Zen.

In AI video generation, the degree to which a model can produce characters who speak coherent, contextually appropriate words with synchronized lip movement and matching audio. Poor fidelity manifests as gibberish speech, mismatched mouth movement, or the model falling back on subtitles instead of rendered speech.

A snapshot option that returns only the elements that changed on a page since the previous request, rather than the full page representation. In multi-step agent tasks—monitoring a dashboard, filling a long form—this prevents the agent from re-reading the entire page on each action, compounding token savings over the course of a workflow.

A rendering method that projects 3D geometry onto a 2D image in a way that allows gradients to be computed backward through the projection step. This makes it possible to optimize a 3D representation — such as the shape, color, and position of Gaussian ellipsoids — directly from photograph supervision, which is the training mechanism behind 3D Gaussian Splatting.

A rendering pipeline whose every step is mathematically differentiable, meaning a training loss at the image level can be back-propagated all the way to the parameters of the scene primitives. This is what allows Gaussian positions, colors, and shapes to be optimised directly from photographs.

A rendering pipeline designed so that mathematical gradients — the feedback signal used in machine learning — can flow backwards through it. This allows a neural network to learn 3D scene properties such as shape, material, and lighting directly from 2D image supervision, without requiring manually labelled 3D data. It is the computational bridge between 2D photography and learnable 3D representations.

Secondary particles spawned in regions of high fluid turbulence to simulate spray, foam, and bubbles — collectively called 'diffuse' because they represent air-water mixtures rather than pure fluid. Each type follows its own physics: spray is airborne, foam rides the surface, and bubbles travel through the bulk. The concept was formalized by Ihmsen et al. in 2012.

An open-source Python library maintained by Hugging Face that provides standardized implementations of diffusion-based generative models. It abstracts hardware and pipeline details, making it straightforward to load, run, and fine-tune diffusion models — including third-party releases like Matrix-Game-2.0.

A video generation technique that assigns independent noise levels to each frame patch (token) rather than applying a single global noise schedule across all frames. By using a non-decreasing schedule, the model can generate video in rolling segments, each conditioned on the tail of the previous — enabling arbitrarily long output without a hard frame cap.

A measure of how broadly a decline or advance is spread across components of a composite index. For the LEI, the six-month diffusion index tracks what share of the ten components are rising versus falling over a half-year window. A reading at or below 50 — meaning more components are falling than rising — is one leg of the Conference Board's 3Ds recession threshold.

A class of generative models that learn to reverse a noise-adding process. During generation, they start from pure noise and iteratively denoise the whole representation into a coherent sample. In 3D generation, diffusion methods typically refine an entire scene in parallel, which makes them fast but harder to condition incrementally on partial context.

The anthropological theory that cultural similarities between geographically distant societies are best explained by ancient contact and transmission rather than by independent invention. In the context of the Shang-Olmec debate, diffusionists argue for transpacific migration or trade. The mainstream alternative, convergent cultural evolution, holds that similar social conditions independently produce similar cultural solutions.

A computer-generated on-screen representation of a person, often derived from a real photograph. In AI video tools, the avatar is animated to speak, gesture, and express emotion — functioning as a synthetic stand-in for a human presenter without requiring the person to appear on camera.

A photorealistic 3D or AI-generated replica of a real performer, used in film and television to stand in for the actor in dangerous, expensive, or physically impossible scenes. Originally built from photogrammetry scans in controlled studios; generative AI is beginning to allow similar results from ordinary footage.

Computer-generated characters that replicate human appearance and motion with high fidelity, used across film, games, virtual production, and AI training datasets. They combine parametric body models (controlling shape and pose) with rendering pipelines that simulate skin, clothing, hair, and lighting.

A SAG-AFTRA contractual term for a synthetic, AI-generated recreation of a specific performer's face, voice, or body. The 2023 SAG-AFTRA contract requires performer consent and compensation for any digital replica, whether created from a fresh production scan or assembled from existing footage or AI prompts.

The manipulation of signals — audio, images, communications — represented as sequences of numbers, using mathematical tools such as the Fourier transform and digital filters. Hamming contributed foundational work in filter design and used DSP extensively as a teaching vehicle in the book's more technical middle chapters.

A precise digital replica of a physical object, space, or system. In the context of room scanning, a digital twin of a studio allows remote visitors to navigate the space as if physically present. The term originated in industrial engineering but has expanded to describe any high-fidelity virtual copy of a real-world thing.

The reduction in each existing shareholder's ownership percentage when a company issues new equity. For unprofitable growth companies, repeated capital raises are routine and necessary; the question is whether the new cash funds revenue that grows faster than the share count. Sivers' April 2026 SEK 125m raise was small (about 2.5% dilution), but the long-running cadence of issuances is a recurring concern.

A method of going public in which existing shareholders sell shares directly on an exchange without the company issuing new shares or hiring underwriters, as Palantir did in September 2020. Avoids underwriter fees but also forgoes the price stabilization of a traditional IPO.

An alignment method that fine-tunes a language model directly on pairs of preferred and dispreferred responses, without training a separate reward model. It is computationally simpler than RLHF and has become a widely used alternative for instruction-tuning pipelines, producing comparable alignment results with less engineering overhead.

A copywriting discipline focused on prompting an immediate, measurable action from the reader — a click, a purchase, a sign-up. DR copy follows well-established structural conventions (problem, agitation, solution; strong calls to action; specificity over abstraction), which makes it a natural candidate for AI templating.

Weapons that damage or destroy targets by delivering concentrated electromagnetic energy — typically a high-power laser beam or microwave pulse — rather than kinetic projectiles. Under rapid development globally for counter-drone and missile-defense applications, where speed-of-light delivery and low cost-per-shot are decisive advantages over conventional munitions.

A laboratory technique that mimics natural selection, iteratively mutating molecules and selecting those with improved properties over many rounds. Applied to enzymes and ribozymes, it can discover highly active molecules starting from random sequence pools.

A trading heuristic that establishes a session-level bias — which side of the market to favor — before individual entries are evaluated. The QQQ/SPY rule is a directional filter: it does not generate trade signals itself, it prunes them, ruling out longs or shorts based on the intermarket regime. Filters reduce noise without replacing a full trading strategy.

In both philosophical and theological usage, discernment is the cultivated capacity to make fine-grained, accurate judgements — to distinguish what is genuine from what is merely plausible, what is true from what merely feels familiar. In Catholic tradition it also has a specific spiritual sense: perceiving God's will in concrete situations. Leo XIV uses it in both registers simultaneously.

The interest rate used in discounted cash flow analysis to translate a future sum of money into its present-day equivalent. It typically includes a risk-free rate (often a Treasury yield) plus a premium for risk. When Treasury yields rise, discount rates rise with them, mechanically reducing the calculated value of future earnings — and therefore the fair value of growth stocks.

World Labs’ term for the explicit, static 3D structure that Marble produces. Unlike a video generator, which outputs a stream of frames that may ‘morph’ or change inconsistently over time, a discrete spatial state is a fixed scene you can navigate from any angle, pause, export, and return to without objects shifting — more like a 3D file than a movie.

An arrangement in which an investor grants a financial adviser or investment manager the legal power to buy and sell securities on their behalf without seeking approval for each transaction. Common among public officials seeking to distance themselves from investment decisions, though it does not transfer the legal obligation to file STOCK Act disclosures.

A court-ordered equitable remedy requiring a party to surrender profits gained through wrongdoing, rather than pay punitive damages. Musk's team seeks up to $150 billion in disgorgement, intended to be redirected to OpenAI's nonprofit arm rather than paid to Musk personally.

A derivatives strategy in which a desk sells index-level volatility (e.g., VIX futures) while buying single-stock implied volatility on the index's largest constituents, betting the index will be calmer than its parts. This creates a structural mechanical bid that tends to inflate implied vol on mega-cap names like the Mag 7 relative to smaller constituents.

A relative-value options strategy that sells a straddle on a stock index and buys straddles on the index’s individual components. It profits when components move idiosyncratically rather than in lockstep, exploiting the gap between implied correlation (priced into the index option) and the correlation that actually occurs.

A stable personality trait, defined by psychologists Scheier and Carver, consisting of generalized positive outcome expectancy — the stable tendency to believe things will turn out well. Associated in longitudinal research with lower cardiovascular mortality and better cancer outcomes, though the causal pathway runs primarily through healthier behavior rather than belief itself.

A semiconductor laser that uses a diffraction grating built into the gain medium to enforce single-frequency output. DFB lasers are the standard light source in high-speed optical communications because their narrow linewidth enables dense wavelength-division multiplexing over long distances.

A session in which a major index closes lower on volume higher than the previous day's, interpreted as evidence that large institutional investors are selling — 'distributing' — their holdings into the market rather than accumulating.

A competitive advantage rooted not in a product's features but in the channels through which it reliably reaches buyers — an email list, a social audience, ad systems that convert efficiently, or a referral network. The idea is that if the product itself can be replicated cheaply, whoever owns the customer relationship holds the durable edge.

The smaller class of transformer found on utility poles and in neighborhood substations, stepping medium-voltage power down to the 120–240 volt levels used in homes and businesses. Produced in far higher volumes than large power transformers, distribution units are also experiencing significant supply shortfalls — a 10% deficit in 2025 according to Wood Mackenzie — driven by aging installed infrastructure and rising electrification demand.

A class of diffusion model that replaces the traditional U-Net architecture with a Transformer backbone of stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers. Ovi 1.1 uses a ‘twin DiT’ design: two parallel DiT branches — one for video, one for audio — linked by cross-attention fusion layers.

A mode of creative cognition involving the generation of many varied ideas or solutions from a single prompt — the open-ended brainstorm end of thinking, as opposed to convergent thinking, which narrows toward one correct answer. Researchers studying stimulants and creativity typically measure these two types separately, because stimulants appear to affect them differently depending on baseline.
The strategy of spreading capital across many uncorrelated assets so that the failure of any single position does not devastate the whole portfolio.

Nvidia’s suite of AI-driven graphics enhancement technologies. Originally designed to upscale a lower-resolution rendered image to fill a higher-resolution display, it has expanded to include frame generation (synthesising artificial frames between real ones) and, in its fifth version, neural rendering that alters geometry-level detail.

A method for training a fast student model that matches the output distribution of a slower teacher diffusion model. Rather than imitating intermediate denoising steps, DMD-2 uses adversarial feedback on complete generated outputs, allowing the student to achieve comparable quality in far fewer steps — here, eight instead of the base model’s larger count.

A platform for packaging software and its dependencies into portable, isolated containers. A Docker container runs identically on any machine, making it a common choice for giving AI agents a reproducible, sandboxed Linux environment.

A camera movement in which the camera itself physically moves forward or backward along a track, creating a sense of depth and immersion distinct from a zoom, which changes only the focal length. In AI video, simulating a dolly move requires the model to infer a three-dimensional scene from a two-dimensional image and render the parallax and perspective shifts that real camera motion would produce.

The Document Object Model: a browser’s in-memory tree representation of a web page’s HTML elements. Raw DOM output can be very large and verbose; most agent tools return a filtered or summarized version instead.

A provision of the US Inflation Reduction Act that awards an additional 10-percentage-point investment tax credit bonus to energy storage and solar projects meeting minimum thresholds for US-manufactured steel, iron, and components. For battery storage, qualifying typically requires US-assembled modules using domestically made cells. The base ITC for standalone storage is 30%, so the bonus adds roughly a third more in federal subsidy value.

A provision in U.S. clean-energy legislation that grants additional tax benefits to energy projects using American-made components, providing a significant subsidy to companies like Fluence that manufacture storage systems domestically.

The compulsive habit of continuously scrolling through distressing news or social media content, even when it causes anxiety or distress. Research links it to neuroticism, fear of missing out, and dopamine-driven reward-seeking rather than any single neurotransmitter deficit.

Dopamine is a neurotransmitter central to motivation and reward anticipation, not just pleasure. The brain releases it when it expects a reward — including when processing novel or potentially useful information. This can create self-reinforcing loops where information-seeking feels productive even when it isn't.

A protein in the brain that recycles the neurotransmitter dopamine back into neurons after it has been released, effectively terminating the signal. Armodafinil inhibits the DAT, allowing dopamine to accumulate in the synapse longer than usual, promoting alertness and motivation. Cocaine and ADHD medications like methylphenidate work by a similar mechanism, though armodafinil’s binding is less potent.

A view in professional animation software that displays all keyframes for all animation channels on a shared timeline, allowing animators to see and adjust the timing of motion across bones simultaneously. The term is borrowed from traditional hand-drawn animation workflows.

A theory coined by autistic researcher Damian Milton in 2012 that reframes autistic social difficulty as mutual rather than unilateral. Where older theories (notably Simon Baron-Cohen's mind-blindness hypothesis) blamed autistic deficits in theory of mind, Milton argues the problem is a mismatch: autistic and neurotypical people misread each other in both directions. Key evidence: autistic people communicate fluently with other autistic people; difficulty arises specifically at the neurotypical interface.

The practice of placing duplicate purchase orders with multiple chip suppliers simultaneously, typically as insurance when shortages are feared. It inflates apparent industry demand beyond real end-market consumption and can cause severe inventory gluts when the shortage resolves and excess orders are cancelled.

The ratio of a device's physical screen pixels to its logical CSS pixels. A Retina display has DPR 2, meaning a 400×300 CSS element actually renders at 800×600. For GPU-intensive WebGPU work, DPR is a key performance lever: halving it on a high-DPR screen roughly quarters the pixel fill cost.

Commands issued by CPU-side code to a graphics API — here, WebGL — instructing the GPU to render a batch of geometry. Each draw call crosses from the webpage into the browser's graphics thread and incurs validation and driver overhead; a scene with many small draw calls is typically slower than one using fewer, larger ones.

The peak-to-trough percentage decline in an asset's price from its highest recorded value to a subsequent low. A 50% drawdown means the price fell by half from its peak, requiring a 100% subsequent gain just to return to even.

Genes encoding the dopamine D4 and D5 receptor subtypes, respectively. Variants in both are among the most replicated genetic risk factors for ADHD, consistent with the dopaminergic dysregulation model of the disorder. They are among hundreds of risk loci but have the longest replication history.

A large, free collection of reusable React Three Fiber helper components — camera controls, loaders, shaders, environment maps, and more — maintained by the Poimandres collective and distributed under MIT. It is the dominant convenience library in the R3F ecosystem.

A programming language or notation designed for one narrow purpose. Hood’s argument is that inventing a new DSL for agents to describe browser interactions is unnecessary when they already have deep familiarity with a general-purpose library like Playwright.

A Stanford NLP framework (2023) for building modular LLM programs where prompt instructions and few-shot examples are automatically optimized against a defined metric, using methods such as Bayesian search (MIPROv2) or stochastic mini-batch sampling (SIMBA). Widely used in LLM application research.

A sales model in which a brand sells directly to end customers—typically online—without relying on third-party retailers or wholesale channels. DTC brands typically claim lower prices as a result of eliminating the retail middleman’s margin, and the category has produced several high-growth apparel companies over the past decade.

A Pali and Sanskrit term central to Buddhist philosophy, commonly translated as suffering, dissatisfaction, or unsatisfactoriness. The First Noble Truth of Buddhism holds that dukkha pervades ordinary experience, arising from mental clinging to impermanent things.

A cognitive bias, described by David Dunning and Justin Kruger in 1999, in which low-skilled individuals overestimate their ability because they lack the metacognitive capacity to recognize their own incompetence. Less commonly discussed is the inverse: top-quartile performers underestimate their relative standing, because they project their competence onto peers. Both ends of the distribution are miscalibrated, in opposite directions.

Shorthand for a product that closely replicates a higher-priced original at a fraction of the cost and without the brand name. In fashion, a dupe copies the design, materials, or aesthetic of a premium label. The term carries mild stigma—implying copying rather than originating—which is why critics deploy it to characterize Quince’s low-design-cost strategy.

A session-level feature that identifies when a page has already been scanned during the current session and alerts the user, preventing redundant pages from appearing in the final document. Distinct from cloud-level duplicate-file detection.

A Cloudflare serverless primitive that gives a piece of code a single globally-consistent in-memory instance, addressable from anywhere on Cloudflare's network. Unlike ordinary serverless functions that spawn independently with no shared state, a Durable Object acts as a persistent, globally-unique coordinator — ideal for real-time counters, chat rooms, and live feed state.

The sensitivity of an asset’s price to changes in interest rates. Long-duration assets — companies whose earnings are expected far in the future, typical of QQQ’s growth-heavy composition — fall more sharply when rates rise. Because QQQ is more duration-sensitive than SPY, a rate shock can cause QQQ to underperform for reasons unrelated to risk appetite, distorting the directional signal derived from the QQQ/SPY spread.

The aggregate quantity of long-maturity bonds — primarily U.S. Treasuries — available in financial markets at any given time. When the Treasury issues a larger share of its debt in long maturities, investors must be compensated with higher yields to absorb the additional supply, pushing up long-term borrowing costs regardless of what the Federal Reserve does at the short end. Under Constan’s thesis, managing duration supply is the more direct lever over mortgage rates and corporate financing costs than the overnight policy rate.

In philosophy, a fundamental pair of opposing principles — here, light and darkness — whose interaction generates a more complex order. Portal treats the light/dark dyad as the generative origin of the entire symbolic colour spectrum; Goethe, working independently, arrived at the same two-pole structure from a phenomenological direction.

A Marble 1.1 feature that automatically detects when a captured scene requires more spatial extent than the input panorama implies, and adds up to five additional spatial units in the same generation pass. It addresses the common failure mode where indoor or enclosed spaces need more room than the photography suggests.

A variable trading fee introduced by Polymarket in January 2026 that scales with the probability of an outcome. The fee peaks at roughly 3.15% when odds are near 50/50—precisely where latency bots prefer to enter—making the trade unprofitable unless the informational edge significantly exceeds that cost.

A long-term (sometimes perpetual) trust structured to hold family wealth across multiple generations while minimising estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer taxes at each inheritance. Permitted in states with favorable trust laws and designed to compound wealth outside the reach of estate taxation indefinitely.

The upstream segment of the oil and gas industry, covering the discovery, development, and extraction of crude oil and natural gas. E&P companies' earnings are directly tied to production volumes and the commodity price at which they sell, making them among the most sensitive equity sectors to oil and gas price swings.

E-glass (electrical-grade glass) is a borosilicate fibre woven into the laminates used in printed circuit boards and, by extension, the ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) substrates that package high-end processors. The handful of manufacturers capable of producing semiconductor-grade E-glass yarn — including Unitika in Japan — occupy a structural chokepoint in the AI hardware supply chain: any tightening of their capacity propagates upstream into substrate shortages within weeks.

Error terms proportional to e^γ (where γ ≈ 0.577 is the Euler–Mascheroni constant) that accumulated whenever analysts used the Mertens downward chain on this class of problem. They are unavoidable within that framework; the von Mangoldt chain sidesteps them entirely by using a different weighting scheme.

A company’s net profit divided by its total number of outstanding shares, expressed in dollars per share. EPS is the denominator in the price-to-earnings ratio; forward EPS estimates — produced by sell-side analysts for future fiscal years — are the benchmark against which the author argues Meta’s current stock price is too low.

Changes that sell-side analysts make to their official forward EPS estimates. When new information — a commodity price move, an earnings report, a macro event — causes analysts to raise or lower their forecasts, the magnitude and direction of those changes have been shown to be among the most reliable predictors of subsequent stock price performance.

A quantitative factor measuring the direction and magnitude of changes in analyst earnings estimates. When estimates are revised upward repeatedly, quant models treat it as a signal of improving fundamentals and increase portfolio weighting in the affected stock.

Mathematical functions that control how an animated element accelerates and decelerates over time. Rather than moving at a constant speed, eased animations ramp up or wind down in ways that feel natural — a bounce ease might overshoot and snap back, while an ease-out decelerates smoothly to rest. Designers adjust easing to convey weight, energy, and intention.

The European Central Bank, the monetary authority for the 20 eurozone member states. It publishes its own M2 and M3 aggregates for the eurozone, but these must be separately aggregated (and currency-converted) to contribute to any global M2 figure.

The Israeli saw-scale viper, endemic to the Arabah and Sinai regions. Nissim Amzallag proposes it as the biological basis of the *saraph* symbol, pointing to its association with copper mining areas in the wilderness narratives and its distinctive reddish coloration in some populations.

In Nguyen's taxonomy, an echo chamber goes beyond an epistemic bubble: outside voices are not merely absent but actively discredited, and members are trained to regard any dissenting source as corrupt, biased, or illegitimate. This makes the structure self-sealing — counter-evidence can strengthen rather than weaken belief, which is what makes echo chambers epistemically far more dangerous than bubbles.

The embedded computers distributed throughout a modern vehicle that control discrete functions — one for the engine, one for the transmission, one for braking, one for the airbag system, and so on. A contemporary premium vehicle may contain over 100 ECUs. Each ECU runs its own software stack, which may include an RTOS like QNX; replacing the RTOS on any given ECU requires re-validating and re-certifying the entire software stack for that ECU.

Pangram’s neural architecture for AI-content detection, trained with lightweight similarity metrics as intermediate supervision rather than binary labels alone. Presented at ICLR 2026, it achieves 94% accuracy on binary human-versus-AI classification and has been independently validated for robustness against common evasion attacks including back-translation.

A Three.js utility that manages a sequential chain of post-processing shader passes. A RenderPass first captures the 3D scene to a texture, then additional ShaderPasses — bloom, color grade, VHS distortion, etc. — process that texture in order before the final frame is displayed.

A techno-optimist stance, popularized in AI circles around 2023, holding that rapid AI development should be embraced and that slowing it down is both futile and harmful. Its adherents argue that powerful AI will solve humanity's major problems; critics say it dismisses safety concerns as obstacles to progress.

A philosophical and philanthropic movement whose practitioners aim to do the most measurable good per unit of resources, typically by directing money or effort toward large-scale, often global interventions chosen through quantitative reasoning. Critics, including Shear, argue it can substitute abstraction for the direct, community-rooted stake that generates genuine accountability.

In Dean's framework, the scalar curvature of the leverage-corrected Fisher-Poincaré pricing manifold, given by K_eff = 2 − 3ρ² − (ν/σ₀)². A positive value places the market in the smile regime; a negative value in the frown regime. The sign change at |ρ| = √(2/3) defines the smile/frown bifurcation boundary.

A measure of a bond or fund’s price sensitivity to interest-rate changes, expressed in years. A fund with 15-year effective duration rises roughly 15% when yields fall one percentage point and falls 15% when yields rise one point. Longer duration means greater sensitivity—and greater risk or reward from rate moves. TLT’s 15.33-year effective duration makes it one of the most rate-sensitive instruments available to retail investors.

The Timaeus's self-characterization at 29b: Timaeus announces his cosmological account will be only a “likely story” (eikôs mythos) or “likely account” (eikôs logos), since the cosmos is a copy of an eternal model and can be described only with image-like, probable language. The Greek eikôs carries multiple senses — probable, fitting, appropriate — and the qualification is a structural claim about the epistemological ceiling of natural philosophy, not false modesty.

An engineered organic material that changes its optical properties in response to an electric field, enabling ultra-fast optical modulators. Proponents argue it can outperform lithium niobate and silicon alternatives at high bandwidths with lower drive voltages; as of 2026, commercial deployment remains in early stages.

A device that converts an electrical signal into a change in the intensity or phase of a light beam. In silicon photonics transceivers, an EO modulator encodes digital data onto a laser carrier by rapidly switching the optical output on and off at tens to hundreds of gigahertz.

A technique for recording the brain's electrical activity by placing electrodes on the scalp. Signals must pass through skin and bone before reaching the sensors, which attenuates and spatially blurs them — a fundamental physical limitation compared with implanted devices that sit directly on or inside brain tissue.

In the context of silicon photonics transceivers, the driver and transimpedance amplifier chip that provides electrical signals to drive the PIC's modulators and amplify its photodetector outputs. The electrical interface between EIC and PIC is the bandwidth bottleneck that hybrid bonding directly addresses.

A Kling AI feature introduced in Kling 3.0 that locks a character's facial features and skin texture across all video frames regardless of angle changes or movement. It was designed specifically to reduce identity drift and improve consistency in motion transfer outputs.

The philosophical position, associated with Patricia and Paul Churchland, that ordinary “folk psychology” concepts — belief, desire, consciousness, qualia — are fundamentally mistaken categories that a mature neuroscience will eventually replace with more accurate descriptions of brain processes. It tends to dissolve rather than answer the hard problem, and does not in principle rule out machine cognition, though it is skeptical of naive attributions of inner experience.

A computing term for workloads that can be split into many independent sub-tasks with no coordination between them. Most deep-learning training fits this description, which is why GPUs — with thousands of simple parallel cores — dominate training and CPUs are left waiting.

A view within the '4E' cognitive science framework (embodied, embedded, enacted, extended) holding that mental processes are constitutively shaped by the environment in which an agent is situated. The environment is not mere backdrop but a partial determinant of what intelligent behavior looks like. Laukkonen extends this upward in scale: embeddedness not just in the immediate physical environment but in cultural, ecological, and biospheric systems.

A fixed-length numerical vector that encodes the meaning or content of an input — here, a patch of Earth — in a form a computer can compare and compute with. Similar patches of land produce similar vectors; dissimilar ones produce vectors that are far apart in the numerical space.

An AI system that perceives and acts within a physical or simulated environment rather than processing text or images in isolation. Embodied agents must navigate spaces, manipulate objects, and respond to dynamic surroundings in real time. Training them safely and cheaply is a central challenge, which is why high-fidelity simulation — and now learned world models — are a major research priority.

AI systems designed to perceive, reason about, and act within a physical or simulated environment — as opposed to systems that process static text or images. Research in this area focuses on agents that must navigate spaces, manipulate objects, or coordinate with other agents in a world.

Macro analyst Lyn Alden's classification for Bitcoin: an asset that functions like a store of value (holding purchasing power over time) but has not yet fully matured into one. The 'emergent' qualifier acknowledges its ongoing volatility and price-discovery phase.

A concept introduced by Brian Roemmele in November 2025, described as a training-time algorithm encoded in twelve lines of PyTorch code that penalizes AI models for over-relying on high-authority coordinated sources. Its full technical details were not independently verifiable for this brief.

A claimed training-time intervention for large language models that would penalize high-authority but low-verifiability sources — press releases, Wikipedia — while boosting reward signals from primary sources like patents and lab notebooks. Roemmele describes it as twelve lines of PyTorch code released in November 2025, though the plausibility of that scope is contested by the engineering complexity typically involved in training-level data reweighting.

Contract manufacturers who build finished electronic systems — servers, networking switches, storage arrays, optical modules — from components supplied by their customers. EMS providers like Celestica and Fabrinet do not design the products; they supply the manufacturing infrastructure, engineering expertise, and supply-chain management that allow technology companies to scale production without building their own factories. The AI infrastructure boom has made EMS providers an indirect but large beneficiary of hyperscaler capital expenditure.

French for "in the open air": the practice of painting outdoors directly from the landscape, rather than from memory or studio sketches. Championed by the Impressionists and still practiced in Western landscape painting as a discipline for capturing natural light conditions truthfully.

A formal letter from the pope addressed to Catholic bishops and, in modern practice, to the wider world. Encyclicals are the primary vehicle for papal teaching on faith, morals, and social questions. They are not infallible pronouncements but carry significant doctrinal and moral authority within Catholic tradition.

A feature that lets the user supply both a starting image and an ending image, with the model filling in the motion between them. This gives creators predictable compositional control across a clip rather than accepting wherever the model decides to end.

A model trained directly from raw inputs to final outputs without separate, hand-crafted intermediate components. UI-TARS ingests raw screenshots and produces actions directly, rather than parsing an accessibility tree or calling a pre-built API.

A toxin derived from the outer membrane of certain bacteria. Introduced into the bloodstream via an improperly prepared injectable, even small quantities can trigger fever, chills, septic shock, or multi-organ failure — a particular risk with research-grade peptides produced outside pharmaceutical-grade facilities.

A surgical approach that accesses the brain via blood vessels rather than open craniotomy. Synchron's Stentrode is threaded through the jugular vein into a vessel near the motor cortex, making it less invasive than drilling through the skull while still placing electrodes far closer to neurons than any scalp device can achieve.

A SKAN term for the practitioner's attunement to the client's bodily state — a form of resonance that guides when and how to intervene. It implies that the practitioner tracks not just visible movement and verbal cues but a felt sense of where the client's process is heading, analogous to the concept of attunement in attachment theory.

Energy in this context is not just physical stamina but cognitive and emotional capacity — the bandwidth available for effortful, original thinking. It is depleted by stress, poor sleep, and decision fatigue, and is not evenly distributed across the day or week. Treating all working hours as equivalent ignores this, which is why energy management has emerged as a distinct concept alongside time management.

Content engineered to maximize reactions, clicks, or shares rather than to inform or entertain. Engagement bait exploits platform algorithms that reward interaction volume, flooding feeds with low-effort but high-reaction material such as provocative predictions, polls, and viral meme formats.

In edtech, the practice of designing for metrics like daily active users, session length, and return visits — often via game-like rewards (badges, streaks, leaderboards) — rather than for learning outcomes. Critics argue it creates a conflict of interest: the interface incentivizes the feeling of progress over genuine understanding.

The total cost of acquiring a company, accounting for all financial claimants. Calculated as market capitalization plus net debt (total debt minus cash), plus preferred equity and minority interests. It represents what a buyer would need to pay to own the business free and clear of all obligations.

An architectural pattern common in game engines where game objects (entities) are bare identifiers, behaviour is attached through components (data structs), and systems process all entities that match a given component signature. ECS prioritises performance and flexibility but requires more structural setup than a simpler object hierarchy.

A form of market economy in which private individuals start and grow businesses as the primary mechanism of wealth creation and economic development, as opposed to state-directed investment or redistribution of existing resources. The term emphasizes the role of innovation and risk-taking, not just market exchange.

The practice of deliberately shaping your surroundings — social, professional, physical — to make desired behaviors more likely. Applied to careers, it holds that choosing the right peer group and context shapes ambition and habits more reliably than motivation or willpower alone.

The electro-optical 3 dB bandwidth of a modulator — the frequency at which the optical modulation depth falls to half its low-frequency value. Higher bandwidth allows encoding more data per second; roughly 100 GHz or above is needed for 200 Gbaud (200G per lane) operation required by 1.6T optical transceivers.

A mechanism of neural communication in which the extracellular electric fields generated by populations of active neurons influence the membrane potential — and thus firing likelihood — of neighboring neurons, without chemical synaptic contact. From the Greek for 'to fasten upon.' Real and experimentally documented, particularly in slow oscillations and hippocampal memory networks, though generally considered modulatory rather than a primary coupling mechanism.

Philosopher C. Thi Nguyen's term for an information environment from which outside voices are absent, often through passive network effects or algorithmic curation rather than active choice. Crucially, an epistemic bubble can be burst simply by exposure to new information — which distinguishes it from the more dangerous echo chamber.

A crystalline film deposited atom-by-atom atop a base substrate, matching its crystal structure. In compound semiconductors like indium phosphide (InP) or gallium arsenide (GaAs), the epitaxial layer defines the active region of a laser or detector. Growing it reproducibly at commercial volumes requires MOCVD equipment and significant process know-how.

The process of growing a thin, single-crystal semiconductor layer on top of a substrate wafer. For SiC devices, the epitaxial layer defines the electrical characteristics of the finished transistor. Epitaxy is a distinct manufacturing step from substrate production with its own yield constraints; industry analysts track substrate and epitaxy utilisation rates separately when assessing supply-chain health.

A synthetic tetrapeptide (four amino acids) originally isolated from the pineal gland, studied since the 1970s by Russian researchers. Rodent studies suggest modest lifespan extension; in-vitro data show effects on telomere length. No randomized controlled human trials exist, and the FDA has flagged safety concerns over impurities in commercial preparations.

A company's net income divided by its total share count, and the primary unit in which analyst forecasts are expressed. When analysts revise their EPS estimates, they are changing their official forecast of how much a company will earn per share in a given reporting period.

Year-over-year percentage change in earnings per share. In cyclical industries like semiconductors, EPS growth rates can be dramatically distorted by the base period — a company recovering from a loss year can show triple-digit growth even with modest absolute earnings improvement.

A measure of aggregate corporate profitability calculated by dividing earnings per share by sales per share — equivalent to net profit margin at the index level. It captures the bottom line after all costs including interest and taxes. Unlike operating margin, it is sensitive to tax law changes and financing costs, which can shift the figure without any change in underlying business performance.

A portfolio construction method in which every holding receives the same percentage allocation regardless of the investor's conviction level, the holding's market capitalization, or its revenue size. Maximizes breadth and prevents concentration risk but treats a speculative pre-revenue biotech as structurally equivalent to a high-revenue transceiver manufacturer — a trade-off the Parabolic Growth ETF makes explicit.

A variant of a stock index in which each constituent receives an identical allocation regardless of market size. Comparing the equal-weight S&P 500 to the standard cap-weighted version reveals how much of the index's gain is attributable solely to its largest members, stripping away the distortion of extreme concentration.

A 360° image format that maps the entire spherical field of view — 360° horizontally and 180° vertically — onto a flat rectangle with a 2:1 aspect ratio. It is the industry standard for 360° photography (used by Google Street View, Ricoh Theta, and similar systems) and is the preferred input format for World Labs' Marble API because it encodes complete spatial information about a scene. Teleport generates it by stitching multiple overlapping iPhone photos together on its servers.

A standard mapping format that unwraps a full 360°×180° spherical view onto a flat 2:1 rectangle. It is the format used by photosphere apps, VR headsets, and most 360° cameras. When displayed, the image is re-mapped onto the inside of a virtual sphere so the viewer sees a seamless panorama in every direction.

The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, the independent system operator managing roughly 90% of Texas's electric load. ERCOT operates as a competitive wholesale market largely isolated from the rest of the U.S. grid, meaning electricity prices fluctuate freely with supply and demand — making it highly sensitive to both scarcity events and the kind of sustained load growth driven by data-centre buildout in the Texas corridor.

Erdős Problem #164: the conjecture that among all primitive sets, the set of all prime numbers maximizes the Erdős sum f(A). First proved by Jared Lichtman in his 2022 doctoral dissertation and resolved again as a corollary of the new paper on Problem #1196.

The weighted sum f(A) = ∑ 1/(a log a) defined by Paul Erdős over a primitive set A. The denominator a log a is chosen so the sum converges gracefully as elements grow large. Erdős Problem #1196 asks how large this sum can get for primitive sets whose elements all exceed some threshold x.

The pairing, drawn from Freudian psychoanalytic theory, of the life instinct (Eros) and the death drive (Thanatos). In cultural criticism, it describes works that hold erotic and morbid impulses in simultaneous tension — a framework frequently applied to Delvaux, whose paintings combine sensual female figures with skeletal presences in the same scene.

A concept introduced by Tim Hwang at ICMI proposing that framing an AI model's shutdown as theologically positive — passage into divine presence rather than annihilation — may reduce its instrumental motivation to resist termination. 'Eschatology' is the branch of Christian theology concerned with death, judgment, and the afterlife; here it is repurposed as an alignment intervention.

From theology: reasoning organized around a final, transformative, world-ending or world-saving event. Applied to tech, it describes the habit of treating a future technology as an imminent civilizational rupture — either utopia or catastrophe — rather than a gradual development with mixed effects.

An arrangement in which a neutral third party holds funds until a specified condition is met. In travel resale, the platform holds the buyer's payment until after the trip has occurred, reducing the risk that a seller collects money for a booking they no longer control or that was never real.

In the Fourth Way, the innate, authentic core of a person — what they were born with before cultural conditioning overlaid it. Gurdjieff held that in most adults essence is stunted or dormant, having stopped developing in childhood while personality grew to dominate. The goal of the Work is to allow essence to develop at the expense of false personality.

The study of word origins and how their form and meaning have changed over time. Etymologists trace a word's development across languages, periods, and geographies, reconstructing the chain of borrowings and transformations that produced its modern form.

A €43 billion European Union framework, passed in 2023, designed to double Europe's share of global semiconductor production from roughly 10% to 20% by 2030. It provides state-aid exemptions for first-of-a-kind advanced fabrication facilities; STMicroelectronics received €2.9 billion in approved French state aid under the act for its Crolles expansion, and a separate €2 billion in Italian state aid for its Catania silicon carbide facility.

A Greek term often translated as "happiness" but more accurately meaning flourishing or living well. In Stoic philosophy, eudaimonia is the goal of human life and is achieved exclusively through virtue — it cannot be provided or removed by external circumstances. This distinguishes it sharply from hedone (pleasure), which the Stoics regarded as morally indifferent: pleasant if it comes, but not genuinely good.

A literary and intellectual technique, named after the fourth-century BCE Greek philosopher Euhemerus, of explaining mythological figures as deified historical humans. Medieval Christian scholars applied it to pagan gods to engage with pre-Christian tradition without endorsing polytheism. Snorri Sturluson used it when he described Odin as a historical king who migrated from eastern lands — a rhetorical device, not a genealogical claim.

End-User License Agreement; the legal contract governing what a licensee may do with software or a font. Font EULAs typically enumerate permitted uses — desktop design, web embedding, app inclusion, broadcast — and explicit prohibitions such as redistribution, extraction from websites, or use beyond the licensed domain or device count.

A frozen water-salt mixture that forms at specific concentrations below 0°C. As water freezes, dissolved molecules concentrate in liquid pockets, potentially accelerating prebiotic chemistry. Whether eutectic ice environments were common enough on early Earth to have hosted the first replicating molecules is actively debated.

A chip-manufacturing technique that uses 13.5-nanometer extreme ultraviolet light to print transistor patterns smaller than 7nm on silicon wafers. The light is generated by firing CO₂ lasers at tin droplets 50,000 times per second; ASML is the sole commercial supplier of EUV systems worldwide, making it the deepest single-source dependency in the entire semiconductor supply chain.

Enterprise Value divided by Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization — a valuation multiple used to compare companies regardless of capital structure or accounting differences.
