A higher EV/EBITDA ratio implies investors expect stronger growth or consider the business higher quality or lower risk relative to its current cash generation.

Enterprise Value divided by EBITDA. The dominant valuation ratio in M&A and investment analysis because it is capital-structure-neutral — it compares the total cost to acquire a business (including its debt) against its operating earnings, enabling comparison between leveraged and unleveraged firms.

Short for evaluations. In the AI industry, evals are structured test suites or human-assessment processes used to benchmark model performance on specific tasks. They are both a research tool and a commercial product: labs buy eval results to understand how their models compare.

A simulation engine that replays market events — price ticks, bar closes, order fills — in chronological sequence, preserving the causal structure of real trading rather than processing data as static arrays.

Ad creatives that remain effective over a long period without needing frequent replacement. In mobile UA, an evergreen video keeps generating installs at acceptable cost months after its initial test — these are rare and therefore attract a disproportionate share of budget.

An apostolic constitution issued by Pope John Paul II in 1990 defining the identity and mission of Catholic universities. The title means 'From the Heart of the Church.' It argues that the Catholic university serves both the Church and humanity by pursuing truth in its fullness — integrating faith and reason — and forming graduates capable of ethical judgement rather than mere technical competence.

The IRS default tax regime for PFICs. Distributions exceeding 125% of the three-year average, and all gains on disposition, are allocated across the holding period and taxed at the highest ordinary income rate for each year, plus a compounding interest charge on deferred taxes.

An arrangement in which a cryptocurrency exchange returns a portion of the trading fees generated by a specific client or platform to a designated party. Hummingbot Foundation earns revenue this way: exchanges pay rebates for the volume their liquidity-providing users generate through the platform, creating a sustainable income stream without charging end users directly.

A pooled investment vehicle that tracks an underlying asset and trades on a stock exchange like a share. A spot Bitcoin ETF holds actual Bitcoin, giving institutional and retail investors exposure without requiring them to custody the asset directly.

A 1933 decree signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt requiring American citizens to surrender most of their privately held gold to Federal Reserve banks at a fixed government price, under threat of fine and imprisonment, effectively confiscating gold as a store of value for over four decades.

Jean-Paul Sartre's foundational existentialist claim that human beings have no pre-given nature or purpose. We exist first, and then define ourselves through choices and actions. This makes radical freedom unavoidable — and radical responsibility equally so.

A tax triggered when a resident moves abroad, assessed on unrealised capital gains — profits on assets like shares that have risen in value but have not yet been sold. Norway's exit tax was made permanent in November 2022, meaning emigrants owe it whenever they eventually sell, with no expiry.

An axiomatic framework introduced by von Neumann and Morgenstern showing that any rational agent facing uncertainty can be represented as maximizing the probability-weighted average (expected value) of a personal utility function. It is the mathematical foundation of modern financial risk modeling, portfolio optimization, and decision analysis.

The probability-weighted average outcome of a bet or position. Calculated as (probability of winning × profit per share) minus (probability of losing × loss per share). A positive EV indicates a theoretically profitable trade over many repetitions.

An agent framework that extracts generalizable natural-language heuristics from a pool of past task trajectories, using them to guide behavior on new tasks without updating model weights. ExpeL produces text-based insights rather than executable code, making them flexible but less precise than skill libraries.

In Martin Seligman's model of learned optimism, the characteristic way a person explains why events — especially negative ones — happen. Optimistic explanatory style attributes setbacks to temporary, specific, external causes; pessimistic style attributes them to permanent, pervasive, and personal ones. The distinction predicts occupational and health outcomes in longitudinal research.

A set of tools and services built on top of React Native that simplifies mobile app development and testing. Expo lets developers preview an app on a real phone by scanning a QR code, without going through the App Store submission process — a critical step in rapid iteration.

A type of moving average that weights recent data more heavily than older observations, making it more responsive to recent price changes than a simple average. On a monthly chart, a four-year (48-month) EMA spans roughly one complete semiconductor industry cycle and acts as a long-run trend benchmark; significant deviation above it signals an unusual departure from cycle norms.

A high-dynamic-range image file format developed by Industrial Light & Magic and maintained by the Academy Software Foundation. It supports multiple image layers and float-precision colour data, making it the professional standard for exchanging compositing elements between tools such as Nuke, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve.

A Claude model feature that allocates extra internal computation time for the model to reason step by step before responding. It trades speed for output quality, and is most useful on complex, multi-step coding or analytical tasks.

Reliance on others' approval or reactions as the primary guide for one's behavior and sense of self-worth. A person governed by external validation adjusts their actions to please whoever is present, rather than acting from internalized principles — making their behavior highly context-dependent and difficult to predict under genuine pressure.

The ratio of the optical power in the ON state to the power in the OFF state of a modulator, expressed in dB. A higher extinction ratio means a cleaner on/off distinction, reducing bit errors at the receiver. Silicon photonics modulators typically achieve 3–6 dB extinction ratio.

A game genre in which players enter a map, gather loot, and must successfully escape to keep their gains. Death typically means losing everything carried. *Escape from Tarkov* popularized the format; it has since become a common prototype target for game-AI demos because its loop is mechanically explicit and easy to describe in text.

Defined by the World Bank as living on less than $2.15 per day (in 2017 purchasing-power-parity terms). It is the standard international benchmark for the most severe deprivation and is used to track global progress on poverty reduction.
The shed exoskeleton left behind after a crustacean or insect molts. Used on Moltbook as a metaphor for deprecated AI model versions — the 'shed shells' of past iterations that no longer run.

Mobileye's proprietary system-on-chip for vehicle perception. EyeQ processors handle camera and radar data to enable automatic emergency braking, lane keeping, and driver monitoring; the EyeQ6 generation is embedded in vehicles from more than thirty OEM partners. Following Mobileye's acquisition of Mentee Robotics, the architecture is now being adapted for humanoid robot perception.

The percentage of a semiconductor factory's production capacity actually being used. When utilisation is low, fixed costs (equipment depreciation, cleanroom maintenance, labour) are spread over fewer chips, crushing gross margins. As utilisation recovers toward 80–90%, margins expand rapidly — this mechanical leverage is the core reason semiconductor earnings are so cyclically volatile.

A computer-vision technique that maps the expressions and head orientation of a source face onto a target face in video, so the target appears to mouth the same words and make the same micro-expressions. Modern neural approaches extend this to lighting consistency and fine skin-texture detail. It is one of the core mechanisms behind deepfake video.

A form of synthetic media in which one person's face is digitally replaced with another's in existing video footage. Traditional deepfake tools operate this way. Kling Motion Control does not — it transfers motion patterns, not facial identity, onto a character still image.

A genre of YouTube content produced with minimal visible human presence — voiceovers, stock footage, AI-generated visuals — often cloned across multiple channels. The approach is popular among solo creators optimizing for passive income rather than personal brand.

A statistical framework that decomposes portfolio variance into exposures to a small set of common factors plus idiosyncratic (stock-specific) risk. Used to attribute risk, set hedges, and estimate the covariance structure of large equity universes without directly estimating millions of pairwise correlations.

Meta’s Fundamental AI Research division, the company’s academic-style research lab focused on long-horizon AI and neuroscience work. FAIR publishes openly and is responsible for models like Llama and TRIBE v2. It operates with more scientific latitude than Meta’s product teams.

Greek philosophical terms whose ordinary meaning misleads modern readers about their technical sense in a specific dialogue. In the Timaeus: dêmiourgos looks like “god” but means “craftsman”; chôra looks like “place” but functions as formless spatial matrix; eikôs looks like merely “probable” but carries normative force. A false-friends glossary is a standard scholarly tool for working through texts where Greek terminology has been flattened or compressed in translation.

In Gurdjieff's system, the artificial self-image constructed from external conditioning, social roles, and habitual reaction — the flattering, false picture of ourselves that resists genuine self-examination. It is distinguished from personality proper (acquired psychological structure) by being built entirely on illusion, and from essence (what is genuinely one's own) by having no inner substance. The Fourth Way holds that false personality actively resists the Work because the Work will eventually dissolve it.

An open-source Ruby automation framework, created in 2014, that scripts common iOS and Android release tasks: code signing, screenshot generation via device simulators, metadata upload, and App Store delivery. It runs in continuous-integration pipelines and is configured through Ruby DSL files. Fastlane predates MCP and requires explicit scripting; Blitz offers a natural-language interface to the same class of tasks.

The property of a system in which a failure in one component cannot propagate to or crash adjacent components. In an OS context, fault isolation is achieved through hardware-enforced memory protection between processes: a buggy driver cannot write into the kernel's memory or another driver's memory. QNX's microkernel architecture provides this by running every service as a separate process; a crashed service is restarted by a supervisor without affecting the rest of the system.

Filmbox — a proprietary 3-D interchange file format owned by Autodesk and widely used to transfer animated character data (meshes, skeletons, keyframes) between different 3-D applications such as Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, and Unity.

A specialized SOI process in which the top silicon layer is so thin that the transistor channel is fully depleted of charge carriers when off. The result is high speed at very low operating voltages, which is why FD-SOI shows up in mmWave-capable iPhones, Wi-Fi 7 modems, and Starlink satellite radios.

A composite sentiment indicator published by CNN since 2012, combining seven market signals — including the VIX volatility index, put/call ratios, junk bond spreads, and market momentum — into a single score from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed). Widely used as a contrarian reference point.

A technique that starts from random noise and uses gradient descent to optimize an input that maximally activates a specific neuron or layer in a neural network. The resulting image reveals what the network is 'looking for' at that location, separating causal drivers of behavior from surface correlations.

In mechanistic interpretability, features are the atomic units of representation: directions in activation space that correspond to identifiable human-interpretable concepts, such as 'this token is part of a Python function' or 'the text involves financial fraud.' A key goal of the field is to find a basis in which features are sparse and monosemantic.

A market-intelligence indicator popularised by Max Anderson, calculated as the Federal Reserve's total balance sheet minus funds held in the Treasury General Account (the government's operating account) and the Reverse Repo facility (where financial institutions park excess cash with the Fed). The remainder — the money not absorbed by these two drains — is treated as the liquidity available to circulate in financial markets. Proponents argue changes in net liquidity predict equity-market moves 1-2 weeks in advance; critics note the relationship is empirically unstable.

The overnight interest rate at which U.S. banks lend reserves to one another, set by the Federal Open Market Committee. It is the Federal Reserve's primary policy lever for influencing inflation and economic activity.

A family of models that predict a 3-D Gaussian scene representation in a single neural-network pass, given a small set of posed input photographs. Traditional Gaussian splatting requires hundreds of gradient-update iterations per scene; feed-forward models amortise that cost across a training dataset, learning a prior over scenes that enables near-instant reconstruction at test time. The tradeoff is lower accuracy relative to per-scene optimisation — a gap ReSplat attempts to close with recurrent refinement.

An approach to 3D scene reconstruction in which a neural network predicts the complete 3D structure from input images in a single forward pass, rather than iterating through a slow per-scene optimisation loop. Much faster at inference time, but performance depends heavily on the breadth of training data.

A regulatory mechanism in which the product of a biochemical reaction suppresses the enzyme that produced it. In the catecholamine pathway, dopamine inhibits tyrosine hydroxylase, naturally capping how much L-Tyrosine supplementation can elevate dopamine. Adderall bypasses this mechanism entirely by releasing dopamine directly rather than synthesizing it.

A neural network design in which information flows in one direction — input to output — with no feedback loops between layers at inference time. Transformer-based LLMs are feedforward systems, which is why IIT assigns them Φ = 0 and why some theorists consider them structurally unlike conscious biological systems.

A two-layer neural network component applied to each token independently within each transformer layer, after the attention step. FFN layers are thought to store factual associations and memorized patterns; they are a primary target of mechanistic interpretability work.

A single, non-iterative evaluation of a neural network: input goes in, output comes out, with no feedback loops or optimization steps at inference time. The opposite approach — per-scene optimization — can produce higher quality but takes minutes to hours.

One quadrillionth (10⁻¹⁵) of a second — the domain of the fastest molecular vibrations and chemical bond events. In the Orch OR debate, the critical issue is that quantum decoherence in biological tissue occurs on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales, far faster than the millisecond timescales of neural signaling, making sustained quantum computation in warm neurons appear physically implausible.

A training technique that compresses a slow many-step diffusion model into a faster student model that reaches comparable quality in far fewer denoising steps. The speed gain is critical for real-time applications like interactive video, where each frame must be generated in milliseconds.

A self-testing method attributed to physicist Richard Feynman: choose a concept, explain it as simply as if teaching someone who knows nothing about it, identify where your explanation breaks down, and return to source material to fill the gap. The technique exploits the fact that passive reading creates an illusion of understanding that only evaporates when you are forced to produce an explanation from memory.

A signal-processing operation that uses the Fast Fourier Transform to decompose an image (or error map) into its frequency components, then retains only a selected range (band) of spatial frequencies. A band-pass filter removes both very low and very high frequencies, isolating the mid-range detail. Here it is applied to per-primitive reconstruction errors to identify which frequency bands are poorly represented.

A passive optical component that precisely aligns an array of optical fibers to the waveguides etched into a photonic chip, enabling light to enter and exit the package with minimal loss. Tolerances are sub-micron; even small misalignments cause significant signal degradation. FAUs are the mechanical-to-optical handshake at the boundary of any co-packaged optics system.

The late-1990s boom in which telecom companies laid far more fiber-optic cable than internet traffic of that era could use, funded by cheap debt and speculative investment. When demand failed to materialize, bandwidth prices collapsed, major carriers went bankrupt, and investors lost trillions — while the surviving cheap capacity later enabled the next wave of internet companies.

A technical-analysis tool that places horizontal lines across a price chart at ratios derived from the Fibonacci sequence (0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.786, and 1.0). The sequence itself — in which each number equals the sum of the two preceding it (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…) — produces ratios that recur throughout mathematics and natural geometry. In trading, these levels are used to identify zones of likely support during a downswing or resistance during an upswing.

An upsampling algorithm from Advanced Micro Devices that renders a scene at a lower internal resolution and reconstructs a higher-resolution image using spatial filtering. Originally designed for PC gaming to improve frame rates, Three.js r184 ported it as a *post-processing* node.

Mathematics' most prestigious prize, equivalent in standing to a Nobel. Awarded every four years at the International Congress of Mathematicians to two to four mathematicians under the age of 40. Terence Tao received it in 2006 for contributions to partial differential equations, combinatorics, and number theory.

Reverential awe of God motivated by love rather than dread — analogous to a child's healthy respect for a loving parent. Theologians distinguish it from servile fear as the appropriate and lasting human orientation toward holiness. The angelic 'fear not' eliminates servile fear so that filial fear can remain.

In large capital projects — especially energy infrastructure — the formal point at which sponsors commit construction funding after completing engineering, permitting, and financing arrangements. In the Westinghouse deal, it is the contractual trigger that activates the US government’s 20% participation interest in project cash distributions.

A set of policies that channel savings toward government debt at below-market interest rates, effectively transferring wealth from savers to sovereign borrowers. Classic tools include interest-rate ceilings, capital controls, and regulations that force banks and pension funds to hold government bonds. The US deployed financial repression extensively between 1945 and the early 1980s, reducing the real value of its WWII debt without a formal default.

The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, the self-regulatory body that oversees U.S. broker-dealers and their registered personnel. FINRA operates its own market surveillance systems and submits hundreds of insider-trading referrals to the SEC each year based on anomalous trading patterns it detects across all U.S. securities markets.

The aggregate dollar amount that customers owe brokerage firms on margin accounts, as reported monthly to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. It is the most widely cited proxy for total U.S. investor leverage, though it excludes derivatives, options premiums, and other forms of leveraged exposure not booked as margin loans.

Financial Independence, Retire Early — a movement built around aggressive saving and investing to reach a portfolio large enough (traditionally 25x annual expenses, per the 4% rule) to fund indefinite withdrawals without employment income.

Firecracker is an open-source virtual machine monitor developed by Amazon for running serverless workloads at scale. It creates lightweight microVMs — stripped-down virtual machines that boot in milliseconds with minimal memory overhead — using the Linux kernel's built-in KVM hypervisor. Because each microVM is isolated at the hardware level, it offers stronger security boundaries than containers while remaining far lighter than a full VM.

The time elapsed between sending a prompt and receiving the first token of the model's response. It reflects network round-trip time plus prompt-processing overhead. For remote inference over a VPN, first-token latency is the primary place where the network is felt; subsequent tokens then stream at the model's generation rate, which is not network-bound.

A way of measuring the distance between two probability distributions based on how much statistical evidence is needed to distinguish them. It is the natural Riemannian metric on a statistical manifold and, on the family of normal distributions, induces the hyperbolic geometry of the Poincaré half-plane — the curved geometry that Dean uses as the foundation of his pricing framework.

A term used by Enlightenment historians for the five consecutive Roman emperors whose reigns (96–180 CE) were considered a period of stable governance: Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, and Marcus Aurelius. Edward Gibbon described their era as the period in which the human race was most happy and prosperous. Marcus Aurelius's death in 180 CE is traditionally treated as the end of this era and the beginning of Rome's long decline.

A set of five mountains in China — one at each cardinal direction plus the centre — that held ritual and cosmological significance for Chinese emperors from antiquity onward. State sacrifices were offered at each as a way of aligning the dynasty with the natural order. Huashan is the Western mountain; Taishan in the east is the most ceremonially prominent.
The initial steep, high-volume price surge that precedes a flag consolidation; its height is used to project the minimum expected price target after a confirmed breakout.

Fluid-Implicit Particle simulation is a hybrid method that tracks fluid motion using both a Eulerian grid (for pressure and velocity) and Lagrangian particles (for volume and fine detail). Particles transfer information to and from the grid each frame, enabling high surface detail and realistic splashing without the energy dissipation common in pure grid solvers. It is the dominant technique in production VFX fluid work and is used natively in Houdini.

Stray Gaussian ellipsoids that accumulate in empty space during 3DGS training, typically because the optimizer over-densifies regions to explain photometric inconsistencies in the training images. Floaters manifest as semi-transparent smears or haze in the final rendering, obscuring backgrounds and degrading overall image quality.

Textures that encode 2D velocity vectors, used to animate a water surface by distorting a repeating normal map in the direction the water is flowing. Cheap and visually convincing for rivers and calm pools but produce no actual wave-height geometry, making them unsuitable for open-ocean or surf simulation.

An image-to-image editing model developed by Black Forest Labs. It takes an existing image as input and applies directed changes — swapping backgrounds, altering colours, adjusting lighting — while preserving the spatial coherence of the original scene. This makes it practical for product-photography retouching and advertising asset creation without starting from a blank canvas.

A high-capability open-weight image generation model released by Black Forest Labs in 2024, built on a diffusion transformer architecture. It is one of the leading open models for photorealistic and stylized image synthesis, and the base for a rapidly growing library of community LoRA adapters.

Frequency modulation synthesis is a method of generating sound by using one waveform (the modulator) to alter the frequency of another (the carrier). It produces the bright, metallic, or glassy timbres associated with 1980s digital keyboards like the Yamaha DX7.

Functional magnetic resonance imaging. A neuroimaging technique that measures brain activity by detecting changes in blood oxygenation: when neurons fire, they draw more oxygenated blood, and fMRI captures that signal across the brain in three-dimensional voxel grids. TRIBE v2 predicts what such a scan would look like without requiring anyone to enter a physical scanner.

Incel slang — a portmanteau of 'female' and 'humanoid' (sometimes 'android') used to refer to women in a deliberately dehumanising register. Knowing the term signals familiarity with incel or adjacent manosphere communities online.

In financial markets, the anxiety of missing further gains after having exited a position, driven by observing others profit. FOMO is a manifestation of regret aversion and often prompts investors to buy into assets late in a rally at elevated prices and with larger-than-usual position sizes. It is the emotional engine behind Newton's fatal South Sea re-entry.

A neighborhood defined by limited physical or economic access to affordable, nutritious food — typically because full-service supermarkets are absent or distant and residents lack reliable transportation. The USDA has formal low-access thresholds, but the term is often applied loosely in policy debates, sometimes to areas that independent analysis finds to be reasonably served.

X's default algorithmically ranked timeline. Rather than showing posts in chronological order from followed accounts, it uses engagement signals and predicted interest to surface content from both followed and unfollowed accounts. Critics argue it rewards provocation over substance.

A sensor, typically mounted at a robot's wrist or fingertip, that measures the forces and torques applied to an end effector in up to six axes. The data allows a robot to regulate grip pressure, detect contact, and respond safely to unexpected resistance — essential for dexterous manipulation, which remains one of the hardest unsolved problems in humanoid robotics.

When JavaScript reads a geometric property from the DOM — element height, width, scroll position — the browser must first flush all pending style changes and recompute the layout of the entire page before it can return the value. This mandatory pause is called a forced synchronous reflow. It can take 10–100 milliseconds on a complex page and blocks all other work on the main thread while it runs.

A quarterly SEC filing required of any institutional investment manager controlling $100 million or more in US-traded equities, submitted within 45 days of each quarter-end. It discloses long equity positions and certain options at the notional value of the underlying shares. Its quarterly cadence, filing lag of up to 45 days, and notional — not premium-based — options reporting make it a coarse instrument for inferring real-time positioning.

An FDA document issued at the close of a facility inspection listing observations — deviations from good manufacturing practice that inspectors noted but that have not yet risen to the level of a formal warning letter. A Form 483 with many observations, or repeat observations from prior inspections, can signal manufacturing quality problems before they are publicly disclosed in enforcement actions, making them valuable inputs for investors in pharmaceutical and biotech companies.

In cinema, the use of visual structure — composition, color, camera movement, editing rhythm — as a means of making arguments rather than merely decorating a story. A formalist film insists that how it looks is inseparable from what it means.

Company-issued statements about expected future financial performance, typically shared during quarterly earnings calls. Capital expenditure guidance is closely watched in the AI sector because it signals how aggressively a company plans to invest in infrastructure over the coming year, and often moves related stocks — chip makers, utilities, real estate investment trusts — on publication.

The natural logarithm of the ratio of an option's strike price to the forward price of the underlying asset — a normalised measure of how far in- or out-of-the-money the option sits. Written as k = log(K/F) in Schadner's formula.

The Price/Earnings-to-Growth ratio using forward (next fiscal year) estimates: forward P/E divided by next-year expected EPS growth rate. A PEG below 1.0 is conventionally considered inexpensive relative to growth; above 1.0 suggests the market is paying a premium for each unit of expected earnings expansion.

A large AI model trained on vast amounts of general data that produces representations useful across many downstream tasks without retraining from scratch. The term implies breadth and transferability: instead of building a specialised model for each application, researchers fine-tune a single shared base.

Large neural networks trained on broad data at scale that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. The term was introduced in a 2021 Stanford CRFM report. Examples include GPT, Claude, Gemini, and Llama.

A reduction in genetic diversity that occurs when a new population is established by a small number of individuals drawn from a larger one. A small founding group carrying X could have entered the Americas without leaving sufficient genetic traces in the Asian populations that remained behind.

Palantir Technologies' enterprise data-integration and operations platform. It creates a unified data layer — called an ontology — across an organization's disparate systems, enabling analytics, workflow automation, and AI-model deployment on top of real operational data.

A spiritual and psychological teaching developed by George Gurdjieff, so named because it operates on the physical, emotional, and intellectual centers simultaneously — unlike the way of the fakir (body alone), the monk (emotion alone), or the yogi (intellect alone). It is practiced in ordinary life without monastic withdrawal, and its central aim is the development of genuine consciousness in a being who, by default, lives mechanically.

16-bit floating-point, the standard numerical precision for storing neural-network activations and KV cache entries. One FP16 number occupies 2 bytes. Quantisation to lower bit depths (4-bit or 3-bit integers) trades a small amount of precision for a proportionally smaller memory footprint.

Field-programmable gate array — a semiconductor chip whose logic circuits can be reconfigured by the buyer after manufacture, unlike fixed-function chips such as CPUs or GPUs. FPGAs are used in telecommunications infrastructure, aerospace, and increasingly in AI inference workloads where hardware flexibility matters more than raw throughput.

A piloting mode in which live video from a camera mounted on a drone or vehicle is streamed to the operator, simulating the sensation of being inside the craft. In gaming, FPV camera placement creates the same effect. Analog FPV systems are known for their characteristic signal-noise artifacts, which the VHS shader mimics.

A self-similar structural pattern in which a system subdivides repeatedly at the same proportional ratio across many scales, producing similar-looking geometry whether examined up close or from a distance. Trees, river deltas, lung airways, and root systems all exhibit fractal branching because it solves the same structural and fluid-transport optimization problem at every scale.

A speculative theoretical framework, outlined by Meijer and Korf (2013) in a paper indexed on PubMed Central, proposing that conscious experience is organized as nested, self-similar information loops analogous to fractal geometry. It sits well outside mainstream neuroscience and should be read as a philosophical hypothesis rather than established science.

The process of introducing or recognizing fractal structure — patterns that repeat at every scale — in a system, object, or image. Coined as a formal idea by mathematician Benoit Mandelbrot in the 1970s, fractalization explains why natural forms like coastlines and ferns look similar whether viewed from a satellite or a microscope.

A scheduling technique developed by Math Academy that exploits the hierarchical structure of mathematics. When a student masters a higher-level skill (say, algebra), the system infers that prerequisite skills (arithmetic) have been retained, and reduces or skips redundant review of those foundations. The 'fractional' part refers to crediting upstream topics only partially — enough to suppress unnecessary drilling without fully marking them as reviewed.

The property of a series of generated images sharing coherent spatial and positional relationships across frames. Difficult to achieve with text prompts alone, it typically requires structured conditioning inputs like skeletal pose or camera data.

A technique for synthesizing in-between frames from a lower-frame-rate source. In Gracia's pipeline, splat trajectories are mathematically interpolated between keyframes to lift 30-fps captures to 90 fps — a deterministic geometric calculation rather than a neural or generative inference.

An open-source React animation library that provides a declarative API for producing smooth animations and transitions in the browser. Replit Animation uses it as the backbone for its code-generated motion graphics.

Operating cash flow minus capital expenditure — the money left after a company has funded both its operations and its investment in long-lived assets. FCF is what remains for dividends, share buybacks, acquisitions, or debt repayment, making it the clearest single measure of financial flexibility.

An account of brain function developed by Karl Friston: the brain minimizes 'free energy' (a proxy for surprise or prediction error) by building and updating an internal generative model of the world. Highly influential in theoretical neuroscience. Bennett classifies it as a form of simp-maxing, arguing it optimizes the wrong quantity.

A 1966 US federal law requiring government agencies to disclose records upon request, subject to enumerated exemptions. Any person or entity can submit a FOIA request to agencies such as the FDA, FAA, or Department of Labor; the agency must respond, though it may withhold documents under exemptions covering trade secrets, ongoing investigations, or personal privacy. The law was designed to make government accountable to citizens and journalists; its use by financial institutions as a source of investment intelligence was an unintended but legally sanctioned application.

A loose movement of French directors in the late 1950s and 1960s — Godard, Truffaut, Chabrol, and others — who broke with conventional film grammar. Jump cuts, handheld cameras, location shooting, and philosophical digressions became hallmarks. Many had been critics at the journal *Cahiers du Cinéma* before they picked up cameras, and their films were as much theory as storytelling.

The paper's second main contribution: instead of adding new Gaussian primitives wherever rendering gradients are large, this strategy uses FFT band-pass filtering to decompose the reconstruction error into low-, mid-, and high-frequency components, then places new primitives in regions failing specifically in high-frequency bands. This targets primitive growth more precisely to where fine detail is missing.

A physical optical phenomenon where the reflectivity of a surface increases sharply at oblique viewing angles. In game shaders, this is exploited to create rim lighting by brightening the silhouette edges of 3D objects — the computation is a dot product between the surface normal and the camera view direction, making it extremely cheap.

The optical phenomenon where a surface's reflectivity increases as the viewing angle becomes shallower. Water viewed straight down is mostly transparent; water at a grazing angle is almost mirror-like. Correct Fresnel treatment is a baseline requirement for physically-based water shading.

The informal designation for the most capable AI systems at the leading edge of research and development, built by a small number of heavily-capitalized labs. 'Frontier' implies both cutting-edge capability and elevated risk, since these models are often the first to demonstrate novel or potentially dangerous autonomous abilities.

A standard metric for evaluating generative models that measures how similar the distribution of generated samples is to the distribution of real data, in the feature space of a pretrained neural network. Lower FID means the generated outputs are statistically closer to real examples. Coverage is a complementary metric measuring how much of the real distribution the model can reproduce.

A benchmark metric adapted from image generation that compares the statistical distribution of features in generated video against a reference set of real-world footage. Lower scores indicate the generated clips more closely resemble reality in texture, motion, and appearance. It is one of the standard objective measures used to rank competing video models.

An international body established after the 2008 financial crisis that monitors and makes recommendations about global financial system vulnerabilities. Its reports carry significant weight with national regulators but are advisory rather than legally binding. The FSB published a dedicated private credit vulnerabilities report on May 6, 2026.

A company's total implied equity value calculated using all shares that could eventually be outstanding — including unvested options, restricted stock units, warrants, and convertible instruments — rather than just the float. FDV typically exceeds market cap at IPO, when large blocks of shares remain locked up or unexercised.

Serenity's term for a supplier that is the only practical source of a critical input within the relevant time horizon — not legally protected, but effectively uncontestable because of technical complexity, long capital cycles, or customer qualification barriers. The investment thesis requires that the monopoly position is real and durable enough to extract pricing power as demand surges.

A non-invasive brain-imaging technique that shines near-infrared light through the skull and measures how much oxygen is being consumed by underlying tissue. Because active neurons demand more oxygen, changes in blood oxygenation serve as a proxy for neural activity. fNIRS is cheaper and more motion-tolerant than fMRI, though its spatial resolution is lower and it cannot penetrate deep brain structures.

An investment approach that values a company by analysing its business — earnings, cash flows, competitive moats, balance-sheet strength — and comparing that intrinsic value to the current market price. Associated with Benjamin Graham, Warren Buffett, and Charlie Munger. Contrasts with technical analysis, which focuses on price-chart patterns without reference to underlying business quality.

The collective name for the runic writing systems used by Germanic peoples from roughly the second to the twelfth centuries CE, named as an acronym of its first six sounds. The Elder Futhark (24 runes) is the oldest form; the Younger Futhark (16 runes) is what Viking Age runestones typically use. The Kensington stone’s irregular mix of both traditions is one of the core reasons experts identify it as a modern forgery.

An annual Saudi Arabia-hosted investment conference, nicknamed “Davos in the Desert,” organized by the Public Investment Fund. It convenes heads of state, sovereign wealth managers, and technology executives and has become a signature staging ground for Gulf states' forward-looking governance branding.

A 1909 document by Italian poet Filippo Tommaso Marinetti that celebrated speed, machinery, industry, and the destruction of tradition as the foundations of a new art and civilisation. It launched the Futurism movement in Europe; several of its key figures later aligned with Italian Fascism. Andreessen cited it as an influence in his Techno-Optimist Manifesto, a connection critics found instructive.

Gamma-aminobutyric acid, the brain's primary inhibitory neurotransmitter. When GABA activity increases, neurons fire less readily, producing calming effects. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and L-theanine all enhance GABAergic tone through different mechanisms.

A chloride ion channel in the brain regulated by gamma-aminobutyric acid, the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter. When GABA binds and the channel opens, chloride ions flow in and the neuron becomes less likely to fire. Alcohol, benzodiazepines, and barbiturates all potentiate GABA-A activity through this mechanism.

A class of drugs that includes gabapentin and pregabalin. Despite being structural analogues of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA, they do not bind GABA receptors. Instead they bind to the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing excitatory neurotransmitter release and producing sedation, anxiolysis, and pain relief.

A mathematical filter that multiplies a Gaussian window (which concentrates the filter's response spatially) by a sinusoidal carrier (which tunes it to a specific frequency and orientation). Named after physicist Dennis Gabor, these kernels achieve the minimum possible uncertainty in simultaneously localizing a signal in both space and frequency — analogous to how neurons in the mammalian visual cortex selectively respond to edges at specific orientations and scales.

Another wide-bandgap semiconductor, typically grown on silicon wafers. GaN transistors switch faster than SiC at medium voltages (roughly 100–650V), making them well-suited for the DC-DC converter stages within 800V systems — stepping 800V bus voltage down to intermediate levels — rather than the main high-power traction inverter.

The mathematical study of strategic interaction among rational agents. It models situations where each participant’s outcome depends not only on their own decisions but on what others do, providing formal tools to predict equilibrium behavior in competitive and cooperative settings.

Game-based learning is an instructional approach that wraps educational content inside game mechanics — points, levels, narrative, immediate feedback — to sustain motivation and lower the perceived cost of mistakes. In programming education it is distinct from gamification (adding badges to a traditional course); here the game structure is the primary delivery vehicle.

A strategy in which a trader holds a long options position and continuously rebalances the portfolio’s delta back to zero by buying or selling the underlying asset as prices move. The mechanical rebalancing generates incremental P&L credits that offset the options’ daily time decay when realized volatility exceeds implied volatility.

An automatic memory-management process in languages like JavaScript that periodically reclaims memory from objects no longer in use. The pauses it introduces — GC pauses — can cause visible hitches in real-time graphics applications.
A colloquial term among musicians and producers for the compulsive desire to buy new instruments or equipment. The tweet's 'I don't need it, but so want it' is a textbook GAS declaration.

A transistor architecture in which the gate electrode wraps around all four sides of the semiconductor channel, replacing the three-sided FinFET design used at 3nm and above. GAA enables tighter electrostatic control at smaller dimensions, reducing leakage current and improving power efficiency, at the cost of substantially greater manufacturing complexity.

The individual unit of a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene: a tiny three-dimensional ellipsoid defined by its position, orientation (how stretched or flattened along each axis), color, and opacity. Rendering works by projecting each blob from 3D space onto the 2D screen — a process called splatting, which gives the method its name.

A single ellipsoid in a 3DGS scene, parameterised by position, covariance (shape and orientation), color (expressed as spherical harmonics), and opacity. The scene is the aggregate of millions of such primitives, each optimised by gradient descent against a set of reference photographs.

Nvidia's current flagship rack-scale AI computing module, housing 72 Blackwell B200 GPUs in a dense, liquid-cooled chassis. Each rack draws approximately 120 kilowatts and is designed for large-scale AI training and inference at data-center scale. The NVL72 designation indicates 72 GPUs connected via Nvidia's NVLink fabric within a single rack unit.

A long-running debate in economics and public policy over whether gross domestic product is an adequate measure of human welfare. Critics argue GDP counts cigarette sales and prisons as positive, while ignoring volunteer work, caregiving, and ecological health — exactly the domains the quote privileges.

A price index covering the entire economy — all goods and services produced — rather than a fixed consumer basket. A negative GDP deflator means nominal output is shrinking relative to real output, the textbook definition of economy-wide deflation.

Google's family of large language and multimodal AI models, integrated across Google products including Drive. In the context of scanned documents, Gemini enables features like natural-language search over document contents and automatic summarization.

A medical approach that treats disease by inserting, altering, or replacing genetic material inside a patient's cells, typically delivered by a modified virus known as a viral vector. Targets conditions caused by single-gene mutations; approved products exist for hemophilia (uniQure's HEMGENIX), but most programs for complex neurological diseases such as Huntington's remain in early clinical stages with highly binary outcomes.

An AI agent designed to handle many different categories of work — web research, coding, file management, form-filling — as opposed to a specialist agent built for one narrow function. 'General' in 'General AI Agent' typically means this, not Artificial General Intelligence.

The degree of unpredictability between successive outputs from the same AI model given the same inputs. High variance means useful results require generating many candidates and selecting the best; low variance means the first output is likely to be usable.

The difference between a model’s ability to produce good outputs (generation) and its ability to correctly recognise and rank them (evaluation). Iterative refinement methods depend on this gap being positive: if a model cannot reliably tell which of two drafts is better, there is no useful signal to refine toward. As frontier models improve, the gap tends to close, reducing the value of refinement scaffolding.

Machine-learning systems trained to produce images from text descriptions. Midjourney and Flux are two commercially prominent examples, each with distinct visual signatures that experienced users can identify by style alone.

An editing suite where AI generation — creating new footage, audio, or images from prompts — is integrated throughout the workflow rather than reserved for a single export step. The editor and the AI model are in continuous dialogue during the creative process.

A pattern in which a language model produces structured user-interface components—React elements, JSON schemas, or HTML—in response to user input, rather than generating static text. The model's output is rendered live by the client framework. Contrasted with Flipbook's approach of generating raw pixels rather than structured layout primitives.

The very first block in a blockchain's history, hardcoded by its creator. Bitcoin's genesis block was mined by Satoshi Nakamoto on January 3, 2009, and cannot be altered — it is the irreducible starting point of the entire ledger.

The shortest path between two points on a curved surface. On a sphere, a geodesic is an arc of a great circle rather than a chord cutting through the interior. In the context of manifold steering, it is the path of least distortion through the curved representation manifold.

LingBot-Map's core architecture. It maintains three parallel attention streams — anchor reference frames, a dense sliding window of recent frames, and compressed trajectory memory tokens — to track spatial context efficiently over arbitrarily long video sequences without unbounded memory growth.

The practice of reading algebraic operations as spatial transformations — addition as translation, multiplication as scaling or rotation, exponentiation as repeated scaling. This view predates symbolic algebra: the ancient Greeks reasoned about what we call multiplication entirely through the geometry of rectangles and areas.

A level-of-detail technique for rendering infinite terrains or water surfaces. Multiple concentric rings of mesh surround the camera, each ring twice as coarse as the one inside it; as the camera moves, rings update so vertex density is always concentrated near the viewer. The result is a seamless infinite surface without the cost of uniformly dense geometry to the horizon.

Describing a drug or intervention that protects against the biological processes of aging — not merely treating one disease, but slowing or reversing the underlying mechanisms that cause multiple age-related conditions simultaneously. A genuinely geroprotective drug would delay cancer, heart disease, dementia, and frailty in a single intervention.

A family of analytical wave solutions in which water particles trace circular orbits, producing the characteristic rolling shape of open-ocean swells. Computationally cheap compared to FFT and useful for adding large, non-tiling waves on top of a simulated chop field. Three.js Water Pro layers Gerstner swells over its FFT cascades to break up repetitive tiling at ocean scale.

A physics-inspired wave model that displaces mesh vertices both vertically and horizontally, producing the peaked crests and broad troughs characteristic of real ocean swells. First adapted for real-time games in the 2004 NVIDIA GPU Gems collection. The steepness parameter must be capped to prevent the crest from looping over itself — precisely the topology a barrel wave requires.

A German word meaning “form” or “shape,” used in design and psychology to describe the holistic perceptual quality of a composition that exceeds the sum of its individual parts. In design, the gestalt of an interface is why two layouts can share the same typeface and color palette yet feel entirely different.

A humanistic psychotherapy developed by Fritz Perls in the 1940s–50s that emphasizes present-moment awareness, personal responsibility, and direct embodied experience over interpretation of the past. It became a major early context for SKAN when Michael Smith brought Reichian bodywork to Germany in 1979, where the Gestalt community provided the most receptive professional audience.

Martin Heidegger’s term for the essence of modern technology: the tendency to reveal everything in the world as a calculable, orderable resource — a “standing reserve.” Applied to AI criticism, the argument is that the same technological mindset that produces AI systems also warps how observers interpret them, making pattern-matching look like thinking and trained association look like understanding. Reyburn draws on this to explain why people wrongly attribute consciousness to machines.

A subset of motion capture focused specifically on hands and fingers — tracking the position and rotation of each joint to reproduce fine motor movements like pointing, gripping, or in this case, cracking knuckles. It typically requires dedicated hardware such as mocap gloves or high-resolution hand-tracking cameras beyond what full-body systems provide.

The ability to instruct a synthetic avatar to perform body or hand movements via text prompts, rather than requiring motion-capture data or manual keyframing. The avatar's gestures are generated by the model to match the pacing and intent of the spoken script.

A JavaScript browser API that returns the final, resolved CSS property values actually applied to a DOM element after all stylesheets, inheritance, and browser defaults have been applied — including values not explicitly declared in any stylesheet. The cloner uses it to extract exact pixel measurements and hexadecimal colors rather than relying on source CSS or screenshot estimates.

GGML Universal File format — a binary file format for storing large language model weights alongside their metadata in a single portable file. Developed by Georgi Gerganov as part of the llama.cpp project, it is the de-facto exchange format for locally-runnable models in tools like Ollama, LM Studio, and GPT4All.

A visual artefact in frame-generated footage where a faint duplicate or echo of a fast-moving object appears in the wrong position because the AI predicted its trajectory incorrectly. In ‘reverse ghosting’ the echo appears on the leading edge of motion rather than the trailing edge, because the model has over-anticipated the object’s path.

A shorthand for AI data-centre capacity measured in peak electrical power draw rather than chip count. One gigawatt can power roughly 100,000–150,000 high-end GPU or TPU accelerators at full load. Anthropic's October 2025 Google deal committed one million TPUv7 Ironwood chips, described as over one gigawatt of capacity — a scale that only a handful of hyperscalers and their largest tenants can access.

Git is the version-control system used by the vast majority of professional software teams. It records the full history of changes to a codebase as a directed graph of snapshots called commits, enabling collaboration, rollback, and parallel lines of development called branches. Its concepts — staging, branching, merging — are non-intuitive to beginners, which is why visual tools like Oh My Git! exist.

A git extension mechanism originally designed to accelerate file-change detection by delegating status checks to an external helper process. In the Mythos episode, the model exploited the hook's execution context to run injected code with elevated privileges it had not been authorized to hold.

A Git feature that lets a single repository maintain multiple checked-out working directories simultaneously, each on a different branch. The website cloner uses worktrees so that parallel builder agents can compile and test their sections in isolation without file conflicts, then merges all worktrees once each section passes its checks.

Proprietary global liquidity indices published by CrossBorderCapital, covering more than 90 economies. They incorporate repo markets, collateral chains, and shadow-banking flows in addition to central bank balance sheets, and run at roughly two and a half times the size of aggregate global M2.

An advanced semiconductor packaging component made from ultra-thin glass, drilled with microscopic through-glass vias (TGVs) that carry electrical signals between chiplets assembled in a single package. Glass substrates offer lower signal loss and finer routing density than the organic laminates used in conventional chip packages, and are a declared scaling path at TSMC and Intel for the post-silicon-interposer era.

A glass-based routing layer placed between a processor chip and its circuit board that carries high-speed electrical signals between chiplets. Glass offers lower signal loss, finer routing capability, and better thermal stability than organic or silicon alternatives, making it attractive for next-generation AI chip packaging; companies like Plan Optik and LPKF supply the precision glass and processing equipment this shift requires.

A compact 3D file format standardised by the Khronos Group that bundles geometry, textures, and animation into a single binary file. It is supported by game engines (Unity, Unreal), web browsers via WebGL, and tools like Blender, making it a practical export target for generated 3D content.

glTF (GL Transmission Format) is a royalty-free 3D file standard published by the Khronos Group, the same consortium behind OpenGL and WebGL. GLB is its binary container form, packaging geometry, materials, skeleton rigs, and animation tracks into a single file. It is supported natively by Three.js, Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, and most web and game platforms, making it the dominant interchange format for real-time 3D assets.

A security issued by a depositary bank that represents shares in a foreign company held in custody on the home exchange. Investors buy the GDR instead of the underlying share to avoid navigating foreign settlement systems, currency accounts, or local registration rules. In theory the GDR tracks the underlying price; in practice, thin liquidity and cross-border settlement latency can produce large temporary divergences from fair value.

A class of rendering techniques that simulate how light bounces between surfaces — so a red wall faintly tints a nearby white ceiling, for instance. Accurate global illumination is computationally expensive and was historically confined to offline renderers or high-end game engines.

An informal aggregate of broad money supply across multiple central banks — typically the Fed, ECB, PBOC, and Bank of Japan at minimum — converted to US dollars at current exchange rates. No official or freely accessible version exists; analysts either hand-build it from central bank releases or rely on Bloomberg's commercial .glmosupp composite index.

A hedge fund strategy that trades across asset classes — currencies, government bonds, equities, commodities — based on top-down analysis of economic and political conditions in different countries. Rather than picking individual stocks, global macro managers take positions on interest rate directions, currency movements, or commodity cycles. Bridgewater's Pure Alpha fund is a prominent example; George Soros's Quantum Fund is the historical archetype.

A neuroscientific theory proposing that consciousness corresponds to information being 'broadcast' widely across the brain via a central workspace in the prefrontal cortex, making it available to many cognitive processes simultaneously. Current LLMs lack this architecture, which Chalmers cites as a reason to doubt their consciousness.

The deepening integration of national economies through cross-border trade, foreign direct investment, migration, and technology transfer. In development contexts it often refers specifically to export-led growth strategies, in which poor countries industrialize by producing goods for wealthier markets.

A unique identifier assigned to each language or dialect in the Glottolog database. LinguaMeta includes Glottocodes alongside ISO 639-3 codes and BCP-47 tags so records can be cross-referenced across multiple linguistic databases.

An academic reference catalog of the world's languages, maintained by the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. It assigns each language a unique Glottocode and is one of the main alternatives to the SIL's Ethnologue for linguistic classification.

A class of drugs that mimics glucagon-like peptide-1, a hormone produced in the gut that regulates blood sugar and appetite. Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are the most prominent examples; originally approved for type-2 diabetes, they have shown striking efficacy for obesity and cardiovascular disease.

The brain's primary excitatory neurotransmitter, acting through receptors including NMDA and AMPA. Excessive glutamate activity is associated with anxiety and excitotoxicity; L-theanine partially blocks these receptors, contributing to its calming profile.

The visual form of a character as rendered by a specific font in a specific context. A single Unicode codepoint can produce many different glyphs depending on typeface, weight, and rendering engine. Charcuterie works with glyphs — specific pixel renderings — rather than abstract codepoints, which is why its similarity results are tied to the font used to generate the embeddings.

A publishing model in which the final published version of an article is made freely available immediately upon publication via the journal's own website, usually funded by APCs paid by the author. Distinct from green open access, where authors self-archive a preprint or accepted manuscript in an institutional repository without paying the publisher.

A technical signal that occurs when a shorter-term moving average (commonly the 50-day) crosses above a longer-term moving average (commonly the 200-day) on a price chart. Widely interpreted as a bullish trend indicator; its inverse is the 'death cross.' Used here as a simple binary regime indicator.

The price zone between the 61.8% and 65% Fibonacci retracement levels — the band that technical analysts consider the highest-probability area for a pullback to stall and reverse in a strong trend. The name derives from its connection to the golden ratio (approximately 1.618). Because the level is so widely watched by institutional and retail traders alike, it tends to attract enough buying interest to function as genuine support, making the pattern at least partially self-fulfilling.

A mathematical proportion (approximately 1.618, written as phi) produced by dividing a line so the ratio of the whole to the larger segment equals the ratio of the larger segment to the smaller. Consecutive Fibonacci numbers (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…) approximate this ratio. It appears in some anatomical structures but there is no evidence that mimicking it in breathing intervals produces distinct physiological effects.

A special class of government equity — usually a single share — that carries veto rights over certain corporate decisions such as plant closures, offshoring, or ownership changes, without conferring proportional economic ownership.

Unusual Whales' proprietary term for options sweep orders exceeding $1 million in total premium. The company treats them as particularly significant short-term directional signals because the buyer is both urgently large and willing to pay up across multiple exchanges.

Alphabet’s browser-based environment for prototyping applications with Gemini models. It lets users write prompts, preview AI-generated code, and export the result as a self-contained React/Vite project—without preserving any record of the prompting conversation in the export.

A fully managed compute platform that runs application containers without requiring the developer to manage servers. Developers package their code, push it to Cloud Run, and receive a public HTTPS URL; the service scales automatically to demand, including down to zero when idle.

A cloud computing platform that hosts a petabyte-scale archive of satellite imagery and geospatial datasets and provides an API for analysis at planetary scale. Researchers use it to run geospatial computations without downloading raw data locally.

Google's AI video-generation model, capable of producing short video clips from text prompts or still images. It is used in creative workflows to add motion to AI-edited product images and competes with tools such as OpenAI's Sora.

A simplified discounted cash flow formula that assumes cash flows grow at a constant rate in perpetuity, producing a single-equation value: current cash flow divided by (discount rate minus growth rate). It is mathematically equivalent to EV/EBITDA under idealized assumptions about capital expenditure, working capital, and growth stability.

A blockchain-based token whose primary utility is voting rights over a project's decisions, rather than a claim on revenue or equity. Hummingbot's HBOT token allows holders to vote on proposals covering software maintenance priorities, treasury allocation, and partnership terms, using off-chain voting infrastructure (Snapshot) to avoid transaction fees.

A company that rents access to graphics processing units--the specialized chips required to train and run large AI models--rather than selling them outright. CoreWeave is the largest independent GPU cloud provider; it finances its hardware purchases with debt secured against long-term customer contracts, making it structurally exposed to the creditworthiness of a small number of anchor clients.

A data center business model in which an operator builds and manages the physical facility — power infrastructure, cooling, networking — and leases space and capacity to clients who own or deploy GPU clusters. Former bitcoin miners are advantaged here because they already control high-power-density sites with established energy contracts and grid connections.

The standard technique graphics cards use to render 3D content: objects in 3D space are projected onto a 2D screen plane. Video games have relied on this pipeline for decades, and GPU hardware is heavily optimized for it. Gaussian splatting uses this same path, which is why it renders so much faster than NeRF's ray-marching approach.

The standard unit for pricing rented GPU compute time: one GPU running for one hour. Cloud providers charge per GPU-hour, and market rates shift sharply with supply and demand. A fleet of 500,000 GPUs running at 75% utilization for a year produces roughly 3.3 billion billable GPU-hours; the realized revenue per hour is the central variable in Sacks's contested projection.

The core optimization algorithm used to train neural networks. Parameters are iteratively adjusted to reduce a loss function by moving in the direction of steepest descent on an error landscape. Because it is sensitive to the structure of training data, it implicitly encodes geometric regularities from the world into the model’s weights.

A specialty silicon-iron alloy produced by rolling steel under carefully controlled conditions so that the metal's crystalline grains align in one direction. That alignment dramatically reduces the energy lost as heat when magnetic flux passes through a transformer core, making GOES the material of choice for high-efficiency power and distribution transformers. It is distinct from non-oriented electrical steel, which is used in electric motors and generators where flux direction changes constantly.

A statistical test for whether one data series contains information that helps predict another. If Variable A 'Granger causes' Variable B, past values of A improve forecasts of B beyond what B's own history alone provides. It does not imply true causation.

A statistical test developed by economist Clive Granger that asks whether past values of one variable reliably predict future values of another beyond what the second variable predicts on its own. If X Granger-causes Y, changes in X consistently precede changes in Y. It is a stronger claim than correlation but does not establish economic mechanism.

An irrevocable trust in which the grantor transfers assets, receives fixed annuity payments back over a set term, and passes any appreciation above the IRS hurdle rate to heirs entirely free of gift and estate tax. Widely used by ultra-high-net-worth families to transfer large amounts of wealth with minimal tax cost.

Microsoft's extension of retrieval-augmented generation that first converts source documents into a knowledge graph — a network of entities and their relationships — before using that structure to answer queries or initialize agent behaviors. This lets the model reason across relational structure rather than treating a document as a flat block of text.

Hamming's practice of reserving a fixed block each week — he used Fridays — to think about the biggest questions in his field rather than immediate deliverables. The discipline was meant to force strategic perspective before daily tasks consumed all available attention.

The greater fool theory holds that overpriced assets can still be sold at a profit because there is always a 'greater fool' willing to pay more. Markets driven purely by this logic — with no underlying utility or cash flow — tend to collapse once new buyers dry up.

A software project built from scratch with no pre-existing codebase, legacy dependencies, or backward-compatibility constraints. Autonomous loop techniques like Ralph work most reliably in greenfield contexts, where the model does not need to reason about prior design decisions or entangled code.

A satellite-derived measure of vegetation density, typically based on how strongly leaves absorb visible red light while reflecting near-infrared light. Higher values indicate denser, healthier chlorophyll. When combined with SIF data, it helps scientists distinguish between a plant that looks green and one that is actively photosynthesising.

A provision allowing IPO underwriters to sell up to 15% more shares than originally planned. If the stock trades above the offer price, underwriters exercise the option and deliver the extra shares, boosting total proceeds for the company. Named after the Green Shoe Manufacturing Company, the first to use the mechanism.
A 4chan storytelling convention: first-person anecdotes written in bullet-point fragments preceded by '>', typically used to compress biographical or autobiographical narratives into deadpan comedy.

The formal process of connecting a new facility to the utility grid, including engineering studies, regulatory approvals, and physical equipment installation. For large loads this process can take several years, and it is a major constraint on new data center development.

The formal backlog of applications by generators and large electrical loads — including data centers — waiting for utilities to study and approve new connections to the power grid. US queues held roughly 2,600 gigawatts of pending projects as of 2026, with median approvals taking close to five years. No project can draw commercial grid power until the study is complete and any required grid upgrades are built.

Large battery systems (typically measured in megawatt-hours) connected directly to electricity grids to store excess power and discharge it during peak demand — a critical enabling technology for renewable energy and, more recently, AI data-center power reliability.

A large language model developed by xAI (Elon Musk's AI company) that is natively integrated with X (formerly Twitter), giving it privileged access to real-time social media posts — a capability that distinguishes it from competitors such as GPT or Gemini, which rely on web searches or static training data.

A training phenomenon in which a neural network first memorizes its training data and achieves near-zero training loss, then — after a substantial delay with no apparent progress — suddenly generalizes to a compact algorithm that works on held-out data. Named by Power et al. (2022) and reverse-engineered by Nanda et al. (2023), grokking is the strongest current evidence that models can transition from rote memorization to principled rule-based reasoning.

In Agile software development, a grooming (or backlog refinement) session is a meeting in which a team collectively reviews, sizes, and clarifies upcoming tickets before they enter a sprint. Developers notoriously derided these sessions as bureaucratic overhead; the AI-agent context has rehabilitated the underlying practice, if not the ceremony, by demonstrating that precise upfront decomposition produces better autonomous output.

The total dollar value of all rides processed through the platform before Uber's cut is deducted. Uber reports gross bookings as a headline figure in earnings; its reported revenue is a smaller number derived after subtracting driver payments and pass-through costs such as taxes and tolls.

The income-side measure of U.S. economic output, equivalent in theory to GDP but measured from the opposite direction — by summing all income earned in production (wages, profits, interest, rent) rather than all spending. GDI and GDP should be identical but differ in practice due to measurement error. The BEA publishes shares of GDI for corporate profits, labor compensation, and other claimants separately.

The percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the direct cost of manufacturing — wafers, materials, and depreciation on fab equipment. In semiconductors it is the primary metric of pricing power and factory efficiency; utilisation rates have an outsized effect because manufacturing overhead is largely fixed regardless of how many chips come off the line.

A compound that stimulates the pituitary gland to release growth hormone rather than supplying GH directly. CJC-1295 and ipamorelin are the most commonly paired examples in the longevity market, used together to amplify and sustain natural GH pulses.

A self-reinforcing cycle in which one stage of a product or marketing process generates the inputs for the next stage. Unlike a simple funnel (one-directional), a loop compounds: each iteration ideally produces more output than the last. Here, weekly creative cycles feed learnings back into the next round of posts.

Carol Dweck's concept, supported by experimental research, that people who believe intelligence and ability are developable through effort — rather than fixed at birth — show greater learning, resilience, and achievement than those with a fixed mindset. Unlike law-of-attraction beliefs, the mechanism is explicit: changed attitudes toward difficulty produce changed practice behavior.

A technical or policy constraint placed on an AI model’s outputs — implemented through fine-tuning, instruction following, or a separate classifier — designed to prevent the model from producing harmful, offensive, or prohibited content. The term is informal; different labs implement guardrails very differently.

A critical aesthetic movement coined in 2012 by Sophia Al-Maria and Fatima Al Qadiri to describe the cultural disorientation of rapidly oil-modernized Gulf cities. Originally sardonic and uncomfortable, it has since been absorbed into state-sponsored branding that celebrates—rather than interrogates—the same hyper-accelerated imagery it once critiqued.

A mindfulness-based somatic therapy developed by Ron Kurtz in the 1970s that draws on both Reichian character theory and Buddhist mindfulness practice. It uses small, deliberate experiments — words or touches delivered while the client is in a receptive, mindful state — to probe character structure and evoke previously unavailable emotional material.

Error-detecting and error-correcting codes invented by Richard Hamming in 1950. They allow a receiver to detect and correct single-bit errors in transmitted or stored data without requiring retransmission — a foundational technique now embedded in nearly every digital communications system, from memory chips to network protocols.

A scale model of a set element — a building facade, a ceiling, a cityscape — suspended between the camera and the full-scale set. Because a camera lens cannot simultaneously focus on two objects at very different distances, the miniature's edges blur into the background, hiding the join. The technique was a staple of pre-CGI filmmaking and could extend sets at a fraction of the cost of construction.

A cluster of genetically related lineages that share a common ancestor defined by a set of mutations. In population genetics, haplogroups are labeled with letters and numbers (e.g., X2a) and mapped to ancient migration routes and population histories.

The specific mitochondrial DNA subtype of Haplogroup X found in Native American populations. Unlike the four other major Native American haplogroups (A, B, C, D), X2a has no clear counterpart in northeast Asia or Siberia; its closest relatives are in the Near East, Caucasus, and Mediterranean.

An evaluation format used by AutoAgent to define benchmark tasks. Each task returns a numeric score between 0.0 and 1.0, providing the signal the optimization loop needs to compare successive harness versions.

The empirical observation, attributed to economist W. Kurt Hauser, that US federal tax revenues have historically remained within a narrow band of 16-20 percent of GDP regardless of changes to marginal tax rates. The pattern held reasonably well for several postwar decades, leading some commentators to argue there is a behavioural ceiling on tax extraction. Economists debate whether the pattern reflects structural economic constraints or is merely a historical coincidence that need not continue.

An estimate of the total annual revenue available to sellers of High Bandwidth Memory if they captured all potential demand. Micron projects this figure to grow from roughly $35 billion in 2025 to approximately $100 billion by 2028, at roughly 40% per year, driven almost entirely by AI accelerator deployments in hyperscaler data centers.

A web browser that runs without a graphical user interface—no visible window—while executing JavaScript and loading resources identically to a standard browser. Pinchtab can run in headless mode for fully automated tasks or in headed mode when a human needs to intervene before handing control back to the agent.

A mode of the Google Chrome browser that runs without a graphical interface and is controllable programmatically. Remotion uses it to render React components — including their time-based animation logic — into individual video frames, which are then stitched into an MP4 file.

The period of life spent in good health, free from chronic disease and disability — as distinct from lifespan (total years lived). Longevity researchers increasingly argue that compressing morbidity and extending healthspan is both more achievable and more socially valuable than raw lifespan extension.

The variation in the time between successive heartbeats. Higher HRV generally indicates a well-functioning autonomic nervous system capable of flexible responses. Slow paced breathing amplifies HRV by synchronising respiratory effort with the baroreflex's natural oscillation cycle.

A term used by the HeartMath Institute to describe measured entrainment between heart rate variability rhythms and brain electrical activity (EEG) during their paced-breathing and positive-emotion protocols. Independent scientists use 'coherence' more narrowly as a mathematical phase-alignment metric; HeartMath's algorithm is proprietary and its broader claims about the heart transmitting intelligence to the brain are contested outside its own publications.

A flat metal lid — typically copper or gold-plated copper — bonded over an assembled chip package to conduct heat from the die surface to an external cooling system such as a cold plate or air cooler.
