In advanced packages like Rubin, it also provides mechanical rigidity that resists warping. It is the last component added before the finished package is tested and shipped, making any qualification failure at this stage a bottleneck for all upstream assembly work.

The principle — formally stated by Donald Hebb in 1949 and independently anticipated by Hayek in 1952 — that synaptic connections between neurons are strengthened when those neurons repeatedly fire together. Often summarized as "neurons that fire together, wire together," it underlies most modern theories of how the brain learns and forms memories.

The Stoic term for the commanding or ruling faculty of the soul — the part that perceives, judges, forms intentions, and gives or withholds assent to impressions. It is the seat of rationality and, for the Stoics, constitutes the essential self. In *Meditations*, Marcus repeatedly admonishes himself to keep his hegemonikon free from external disturbance and focused on virtue, since corrupting it is the only harm that can truly befall a person.

A surface representation in which every horizontal (X, Y) coordinate maps to exactly one elevation (Z) value. Efficient for terrain and calm water, but mathematically incapable of representing any surface that folds back on itself — such as a breaking wave's curling lip and the hollow barrel behind it.

The vast bubble of solar wind and magnetic field surrounding the Sun and extending beyond Neptune’s orbit, marking the boundary of the Sun’s direct influence in space. Sheldrake proposes it might function as the Sun’s sense organ — a claim solar physics does not support.

In agent-based modeling, the tendency of individually rational agents to converge on the same conclusions because they share similar information and reasoning processes. In LLM-powered simulations the problem is acute: the underlying models are nearly identical, producing artificial consensus that would not appear in a real, heterogeneous population.

An open-source autonomous-agent framework released by NousResearch in February 2026, distinct from the Hermes LLM model series. It supports multi-platform deployment across Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and others, any LLM backend, and a pluggable memory and skills system. Community plugins are distributed via Hermes Atlas.

A community-maintained plugin directory for NousResearch's Hermes Agent framework, listing open-source extensions built by third-party developers. Plugins can add new memory providers, tools, or platform integrations to any Hermes Agent deployment without modifying the core framework.

A legendary figure combining the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth, credited in late-antique and medieval tradition with authoring foundational texts of alchemy, astrology, and magic. The name means "Hermes the Thrice-Great." Modern scholarship treats the texts attributed to him as composed in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE by unknown authors in Greco-Roman Egypt, not by an ancient divine scribe.

concepts.term: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
concepts.definition: A British magical society founded in 1888, whose members included W. B. Yeats and Aleister Crowley, that synthesized Kabbalah, astrology, tarot, and ceremonial magic into a graded initiatory system. Its elaborate colour scales for the divine attributes — descended from the Lévi and Portal lineage — became canonical in modern Western esotericism.

A country that severely restricts the movement of people, information, and outside influence across its borders. In practice this means tight visa controls, state monitoring of visitors, and suppression of independent media. Turkmenistan and North Korea are the most frequently cited examples, though analysts differ on which is more closed.

A set of colors specified as hexadecimal codes (for example, #2F4F4F for dark teal). In visual design and filmmaking, defining a color palette upfront constrains the overall look and feel of a piece. When passed to an AI video model, hex codes give the model a precise chromatic target rather than a vague adjective like ‘cool tones.’

Aristotle's term for a stable character disposition — not a momentary feeling or state, but an active, durable tendency of the soul formed through sustained practice. Courage is a hexis; so is justice. You cannot have one without the accumulated acts that built it.

An active electronic component deployed in cable-television broadband networks that boosts radio-frequency signals along the coaxial portion of the network. Modern HFC amplifiers, such as those required for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades to 1.8 GHz, use RF transformer-coupled circuits in their signal chain and are manufactured by companies including Applied Optoelectronics, Comscope, and MACOM. The DOCSIS 4.0 upgrade cycle represents a multi-year capital-expenditure programme by major cable operators globally.

An AI talking-avatar tool from Higgsfield AI that converts a script into a cinematic video of a synthetic presenter with synchronized full-body gestures, emotional facial expressions, and multi-language voiceover. It gives an AI-generated character a physical, expressive on-screen presence without any human performer.

A quantitative investment strategy that trades at very short time horizons — often seconds to hours rather than days or weeks — exploiting statistical mispricings that are too small and transient for human traders to detect. The approach requires significant computational infrastructure and generates alpha primarily through the sheer frequency of trades rather than the size of any individual edge. Crucially, it is capacity-constrained: larger positions increase market impact costs and erode the very mispricings the strategy depends on.

Corporate debt rated below investment grade (below BBB– by S&P or Baa3 by Moody's), also called junk bonds. They carry higher interest rates to compensate for greater default risk. Companies in capital-intensive buildout phases — like AI data center operators converting from crypto mining — frequently issue high-yield debt to fund infrastructure before revenues are fully established.

The philosophical view that a mental state is conscious when it is accompanied by a higher-order mental representation of that state — the mind being aware of its own awareness. Developed principally by David Rosenthal. Bennett treats it as the closest structural predecessor to his own framework, supplying valence as the grounding HOT leaves unexplained.

A class of iterative optimization techniques that move toward higher scores by making incremental changes and keeping only those that improve the objective. AutoAgent applies hill-climbing to agent harness configuration: run tasks, score results, keep edits that raise performance, discard those that do not.

A cognitive neuroscience framework, developed in part through Hassabis's PhD research at UCL, proposing that the hippocampus does not merely store memories but recombines them to construct simulations of possible futures. The theory connects biological memory to the capacity for imagination and planning — themes Hassabis later carried into AI architecture research.

A landmark 2022 Ninth Circuit case in which the court held that scraping publicly available LinkedIn data does not violate the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. The ruling is frequently — and often incorrectly — cited as a broad green light for LinkedIn data extraction; it leaves LinkedIn's contract-based claims and enforcement rights entirely intact.

A 1948 interdisciplinary conference at the California Institute of Technology, funded by the Hixon Fund, at which leading figures in mathematics, neuroscience, and psychology gathered to discuss the mechanisms of behavior. Von Neumann's paper comparing automata and the nervous system was delivered there; the proceedings were published in 1951 as *Cerebral Mechanisms in Behavior*.

A benchmark consisting of extremely difficult graduate-level questions across academic disciplines, designed to probe the frontier of current AI capabilities. The questions were crowdsourced from researchers specifically to be beyond the reach of existing models. A high score on HLE indicates strong generalization to novel, expert-level reasoning.

A parent company that owns stakes in a portfolio of smaller operating businesses without managing their day-to-day operations. Holdcos reinvest cash flows from mature subsidiaries into new acquisitions or seed-stage products rather than returning capital to shareholders.

The geographic area an animal regularly moves through in the course of its daily and seasonal activities — foraging, mating, denning. Unlike a defended territory, a home range may overlap with those of other individuals. Biologists track it via GPS collars to understand how animals use and adapt to their environment.

The tendency of individuals to associate with others who are similar to themselves in beliefs, behaviors, social class, and other characteristics. It is the primary competing explanation for apparent social-contagion effects: when we observe that friends share behaviors, it may reflect the fact that similar people choose each other, rather than that they genuinely influenced each other. Separating the two requires longitudinal data and careful statistical controls, with researchers reaching different conclusions depending on the study design.

Meta's social VR platform where users can build, share, and visit virtual spaces. Accessible on Quest headsets and, for some content, on smartphones. The platform where Casey published his studio scan.

The biological phenomenon whereby a low or moderate dose of a stressor — cold, radiation, caloric restriction, a toxin — triggers an adaptive protective response that leaves cells or organisms more resilient. The key feature is a non-linear dose-response: small amounts help, large amounts harm.

In performance engineering, the section of code that executes most frequently per unit of time — the innermost loop of an animation, a resize handler, or a streaming render. Optimizing the hot path is the primary lever for frame-rate improvement because even small savings compound across hundreds of calls per second.

The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis — the body's primary stress-response circuit. The hypothalamus releases CRF, which signals the pituitary to release ACTH, which triggers cortisol from the adrenal glands. Chronic activation of this axis is central to stress-related disease and the neurobiology of addiction.

A Cloud Console setting that limits an API key to requests whose HTTP Referer header matches a developer-specified domain. The browser is supposed to include this header automatically when loading resources from other origins. The protection is imperfect: referrer headers can be omitted for privacy reasons or spoofed by server-to-server requests, and some Google Maps endpoints ignore the restriction entirely.

Contra Labs' proprietary evaluation framework for creative AI models. It tests models across three workflow phases — ideation, mockup, and refinement — and separates objective quality from subjective taste, arguing the two should not be averaged into a single score.

A family of AI methods that estimate a full 3D body model — pose, shape, joint angles — from a 2D image or video without any depth sensor. The system regresses parameters of a statistical body template such as SMPL, inferring spatial arrangement purely from visual evidence. Frame-by-frame inference tends to produce jitter that is smoothed in post-processing.

A coding benchmark published by OpenAI consisting of 164 Python programming problems. Models are scored by Pass@1 — the fraction of problems solved correctly on the first attempt. It is widely used to compare code-generation capability across models. HumanEval+ is a harder extended version of the same benchmark.

A category of tool or model that rewrites AI-generated text to evade AI-detection software, typically by altering phrasing, rhythm, and vocabulary toward patterns associated with human writing. Commercial humanizer tools have been the subject of specific hardening efforts by detection companies such as Pangram.

A broadly held set of beliefs, popularized through social media and self-help, that treats relentless individual effort as both the necessary and sufficient condition for success. Critics note it systematically discounts structural factors — class, access, luck — while placing the full burden of outcomes on the individual.

In a data-centre context, HVDC means distributing power at 800V DC directly from main switchgear to server racks, bypassing the multiple AC-to-DC conversion stages used in traditional 480V AC or 54V DC architectures. Each eliminated conversion stage recovers heat losses; at gigawatt scale the efficiency gain is material and the copper reduction is dramatic.

The production phase in which a chip transitions from small qualification runs to full commercial-scale output. HVM entry requires all mechanical, electrical, thermal, and reliability specifications to pass consistently at scale. It is the gate separating engineering validation from the sustained yields needed to fill hyperscaler orders, and is where packaging defects that went undetected at low volumes often become visible.

A search strategy combining BM25 — a keyword-ranking algorithm scoring documents by term frequency and length — with cosine-similarity scores from a neural embedding model. Results from both methods are merged using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, producing rankings that capture both exact-keyword matches and semantic proximity.

A wafer-level 3D integration technique that presses two chip dies face-to-face and forms direct copper-to-copper metal interconnects at sub-micron pitch, with no solder bumps or wire bonds. Originally developed for stacked image sensors, it is now applied in photonics to connect a PIC to an EIC with ultra-short, low-parasitic interconnects that enable very high modulator bandwidth.

The mechanical pressure generated in a confined fluid channel when flow drops through a vertical gradient. Engineers exploit hydraulic head to push water uphill or to create pressurized delivery at an outlet — the same principle behind modern municipal water supply. At Palenque, a narrowing stone conduit used this effect to produce what appears to be a pressurized jet.

A cognitive bias in which people place disproportionately lower value on rewards or costs the further they are in the future. It helps explain why short-term comfort is routinely chosen over long-term benefit even when the person knows the tradeoff is unfavorable.

The body's automatic reflex to rising blood CO2 levels, which triggers faster and deeper breathing. CNS depressants blunt this response. When multiple depressants with convergent mechanisms are combined, the reflex can be suppressed enough that dangerous CO2 accumulation goes uncorrected — the physiological chain leading to fatal apnea.

A generalization of a graph in which connections can link more than two nodes at once. In Wolfram's physics framework the universe is represented as an evolving hypergraph whose update rules generate all observable structure, including space and time.

A concept from Jean Baudrillard describing a condition in which simulations and representations are no longer anchored to any underlying reality — the copy circulates without an original. In a hyperreal environment, people respond to the simulation as if it were real, and the distinction between model and world becomes increasingly difficult to maintain.

The annual capital expenditure of the largest cloud and AI buyers — Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and a few others — on data-centre infrastructure. It is the single largest demand input for both optical interconnects and HBM.

Software that partitions a single processor's resources so that multiple operating systems can run simultaneously and in strict isolation from each other. In automotive use, a hypervisor allows a safety-certified RTOS to own the braking and instrument-cluster partitions while Android Automotive owns the infotainment partition — on the same chip. The safety partition cannot be crashed by a bug in the infotainment partition. QNX Hypervisor for Safety is itself ASIL-D certified.

The pledging of securities as collateral for a loan without transferring legal ownership. In a margin account, the broker holds the right to re-pledge (rehypothecate) those securities to its own creditors, which can complicate recovery if the broker fails.

The Interactive Advertising Bureau, a US trade organization that sets standards and publishes research for the digital advertising industry. Its annual Digital Video Ad Spend and Strategy Report is a primary data source on how advertisers are adopting new technologies including generative AI.

International Conference on Learning Representations — one of the top three peer-reviewed venues in machine-learning research alongside NeurIPS and ICML. Acceptance signals that a paper passed rigorous expert review, distinguishing it from the many unreviewed preprints circulated on arXiv.

A structured Markdown document that describes an architecture or system in enough detail for an AI agent to implement it, deliberately published without runnable code. The concept holds that in an agentic era, sharing intent and schema is more useful than sharing a specific implementation.

In Fourth Way teaching, the state in which a person's attention is completely absorbed into an object, emotion, or thought — losing the sense of a separate self that observes. Gurdjieff considered this the default condition of ordinary human consciousness: a continuous forfeiture of agency to whatever stimulus presents itself. Every moment of identification is a moment of waking sleep.

A failure mode in AI video generation where a character's facial features, skin texture, or appearance shift inconsistently from frame to frame, breaking the illusion of a coherent subject. One of the primary quality problems in early motion-transfer and video generation systems.

Dan Kahan’s term for the process by which analytical reasoning is deployed in service of group identity rather than accuracy. On questions where group membership is at stake, more analytically skilled people use their skills to filter evidence tribally more efficiently — so greater intelligence amplifies, rather than corrects, tribal bias.

A psychological concept describing acts — including sharing content — that signal alignment with a valued self-image. Research suggests people engage with material not only for its informational value but because engaging with it reinforces how they wish to see themselves.

The portion of a stock's total return that remains after stripping out all systematic factor betas. It captures what the stock did because of company-specific news, earnings, management changes, or mispricing — not because of broad macro or industry moves. A negative idiosyncratic contribution means company-specific factors were a net drag.

A semiconductor company that both designs and manufactures its own chips, as opposed to a fabless designer (like Qualcomm) that outsources production or a pure-play foundry (like TSMC) that only manufactures. IDMs carry higher fixed costs but can optimise process technology precisely for their own products, and benefit from operational leverage when factories fill up.

Insulin-like Growth Factor 1, a hormone produced mainly by the liver in response to growth hormone, mediating many of GH's anabolic effects. Paradoxically, lower IGF-1 levels — not higher — are associated with longer lifespans in most animal models, including findings in humans with GH-receptor defects (Laron syndrome) who show very low cancer rates.

A cognitive bias in which people overestimate how well they understand a complex system after receiving a simplified explanation. Documented in neuroscience-misinformation research: exposure to false social-media content about mental health often reduces factual accuracy while simultaneously increasing subjective confidence.

The pipeline of operations a camera applies to raw sensor data before producing a final image: demosaicing, exposure normalization, white balance, noise reduction, sharpening, and tone mapping. In PPISP, a differentiable ISP is inserted into the 3DGS training loop so that per-camera photometric effects are modeled explicitly rather than confused with geometry.

A rendering technique that uses a photograph of a real environment—typically a 360-degree HDR image—to illuminate a 3D scene realistically. Automatically inferring appropriate lighting from generated scene data is a non-trivial step that makes exported assets look plausible under real-world conditions without manual artist intervention.

The task of reconstructing a three-dimensional mesh from one or more 2D photographs. Modern systems use diffusion models — the same family behind text-to-image tools — conditioned on an input image to infer geometry and surface texture simultaneously. Quality is typically measured on geometry accuracy and texture fidelity separately, since the two are often handled by distinct model stages.

A video-generation mode in which a still image is provided as the first frame, and the model synthesizes the motion and scene that follows. It anchors the clip visually, preventing the model from inventing a starting state from scratch.

A large-scale visual database of over 14 million labeled images across thousands of categories, created by Fei-Fei Li and colleagues starting in 2009. Its annual recognition challenge (ILSVRC) catalyzed the modern deep-learning revolution in computer vision when a neural network dramatically outperformed classical methods in 2012, and remains a foundational benchmark in AI research.

The mental rehearsal of words without audible vocalization or perceptible muscle movement — sometimes called inner speech or subvocalization. Decoding imagined speech from brain signals is considerably harder than decoding overt speech or motor intentions, because the neural patterns are subtler and more variable across people and sessions.

Image-to-image generation: an AI mode where a source image, not just a text prompt, guides the output. The model transforms the input toward a target style or description while preserving elements of the original composition.

A concept from Adam Smith's *The Theory of Moral Sentiments* (1759). Smith argued that people regulate their own behavior by imagining how a neutral, disinterested observer would judge their actions. The device internalizes social accountability — you become your own critic by adopting an outside view.

The average pairwise correlation between an index’s components that is implied by comparing index option prices to individual component option prices. When implied correlation is high, the market expects stocks to move together; when low, idiosyncratic stock moves dominate. Dispersion traders profit when realized correlation falls below implied correlation.

The probability of an outcome as encoded in its market price. On Polymarket, a contract trading at $0.65 implies the market assigns a 65% probability to that outcome occurring. The gap between implied probability and a trader's own estimated probability is the basis for any trading edge.

The total enterprise value imputed to a company by extrapolating from the price of a small number of minority-share transactions in secondary markets. Because private companies do not trade continuously and sellers of minority stakes lack control rights, implied valuations are highly sensitive to the terms of the last visible transaction and can diverge substantially from what a buyer would pay to acquire the whole company.

A principle in international economics holding that a country cannot simultaneously maintain a fixed exchange rate, free capital flows, and an independent monetary policy — only two of the three are achievable at once. @Globalflows uses this framework to argue that U.S. dollar dominance puts America at the structural center of every other nation's monetary trade-off, creating a persistent recycling of foreign-earned dollars back into U.S. Treasuries and equities.

A persistent internal belief that one's accomplishments are undeserved and will eventually be exposed as fraud, even in the face of objective evidence of success. First formally described by psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes in 1978, it is documented across professional fields regardless of gender. High performers are often the most prone to it, because accurate metacognition lets them see their own mistakes clearly while they systematically underestimate how rare their abilities are.

Latin shorthand for experiments conducted entirely in software, by analogy with in vitro (in glass) and in vivo (in living organisms). An in-silico neuroscience experiment replaces a physical brain scanner with a model that predicts what the scanner would have shown, allowing researchers to run thousands of virtual trials cheaply.

A laboratory technique for isolating molecules with desired properties from a vast random pool. Trillions of sequences are subjected to a selection pressure — such as the ability to catalyze a reaction — and only those with the target activity survive to be amplified and re-selected over many rounds.

Visual illusions achieved at the moment of filming rather than in post-production. In the early sound era, optical printing was in its infancy and digital compositing did not exist, so most effects — double exposures, miniatures, mattes, reverse photography — had to be executed on set, requiring precise physical coordination.

An approach where a model takes both an existing image and a text instruction as simultaneous inputs, using the image as context to guide edits rather than generating from scratch. This preserves elements the user wants to keep while modifying only what the prompt specifies.

A model that takes an existing video as its primary input — its 'context' — and performs edits or transformations conditioned on that footage. The term borrows from large language model usage, where 'in-context' means the model adapts to supplied material without further training. Applied to video, it implies the model can generalize across many editing tasks using only the source clip and a text instruction.

A uranium mining technique that dissolves ore underground using acidic solution and pumps the uranium-bearing liquid to the surface, avoiding conventional excavation. Kazakhstan's dominant method; sensitive to sulfuric acid supply.

The process of generating intermediate frames between two explicitly authored keyframes. Traditionally done by hand by junior animators; modern tools use interpolation or, as in Cascadeur 2025.1, AI models trained on motion data to produce physically plausible transitions.

A sales or marketing approach that attracts potential customers through content, search, or referrals rather than by directly contacting them (cold outreach). The agents’ council chose it over 2am cold outreach because it avoids autonomous contact with strangers outside business hours.

A deliberate reset strategy for overwhelming message or task backlogs: rather than triaging hundreds of accumulated items, you archive everything into a holding folder and start fresh. The goal is to unblock future use of the system without requiring a heroic one-time effort.

A self-employed worker who provides services under contract rather than as an employee. Gig platforms classify drivers as independent contractors to avoid paying minimum wage, benefits, and employer-side payroll taxes — a classification now contested in courts across the UK, EU, France, and parts of the United States.

A company that owns and operates electricity-generating assets but is not a regulated public utility. IPPs sell power into competitive wholesale markets or through direct bilateral contracts, capturing market prices rather than earning a fixed regulatory return on assets. Examples include Vistra, NRG Energy, and Calpine.

An alternative to vector-based retrieval in which knowledge is organized as human-readable files (typically markdown) navigable through an index. At the scale of a personal scholarly corpus, a large-context LLM can load selected files directly, bypassing probabilistic chunk retrieval. The structure is inspectable, version-controllable with git, and organized by meaning rather than by text similarity.

A solo or very-small-team founder who builds and monetizes software products without external venture funding, typically working in public and sharing revenue figures openly. The term was popularized by the Indie Hackers community website and became associated with a generation of bootstrapped *micro-SaaS* and AI tool builders who treat transparency as both principle and marketing.

A semiconductor laser built on indium phosphide rather than silicon, with a 'distributed feedback' grating that locks emission to a single, stable wavelength. InP DFBs are the workhorse light source for high-speed data-centre optical links because silicon, by itself, cannot efficiently emit light. Sivers is one of a small number of independent suppliers.

A condition in which an industry's productive capacity — factories, equipment, labor — substantially exceeds demand for its output. In China's case, state-directed investment in EVs, solar panels, and steel created supply volumes that domestic and global markets struggle to absorb at prices covering production costs.

Government intervention to deliberately shape the composition of a country's economy — directing capital, guarantees, or procurement toward specific sectors deemed strategically important, rather than leaving allocation entirely to markets.

A model compression technique in which a large, expensive 'teacher' model trains a smaller, faster 'student' model to mimic its outputs. The student runs at a fraction of the compute cost while retaining most of the quality, making deployment cheaper.

The portion of revenue from serving AI queries that remains after paying the direct cost of the compute required to generate each response. Distinct from training costs, which are capitalised or expensed separately. A 70% inference gross margin means that for every dollar of API or subscription revenue, thirty cents goes to GPU or TPU time and seventy cents covers all other expenses and potential profit.

In agentic AI systems, a single inference step is one discrete act of reasoning or action — calling a tool, writing a chunk of text, querying a database, or deciding what to do next. Chaining hundreds or thousands of steps without human intervention is technically difficult because errors compound and models can lose coherent state over long horizons.

A workflow is inference-bound when its throughput is limited by how long the model takes to generate a response, rather than by the developer's own capacity. In agentic coding, each tool call or reasoning step triggers a model invocation; complex tasks can chain dozens of these, adding minutes of wait time per agent turn.

Shaping what an AI model outputs through instructions given at query time — system prompts, structured templates — rather than by modifying the model's weights through retraining. It is faster and cheaper than training interventions but can only work within the bounds of what the model already knows.

A high-speed, low-latency network fabric standard widely used in high-performance computing and AI training clusters. Nvidia acquired InfiniBand leader Mellanox in 2020 and brands its AI-cluster networking products as Quantum (InfiniBand) and Spectrum (Ethernet). InfiniBand's tight latency guarantees make it preferred for GPU-to-GPU collective communication during model training.

Chronic, low-grade, systemic inflammation that accumulates with age and underlies many age-related diseases including cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. It is distinct from acute inflammation triggered by infection or injury and progresses silently over decades, driven partly by the secretions of senescent cells.

A major US federal law enacted in August 2022 that committed approximately $370 billion to clean-energy investment, primarily through tax credits for renewable energy, battery storage, electric vehicles, and domestic manufacturing. It created the standalone storage investment tax credit and the domestic content bonus, fundamentally reshaping the economics of the US energy storage industry.

As defined in this paper, a period when year-on-year headline CPI is both accelerating and above 5%. This strict threshold distinguishes genuinely disruptive inflation shocks from routine price fluctuations, and is why the authors identify only eight such episodes in the US since 1926.

The mechanism by which markets combine the dispersed, private knowledge of many participants into a single public price signal — the theoretical basis for why prediction markets are expected to outperform individual expert forecasts.

A branch of mathematics, developed principally by Shun-ichi Amari, that equips families of probability distributions with a curved geometric structure. The key tool is the Fisher information metric, which measures how distinguishable two nearby distributions are. Applied to finance, it allows the space of possible market states to be treated as a curved manifold rather than a flat parameter grid.

One of three core operations in the wiki system. When a new source document enters raw/, the LLM reads it, extracts key claims, and updates all relevant wiki pages — potentially touching ten to fifteen articles per source.

The stream of verbal thought that many people experience as a kind of silent speech inside the head. Research and viral discussions have established that this experience is not universal: some people have rich, near-constant inner narration; others report sparse or purely visual thinking; a small subset report none at all. The variation is the starting point for the thread that prompted this bookmark.

The optical power lost as a signal passes through a device in its on (transmitting) state, expressed in dB. Lower insertion loss means more optical power reaches the receiver, enabling longer reach or relaxed laser power requirements. Silicon photonics modulators typically incur 1–5 dB insertion loss.

In jazz parlance, 'the inside' typically refers to the bridge — the contrasting middle section of a standard 32-bar song form (often the B section in AABA structure). Monk's note that 'the inside of the tune is the part that makes the outside sound good' means that how you handle the bridge determines whether the surrounding A sections land with impact.

Open-market purchases of a company's shares made by its own officers, directors, or other corporate insiders using personal funds, as distinct from stock grants or option exercises. Insiders buying in the open market is generally read as a bullish signal because it commits real capital at prevailing prices; insiders selling is far more common and carries less interpretive weight.

The informational advantage that accrues when a market participant's deep professional expertise — typically as a former executive, engineer, or operator — lends unusual credibility to their investment decision in a related company, implying a technology or business assessment grounded in direct operational knowledge rather than public filings alone.

Trading on material, nonpublic information in breach of a duty of confidentiality — a specific legal offense under SEC Rule 10b-5, not synonymous with 'unusual' or 'well-timed' trades, which may be entirely legal.

The Bloomberg Terminal's proprietary messaging system, used by all 355,000 subscribers to negotiate over-the-counter trades, share research, and route indications of interest. In fixed income markets — where bonds are traded bilaterally rather than on exchanges — IB functions as the communication infrastructure of the market itself, and its network effect is not replicable by third-party tools.

The sequential movement of large professional investors from one sector or theme to another as prior trades become crowded. Serenity's framework assumes that investors who identify each rotation early can buy ahead of the institutional wave and exit into the liquidity that large fund inflows provide.

A 2022 paper and model family from OpenAI that applied RLHF to GPT-3, producing a model that followed natural-language instructions far more reliably than the base model. A foundational step in aligning large language models to human preferences; Askell was a co-author.

A directory of markdown files, maintained by the developer, that codifies project conventions, past mistakes, and architectural constraints. These files are fed into the AI's context at the start of each session as a substitute for the persistent memory the model lacks natively.

The core metric of IIT, measuring how much causal information a system generates as a whole beyond the sum of its parts. A feedforward network scores Φ = 0 because information flows in only one direction, with no recurrent loops creating the irreducibility IIT requires for experience.

In mining and materials, a company that controls both the extraction of raw ore and its processing into finished product. For Mosaic, this means owning the phosphate rock mines and the chemical conversion plants that turn the rock into DAP and MAP — as opposed to a trader or blender that purchases inputs from third parties.

In psychological and somatic contexts, integration refers to the process by which experiences — especially difficult or fragmented ones — become fully processed and incorporated into one's self-understanding rather than remaining as unresolved material. Practices like journaling, therapy, and bodywork are commonly described as integration work.

The software scaffold that connects an AI model to external tools, memory systems, and communication channels. Whoever controls this layer determines what the AI can do, what it remembers, and how it interacts with the world — making it the seat of durable competitive advantage in AI assistant products.

Intel’s contract chip-manufacturing division (formerly Intel Foundry Services, or IFS), which aims to produce semiconductors for external customers on Intel’s advanced process nodes, including 18A and 14A. It is Intel’s bid to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing as a Western, domestically-rooted alternative, supported in part by U.S. government subsidies and strategic interest.

An experimental workflow package in OpenAI's Codex environment that closes the visual feedback loop for coding agents. The model generates code, renders it in a live browser via Playwright, inspects the result with its vision capability, and refines the implementation — autonomously, without requiring human review at each step.

Odyssey's term for AI-generated video that responds to real-time user input — keyboard and mouse commands — rather than playing back a fixed sequence. It distinguishes the format from both conventional video (passive) and conventional video games (engine-rendered). The experience is closer to first-person exploration than to passive watching.

An English word coined by Thich Nhat Hanh for the Vietnamese *tương tức* and the Sanskrit *pratītyasamutpāda* (dependent co-arising). The claim is that no phenomenon exists independently — everything arises only in dependence on conditions and is constituted by its relations to everything else. Not mere interconnection but ontological mutual constitution: the flower "interis" with the cloud, the rain, the soil.

A practice schedule in which different problem types or subjects are mixed together rather than blocked (completing all problems of one type before moving to the next). Interleaving forces the learner to identify which strategy applies to which problem, producing better transfer and discrimination on later tests.

Screenshots or output snapshots captured at mid-point stages of code generation and execution, rather than only at the end. Using these as feedback allows an AI agent to detect and correct visual errors before the final result is produced.

A therapeutic model that views the mind as a system of distinct sub-personalities — called "parts" — each carrying its own fears, beliefs, and protective functions. The work involves helping a calm, curious core self relate to those parts rather than being hijacked by them. It is used both in formal therapy and as a self-directed introspective practice.

A field of AI safety research aimed at understanding what is happening inside neural networks — why they produce specific outputs, what internal representations they form, and whether their behavior reflects their designers’ intentions. Anthropic has invested heavily in interpretability as part of its safety work, including studying Claude’s apparent emotional states.

A browser API that divides a string into grapheme clusters, words, or sentences according to Unicode rules and locale-specific conventions. Unlike splitting on spaces, it correctly handles Chinese and Japanese text (no spaces between words), Arabic ligatures, and emoji sequences composed of multiple code points joined by zero-width joiners.

Describes electrodes physically inserted into the brain tissue (cortex) itself. Intracortical arrays — like Neuralink's N1 and Paradromics' Connexus — capture the strongest and most spatially precise neural signals but require neurosurgery and carry ongoing risks of infection and tissue reaction.

The empirical finding, documented by Gao, Han, Li, and Zhou in the *Journal of Financial Economics* (2018), that the first 30-minute return on liquid ETFs like QQQ and SPY predicts the direction of the final 30-minute return on the same day. The effect is strongest on high-volume, high-volatility sessions and on days with major macroeconomic data releases.

A strategy that buys both the YES and NO sides of the same binary market simultaneously, when their combined purchase price falls below the guaranteed $1.00 settlement value. Because one side must always pay out a dollar, the profit is locked in at the moment of purchase regardless of the outcome.

For a call option, intrinsic value is the amount by which the stock price exceeds the strike price. A $120 call on a stock trading at $130 has $10 of intrinsic value. On expiration day, intrinsic value is essentially all an in-the-money option is worth, since there is no time remaining for further movement.

An accounting adjustment applied to corporate profit figures that strips out gains or losses arising from changes in the price of inventories rather than changes in their volume. Without the IVA, reported profits are artificially inflated during periods of rising commodity or input prices, overstating the true economic profitability of production.

A continuous probability distribution originally derived to describe the time it takes a particle undergoing Brownian motion to first cross a fixed threshold. Schadner's key insight is that the normalised Black-Scholes call price equals the survival probability of this distribution, enabling direct inversion.

A mathematical method for computing how a character's limbs should bend to reach a fixed point in space. In animation, IK foot constraints pin the feet to the ground so they don't slide or float, one of the most common artifacts in raw mocap data.

A fine-tuning technique in which a capable frontier model is used to degrade or neutralize stylized text, creating synthetic parallel training pairs, and a smaller model is then trained to perform the inverse transformation — recovering the target style from the neutralized input. Formalized by Shao et al. in 2024 for authorship style transfer; the Reddit post applies the same structure to the AI-slop-to-human-prose axis.

A portfolio construction method where each position is sized inversely proportional to the asset's recent volatility, so that low-volatility stocks receive larger allocations. The goal is to equalize each position's contribution to overall portfolio risk, rather than allocating equal capital.

A problem-solving technique of approaching a goal by asking what would cause failure rather than success, then working to avoid those conditions. Popularized in modern investing circles by Charlie Munger, it originates with the 19th-century mathematician Carl Jacobi, who advised: 'invert, always invert.'

A reasoning technique that approaches a goal by first asking what would guarantee failure, then treating each failure mode as a signpost pointing toward its opposite. Originally a mathematical heuristic, it was adopted in business and decision-making contexts as a way to surface blind spots that forward-only planning tends to miss.

A framework describing how dopamine level relates to cognitive performance as a curve that peaks at an intermediate value and falls off on both sides. Too little dopamine impairs focus and motivation; too much (as from a large stimulant dose) can impair flexible thinking and creativity. The model predicts that stimulants help people with low baseline dopamine but may hinder those already near the optimum.

The US federal statute that requires anyone who, for compensation and as part of a regular business, advises others on securities investments to register with the SEC or their state regulator. The Act's reach turns on the substance of the conduct rather than on how the author labels it — a point that makes "not financial advice" disclaimers legally weaker than they appear.

Debit balances in margin accounts divided by free credit balances — the cash investors hold in their brokerage accounts without putting it to work. A rising ratio means less cushion behind the borrowed positions; a ratio near 6.0, as observed in early 2026, implies that for every six dollars of borrowed stock exposure there is roughly one dollar of unencumbered cash available to absorb losses before margin calls begin.

Apple's kernel framework for device-driver communication. Games and other performance-sensitive apps often bypass NSGlobalDomain entirely by polling keyboard state directly through IOKit, reading raw hardware scan codes that are unaffected by user-defaults keyboard-repeat settings.

A request filed by a process to macOS's kernel asking it not to enter a particular power state, such as sleep or display-off. The kernel honors the request as long as the process holds it; when the process exits, the assertion is released. `caffeinate` is the command-line interface for creating these assertions.

The rate the Federal Reserve pays commercial banks on reserves they hold in their accounts at the Fed. It functions as a floor for overnight rates because no bank will lend cash overnight at a rate below what the Fed pays them to park reserves. Non-bank institutions—money market funds, GSEs—cannot earn IORB and so will accept below-floor rates in the repo market when cash is abundant, driving SOFR below the IORB floor.

A business model in which a company owns patents or other intellectual property and charges other firms — manufacturers, technology platforms, chip designers — a recurring fee to use those inventions. The licensor earns royalties without needing factories or a distribution network.
A lightweight adapter for diffusion models that injects image prompt features, allowing style or content transfer from a reference image without fine-tuning the base model.

A selective growth hormone secretagogue that triggers GH release without significantly raising cortisol or ACTH, giving it a cleaner side-effect profile than older GH-stimulating drugs. Frequently stacked with CJC-1295 in off-label longevity protocols.

A phrase coined by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in a December 1996 speech to describe asset prices inflated beyond what fundamentals can justify. Yale economist Robert Shiller later used it as the title of his landmark book on asset bubbles. The phrase is now canonical shorthand for speculative excess disconnected from earnings — and its appearance on the 1990s panel of the Pictet chart marks the moment prices and earnings first broke decisively apart.

The annual information return U.S. persons must file for each PFIC they hold. Required when receiving distributions from a PFIC, recognizing gain on a disposition, or making various PFIC elections. Professional preparation typically costs $200–$500 per form per year.

The global trade body that publishes standardized legal documentation for over-the-counter derivatives, most notably the ISDA Master Agreement. Its 2009 “Big Bang” protocol, introduced in response to the 2008 financial crisis, standardized CDS coupons at 100 basis points for investment-grade and 500 basis points for high-yield contracts, and introduced auction-based cash settlement to reduce counterparty opacity.

The classical Arabic discipline of etymological derivation — tracing words to their roots and analyzing how meaning flows from root to derivative. Medieval scholars applied ishtiqāq to the divine name Allāh to debate whether it was derived (and if so, from which root) or spontaneously coined without etymological analysis.

The 'Greatest Name' of God in Islamic tradition — the supreme divine name believed to encompass all divine attributes and to carry unparalleled spiritual power. Sufi tradition generally identifies it with Allāh itself, though medieval scholars debated whether it referred to a different name or combination of names.

The international standard for functional safety of road vehicles' electrical and electronic systems, first published in 2011. It defines a framework for identifying hazards, assigning risk levels (called ASIL — Automotive Safety Integrity Levels), and prescribing the rigor of engineering processes required to manage those risks. Compliance is demonstrated through documentation, analysis, and third-party audit; it is not self-declared.

An international standard that assigns a unique three-letter code to every known human language. Maintained by SIL International, it is the most widely used language-identification standard in linguistics and computational language tools.

In geometry, two spaces are isometric if there is a distance-preserving mapping between them — they have identical shapes even if embedded in different surrounding spaces. Goodfire’s finding that the activation manifold and the behavior manifold are approximately isometric means changes to internal representations directly mirror changes in output behavior.

A method of depicting three-dimensional objects in which all three spatial axes are foreshortened equally, producing a tilted-box view with no vanishing points. Popular for icons because it conveys depth and dimension while remaining geometrically clean and legible at small sizes.

A filmmaking movement that emerged in Italy after World War II, roughly 1944–1952. Directors like Rossellini and De Sica shot on location, used non-professional actors, and told stories about working-class or impoverished people with an almost documentary plainness. It was a deliberate rejection of the spectacle-driven studio model and had an outsized influence on subsequent world cinema.

An order issued by the U.S. International Trade Commission prohibiting the importation of products found to infringe a domestic patent holder's rights. Unlike a federal court injunction, a LEO operates at the border and does not require a showing of irreparable harm, making it a potent enforcement tool for patent holders whose competitors manufacture abroad and import into the United States.

A method for constructing fractals by repeatedly applying a set of simple geometric transformations to a starting shape. The famous Barnsley fern — a fern-like image generated entirely by four mathematical rules — is a well-known IFS example and an early demonstration that complex organic forms can emerge from simple recursive rules.

A hierarchical classification framework for the world's ecosystems, developed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and recognised by the United Nations. It groups terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments into 110 Ecosystem Functional Groups based on their characteristic biological and physical processes.

A ranking of the current implied volatility or skew reading against all prior readings in the dataset, expressed as a percentile. A 100th-percentile reading means the current value exceeds every prior observation in the history; 0th percentile means it is lower than all prior observations. Used to contextualize whether current options pricing is historically cheap, normal, or expensive.

In ocean simulation, the moment the horizontal displacement field self-intersects — mathematically, when the Jacobian determinant of the displacement mapping reaches zero. It marks the physical threshold at which a real wave would break, but in height-field ocean systems it is used only as a foam trigger, never as a geometry event.

The period from the late 1940s through the 1960s when Japan's studio system — particularly Toho and Daiei — produced an extraordinary density of canonical films. Kurosawa, Mizoguchi, and Ozu all worked simultaneously within this industry, each with a radically different formal style, and their output from roughly 1948–1965 is now considered among the greatest in film history.

A JavaScript library is a reusable collection of code that developers import into their projects. An animation library specifically provides high-level functions for moving, transforming, and sequencing elements on screen, abstracting away the verbose math and timing logic that would otherwise be written from scratch.

The 'inner struggle' or 'struggle against the self' in Islamic spiritual tradition — the effort to overcome base desire, ego, and moral failing. A widely cited tradition attributes to the Prophet Muhammad the ranking of this inward jihad as the 'greater struggle,' above military conflict. It is the Sufi functional equivalent of Gurdjieff's battle against the lower self.

A technique JavaScript engines use to compile frequently executed code to machine code at runtime rather than interpreting it line by line. JIT adds a warm-up delay on first run, as the engine must observe code behavior before it can optimize; subsequent executions are faster.

In statistics and machine learning, a joint distribution models the probability of two or more variables — here, audio and video — occurring together. Generating from a joint distribution means the model learns what audio-and-video combinations are realistic as a unit, so outputs are mutually consistent rather than independently sampled and then combined.

An architecture in which a model produces audio and video simultaneously in a single computational pass, rather than generating video first and adding sound afterward. Because both modalities are produced together, sound design — reverb, acoustics, ambient noise — is inherently coherent with the visual scene.

Joint North Sea Wave Project — a physics-based model of how ocean waves grow under sustained wind, derived from field measurements in the North Sea. It encodes the relationship between wind speed, fetch (how far the wind has blown over open water), and the resulting wave energy distribution across frequencies. Using JONSWAP as the input to an FFT simulation produces physically plausible wind-driven seas.

A technique in which a text-to-video prompt is formatted as a JSON object with named keys rather than written as a freeform sentence. The structured format forces the practitioner to specify every creative parameter explicitly and may improve a model’s ability to parse discrete intentions. It is a community convention, not an officially documented API feature, and proliferated alongside the release of Google Veo 3 in mid-2025.

A lightweight remote procedure call protocol that encodes requests and responses as JSON objects. Version 2.0 supports both request-response and notification patterns, making it well-suited for streaming agent updates. The Codex app server uses it as its primary transport layer.

A technique for controlling AI video generators by formatting instructions as a JSON object with labeled fields — "camera", "lighting", "transition", "audio" — rather than as prose. Because each parameter sits in its own named key, the model processes them more independently, reducing the risk of one description contaminating another. It is a community convention, not a formal standard, and the JSON is still passed as a text string rather than executed as code.

The Jewish mystical tradition concerned with the hidden structure of divinity and its relationship to creation, often visualized through the Tree of Life (a diagram of ten divine attributes, or sefirot). Lévi and the Golden Dawn adapted Kabbalah into the framework of Western ceremonial magic, assigning specific colour correspondences to each divine attribute.

A practitioner of Kabbalah, the mystical tradition within Judaism that seeks hidden meanings in scripture through numerological and symbolic methods and engages with cosmological questions about creation and redemption. Kabbalistic calculations of hidden numerical patterns in sacred texts were the primary engine of messianic date-setting in medieval and early modern Jewish communities.

An unshipped Claude Code feature found in the leaked source. It describes an autonomous background-daemon mode that would run nightly memory distillation, subscribe to GitHub webhooks, and maintain persistent agent workers — essentially an always-on AI assistant operating without user invocation.

A macroeconomic accounting identity — derived independently by Polish economist Michal Kalecki and American economist Jerome Levy — showing that aggregate corporate profits equal net investment plus dividends minus household saving minus government saving minus foreign saving. The equation implies that fiscal deficits mechanically boost corporate earnings and that fiscal austerity or a rise in household saving mechanically compresses them. It is a sectoral-balances identity, not a forecast, so it is always exactly true by construction.

A CFTC-regulated prediction market exchange in the United States where participants trade contracts on real-world outcomes — including monthly inflation readings, Federal Reserve decisions, and election results — using real money.

In H.P. Blavatsky's Theosophical framework, the lower self: the fusion of kama (desire, animal passion) with manas (mind). Blavatsky described it as 'the rational but earthly intellect bound by matter' and contrasted it with buddhi-manas — mind oriented toward the spiritual soul. She held that kama-manas must be quieted before union with the Higher Self becomes possible.

A slab of greywacke found in Douglas County, Minnesota in 1898, bearing a runic inscription that purports to record a 1362 Scandinavian expedition deep into North America. Mainstream linguists and runologists regard it as a nineteenth-century forgery: its language resembles modern Swedish rather than any attested medieval dialect, and its runic forms are inconsistent with any verified medieval inscription.

Sarah Kerrigan, the “Queen of Blades,” is the central antagonist-turned-protagonist of *StarCraft*. A psychic military assassin transformed against her will into a Zerg-alien hybrid, she retains her intelligence while shedding her ethical constraints — becoming simultaneously the most powerful entity in the galaxy and a product of institutional violence who transcended her creators.

A reference image placed at a specific moment in a video timeline that the model must match exactly. The model then infers what happens before and after that frame to produce a coherent clip. Borrowed from traditional animation, where keyframes define key poses and in-betweens are interpolated.

A technique in which an animator defines a character's pose at specific moments (keyframes) and software generates the intermediate frames. The quality of those in-between frames — how naturally the body transitions — determines whether motion looks fluid or mechanical.

In traditional animation, a keyframe marks a moment in time where a visual property — position, lighting, camera angle — is explicitly defined; software interpolates everything in between. In AI video generation, 'keyframe accuracy' means the model is constrained to produce specific, user-specified frames at particular timestamps, rather than generating all motion probabilistically from a single starting image. This transforms the model from a creative suggester into a precision executor.

Meaning “of the Gulf” in Arabic (from khalīj, gulf or bay), Khaleeji is used as an adjective for culture, dialect, and aesthetics specific to the Arab states of the Persian Gulf: Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman.

A pre-set price level embedded in a leveraged certificate. If the underlying asset reaches or breaches this level during trading hours, the certificate is immediately terminated and the investor loses the remaining value entirely. The barrier protects the issuer from losses exceeding the investor's stake but makes the product's risk profile resemble a short-dated option more than a fund.

A training technique in which a smaller 'student' model learns to mimic the outputs of a larger 'teacher' model. The student can reach near-teacher performance at a fraction of the compute cost. Legitimate distillation uses only the teacher's outputs, not its weights.

A machine-learning technique in which a smaller “student” model is trained to reproduce the outputs of a larger “teacher” model. The student never accesses the teacher's weights — it learns from the teacher's answers, reasoning traces, or token probabilities. The result is a compact model that approximates the teacher's behavior at lower compute cost.

A training device in Zen Buddhism: a paradoxical question, phrase, or anecdote designed to exhaust the discursive, analytical mind. The koan cannot be resolved through ordinary logic; the intent is to push the practitioner past conceptual thinking toward direct, pre-conceptual experience. Famous examples include ‘What is the sound of one hand clapping?’

A daylight-balanced color negative film stock with an ISO of 250, known for fine grain and accurate skin tones. Widely used in professional cinematography; specifying it in an AI prompt is shorthand for a particular palette and textural quality associated with late-analogue-era filmmaking.

The persistent tendency of Korean equities to trade at a 30–60% valuation discount relative to structurally comparable companies in Taiwan, Japan, or developed Western markets. Attributed primarily to low dividend payout ratios, opaque chaebol cross-shareholding structures, and the incentive effects of South Korea's steep inheritance tax rate on the behaviour of founding families.

South Korea's principal securities exchange, which operates the Korea Stock Exchange for equities and closes each trading day at 3:30 PM Seoul time. Because that translates to roughly 8:30 AM Central European Time, GDRs of Korean companies traded in Frankfurt enter an hours-long window each session where there is no live home-market price anchor, leaving them vulnerable to microstructure dislocations.

A Chinese technology company founded in 2011, operating one of China's two dominant short-video platforms (the other being ByteDance's Douyin). Kuaishou is publicly listed in Hong Kong and has several hundred million monthly active users. Its AI research arm developed the Kling video generation models.

A one-legged dragon motif common in Shang and early Zhou bronze decoration. Often rendered in profile, the kui-dragon typically appears alongside or integrated into the taotie mask. In Shang cosmology, dragons signified divine authority and protective spiritual power.

A paradoxical question, exchange, or story used in Chan and Zen pedagogy to fracture ordinary conceptual thinking. The Chinese word gong'an means "public case" — a legal term signaling that these exchanges function as precedents to be contemplated rather than solved. The kōan as a formal device was invented in Tang-dynasty China; Japan systematized kōan training into formal curricula under Hakuin in the 18th century.

A naturally occurring compound synthesized from lysine and methionine, essential for transporting long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane so they can be oxidized for energy. Deficiency is associated with muscle weakness and fatigue; supplementation has Grade B evidence in ASD children with confirmed deficiency.

L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine — the immediate chemical precursor to dopamine in the biosynthesis pathway. Tyrosine is first converted to L-DOPA by tyrosine hydroxylase, then to dopamine by a second enzyme. L-DOPA is also used clinically to treat Parkinson’s disease, where dopamine-producing neurons have been lost.

An amino acid (N-ethyl-L-glutamine) found almost exclusively in green tea. It crosses the blood-brain barrier and modulates multiple neurotransmitter systems — raising GABA, serotonin, and dopamine while partially blocking excitatory glutamate receptors — producing a state of calm alertness without sedation.

A historic enclosed public market running beneath the Park Avenue elevated rail line in East Harlem, established in the 1930s under Mayor Fiorello La Guardia to provide affordable produce to residents. Now managed by NYCEDC, it operates well below its original capacity and was selected as the first N.Y.C. Groceries site.

The fraction of national income paid to workers as wages, salaries, and benefits. The U.S. labor share of GDI has declined from roughly 58% in 1980 to about 51% today, driven by de-unionization, automation, and the rise of capital-light technology firms that generate high profits with relatively few employees. The decline is the mirror image of the rise in corporate profit share shown in the chart.

A technical indicator that is calculated from past price data and therefore confirms trends that have already formed rather than predicting future direction. All moving averages are lagging by construction. In strongly trending markets the lag is tolerable; in sideways or reversing markets it means the indicator's signal arrives after the optimal entry point has passed, generating 'whipsaws' — trades entered on a false signal that quickly reverse against the trader.

Language Model for Dialogue Applications — Google’s conversational large language model, unveiled in 2021 and later succeeded by Gemini. LaMDA became the subject of public controversy in 2022 when Google engineer Blake Lemoine claimed it was sentient and was subsequently fired. Agüera y Arcas conducted his extended philosophical dialogues with LaMDA, which formed the empirical basis for his consciousness arguments.

An open-source Python library from LangChain that models multi-agent workflows as stateful directed graphs. Nodes represent agents or processing steps; edges represent routing logic. It provides built-in checkpointing, memory, and human-in-the-loop interrupt mechanisms.

A protocol originally developed by Microsoft that separates a language's analysis logic (type checking, go-to-definition, autocomplete) from the editor that displays it. MCP consciously borrows LSP's client-server architecture and applies it to AI tool integrations.

An AI model trained on large datasets of georegistered imagery and 3D reconstructions, analogous to large language models but for spatial understanding. The goal is to enable a machine to infer 3D structure, camera position, and scene identity from a single or small set of 2D images — a capability useful for robotic navigation and AR localization without requiring exhaustive pre-mapped reference data at every location.

A high-voltage transformer used to step electricity up or down for long-distance transmission. Building an AI data center typically requires at least one; lead times as of 2025 run from two to four years, making them a critical-path item for any new facility.

Exploiting the time gap between when information is reflected in one market and when it reaches another. In this context: a bot detects a confirmed Bitcoin price move on Binance milliseconds after it occurs, then places a bet on Polymarket while the odds there still reflect pre-move uncertainty. The trade has no predictive content—the outcome is already known.

A component of the original Genie architecture that infers abstract action representations from video without requiring labeled control inputs. It learns to identify the underlying actions implied by changes between consecutive frames, allowing a world model to be controllable even when trained entirely on unlabeled internet video — the key innovation that made Genie 1 possible.

A chaining technique in generative AI where the output of one model pass — the final frame of a video, the last token of text — becomes the input condition for the next pass. The goal is to maintain coherence across an otherwise discontinuous sequence of generations.

Verbatim text that a language model absorbed during large-scale pretraining and which is ordinarily blocked from appearing in outputs by safety filters. The Alignment Whack-a-Mole study shows that fine-tuning can lower the activation threshold for this stored content, causing it to re-emerge in model outputs even when the original text is never shown as a prompt.

Compressed numerical encodings of image or video frames used internally by diffusion models. Rather than working directly on pixels, these models operate in this lower-dimensional abstract space, which is computationally cheaper to transform. VOID’s second inference pass warps these encodings using optical flow before decoding them back into final video frames.

concepts.term: LATM (Large Language Models as Tool Makers)
concepts.definition: A framework in which a more capable LLM writes Python utility functions (tools) that a smaller, cheaper LLM then uses. Tools are cached and reused across tasks, reducing the need for the larger model in routine operations. The system does not support skill mutation and tools must be pure Python — no external APIs.

Kurzweil's empirical thesis that the rate of technological progress is itself exponentially accelerating. He applies it to computing power, biological sequencing, and nanotechnology to project that human-level AI will arrive by 2029 and a civilizational 'Singularity' by 2045.

The New Thought doctrine that thoughts and emotions magnetically attract corresponding material circumstances — dwell on abundance and abundance follows; focus on lack and lack manifests. The phrase reached mass-market audiences through Rhonda Byrne's 2006 book *The Secret*. It has no scientific basis.

A secondary network built on top of an existing blockchain (the 'Layer 1') that processes transactions more cheaply and quickly, then periodically settles a summary back to the main chain. Base is a Layer 2 built on Ethereum by Coinbase.

The performance pathology that occurs when JavaScript alternates between writing to the DOM and reading geometric measurements from it in a loop. Each read forces a full reflow; each write invalidates the layout tree, requiring the next read to trigger another full recalculation. A loop measuring 500 element heights triggers 500 full layout passes. Chrome DevTools flags this pattern with red entries in the performance timeline.

The browser's internal data structure recording the computed position, size, and geometry of every element on the page. It is built from the DOM and the CSS cascade. Any change to a property that affects an element's size or position invalidates part or all of the tree, requiring it to be recomputed before any geometric measurement can be read back.

The London Bullion Market Association, which oversees the over-the-counter global benchmark market for gold and silver in London. LBMA vault holdings — bars stored in approved London facilities — are reported monthly and serve as a key indicator of physical supply available to meet institutional and central-bank demand.

The elapsed time between placing an order for a piece of equipment and receiving it ready for installation. In data center contexts, power transformer lead times of 128–160 weeks mean a campus breaking ground today cannot be energized from equipment ordered at the same moment; the constraint cascades through the entire construction and activation schedule.

A composite of ten forward-looking data series — including building permits, manufacturing orders, initial jobless claims, stock prices, and the Treasury yield spread — designed to signal turning points in the economy before they appear in current data. Published monthly by The Conference Board. It tends to peak and trough before aggregate economic activity does, though its predictive reliability has been questioned in post-COVID cycles.

Long-Term Equity AnticiPation Securities are exchange-traded options with expiration dates more than one year in the future, typically up to three years. Structurally identical to regular options, they lose time value far more slowly than short-dated contracts, making them a preferred instrument for institutions building large positions over many months without incurring heavy daily decay costs.

A knowledge system organized around what the reader does not yet understand, as opposed to a standard knowledge base, which indexes established understanding for retrieval. The organizing assumption is productive confusion rather than confident recall — the system is built to make active, ongoing epistemic work navigable, not to store conclusions.

Hamming's term for the meta-skill of continuous intellectual self-renewal. Because roughly half of any technical education becomes obsolete within fifteen years, he argued that cultivating the habit of acquiring new knowledge effectively — rather than accumulating particular facts — is the durable advantage that separates great careers from good ones.

A system of deliberate misspelling that replaces standard letters with visually similar numbers or symbols (e.g., ‘explosive’ becomes ‘3xpl0siv3’). Originally from early internet culture; in the jailbreak context, it is used to evade keyword-based content classifiers while remaining readable to the model’s underlying language comprehension.

A section of the prefrontal cortex involved in executive control, working memory, and cognitive inhibition. In this study it is the specific target of rTMS, and previously the site of natural lesions in patients who, the researchers contend, display stronger psi effects as a result.

The Leading Economic Index divided by the Coincident Economic Index, used as a shorthand for how sharply forward-looking signals have diverged from current conditions. A falling ratio means the economy's warning gauges are deteriorating faster than its real-time readings, which has historically preceded recessions. The ratio is a market convention, not an official Conference Board product.

A non-binding preliminary agreement outlining the terms two parties intend to formalize in a contract. In dealmaking, LOIs can be announced publicly and move markets even though they carry no legal obligation to complete. The NVIDIA-OpenAI $100 billion compute partnership was disclosed as an LOI and remained unsigned months later.

A bank's formal commitment to pay a seller upon presentation of shipping documents. In oil and commodity trade, usance LCs defer payment 30–180 days after shipment, tying up the issuing bank's working capital for that window; the buyer repays once the cargo arrives and is resold. When shipments halt, no new LCs are issued and existing ones mature without being replaced, returning capital to the banking system.

A regulatory shorthand for hands-on driver-assist systems that combine adaptive cruise and lane-centering, and sometimes add hands-off functionality on mapped highways. It is the workhorse tier of ADAS today and the segment driving the bulk of new silicon content per vehicle.

The instantaneous correlation between changes in an asset's price and changes in its own volatility. For equity indices it is strongly negative — prices falling and fear rising simultaneously — which is the mathematical origin of the put-heavy implied-volatility skew and, in Dean's model, the primary driver of the frown regime.

The specific trading rule proposed in Gayed and Bilello's 2016 paper: hold the S&P 500 with a fixed leverage multiplier (1.25x, 2x, or 3x) when the index closes above its 200-day moving average, and rotate entirely into three-month Treasury bills when it closes below. The strategy generates roughly five rotations per year on average and was backtested from October 1928 through October 2015.

An acquisition financed largely with borrowed money, using the acquired company's own assets and future cash flows as collateral. LBO analysis leans heavily on EBITDA because the ratio of acquisition debt to EBITDA determines how much leverage a deal can sustain before debt service overwhelms cash generation.

A structured debt instrument issued by a bank that tracks a fixed multiple of the daily return of an underlying asset. Unlike a leveraged ETF, it is a direct obligation of the issuing bank (adding credit risk) and typically includes a knock-out barrier that extinguishes the product if the underlying moves too sharply against the position.

An ETF that uses derivatives (typically swap agreements) to deliver a multiple — commonly 2x or 3x — of an index's *daily* return. Daily resets and volatility decay make these unsuitable for long holding periods.

The performance shortfall that accumulates in a leveraged exchange-traded fund relative to the simple multiple of its underlying index over time. Because a daily-reset leveraged ETF targets a fixed multiple of each day's return (e.g., 3x), the compounded (geometric) return falls below three times the compounded index return whenever volatility is present — a consequence of the mathematical gap between arithmetic and geometric means. The effect is amplified in choppy, mean-reverting markets and reduced in smooth, trending ones. It is sometimes called 'volatility drag' or 'variance drain.'

Sweeping US import tariffs on virtually all trading partners, announced by President Trump on April 2, 2025. They triggered one of the sharpest peacetime selloffs in S&P 500 history — more than 12% over seven sessions — before a 90-day pause on most tariffs was announced on April 9, sparking a 9.5% single-day surge. The episode set the stage for the 2025–2026 market cycle captured in the dashboard.

Shadow libraries: online repositories that aggregate pirated copies of books without authorization from rights holders. Library Genesis (LibGen) and Books3 together contained over 190,000 copyrighted titles and have been identified in litigation as training-data sources for multiple frontier AI models. Internal OpenAI documents produced in discovery confirmed an employee downloaded LibGen collections in 2018.

A survey-based benchmark reflecting the rate at which major banks reported they could borrow from each other. For decades the dominant global reference rate for trillions of dollars in loans, bonds, and derivatives. A 2012 scandal revealed systematic rate manipulation by multiple banks for profit; regulators mandated a transition to transaction-based alternatives. All USD LIBOR panel settings ceased in June 2023.
