Anthropic's next-generation frontier AI model, internally codenamed Capybara. Its existence leaked in March 2026 via unsecured documents; it was formally previewed the following month through Project Glasswing. It is positioned as a successor to the Claude Opus 4.x series with substantially greater autonomous capabilities, particularly in cybersecurity tasks.

A program announced by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in April 2026 to build and own five grocery stores across the five boroughs. The city funds construction and owns the buildings; a private operator selected through competitive procurement runs daily operations under a contract requiring below-market prices for customers.

TSMC's designation for its 2nm-class semiconductor manufacturing process, which entered mass production in 2025. The '2nm' label refers to a benchmark of transistor density and performance rather than a literal physical dimension. N2 is the first TSMC node to deploy gate-all-around transistors at volume, and the first to achieve this at the scale required for consumer-grade chips.

A stable, orally bioavailable precursor to glutathione, the body's principal endogenous antioxidant. It is well-studied clinically — used in hospitals to treat acetaminophen overdose — and has a broad research base in respiratory and metabolic conditions.

Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, a coenzyme found in all living cells that is central to energy metabolism and DNA repair. NAD+ levels decline with age, making it a focus of longevity research; most clinical work uses precursor molecules (NMN, NR) rather than NAD+ itself.

Arabic for 'soul' or 'self'; in Islamic theology and Sufi practice, the term for the ego or lower self in its unreformed state. The Quran identifies stages from the nafs al-ammara (the 'inciting self' that commands toward evil) through progressive levels of purification to the nafs al-mutma'inna (the soul at peace). Taming and purifying the nafs is the central work of Sufi spiritual practice.

The maximum output a plant is designed to produce under normal operating conditions, as specified by its engineering design. Running at 50 percent of nameplate — as Mosaic did at its Florida and Louisiana plants in Q1 2026 — means the facility is operating at half its rated throughput, typically because feedstock costs make full-rate production unprofitable.

A type of non-volatile semiconductor storage that retains data without power by trapping electric charge in floating-gate transistors. The dominant technology in solid-state drives, smartphones, and data center storage arrays. AI training and inference workloads require vast amounts of fast, high-density NAND to store model weights, datasets, and intermediate activations.

Google DeepMind's internal codename for the Gemini 3 Pro Image model, the image-generation system underpinning Gemini 3 Pro's visual capabilities. It succeeded the Nano Banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image model and is built on Gemini 3 Pro, emphasising control, text fidelity, and factual grounding over fast casual image output.

The condition in which an investment thesis has been so widely discussed and adopted that the information advantage that originally made it valuable has been largely arbitraged away, and the primary remaining risk is the crowding and valuation premium that broad adoption has produced.

Fire Information for Resource Management System — a free NASA platform that distributes near-real-time thermal-anomaly and active-fire data globally, refreshed roughly every three to six hours, drawn from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments aboard several Earth-observation satellites. Originally designed to track wildfires, it has been applied to conflict monitoring because large-scale bombardment and destruction generate thermal signatures detectable from orbit.

A network of alternative trading venues operated by Nasdaq across the Nordic countries, classified legally as a multilateral trading facility (MTF) rather than a fully regulated market under EU rules. It carries lighter listing requirements than the main Nasdaq Stockholm market and is the standard listing venue for Nordic growth-stage companies and for structured products such as leveraged certificates.

A stable outcome in a game where no individual player can improve their result by unilaterally changing strategy, assuming all others hold their strategies fixed. Proved to always exist by John Nash in 1950, it extends game theory beyond zero-sum settings to arbitrary competitive scenarios — including markets, arms races, and auctions.

A late prehistoric culture of the Levant (roughly 14,500–11,700 years ago) representing one of the earliest known semi-sedentary societies: hunter-gatherers who built permanent stone structures before the invention of agriculture. Key sites include Eynan (Ain Mallaha) and Nahal Oren in present-day Israel. Natufian communities practiced elaborate burial rites, often interring the dead inside or adjacent to dwellings.

The per-share value of a fund, calculated as total assets minus liabilities divided by shares outstanding. For private funds holding illiquid loans, NAV is estimated rather than derived from market prices, and the frequency and rigor of that estimation is the central controversy the Apollo announcement addresses.

The gap between a holding company's market price and its net asset value — the sum of its underlying stakes. SK Square has historically traded at a 25–47% discount to the value of its SK Hynix stake and other assets.

The best available bid and ask prices for a security, aggregated in real time across all U.S. exchanges and mandated by SEC Regulation NMS. Providing NBBO context alongside a dark pool print reveals whether an institutional trade occurred at a premium or discount to the public market.

The Nasdaq 100 index, which tracks the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. Heavily weighted toward US technology and semiconductor companies, it serves as the primary market barometer for the technology sector's health and is the underlying index for the QQQ ETF and a large suite of futures and options contracts.

Informal social media shorthand for a recurring visual cluster of the 2020s: white-minimal institutional interiors, crystalline architecture, AI governance imagery, and smart-city renders associated with Gulf states and technocratic international forums. Not a coined critical term but a recognized pattern in how certain governments perform modernity.

A computational method for finding the k items in a dataset whose vectors are closest to a query vector, typically measured by cosine or Euclidean distance. In Charcuterie, it retrieves the Unicode characters whose CLIP embeddings most closely match the query glyph's embedding, producing the visual-similarity results the user sees.

The Tibetan State Oracle, institutionally based at Nechung Monastery, through whom the protector deity Pehar is believed to communicate with Tibet’s political leadership. The oracle — a human medium — enters a trance and speaks as the deity. Julian Jaynes Society scholars have cited it as a surviving example of institutionalized bicameral-style divine communication, analogous to the Delphic oracle of ancient Greece.

A learning mechanism in which a behavior is strengthened because it removes or reduces an aversive state — not to be confused with punishment. Stress-driven drinking is a textbook case: alcohol relieves anxiety and cortisol dysregulation, so the relief itself strengthens the habit over time.

A Stoic practice of deliberately picturing the loss or absence of things one values, including the possibility of far worse circumstances. The goal is not pessimism but recalibration: what you have becomes easier to appreciate once you have genuinely imagined losing it or never having had it.

The copper serpent on a pole that Moses fashioned in the wilderness (Numbers 21:8–9), used as a healing object against snakebite. It was kept as a cult object until King Hezekiah destroyed it (2 Kings 18:4) around 700 BCE. In the original text, God instructs Moses to make a *saraph* — the same word as Isaiah's throne-beings — and Moses makes a *nachash* (serpent), treating the terms as functionally synonymous.

A loose family of body-oriented therapies that drew on Reich's clinical framework — armoring, character structure, vegetotherapy — while departing from his later theoretical claims about orgone energy. Major branches include Bioenergetics (Alexander Lowen), Core Energetics (John Pierrakos), Somatic Experiencing (Peter Levine), Hakomi (Ron Kurtz), and SKAN. They share a foundational commitment to treating the body as a site of psychological healing.

The two most commercially important rare earth elements, combined to make the high-strength permanent magnets found in electric-vehicle motors and wind turbines. NdPr oxide is traded by the kilogram; the government's guaranteed floor price of $110/kg for MP Materials' output represents roughly double recent market rates, effectively subsidizing domestic production against cheaper Chinese supply.

A refined rare-earth compound used to make the powerful permanent magnets found in EV motors, wind turbines, and precision-guided weapons. China dominates global processing; domestic US supply is a declared national-security priority.

A political-economic philosophy that emphasizes free markets, deregulation, private enterprise, and reduced state intervention. In housing policy, neoliberal positions favor supply-side solutions — enabling developers to build — over rent control, public housing subsidies, or redistributive programs. The term is far more commonly used by critics than by adherents.

A real-time options flow metric that sums premium from buyer-initiated trades (executed at the ask) and subtracts premium from seller-initiated trades (at the bid). A positive net drift suggests more bullish premium activity; negative, more bearish. Platforms such as Quant Data and Unusual Whales plot this line intraday to track directional bias in options flow.

The spread between the interest income a bank earns on loans and securities and the interest it pays on deposits and borrowings, expressed as a percentage of earning assets. It is the primary driver of bank profitability. NIM compresses when rate-cut expectations reduce future loan yields before deposit costs fall in step, shrinking the profitable gap banks rely on.

concepts.term: Net Present Value and Internal Rate of Return (NPV / IRR)
concepts.definition: Standard project-finance metrics. NPV discounts projected future cash flows back to today's dollars at a chosen rate (here, 5% annually); a positive NPV suggests the project creates value above the cost of capital. IRR is the discount rate at which NPV equals zero — essentially the project's implied return. Both figures are highly sensitive to metal prices, capital cost estimates, and production schedules, all of which at the PEA stage carry wide uncertainty ranges.

The phenomenon by which a platform becomes more valuable as more people join it, because each additional user enlarges the pool of potential matches or connections. Co-founder matching platforms depend on network effects to surface quality candidates, but few have achieved the critical mass needed to become the obvious first stop for solo founders.

A neural network that compresses and decompresses audio by learning a compact, high-fidelity representation of sound. In modern TTS pipelines, a codec converts intermediate model outputs (audio latents or tokens) into the final waveform. Neural codecs have largely replaced traditional signal-processing codecs for high-quality speech synthesis.

A compact neural network that maps a time value and a Gaussian’s identity to a spatial displacement — translating, rotating, or scaling that ellipsoid for a specific frame. It allows a single set of Gaussians to animate across time without storing separate Gaussians per frame.

A small convolutional neural network trained to reconstruct a clean rendered image from a very noisy one — typically produced at one sample per pixel. It is guided by auxiliary buffers (surface normals, albedo, depth) that convey scene geometry independent of the lighting noise. Intel’s OIDN and NVIDIA’s OptiX Denoiser are the leading implementations; oidn-web ports OIDN to WebGPU via TensorFlow.js.

The structured shapes — loops, open curves, surfaces — that emerge when a neural network’s internal activations are plotted in high-dimensional space. Unlike a flat grid of independent features, neural geometry reflects the geometric organization of the world the model was trained on: cyclical concepts form rings, sequential ones form arcs, spatial ones form maps.

A deep-learning approach to translating text between languages. An encoder compresses the source sentence into a dense vector; a decoder generates the target-language sentence from that vector. The technique underpins most modern translation services and is the original domain of the seq2seq architecture.

A method introduced in 2020 for reconstructing a complete 3D scene from a set of 2D photographs taken at different angles. The neural network learns to predict the colour and density of light at any point in space, enabling novel-view synthesis — rendering the scene from angles that were never photographed. NeRF is the conceptual ancestor of the Gaussian Splatting approaches that succeeded it.

A broad term for using neural networks to produce or modify images within the rendering pipeline. In DLSS 5 specifically, it refers to a generative model applied at the geometry level that alters lighting, textures, and surface detail — in contrast to post-process upscaling, which operates on an already-rendered 2D frame.

Misconceptions about the brain that originate in misreadings or oversimplifications of genuine scientific findings. The OECD coined the term in 2002. Documented examples include the belief that people use only 10% of their brains, that left-brain and right-brain types are real, and that visual/auditory/kinesthetic learning styles have neurological validity.

A device or external system that compensates for a neurological deficit. Borretti uses the term to describe a todo list as a substitute for impaired working memory: rather than relying on the brain to surface tasks at the right moment, the list stores them externally and reliably.

A term used by psychologist Gregg Henriques for the pattern in which the self-monitoring function turns against its own emotional states, generating meta-emotions that are often more disabling than the original feeling. Considered a core mechanism in many common mental disorders, including depression, anxiety, and OCD.

A chemical messenger released by a neuron into the synaptic cleft. Binding to receptors on the next neuron, it either increases (excitatory) or decreases (inhibitory) the probability that the receiving cell will fire. Common examples include dopamine, serotonin, glutamate, and GABA.

A West German filmmaking movement from roughly 1962 to the mid-1980s, associated with Fassbinder, Wenders, Herzog, and Schlöndorff. Often funded by public television rather than commercial studios, it was marked by personal and formally adventurous work and a willingness to confront the legacy of Nazism and German national identity in ways mainstream cinema avoided.

concepts.term: New York City Economic Development Corporation
concepts.definition: NYCEDC is a quasi-public nonprofit that implements the city's economic development policy — managing public markets, coordinating real-estate projects, and running business incentive programs. It operates under city contract and pursues goals set by the mayor, but is not a formal city agency, giving it some flexibility in procurement.

A classical root-finding algorithm that solves equations iteratively: it starts from an initial guess, uses the function's slope (derivative) to project a better guess, and repeats until the answer converges to within a desired tolerance. Long the dominant technique for extracting implied volatility from option prices.

The core training objective of most large language models: given a sequence of tokens, predict the most likely next token. The model learns a probability distribution over vocabulary items conditioned on context. Critics argue this process has no necessary relationship to meaning, understanding, or consciousness.

A React-based web application framework developed by Vercel that supports server-side rendering, static site generation, and integrated API routes within a single project. It is the most widely adopted framework for building production React applications and is the underlying technology stack for Font-Stealer.

A boilerplate notice prepended to investment commentary on social media and newsletters, intended to distinguish informal opinion from regulated investment advice. In legal terms it signals that the author is not acting as a licensed investment adviser; in practice, it is widely understood by both writers and readers to be a formality that does not meaningfully alter how the analysis is received or acted upon.

National Instrument 43-101 is the Canadian regulatory standard governing public disclosure of mineral project information. It requires that resource and reserve estimates be prepared and signed off by a 'qualified person' — a geoscientist or engineer with relevant credentials and professional liability. The standard exists partly in response to historical mining frauds; compliant disclosure is more trustworthy than promotional tweets but does not guarantee economic viability.

A halo or luminous aura surrounding the head — or, in some traditions, the entire body — of a divine or sanctified figure in religious art. Found across Christian, Buddhist, Hindu, and Zoroastrian iconographic traditions, though its theological meaning differs in each, and its historical transmission often followed trade and conquest routes rather than independent invention.

An aphorism from Bell Labs researcher Tom Cargill, published in 1985: the first 90% of the code takes 90% of the development time; the remaining 10% takes another 90%. It captures the consistent underestimation of the work needed to complete, test, and harden software — particularly the non-functional requirements that emerge only under real usage.

A Linux distribution where the entire operating system — installed packages, services, settings — is declared in a single version-controlled configuration file. This makes the system reproducible and auditable: any machine with the same config file produces an identical environment, aligning with a security posture that treats the OS as code.

N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor — a subtype of glutamate receptor involved in synaptic plasticity, memory, and arousal. Alcohol partially blocks NMDA receptors, explaining some of its sedating effects. L-theanine also binds here as a partial antagonist, creating a mechanistic overlap between the two substances.

Shannon's stated policy of including only confirmed, copy-paste–reproducible exploits in its final assessment report. The intent is to eliminate false positives — vulnerabilities flagged theoretically but never actually triggered — at the cost of potentially missing attack chains too complex for the current AI agent to replicate end-to-end.

A visual development environment where users assemble software behavior by connecting graphical components rather than writing source code. No-code tools lower the barrier to building automations but typically impose limits on customization compared with hand-written code.

A web-based tool that extracts data from websites through a visual interface — typically a point-and-click element selector — without requiring the user to write any code. The underlying scraping logic, proxy management, and infrastructure are handled by the service provider.

In a vibrating surface, nodal lines are the regions that remain stationary while the rest of the surface oscillates. In Chladni figures, granular material collects along these lines because the vibration drives it away from the antinodes (peaks of motion) toward the still points. They are the visible skeleton of a standing-wave pattern.

A small Node.js server that acts as the connector between the browser-rendered Phaser frontend and the live system state the agents are managing. It relays data — task counts, agent outputs, system events — to the visual interface in real time.

A visual programming pattern in which logic is expressed as a directed graph of connected nodes rather than lines of text code. Widely used in shader editors, VFX tools, and game engines; Three Shading Language applies the same idea to browser-based GPU materials.

A visual programming paradigm in which processing steps are represented as rectangular blocks (nodes) connected by lines representing data flow. Common in professional VFX and video tools; adopted by AI generation tools like ComfyUI and Flora as a way to build complex multi-step pipelines without writing code.

A visual programming interface in which discrete processing steps (e.g., 'text to image', 'image to video') are represented as boxes connected by lines. Users build pipelines by linking nodes rather than writing code, a paradigm popularized by tools like Blender's shader editor and ComfyUI.

A material system where shading logic is defined as a graph of interconnected nodes — each node performing one operation — rather than as raw shader code. It offers composability, cross-backend portability, and visual editability, and is the foundation of TSL in Three.js.

A term coined by William James to describe one of the hallmarks of mystical experience: the strong sense that the experience is conveying genuine knowledge or insight, not mere feeling or sensation. The noetic quality is what makes a mystical experience feel like discovery rather than dream — and what makes it so philosophically inconvenient to dismiss.

MiniMax's proprietary architectural modification to standard diffusion pipelines. Rather than applying equal compute across all denoising steps, NCR allocates more processing to the steps with the highest prediction error, skipping or simplifying steps that contribute little to final quality. The company claims this achieves roughly 2.5x throughput gains without degrading output.

Philip Converse’s 1964 term for the unstable, internally inconsistent political opinions held by most citizens — opinions that change near-randomly when re-surveyed over time, suggesting they are not genuine beliefs at all but responses generated on the fly. Citizens without coherent ideological frameworks navigate politics primarily through partisan loyalty and group cues, not belief evaluation.

A property of an operation where swapping the order of inputs changes the result. Matrix multiplication is non-commutative: AB and BA generally differ, and one may not even be defined. This follows naturally from the fact that composing transformations is order-dependent — the sequence in which you apply them matters.

Allowing feelings to arise and pass without layering evaluative thought on top of them — noticing what one feels without immediately assessing whether the feeling is appropriate or proportionate. Appears in mindfulness traditions, acceptance-based therapies, and psychedelic-assisted therapy as a mechanism of emotional integration rather than suppression.

The standard professional approach to video editing where clips are arranged on a timeline and can be rearranged or trimmed freely without altering the original source files. Contrasted with older 'linear' tape-based editing where cuts were permanent.

The one-time design, simulation, and verification costs required to bring a chip from concept to a manufacturable product. NRE at the 2nm node is estimated at $725 million or more and must be paid before volume production begins — making NRE recovery through high unit volumes an existential requirement for any advanced chip program.

One-time payments a customer makes to cover the cost of designing or qualifying a custom component. NRE fees appear in revenue during the development phase but do not repeat once a product enters volume production — at which point unit shipments replace them. FOCI's current CPO-related revenue is almost entirely NRE, signaling that the program is still pre-production.

Memory that preserves stored data even when power is removed, as opposed to volatile memory (like DRAM) that loses its contents when unpowered. NAND flash and NOR flash are the most common types in consumer and industrial electronics.

A travel reservation — flight, hotel night, or package — whose purchase price cannot be returned if the buyer cancels. Airlines and hotels typically price these fares lower upfront in exchange for keeping the money if plans change. The arrangement creates stranded value when genuine emergencies force cancellations, which resale platforms now try to recover.

A type of non-volatile (data-retaining without power) flash memory optimized for fast random reads and in-place code execution, used primarily in automotive control units, industrial sensors, and networking equipment. It is smaller in capacity but more reliable and faster-access than NAND flash, which dominates bulk storage applications like SSDs and smartphones.

Internet slang for a person who participates in mainstream culture and is unaware of niche online subcultures. Used descriptively and, depending on context, with varying degrees of contempt, affection, or envy.

A seasonal wind shift that draws moisture from the Gulf of Mexico and Gulf of California northward into Arizona and New Mexico each July through September, triggering afternoon thunderstorms and the towering cumulonimbus formations the region is known for. Locally called simply "the monsoon."

Also called Dated Brent, this is the physical benchmark price for crude oil loading from North Sea fields within a specific near-term delivery window. It serves as the global reference price for roughly two-thirds of internationally traded crude, making it the number most commonly cited when analysts describe where oil prices stand.
The face value of all positions traded — including leveraged instruments like futures — which can be a much larger number than the actual capital deployed.

A work of prose fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel — typically 20,000 to 40,000 words. The form allows sustained character development without the sprawling sub-plots of a full novel. Publishers have historically been reluctant to market novellas on their own, though they are a format beloved by many major writers.

A reusable software module distributed through npm (Node Package Manager), JavaScript's dominant package registry. Running `npm install -g openclaw` downloads OpenClaw and makes it available as a system-wide command. npm ships bundled with Node.js, which on macOS is itself installable via the Homebrew package manager.

A Node.js tool runner that executes a package from the npm registry without requiring a prior global install. In the Agent Skills context, `npx claude skills add <name>` fetches and installs a skill into the current project in a single command.

Formal approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) that a reactor design meets federal safety requirements. A certified design can be referenced in construction permit applications without re-litigating design-level safety questions — a significant regulatory shortcut that can shave years off a project timeline.

A special preferences domain in macOS, addressable as `-g` in the `defaults` command, that stores settings shared across all Cocoa applications. Values written here act as a system-wide fallback for any app that does not define its own override in its per-app domain.

A subgenre of heavy metal that emerged in the mid-1990s, blending alternative metal with elements of hip-hop, funk, and grunge. Prominent acts included Korn, Limp Bizkit, and Linkin Park. The genre reached peak commercial popularity between roughly 1999 and 2003 before a sharp critical and commercial decline.

The U.S. federal agency that licenses and oversees civilian nuclear facilities, including uranium enrichment plants. An NRC license is required before any facility can legally produce enriched uranium on American soil; Centrus received its HALEU-specific license amendment in June 2021.

A region in the brain's basal forebrain that is central to reward, motivation, and addiction. Dopamine released here reinforces drug-taking behaviour. Animal research shows pregabalin activates this circuit through D1 dopamine receptors — the same pathway engaged by cocaine and opioids — explaining its genuine addiction potential.

An inference technique for autoregressive models in which, at each prediction step, the model samples only from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability mass exceeds a threshold (the nucleus). This balances output diversity against coherence, and is borrowed directly from NLP text generation practice.

A straight line on which every point corresponds to a real number, with positive numbers to the right and negative to the left. It makes arithmetic operations visually concrete: addition is rightward movement, subtraction leftward, and so on. The number line is the simplest one-dimensional geometric space.

The functional ability to reason with numbers in everyday contexts: comparing quantities, interpreting statistics, estimating magnitudes. Distinct from mathematical expertise; considered a basic component of adult literacy.

Nvidia's proprietary high-bandwidth chip-to-chip interconnect, used to connect multiple GPUs within a single server or rack at speeds far higher than PCIe. NVLink 6, used in the GB200 NVL72 rack system, connects 72 Blackwell GPUs via a passive copper backplane at aggregate bandwidths of hundreds of terabytes per second — without requiring any optical interconnect inside the rack.

The Original band of optical fiber transmission, centered near 1310 nm wavelength. Chromatic dispersion — the frequency-dependent spreading of optical pulses — is near zero in standard single-mode fiber at this wavelength, making the O-band preferred for short-reach datacenter links where dispersion compensation would otherwise add cost and complexity.

A model of production developed by economist Michael Kremer in 1993 in which total output equals the product, not the sum, of each task’s quality level. Named after the Challenger disaster, where a single failed rubber seal destroyed the whole mission. The implication is that small improvements in any component compound multiplicatively across the whole project, so high-skill inputs cluster together and the weakest link dominates.

Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations, an academic simulation engine maintained by the CAMEL-AI research community. It can model up to one million AI agents interacting on social media-like platforms, supporting 23 action types such as posting, liking, and following. MiroFish uses OASIS as its underlying simulation infrastructure.

A credential issued by a subscription-based service that authenticates the holder as a paying subscriber. Unlike a metered API key, usage is counted against a flat monthly allowance rather than billed per request. In OpenClaw's setup, the relevant token is generated via `claude setup-token` in the terminal and is tied to a Claude.ai Pro or Max account.

A SAM 3.1 capability that groups multiple tracked objects into a single forward pass through the model, eliminating the per-object compute overhead of earlier versions. It enables roughly a 7× throughput improvement when tracking large numbers of objects in a video stream.

A technique introduced in SAM 3.1 that processes multiple tracked objects together in a single neural-network forward pass, rather than one pass per object. At 16 objects on an H100 server GPU, this roughly doubles throughput compared with the serial approach in the original SAM 3. The mechanism is implemented in SAM 3.1's MultiplexMaskDecoder component.

A local-first, Markdown-based note-taking application with a graph-based backlink visualiser, widely used in personal knowledge management. In Karpathy’s architecture, Obsidian serves as the ‘IDE’ for browsing the LLM-maintained wiki — a read interface the human uses, not a writing environment.

An industry-wide interoperability standard for co-packaged optics that defines the interface between photonic modules and switch or compute ASICs. MSA compliance allows modules from different vendors to work together, a prerequisite for a commercial CPO ecosystem to form around the technology.

Software that converts images of printed or handwritten text into machine-readable, searchable, and editable text. A core capability in document-scanning apps, enabling a photo of a contract to become a text file rather than a static image.

An octree is a tree data structure that divides 3D space by recursively splitting it into eight sub-cubes. In 3D shape generation, octree resolution controls the maximum fineness of spatial detail that can be represented. Higher resolution captures sharper edges and finer geometry but requires more memory and compute to generate.

Financial commitments that do not appear as liabilities on a company's balance sheet under standard accounting rules — such as operating leases, non-cancelable purchase contracts, and take-or-pay agreements with data center developers. These represent real future cash outflows that can materially affect financial flexibility but are easy for investors to overlook in headline debt figures.

Using a drug for a purpose, patient population, or dosage not specified in its regulatory approval. Off-label prescribing is legal and common in medicine, but it means the specific use has not been formally evaluated for safety and efficacy by a regulatory body.

A variant of reinforcement learning in which an agent is trained on a fixed dataset of previously collected experiences, rather than by interacting live with an environment. This avoids the safety and cost risks of live exploration but requires the historical data to cover the scenarios the agent needs to learn from. Memento-Skills uses it to train the skill router on historical execution-success signals.

Companies that provide the equipment, technology, and labor that oil and gas producers use to drill, complete, and maintain wells. Major players include Baker Hughes, Halliburton, and SLB. OFS earnings are a leveraged proxy for overall industry drilling activity — rising when producers actively drill and falling when they pull back.

A popular open-source tool that packages and serves LLMs locally via a REST API, with a Docker-like model management interface. It has become the de facto standard for running language models on developer machines; rkllama is designed to be API-compatible so existing Ollama integrations work on Rockchip hardware.

The first major civilization of Mesoamerica, flourishing in the Gulf Coast lowlands of modern Mexico from approximately 1500 to 400 BCE. The Olmec are known for colossal stone heads, jade carving, and zoomorphic imagery — particularly the were-jaguar motif — that influenced later Mesoamerican cultures including the Maya and Aztec.

A measure of a stock's sensitivity to a risk factor, estimated by ordinary least squares regression of daily stock returns against the factor's returns over a rolling window. A market beta of 0.81 means the stock historically moves about 81 cents for every dollar the broader market moves.

An intermittent fasting protocol in which a person eats only one meal within a narrow daily window, typically one to two hours. Proponents claim benefits including metabolic flexibility and autophagy induction; critics cite risks of nutrient deficiency, muscle loss, and disordered eating patterns.

A reinforcement-learning practice where the model being trained generates its own training data by acting in the environment — here, real virtual machines. The model learns from its own mistakes rather than a fixed human-annotated dataset, improving robustness over time.

An electrical facility containing transformers and switching gear that steps voltage up or down between a power source and end users. Owning a substation eliminates the need to queue for utility-owned infrastructure and is a key element of DGXX’s claimed supply chain advantage.

In machine learning and robotics, online learning refers to a system's ability to update its model or policy continuously from live experience, in contrast to training once on a fixed dataset. The field has long grappled with challenges of stability (avoiding catastrophic forgetting), safety (exploration that does not damage hardware), and drift (what happens when errors compound over time).

Hamming's observation that scientists who kept their office doors open were less productive day-to-day but more productive over careers, because open doors kept them calibrated to what problems actually mattered. Closed doors optimized for current tasks at the cost of long-run direction.

A securities transaction executed through a public exchange at the prevailing market price, as opposed to grants, awards, or private placements. Open-market purchases by insiders are considered a stronger signal than compensatory equity because they involve the insider's own money at the same price available to any retail buyer.

A widely adopted API standard, originated by OpenAI, for sending messages to a language model and receiving a structured response. Many providers now implement the same interface, making it a de facto interoperability standard: a client built for one model can switch to another by changing a single endpoint URL.

An HTTP API that accepts requests in the same format OpenAI defined for its own models — the same URL paths, authentication scheme, and JSON request/response shapes. Because many providers now speak this de-facto standard, any client written for OpenAI can talk to compatible endpoints with a single URL change. OpenClaw uses this to make its local gateway swappable across providers.

A modular add-on that extends an OpenClaw agent's capabilities — web search, voice transcription, document indexing, and so on. Skills are installed from the ClawHub marketplace and execute within a single agent process, allowing one agent to call specialized tools without spawning competing agent instances that lose shared context.

Universal Scene Description, an open-source file format and ecosystem developed originally by Pixar and now stewarded by the Alliance for OpenUSD. It provides a common language for 3D assets, allowing tools from different vendors — renderers, AI generators, game engines — to exchange scene data without losing information. Think of it as the PDF of 3D content.

The cash actually generated by a company's core business activities in a given period. Unlike operating income, it adds back non-cash charges such as depreciation and stock-based compensation, and adjusts for changes in working capital. It is generally considered a harder-to-manipulate measure of earnings quality than accounting income.

An interdisciplinary field applying mathematical optimization — linear programming, simulation, queuing theory, dynamic programming — to complex organizational decisions. Born from World War II logistics problems, it became the quantitative backbone of business management science in the postwar decades and the subject of Trueman’s textbook.

Hebrew word for 'wheels.' In Ezekiel 1:15–21, the *ophanim* appear alongside the Cherubim as immense wheels within wheels, their rims covered in eyes, able to move in any direction without turning. Tradition identifies them with the 'Thrones' in the nine-fold hierarchy, though this equation is a theological inference rather than an explicit biblical equation.

A low-income census tract designated under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act in which investors may defer or reduce capital-gains taxes by deploying proceeds into qualifying investments. Intended to spur economic development; critics note the benefits have often flowed to projects in already-appreciating areas.

The difference in optical power between the high and low levels of a modulated optical signal, expressed in mW or dBm. OMA directly determines how easily a receiver can distinguish ones from zeros; standards bodies specify minimum OMA values for compliant transceivers.

The stock price at which an options trade neither gains nor loses at expiration. For a call, it equals the strike price plus the premium paid. A $22 call bought for $3.50 breaks even only if the stock reaches $25.50.

The date on which a tranche of options contracts expire, obligating their settlement or lapse. For U.S. equity index options, the standard monthly cycle expires on the third Friday of each month. Large open-interest concentrations at a given OPEX date can create structural market pressure as dealers simultaneously unwind their hedges.

Real-time data on options contract activity, specifically large orders filled at or above the ask price — indicating a buyer willing to pay up. Calls skew bullish, puts bearish. Widely used as a leading indicator of institutional intent, since options buyers often telegraph moves in the underlying stock before those moves appear on the equity tape.

Options amplify percentage moves relative to the underlying stock. A moderate gain in the stock can translate to a much larger percentage gain in an OTM call, because the absolute price change represents a large fraction of the small premium. This cuts symmetrically: a stock that goes nowhere renders the option worthless.

The pattern by which implied volatility differs across strike prices for options at the same expiry. In most equity markets, out-of-the-money puts carry higher IV than equivalent calls — a negative skew reflecting institutional demand for crash insurance. When skew inverts — calls more expensive than puts — it signals unusual demand for upside speculation relative to downside protection.

Intermarket sweep orders that execute across multiple exchanges simultaneously in rapid succession, prioritizing speed over price. The urgency is the signal — a buyer willing to fill across many venues at once is typically expressing high conviction. Unusual Whales tracks individual sweeps and flags aggregated sweep activity as particularly significant.

Tortoise shells and ox shoulder blades used by Shang diviners to communicate with ancestors and gods. Scribes would inscribe a question, apply heat until the bone cracked, and read the crack pattern as divine answer. The inscriptions, known as jiaguwen, constitute China's earliest confirmed writing and record detailed sacrificial protocols.

A theory of consciousness proposed by Hameroff and Penrose in the 1990s, holding that consciousness arises from quantum-mechanical wave-function collapses — 'objective reductions' governed by gravitational effects — inside neuronal microtubules, with the process 'orchestrated' by synaptic inputs. It is a minority view contested on both physical grounds (decoherence) and biological grounds (no experimental evidence).

In an AI pipeline, the component that coordinates other models — deciding what to ask them, in what sequence, and with what inputs. Here, Claude acts as the orchestrator: it writes the prompts that direct Veo 3, while Veo 3 does the actual rendering.

A multi-agent architecture in which one AI instance (the orchestrator) decomposes a high-level task and dispatches subtasks to subordinate instances (subagents). The orchestrator aggregates results and handles conflicts; each subagent focuses on a narrow, well-defined piece of work.

Emmett Shear's term for the way a group of intelligent agents achieves genuine coordination — not through externally imposed rules but through each agent internalizing values by taking a real stake in the system they inhabit. Shear applies the concept to AI systems at Softmax, but it maps directly onto his view of human community and character.

A term coined by Wilhelm Reich for what he claimed was a measurable universal life force permeating all living matter. He built orgone accumulators — layered wood-and-metal enclosures — to concentrate it, and treated patients including cancer patients with them. Scientists could not replicate his findings, the FDA obtained an injunction against the devices, and Reich died in federal prison in 1957. Contemporary Reichian practitioners generally treat 'energy' as a phenomenological description of felt bodily experience rather than a physical-science claim.

The segment of the semiconductor supply chain that handles the back-end steps of chip production: packaging finished silicon dies into protective housings, bonding wire connections, and testing completed chips before they ship to device manufacturers. Major OSATs include Amkor (Western) and ASE Technology (Taiwanese). Advanced packaging — techniques like 2.5D interposers and 3D die stacking — has made this once-commoditized business a critical bottleneck in AI chip supply.

A benchmark for evaluating GUI automation agents on real desktop-computer tasks across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Tasks are scored on completion rate across up to 50 interaction steps, making it one of the most demanding public tests for computer-use systems.

A benchmark that tests AI models on autonomous desktop tasks — navigating file systems, operating GUI applications, completing multi-step workflows — using a standardised virtual machine environment. It is one of the primary measures used to evaluate computer-use capability, with a human baseline of 72.4%.

Over-the-counter bond trading, in which buyers and sellers negotiate directly with dealers rather than through a centralized exchange. Because prices are not publicly posted, the communication channels between participants — historically, Instant Bloomberg — carry significant structural importance.

The practice of testing a trading rule or predictive model on data it was not used to construct — events that occurred after the strategy was designed — to distinguish genuine predictive power from retrospective curve-fitting. A strategy back-tested only on the same events that inspired its construction has not been out-of-sample validated and cannot reliably claim forward-looking edge.

A method of flagging videos whose view counts substantially exceed a channel's historical average. A high outlier score is read as evidence that a format or topic resonated unusually well, making it a candidate for imitation across similar channels.

Extending a scene beyond its current boundaries by generating new content consistent with what already exists. In 2D image editing this means growing an image at its edges; in GaussianGPT it means iteratively sliding a context window across a floor plan, generating new 3D Gaussian columns conditioned on the previously generated ones.

A technical condition in which an asset's price has risen so sharply that momentum indicators exceed a set threshold, suggesting buying pressure has become extreme. It describes intensity, not direction — in strong uptrends, assets can remain overbought for weeks or months before correcting. It is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a top.
Calibrating a model so precisely to historical data that it captures noise rather than signal, causing it to underperform in live markets.

A Federal Reserve facility that allows money-market funds and other counterparties to park cash at the Fed overnight in exchange for US Treasury securities, earning a set interest rate. Large RRP balances effectively remove money from the banking system, suppressing M2. As those balances drain, M2 rises — again with no direct implication for global conditions.

A sharp, rapid recovery in an asset or index that follows a period of extreme selling pressure, typically when technical indicators such as the RSI (Relative Strength Index) have fallen below 30. Oversold bounces are mechanically distinct from melt-ups: they are relief rallies driven by the reversal of extreme pessimism — short-sellers closing positions, value buyers stepping in — rather than by fresh enthusiasm. The historical NASDAQ top-25 thirteen-day return episodes are almost all oversold bounces; the April 2026 episode is not.

A complete RSI round-trip from below 30 (oversold) to above 70 (overbought). Tracking the speed of this journey is one way analysts gauge the ferocity of a market reversal. The Nasdaq 100 historically completes this cycle in roughly 67 trading sessions on average; doing it in 11, as in April 2026, is unprecedented in forty years of data.

The Open Web Application Security Project, a nonprofit that publishes and maintains the OWASP Top 10 — an authoritative list of the most critical web application security risk categories. Organizations worldwide use the Top 10 as a baseline checklist for secure development and security testing.

A free, deliberately vulnerable Node.js e-commerce application maintained by OWASP for security training and practice. It is intentionally riddled with exploitable vulnerabilities across every OWASP Top 10 category and is the most widely used target for security tool demonstrations — meaning a successful attack against it is a baseline expectation, not evidence of novel capability.

Price-to-earnings ratio: share price divided by earnings per share. A high P/E means investors are paying more for each dollar of profit, often because they expect rapid growth. Used as a shorthand for how expensive a stock appears relative to its current earnings.

A term in the solopreneur app community for a subscription product targeting an acute, emotionally charged behavioral problem — addiction, anxiety, lack of discipline — rather than a nice-to-have feature. The theory is that users experiencing genuine pain are more likely to pay immediately, renew persistently, and recommend the app to others in the same situation.

Pulse Amplitude Modulation with 4 levels — a signalling scheme that encodes 2 bits per symbol by using four distinct signal amplitudes instead of the two used in simpler NRZ signalling. At a given baud rate, PAM4 doubles data throughput, but it is more sensitive to noise and requires tighter modulator linearity and higher bandwidth. It is the standard for 100G/lane and 200G/lane optical transceivers.

Pulse-Amplitude Modulation 4-level Digital Signal Processor — a specialized chip that encodes and decodes the PAM4 signaling scheme used in 400G and 800G optical transceivers. PAM4 doubles throughput by transmitting two bits per symbol using four distinct light intensity levels. MaxLinear's Keystone chips are a leading commercial example.

In commodity markets, accelerated purchasing driven by fear of future scarcity rather than immediate operational need. It is self-reinforcing: each purchase depletes available stock, confirming others' fears and prompting more buying. The result is a spike in spot prices that can far exceed what underlying supply-demand fundamentals would justify.

A weaker variant of panpsychism holding that subatomic matter carries 'proto-conscious' properties — not full experience, but its building blocks — that combine into consciousness at sufficient complexity. David Chalmers has associated this position with his approach to the hard problem; it is the framing Kurzweil borrows in his 2024 book.

An unrealised decline in the value of an investment that exists only as an accounting entry until the asset is actually sold. Large aggregate paper losses in market capitalisation do not represent cash leaving the economy — only a revision in the price at which willing buyers and sellers agree to transact.

Simulated trading in which orders are logged and position P&L is tracked against live market prices, but no real money changes hands. Used for strategy testing and agent experiments. Paper trading eliminates real-world execution risks — slippage, partial fills, margin calls arriving faster than software can respond — which means results cannot be directly extrapolated to live trading performance.

A verification workflow that compares the claims and methodology described in a published research paper against the actual code in its accompanying public repository, flagging discrepancies, undocumented assumptions, and reproducibility risks. Feynman's /audit command automates this check.

An atmospheric optical phenomenon — also called 'mock suns' or 'sun dogs' — in which bright spots of light appear to the left and right of the sun, caused by sunlight refracting through hexagonal plate-shaped ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere. Medieval and early modern observers frequently interpreted parhelia as divine portents; the Wunderzeichenbuch records at least a dozen separate occurrences.

John Vervaeke's term for the mode of cognition in which an agent is not an external observer of reality but is constitutively shaped by, and co-creates, the patterns it engages with. Distinct from propositional knowing (knowing that), procedural knowing (knowing how), and perspectival knowing (knowing what it's like). Vervaeke argues that modernity's over-reliance on propositional knowledge has atrophied participatory knowing, severing agents from the sense of meaningful embeddedness.

The widespread career belief that you should identify a pre-existing passion and then seek work that matches it. Critics argue this gets causality backwards: passion typically emerges from developing rare, valuable skills over time rather than preceding the work itself.

A photorealistic rendering technique that simulates light by firing thousands of random rays per pixel, following each ray as it bounces off surfaces, and averaging the results to solve the full rendering equation. It produces physically correct global illumination — including indirect light, caustics, and soft shadows — but converges slowly, making real-time use without denoising impractical.

The Stoic term for irrational passions or emotions that disturb rational judgment. The four primary pathê are: desire (for what one doesn't have), fear (of what one doesn't want), irrational pleasure (in present circumstances), and distress (irrational pain about present circumstances). The Stoic goal is not to eliminate feeling but to replace these irrational states with the eupatheiai — good emotions consistent with virtue.

A pricing model in which charges are based on the number of tokens — roughly, word-fragments — processed in each AI request. Input and output tokens are billed separately at different rates. Agentic tools that run many sequential steps consume tokens far faster than conversational use, making per-token billing expensive relative to a flat monthly subscription.

In mobile apps, a paywall is the screen at the end of an onboarding flow that asks the user to subscribe or start a free trial before accessing core features. A hard paywall gives users no way to skip it — subscribe or leave. SDKs such as Superwall let developers A/B-test paywall designs, pricing, and timing without resubmitting the app to the App Store.

The People's Bank of China, China's central bank. It publishes M2 data in yuan, making it the world's largest single-country M2 aggregate by some measures — yet it is excluded from most casual references to “M2” in Western financial media, which default to the US figure.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, published by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, is the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. It covers a broader basket of goods and services than the CPI and uses chain-weighting to adjust for consumer substitution behavior. “Core PCE,” which strips out food and energy prices, is the primary measure the Fed monitors when assessing progress toward its 2% inflation target.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of U.S. consumer inflation. It differs from the more familiar CPI in its weights and methodology, and tends to run somewhat lower, making it a slightly less alarming headline number.

Informal name for the dietary and metabolic framework developed by biologist Ray Peat, centred on thyroid health, high fruit-sugar intake, saturated fats, and avoidance of polyunsaturated fatty acids. It attracts a dedicated online following that is broadly suspicious of mainstream nutrition science and institutional medicine.

The process by which scientists evaluate each other's manuscripts before publication, assessing methodology, originality, and accuracy. Reviewers are almost universally unpaid by publishers, treating it as a professional obligation. The aggregate value of this labor has been estimated at over $1.5 billion annually in the United States alone.

The logical problem inherent in relative valuation: a multiple derived from comparable companies assumes those companies are correctly priced by the market. If an entire sector is overvalued, every firm within it will screen as fairly priced against its neighbors, embedding the shared mispricing invisibly into the valuation.

The Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills, developed by Elizabeth Laugeson at UCLA. The most rigorously validated social-skills training program for autistic adolescents and adults, with randomized controlled trial evidence showing durable improvements in social knowledge, engagement frequency, and reduced symptoms. Unlike script-based approaches, PEERS uses role-play video analysis, group discussion of what worked, and naturalistic peer practice.

Price/Earnings-to-Growth ratio: a stock’s price-to-earnings ratio divided by its projected earnings growth rate. A PEG below 1.0 is conventionally considered undervalued relative to growth; below 0.5 is unusually cheap. It adjusts for the fact that fast-growing companies deserve higher P/E multiples than slow growers.

Short for penetration tester: a security professional — or, increasingly, an automated tool — that probes systems by simulating real-world attacks to discover exploitable weaknesses before a malicious actor does. Ethical pentesting requires explicit written authorization from the system owner.

The zone of partial shadow surrounding the fully dark core (umbra) of a shadow, produced because the light source has a finite angular width rather than being a perfect geometric point. In sunlight, the penumbra around a twig's shadow widens with distance from the branch, since more of the sun's disk can be partially obscured at greater distances.

A Gemma 4 architectural feature in which a second embedding table provides a separate conditioning signal at each transformer layer, rather than sharing one embedding across all layers. This improves model quality but requires special handling during quantization, since naive compression of PLE layers degrades output.

A measure of copying accuracy expressed as the probability that each individual position in a newly synthesized strand is correctly matched to the template. At 94.1%, QT45 makes roughly one error in every seventeen positions.

A feed-forward 3-D reconstruction approach that assigns one Gaussian primitive to each pixel of each input image, yielding a Gaussian count equal to the total number of input pixels across all views. This is straightforward but produces extremely large Gaussian clouds — often tens of millions of primitives — making subsequent processing expensive. ReSplat's initialisation stage operates in a 16× subsampled space to avoid this overhead while improving quality.

A comparison technique that measures visible pixel-level differences between two screenshots, weighted by how noticeable the differences would be to the human eye. Used in UI testing to catch visual regressions that code assertions miss — a perceptual diff can flag a subtle color shift or spacing error that an exact byte comparison would not surface.

A higher-fidelity form of motion capture that records not just body movement but also subtle facial acting and finger detail simultaneously, as used in films and AAA video games. It typically requires professional studios and is distinct from the lighter 'body-only' capture used for blocking and reference.

Data extracted from a video clip that captures how a subject is moving and expressing — including body pose, facial muscle positions, and lip-sync timing. Modify Video uses these as anchors: they tell the AI what to preserve (the acting, the movement) while everything else in the frame is free to be transformed.

The standardised disclosure form that members of Congress and covered federal employees must file within 45 days of any securities transaction exceeding $1,000 in value. PTRs are publicly posted by the House Clerk and Senate Secretary and form the raw data for congressional trading trackers.

A gradient noise algorithm invented by Ken Perlin in the early 1980s that produces smooth, organic-looking randomness without blocky artifacts. Widely used in shaders to simulate natural phenomena — water ripples, terrain, fire, shimmer — by feeding a time-varying noise value into vertex displacement or UV distortion.

A derivative contract that functions like a futures contract — allowing leveraged exposure to an asset's price — but with no expiry date. Traders can hold positions indefinitely. Because there is no settlement date, perpetuals use a funding rate mechanism to keep the contract price anchored to the underlying spot price. They are the dominant trading instrument on both centralised and decentralised crypto exchanges.

A standard benchmark metric for language models measuring how well the model predicts a held-out text corpus — lower is better. A 1% perplexity increase from compression means the model finds text marginally less predictable than the uncompressed baseline, a degradation typically considered acceptable.

Borrowed from startup finance, where burn rate measures how fast a company spends cash before becoming profitable. Applied to personal life, it means monthly living expenses. Keeping it low preserves optionality — the freedom to change direction without financial pressure forcing the decision.

Originally a New Thought–era term for a purported psychic or energetic force that makes certain individuals uniquely attractive and influential. In contemporary self-improvement usage it refers more mundanely to charisma, commanding presence, and social dominance — the ability to draw others’ attention and compliance without apparent effort.

A category of product where individuals create software applications for their own use through natural-language descriptions alone, with no programming involved. Wabi applies this label to itself. The concept extends vibe coding into pure consumer territory: the output is not code a developer iterates on but a finished app that a non-technical user owns, shares, and remixes.

Positron emission tomography — a brain-scanning technique using radioactive tracers to measure receptor availability and metabolic activity in living tissue. PET studies have quantified what percentage of a brain’s serotonin-2 receptors are occupied (blocked) at a given drug dose, providing direct evidence of cyproheptadine’s central action.

An IRS designation for a foreign corporation that earns 75% or more of its gross income from passive sources (dividends, interest, rents, royalties, capital gains) or holds 50% or more of its assets in passive-income-producing investments. PFIC status triggers punitive tax treatment on gains and distributions for U.S. shareholders.

CitriniResearch's label for the first wave of AI investment: the hardware and infrastructure buildout — GPUs, memory, networking, advanced packaging, and power — that preceded the application-layer software wave. The framework held that investors should identify and rotate into each successive hardware bottleneck, then exit to 'Phase 2' software and deployment names once market pricing had fully absorbed each bottleneck thesis.

An early-stage human drug trial combining first-in-human safety testing (Phase I) with initial evidence of efficacy (Phase II) in a single study design. Common in rare-disease and neurological programs where eligible patient populations are too small to run sequential studies; positive Phase I/II data is encouraging but does not guarantee later-stage success or regulatory approval.

An investment thesis holding that capital migrates in sequence across distinct segments of a technology build-out — in the AI case, from semiconductor makers to data-centre infrastructure to physical-world AI applications and finally to software. Investors who correctly anticipate each rotation aim to own the next phase before it is widely recognised and priced in, accepting that early-phase winners may underperform once capital moves on.

An open-source JavaScript game engine for building 2D games that run in any web browser. It handles sprite rendering, tilemaps, and character animation. Originally built for games, it has been adopted as a lightweight visual layer for agent-management interfaces because it can run entirely in a single HTML file with no dedicated backend required for the frontend.

A capitalization-weighted index of 30 companies involved in the design, distribution, manufacturing, and sale of semiconductors, maintained by Nasdaq OMX. It is the primary benchmark for the sector's stock-market performance and serves as a proxy for the health of the global chip industry across economic cycles.

A stock index tracking 30 major U.S.-listed semiconductor companies, maintained by Nasdaq. It is the standard benchmark for the chip sector’s overall performance and is widely referenced by equity analysts and traders as a read on sector sentiment.

Latin for 'perennial philosophy': the idea, associated with Leibniz and popularized in the 20th century by Aldous Huxley and the Traditionalist School, that a single universal truth underlies all major world religions. In its strongest form it claims that surface doctrinal differences are secondary to a shared metaphysical core; in its weakest, it simply notes recurring themes across independent religious developments.

The use of red or near-infrared light (typically 600–1100 nm) to stimulate cellular processes, particularly in mitochondria. Also called red light therapy or low-level laser therapy. Evidence exists for skin, muscle recovery, and some cognitive applications, though protocols are not yet standardized.

Relating to the generation, manipulation, and detection of photons (light particles) in semiconductor devices. Photonic integrated circuits combine lasers, modulators, and photodetectors on a single chip, enabling the compact, power-efficient optical engines used in co-packaged optics and high-speed transceivers.

A semiconductor chip that combines optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors — on a single substrate, analogous to how CMOS integrated circuits combine transistors. PICs allow coherent transceivers to be manufactured at scale and declining cost.

A chip that contains multiple photonic components — waveguides, modulators, splitters, photodetectors — on a single substrate. In optical transceiver design, the PIC handles all light-routing and modulation functions.

The use of light-based components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and optical fibres — to transmit data inside computing facilities. In AI infrastructure, photonics is positioned as a successor to copper-wire interconnects for linking GPUs at high speed and low power, particularly in co-packaged and rack-scale architectures.

An SOI wafer engineered to extreme uniformity (silicon thickness held within roughly one nanometer across the wafer, defect density below 0.1 per square centimeter) so that light can be guided losslessly through patterned silicon waveguides. It is the foundation substrate for silicon photonic integrated circuits.

A 360° photograph mapped onto the inside surface of a virtual sphere, allowing the viewer to look in any direction. Unlike a true 3-D environment, a photosphere has no depth: moving the camera forward or sideways produces no parallax, so the illusion of space collapses quickly under movement.

The process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into sugars and oxygen. It is the primary mechanism by which carbon moves from the atmosphere into the biosphere, making it central to climate regulation and the global carbon cycle.

A term popularized by NVIDIA and others from 2024 onward for AI systems that operate in and reason about the physical, three-dimensional world — robots, autonomous vehicles, embodied agents. It contrasts with AI that processes only text or images, and reflects an investment thesis that the next frontier of AI capability requires rich spatial and sensory understanding of real environments.

A rendering approach where materials and lights obey real-world energy conservation laws — light that bounces off a surface cannot be brighter than what arrived. PBR became the dominant paradigm in game engines and browser 3D libraries in the 2010s because it produces consistent, predictable results under varied lighting.

Animation constrained by physical laws such as gravity, momentum, and center-of-mass balance. Instead of purely interpolating joint angles, physics-based systems model how a body would actually move, reducing the 'floaty' or robotically stiff artifacts common in simpler software.

An open-source, minimal terminal agent framework by Mario Zechner that provides a model-agnostic agent loop, tool execution, and a skills system for loading capabilities as Markdown instruction files. Feynman wraps Pi rather than reimplementing the core agent logic, and its research workflows are Pi skills.

STMicroelectronics' first proprietary silicon photonics process technology, manufactured on 300mm wafers at its Crolles fab in France. It entered high-volume production in March 2026 and supports optical transceiver modules operating at 800 Gbps today, with a roadmap extending to 1.6 Tbps aggregate bandwidth — the scale required by next-generation AI hyperscale datacenters.

The bronze-working technique used by Shang craftsmen, in which a design was first modeled in clay, then used to create a multi-part fired clay mold into which molten bronze was poured. The method permitted intricate surface decoration but constrained certain design features — a fact central to Robert Bagley's formalist argument about the origins of the taotie.

Unreal Engine's approach to browser delivery: the game runs on a remote server and only compressed video frames are sent to the user's browser. This avoids porting the engine to WebGL or WebGPU but requires persistent server infrastructure and introduces latency, making it unsuitable for fast-paced interactive use cases.

PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission organisation coordinating the electricity grid across 13 Mid-Atlantic and Midwest U.S. states plus the District of Columbia — from Virginia and New Jersey through Ohio, Illinois, and beyond. PJM runs both a real-time energy market and a forward capacity market (the RPM auction) that pays generators for committing available megawatts up to three years ahead, providing revenue visibility for generators like Vistra.

A markdown file written to disk at the start of an agentic session, serving as persistent working memory. Because it lives on the filesystem rather than in the conversation, it survives context resets. When a session overflows and a new conversation begins, the agent reads the plan file and resumes from the exact stopping point — making resets a minor inconvenience rather than a project failure.

A Claude Code feature (activated with Shift+Tab twice) that puts the AI into a read-only planning state before it makes any file edits. The developer and model iterate on an approach until the plan is satisfactory, then execution is enabled. It reduces wasted work caused by early incorrect assumptions.

An optical waveguide chip made by depositing silica glass layers on a silicon substrate. Routes and splits light beams passively — without electrical power — and is used in fiber splitters, optical couplers, and the passive sections of co-packaged optical modules. Enablence Technologies is a specialist manufacturer of PLC components.

A linear-motion transmission that converts rotary motor output into linear displacement using threaded rollers arranged around a central screw. Compared with conventional ball screws, roller screws distribute loads across more contact points, survive higher shock loads, and tolerate the heel-strike forces in bipedal walking.

A contested but active research area studying whether plants exhibit behaviors analogous to learning, memory, and decision-making, without neurons or brains. Monica Gagliano's published work demonstrated that the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica can be conditioned to stop closing its leaves in response to a repeated benign stimulus — a process resembling habituation in animals — suggesting that information-processing in plants is more sophisticated than classical biology assumed.

Bypassing a marketplace intermediary to transact directly between buyer and seller. In gig-economy contexts this typically means a driver and passenger completing a trip outside the app — benefiting both economically at the expense of the platform's margin, but at significant contractual and financial risk to the driver.

A hypothesis from MIT researchers (published at ICML 2024) proposing that as neural networks grow more powerful, they converge on similar internal representations of reality — regardless of whether they were trained on text, images, or other modalities. The name invokes Plato’s cave: all models are shadows of the same underlying world-structure. Follow-up experiments in 2026 found that more capable models show stronger cross-model representational alignment.

The Timaeus's mathematical physics: the four classical elements are assigned regular geometric solids — fire gets the tetrahedron, air the octahedron, water the icosahedron, earth the cube. All faces reduce to two types of right triangle; since fire, air, and water share the same base triangle, those three can transform into one another while earth cannot. It is the first mathematical physics in Western thought: matter is geometry all the way down.

An open-source, WebGL-based 3D game engine designed to run in the browser without plugins. It is used for interactive experiences, games, and product visualisations on the web. Its JavaScript runtime and editor are maintained as an open-source project.

Claude Code’s system for distributing third-party extensions. Developers publish a GitHub repository in a specific format; users register it with a slash command and then install individual skills from its catalog.

A file format originally designed for 3D polygon meshes that has become the standard container for raw Gaussian Splat data. A PLY file for a splat scene stores the position, colour, opacity, and shape parameters of every ellipsoid in the scene.

A macOS command-line utility for reading and writing power-management settings, such as sleep timers, display-off delays, and the `disablesleep` flag. It operates at a lower level than `caffeinate` but is also constrained by hardware enforcement on Apple Silicon.

The current skeleton-and-mesh model format used in MikuMikuDance. A PMX file contains the 3D mesh, bone hierarchy, physics rig, and material definitions for an animated character. Community-created PMX models are freely distributed across Niconico and YouTube.

A collection of data points, each defined by X, Y, and Z coordinates, used to represent a three-dimensional object or scene. In AI image tools, a point cloud is typically inferred from a single flat photograph using depth-estimation models rather than measured with physical sensors.

The observable difference in perceived quality between a raw, unedited screen recording and one processed with cinematic effects, motion design, and post-production. In the startup context it specifically describes the impression gap between utilitarian tools like Loom and dedicated demo-video platforms.

A two-axis political classification tool that separates economic views (left vs. right) from social views (authoritarian vs. libertarian). Unlike simple left-right scales, it places entities in one of four quadrants. AI bias researchers have adopted it as a standardized benchmark for comparing model political orientations across studies — the libertarian-left quadrant, where most LLMs cluster, combines market-skeptical economics with socially progressive or permissive values.

A daemon architecture pattern in which a long-running process wakes on a fixed interval (a tick), evaluates system state (the poll), and assigns work to available handlers (the dispatch). Symphony's orchestrator uses this to periodically check Linear for eligible issues and route them to Codex agent workers.

A layer-2 scaling network built on top of Ethereum that processes transactions faster and at lower cost than the Ethereum mainnet. Polymarket uses Polygon to settle trades on-chain while maintaining an off-chain order book for execution speed.

The number of flat triangular or quadrilateral faces that make up a 3D mesh. Higher counts allow finer geometric detail but demand more GPU memory and processing. A 1.5-million-triangle mesh is considered high-resolution; it sits in the range of hero game characters or cinematic props.

Potato-sized mineral concretions that form on the deep ocean floor over millions of years, containing commercially interesting concentrations of nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese — all critical inputs for lithium-ion batteries and electronics. Mining them is technically feasible but faces significant environmental and international regulatory scrutiny; TMC the metals company holds exploration rights to a large nodule field in the Pacific.

Informal term for routine position management — trimming holdings that have grown outsized relative to their original thesis weight, taking profits after extreme runs, or reducing exposure where the risk/reward has shifted. The goal is to prevent any single position from dominating the book in a way the manager did not intend, regardless of conviction.

The fraction of a portfolio's holdings bought or sold over a given period, usually expressed as an annual percentage. High turnover generates more transaction costs. A 28 percent annual turnover means roughly a quarter of the portfolio is replaced each year.

A technique for guiding an AI image-generation model using skeletal or mesh data that specifies where body joints should appear in the output. The pose data is supplied as auxiliary input alongside the text prompt.

A real-time fluid simulation method introduced by Macklin and Müller (2013). Instead of solving Navier-Stokes differential equations directly, it represents the fluid as particles and iteratively adjusts their positions each frame to satisfy a density constraint. The result is stable, controllable, and fast enough for interactive use — properties that make it popular in games and real-time graphics.

A compound that binds to a receptor at a site other than the primary binding site and enhances the receptor's response to its natural ligand. Diazepam is a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors: it does not activate them directly but amplifies GABA's inhibitory effect when GABA is present.
