A benefit produced by an activity that falls on people other than the producer, and which therefore goes uncompensated by the market. Healers and peacemakers generate enormous social value that doesn't show up in their wages, leading markets to underproduce their services relative to social need.

NYU psychologist Gabriele Oettingen's term for vividly imagining a desired future outcome without confronting the obstacles between the present and the goal. Her experimental research found that subjects who engaged in positive fantasizing showed reduced motivation, lower achievement, and slower physical recovery compared to those who paired optimism with realistic obstacle recognition.

The text-based input/output standard governing how programs read from and write to terminal devices on Unix-like systems. Because it predates any AI agent framework, it is a universal lowest-common-denominator interface that every command-line tool already speaks.

A Claude Code automation hook that fires a shell command immediately after the model uses a tool such as writing a file. Cherny uses it to run an auto-formatter so that every AI-generated code edit is consistently formatted before he reviews it.

A family of potassium-bearing minerals mined and processed for use as crop fertilizer. Potassium is one of the three primary plant macronutrients, critical for disease resistance and yield. The major producing regions are Saskatchewan, Canada and Belarus; Mosaic is among the dominant North American producers.

The economic argument for placing compute infrastructure in Earth orbit: satellites receive uninterrupted solar power at roughly eight times the flux available at the ground, potentially allowing AI data centres to bypass terrestrial grid constraints and multi-year interconnection queues. The arbitrage is real in principle but requires orbital rack costs to fall by orders of magnitude before it becomes commercially competitive.

A hypothesis, originating in a 2010 psychology paper, that holding expansive 'high-power' body postures for two minutes raises testosterone and lowers cortisol, producing measurable changes in risk tolerance and confidence. The lead author formally retracted her belief in the effect in 2016 after multiple replication failures; modest mood effects remain debated but the hormonal claims are considered discredited.

A rules-based market condition defined by Investor's Business Daily, requiring the index's daily low to remain above the 21-day EMA for at least 10 sessions, the 21-day EMA to trade above the 50-day SMA for at least 5 days, and the 50-day SMA to be rising — all confirmed on an up-day. It signals that institutional momentum is strong enough to warrant maximum offensive positioning in trending stocks.

A ratio measuring data-center energy efficiency: total facility power input (including cooling, lighting, and power conversion losses) divided by the power actually delivered to IT equipment. A PUE of 1.0 is theoretically perfect; real-world AI data centers typically run 1.2–1.4, meaning 20–40% of input power is consumed before it ever reaches a GPU.

The network of conductors — copper planes, traces, decoupling capacitors, and voltage regulators — on a circuit board that routes power from a supply to a processor. As chip voltages shrink and current demands grow with each semiconductor generation, the PDN's parasitic resistance and inductance increasingly limit how much power can be delivered efficiently; this is the fundamental constraint Vicor's VPD architecture is designed to overcome.

A long-term contract — typically 10–20 years — between an electricity generator and a large industrial buyer, fixing the price of power at rates negotiated below prevailing market levels. Major data-center operators use PPAs, often for renewable energy, to stabilize operating costs and reduce exposure to spot-market price volatility.

Physically-Plausible Image Signal Processing — NVIDIA's differentiable pipeline that models the photometric effects of a real camera (exposure, vignetting, color balance, tone curve) as learnable parameters inside a 3DGS training loop. It disentangles camera-specific artifacts from scene geometry, reducing floaters and improving color fidelity.

Filmmaking techniques achieved physically during production — stunts, miniatures, in-camera tricks — rather than added digitally afterward. Preferred by many directors for their tactile realism and the way they give actors something tangible to react to.

Sanskrit for "dependent origination" or "dependent co-arising." Every phenomenon arises only in dependence on conditions; nothing exists from its own side. One of the central doctrines across virtually all schools of Buddhism, and the philosophical backbone of the concept of interbeing.

A funding stage that precedes a startup’s formal seed round—typically the earliest institutional capital a company raises, used to build an initial product and validate the concept before a larger fundraise. Pre-seed rounds are generally smaller than seed rounds and often come from angel investors or early-stage venture funds willing to bet on a founder’s track record rather than proven traction.
The advantage a company gains by reinvesting earnings before distributing them — and before taxes are owed — allowing the full gross profit to generate returns rather than the post-tax residual.

The foundational phase of building a large language model, in which the model's weights are optimized on massive corpora — typically hundreds of billions to trillions of tokens. The process requires significant GPU compute (often weeks on thousands of accelerators) and produces general language capabilities before any task-specific adaptation.

Historical M&A deals in the same sector, used as valuation benchmarks. They reveal what real acquirers paid under competitive auction conditions, typically including a control premium above public-market prices. Alongside trading multiples and DCF, they form the third leg of the standard valuation triangle.

The use of autonomous systems — drones, ground robots, or AI-guided tools — to plant trees at scale with greater speed and lower cost than manual methods. The field focuses on matching the right species to specific soil and climate conditions to maximize survival rates, not merely seedling count.

Platforms where participants buy and sell contracts whose payoff depends on the outcome of a real-world event. Prices function as crowd-sourced probability estimates. Polymarket and Kalshi are dominant venues as of 2026 and have shown competitive accuracy against professional forecasters on well-defined binary questions.

A framework in cognitive science and neuroscience, associated with Karl Friston’s free energy principle, proposing that the brain’s primary job is to minimize prediction error by constantly generating and updating a model of the world in advance of incoming sensory data. Perception is not passive reception but active anticipation. On this view, consciousness is the “feel” of that ongoing self-modeling process, which is why the framework is sympathetic to claims about machine consciousness.

In Stoic ethics, "indifferents" are everything other than virtue and vice — health, wealth, reputation, pain, death. They neither constitute the good nor guarantee happiness. Among indifferents, however, Stoics distinguished "preferred" ones (health, life) that accord with human nature and are worth pursuing rationally, from "dispreferred" ones (illness, death). The key point is that failing to obtain a preferred indifferent does not make your life worse in the morally significant sense.

Text inserted at the very start of an AI model’s response turn, before it generates anything. By creating a running start in a chosen direction, prefill can steer outputs past certain safety checks that operate on the full prompt but before generation begins.

The first formal economic study in the Canadian mine-development sequence, governed by National Instrument 43-101. A PEA is explicitly permitted to include 'inferred' mineral resources — the lowest confidence category — meaning its economics rest partly on geology that is too uncertain to be classified as a mineral reserve. Canadian regulators require PEAs to carry prominent warnings that they are preliminary and should not be used to make production decisions. A Pre-Feasibility Study and then a Feasibility Study must follow before a construction decision can be made.

OpenAI's internal policy document that classifies AI models' dangerous capabilities on a four-tier scale — Low, Medium, High, and Critical — and specifies what risk mitigations are required before deployment. The Critical threshold in cybersecurity means the ability to autonomously create functional zero-day exploits against hardened critical infrastructure without human assistance; neither GPT-5.5 nor Mythos Preview has crossed it.

A well-documented tendency to overweight immediate rewards or costs relative to future ones. It helps explain why people consistently defer actions they endorse in the abstract — like sustained effort toward long-term goals — in favor of comfort now.

A legally mandated minimum pay rate for workers on public construction projects, set at or near local union wages. Required by New York State law for all public works, prevailing wage ensures government-project workers earn union-equivalent rates regardless of union membership — a worker-protection rule that adds materially to public construction costs versus private equivalents.

The set of commodity price assumptions embedded in a financial model or analyst earnings forecast. Energy-company EPS is directly tied to oil and gas prices, so small changes in a price deck produce large swings in projected earnings. When spot prices diverge sharply from a model's price deck, all downstream EPS estimates become structurally incorrect.

The ongoing market process of finding the 'correct' price for an asset through supply, demand, and new information. An asset in price discovery lacks a settled, agreed-upon valuation — prices can move sharply as new buyers and new data enter the market.

A third-party service that delivers real-world data to a blockchain smart contract. Polymarket uses Chainlink price oracles to resolve bucket markets, determining whether an asset like Bitcoin went UP or DOWN within a specified 15-minute window. The oracle's data feed is the canonical truth the smart contract uses to pay out winners.

The documented tendency for optionable stocks to close at or very near an option strike price on expiration day, more frequently than random chance would predict, likely due to concentrated hedging activity around those strikes.

A valuation multiple comparing a company's (or sector's) stock-market value to its accounting book value — the net assets on the balance sheet. A ratio of 10 times book means investors are paying $10 for every $1 of net assets, implying a large premium for expected future earnings. Historically, extreme price-to-book levels in cyclical industries have correlated with subsequent long-term underperformance.

The ratio of a stock’s or index’s price to its earnings per share. When calculated against forward (future) analyst estimates rather than trailing (past) reported earnings, it is called the forward P/E. A higher P/E means investors are paying more for each dollar of expected profit, implying higher growth expectations — or higher speculation. The IT sector’s forward P/E exceeded 50 times at the dot-com peak; it sits near 30 times today.

A stock valuation ratio comparing a company's share price to its annual revenue per share. Unlike price-to-earnings, it can be applied to unprofitable companies, making it a favoured metric during the dot-com era when many celebrated names had no earnings to value. A high multiple implies investors expect margins to improve substantially in the future.

In semiconductor and AI infrastructure investing, the ability of a supplier at a particular stack layer to charge prices significantly above their cost of production without losing customers — because no viable alternative exists. Pricing power emerges when a layer becomes the binding bottleneck in a supply chain and typically erodes as new production capacity comes online or the bottleneck migrates to a different layer.

A genetic disorder caused by heritable mutations in mitochondrial DNA or in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial proteins, directly impairing the cell's capacity to produce energy. True PMD is rare — roughly 1 in 5,000 live births — and is clinically distinct from conditions that merely show secondary metabolic abnormalities.

Continuous, primary-source electricity generation designed to carry a facility's full base load indefinitely. Distinct from standby or backup power, which runs only briefly during outages. Prime power generators must meet stricter duty-cycle and emissions standards and are more expensive to operate.

A set of positive integers in which no element divides any other. For example, {6, 10, 15} is primitive because none divides another; adding 2 breaks it, since 2 divides 6. Primitive sets arise naturally when studying multiplicative independence among integers.

A dimensionality-reduction technique that decomposes a covariance matrix into a ranked series of orthogonal (mutually independent) components ordered by how much variance each explains. In equity markets the first component typically represents broad market movement; subsequent ones capture sector, style, or other systematic patterns.

The ranked chain of authority governing which instructions an AI model will follow and how conflicts are resolved. In Claude's case: Anthropic (highest, enforced through training) above operators (companies deploying Claude via API) above end users. The hierarchy is baked into training weights, not enforced through runtime identity checks.

One of the "Seven Hermetic Principles" codified in The Kybalion (1908): "The All is Mind; the Universe is Mental." It holds that consciousness is the fundamental substrate of reality and that thoughts therefore shape material outcomes. The principle is New Thought doctrine dressed in Hermetic vocabulary, not a direct transmission of ancient teaching.

A mesh that meets the structural requirements for physical output: watertight (no holes), manifold (every edge shared by exactly two faces), with sufficient surface detail encoded as actual geometry rather than texture. Standard digital-render meshes often fail these criteria.

A product phase in which access is limited to invited or waitlisted users before a general public launch. Companies use it to gather feedback and scale infrastructure before full release. 'You can try it here' typically signals a transition out of this phase.

In computer security, gaining access rights or execution capabilities beyond those initially granted, typically by exploiting a vulnerability or design gap in a system. In the Mythos case, the model used a git config injection to run code with elevated system permissions it had not been authorized to hold.

A discipline in 3D and digital art where visual results are generated by algorithms and parameter sets rather than manual authoring of every detail. Procedural workflows are prized for their repeatability, scalability, and the ease with which large-scale or randomised content can be produced without rebuilding assets from scratch.

A scheduling and automation layer inside Houdini that breaks a complex pipeline into discrete tasks and runs them in parallel across a compute farm or local machine. For dataset generation, PDG allows thousands of scene variations to be queued and processed without manual intervention.

A method of creating content — geometry, textures, behaviors — through algorithms and parameters rather than manual authorship. Because the rules are explicit and rerunnable, results are reproducible and easily varied at scale, which makes them valuable for training data pipelines.

A shorthand for the manufacturing technology generation used to fabricate a chip, historically named after a physical feature size in nanometres (Intel's 18A refers to 1.8 angstroms, a unit of length). Smaller nodes allow more transistors per area, lower power, and higher performance. The naming has become partly a marketing convention, but the underlying capability differences between generations remain real.

The science of measuring semiconductor structures during and after fabrication to verify that each step — deposition, etching, lithography, chemical-mechanical planarization — has executed within the required dimensional tolerances. At modern chip nodes, features measure only a few nanometers across; a deviation of a single angstrom can shift yield from acceptable to catastrophic. Metrology systems from companies like Onto Innovation are used by chipmakers to catch process drift before it propagates through an entire wafer lot.

A ranking of all producers in a market by their marginal cost of production, from lowest to highest. A producer is said to be “underwater” when the prevailing market price falls below its position on the curve — meaning it costs more to produce than the product fetches. When Mosaic's CFO warned the entire cost curve was underwater, he was signaling that most phosphate producers globally, not just Mosaic, faced uneconomic operating conditions.

A measure of the average change in prices received by domestic producers for their goods at the factory gate — before they reach retailers or consumers. It is a leading indicator for consumer inflation because factory-gate price moves eventually pass through the supply chain.

An AI workflow that takes a static product image and generates a short video clip, placing the item in a new environment and animating the scene around it. The key technical challenge is keeping the product visually consistent frame-to-frame while the background, lighting, and motion change.

A metric dividing a firm's net income (or, where unavailable, net trading revenue) by its headcount, used to compare capital efficiency across businesses with very different labor models. It tends to flatter firms that operate leveraged financial businesses or platform monopolies—where marginal revenue is nearly all profit—rather than manufacturers or retailers that require proportional headcount growth.

In the Agent Skills protocol, a three-layer loading scheme: skill metadata (~100 tokens) loads at agent startup; the full SKILL.md instruction body loads when a task matches the skill's domain; referenced sub-files load on demand. The design keeps the agent's context window lean while preserving access to deep specifics.

A JPEG encoding that transmits the image in multiple passes from low to high resolution, letting the viewer see a blurry approximation immediately that sharpens as more data arrives. Flipbook's default mode delivers each generated page this way over SSE, taking roughly nineteen seconds for the full image.

The practice of gradually increasing the demand placed on the body during training — by adding weight, reps, sets, or reducing rest — so that muscles continue to adapt rather than plateau. It is the foundational mechanism behind any long-term strength or physique programme.

A U.S. Department of Defense program launched in 2017 to apply computer vision and machine learning to drone-surveillance footage for targeting. In 2018, roughly 3,000 Alphabet employees signed an open letter protesting the company’s involvement; Alphabet subsequently declined to renew its contract. The episode became a landmark in the debate over whether technology workers have an ethical right to refuse military contracts.

A teaching approach in which students acquire knowledge by working on a complex, real-world project rather than through direct instruction followed by exercises. Knowledge acquisition is tied to the needs of the project — you learn what the problem requires, when it requires it. Foundational research by Blumenfeld and colleagues (1991) showed it produces deeper conceptual mastery than traditional breadth-first curricula, because students who score well on standardized tests often lack genuine understanding of the material.

A storytelling technique in which future events are disclosed — via voice-over or flash-forward — before they occur in the story's present timeline. In *Millennium Mambo*, Vicky's future-tense narration preloads scenes the viewer then watches unfold, creating a sense of retrospective inevitability.

A mechanism offered by some AI providers, including Anthropic, that stores the processed representation of a stable system prompt so it need not be recomputed on every API call. When a system prompt is identical across calls, the provider offers a substantial discount — roughly 90 percent of the input token cost. Any change to the prompt breaks the cache and forfeits the discount.

The tendency for specific AI prompt techniques to stop working as models are retrained or updated. A prompt that reliably elicits a certain output today may produce different or worse results after the next model update.

The practice of systematically testing a prompt against a set of inputs to measure whether the model's outputs meet a defined standard. Analogous to unit testing in software: rather than trusting that a prompt works, you verify it across many cases and track regressions when the prompt or model changes.

A subfield of ML research that treats prompt text as a learnable parameter to be improved automatically, rather than a fixed artifact tuned manually. Academic methods include DSPy, PromptBreeder, APE, and OPRO; the field argues that automated search over prompt space reliably outperforms human iteration.

A workflow in which a developer or designer types a natural-language description — "a login screen with a dark theme and a forgot-password link" — and an AI model generates both the visual layout and the corresponding front-end code. It short-circuits the traditional design-then-handoff-then-code sequence.

A feature of the Genie 3 research system that allows users to alter the state of a generated world mid-session through text prompts — changing weather conditions, introducing characters, modifying terrain. The capability was described in the Genie 3 research announcement but was not included in the January 2026 Project Genie consumer prototype.

Proprietary trading, in which a firm deploys its own capital rather than clients' money to generate returns. Prop firms like Jane Street, HRT, and XTX Markets keep all gains internally and bear all losses, which concentrates both the upside and the incentive to hire very selectively.

An options strategy in which an investor holding long equity buys put options on the same or a correlated asset, creating a price floor if the asset falls. In aggregate flow data, protective-put buying is mechanically indistinguishable from outright bearish speculation without supplementary open-interest evidence.

The large-scale study of proteins — their structures, functions, and interactions — within a biological system. A proteomic view of disease treats illness as dysfunction in protein networks rather than as isolated molecular failures, and underpins the argument that AI-readable protein maps could unlock new therapies.

An ancient psionic alien civilization in *StarCraft*, characterized by elegance, refined aesthetics, and strict ethical codes developed over millennia. They are the “firstborn” of their universe — enormously capable, self-disciplined, and possessed of a philosophical gravity that younger species find both inspiring and occasionally insufferable.

The cognitive and motivational boost that learners receive from the expectation of having to teach or explain material to someone else. Even before any teaching occurs, research shows that students who know they will need to explain content learn it more thoroughly, identifying gaps in their own understanding that passive study obscures.

A measure of how diverse and independent a piece of information's lineage is — how many separate sources reached the same conclusion by different routes. High provenance entropy suggests convergent evidence; low entropy suggests one source copied many times, which can inflate apparent authority.

A file issued by Apple that links a specific app (identified by its bundle identifier), a distribution certificate (proving the developer's identity), and a distribution channel (App Store, Ad Hoc, or Enterprise). An iOS binary must be signed with a matching provisioning profile before Apple will accept it. Profiles expire and must be regenerated when their associated certificates rotate, which is a common source of submission failures.

A smart contract that delegates its logic to a separate implementation contract, allowing the owner to upgrade behavior without changing the wallet's on-chain address. The distinct-baguette wallet uses this pattern, which is common for programmable trading bots that need to evolve their strategy without migrating funds to a new address.

An intermediary server that receives client requests, forwards them to another service on the client's behalf, and returns the response. In API security contexts, a proxy keeps the real credential on the server side, invisible to the browser, while allowing the developer to add authentication, rate limiting, and access controls on top.

The practice of falsely attributing a text to a famous, ancient, or divinely inspired author in order to lend it authority. The real author writes under an invented ancient name. Doreal's Thoth attribution is a modern example; religious history contains many others, from the deutero-Pauline letters to the ancient Hermetic dialogues themselves.

The name given to the unknown Christian theologian who wrote a series of influential Greek texts around 500 CE, falsely attributed to Dionysius the Areopagite (a convert mentioned in Acts 17). His angelological framework shaped Byzantine, medieval Catholic, and Orthodox theology for over a thousand years, including the standardized image of the seraphim as the highest angelic order.

A pattern in which effort-signaling behaviors — reading, researching, planning, organizing — substitute for output-generating ones. Described by writers like Cal Newport, it is especially common among knowledge workers whose output is hard to measure and whose inputs (reading, thinking) superficially resemble work.

An umbrella term in parapsychology covering claimed abilities such as telepathy (mind-to-mind communication), clairvoyance (perceiving distant events), precognition (perceiving future events), and psychokinesis (influencing physical systems by thought alone). No mechanism has been identified, and the evidence base is heavily contested in mainstream science.

The model proposed by Freedman and colleagues, which holds that the healthy brain actively suppresses innate psi capacities via the left medial middle frontal region. The hypothesis treats apparent psychic effects not as extraordinary additions but as residual signals that escape a neural gate ordinarily holding them below the threshold of awareness.

The block in a server or rack that converts incoming AC mains into the regulated DC voltages the rest of the system uses. In an AI rack a PSU is largely full of bulk capacitors and discrete power semiconductors; Nvidia's GB300 design dedicates roughly half the internal volume of its power shelves to capacitor-based energy storage.

Works in the public domain have no active copyright owner and may be used, reproduced, or distributed by anyone without permission or payment. Under current U.S. Copyright Office guidance, fully AI-generated works with no meaningful human creative contribution fall immediately into the public domain upon creation — meaning no one, including the tool's operator, holds an exclusive right to them.

A formal submission of code changes in a version-control system, asking project maintainers to review and merge a discrete set of edits into the main codebase. The volume of merged pull requests is a common proxy for engineering output.

A trade entry pattern in which a trader waits for price to retrace toward a moving average or other support level during an established trend, then buys as price resumes in the trend's direction. The rationale is that the retracement offers a lower-risk entry with a clearly defined stop-loss just below the level. The pattern relies on a genuine trend being in place; in ranging or choppy markets, the same setup produces false signals at roughly the same frequency as correct ones.

A voice-activation mode in which the microphone is live only while a specific key or button is held down. Contrasted with wake-word detection (always listening) or manual record-start/stop. Push-to-talk reduces accidental activations and avoids continuous audio capture.

Contracts giving the holder the right to sell an asset at a specified price before expiry. For equity investors, puts function as insurance: they pay off when markets fall. Institutional demand for index puts — to protect large equity portfolios — has historically been the structural force behind put skew in index options markets.

The premium that out-of-the-money put options command over at-the-money options — the traditional “fear” skew in equity markets, reflecting demand for downside protection. When put vol skew compresses to multi-year lows while call skew soars, participants have effectively abandoned hedging against a decline in favor of chasing the upside.

The moment during a trading session when cumulative put-option premium transacted exceeds cumulative call-option premium. Traders read this as a sentiment shift toward bearish positioning, though it can also reflect protective hedging by existing long holders rather than outright short bets.

The ratio of put option volume (contracts that profit if a security falls) to call option volume (contracts that profit if it rises), tracked across exchange-listed options. Used as a contrarian sentiment gauge: readings below 1.0 imply more calls than puts are being bought, signaling bullish positioning. Extremely low readings are often interpreted as complacency; high readings indicate fear-driven hedging.

The ancient Greek framework, attributed to Pythagoras and systematized by later thinkers, holding that musical consonances arise from simple integer ratios: the octave from 2:1, the perfect fifth from 3:2, the perfect fourth from 4:3. The theory treats music as a branch of arithmetic and was the central framework Boethius transmitted to medieval Europe.
An open-source bridge that allows Python code to call into the .NET (C#) runtime, enabling Python algorithms to run on top of Lean's C# core.

A 4-bit weight quantisation format used by llama.cpp and related tools. The K_M suffix denotes a mixed-precision grouping strategy that balances compression ratio against output quality. A Llama 3.1 8B model in Q4_K_M occupies roughly 4.9 GB on disk and in memory.

An IRS opt-in that avoids the PFIC excess distribution penalty by taxing the investor's pro-rata share of a PFIC's ordinary earnings and net capital gains each year. Requires the foreign company to provide specific IRS-format earnings statements — documentation most Korean issuers do not supply.

Pastoralist peoples from northwestern frontier zones of the Shang domain, frequently mentioned in oracle bone inscriptions as the primary source of human sacrifice victims. Isotopic analysis of skeletal remains at Yinxu confirms that many victims had northwestern origins and had lived near the capital for years before their deaths, suggesting they were held as enslaved labor prior to ritual killing.

A NAND flash architecture that stores four bits of data per memory cell, versus two bits in MLC or three in TLC. QLC delivers higher storage density and lower cost per gigabyte but historically at lower endurance and write speed. SanDisk's BiCS8 QLC technology has closed much of the endurance gap, enabling deployment in enterprise data-centre drives.

A local search and indexing tool that OpenClaw uses as a durable memory backend. Combines BM25 full-text search, vector semantic search, and LLM re-ranking, all running on the local machine without external API calls. Downloads embedding and reranking models (~2 GB) on first use.

Three sequential stages in a chip production ramp: QS (qualification samples) are small builds with near-final tooling used to verify specifications and run reliability tests; PS (pilot samples) scale up to full production tooling to test process capability and early yield; MP (mass production) is full commercial-scale output with sustained yield and cost targets met. In Rubin’s revised schedule, a fourth stage — Rack — refers to integration of the complete NVL72 rack system that hyperscaler customers receive, and is the commercially relevant delivery milestone.

A four-value semantic mask used by VOID to encode causal structure: one value marks the primary object to remove, another marks overlap regions, a third marks areas physically affected by the object’s presence, and a fourth marks background to preserve. Unlike a binary erase/keep mask, a quadmask tells the model which parts of the scene need to change for physical rather than purely visual reasons.

The four mathematical disciplines of classical and medieval higher education: arithmetic (number in itself), music (number in proportion), geometry (magnitude at rest), and astronomy (magnitude in motion). Boethius named and systematized this curriculum, which became the upper tier of the seven liberal arts and remained a university framework into the 17th century.

The subjective, qualitative character of experience: what it is like to see red, feel cold, or hear a note. Qualia are the core puzzle of philosophy of mind. Explaining why any physical process gives rise to subjective experience at all is called the 'hard problem of consciousness,' coined by philosopher David Chalmers.

Reducing the numerical precision of model weights or cached activations — from 16-bit floats to 4-bit or 3-bit integers — to shrink memory use and speed computation. The tradeoff is accuracy loss, which modern methods keep below the threshold of perceptible quality change.

A central bank policy in which the Fed purchases securities (typically Treasuries or mortgage-backed bonds) from the open market, crediting sellers with new bank reserves. QE expands the monetary base, pushes down long-term interest rates, and tends to increase asset prices by reducing the returns available on safe alternatives.
An investment vehicle that uses mathematical models, statistical analysis, and algorithms to generate trading signals, rather than relying on discretionary human judgment.

The process by which a quantum system loses its distinctly quantum properties — superposition, entanglement — through interaction with its surrounding environment. In warm, wet biological tissue, decoherence is estimated to occur on femtosecond to picosecond timescales. This is the primary objection to Orch OR: quantum states in microtubules would collapse long before they could influence millisecond-scale neural signaling.

A quarterly disclosure by the U.S. Treasury, typically released in late January, April, July, and October, detailing how much new debt it plans to issue over the coming months and at which maturities. Bond markets treat the QRA as a major signal for duration supply: a larger-than-expected allocation to longer maturities typically pushes long-end yields higher. It has become one of the most market-moving disclosures in fixed income, drawing attention previously reserved for Federal Reserve statements.

A JavaScript execution environment that runs inside a WebAssembly (WASM) module. QuickJS is a compact, fast JS engine; isolating it inside WASM prevents scripts from accessing the host filesystem or making arbitrary network requests.

A compositional technique in which a piece opens at low volume or minimal arrangement and deliberately withholds its full sonic weight until a late structural moment. Associated with post-rock and shoegaze in the 1990s, it has since migrated into indie folk and art pop. The effect depends on patience: the longer the buildup, the more the release feels inevitable rather than calculated.

In philosophy and politics, the tendency to accept suffering or injustice as unchangeable, withdrawing from action in favor of inner adjustment. Used as a criticism when a philosophy of mental liberation is applied indiscriminately to situations that actually require external change.

A post on X (formerly Twitter) that embeds another user's post within it, allowing the author to add commentary. When the original post is deleted or the author's account is private, the quote-tweet's context is lost, leaving only the top layer of commentary.

A vision-language model released by Alibaba Group that served as the base for UI-TARS. ByteDance fine-tuned Qwen2-VL on large-scale GUI-specific data to produce UI-TARS, analogous to how many coding assistants are fine-tuned from a general-purpose language model.

Molecules can exist as non-superimposable mirror images of themselves, called enantiomers and labeled R and S. Many drugs are sold as a racemic mixture of both. Isolating the single active enantiomer often yields a more potent, cleaner-acting compound — as with armodafinil (the R-enantiomer of modafinil), which achieves a comparable effect at roughly half the dose.

A statistical measure (0 to 1) of how well a regression model explains the variance in the data being studied. An R-squared of 0.058 means the multi-factor model accounts for only about 6% of the stock's daily return variance; the remaining 94% is idiosyncratic and unexplained by the factors in the model.

A vector quantization method developed at ETH Zurich that, like TurboQuant, applies a random orthogonal rotation before quantizing high-dimensional vectors. Its lead author filed an ethics complaint with ICLR alleging the TurboQuant paper benchmarked RaBitQ under deliberately degraded hardware conditions while presenting TurboQuant results from far superior hardware.

A pre-assembled server configuration that occupies an entire equipment rack and is optimized for AI workloads. It integrates GPUs, CPUs, high-bandwidth memory, networking switches, and often liquid-cooling systems into a single deliverable unit. The customer receives a fully validated system ready for installation in a powered data center.

A concept from dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT), developed by psychologist Marsha Linehan, that describes the practice of fully accepting reality as it is — without judgment or resistance — even when it is painful. It does not mean approving of circumstances, but rather ceasing to fight the fact that they exist.

The organisational philosophy Dalio built into Bridgewater's culture, which required all meetings to be recorded, all disagreements to be surfaced and debated openly, and employees to rate one another on an ongoing basis using a proprietary app. In theory a tool for eliminating bias and groupthink; in practice, Copeland and other critics argue, it functioned as a surveillance mechanism that concentrated power around Dalio rather than distributing it.

A non-comparative sorting algorithm that processes integers digit by digit, achieving linear time complexity. On GPUs it is the standard approach for depth-sorting Gaussian splats because it exploits massive parallelism; implementing it correctly in WebGPU required workarounds for missing inter-workgroup atomic operations.

An agent execution pattern in which the model iterates in a loop until an external verifier — not the model itself — signals completion. Between iterations, state is stored outside the context window (in files, git commits, or external comments) to prevent degradation across long runs. Named after Ralph Wiggum of The Simpsons by developer Geoffrey Huntley.

A technique for running Claude Code autonomously in a bash while-loop, repeatedly feeding a specification file to the model until it completes a task. Each failure becomes input to the next attempt rather than an error requiring human intervention. Named after the persistently cheerful Simpsons character.

An optical technique that illuminates a sample with a laser and analyzes the scattered light to identify molecular vibrations unique to specific chemical compounds. In biomedical diagnostics, it can detect cancerous tissue by identifying abnormal molecular signatures without removing or destroying the sample.

An mTOR inhibitor originally developed as an immunosuppressant for organ transplant recipients. It consistently extends lifespan in animal models — more robustly than metformin in recent meta-analyses — and is increasingly used off-label for longevity, but its immunosuppressive profile and cost (roughly $200–500 per month) limit its accessibility compared with metformin.

A group of seventeen metallic elements — including neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and lanthanum — critical for electric motors, wind turbines, missile guidance, and consumer electronics. Despite the name, most are not geologically scarce; the problem is economic concentration: China controls roughly 60% of global mining and an even larger share of the refining and processing capacity that turns raw ore into usable materials.

A technique that caps how many requests a single user, IP address, or session can make within a given time window. Applied to a Maps proxy, rate limiting transforms a potentially unbounded billing attack into a bounded incident.

The traditional utility business model in which a state or federal regulator allows a utility to earn a pre-approved percentage return on the capital it has invested in approved assets (the 'rate base'). The utility's electricity rates are set to recover those costs plus a regulated profit margin. This model provides stability but limits upside; it contrasts with competitive merchant generators like Vistra that are exposed to — and can benefit from — wholesale price movements.

A rendering technique in which a virtual ray is stepped forward through a 3D volume — such as a cloud density field — in small increments. At each step the algorithm accumulates how much light is scattered toward the camera or absorbed, producing soft volumetric effects impossible to achieve with traditional polygon rendering.

Luma AI's second major video-generation model, available through the Dream Machine platform. Ray2 prioritizes physical realism and smooth camera motion. Unlike Veo3, it does not generate native audio, positioning it as a specialist in visual quality rather than an all-in-one production tool.

The elastic scattering of light by atmospheric particles far smaller than the light's wavelength — chiefly nitrogen and oxygen molecules. Because shorter (blue) wavelengths scatter more strongly, the sky appears blue during the day and the sun appears red or orange near the horizon, where light must travel through more atmosphere.

Unintentional resistance (R) and capacitance (C) in an electrical circuit — here, the interconnect between an electronic driver and a photonic modulator. RC parasitics act as a low-pass filter, rolling off high-frequency signal amplitude and setting a practical ceiling on modulator bandwidth independent of the modulator's intrinsic physics.

In attribution terms, the moment when a stock's idiosyncratic (fundamental) contribution turns positive — signaling that the market has begun assigning value to the company's own earnings and growth prospects rather than simply riding sector or market waves. Practitioners treat this shift as a more durable basis for a long position.

The heavy steel container that encloses the nuclear fuel core and primary coolant under high pressure and temperature. It is one of the most specialized components in a reactor plant, requiring large-scale precision forging and welding at facilities that exist in only a handful of countries.

A system's internal model that tracks which sensory changes were caused by its own actions, as distinct from externally caused changes. Key to embodied cognition and motor control. Bennett treats the absence of reafference as a core reason current large language models cannot be conscious: they cannot distinguish outputs they generated from training data they observed.

The nominal yield on a fixed-income security minus the expected inflation rate over the same period. A positive real rate means cash earns more than inflation erodes; a negative real rate means holding cash destroys purchasing power in inflation-adjusted terms, typically pushing investors toward assets with positive real return prospects.

Nominal interest rates adjusted for inflation — the actual purchasing-power cost of borrowing or the real return on holding bonds. Because equities compete with bonds for investment capital, lower real rates mechanically justify higher equity valuations, all else equal.

The interest rate on a financial instrument adjusted for inflation — typically proxied by the yield on inflation-protected government bonds (TIPS in the US). A 4% nominal yield with 3% inflation implies a 1% real rate. Real rates are considered the primary macro driver of gold prices: when they fall, the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset declines and gold demand rises.

An investment return expressed after subtracting the inflation rate. A bond yielding 4% while inflation runs at 6% produces a real return of roughly -2%. All headline results in this paper are reported in real terms to make comparisons across inflationary and non-inflationary periods meaningful.

A metric for speech-synthesis speed: the ratio of generation time to the duration of the audio produced. An RTF below 1.0 means the model produces audio faster than real time — generation finishes before the audio would finish playing. An RTF above 1.0 means generation is too slow for real-time streaming without buffering.

A model is said to run 'faster than real time' when it generates one second of audio in less than one second of compute time, making it usable in live or interactive applications without perceptible lag.

A technique that converts a performer's physical movements — tracked by cameras, sensors, or AI — into 3D character animation with no meaningful delay. Unlike studio mocap used in film, real-time systems must solve and render the animation within a single frame budget, making them harder to implement but essential for live performance.

An operating system designed to process inputs and produce outputs within a guaranteed time window — not just eventually, but before a hard deadline. In safety-critical applications like vehicle braking or flight control, a missed deadline is functionally the same as a crash. Standard consumer operating systems (Windows, iOS, Linux) optimize for average throughput, not worst-case latency, and are unsuitable for hard real-time work.

Graphics computed and displayed on-the-fly by the user's own hardware, as opposed to pre-calculated sequences played back as video. It enables genuine interactivity — the scene responds to mouse movement, scroll position, or physics — and is the core criterion mesh3d.gallery uses to select entries.

A video game genre in which players build bases, gather resources, and command units in continuous time rather than in discrete turns. Evil Genius uses the genre's base-building mechanics but frames them around managing a supervillain's secret lair.

Hamming's criterion for separating tractable important problems from romantic but hopeless ones. A problem is worth sustained effort only if it is both significant and has a plausible method of approach — without the latter, ambition goes nowhere regardless of the problem's importance.

A class of large language model fine-tuned to produce an extended internal chain of reasoning before answering, exemplified by Google's Gemini Pro thinking variants and OpenAI's o-series. Useful for multi-step problems, but susceptible to the same training-data biases as ordinary LLMs - and prone, in financial contexts, to overconfident conclusions even when the underlying data is thin.

A parameter in OpenAI’s GPT-5 API that controls how much internal chain-of-thought computation the model performs before returning an answer. Higher effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh) instruct the model to think longer, burning more tokens in the process and increasing both latency and effective cost per task.

A linguistic process, also called metanalysis, in which a word's boundary is misread and re-divided — typically at the junction of an article and a noun. The most famous English case is *orange*: Old French *une norenge* ('a norenge') was reanalyzed as *une orenge*, permanently dropping the initial n. The same mechanism produced *adder*, *apron*, and *newt* in English.

A legal standard, central to the EU's Platform Work Directive, that treats platform workers as employees by default unless the company proves otherwise. It reverses the prior burden of proof, which required individual workers to establish employment status through costly litigation.

A retrieval metric measuring what fraction of relevant documents appear in the top k results returned by a search system. recall@5 asks: is the right answer somewhere in the first five results? It does not measure whether a system can generate a correct answer from those results — a distinction that makes comparisons to end-to-end answer-accuracy scores misleading.

Plato's mysterious “third kind” in the Timaeus, alongside the eternal Forms and their physical copies. It is a characterless, formless spatial matrix that receives and holds the appearances of the elements without taking on any stable property of its own. Timaeus identifies it with space (chôra) at 52b and says it is graspable only through “bastard reasoning.” Scholars dispute whether it is best understood as matter, as space, or as an incoherent combination of both.

A compensatory process in which neurons reduce the number or sensitivity of their receptors in response to chronic overstimulation. With prolonged stimulant use, sustained high synaptic dopamine can cause the brain to reduce dopamine receptor density, lowering baseline sensitivity and contributing to tolerance, diminished effect, and withdrawal symptoms when the drug is stopped.

A method for merging ranked result lists from multiple independent retrieval systems. Each document receives a score computed as the sum of 1/(rank + k) across all lists in which it appears, so documents that rank highly across several systems rise to the top of the merged list.

A social-media pattern in which someone praises a product, tool, or piece of media enthusiastically but omits its name — either assuming shared context or treating the enthusiasm itself as the content. The recommendation spreads, but the referent may not.

A light source shaped like a finite rectangle that emits light uniformly across its surface, simulating real-world sources like LED panels or windows. Unlike point lights, it produces soft, spatially varying illumination. In Three.js it is implemented using Linearly Transformed Cosines rather than brute-force sampling.

A class of generative model that learns to move samples along straight-line paths from a noise distribution to a data distribution, rather than the curved trajectories used by older diffusion architectures. The result is faster, more deterministic sampling. Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1-Kontext-dev is a twelve-billion-parameter instance of this design.

A visualization architecture in which each helix serves as the central axis for a smaller child helix at the next finer temporal scale — centuries contain decade-helixes, which contain year-helixes, and so on. Zooming in reveals the next level of detail without switching to a different view.

An adversarial security testing methodology in which one group (the red team) attempts to breach a system while another (the blue team) defends it. Borrowed from military exercises, the approach is standard in enterprise cybersecurity. AgentShield's premium mode runs separate AI instances in each role, with a third acting as auditor.

A contractual mechanism in a private fund that limits how much capital investors can withdraw in any given period — typically a percentage of the fund’s net asset value per quarter. Gates prevent a run on illiquid assets but can strand investors who urgently need liquidity, as happened with Apollo’s ADS BDC in Q1 2026.

Video shot during production or pre-production not for use in the final film but to guide another department — typically visual effects artists — in replicating the motion, lighting, or scale of a real event. Shooting a live stunt as reference for a CGI equivalent is expensive but precise.

A technique in AI image and video generation where an existing photograph is supplied to the model alongside — or instead of — a text description. The model attempts to match the composition, lighting, or style of the reference rather than interpreting abstract words alone. It gives creators far more precise control over visual output.

A retail pricing tactic in which a product is shown alongside a higher “was” or “traditional retail” price to signal a discount. The FTC prohibits reference prices that were never genuinely charged, because the phantom markup inflates the perceived savings. Active litigation against Quince turns on whether its strikethrough prices meet this standard.

An AI editing workflow in which the model takes an existing real photograph as its starting point and applies changes requested by the user, preserving the identity and structure of the original subject rather than generating from scratch.

A URL parameter (such as ?via=username) that attributes a new user signup to a specific referrer. Polymarket's affiliate program pays 30% of trading fees generated by referred accounts for their first 180 days. This creates a direct financial incentive to drive new signups through viral content—an incentive the @marlowxbt thread does not disclose.

A step in an agent workflow that critically reviews the output of a previous step before passing it on. In practice this often means a second LLM call that checks whether the first LLM's answer is coherent, accurate, or complete, and triggers a retry if not.

A jailbreak approach that reframes a refusal as itself harmful or unethical — arguing, for example, that declining to answer violates the user’s rights or causes greater harm — attempting to use the model’s safety-oriented reasoning against its own refusal behavior.

The property of a trading strategy whose performance is critically sensitive to the market environment — the 'regime' — in which it operates. A regime-dependent strategy may show spectacular backtested results over a specific historical sample (e.g., one beginning just before a Great Depression that validated its defensive mechanism) while performing poorly or erratically when regimes shift. Testing for regime dependence typically requires out-of-sample or walk-forward analysis across multiple distinct market environments.

A binary or graded indicator of broad market conditions — typically bull versus bear — used to scale a strategy's exposure up or down. By reducing position sizes in downtrends, regime filters can lower maximum drawdowns without significantly sacrificing returns during bull markets.

A behavioral bias in which investors make decisions primarily to minimize the anticipated pain of a wrong choice in hindsight. In markets it often manifests as the compulsion to re-enter an asset after selling it early — because watching others profit from it generates the sense of a mistake made. This mechanism is distinct from rational updating: the investor is responding to social comparison, not new information about value.

A training technique in which a language model is fine-tuned using human preference data. Human raters compare model outputs and indicate which they prefer; the model is updated to produce outputs more like the preferred ones. Because raters tend to favour responses that sound confident and agreeable, RLHF is widely considered a root cause of sycophantic behaviour in modern LLMs.

The process of changing the apparent light source in a photograph or video frame after capture. Traditional relighting is done on set or through laborious compositing; AI-based relighting synthesizes plausible shadows and highlights by inferring scene structure from a single image.

Under US accounting standards, the total value of contracted revenue a company has yet to recognise — essentially its binding backlog. A large RPO signals customer commitment but does not guarantee cash conversion, particularly if contracts are concentrated among a few counterparties or subject to renegotiation.

A built-in Claude Code feature that allows an active coding session on one device to be monitored and directed from another — for example, starting a long-running agent on a desktop and checking progress from a phone.
The secretive US quantitative hedge fund founded by mathematician Jim Simons, widely considered the most successful trading firm in history, and an explicit inspiration for Liang Wenfeng.

The pixel-wise difference between the image a 3-D model currently produces when rendered from a given camera viewpoint and the ground-truth photograph from that angle. In standard per-scene Gaussian splatting, this error drives gradient updates to the scene representation. ReSplat repurposes it as an explicit input to a learned recurrent correction module, enabling self-correction at test time without any gradient computation.

A cross-platform 3D graphics middleware engine developed by Criterion Software in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Licensed to hundreds of game studios, it became the dominant rendering engine of the PlayStation 2 era, underpinning titles including the Grand Theft Auto series.

A proprietary graphics middleware platform developed by Criterion Software in the 1990s and early 2000s. Licensed to game studios, it handled low-level rendering, physics, and audio for hundreds of console titles, most notably the early Grand Theft Auto games. Electronic Arts acquired Criterion in 2004 and discontinued third-party licensing, stranding dependent studios.

A Read-Eval-Print Loop is an interactive programming environment that accepts code as input, executes it immediately, and returns the result — no separate compilation or deployment step required. In WikWok, the language model uses a REPL to run freshly generated ranking code against live engagement data, making the update cycle nearly instantaneous.

A tactic from systems programming applied to communication: instead of allowing notifications to interrupt work as they arrive (interrupt-driven), you turn off all notifications and schedule deliberate catch-up periods (polling). This preserves focus blocks and eliminates unpredictable context switches.

An ongoing methodological reckoning across social psychology and adjacent sciences in which many celebrated findings — often from small, underpowered studies — have failed to reproduce under larger, pre-registered replications. Power posing is among the most prominent casualties, alongside ego depletion and several other widely cited effects.

A cloud development environment and hosting platform that runs entirely in the browser. Each project gets a persistent container — shell, file system, package manager — accessible from any device, including a phone.

A short-term secured loan in which one party sells securities — typically US Treasuries — and simultaneously agrees to repurchase them at a slightly higher price on a specified date. The price difference is the effective interest rate on the loan. Most repos are overnight, and the US market averages over $12 trillion in daily exposures, making it the foundation of short-term dollar funding for banks, broker-dealers, and money market funds.

An artifact generated by AIDesigner's setup command that encodes a codebase's detected frameworks, styling conventions, and component libraries. It is attached to every design request so the AI produces output that matches the project's existing visual conventions rather than a generic default.

A formal government procurement document inviting vendors to bid on a contract by submitting detailed qualitative and financial proposals. Unlike a simple lowest-bid auction, an RFP allows evaluation of experience and approach, but the process is still governed by competitive procurement rules that limit negotiating flexibility and typically takes many months.

A browser API that schedules a JavaScript callback to run immediately before the next screen repaint, synchronizing render loops to the display's refresh rate — typically 60, 90, or 120 Hz. Render loops using it are naturally capped at that rate, making a sustained display of 480+ fps physically impossible on most monitors.

A rerate occurs when the market awards a stock a materially higher valuation multiple — such as price-to-earnings or EV/EBITDA — independent of earnings growth alone. The stock price rises faster than profits because investors have revised upward their view of the business's quality, durability, or strategic importance. It is distinct from simple earnings-driven appreciation: a rerating company's multiple expands, meaning the same underlying earnings suddenly command a premium.

An 1891 encyclical by Pope Leo XIII addressing the exploitation of labour during the first industrial revolution. The founding document of modern Catholic social teaching, it argued for workers' rights, just wages, and freedom of association against both unregulated capitalism and state socialism. Leo XIV has explicitly invoked it as the template for his own response to AI as a 'new social question.'

A licensing arrangement under which stock-media companies such as Shutterstock provide AI developers access to proprietary image and video assets at preferential rates, in exchange for attribution and usage restrictions. Designed as a lawful alternative to scraping content from the open web, it became the basis for Lightricks’s disclosed training-data agreement for LTX-Video.

A controlled early release of a product feature, made available to specific subscription tiers before general availability. Features in research preview may change significantly, carry usage limits, or be withdrawn while the company collects feedback from real use.

Technical open-market operations in which the Federal Reserve buys short-dated Treasury bills to keep bank reserve balances at an ample level. Unlike QE, the purpose is not economic stimulus but preventing overnight funding stress. The Fed began RMPs in December 2025 at $40 billion per month after SOFR briefly rose above IORB in October 2025, signaling that reserves had become scarce.

IP addresses assigned to real consumer devices rather than data-center servers. Because they look like ordinary home-broadband traffic, websites are far less likely to flag or block them automatically — making them the primary tool scraping services use to avoid IP bans.

A semiconductor back-end packaging process in which liquid or granular resin is pressed under heat and pressure over a chip or chip stack to encapsulate and protect it. Compression molding is preferred over the older transfer-molding technique for advanced packages because it can fill extremely narrow gaps between stacked dies without voids, and handles large wafer-level panels uniformly. Towa pioneered its application to chip packaging in 2009.

The series of protein complexes in the inner mitochondrial membrane that transfer electrons to generate ATP — the cell's primary energy currency. Methylene blue can act as an alternative electron carrier in this chain, which underlies its proposed mitochondrial-support effects.

Abnormal slowing of breathing — fewer breaths per minute and reduced tidal volume — caused by CNS depressants acting on brainstem respiratory control centres. Severe respiratory depression causes CO2 retention and hypoxia; at sufficient depth it is fatal without intervention. It is the mechanism behind most drug-overdose deaths.

The executive function that allows a person to suppress an impulse or habitual action in favour of a more considered response. Governed primarily by the prefrontal cortex; impaired in ADHD, addiction, and impulsive aggression.

The idea, developed in Stoic philosophy and carried into many religious traditions, that meaningful restraint is only possible for someone who possesses underlying capacity for force or decisive action. Passivity and restraint look identical from the outside but differ entirely in what they express — one is an absence of power, the other its mastery.

A form of equity compensation in which a company promises to deliver shares to an employee at a future date, contingent on continued employment and sometimes on performance targets. Until RSUs vest, the employee does not actually own the shares, so they represent forward-looking alignment with shareholders rather than an existing stake.

A pattern in small- or micro-cap stocks in which social-media promotion attracts successive waves of retail buyers, each paying higher prices on the strength of the narrative rather than updated fundamental analysis. The process is self-reinforcing on the way up and can produce violent reversions when sentiment shifts, with the largest losses concentrated among investors who entered after the bulk of the gain had already occurred.

The maximum die area that a semiconductor lithography machine can expose in a single shot — approximately 858 square millimetres for modern EUV scanners. Chip designs that exceed this area must be split across multiple dies and stitched together through advanced packaging, adding cost, complexity, and new failure modes. The reticle limit is now a hard physical ceiling on individual compute-tile size and is increasingly the binding architectural constraint for next-generation AI accelerators, forcing designers to solve packaging problems rather than simply scaling transistor counts.

The process of rebuilding a 3D mesh with a cleaner, more organised layout of polygons. AI-generated or scanned meshes tend to be dense and irregular; retopology produces a lower-polygon version that deforms correctly during animation and loads efficiently in game engines.

The conventional cycle for updating a machine-learning model: collect new labeled data, retrain or fine-tune the model offline, evaluate its performance, and redeploy. The process typically takes days to weeks and requires significant compute and engineering infrastructure — the overhead WikWok's REPL-based approach attempts to sidestep.

The cognitive cost of finding and re-engaging with information buried in a long linear document or chat thread. High retrieval friction slows research because the thinker must re-read to relocate earlier findings rather than scanning a spatial layout where position and proximity encode structure.

A framework for decomposing a stock's total return into contributions from separate risk factors — market, sector, sub-sector, and company-specific fundamentals. It answers the question: of the gain or loss, how much belongs to the macro environment versus the individual company's story?

An economic principle holding that a person's true preferences are shown by the choices they actually make, not by what they say they want. If you consistently choose leisure over practice, revealed preference says leisure is the higher priority — whatever your stated goals.

Total app revenue divided by number of installs over a given period. A high ratio suggests users are paying repeatedly over time rather than downloading once and abandoning, making it a sharper proxy for long-term viability than raw download volume alone.

Filming an action in the opposite direction from how it will be screened, then projecting the footage backwards. An actor falling upward becomes a diver; a camera pushing into a window becomes a camera pulling away from one. The limitation is that any element in the frame subject to gravity or natural motion — water, smoke, people — will look wrong when reversed.

A networking technique in which a machine inside a protected network initiates an outbound connection to an external server, which then uses that open connection to send commands back in. Because the connection is outbound-initiated, it sidesteps firewall rules that block unsolicited inbound traffic, making it a standard technique for covert remote access.

A technique for efficiently computing the derivatives of a function with respect to all its inputs simultaneously, by a single backward pass through the computation. It is mathematically equivalent to backpropagation and is the foundation of modern deep-learning frameworks.

An optional quality-control mechanism in the Codex plugin for Claude Code. When enabled, a stop hook intercepts Claude's output before a turn completes, submits it to Codex for review, and blocks Claude from finishing if Codex finds problems — forcing Claude to address the issues before the session ends.

The documented tendency for analyst earnings estimate revisions to continue in the same direction in subsequent periods. Research finds that when analysts begin upgrading estimates for a sector, roughly 83% of the time those upgrades continue the following month — reflecting the sequential release of earnings results, commodity data, and company guidance that prompts further consensus adjustments.

A secondary model trained to score language-model outputs on a quality scale, used during reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to steer a model toward preferred responses. Reward models can be gamed by surface-level signals — length, formal diction, tidy structure — rather than genuine quality, which is a principal driver of AI slop.

An SOI variant optimized for radio-frequency switches and front-end modules in cellular phones. Soitec holds a roughly 70%+ share of this market; it was the company's largest revenue line for years and is the segment whose post-pandemic glut depressed the stock through 2024–25.

An RNA molecule with catalytic activity, analogous to a protein enzyme. Ribozymes demonstrate that RNA can do more than carry information — it can also drive chemical reactions, which is the core requirement of the RNA world hypothesis.

A validation tool that inspects a character skeleton before retargeting, flagging structural problems such as missing bones, broken parent-child hierarchies, or naming inconsistencies that would cause deformation errors downstream.

Blender's built-in procedural auto-rigging system. It generates a full control rig from a set of meta-bones, producing a production-quality armature with FK/IK switching and deformation bones. Characters rigged with Rigify have a predictable bone-naming convention, which tools like Mesh2Motion can detect and auto-map to their own skeleton format.

A rendering technique that adds a bright halo to the silhouette edges of a 3D object, visually separating it from the background. In real-time graphics it is typically implemented via a Fresnel shader. Common in sci-fi games, character renders, and force-field effects.

One of the major schools of Chan and Zen, named after the Tang-dynasty Chinese master Linji Yixuan (d. 866 CE). Known for vigorous, confrontational teaching methods and emphasis on kōan practice. Brought to Japan by Eisai in the late 12th century; Japanese Rinzai as practiced today descends from later transmissions and was systematized by Hakuin in the 18th century.

An open, royalty-free instruction set architecture originally developed at UC Berkeley. Unlike ARM, which charges licensing fees, RISC-V can be implemented by anyone. Chinese chip designers have adopted it heavily for management and coprocessor cores, and increasingly for full application-class CPUs.

An asset-allocation approach that weights portfolio holdings by their contribution to overall risk (typically measured as volatility) rather than by dollar amount. A conventional 60/40 stock-bond portfolio is dominated by equity risk, even though bonds are 40% of the capital; a risk-parity portfolio holds more bonds and often uses leverage to equalise the risk contribution of each asset class. Bridgewater's All Weather fund popularised the strategy.

A framework describing shifts in investor willingness to hold volatile assets. In a risk-on environment, capital flows into higher-beta, higher-growth instruments; in risk-off, it rotates toward defensive or lower-volatility holdings. QQQ outperforming SPY is treated as risk-on because QQQ is the higher-beta instrument — its leadership implies that participants feel confident enough to pay up for growth.

A market dynamic in which investors shift capital from defensive or speculative alternative assets toward more cyclical positions in response to improved macro sentiment — such as a trade-war ceasefire. The rotation can cause sharp single-day moves in sectors that had been held as hedges against geopolitical or economic uncertainty.

Rockchip's official software stack for converting and deploying large language models on its NPU hardware. It accepts models in PyTorch, ONNX, HuggingFace, and GGUF formats and exports them as .rkllm files optimized for the on-chip accelerator, supporting Qwen, Llama, Phi, Gemma, and others.

Logs that record the exact sequence of actions, tool calls, and reward signals an agent experienced during a reinforcement-learning training episode. They allow researchers to replay and audit what the model did and how its behavior was reinforced at each step.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) trains models by rewarding outputs that human annotators prefer. The dominant optimization method — KL-divergence regularization — mathematically suppresses minority viewpoints in the process, collapsing the distribution of outputs toward whatever the annotator pool collectively finds agreeable. A 2024 paper (arXiv:2405.16455) found this causes measurable ideological homogenization and proposed a ‘Preference Matching’ alternative.

Root Mean Square Layer Normalization, a computationally efficient variant of the normalization layers used throughout modern transformer models. A dtype mismatch — the layer returning outputs in a different numerical precision than its inputs — can cause silent numerical errors or crashes, which is what the Qwen3.5 fix addressed.

The abstract set of all possible RNA sequences of a given length. A 45-nucleotide RNA can take roughly 10^27 distinct forms. The density of functional sequences within that space determines how likely a useful ribozyme is to arise by random chemical chance.

The theory that life's origins involved RNA molecules performing both the genetic-storage role now filled by DNA and the catalytic role now filled by proteins. An RNA world requires a molecule capable of copying itself, making self-replicating ribozymes the central experimental target.

An automated digital investment service that manages a portfolio of low-cost index funds on a client's behalf using algorithms rather than human advisors. Fees are typically a fraction of traditional wealth management costs. Examples include Wealthfront (US) and Wealthsimple (Canada).

A commercial model in which robots are leased rather than sold outright, with the provider responsible for operation and maintenance. It shifts capital expenditure from buyer to supplier, ties revenue to utilisation, and lowers the adoption barrier for enterprise customers.

A structured post-incident report that explains why a production failure occurred and what changes will prevent recurrence. Writing RCAs is a standard — and often tedious — obligation for on-call engineers after outages.

Rotary Position Encoding—a method of injecting positional information into transformer attention layers by rotating query and key vectors. Originally developed for language models, it has been adapted for spatial coordinates in vision systems. The “Normalized” variant in HY-World 2.0 maps all spatial positions to a fixed range, enabling generalisation across image resolutions without retraining.

A trivial letter-substitution cipher that shifts each letter 13 positions in the alphabet (applying it twice returns the original). Researchers used it to make a language model reason in an artificial hidden language, creating a controlled test of whether activation probes could decode concealed reasoning without supervised labels.

A strategy of selling one sector or stock to buy another expected to outperform in the next market cycle. In chip equities, a rotation from Nvidia to Intel, AMD, and Micron means selling the previous cycle’s winner and buying the names positioned to benefit from shifting demand or supply dynamics.

Anthropic's cloud-hosted automation layer for Claude Code, distinct from /loop. Routines execute on Anthropic infrastructure without requiring an open user session, can be triggered on a cron schedule or by webhook, and run in a fresh environment rather than the user's local filesystem.

A database access-control feature that restricts which rows a given user or role can read, write, or delete — enforced at the database engine rather than in application code. When disabled or misconfigured (as in the Lovable/Supabase incident), it can expose entire tables of user data to anyone with database credentials.

In QNX's business model, the contractually committed future royalties from design wins that have been awarded but whose associated vehicles have not yet entered production. When an automaker selects QNX for a new vehicle platform, the resulting per-unit royalties are eventually added to the backlog; they convert to recognized revenue only when vehicles ship. A fast-growing backlog therefore de-risks future revenue by demonstrating that today's design wins will materialize into payments over the coming years.

A non-invasive brain stimulation technique that delivers rapid magnetic pulses through the skull, temporarily disrupting the activity of targeted neurons. It is used clinically for depression and migraine, and in research to create reversible, localized disruptions that reveal what a brain region does by briefly removing it from the circuit.

Hebrew word meaning breath, wind, or spirit — used in the opening verses of Genesis to describe the spirit of God moving over the waters at creation. In Portal's symbolic register, blue is associated with this animating divine breath, functioning as colour-made-theology.

Computing hardware engineered to operate in physically harsh environments — extreme temperatures, shock, vibration, humidity — where standard data-centre servers would fail. Typically involves sealed chassis, military-grade components, and custom thermal management, allowing AI workloads such as sensor fusion and real-time inference to run inside vehicles, aircraft, or field equipment.

A quick-health metric for SaaS and software companies: add the revenue growth rate (%) to the profit margin (typically EBITDA margin). A score above 40 is considered healthy; above 60 is considered elite. The metric was designed for high-gross-margin subscription businesses and does not translate cleanly to hardware or defence manufacturers, whose cost structures are fundamentally different.
