A benchmark for software companies: revenue-growth rate (%) plus operating-margin (%) should sum to at least 40. Scores above 40 indicate a healthy balance of growth and profitability; Palantir's Q1 2026 score of 145 was exceptional.

A stricter tier introduced by Palantir in its Q1 2026 earnings slides, identifying large-cap companies whose Rule of 40 composite score exceeds 80. The Q1 2026 list: Nvidia 122%, Palantir 94%, Eli Lilly 89%, TSMC 88%, Visa 83%.

A scholar who specializes in runic inscriptions — their linguistic content, historical dating, regional forms, and archaeological context. Runologists have been the primary academic voice in debunking the Kensington Runestone, citing linguistic anachronisms and irregular rune forms that no genuine medieval inscription shares.

A GPU cloud marketplace offering per-second billing across 30-plus global regions, with SSH access to persistent virtual machines. Priced significantly below major cloud providers (roughly $0.39–$2.99 per hour depending on hardware), it is commonly used for machine-learning training and inference workloads. Feynman uses RunPod for stateful experiment-replication workloads that require persistent storage.

The share of the S&P 500’s total market capitalization held by its largest components. Because the S&P 500 is market-cap weighted, a small number of very large companies can dominate the index — amplifying gains when those companies rise and amplifying losses when they fall. Concentration is a common proxy measure of bubble risk.

A scattering (S) parameter that measures how much signal power travels from port 1 (the electrical input) to port 2 (the optical output). In EO modulator characterization, the S21 curve plotted versus frequency shows how efficiently high-frequency electrical signals are converted into optical modulation; the 3 dB point is where that efficiency drops by half, defining the modulator's usable bandwidth.

Software-as-a-Service: a software delivery model in which an application is hosted centrally and accessed over the internet via subscription, rather than installed locally. The term is used here as shorthand for a category of commercially polished web product with recognizable UI conventions — hero sections, pricing grids, feature-card layouts.

A stochastic-volatility model (Stochastic Alpha Beta Rho) introduced by Hagan et al. in 2002 and widely used to fit the implied-volatility smile in interest-rate and equity-options markets. Its key parameters — α (initial vol), ν (vol-of-vol), and ρ (price-vol correlation) — map directly onto the coordinates of Dean's information-geometric phase plane.

A tradition of esoteric thought that attributes spiritual or cosmic significance to specific geometric shapes, ratios (such as the golden ratio), and numbers. Practitioners argue that these patterns underlie the structure of the universe and appear in ancient architecture, nature, and music. The field is not recognized as a scholarly discipline; its methods involve selective pattern-matching rather than rigorous mathematical or empirical analysis.

The visual imagery used in religious traditions to represent the divine — figures, symbols, geometric forms, and narrative scenes. Scholars study these images both as historical artifacts and as carriers of theological meaning, and compare them across traditions to find recurring structures.

LinkedIn's premium sales intelligence product, owned by Microsoft, that layers prospecting and relationship-mapping features on top of the standard LinkedIn platform. It includes native buyer-intent signals inferred from platform activity and is the dominant terms-of-service-compliant option for intent-based prospecting on LinkedIn.

Segment Anything Model 2, developed by Meta. A computer vision model that identifies and tracks arbitrary objects across video frames without needing object-specific training. VOID uses SAM2 as the first step in its automated mask-generation pipeline, isolating the object targeted for removal before passing that segmentation to a language model for causal reasoning.

A loose literary tradition set in medical retreats or convalescent institutions, where enforced withdrawal from society creates conditions for intense philosophical reflection. The enclosed, time-dilated world of the sanatorium became a powerful metaphor for the dislocations of early 20th-century European culture, and Mann's Davos setting is its defining example.

An isolated compute environment — typically a container or virtual machine — where untrusted code can run without affecting the host system. In AI agent contexts, it prevents an autonomous agent from accidentally or maliciously modifying files or systems outside its designated workspace.

A Bronze Age archaeological site and culture in Sichuan province, China, dating to roughly 1700–1100 BC. It is notable for its otherworldly bronze masks, giant bronze trees, and jade artifacts, which differ markedly from other contemporary Chinese civilizations and have no clear parallel in the Chinese historical record.

The Hebrew word שָׂרָף (*saraph*, plural *seraphim*), derived from a root meaning "to burn." It appears seven times in the Hebrew Bible: six times referring unambiguously to fiery or venomous serpents, and once — in Isaiah 6 — describing celestial throne-attendants. The shared etymology and lexical overlap are the foundation of the serpent-seraph identification.

Age-related progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength. It is a recognised risk factor for falls, disability, and mortality in older adults, and defined the patient population in the MET-PREVENT trial, which tested metformin specifically in sarcopenic or pre-frail individuals aged 65 and older.

The cocktail of inflammatory cytokines, growth factors, and proteases secreted by senescent cells — cells that have permanently stopped dividing but remain metabolically active. SASP signals inflame neighbouring tissue and are a key driver of inflammaging. Drugs that eliminate senescent cells are called senolytics; drugs that suppress SASP without killing the cells are called senomorphics.

On platforms like TikTok and Instagram, saving a post requires deliberate action and implies the user intends to return — a higher-intent signal than a view or like. Marketers increasingly treat saves as a proxy for purchase consideration, particularly for products that require some research before buying.

New York Labor Law §240, which holds property owners and general contractors absolutely liable for gravity-related injuries on construction sites. No other US state applies this absolute standard; even a partially negligent worker can recover full damages. The result is dramatically higher insurance premiums — driving project insurance costs from roughly 4 percent of total value in 2010 to over 12 percent today.

An imaging technique that maps surfaces at atomic resolution by measuring the quantum-mechanical tunneling current between a sharp metal tip and the surface as the tip is scanned across it. STM was developed in the early 1980s by Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer, earning them the Physics Nobel in 1986. In *Ultimate Computing*, Hameroff foresaw STM as a tool for studying living biomolecules at the nanoscale.

A failure mode in long-form AI video generation where subtle inconsistencies — changes in a subject's appearance, shifts in background detail, gradual loss of stylistic coherence — accumulate across segments over time. It is the primary practical limit on so-called 'infinite-length' video generation.

A category under the US Controlled Substances Act for drugs with accepted medical use but recognized potential for dependence and abuse. Schedule IV includes benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium), certain sleep aids, and modafinil and armodafinil. They may not be legally obtained without a prescription and are subject to DEA oversight on manufacturing, distribution, and prescribing.

A visual style drawn from engineering and technical illustration: precise line work, annotated geometry, cross-section diagrams, and blueprint-like composition. In AI-generated imagery, it refers to outputs resembling technical drawings or industrial schematics rather than photographs or painted art.

A set of electromagnetic resonance frequencies in the cavity between Earth's surface and the ionosphere, generated by global lightning activity. The fundamental frequency is approximately 7.83 Hz. Some proponents of alternative tuning theories claim 432 Hz resonates with this value, but the arithmetic required to connect 7.83 Hz to 432 Hz involves several arbitrary steps and works equally well with other frequencies, including the standard 440 Hz.

In Lehmann's autoresearch adaptation, the human-supplied set of three to six yes/no questions that define what a good skill output looks like. It replaces val_bpb as the evaluation signal: each output is scored by counting how many binary criteria it passes, yielding a comparable keep/revert decision.

A third-party API service that provides programmatic access to content from Reddit, TikTok, Instagram, and other social platforms that restrict direct scraping. One API key covers multiple platforms simultaneously.

A real-time rendering technique that approximates reflections by ray-marching within the 2D pixel buffer of the current frame, rather than re-rendering the scene from a reflected camera. Cheaper than true reflections and convincing for water surfaces, but limited to objects currently visible on-screen — off-screen objects cannot be reflected.

Apple's framework, introduced in macOS 12.3 and substantially expanded in 14.x, for capturing screen content with system-enforced user-permission prompts. It is faster and more privacy-aware than older approaches and supports capturing individual windows, specific displays, or particular applications.

A subtype of recurrent depression linked to reduced daylight in autumn and winter, affecting an estimated 1–3% of adults in temperate climates. Morning light therapy is a first-line treatment with efficacy broadly comparable to antidepressants for mild-to-moderate presentations.

An annual report that U.S.-listed companies must file with the Securities and Exchange Commission, containing audited financial statements, business descriptions, risk factors, and competitive landscape disclosures.

A disclosure form filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission within two business days whenever a corporate insider — officer, director, or 10-percent-plus shareholder — buys or sells shares of their own company. Form 4 filings are public, machine-readable, and aggregated by services such as OpenInsider and QuiverQuant into screeners that traders use to track coordinated insider activity.

A zoom parameter in the prototype UI — seconds per screen pixel — that controls how much time each pixel of the helix represents. Reducing it zooms in to show finer time resolution; increasing it zooms out to encompass longer spans.

Reasoning about the downstream effects of effects — not just "what happens next?" but "and then what?" Most people stop at first-order consequences; second-order thinking is what separates decisions that look good immediately from those that hold up over time.

Abnormal mitochondrial biomarkers — elevated lactate, altered mtDNA copy number, reduced ATP — that arise as a downstream consequence of another primary disease process rather than from a genetic defect in the mitochondria themselves. SMD does not constitute a mitochondrial disorder in the clinical sense.

A provision of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 that allows the U.S. president to impose tariffs or quotas on imports determined to threaten national security. The Trump administration used it in 2018 to impose broad tariffs on imported steel and aluminum. A 2020 Section 232 action extended the regime to transformer laminations and cores made from electrical steel, closing a loophole that foreign producers had used to avoid the original steel tariffs.

A U.S. customs rule that historically allowed packages valued under $800 to enter the country duty-free. It was a significant cost advantage for direct-from-factory e-commerce brands shipping from overseas. The exemption was eliminated for Chinese-origin goods in May 2025 and for all countries by August 2025, materially raising import costs for brands whose model depended on it.

An exchange-traded fund that holds a basket of stocks within a single industry or theme, spreading single-company risk across many positions while preserving exposure to the sector's overall performance.

The proportion of a stock market index — such as the S&P 500 — represented by companies classified in a given industry sector. A sector weight of 43 percent for technology means 43 cents of every dollar invested in the index goes to technology companies. Weights shift automatically as market capitalizations change.

An accounting identity derived from national income accounts, developed by British economist Wynne Godley. It states that the financial surplus or deficit of the government sector, the domestic private sector, and the foreign (current account) sector must always sum to zero. When the government runs a surplus and the current account is in deficit, the domestic private sector must run a financial deficit — not as a policy choice, but as arithmetical necessity. The framework explains how fiscal stance directly shapes household and corporate financial conditions.

A classified Department of Defense program that funds dedicated, physically isolated semiconductor fabrication capacity within U.S. borders for defense applications. The $3.2 billion contributed to the Intel deal from this program blended defense and commercial objectives in a single transaction, a structural novelty that critics say obscures accountability.

A small initial ad budget — here $15–$20 — used to test whether a new creative has any market signal before committing larger sums. The logic is that cheap, fast failure enables far more experiments per dollar than betting on untested videos at scale.

The informal practice of re-explaining a project's conventions, architecture, and in-progress decisions at the start of a new AI session, because the previous session's context was lost. Developers who work with AI assistants across many sessions treat this as a recurring tax on productivity.

A term from humanistic psychology, associated with Abraham Maslow and Carl Rogers, describing the process of realising one's fullest potential. Rogers distinguished between growth driven by genuine inner needs and growth distorted by the desire for external approval — a distinction the concept of self-creation depends on but rarely makes explicit.

A tendency documented by Xu et al. (ACL 2024) in which language models systematically favour outputs they themselves generated when asked to compare two versions. This creates a circular problem in self-refinement pipelines: the same model generating and judging its own output will evaluate successive revisions as improvements even when quality is unchanged or declining.

Defined and studied empirically by psychologist Kristin Neff, self-compassion involves treating oneself with the same kindness one would extend to a friend facing failure or inadequacy. Research consistently finds it correlates with higher mastery goals, lower fear of failure, and reduced anxiety — and contrary to popular intuition, does not reduce standards or ambition. It provides a more stable motivational foundation than self-esteem because it is not contingent on success.

A major theory of human motivation developed by Richard Deci and Edward Ryan, holding that people are most motivated and perform at the highest quality when three basic psychological needs are satisfied: autonomy (acting from one's own values), competence (feeling effective), and relatedness (feeling connected to others). It is among the most replicated theories in social psychology, validated across hundreds of studies and more than 200,000 participants.

A concept from Albert Bandura's social cognitive theory: a person's belief in their own ability to execute a specific behavior or complete a specific task. Self-efficacy is task- and domain-specific — distinct from general optimism — and consistently predicts effort, persistence, and performance within that domain.

A practice in which an individual guides themselves into a state of heightened mental focus or suggestibility, typically using scripted language, visualization, or breathing. Scientific literature supports its use for sleep quality, pain management, and anxiety reduction, though the mechanisms remain debated.

Daryl Bem's 1967 psychological theory holding that people infer their own attitudes, emotions, and character traits from their observable behavior, exactly as an outside observer would. We are not transparent to ourselves; we read our own character from the outside in. The implication is that acting prosocially does not merely express a caring identity — it produces one.

A cyclical mental pattern in which an emotion triggers self-evaluative thought — criticism, shame, analysis — which intensifies the original emotion, which demands more evaluation. Distinguished from simply having a feeling by the layer of meta-commentary attached to it. Common substrate of rumination, anxiety, and depression.

The central practical method of the Fourth Way: a divided, double attention — simultaneous awareness of the outer world and of the inner observer — that resists the collapse into identification. Each genuine moment of self-remembering is held to be a small but real increment of consciousness, weakening the hold of false personality over time.

Machines or software capable of producing functional copies of themselves without direct human instruction. In Simak's story, Albert the android builds three specialized derivative machines autonomously, triggering an exponential cascade. The concept is central to contemporary discussions of AI capability growth, autonomous robotics manufacturing, and the legal question of who owns or is responsible for machines a machine has made.

A property of objects or processes where a smaller part, when magnified, looks like the whole. Self-similarity is the defining feature of fractals. It can be exact (as in mathematical constructions like the Sierpiński triangle) or statistical (as in natural textures like clouds or tree branching).

In Joscha Bach's account of mind, the brain's running model of itself: a compressed internal representation that tracks the system's own state and goals, enabling flexible goal-directed behavior. Bach argues this self-modeling loop is what gives rise to the experience of being a subject.

A securities analyst employed by a brokerage or investment bank whose research is distributed to institutional clients. Sell-side analysts publish earnings models, price targets, and buy/hold/sell ratings that aggregate into the "consensus" figures quoted by financial data terminals. Their coverage decisions — which companies they follow and how frequently — directly influence capital flows, because fund managers at buy-side firms (asset managers, hedge funds) frequently use sell-side estimates as inputs to their own models.

A formal research note published by an investment bank's equity research department when it begins coverage of a company. Sell-side reports carry price targets, earnings models, and explicit buy/sell/hold ratings; they are produced by registered analysts under strict compliance oversight and distributed to institutional clients. Independent Substack newsletters mimic the analytical format without the regulatory apparatus.

The well-documented tendency for equity analysts at investment banks to publish earnings and margin forecasts that are systematically too high, particularly for periods more than two quarters out. The bias reflects both commercial incentives and the difficulty of accounting for macro shocks not yet visible in the data.

A retrieval method that matches documents to queries by meaning rather than exact keywords. Text is encoded as numerical vectors, and results are ranked by vector similarity — so a query about “dog food” can surface a document mentioning “pet nutrition” without sharing a single word.

A private fund structure — including interval funds and non-traded BDCs — that offers periodic but limited redemption windows, more liquid than a locked closed-end fund but far less so than a mutual fund or ETF. The mismatch between daily NAV pricing and infrequent actual liquidity is the structural tension at the center of this debate.

The recurring boom-and-bust pattern in chip industry revenue, typically spanning four to five years. It is driven by the multi-year lag between demand signals and new fabrication capacity coming online, which produces alternating periods of shortage and glut. Semiconductor stocks tend to lead the revenue cycle by one to two quarters.

A term from contemplative and mindfulness traditions referring to the sharpness or resolution with which a practitioner can observe experience — bodily sensation, emotion, or thought — as it actually arises, rather than through a fog of habitual interpretation. Higher clarity allows finer-grained attention to what is actually happening moment to moment.

A website whose domain name is chosen to rank highly in search results by closely mimicking a well-known product or brand, rather than identifying its own operator. Common in the AI-tools space, where products like ChatGPT carry enormous search traffic.

The Greek translation of the Hebrew scriptures, produced by Jewish scholars in Alexandria between roughly the 3rd and 1st centuries BCE. It is significant for the seraphim question because it translates the serpents in Numbers 21 as *drakones* (dragons/serpents) while leaving the term *seraphim* untranslated in Isaiah 6 — preserving the word's ambiguity in a theologically charged context.

An encoder-decoder architecture introduced by Sutskever, Vinyals, and Le in 2014 that maps an input sequence to an output sequence of potentially different length. It became the foundation for neural machine translation and is the architecture Sutskever proposed — by analogy — for decoding activation sequences into human language.

A mechanism in FLUX.1-Kontext-dev that converts the input (source) image into a sequence of tokens and appends them directly to the output image tokens before the model processes them. This gives the model simultaneous attention over both the source structure and the image being generated at every layer, which is why geographic features — roads, building footprints, coastlines — are preserved even as the visual style is transformed.

Quarter-over-quarter percentage change in revenue, as opposed to year-over-year. Companies emphasize sequential growth when the prior-year quarter is unflattering or when they want investors to focus on trajectory rather than absolute level.

A method of simulating physics constraints — collisions, joints, cloth — by iteratively resolving collision impulses across many small time steps. Common in real-time physics engines; REZE Studio's implementation runs at a fixed 60Hz timestep with up to six substeps per frame.

The highest order in the traditional angelic hierarchy, described in Isaiah 6 as six-winged fiery beings surrounding God's throne. The Hebrew root *saraph* means 'to burn.' They cover their faces with two wings, suggesting even they cannot fully bear the direct divine presence — a detail that undercuts the popular image of angels as comfortable, luminous messengers.

A potentially life-threatening drug reaction caused by excessive serotonin activity, typically from combining two or more serotonin-boosting medications. Symptoms include agitation, rapid heart rate, muscle rigidity, and hyperthermia. Cyproheptadine is used off-label to reverse it by blocking 5-HT2A receptors.

A class of compounds — including DMT and psilocybin — that bind to 5-HT2A receptors densely located in the prefrontal cortex. Activation of these receptors is associated with the profound alterations in perception, self-boundary, and sense of significance characteristic of psychedelic experiences. The mechanism is well-characterized; what, if anything, it tells us about the content of the resulting experiences remains an open question.

A browser protocol that keeps a one-directional connection open from server to client, pushing data as it becomes available without the client needing to poll. Commonly used for streaming text or binary chunks incrementally—in Flipbook's case, progressive JPEG image data as the model refines its output.

In Catholic moral theology, a form of fear that motivates avoidance of sin purely out of dread of punishment, without love. In the context of angelic appearances, it denotes the incapacitating terror that closes a person to divine messages — precisely what the 'fear not' command is meant to dissolve before any communication can occur.

A resource or process that exists only for the duration of a single interactive session. A session-scoped scheduled task stops when the terminal session ends, as opposed to a persistent background service that survives restarts.

An open-source collection of accessible React UI components built on Radix primitives and styled with Tailwind CSS. Unlike a traditional component library installed as a package dependency, its components are copied directly into a project's source tree, giving developers full ownership of the code.

A small program that runs directly on the GPU, executing in parallel across thousands of cores simultaneously. In WebGL, vertex shaders transform 3D geometry into 2D screen positions; fragment shaders calculate the final color of each pixel.

Carl Jung's term for the unconscious repository of disowned, repressed traits, impulses, and tendencies — aspects of the personality condemned by the ego-ideal and pushed out of awareness. Jung held that the shadow does not disappear when repressed but continues to operate autonomously, shaping behavior without the person's knowledge. Integration of the shadow, rather than its conquest or denial, is central to Jungian individuation.

In Jung's model of the psyche, the shadow is the unconscious collection of traits, impulses, and memories a person represses because they conflict with their conscious self-image. It holds both feared and potentially valuable material. Integration — acknowledging rather than suppressing the shadow — is central to psychological health in Jungian thought.

Credit intermediation that occurs outside the traditional regulated banking system — through money-market funds, hedge funds, securities dealers, and structured vehicles. Shadow banks create credit and liquidity but hold no central bank reserves, so their activity is largely invisible in M2 figures.

A form of insider trading in which someone uses material non-public information about one company to trade securities of a related or correlated company — for example, trading a competitor’s options after learning about an acquisition at one’s own employer. Established as legally actionable by the SEC in SEC v. Panuwat, where a jury found the defendant liable in April 2024.

A practice derived from Jungian psychology in which a person deliberately examines the repressed or disowned parts of their personality — often through journaling, therapy, or dream analysis. The goal is to bring unconscious patterns into awareness so they no longer drive behavior invisibly.

A cinematographic term for the effect produced by a wide-aperture (low f-stop) lens, where only a narrow plane of the scene is in focus and objects in front of or behind it blur. In software demos it is simulated in post-production rather than captured in-camera.

A simplified fluid-dynamics model that assumes water depth is much smaller than horizontal scale. Computationally tractable for real-time simulation of waves near shore, but still grounded in a height-field formulation and therefore unable to produce the overhanging geometry of a barrel wave.

A stored snapshot of a mesh's vertex positions in Blender. Artists blend between Shape Keys to animate deformations or, as in this add-on, use a mid-simulation pose as the starting point for a new physics run.

A 2022 taxonomy attributed to roon (@tszzl) distinguishing two cognitive styles: shape rotators (empirical, spatial, intuition-driven thinkers, associated with engineers and mathematicians) and wordcels (linguistic, theoretical thinkers who work through argument and abstraction). The meme spread widely in tech circles and was amplified by Sam Altman, Marc Andreessen, and others.

The reduction in each existing shareholder's proportional ownership — and, all else equal, in earnings per share — that results when a company issues new shares. For cash-burning small-caps that cannot fund operations from revenues, recurring equity raises are a structural feature rather than a one-time event, creating a persistent headwind for long-term holders even as near-term capital injections extend the company's runway.

Originally a biblical password whose correct pronunciation identified members of a tribe. In modern usage, any word, phrase, or cultural reference whose fluent use marks the speaker as an insider to a particular community.

A character encoding for the Japanese writing system common in legacy Windows software. VMD files use Shift-JIS to encode bone names, a format detail that any modern tool must handle explicitly to remain compatible with the existing archive of community-created MMD content.

An inference strategy in which the model processes a sliding temporal window of frames during the denoising pass rather than the entire video at once. Shifting the window forward one frame at a time makes continuous, unbounded video generation tractable while keeping memory and latency bounded.

A Japanese Sōtō Zen practice meaning "just sitting" — objectless, goalless meditation in which the sitting itself is held to be the expression of awakening, not a technique aimed at producing it. Developed philosophically by Dōgen (1200–1253) in Japanese, shikantaza is considered a distinctly Japanese elaboration within the broader Chan tradition rather than a direct Chinese import.

The Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings ratio, developed by Nobel laureate Robert Shiller, which compares current stock prices to inflation-adjusted average earnings over the prior ten years. It smooths out single-year distortions and has historically been associated with below-average long-run returns when elevated to near-record levels.

An apocryphal contrarian sell signal, attributed to Joseph Kennedy Sr. in 1929, holding that when unsophisticated members of the public begin offering stock tips it signals that retail euphoria has fully priced the market and a top is near. Historical record suggests the story originates in Bernard Baruch's 1957 memoirs rather than contemporary sources.

The risk profile of a party — typically a dealer — that has sold options and whose losses accelerate as the market moves against them. A short-gamma dealer must continuously buy into rising markets or sell into falling ones to stay hedged, mechanically amplifying the underlying trend in both directions.

The percentage of a company's tradable shares (the float) that investors have borrowed and sold short, betting the price will fall. Elevated short interest — above roughly 15–20% of float — can amplify upward price moves if positive news forces short-sellers to buy back shares quickly, a dynamic sometimes called a short squeeze.

A strategy in which an investor borrows shares of a security and immediately sells them, hoping to buy them back later at a lower price and pocket the difference. The seller profits if the price falls, but faces theoretically unlimited losses if it rises — making timing and a specific downside catalyst essential, not merely a chart reading.

A self-reinforcing price spike that occurs when heavily shorted shares become scarce: as rising prices force short sellers (who have borrowed shares and bet on a decline) to buy them back, those purchases push prices even higher, triggering further covering.

A pre-production document in filmmaking that enumerates every planned shot: camera angle, movement, focal length, subject position, and duration. Directors hand shot lists to cinematographers as a blueprint for a shooting day. In AI video contexts, the term is borrowed to describe the same level of compositional specificity applied to a text prompt.

A metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor fabricated on silicon carbide. MOSFETs are the dominant switching device in modern power converters; the SiC variant can handle the 1,200V voltage ratings required when a battery bus or data-centre distribution bus operates at 800V. The key figure of merit is RDS(on) — on-state resistance — which determines heat dissipation during conduction.

The polished silicon carbide crystal wafer on which SiC power devices are grown via epitaxy. Producing large-diameter, low-defect-density SiC substrates is the most technically demanding step in the supply chain — defects propagate into the active device layers and reduce yield. This bottleneck gives substrate makers unusual pricing leverage over the downstream chip industry.

The ACM Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques, which organizes the most prestigious annual conference and paper track in computer graphics research. A result published at SIGGRAPH is considered top-tier; the 2023 Gaussian Splatting paper by Kerbl et al. appeared there before being published in ACM Transactions on Graphics.

A Unix signal (number 1) historically sent when a modem connection hung up, and today sent to a shell process when its controlling terminal closes. By default it cascades to all child processes, killing them. tmux intercepts this signal so its managed processes never receive it.

A go-to-market motion in which outreach is triggered by a real-world behavioral event — a job change, a public question, a competitor mention — rather than sent on a static schedule to a cold list. The aim is to reach prospects at moments of genuine relevance, when context makes a reply feel timely rather than intrusive.

A mathematical function that takes any point in space and returns that point's shortest distance to the nearest surface — negative if the point is inside the object, positive if outside, zero if exactly on the surface. By combining simple SDF primitives (spheres, cylinders, toruses) with Boolean operations, arbitrarily complex shapes can be built without any polygon mesh or model file.

A regulatory technique in which a bank shifts the credit risk of a loan portfolio to outside investors — often via credit-linked notes or guarantees — so the loans can be removed from the bank’s risk-weighted-asset calculation, freeing up capital to extend new credit. It allows banks to originate large deals without permanently holding the full exposure.

A free, open-source license for typefaces developed by SIL International. Fonts under the OFL may be used, modified, and redistributed freely — including in commercial products — provided that derivatives carry the same license. Google Fonts uses the OFL for the majority of its catalog, making those typefaces genuinely free to download and use.

A compound semiconductor with a wider energy bandgap than silicon, allowing operation at higher voltages, temperatures, and switching frequencies. In power electronics, SiC MOSFETs handle the switching duties in EV traction inverters and power converters that silicon devices cannot sustain at 800V — an 800V battery bus requires 1,200V-rated switches to safely handle transient overvoltages during switching.

A wide-bandgap semiconductor material that handles higher voltages, higher temperatures, and higher switching frequencies than conventional silicon. Dominant in electric vehicle traction inverters and increasingly used in high-voltage datacenter power supplies, SiC is harder and more expensive to manufacture than silicon, creating meaningful barriers to entry for qualified suppliers.

A campaign, originating on Reddit in early 2021 and revived periodically since, premised on the idea that the global silver market is structurally short — that more paper claims on silver exist than physical metal to back them — and that coordinated buying of physical silver or silver ETFs could force a dramatic short-covering rally. The thesis has repeatedly attracted speculative interest without producing a sustained delivery crisis, though genuine physical tightness in 2025–2026 gave the narrative fresh legs.

A Google DeepMind AI agent designed to follow natural language instructions across a wide variety of 3D environments, including video games and simulated spaces. SIMA takes actions in real time in response to instructions and has been used as a testbed for embodied AI training alongside Genie 3, including in warehouse navigation tasks.

Bennett's term for the dominant machine learning strategy: optimizing for the simplest, most compressed hypothesis. Rooted in Kolmogorov complexity and Bayesian inference, it underlies most regularization techniques. Bennett argues it is the wrong target for genuine generalization and that the free energy principle commits the same error.

A faster, lower-artifact successor to Perlin noise, also developed by Ken Perlin (2001). Uses triangular grid cells instead of square ones, reducing directional artifacts and computational cost — making it preferable for higher-dimensional shader applications.

In Baudrillard's framework, simulacra are copies or representations that have lost their connection to the originals they supposedly represent. At the extreme stage, the simulacrum precedes and determines what counts as 'real,' inverting the normal relationship between model and copy.

A generative AI workflow that takes one static image of a person and produces a video clip in which that figure appears to speak and move. The model infers three-dimensional structure, lighting, and motion from the single frame.

The process of cutting a molded panel or wafer into individual chips using a diamond-blade saw or laser. It is the final step that separates packaged devices from one another. Towa makes automated singulation systems (its FMS Series) capable of cuts as small as 1.0 mm × 1.0 mm.

A class of implicit neural network that uses sin(ω₀ · Wx + b) as its activation function rather than the more common ReLU or sigmoid. Sinusoidal activations allow the network to represent signals with high spatial frequency detail efficiently, and their derivatives are also sinusoidal, making them well-suited to tasks that require smooth, oscillatory functions like surface reconstruction or signal encoding.

The ability to move freely in all six ways a rigid body can move: translate left/right, up/down, forward/back, and rotate yaw/pitch/roll. A 6DoF viewer can physically walk around a captured scene, unlike 3DoF (rotation-only) 360-degree video.

In Buddhist philosophy, the five categories of phenomena whose combination produces the appearance of a self: form (rūpa), sensation (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), mental formations (saṃskāra), and consciousness (vijñāna). No single aggregate is the self; ‘self’ is the label placed on their interaction, not an entity behind them.

Specific anatomical landmarks — joints, fingertips, facial landmarks — that a pose-estimation model predicts from image data. Each key point is expressed as a 3-D coordinate; connecting them produces a skeleton that can drive a character rig.

The process of transferring animation curves — per-frame rotations and positions of each bone — from one skeleton onto a structurally different skeleton. Because different rigs may have different bone names, proportions, or rest positions, a direct copy of the curves usually produces distorted motion; retargeting software applies remapping and scaling to make the result look natural on the target character.

A design approach in which digital interfaces mimic the appearance of real-world physical objects and materials — a notes app styled as lined paper, a calendar with leather stitching. Dominant in Apple's iOS and macOS through 2012; largely displaced by flat design in 2013 and now undergoing a revival in the form of soft 3D illustration styles associated with Airbnb's recent visual identity.

Positions taken on the shape of the implied volatility curve across strike prices. Equity options persistently show higher implied vol on downside puts than upside calls (the “put skew”), driven by demand for crash protection. Skew traders take views on whether this structural premium will widen or narrow.

A self-contained, installable script that extends what the Hermes Agent can do. Skills can be added at runtime; the agent invokes them when relevant tasks arise, and a curator subsystem grades and refines them over time, making the skill library itself a kind of evolving institutional memory.

An emerging ecosystem of third-party Claude Code skills distributed through community aggregator sites and installed via Claude Code's plugin system. It functions as an informal app store for AI workflows, where contributors publish instruction files that others can download and invoke as slash commands.

In Memento-Skills and similar agent frameworks, the component responsible for selecting which skill from the library to apply to a given task. Unlike simpler approaches that retrieve by cosine similarity between embeddings, Memento-Skills trains its router via offline reinforcement learning to predict which skill will actually succeed on execution — a behavior-aligned objective rather than a text-similarity one.

The file at the heart of the Agent Skills standard: a single markdown document with YAML frontmatter declaring name, version, and tags, followed by natural-language instructions for the AI agent. Placed in the right directory, it becomes a slash command the agent can invoke on demand.

Modular capability plugins in the OpenClaw framework. Each skill is a self-contained directory of code and metadata granting the agent access to a specific tool or service — an email inbox, a calendar API, a browser — and can be installed, removed, or shared independently.

Built-in commands in Claude Code invoked with a leading slash (e.g., `/clear`, `/compact`, `/btw`). They control session state, context management, workflow automation, and tool configuration. Claude Code ships with over sixty of them; most users encounter only a handful.

Internet slang, formalized in 2024, for digital content of low quality produced in bulk, usually by AI tools. The term draws a deliberate parallel to spam: just as spam means unwanted bulk email, slop means unwanted bulk AI-generated content thrust on audiences who did not request it. Merriam-Webster named it its 2025 Word of the Year.

In music criticism, a track described as a slow burn takes an unusually long time to develop its emotional or sonic climax, often sustaining a single mood or texture for several minutes before escalating. The term is borrowed from narrative fiction, where it describes a plot that withholds its payoff. In music, the slow burn is often deliberate — the accumulated tension is the point.

A filmmaking style defined by long takes, minimal dialogue, and deliberate pacing that favors atmosphere over narrative incident. Associated with directors such as Hou Hsiao-hsien, Abbas Kiarostami, and Béla Tarr, it asks audiences to inhabit a moment rather than follow a plot.

A movable barrier set into a dam or channel to control the volume and direction of water flow. In the Aztec dike network, sluice gates regulated salinity levels and water distribution between lake zones and the chinampa irrigation canals, allowing operators to fine-tune freshwater access across thousands of hectares.

A network interface card equipped with an FPGA (field-programmable gate array) or a dedicated processor that handles packet processing, encryption, and traffic steering independently of the host CPU. Smart NICs accelerate data handling at the network edge of AI data centres and are increasingly used to offload the overhead of distributed inference workloads.

Fluence Energy's next-generation storage platform, unveiled in early 2025. It uses a split architecture — a Smart Skid base housing controls, cooling, and power hardware, with separate battery pods that sit on top — and claims energy density above 500 MWh per acre, roughly 30% higher than conventional AC-coupled storage solutions. Its first commercial deployment reached substantial completion in Q2 FY2026.

A statistical body model developed at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems that represents human body shape and pose as a compact set of numerical parameters. It is widely used in computer vision and animation pipelines that need a realistic, controllable 3D human body without hand-crafted rigs.

A nuclear fission reactor with an electrical output typically below 300 megawatts, designed to be factory-built and deployed modularly rather than constructed on-site like traditional large nuclear plants. Tech companies including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are signing conditional offtake agreements with SMR developers to secure carbon-free baseload power for AI data centers.

Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module — the compact memory-stick form factor used in laptops and embedded systems. Rockchip's RK182X LLM accelerators ship in SO-DIMM packaging, meaning they plug into a standard laptop memory slot on a compatible host board.

A grayscale image produced by applying the Sobel operator, a spatial filter that estimates image gradient magnitude to highlight boundaries between regions of different brightness. In MRNF, the edge map acts as a priority buffer, directing new Gaussian ellipsoids toward visually important high-contrast regions during training.

Leon Festinger's 1954 framework proposing that individuals have a drive to evaluate their opinions and abilities, and do so by comparing themselves to others when objective benchmarks are unavailable. Upward social comparisons — against people perceived as more capable — tend to be self-undermining, lowering self-assessment and well-being rather than motivating improvement.

The spread of behaviors, attitudes, or outcomes through social networks, beyond what can be explained by individual choice or shared physical environment. Research by Nicholas Christakis and James Fowler showed that obesity, smoking behavior, and other outcomes spread through networks up to three degrees of separation. The mechanism is methodologically contested — homophily is a competing explanation — but directional peer-influence effects are well-documented across multiple studies.

Henri Tajfel and John Turner’s theory that a significant portion of self-concept derives from group membership, and that people systematically favor in-group members to maintain positive self-esteem. The theory predicts that merely being assigned to a group — without shared history, interests, or contact — is enough to generate discriminatory behavior toward out-group members.

Using social media platforms — primarily LinkedIn — to identify, understand, and engage with prospects. Social selling emphasizes relationship-building over automation, though the line between the two has blurred as monitoring and reply-assistance tools have proliferated.

The practice of mining text from social media, news, or other public sources to measure aggregate investor mood — positive, negative, or neutral — with the hypothesis that shifts in mood anticipate or correlate with subsequent price movements in financial markets.

A method of structured inquiry through sequential questions, named after the ancient Greek philosopher Socrates. In the context of AI prompting, it means the model asks the user questions one at a time rather than all at once, slowing down the interaction to elicit more considered answers before rendering any analysis.

Day traders in the late 1980s and 1990s who exploited NASDAQ's Small Order Execution System — a retail-protection mechanism — to electronically front-run slower, phone-bound market makers, earning short-lived but real profits before the market closed around them.

A fundamental distinction in photography and cinematography. Hard light comes from a small, distant, or direct source and produces sharp-edged shadows; soft light comes from a large or diffused source and wraps around subjects with gradual shadow transitions. The quality of shadows is often more expressive than their direction.

A conceptual framework articulated by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy in which Software 1.0 is explicit human-written code, Software 2.0 is neural networks trained on data, and Software 3.0 is prompts—programs written in natural language and interpreted by large language models at runtime. Karpathy has extrapolated the idea to interfaces rendered entirely by generative models.

PlayCanvas's open-source compression format for 3D Gaussian Splat data, released in September 2025. By spatially ordering Gaussians and applying GPU-friendly encoding, it reduces a four-million-Gaussian scene from roughly one gigabyte to 42 megabytes — a 95 percent reduction — without requiring decompression at load time.

TSMC's bumpless die-stacking technology that bonds two or more chips face-to-face with direct copper-to-copper interconnects, eliminating the solder bumps used in conventional flip-chip packaging. The bumpless interface achieves higher bandwidth density and lower signal latency than bumped alternatives — essential for tightly coupling photonic and electronic dies in COUPE.

The angle between the sun and the horizon, measured in degrees. At sunrise and sunset it is 0°; at local noon it peaks, reaching 90° only at tropical latitudes during zero-shadow day. Shadow length is inversely related to the tangent of this angle: a higher sun produces shorter shadows, approaching zero length as the angle approaches 90°.

An electrochemical device that generates electricity by oxidizing a fuel — typically natural gas or hydrogen — across a ceramic electrolyte, without combustion. Produces lower emissions than gas turbines, generates negligible NOx, and can operate entirely off-grid. AI data centers prize them for dispatchable, grid-independent power at scale.

Solidity is the most widely used programming language for writing smart contracts on the Ethereum blockchain. It is statically typed and compiles to bytecode that runs on the Ethereum Virtual Machine. Errors in Solidity code can be expensive or irreversible once deployed, which is why tooling and education around it have grown substantially.

A mathematical framework for universal prediction that defines the optimal hypothesis as the shortest program consistent with observed data. It provides the theoretical foundation for algorithmic information theory and formal Bayesian machine learning. Named after Ray Solomonoff, it is the rigorous statement of Occam's razor that Bennett directly contests.

A largely rejected theory proposing that people from the Solutrean culture of Ice Age Iberia crossed the North Atlantic to reach North America around 20,000 years ago, potentially carrying Haplogroup X with them. The absence of corroborating archaeological or genetic evidence has led most researchers to dismiss it.

A trauma therapy developed by Peter Levine based on the observation that animals in the wild discharge traumatic activation through shaking and trembling, and that humans suppress this. It uses careful, titrated attention to bodily sensation to help clients complete interrupted defensive responses. It has the strongest clinical evidence base among neo-Reichian-adjacent approaches, with published randomized trials showing large effect sizes for PTSD.

A hot desert spanning southern Arizona, southeastern California, and northwestern Mexico. It is characterized by extreme summer heat, saguaro cactus, and a bimodal precipitation pattern that produces both winter rains and a dramatic summer monsoon season each July through September.

In Liu Cixin’s *The Three-Body Problem*, a sophon is a civilization-scale supercomputer constructed inside a single proton. In humanoid form, Sophon appears as an extraordinarily beautiful and composed ambassador — elegant, principled, operating on a plane of intelligence incomprehensible to the humans she interacts with, while simultaneously undermining their civilization from within.

The branch of theology concerned with salvation — rescue from death, suffering, or damnation. In critiques of techno-religious belief, mind uploading and digital immortality serve the soteriological function: the promise of escape from biological mortality through technological transcendence.

Higgsfield's identity-persistence technology. Given a reference image, it derives a reusable token encoding the subject's visual characteristics — face, style, or aesthetic — so subsequent AI generations can reproduce that appearance consistently without retraining a model from scratch.

Jazz slang meaning to approach or solicit someone for a job or performance booking. Monk's instruction — 'don't sound anybody for a gig, just be on the scene' — advises against hustling: show up, be visible, let work come to you rather than chasing it.

A speculative mania that inflated shares of England's South Sea Company from roughly £128 in January 1720 to over £1,000 by August of that year before collapsing to around £100 by year-end. The bubble was sustained by insider manipulation and narrative rather than commercial substance, and it is considered one of the earliest and most studied financial collapses in history. Its aftermath contributed to early securities regulation in Britain.

An exchange-traded fund managed by BlackRock that tracks the ICE Semiconductor Index, holding 34 stocks spanning chip designers, manufacturers, and equipment makers. A modified-cap weighting rule limits any single holding to roughly 8%, preventing mega-caps from dominating the fund's return profile.

A broad term for computing experiences where three-dimensional space — rather than a flat screen — is the interface. It encompasses VR headsets, AR glasses, and devices like the Quest 3 that let users manipulate digital objects anchored to physical locations.

How packed or airy a layout feels — a function of margins, padding, element sizing, and white space. High density crams many elements into a compact area; low density spreads them out. It is one of the primary levers that distinguishes, say, a Bloomberg terminal from an Apple product page.

World Labs’ term for an AI system’s ability to perceive, generate, reason about, and interact with 3D environments. The company frames it as the spatial analogue to language intelligence in large language models: just as LLMs learned to understand and produce text, a spatially intelligent model should understand and generate physical space, including geometry, lighting, and physics.

The process of using sensors — typically on a device like a phone or VR headset — to capture the three-dimensional geometry of a real environment. The output is a navigable digital model of the physical space, not merely a photograph or video.

Pabrai's investment framework targeting companies whose core business generates the capital, talent, and infrastructure to launch entirely new businesses — compounding value not just within a single product but across an expanding portfolio of ventures.

An unsolicited, unofficial advertisement made without a brand's commission or approval — typically by a filmmaker, student, or enthusiast demonstrating their skills or a tool's capabilities. Spec ads featuring real brands and products do not carry the brand's endorsement and sometimes draw legal attention, though they are common in creative portfolios.

A standardized suite of compute-intensive programs maintained by the Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation, widely used in academic and industry research to compare CPU performance across language runtimes and architectures. Results are considered more representative of real-world workloads than narrow micro-benchmarks.

A one-time, non-recurring cash payment to shareholders, distinct from a regular quarterly dividend. Companies typically issue special dividends after an asset sale or when surplus cash accumulates with no immediate reinvestment use. Pioneer paid $16.7 million as a special dividend following its $50 million PCEP divestiture in late 2024.

A US federal appointment category for temporary advisers and consultants, capped by law at 130 working days per calendar year. SGEs face narrower financial-disclosure and ethics-recusal requirements than permanent federal employees, a distinction that critics argued allowed Sacks to retain his VC portfolio while setting AI policy his investments stood to benefit from.

In Frankfurt's model for low-volume securities, a designated specialist both quotes prices and executes trades. The specialist must maintain two-sided quotes but may widen bid-ask spreads aggressively when order flow is thin or one-sided. Unlike a deep electronic order book with many competing participants, a specialist model provides limited price support when a large sell order arrives with no natural counterpart.

The recurring social-media cycle in which a macro narrative (AI, space, biotech, crypto) is packaged with a short list of stock-market proxies and circulated as the site of the next generation of outsized returns, typically just after a prior theme has already produced its visible winners.

A deliberate processing delay applied to certain order types in an electronic market to protect slower participants from being picked off by fast-moving algorithms. Polymarket operated a 500-millisecond speed bump on taker orders; its silent removal in February 2026 eliminated a structural defense for market makers against latency bots.

A visualization technique, formalized in a 2001 IEEE InfoVis paper by Weber, Alexa, and Müller, that maps a time series along an Archimedean spiral rather than a horizontal axis. Periodic patterns appear as alignment across adjacent loops, revealing regularities that a linear chart would obscure.

Informal term for a single 3D Gaussian in a Gaussian Splatting scene. Each splat is a tiny, semi-transparent, color-bearing ellipsoid defined by its position, shape, orientation, and opacity. A typical photorealistic scene contains millions to hundreds of millions of them.

A training structure in which different sessions target different muscle groups — chest and triceps on Monday, back and biceps on Wednesday, and so on. Contrasted with full-body sessions, where every major muscle group is trained each workout. Research suggests both approaches produce similar results when total weekly volume is matched.

A design pattern using two separate API keys for distinct roles: one key (restricted by referrer and narrow API scope) handles the browser-facing JavaScript widget load, while a second key (kept entirely server-side) authenticates all data API calls through a proxy. Each key's exposure and potential damage are isolated from the other.

An open-source browser extension that lets YouTube users submit and share timestamps of sponsored segments, causing other users’ players to skip them automatically. It is the most widely cited architectural precedent for crowdsourced, threshold-based content filtering at scale.

The sensitivity of a mining stock's price to moves in the underlying commodity's spot price. High beta means a 10% rise in uranium translates into a disproportionately larger move in the miner's equity.

The job-search strategy of submitting as many applications as possible with minimal tailoring, betting that volume compensates for a low individual match rate. Automated tools such as LazyApply and Sonara are built around this approach. career-ops explicitly positions itself as the structural opposite.

A benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on spreadsheet-manipulation tasks, created by researchers at Renmin University of China, Tsinghua University, and Zhipu.AI. Accepted as a NeurIPS 2024 spotlight, it draws real-world questions from Excel user forums and scores answers using automated, OJ-style evaluation.

An animation model that mimics the behavior of a physical spring — overshoot, settle, and damping — to produce motion that feels natural rather than mechanical. Remotion exposes a `spring()` function that takes stiffness and damping parameters and returns an interpolated value for any given frame number.

The S&P 500 index level divided by M2 money supply (in billions of dollars), yielding a dimensionless number that tracks how expensive equities are relative to the pool of broad money in the economy. A rising ratio means stocks are absorbing more of each dollar of money supply; historically, extreme readings have coincided with major market peaks.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, which tracks the S&P 500 index and has the largest and most liquid options market of any single instrument in the world. It is used by institutions to hedge broad equity exposure and by speculators to trade macro direction. When a single company's call volume rivals or exceeds SPY's, it registers an extraordinary concentration of directional bets in that name.

A compressed file format for Gaussian splat data, open-sourced by Niantic. It is roughly 90 percent smaller than the standard PLY point-cloud format while preserving visual fidelity, making splats practical to share, stream, and embed. LichtFeld Studio can export directly to SPZ.

An attack technique in which malicious SQL code is inserted into an input field that is passed directly to a database without sanitization. A payload like `' OR 1=1--` can force a database to return all rows or skip password verification entirely. SQL injection has appeared in the OWASP Top 10 since the list began.

Static random-access memory — fast, low-latency memory that can be fabricated directly onto a processor die. Unlike HBM (stacked memory modules mounted alongside a GPU), on-chip SRAM is accessed without leaving the chip, eliminating the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that constrains large-batch GPU inference.

The practice of combining two or more style reference codes in a single Midjourney prompt to produce a hybrid aesthetic. For example, --sref 1995773328 2770200552 would interpolate between the visual character of both codes. Blended SREFs are popular for producing novel styles that no single code achieves alone.

A numeric parameter added to a Midjourney prompt (e.g. --sref 3743853584) that applies a consistent artistic style to any generated image or video. The number acts as a coordinate in Midjourney's style-vector space, allowing artists to share and reproduce a specific aesthetic without describing it in words. Over 4.2 billion possible codes exist.

The Science and Technology Innovation Board (科创板), launched by the Shanghai Stock Exchange in July 2019 as China's domestic answer to NASDAQ. It allows high-growth technology companies — including those that are pre-profit or face barriers to overseas listing — to raise capital domestically. Its 50 largest constituents by market cap form the STAR 50 Index, which KSTR tracks.

Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor — a class of antidepressants (including fluoxetine and sertraline) that raise serotonin levels by blocking its reabsorption into neurons. Cyproheptadine directly counteracts SSRIs by blocking serotonin receptors; the two taken together can eliminate the antidepressant effect.
An advanced version of the Stable Diffusion text-to-image model, offering higher resolution and improved image quality compared to its predecessor, commonly used for AI-assisted content creation.

A moderation architecture introduced by Bluesky in 2024 in which users subscribe to independent third-party labeling services, each applying its own rules for flagging or hiding content. Different users can choose different stacks, allowing pluralistic content standards without centralized enforcement.

Used colloquially to mean that something is impressively dense with quality content — packed with substance, well-curated, or unusually high in value relative to expectations. It carries an endorsement: the thing described is worth your time.

A simultaneous combination of stagnant economic growth and elevated inflation. It complicates monetary policy because rate cuts that might support growth would worsen inflation, while rate hikes that might control inflation risk deepening the slowdown. The paradigm case is the 1970s U.S. economy, when both unemployment and CPI rose together.

Staggering applies the same animation to a group of elements but offsets the start time of each by a fixed interval. The result is a cascade or wave effect — all elements perform the same motion, but sequentially rather than simultaneously — achieved with a single configuration value rather than per-element delays.

A small carved stone or metal object used in the ancient Near East to press an identifying mark or image into clay or wax. Hundreds have been recovered from Judah, Ammon, Phoenicia, and neighboring regions dating to the 9th–7th centuries BCE, many depicting four-winged serpents (*uraei*). They are primary archaeological evidence for the visual world contemporaneous with Isaiah.

The set of unit vectors that point along each coordinate axis: e₁ = (1,0,...,0), e₂ = (0,1,...,0), and so on. Any vector in the space can be expressed as a weighted sum of them, making them a minimal skeleton that fully determines what a linear transformation does to every possible input. The columns of a matrix are precisely the images of these basis vectors.

A wave pattern produced when two waves of the same frequency travel in opposite directions and superpose. Instead of propagating through space, the combined wave appears to stand still, with fixed nodes and antinodes. Resonant cavities — guitar bodies, organ pipes, soap-film membranes — naturally produce standing waves at specific frequencies.

When two waves of the same frequency travel in opposite directions and overlap, they produce a pattern that appears stationary — some points oscillate maximally (antinodes) while others remain still (nodes). In a confined space, only frequencies whose wavelengths fit the geometry can sustain themselves, which is why each cavity or surface has characteristic resonant modes.

A structured storytelling framework used in job interviews: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Candidates prepare short anecdotes in this format to answer behavioral questions. career-ops builds a running story bank in STAR format that is enriched with each new job evaluation, accumulating reusable interview material across the whole search.

A joint venture announced in January 2025 by OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, and MGX to build AI data center infrastructure across the United States, targeting up to $500 billion in investment by 2029. President Trump announced it at a White House press conference. Critics note the consortium's headline figures include planned spending, not committed capital.

Informal term for participation in startup or tech communities primarily for social exposure or credential accumulation rather than genuine product development. Communities use the phrase as shorthand for the problem of attracting attendees who consume shared resources — introductions, knowledge, event seats — without contributing reciprocal value.

In interactive animation, a state machine defines a set of states (idle, hover, pressed) and the rules for transitioning between them in response to user input or runtime events. Rive uses state machines to build animations that respond dynamically to live conditions — behavior that a static exported video file cannot replicate.

A cyberattack that exploits a system's persistent memory, allowing malicious instructions to survive across sessions and execute later rather than failing when a single session ends. Agents that store long-term memory are particularly vulnerable because a seemingly minor compromise can propagate forward in time.

A formal framework introduced in the Memento-Skills paper that extends the standard Markov decision process by augmenting the agent's state with episodic memory M. Because memory grows with each interaction, the raw trajectory is non-Markovian; SRDP recovers the Markov property by treating the augmented state (task state plus skill memory) as the unit of analysis. The paper proves convergence of soft policy iteration in this framework under bounded rewards.

In information geometry, the abstract curved surface formed by all distributions in a parameterized family. Each point on the manifold represents one distribution (e.g., one set of volatility and correlation parameters); distances between points are measured by the Fisher information metric; and the curvature of the manifold determines how rapidly the geometry departs from flat Euclidean space.

In trading, the minimum number of independent trade observations required before a performance metric — win rate, Sharpe ratio, excess return — carries statistical weight. Academic convention sets a rough floor of 30 trades for basic inference; professional quant standards typically demand several hundred, diversified across market regimes. Below that threshold, any apparent edge is indistinguishable from a random run of good luck. Twenty-three trades on a single afternoon falls well short of this floor.

A configurable bar at the bottom of the Claude Code terminal interface. Any shell script can populate it, receiving session data (current model, cost, context usage, git branch) as JSON on stdin and returning whatever text should be displayed. It runs locally with no API cost.

A policy introduced by Valve requiring developers to declare whether a game contains AI-generated content. It distinguishes pre-generated content (AI ran during development) from live-generated content (AI runs at runtime for each player), applying stricter review to the latter category.

The practice of constructing the strongest possible version of an opposing argument before engaging with it — the opposite of a straw man. Used in structured reasoning to prevent dismissing a position on the basis of its weakest or most easily mocked expression.

The inverse of strawmanning: constructing the strongest possible version of an opposing argument before responding, rather than a weakened version easy to defeat. Associated with philosopher Daniel Dennett and game theorist Anatol Rapoport’s rules of debate, it is used in AI alignment contexts to ensure critical arguments are taken at their most robust before being dismissed.

Synchron's proprietary endovascular BCI electrode array. Deployed by threading it through the superior sagittal sinus — a blood vessel near the motor cortex — it unfurls against the vessel wall to record nearby neural activity, eliminating open-brain surgery while keeping sensors far closer to neurons than scalp EEG permits.

A provision in U.S. tax law (IRC §1014) that resets the cost basis of inherited assets to their fair-market value at the date of the original owner's death, permanently eliminating any capital-gains tax liability that had accrued during the decedent's lifetime.

The standard citation system for Plato's texts, based on a 1578 edition published by the French scholar Henri Estienne (Stephanus in Latin). Every page of that edition is divided into five sections labeled a through e, and this alphanumeric reference — e.g., 52b — is used universally across all modern translations and editions, allowing scholars to cite the same passage regardless of which text or language they are working in.

A rare but potentially life-threatening immune reaction, usually triggered by a drug, that causes severe blistering and sloughing of skin and mucous membranes. It is listed as a serious adverse event in the FDA prescribing label for armodafinil and modafinil. It occurs in roughly one to two people per million per year in the general population but carries serious morbidity when it does occur.

Short-Term Interest Rate futures — exchange-traded contracts whose underlying benchmark has a maturity of less than one year. Quoted as 100 minus the implied rate (a price of 95.50 implies a 4.50% rate), so prices fall when rate expectations rise. They are the world’s most liquid expression of central bank policy expectations and are used for directional bets, curve trades, and hedging interest rate exposure.

STMicroelectronics' family of 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, among the most widely deployed embedded processors globally. Used in industrial automation, consumer electronics, IoT devices, automotive subsystems, and medical equipment. The surrounding ecosystem of development tools, certified firmware libraries, and reference hardware creates high switching costs that make the installed base durable across semiconductor cycles.

An optimization method that adds calibrated Gaussian noise to stochastic gradient descent steps, converting a deterministic optimizer into a Bayesian sampler. In the MCMC 3DGS paper, SGLD noise injected into Gaussian updates lets the model explore a posterior over scene representations rather than collapsing to a single local optimum.

A term coined in a 2021 paper by Bender, Gebru, and colleagues to characterize large language models as systems that stochastically sample plausible-sounding text from learned probability distributions, without any genuine semantic understanding. The thesis holds that text-only training cannot ground meaning, because meaning requires embodied, social experience — a position Beckmann and Queloz argue is empirically undercut by mechanistic interpretability evidence.

A Runway ML feature that generates multi-frame visual narratives from a single input image or prompt. It automates the storyboarding process by producing sequenced, stylistically consistent panels suitable for pre-visualization or short-form storytelling.

An options position constructed by buying (or selling) both a call and a put at the same strike price and expiration. A long straddle profits if the underlying moves sharply in either direction; a short straddle profits if the underlying stays near the strike. Straddles are a direct expression of a view on realized volatility, stripped of directional bias.

A precision mechanical gear system (also called a harmonic drive) in which a thin, elliptical flexspline meshes with a rigid circular spline via a rotating wave generator. This produces very high gear-reduction ratios in a compact, lightweight package with near-zero backlash — making it the dominant joint-actuator technology in collaborative and humanoid robots.

A precision gear reduction mechanism — sold commercially as a Harmonic Drive — that uses the controlled elastic deformation of a thin metal cup to achieve near-zero backlash and high torque density in a compact form. Widely used in robot rotary joints. Zero backlash means no lost motion when a joint reverses direction.

A narrow waterway between Iran and the Oman peninsula, roughly 33 miles wide at its narrowest navigable channel. Approximately 20 million barrels of oil per day—around 20% of global supply and 25% of all seaborne oil—transit the Strait. Its closure following the Iran conflict of early 2026 severed the primary artery of Gulf oil exports, affecting roughly one in five barrels consumed globally.

indie's term for the projected lifetime revenue of awarded customer design wins, typically measured over a roughly ten-year horizon. It is a forward indicator of demand rather than a contractual obligation, and conversion to actual revenue depends on the customer's vehicle programs reaching production at expected volumes.

A practice developed by Al Bauman that synthesizes Reichian bodywork with acting-training methods drawn from Stanislavski and Chekhov. The techniques of the actor's craft — presence, voice, spontaneous movement, emotional availability — are used as a form of bodywork that helps clients integrate released emotional material into ordinary relational life, rather than leaving catharsis as an isolated event on the mat.

The fixed price at which an options contract gives the holder the right to buy (call) or sell (put) the underlying stock. A $120 call gives the holder the right to buy Intel shares at $120 regardless of the market price; that right is valuable only if the market price exceeds $120 before or at expiration.

A company whose competitive position is tied to a secular, multi-year demand shift in the underlying economy rather than a product cycle or macro tailwind. The idea is that the thesis survives — and often strengthens — through short-term price volatility, because the structural need being addressed does not go away.

A photogrammetry technique that infers the 3D structure of a scene and the positions from which photographs were taken by analyzing how features move across multiple overlapping images. COLMAP is the most widely used open-source implementation.

A debt security issued by a bank whose return is linked to the performance of a reference asset — here, a proprietary equity basket. Unlike a plain bond, the investor’s repayment may be contingent on the basket staying above certain price levels. Structured notes can be configured as autocallables, reverse convertibles, or principal-protected products, giving issuers flexibility in shaping risk-return profiles.

A technique for directing AI models in which the input is organized into hierarchical fields — shot, subject, scene, audio — rather than free-form prose. Borrows conventions from production documents like shot lists and VFX briefs, and tends to produce more predictable, controllable outputs.

An AI's ability to generate images that closely resemble the distinctive look of a specific artist or platform. Style itself is generally not copyrightable under US law, but the training images used to teach that mimicry may be — a tension at the heart of the ongoing lawsuits.

A Midjourney parameter that accepts a numeric code and constrains the model's output to match a specific visual aesthetic. The codes are derived from existing images or discovered by community experimentation, and can be blended by chaining multiple numbers together. They function as reproducible style presets, shareable across users.

A structured set of reusable design decisions — color palettes, typography scales, spacing units, component patterns — that enforces visual consistency across a product. Analogous to a house style in publishing: once defined, every new element is derived from it rather than invented from scratch.

A class of AI techniques that separate the *content* of an image (what objects are depicted) from its *style* (color palette, brushwork, compositional mood) and apply the style to new content. Modern diffusion models can do this implicitly without an explicit two-stage process.

Isolated Claude Code worker processes spawned by the main session via the Task tool. Each sub-agent has its own context window, tool access, and system prompt; the parent receives only the summary result, keeping the main context window clean. Up to roughly ten can run concurrently, enabling parallel work across long agentic sessions.

A function h is sub-invariant under a Markov chain if its expected value after one transition step is at most its current value — it does not increase on average.
