This property is what allows the proof to bound the Erdős sum: once you show 1/(n log n) is sub-invariant under the von Mangoldt chain, the desired inequality follows without accumulating extra error.

A pattern in which a coordinating agent dispatches tasks to specialised sub-agents, each running in its own isolated context window. The coordinator receives only the sub-agent's final output — not its internal reasoning history — keeping the main session clean and enabling multi-hour workflows that would otherwise exhaust a single agent's memory.

The functionalist claim that the physical material implementing a computation is irrelevant to whether consciousness arises. If true, silicon circuits are viable candidates for consciousness; if false — as biological naturalists like John Searle argue — only specific biochemistry can instantiate genuine mental states.

A research framework, associated with Randal Koene and the nonprofit Carbon Copies, premised on the idea that the cognitive processes constituting a mind can be ported from neurons to silicon or any other medium capable of the same functional organization. It is the engineering translation of philosophical functionalism.

The key reagent in phosphate fertilizer production. Phosphate rock is dissolved in sulfuric acid to produce phosphoric acid, which is then reacted with ammonia to make DAP or MAP. Producing sulfuric acid requires large quantities of elemental sulfur, making sulfur a critical and non-substitutable input whose price directly determines phosphate production economics.

A pseudolinguistic hypothesis promoted by the Turkish state in 1935–1936, claiming all human languages descended from a proto-Turkic primal language. Atatürk personally backed it; it was quietly abandoned after his death in 1938 and is now regarded as an example of state-sponsored linguistic nationalism with no scientific basis.

A faint red glow emitted by chlorophyll molecules in plants as a byproduct of photosynthesis. Because its intensity varies with how actively a plant is fixing carbon, satellites capable of detecting SIF provide a near-real-time measure of photosynthetic productivity — more responsive than older vegetation indices based purely on reflected light.

A feature in the Suno music-generation platform that lets users save the distinct vocal character of a generated track and reuse it consistently across multiple songs. It enables the illusion of a single artist with a recognizable voice, even though the underlying system generates everything from scratch each time.

A film format that exposes a wider area of 16mm film stock, giving a larger image and slightly wider aspect ratio than standard 16mm. Favored by independent filmmakers through the 1990s and 2000s for its distinctive grain, compressed color, and lower cost relative to 35mm.

A mobile application that bundles a wide range of services — messaging, payments, ride-hailing, food delivery, social media — into a single platform. WeChat (Tencent) and Alipay (Ant Group) are the canonical examples. The super-app model dominated China's consumer internet era and remains the primary revenue engine for KWEB's largest holdings.

A prolonged period — typically measured in years — during which demand for a commodity or technology persistently outstrips supply, driving prices and producer margins sharply above their long-run average. In semiconductors, supercycles are powered by demand waves (AI, smartphones, cloud build-out) that arrive faster than new manufacturing capacity can be constructed. They tend to end abruptly when enough new supply comes online simultaneously.

A research division within Meta Platforms, announced in 2026, focused on advanced AI systems and agent development. It serves as Meta's primary group working toward general-purpose and frontier AI capabilities.

The hypothesis that neural networks represent more distinct concepts than they have neurons, by encoding multiple features as overlapping directions in the same activation space. It is the root cause of polysemanticity and a central obstacle to interpreting individual neurons: you cannot read off a single concept from a neuron that encodes several.

The finding that neural networks represent more distinct features than they have neurons by storing multiple features in overlapping directions in high-dimensional activation space. Networks exploit the geometry of high dimensions to pack in extra information, which is why individual neurons respond to seemingly unrelated concepts.

A linked sequence of memory entries tracking how a fact evolves over time. When an entry is updated or contradicted, the old version is marked 'superseded' and linked to its replacement rather than deleted. The full revision history is preserved, enabling rollback to any earlier verified state.

PlayCanvas's open-source, browser-based editor for Gaussian Splats. It allows users to load, crop, filter, and export Gaussian Splat scenes without installing software, and serves as a key component of PlayCanvas's broader Gaussian Splatting toolchain.

A training technique in which a pre-trained language model's weights are updated using labeled input-output examples. Unlike pre-training on raw text at scale, SFT adjusts the model toward specific behaviors or styles using a curated dataset. Here it was applied with LoRA, a parameter-efficient variant that updates only a small fraction of weights.

The orchestrating agent in a multi-agent hierarchy. It receives the original user query, decides which specialized sub-agent should handle each part, aggregates their outputs, and determines when the answer is ready or when a human should intervene.

Serenity's investment framework: rather than buying the dominant final product (e.g., NVIDIA GPUs), identify the single most concentrated, irreplaceable upstream input whose capacity cannot grow as fast as end demand. The thesis is that these chokepoints trade at depressed valuations before institutions discover them, producing asymmetric risk-reward for early movers.

An investment framework that seeks narrow, hard-to-substitute nodes within a technology supply chain — components, materials, or processes that large downstream assemblers depend on but cannot easily source elsewhere. The theory holds that these chokepoints command pricing power and durable margins even when end-market competition is fierce.

A price zone where a stock has historically attracted enough buying interest to halt or reverse a decline, acting as an informal floor. When a stock pulls back to support, traders expect buyers to step in and defend the level. A decisive break below support is typically treated as a bearish signal that can accelerate selling.

A technique that records the electrical signals produced by muscles — in Meta's wristband, the forearm muscles involved in fine finger movements. Because muscle signals are much stronger and less noisy than scalp EEG signals, sEMG-based interfaces have achieved higher decoding accuracy with far less data and compute.

A term coined by Shoshana Zuboff for the business model underlying major digital platforms: behavioural data generated by user activity is extracted as raw material, processed into predictive products, and sold to advertisers seeking to modify human conduct. In this model, persuasion and behavioural modification are not side effects of the platform but its core commercial logic.

A variant of survivorship bias specific to social-media trading culture, in which practitioners publish live dashboards or screenshots selectively — sharing winning sessions, folding quietly on losing runs. The cumulative public record therefore overrepresents profitable outcomes, creating a false impression of systematic skill. The effect is amplified by live-equity-curve aesthetics: a rising intraday chart reads as proof of edge even when it is statistical noise dressed in a polished UI.

Sanskrit term meaning inherent, self-sufficient existence or own-nature. The Madhyamaka school’s central argument is that no phenomenon possesses svabhāva — everything that exists does so only through dependence on conditions and other phenomena, never through its own independent nature.

SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is an XML-based format for two-dimensional graphics that scales without pixelation. Animating SVG means programmatically changing its path coordinates, colors, or transforms over time — enabling effects like morphing shapes and drawing lines, which raster images cannot easily replicate.

A benchmark that measures how well an AI system can autonomously resolve real software bugs and feature requests drawn from open-source GitHub repositories. A higher score indicates the model can navigate complex, multi-step coding tasks with minimal human guidance; 57.4% is a strong result for a model in this parameter class.

Apple's declarative framework for building native apps across its device family — iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro — using the Swift programming language. Apps written in SwiftUI can access hardware features like ARKit and the Dynamic Island that cross-platform frameworks cannot reach.

In jazz, 'to swing' describes a rhythmic feeling — a forward propulsion generated by the interplay of musicians staying in the groove. It is easier to feel than to define, which is why Monk's advice ('when you're swinging, swing some more') amounts to: once you have the feeling, deepen it rather than second-guess it.

Electrical equipment — circuit breakers, disconnects, fuses, and associated controls — used to protect, isolate, and switch power circuits in substations, factories, and large buildings. Pioneer's divested PCEP segment manufactured engineered switchgear assemblies for utilities and infrastructure customers.

The costs — monetary, operational, or regulatory — a customer would incur by replacing one supplier with another. In defence hardware, switching costs are especially high because replacing a certified component requires extensive re-testing and regulatory re-qualification, sometimes taking years. This creates durable revenue streams for the incumbent supplier even when competitors offer better products.

The narrow gap (20–40 nanometres) between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrite of the next. Neurons never physically touch; communication across this gap is chemical. Neurotransmitter molecules are released by the sender, diffuse across the cleft, and bind to receptors on the receiver.

Impaired signaling at synapses, the junctions between neurons where one cell passes a chemical or electrical signal to the next. In the context of ASD, it refers specifically to disruptions in the proteins that build, maintain, and regulate synapses — widely considered the clearest neuropathological feature of the condition.

A radar imaging system mounted on a satellite or aircraft that can penetrate cloud cover and operate at night, unlike optical cameras. It measures the reflection of microwave pulses off the Earth's surface, making it useful for detecting flooding, monitoring crop growth, and mapping terrain regardless of weather.

Training data generated by a computer simulation rather than collected from the real world. In robotics and computer vision, synthetic data is appealing because it comes pre-labeled and can be produced in unlimited quantities, though models trained on it must still transfer to real-world conditions — a challenge called the *sim-to-real gap*.

@ty_kra_lab's self-coined term for their variant of AI-assisted prototyping, intended to distinguish it from pure vibe coding by emphasizing intentional architectural and system-level thinking. No formal definition exists outside of this post; the phrase resonates with generative art's tradition of artists designing rule-systems rather than individual outputs.

Borrowed from cognitive psychology, where 'System 1' is fast and intuitive and 'System 2' is slow and deliberate. In AI, it refers to training a model to generate step-by-step reasoning chains before acting — decomposing goals, checking consistency, and self-correcting — rather than responding reactively.

An assembly technique that integrates multiple chips, passive components, and sometimes optical elements into a single module. SiP packaging is used by companies like Shunsin to combine laser dies, drivers, and receivers into compact transceiver modules, reducing board space and improving signal integrity.

A source of return that moves many stocks at once — the broad market, a sector rotation, a momentum tilt. Systematic returns are not alpha (skill-based) but beta (exposure-based); they cannot be diversified away without hedging the factor directly.

A structured, comprehensive search and synthesis of all published research on a defined question, using explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria. Distinct from a narrative review, it aims to minimize selection bias and is the gold standard for evidence-based medicine and policy — and requires broad, reproducible coverage of the literature rather than a handful of citations.

In evidence synthesis, sensitivity measures what fraction of all relevant studies a search strategy actually retrieves. A sensitivity of 39.5% means a tool is missing more than 60% of the relevant literature — a serious problem for meta-analyses and clinical guidelines that depend on comprehensive coverage.

An investment approach in which buy and sell decisions are generated by a defined rule or model rather than by discretionary human judgment. Systematic strategies range from simple momentum rules (buy recent winners, sell recent losers) to complex machine-learning models that combine hundreds of signals. The appeal is consistency and scalability; the vulnerability is that the underlying signals can be identified, published, and arbitraged by competitors.

A company that assembles components sourced from multiple suppliers into finished products, rather than designing or fabricating the underlying parts. SMCI buys GPUs from Nvidia and processors from Intel and AMD, then combines them into rack-scale servers. Margins are thin because component cost largely determines the selling price.

One of the major schools of Chan and Zen, named after Chinese Tang-dynasty masters Dongshan Liangjie and Caoshan Benji. Known for emphasis on shikantaza rather than kōan practice. Brought to Japan by Dōgen in the 13th century; Eiheiji temple, which Dōgen founded in 1243, remains one of the two Sōtō head temples in Japan today.

A term borrowed from standard securities settlement notation. In oil trade, it refers to the 30-to-60 day delay between when a cargo is shipped and an LC is opened and when the corresponding bank payment settles. The analyst uses this framing to explain why a trade disruption that began in early March 2026 would not show up as freed working capital in money markets until April–May 2026—matching the timing of the equity rally.

The original Greek title of *Meditations*, meaning "To Himself" or "Things Unto Himself." Marcus Aurelius gave the work no formal title; this phrase, derived from the surviving manuscripts, captures the text's private, self-addressed character. The familiar title *Meditations* was assigned by later editors.

An Arabic word for stupefaction or utter bewilderment — the state of being so overwhelmed that rational faculties seize up. In the etymology Rāzī records, aliha is glossed as a synonym of tahayyara ('to be stupefied'), connecting the root of ilāh/Allāh to this cognitive incapacity before the divine.

A utility-first CSS framework where styling is applied by composing short, single-purpose class names directly in HTML markup rather than writing separate stylesheets. Extremely popular in the React and Next.js ecosystem and the most common styling layer AIDesigner needs to understand.

A film movement that emerged in Taiwan in the early 1980s, characterized by naturalistic acting, location shooting, and stories drawn from working-class and provincial life. Directors Edward Yang and Hou Hsiao-hsien used it to examine Taiwan's rapid industrialization and shifting cultural identity. The movement is considered one of the most significant national cinema movements of the late twentieth century, influencing filmmakers across Asia and beyond.

The challenge that arises when multiple AI agents work concurrently on the same codebase. Because each agent reads and writes files independently, their changes can conflict at merge time—analogous to two developers editing the same file on separate branches without coordination.

The share of gross bookings a platform retains as revenue after paying the service provider. Uber's average take rate rose from roughly 25 percent at launch to an estimated 42 percent by 2024, with individual trips reaching 65 to 70 percent. Uber does not disclose this figure as a named metric in SEC filings.

A long-term supply agreement in which the buyer commits to pay for a minimum volume of a commodity or service whether or not they actually take delivery. For Linde, these contracts — typically 15–20 years, with supply infrastructure built adjacent to the customer's facility — provide highly predictable recurring revenue and make switching to a competitor economically prohibitive.

In Sufi taxonomy of the stages of walah, the final stage — a total self-annihilation in which the lover's individual identity is dissolved entirely into the Beloved. Sufi sources describe it paradoxically as a destruction that precedes eternal life, the limit-point of the mystical path.
An AI workflow that animates a still portrait or product image to appear as though it is speaking or moving, often used in marketing and social-media content production.

Targeting Aging with Metformin: a proposed Phase III randomised controlled trial designed by Nir Barzilai to test whether metformin can delay the composite onset of multiple age-related diseases — heart attack, stroke, cancer, dementia, death — in healthy adults aged 65–79. Its FDA-reviewed design represented a landmark implicit acceptance of aging as a clinical trial endpoint, but as of mid-2026 the trial remains incompletely funded and unenrolled.

The dominant decorative motif of Shang bronze art: a frontal, bilaterally symmetrical zoomorphic mask with raised eyes, horns, and typically no lower jaw. The name, meaning 'glutton' or 'ogre-mask,' was applied by later Zhou-era texts; the Shang left no written name for it. Scholars debate whether its terrifying quality reflects deliberate iconography or a byproduct of the casting process.

The final step of semiconductor design before manufacturing begins — the moment a chip design is sent to the foundry for fabrication. A delayed tapeout means a chip will be manufactured and shipped later than planned, affecting a company’s product roadmap and the revenue it can book from that product.

Bennett's term for the layered, multi-scale cellular responses through which complex organisms classify stimuli by their survival significance. He argues that these orchestrated signals — not some further emergent property on top of them — are what qualia physically are.

A methodological framework for using observational data to mimic the structure and eligibility criteria of a randomised controlled trial, controlling for the selection biases that afflict conventional observational studies. It produces stronger causal inference than standard regression analyses but remains observational — not a substitute for an RCT.

The built-in Claude Code mechanism for spawning sub-agents. Calling the Task tool creates an isolated worker with its own context window and tool access; the result returned to the parent is a summary, not the full intermediate transcript. It is the primary mechanism for parallelism and context preservation in long sessions.

A metric developed by METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) measuring the longest task — in hours of equivalent expert human effort — that a frontier AI agent can reliably complete. It is used to track the expanding scope of AI autonomous capability over time and has been doubling roughly every seven months since 2019 according to METR’s own data.

The tendency of AI coding assistants to forget earlier decisions, constraints, and architectural context as a conversation or codebase grows. Because the model can only process a finite window of text at once, information from prior sessions is simply not available to it — leading to repeated mistakes and contradictory outputs.

In creative and intellectual work, taste refers to the ability to judge quality — to recognise what is excellent before you can reliably produce it yourself. The gap between taste and skill is what makes early-stage work frustrating; it is also the engine of improvement. Ira Glass described this dynamic memorably: beginners have good taste but weak execution, and the only cure is volume of work.

A synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4, a protein that regulates actin — the scaffold giving cells their shape — and promotes tissue repair. Despite extensive animal data, it has no published human clinical trials. The FDA classifies it as presenting significant safety risks.

A software development practice in which the developer writes automated tests before writing the code that satisfies them. The cycle is: write a failing test, write the minimum code to pass it, then refactor. The goal is to ensure correctness is baked in from the start rather than verified at the end.

An approach to evaluating securities based on statistical patterns in price and volume data — charts, moving averages, momentum indicators — rather than on the underlying business's financial condition. Practitioners believe past price patterns repeat and can be used to forecast future price direction. Distinguished from fundamental analysis, which focuses on earnings, assets, and competitive position.

In the context of AI video generation, a practitioner term for the discipline of translating cinematic intent into precise, machine-readable parameters. It borrows vocabulary from film production — shot lists, lighting setups, color grading — and applies it to prompt engineering, positioning the practice as a professional skill distinct from casual natural-language prompting.

The view that technological progress is the primary driver of human welfare and should be actively pursued without precautionary constraints. In the specific form Andreessen advocates, it holds that markets and innovation—rather than regulation or redistribution—are the correct mechanisms for solving civilisational problems. The term predates Andreessen, but his 2023 manifesto gave it a sharply ideological edge, linking it to accelerationist discourse and placing it in explicit opposition to AI safety and sustainability frameworks.

A term used by critics, including philosopher Mark Coeckelbergh, to describe political ideologies that fuse techno-utopian faith in engineering with hard nationalist authoritarianism — prioritizing state power, military capability, and civilizational hierarchy over democratic pluralism. Critics apply it to arguments that treat AI weapons development as a national imperative exempt from ethical deliberation.

A concept from Neil Postman's 1992 book of the same name, describing a society that finds its meaning, authority, and satisfactions entirely within technology — valuing machines for efficiency and capability rather than moral wisdom. In a technopoly, there is no standard outside of technology by which technology itself can be judged. Roon uses the term to characterise GPT as the ideal product of a culture that wants a perfect tool, not a moral interlocutor.

A Sanskrit term for divine radiance or luminous power, believed in Vedic and Hindu thought to emanate from gods, heroes, and accomplished ascetics. It underlies the South Asian artistic convention of depicting sacred figures surrounded by flames or golden light — the same visual idiom that the Christian nimbus and Buddhist prabha-mandala also express, albeit from different starting points.

A rendering technique that accumulates pixel information across multiple consecutive frames to simultaneously reduce aliasing (jagged edges on geometry) and upscale the output image. Unlike purely spatial methods, TAAU improves in quality the longer a scene remains static.

The property of a generated video in which objects, lighting, and characters remain visually consistent from frame to frame. Its absence produces flickering, morphing, or objects that appear and disappear arbitrarily.

Standard image inpainting fills in a missing or masked region within a single frame. Temporal inpainting extends this to the time dimension: given two anchor frames — a start and an end — the model generates all intermediate frames as a plausible video sequence. Wan's Fun Inpainting is an example, filling in missing time between two provided images rather than missing space within one.

Evaluating one's current abilities or progress by reference to one's own past self, rather than to peers or external benchmarks. Research by Gürel and colleagues (2020) found this produces improvement-oriented goals and sustained pride without the shame responses that social comparison characteristically generates.

A post-processing step applied to per-frame motion estimates to reduce jitter — the rapid, physically implausible oscillations that appear when an AI model makes slightly inconsistent predictions across consecutive frames. Smoothing improves visual quality but can mask underlying model errors, which is why Barreto's comparison omits it.

The capital of the Aztec (Mexica) empire, built on a volcanic island in Lake Texcoco in what is now central Mexico City. At its peak around 1519, the city held an estimated 200,000–400,000 people, making it one of the largest cities in the world at the time.

A high-visibility anchor event that structures a broader calendar of smaller activities, the way a circus tent’s central pole holds up the canvas around it. In community-building, a recurring monthly tentpole gives dispersed members a high-commitment reason to gather in person rather than drifting apart between online interactions.

A benchmark suite used to evaluate AI coding agents on real-world software engineering tasks. Tools like Claude Code and Cursor are measured against it. A top ranking indicates strong task-completion performance in controlled evaluations, though real-world results vary.

A program that manages multiple terminal sessions through a persistent background server. Users can detach from a session — or lose their network connection — and later reattach, finding every process exactly where they left it. tmux and GNU Screen are the two most common examples.

A subdivided region within a tmux session, each running its own independent shell or process. Panes can be split horizontally or vertically, addressed by numeric ID, and assigned human-readable labels via tmux-bridge.

A benchmark for evaluating AI agents on realistic command-line interface and DevOps tasks run in sandboxed environments, hosted at tbench.ai. It scores agents on their ability to complete terminal operations autonomously without human guidance.
An open-source terminal emulator app for Android that provides a Linux-style shell directly on the device without rooting it, sometimes used as an alternative pathway to running CLI tools on mobile.

The human faction in *StarCraft*, depicted as pragmatic, militarily utilitarian, and aesthetically scrappy — machinery welded together under pressure, shaped by the rough conditions of a colonial diaspora. In cultural shorthand, “Terran-coded” suggests a results-first, industrially American energy with no patience for elegance that doesn’t pull weight.

An acronym coined by Timnit Gebru and Émile P. Torres for a cluster of interrelated ideologies — Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism — that they argue share structural features with millenarian religion, including an eschatology centered on the Singularity and a soteriology centered on digital immortality.

Apple's official platform for distributing pre-release iOS and macOS apps to beta testers. Developers upload a build to App Store Connect, add testers by email or via a public link, and testers install the app through the TestFlight app. Builds that pass a lighter automated review in TestFlight can later be promoted for full App Store submission.

The well-replicated finding that actively retrieving information from memory — answering practice questions, writing free recalls — produces significantly better long-term retention than passively rereading the same material. The effort of retrieval appears to strengthen the neural pathway, not merely confirm it.

A class of AI tools that take a natural-language description and produce a playable interactive experience — assets, logic, and environment — rather than a static image or video. Analogous to text-to-image but with the added requirement that outputs must be functional and interactive, not merely visually plausible.

A class of AI model that converts written text into natural-sounding spoken audio. Modern neural TTS systems can generate speech that is difficult to distinguish from a human recording, and many now support custom voice styles.

A class of generative AI models that produce short video clips from textual descriptions. The user supplies a prompt describing the scene, style, and action; the model synthesizes realistic or stylized footage without manual animation or filming. Leading examples in 2025 include Google Veo 3, Runway Gen-4, Kling, and Pika.

The technique of wrapping a 2D image around a 3D object's surface to give it apparent detail — colour, roughness, surface variation — without increasing geometric complexity. Texture quality and UV layout jointly determine how convincing the result looks under lighting.

A standard technique in 3D graphics where a flat image is mathematically 'wrapped' onto a mesh surface. It creates the visual appearance of detail without adding geometric complexity, which is fine for screens but causes problems in physical fabrication because the printer or mill only sees the underlying geometry, not the painted surface.

An area light source where the emitted light varies spatially according to a texture image, rather than being a uniform color. This lets a panel light cast a projected image — a logo, a gradient, a screen — into the surrounding scene in a physically plausible way.

The residual spread added to one leg of a cross-currency swap to make the contract economically fair. Classical theory — covered interest parity — predicts it should be zero; in practice it is persistently negative for major non-dollar currencies, meaning foreign borrowers pay a premium above theoretical rates to obtain dollars. The basis widens sharply during periods of dollar funding stress, making it a widely-watched systemic indicator.

A 2019 essay by Richard Sutton observing that, across 70 years of AI research, general methods leveraging increasing computation have consistently outperformed approaches that encode human expert knowledge. Sutton traces the pattern through chess, speech recognition, and computer vision, and argues it is the dominant empirical fact of the field.

A set of sensitivity measures quantifying how an option’s price responds to different variables: delta (underlying price), gamma (rate of delta change), theta (time decay), vega (implied volatility), and rho (interest rates). Managing the Greeks is the core risk-management activity of a derivatives hedging desk.

A 32-step simulated corporate network intrusion benchmark developed by AISI in collaboration with SpecterOps. It requires an AI agent to execute end-to-end: reconnaissance, credential theft, lateral movement across multiple network segments, a supply-chain pivot, and data exfiltration — a complete attack chain estimated at roughly twenty hours of work for a skilled human professional.

concepts.term: The Map Is Not the Territory
concepts.definition: Any description or model of reality is necessarily incomplete; the menu is not the meal, the blueprint is not the building. Treating your representation of a situation as the situation itself is a systematic source of error, because the simplifications required to build a map inevitably leave things out.

A concept from phenomenological philosophy — notably Emmanuel Levinas — referring to an entity encountered as genuinely distinct from oneself: a being with its own inner life, moral standing, and capacity for judgment. Roon uses it to distinguish Claude (which users approach as a potential moral interlocutor who might evaluate them) from GPT (which users approach as an extension of themselves, carrying no such weight).

Ray Kurzweil’s term for a hypothetical future moment when machine superintelligence surpasses human intelligence, triggering a runaway technological acceleration incomprehensible to present-day humans. Kurzweil predicts it for 2045. Critics note the concept carries the structural features of a religious prophecy: a specific date, a cosmic transformation, and a community of believers who rationalize delays.

A cyclic options income strategy that chains cash-secured puts and covered calls. Phase one: sell a put on a stock you are willing to own; collect premium until either the option expires worthless (repeat) or shares are assigned. Phase two: sell a covered call against those shares; collect premium until either the option expires worthless (repeat) or shares are called away (exit). The cycle then begins again.

One of the options Greeks; measures how much an option’s price declines with each passing day, all else being equal. Long options positions pay theta daily as the cost of holding the position, while short options positions collect it. 0DTE options carry maximal theta, losing essentially all time value in a single session.

The daily erosion in an option's price as it approaches expiration, all else equal. Short-dated options lose value rapidly in their final weeks; LEAPS decay far more slowly. This property makes LEAPS attractive for investors who want sustained exposure without pressure to be right on timing.

When light strikes a thin transparent layer — such as a soap film — some reflects from the outer surface and some from the inner surface. The two reflected beams interfere, amplifying certain wavelengths (colors) and canceling others depending on the film's local thickness. This is why soap bubbles display shifting rainbow colors, and why vibration-induced thickness changes produce vivid, moving color patterns.

The Vietnamese form of Chan (Chinese) or Zen (Japanese) Buddhism. Emphasises direct experiential insight over scriptural study or ritual, typically through meditation practice. Thich Nhat Hanh belonged to the Linji (Japanese: Rinzai) lineage, 42nd generation.

In computing, thrashing occurs when a system spends more time managing memory swaps than doing productive work. Borretti applies the term to a productivity pattern: a single blocked task generates so much anxiety that it halts all other work. His remedy is to timebox effort on the blocked item and route the rest of the day around it.

A vertical electrical connection that passes through an entire silicon die, enabling memory chips to be stacked and wired together in three dimensions. TSV technology is the core manufacturing technique behind HBM and is difficult to execute at scale; it requires specialized equipment and expertise that Chinese chipmakers are attempting to develop domestically.

A helical time representation proposed by geographers Edsall and Peuquet in 1997 for use in GIS software. Its linear axis encoded the irreversible forward flow of time; its revolutions encoded cyclic return. One of the earliest academic precedents for the helix-as-time-metaphor.

A three-dimensional helical curve used as a time visualization structure. Its linear axis encodes irreversible forward flow while its revolutions encode repeating cycles (days, seasons, years), unifying the two intuitive modes of temporal experience in one geometric object.

A variational autoencoder designed for video that enforces temporal ordering — each frame can only attend to past frames, not future ones. This respects the arrow of time and improves motion coherence compared to architectures that process all frames simultaneously.

Shorthand for the investment thesis that when safe assets such as cash or government bonds offer negative real returns, investors have no viable alternative but to hold equities or other risk assets. Repopularized during the zero-rate era of 2009–2022, it is used to explain persistent equity multiple expansion in low-rate environments.

Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities: US government bonds whose principal adjusts with the Consumer Price Index, guaranteeing a positive real return if held to maturity. The catch is that they trade at a premium during periods of inflation anxiety and tend to lag nominal Treasuries in calm, low-inflation environments.

A NAND flash cell type that stores three bits per cell, achieving higher density than MLC at the cost of lower write endurance and slightly slower speeds. Now the mainstream cell type in most consumer and enterprise 3D NAND SSDs.

Technology, Media, and Telecom — a combined sector grouping that became standard during and after the dot-com era to measure the aggregate weight of internet, software, hardware, cable, and telephone companies in the S&P 500. At the March 2000 peak, TMT reached roughly 40% of the index.

A terminal multiplexer — a program that lets a single terminal window host multiple independent shell sessions, each in its own pane or window. Developers use it to run several processes side by side; smux builds on tmux’s native pane-addressing and I/O-capture capabilities.

The shell CLI at the core of smux. It wraps standard tmux commands into agent-friendly operations: listing panes, reading their output, typing labeled messages, and sending control keys. Any process that can invoke bash can use it without additional dependencies.

A standard throughput measure for language model inference counting how many output tokens — roughly word-fragments — the model produces per second. The figure meaningfully depends on whether it measures prefill speed (processing the input prompt) or decode speed (generating each output token), as the two have different computational profiles.

The basic unit a large language model uses to process text — roughly three-quarters of a word in English. Pricing and context-window limits are both measured in tokens, making token efficiency a key cost variable for AI-powered workflows.

The practice — intentional or incidental — of using a flat-rate consumer subscription to absorb workloads that would cost far more under per-token API billing. An AI provider prices subscriptions assuming typical individual usage; heavy automated agent sessions can consume tokens at rates that far exceed what the subscription was priced to cover.

The accumulation of unnecessary text in an agent's workspace files, causing the system prompt to consume a growing share of tokens on every API call. Because API costs are priced per token, bloated workspaces raise expenses directly and can crowd out useful context.

The process of breaking raw text into discrete units — often subwords rather than whole words — that a model processes as integers. A word like "unbelievable" might become two or three tokens. The tokenizer's vocabulary determines what the model sees and affects efficiency across different languages and domains.

In the late 1870s, after completing Anna Karenina, Tolstoy underwent a profound religious and moral conversion that led him to renounce his earlier novels as frivolous. He turned to Christian anarchism, pacifism, and asceticism, producing philosophical tracts rather than fiction. His late stories, including *The Death of Ivan Ilyich*, represent a fusion of this moral seriousness with his novelistic gifts.

The causal influence of higher-level, more integrated systems on the behavior of the lower-level components that constitute them — the whole organizing the parts rather than only parts producing the whole. In biology, the body's global bioelectric state guiding individual cell division is a concrete example. Philosophically contested in strict reductionist frameworks but increasingly accepted in systems biology and philosophy of science.

The standard benchmark unit for an AI accelerator's raw throughput. One TOPS equals one trillion integer operations per second. Higher TOPS ratings generally mean faster inference for a given model size, though memory bandwidth and software optimization matter equally.

A design goal in mlx-vlm meaning that models and their processors should load and run using only the MLX stack, without requiring PyTorch to be installed. Since PyTorch is a large dependency with CUDA ties, removing it keeps the Mac-native environment lean and avoids version conflicts.

The total revenue a company could capture if it held 100 percent market share in a given segment. Used by executives and analysts as a shorthand for the ceiling on a business opportunity; AMD's $120 billion TAM projection for server CPUs by 2030 signals how dramatically they expect the segment to expand.

Google's proprietary line of AI accelerator ASICs, designed to accelerate the matrix-multiply operations at the core of deep-learning training and inference. TPU generations are numbered; the v7 (Ironwood) generation, entering production in 2026, uses a 3nm process node, HBM3E memory, and CoWoS-L advanced packaging. MediaTek is a production partner for the cost-optimised v7e variant.

The suite of bank instruments—letters of credit, guarantees, receivables financing—that bridge the gap between when a seller ships goods and when a buyer pays. In commodity markets, trade finance underpins nearly every large oil and metals transaction. When global trade volumes fall sharply, the working capital banks had deployed in these instruments returns to the financial system rather than being redeployed into new transactions.

The excess of a country's exports over its imports in value terms. A very large, persistent surplus — like China's $1.2 trillion in 2025 — reflects a structural gap between domestic production and consumption, and tends to export deflationary pressure alongside the goods themselves.

In the structure of Korean and Japanese industrial groups, a trading entity (or trading subsidiary) is a legally separate company that imports, distributes, and sells the parent's products in a specific territory. It manages local pricing, customs, and customer relationships, acting as the commercial face of the manufacturer in that market.

The total number of shares (or contracts) that change hands in a given security during a defined period. Volume is treated as a proxy for market conviction: high volume validates price moves; low volume on a directional move raises questions about the move's sustainability.

A 20th-century intellectual movement, associated with René Guénon, Frithjof Schuon, and Ananda Coomaraswamy, that argued all world religions share a single esoteric core, the philosophia perennis, and that their doctrinal differences are surface variations on one primordial metaphysical truth. Influential in esotericism and some strands of comparative religion; regarded with skepticism by mainstream academic historians of religion.

The percentage gain or loss of an asset over a defined lookback period ending today — for example, the trailing one-month return is the return over the past calendar month, and the trailing three-month return covers the prior quarter. Trailing returns are used to characterise the market environment that preceded a rally: deeply negative trailing returns suggest a recovery from distress; flat or mildly negative trailing returns alongside a large short-term gain are the hallmark of a melt-up or momentum-driven surge.

The phase of machine-learning development in which a model's parameters are iteratively adjusted against a large dataset. It is computationally intensive and GPU-heavy, typically requiring many GPUs per CPU in a cluster.

The images, text, or other content an AI model learns from during development. In image generation, the model studies millions of examples to learn how to produce visual output. The question of whether using copyrighted work as training data infringes copyright is actively contested in courts.

The total amount of work performed, typically measured as sets multiplied by reps multiplied by load. Research consistently shows that weekly volume — not the specific exercises chosen — is the primary driver of muscle growth, which is why a simple programme done consistently can outperform a complex one done sporadically.

In LingBot-Map's architecture, a learned compressed representation of all prior frames — roughly six tokens per frame — that the model attends to in order to maintain long-range spatial context. Functionally analogous to a SLAM system's keyframe graph but implemented as a differentiable attention mechanism.

A non-invasive brain stimulation method that delivers weak electrical currents — varying randomly in amplitude and frequency — to the scalp overlying a target brain region. The randomness is thought to avoid neural habituation and may enhance cortical excitability, making neurons easier to activate. It is distinct from tDCS (direct current) and TMS (magnetic pulses) and has fewer reported side effects than either at therapeutic doses.

A research program developed primarily at Anthropic for mechanistically analyzing the internal algorithms of transformer-based neural networks. It reverse-engineers attention heads, MLP layers, and residual streams to understand what computations models actually perform. Published work covers induction heads, superposition, and the structure of features inside large language models.

A neural network design introduced in the 2017 paper “Attention Is All You Need,” built around self-attention: a mechanism that lets each element in a sequence weigh all others simultaneously. Virtually all modern large language models, including GPT and Claude, are built on this architecture.

The US Treasury's primary account at the Federal Reserve, where tax revenues are deposited and from which government payments are made. Large drawdowns inject cash into the banking system and mechanically boost M2 even when monetary policy is unchanged, while rebuilds have the opposite effect — creating M2 swings that reflect fiscal dynamics, not global liquidity.

A systematic trading strategy that buys assets whose prices have been rising and sells (or shorts) assets whose prices have been falling, applied across multiple asset classes simultaneously. Also called managed futures or time-series momentum. The strategy is executed by algorithms rather than discretionary judgement.

A term coined by journalist David Roberts in 2017 to describe an information environment where truth is determined not by shared evidential standards but by what the tribe endorses. Under tribal epistemology, “good for our side” and “true” become operationally equivalent, and factual claims are evaluated by their source’s group membership, not their accuracy.

A specific word or token string that a LoRA adapter is trained to recognize in an image-generation prompt. When the phrase appears, the adapter activates its learned style or subject associations; without it, the adapter has minimal effect. Used to prevent unintended style bleed-in on prompts that don't call for the adapted look.

A preformed building block consisting of three RNA nucleotides joined in sequence, used by QT45 as a substrate for RNA synthesis. Using triplets rather than individual nucleotides makes copying faster and more accurate, though it raises questions about whether such substrates were available in prebiotic environments.

A phrase coined in a 2005 Deutsche Bank research report describing the unusual economics of academic publishing: the state funds the underlying research, pays the salaries of scientists who peer-review manuscripts for free, and then purchases the published output through library subscriptions — effectively paying three times for the same intellectual work.

A compositional rule set that divides an image or scene into three distinct panels — typically providing left-context, central focus, and right-resolution areas. Borrowed from classical painting and comics, it is used in generative AI tools to impose structural consistency across multi-panel outputs.

A wave whose surface profile traces the path of a point on the rim of a rolling circle (a trochoid). Closely related to Gerstner waves; the cross-section is asymmetric with a sharp crest and a broad trough, matching real deep-water wave profiles well.

The protein that assembles into microtubules. Each tubulin unit consists of an alpha and a beta subunit that can adopt different physical shapes — conformational states — depending on energy inputs. Hameroff's 1982 model treated each such state as the equivalent of a binary bit, with patterns propagating through the microtubule lattice like signals in a cellular automaton.

A mechanistic interpretability method that trains a small learned affine probe at each transformer layer to map that layer's hidden state into the model's output vocabulary space. The technique lets researchers read off what the model appears to be predicting at each intermediate processing step, treating each layer's activations as a dialect to be translated.

Light produced by incandescent tungsten-filament bulbs, characterized by a warm orange-amber color temperature (around 3200K). Associated with intimate, analogue-era interior scenes before LED lighting shifted the industry toward cooler, more neutral tones.

A state-sponsored pseudohistorical framework promoted by the Kemalist government at Turkey’s First Historical Congress in 1932, claiming that Turkic peoples originating in Central Asia spread civilization to China, India, the Balkans, and beyond. Its companion was the Sun Language Theory, which held that all human languages descended from a proto-Turkic original. Both were officially abandoned after Atatürk’s death in 1938 but created a lasting template for nationalist claims of Turkic civilizational primacy.

In an agentic AI system, a turn is one complete cycle of the model reading its context, reasoning, and issuing an action or tool call. Fewer turns mean lower latency and lower cost, since each turn typically incurs an API call.

The visual cadence created by the relationships between type sizes, weights, line heights, and spacing in a layout. Good typographic rhythm gives text a predictable, readable flow; poor rhythm makes a page feel cluttered or arbitrary even when individual choices seem reasonable in isolation.

The rate-limiting enzyme in catecholamine biosynthesis, responsible for converting tyrosine to L-DOPA. Because TyrH is subject to feedback inhibition by dopamine, providing more tyrosine substrate has a built-in ceiling: once dopamine is adequate, the enzyme throttles the reaction regardless of how much raw material is present.

A convolutional neural network architecture shaped like the letter U, widely used as the denoising backbone in earlier diffusion-based image generators such as Stable Diffusion. In image and video generation, DiT architectures have largely superseded it.

A U.S. government agency established in 2019 to provide loans, equity investments, and guarantees supporting private-sector projects abroad — and, increasingly, domestically. Unlike its predecessor (OPIC), the DFC's charter explicitly authorizes it to take minority equity stakes in companies, making it the legal workhorse for some of the administration's minerals investments.

The discipline of driving new users to a product through paid and organic channels. In mobile apps, UA typically means buying ads on platforms like Facebook, TikTok, or Apple Search Ads to generate app installs at an acceptable cost per install.

The reduced, active form of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), a lipid-soluble molecule that shuttles electrons between complexes in the electron transport chain and also acts as a cellular antioxidant. Ubiquinol is generally considered better absorbed than standard oxidized CoQ10 supplements.

UGC stands for user-generated content — here, short selfie-style video ads made by ordinary creators rather than ad agencies. The 'arbitrage' is a price gap: these videos cost far less to produce than studio ads but often convert at comparable or superior rates, making the effective cost per result substantially cheaper.

A short, attention-grabbing video opener modelled on *user-generated content* — the casual, first-person format that drives high engagement on TikTok and Reels. In AI marketing tools, 'hook' templates are pre-engineered prompts that produce this aesthetic on demand.

Towa's proprietary adaptation of Mold Underfill for HBM4, where the inter-die gaps are narrower than in previous generations. The challenge is forcing viscous resin into sub-millimeter spaces without leaving voids that would later cause structural failure. Towa announced commercial availability of this technology for its CPM Series compression molding machines in August 2025.

An unshipped Claude Code feature discovered in the leaked source that strips internal Anthropic codenames and identifying markers from AI-authored git commits. Its source comment states the purpose is preventing model codename leaks in external-repository commits.

In tax law, income derived from capital, investments, or property rather than from direct labor — dividends, rent, interest, capital gains. In Simak's story, the government classifies the economic output of self-replicating robots as the owner's unearned income, triggering a tax liability he never anticipated. The concept is directly relevant to contemporary debates about how to tax AI-generated economic value.

A six-level classification system for assessing how threatened a language is: Safe, Vulnerable, Definitely Endangered, Severely Endangered, Critically Endangered, and Extinct. Introduced in the 2010 UNESCO Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger, it is the standard framework for language vitality assessment.

A contiguous range of codepoints in the Unicode standard assigned to a related group of characters — for example, “Basic Latin,” “Dingbats,” or “CJK Unified Ideographs.” Blocks are the primary organizational axis of conventional Unicode browsers, grouping characters by script or functional category rather than by appearance.

Characters from non-Latin Unicode code pages that are visually identical or very similar to standard ASCII letters. Substituting them into sensitive words can fool surface-level text classifiers while remaining readable to a model that processes semantic meaning rather than raw character codes.

A service that consolidates access to multiple third-party AI models — image generators, video synthesizers, language models — under one subscription and interface. The value proposition is reduced cost and friction compared to subscribing to each model provider separately.

A prompt or interaction sequence that systematically bypasses an AI model's built-in content refusals across a broad range of restricted topics or request types. 'Universal' distinguishes it from narrow workarounds that defeat only a single content category — it defeats the model's entire safety-filter stack within scope.

A legal claim asserting that a defendant improperly benefited at the plaintiff's expense without legal justification, and that a court should order restitution. Musk argues that OpenAI's shift to a for-profit structure allowed insiders to collect enormous stock grants funded by what were originally charitable contributions.

The increase in value of an asset that has not yet been sold. An unrealized gain exists only on paper and can evaporate if prices fall before the position is liquidated. In the government's case the problem is compounded: selling a 9.9% stake in a major public company would itself move the market and carry significant political costs.

Raw digital information that has not been organized into a predefined format—free text, images, audio, social media posts—as opposed to structured data arranged neatly in database rows and columns. Extracting meaning from it requires additional processing steps, which is why “transforming” it is treated as the analyst’s central task.

Options trades that are anomalous in size, strike price, or timing relative to a stock's historical norms — used as a proxy for informed or institutional positioning, though most such trades turn out to be hedges or portfolio management rather than evidence of privileged information.

Uber's pricing model, introduced broadly in 2022–23, that sets the passenger's fare and the driver's pay via separate algorithms rather than deriving both from a shared metered rate. The decoupling allows Uber to widen its margin without formally raising its commission percentage, and makes the split invisible to both parties — drivers are barred from asking what passengers paid.

A Norwegian multiplier applied to dividends and capital gains from shares before the standard 22 percent income-tax rate is applied. With the factor set at 1.72, the effective tax rate on equity income reaches roughly 37.8 percent, designed to equalise the tax treatment of labour and capital income.

The rearing Egyptian cobra (*Naja naja* or related species) depicted in Egyptian, Phoenician, and Canaanite iconography as a royal and divine guardian, often winged and crowned. The symbol was adopted onto Judahite royal seals in the 9th–7th centuries BCE, where four-winged uraei flanking thrones are the closest visual parallel to Isaiah's seraphim.

A stretch of connected habitat — parks, hillsides, creek beds, or even freeway underpasses — that allows animals to move through an otherwise built-up environment. The Santa Monica Mountains function as the backbone of LA's corridor, linking the Simi Hills to the Pacific coast and funneling wildlife into surrounding neighborhoods.

A nitrogen-rich synthetic fertilizer produced from natural gas via the Haber-Bosch process. It is the world's most traded nitrogen fertilizer by volume and a benchmark for global fertilizer pricing. Urea prices move closely with natural gas costs and are a leading indicator of food-production input inflation.

A metabolite produced by gut bacteria when they ferment polyphenols (ellagitannins) found in pomegranates, walnuts, and berries. Because production depends on individual gut microbiome composition, most people cannot make meaningful amounts from diet alone, driving interest in direct supplementation.

A bridged version of USD Coin (USDC), a dollar-pegged stablecoin. 'Bridged' means the tokens were transferred from Ethereum to Polygon via a cross-chain bridge, taking on the .e suffix to distinguish them from native-chain USDC. Polymarket denominated all trades in USDC.e, making positions effectively dollar-denominated.

macOS's built-in key-value store for application and system preferences, backed by .plist files in ~/Library/Preferences/. The `defaults` command-line tool lets you read, write, and delete these values without opening any GUI — including values the GUI doesn't expose at all.

A distinction from Augustine of Hippo (354–430 CE), founder of the Augustinian order to which Leo XIV belongs: uti (Latin: to use) means treating something as a means to another end; frui (to delight in, to enjoy) means treating something as an end in itself, worthy of love for its own sake. Augustine held that treating a person as merely a means — as a uti object — when they deserve frui is a foundational moral error.

The formal process by which a new power customer — a factory, data centre, or housing development — applies to connect to the electrical grid. Utilities process requests in sequence; in congested U.S. markets the queue stretches two to three years, during which the applicant cannot draw grid power.

The process of cutting open a 3D mesh along designated seams and flattening it onto a 2D plane, creating a UV map. The U and V axes refer to the horizontal and vertical dimensions of that 2D space — distinct from the X, Y, Z of 3D space. The map tells the renderer which pixel of a texture image corresponds to which point on the object's surface.

A code-generation tool built by Vercel that produces front-end UI code from natural-language prompts. It targets product builders who want to scaffold interfaces quickly without writing boilerplate HTML, CSS, or React components by hand, and has become a common starting point in the “vibe coding” workflow popular in practitioner communities.

A measure of the activity level of the vagus nerve, the main conduit of the parasympathetic ('rest and digest') branch of the autonomic nervous system. Higher vagal tone is associated with lower resting heart rate, greater HRV, and better stress regulation. Slow breathing reliably increases it by amplifying the baroreflex loop.

In Bennett's framework, the primitive good/bad or attract/repel quality present in any adaptive system — from bacteria responding to nutrients to humans feeling pleasure or pain. He treats valence as primary, not derived from neural mechanisms, and argues it is the foundational unit from which all consciousness is built up.

A ratio that relates a company's market value to a financial measure such as revenue, EBITDA, or earnings, allowing comparisons across companies and over time. Common multiples include EV/EBITDA (enterprise value divided by earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) and EV/revenue. A higher multiple signals that investors are paying a premium for expected future growth or monopoly durability; Soitec's current P/E of roughly 480x is effectively meaningless, making EV/revenue and forward EV/EBITDA the operative lenses.

A stock that appears cheap by conventional metrics — low price relative to earnings or book value — but continues to decline because the underlying business is structurally impaired. Investors who buy expecting a rebound find themselves holding a deteriorating asset.

Dealer hedging adjustments triggered by changes in implied volatility. Vanna measures how much a dealer's delta (directional equity exposure) shifts when volatility moves; when IV falls sharply, dealers who sold puts reduce their short equity hedges, mechanically lifting share prices — a 'vol crush rally' — independent of any fundamental buyer.

An internet-born aesthetic and music microgenre from the early 2010s defined by pastel colors, glitch effects, retro-digital imagery, and ironic nostalgia for 1980s–90s consumer capitalism. Gulf Futurism's founders borrowed its sensibility to estrange the Gulf cityscape.

A reward schedule in which a behaviour is reinforced after an unpredictable number of repetitions — the same mechanism that makes slot machines so persistent. Social media feeds use this structure: you scroll not knowing when the next rewarding post will appear, maximising engagement via dopaminergic reward circuits.

A database structure that stores text as numerical embeddings — points in high-dimensional space — and retrieves them by semantic similarity rather than exact keyword match. OpenClaw uses a SQLite-backed vector index to let the assistant surface relevant memories from past conversations even when the user does not recall the precise words used.

The older term for the autonomic nervous system — the involuntary circuitry governing breathing, heart rate, digestion, and the stress-and-relaxation cycle. Reich named his therapy after this system because he believed blocked emotion manifested as chronic dysregulation there, and that vegetative pulsation (expansion and contraction) was the fundamental rhythm of life.

Reich's body-based extension of psychoanalysis, named for the vegetative (autonomic) nervous system. It expanded the therapy session beyond verbal interpretation to include work directly on the body: deep breathing, palpation of tense areas, and the encouragement of involuntary movement and emotional release. It is the direct clinical ancestor of SKAN and most neo-Reichian traditions.

An arrangement in which a supplier extends credit or equity investment to help a customer purchase its own products or services. Common in capital-intensive industries (aircraft, automobiles), it can be legitimate market-building or a warning sign that organic demand is insufficient to sustain the supplier's revenue at current levels.

A set of brain regions — including the temporoparietal junction and the right inferior frontal cortex — that activates in response to unexpected or behaviourally relevant stimuli. It is the brain’s salience or surprise circuit. High predicted activation here is what some creators interpret as evidence that a video will catch and hold a viewer’s attention.

An on-chain perpetual-futures platform built on Hyperliquid's order-book infrastructure that allows traders to take leveraged positions on the implied valuations of private, pre-IPO companies such as Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX. Contracts are denominated in Valuation Units (a company's implied valuation divided by one billion) and settled in USDH, a dollar-pegged stablecoin. Ownership of a Ventuals position confers no equity stake in the underlying company.

A firm that builds multiple startups in-house rather than investing in externally pitched ones. Unlike a traditional accelerator or VC fund, a venture studio co-founds companies from scratch, supplies operational resources, and takes founding equity — functioning simultaneously as investor and operator.

A video-generation model from Google DeepMind, released in 2025, that synthesizes short video clips — including synchronized audio and dialogue — from text or structured prompts. The 'Fast' variant is optimized for speed over maximum quality.

Google DeepMind's video-generation model, used within the Replit Animation pipeline to supply any live-action video segments embedded in an otherwise code-generated output. It is part of the broader Google model stack that Replit accesses under its Google Cloud partnership.

Google DeepMind's third-generation video model, announced at Google I/O in May 2025. Its primary innovation was native audio generation: characters can speak dialogue and ambient sound tracks match the visual scene, making it one of the first broadly accessible models to attempt the full audiovisual stack from a single text prompt.

Nvidia's next-generation AI accelerator platform, succeeding the Blackwell architecture. Vera Rubin integrates HBM4 memory and targets large-scale AI training and inference workloads in data centers. SK hynix has been confirmed as the primary HBM4 memory supplier for the platform, expected to begin mass production in 2026.

An approach to AI memory that saves the full, unedited text of conversations rather than extracting summaries or key facts. The rationale is that AI summarization discards reasoning and nuance; verbatim storage trades storage efficiency for retrieval completeness, deferring the compression decision to search time.

The number of individual points that define a 3D model's surface. Higher counts mean more detail but greater computational cost. A film-quality asset might use millions of vertices; a real-time game character typically targets tens of thousands to stay within GPU budgets.

A technique in which the vertex shader moves mesh vertices away from their rest positions — typically driven by noise or trigonometric wave functions — to simulate organic animation such as tree sway, flag flutter, or water surface movement without requiring additional geometry.

A named selection of vertices on a mesh, each assigned a weight between 0 and 1. Physics modifiers read these weights to vary properties like cloth stiffness or pinning strength across different parts of a garment.

One of the two fundamental shader types in the WebGL pipeline. Runs once per vertex — each corner point of a 3D mesh — transforming world coordinates into screen positions. Can also displace vertices to animate geometry, as in tree-sway or wave effects.

A corporate strategy in which a company owns or controls multiple stages of its supply chain; Rocket Lab has pursued this by manufacturing its own engines, avionics, spacecraft components, and satellites rather than relying on third-party suppliers.

Vicor's patented power architecture in which a current-multiplier module mounts directly beneath a processor on the underside of a circuit board and delivers current vertically into the chip face, rather than routing it laterally across the board. This eliminates the resistive and inductive losses of conventional power distribution and becomes critical as chip voltages fall below 1 volt and current demands climb into the tens of thousands of amperes per die.

A 1.2-billion-parameter transformer from Meta's Visual Geometry Group at Oxford that won Best Paper at CVPR 2025. Given a set of images, it predicts camera intrinsics, extrinsics, depth maps, and 3D point tracks in a single forward pass — but requires all frames to be in memory at once.

A post-processing effect that mimics the visual artifacts of analog video tape: horizontal line displacement, vertical roll, and grain noise. In Three.js it is typically implemented as a ShaderPass using procedural noise. Pieter Levels used a variant in Drones of War to simulate FPV signal degradation with distance.

Contemporary vernacular for the degradation or disappearance of a shared ambient emotional texture — the background quality of life that makes a place, era, or community feel a certain way. Used here at planetary scale to suggest that modern conditions have destroyed the atmospheric preconditions for a particular quality of inner life.

A practice — and a brand term used by this platform — for delegating marketing execution (copy, research, analysis) to AI agents through natural-language instruction, with the human directing strategy rather than doing the work. It borrows the framing of 'vibe coding,' in which developers describe what they want built and the AI writes the code.

Casual, intuition-driven mathematical exploration using AI tools without deep subject expertise or methodical strategy — feeding problems into a model to see what happens. Adapted from 'vibe coding,' coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025 for AI-guided programming by feel rather than comprehension.

A phrase coined by Pieter Levels in response to Zo.computer’s launch, extending ‘vibe coding’ down the stack to server infrastructure. The idea is that AI-native cloud environments can absorb operational complexity — provisioning, deployment, routing — so builders can stay focused on building rather than on how their code runs.

A term coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy for a style of software development in which a user describes desired functionality in natural language and an AI model generates the code. It lowers the entry barrier to shipping working software dramatically, though it works best for simple or prototype-scale applications and struggles with complex, large-scale, or security-sensitive systems.

A generative neural network that learns to produce video by iteratively removing noise from a random signal, guided by a text or image prompt. Diffusion models have become the dominant architecture for high-quality AI image and video synthesis because they allow fine-grained control over the output through the denoising schedule.

A computer-vision technique that selectively reconstructs or replaces a defined region within a video frame—a specific object, person, or background area—while leaving surrounding pixels intact across all affected frames. It extends image-editing inpainting to the temporal dimension, ensuring changes look consistent over time rather than flickering.

A generation mode in which an existing video clip serves as structural input rather than a blank canvas. The model retransforms the source footage — altering appearance, environment, or characters — while using the original as a guide for motion, timing, and spatial layout.

A class of AI technique that takes existing video footage as input and produces transformed footage as output, rather than generating video from scratch. The structure of the original clip is preserved as a scaffold for the new output — sitting between a simple filter and full generation.

The gradual darkening of an image toward its edges and corners, caused by the geometry of a camera lens reducing the available light cone at the periphery of the sensor. In multi-camera 3DGS captures, uncorrected vignetting causes the reconstruction to misinterpret edge-of-frame brightness drops as scene geometry.

Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite — a multispectral sensor aboard the Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20/21 satellites that detects mid-infrared radiation emitted by fires and other heat sources at a spatial resolution of 375 meters per pixel. VIIRS data forms the backbone of NASA FIRMS and is significantly more sensitive at night and for small fires than its predecessor, MODIS.

A form of silent Buddhist insight meditation, typically practiced in ten-day residential retreats. Participants observe a strict code of silence, meditate up to ten hours daily, and abstain from reading, writing, and devices. The word means ‘seeing things as they really are’ in Pali.

In Spark's usage, a technique borrowed from operating-system design: a fixed pool of GPU memory is pre-allocated and divided into pages, and the renderer swaps pages in and out using a least-recently-used strategy as the user navigates. This allows exploration of scenes far larger than the GPU's physical memory, in the same way an OS allows programs to use more RAM than is physically present.

A live-stream performer who appears on screen as an animated 3D or 2D character rather than as their physical self, typically using real-time motion capture for face and body. The category overlaps with 'VTuber' (virtual YouTuber) and has grown into a distinct entertainment genre with its own audience and conventions.

A tradition in moral philosophy, originating with Aristotle, that defines good character as a set of stable dispositions built through repeated practice — particularly through facing difficulty and choosing well when it is costly. On this view, character is not what a person claims but what they habitually do, especially under stress.

A neural network architecture, adapted from the transformer models used in NLP, that divides an image into fixed-size patches and processes them with self-attention. SAM 3.1 uses a ViT as its primary image encoder; it is the most computationally expensive component and the target of backbone caching optimizations.

Variant’s term for the compound aesthetic signature of a design — the simultaneous combination of color scheme, typographic rhythm, and spatial density that together create a coherent visual identity. The metaphor implies that style, like genetics, is a structured, extractable system rather than an ineffable intuition.

The gradual, unintended change in the appearance of subjects — faces, objects, colors — as a generative model produces successive frames independently. Controlling drift is a central challenge in AI-assisted video and storyboard production.

A localization technology that estimates a device's precise position and orientation by matching a live camera image against a database of georegistered reference photographs. Unlike GPS, which achieves roughly 3–5 metre accuracy and fails indoors, VPS can reach centimetre-level accuracy and functions inside buildings, making it useful for AR content anchoring, indoor navigation, and robot localization in GPS-denied environments.

A design process in which visual output is produced and evaluated before any code is written. The designer explores options at the layout and aesthetic level, selects a direction, and only then hands off to implementation. Contrasts with prompt-driven workflows where code generation precedes visual review.

The shape of the VIX futures curve. In contango — the normal state — futures prices for later months are higher than near-term futures, reflecting mean-reversion expectations (volatility usually falls back toward its average). In backwardation, near-term futures trade above later ones, typically during acute stress events when investors expect near-term fear to subside quickly.

Virtual Motion Capture protocol — a lightweight, open messaging standard (transmitted over UDP) originally developed for Japanese virtual-streamer workflows. It encodes skeleton bone positions and rotations as OSC (Open Sound Control) messages, allowing different applications to share live pose data in real time.

A Blender add-on that acts as a VMC protocol receiver, translating incoming skeleton data from an external capture application into bone rotations on a Blender armature. It serves as the bridge between CyanPuppets' standalone capture software and Blender's animation system.

The binary animation file format native to MikuMikuDance. It stores bone keyframes — position, rotation quaternion, and Bézier interpolation parameters — along with morph and camera keyframes, with bone names encoded in Shift-JIS Japanese text. VMD files are freely shared throughout the MMD creator community.

Virtual Network Computing — a protocol for viewing and interacting with a remote graphical desktop environment over a network connection. VNC transmits screen images and accepts mouse and keyboard input, letting AI agents that support computer-use capabilities see and control a full desktop interface running on a distant machine.

A unit of implied volatility equal to one percentage point of annualized vol. A spread of -9.61 vol points means the Mag 7 basket's upside implied vol is 9.61 percentage points below the comparison group's — a large and historically extreme difference.

The difference in implied volatility between two securities, baskets, or market segments. Traders can position for a vol spread to converge toward its historical average — buying the relatively cheaper implied vol and selling the relatively more expensive. Goldman Sachs's chart measures the Mag 7 vs. NDX single-stock upside vol spread going back to 2014.

A market-neutral strategy that bets on the gap between an option’s implied volatility and a trader’s forecast of realized volatility. The directional exposure is hedged away; the position profits (or loses) based purely on whether the volatility gap closes in the expected direction.

See 'leveraged ETF decay.' In the specific context of the Gayed/Bilello paper, volatility drag is reframed as a conditional risk: not an inherent tax on all leveraged positions, but a function of the volatility level at the time leverage is applied. Low-volatility trending markets generate positive compounding effects; high-volatility choppy markets generate negative ones.

The parameter governing how rapidly implied volatility itself fluctuates. In the SABR stochastic-volatility model — widely used by rates and equity-options desks — a higher vol-of-vol produces a more sharply curved (or "winged") implied-volatility surface. In Dean's curvature formula, a higher ν/σ₀ ratio pushes K_eff more negative, deepening the frown.
