A persistent state of the market characterized by a particular level and behavior of volatility — e.g., a 'low-vol regime' where daily price swings are small and stable, versus a 'high-vol regime' following a shock. Identifying regime transitions in advance is a core aim of volatility trading.

The pattern observed when implied volatility — the volatility figure that makes Black-Scholes reproduce a market option price — is plotted against strike price. Rather than the flat line Black-Scholes predicts, it typically forms a curve: higher implied vol at out-of-the-money strikes on both sides (a "smile") or, for equity indices, a downward slope toward higher strikes (a "skew" or, in Dean's terminology, a "frown").

A three-dimensional plot of implied volatility across different strike prices and expiration dates for options on the same underlying. In theory it would be flat; in practice it curves into smiles, skews, and term structures reflecting crash risk, event uncertainty, and supply-demand imbalances. Managing and modeling the surface is the central activity of a derivatives desk.

Borretti’s metaphor for cognitive capacity: rather than a battery that depletes uniformly, he frames mental energy as voltage — a measure of what tasks are currently within reach. High-voltage states (early morning, post-medication) can power demanding or aversive work; low-voltage states can only sustain routine tasks.

A trading signal based on whether a stock's recent trading volume is rising relative to its longer-term average. A high 60-day-to-200-day volume ratio is interpreted as evidence of accumulation by institutional buyers, signaling potential future price appreciation.

A filming technique using a large array of cameras arranged around a subject to record it from every angle simultaneously. The footage is processed into a 3D or 4D representation — such as a Gaussian splat or a mesh — that viewers can inspect from any vantage point.

A Markov process on the integers where, starting from n, the chain moves to n/q with probability Λ(q)/log n for each divisor q. Because the weights sum exactly to 1 (due to ∑Λ(d) = log n) and the Erdős weight is sub-invariant under this chain, it yields the desired bound on primitive sets without the e^γ losses that plagued the Mertens approach.

A function Λ(n) in analytic number theory equal to log p if n is a power of a prime p, and zero otherwise. Available since the 1880s, it encodes prime factorization through the identity ∑_{d|n} Λ(d) = log n — precisely the property that makes it useful in the new proof.

A measure of the internal three-dimensional grid — *voxels* being the 3D equivalent of pixels — used during AI model generation. A 1536³ grid means 1536 units along each axis, giving finer detail capture than lower-resolution generation stages.

A 2023 research system from Caltech and NVIDIA that demonstrated open-ended, lifelong learning in Minecraft by maintaining an ever-growing library of executable JavaScript skills, each stored with a natural-language description and retrieved by semantic similarity. Voyager is append-only — it does not rewrite or delete existing skills — and served as an influential proof-of-concept for the skill-library paradigm.

Virtual private server: a rented partition of a physical server, accessible over the internet, running its own operating system. Entry-level plans start around $5 per month and are sufficient for lightweight background software like an AI agent gateway.

An open file format for humanoid 3D avatars built on the glTF 2.0 standard, maintained by the VRM Consortium and favored by the VTuber and virtual-avatar industry. It is a browser-friendly, standardized alternative to proprietary formats like PMX, with a companion animation format called VRMA.

Vicor's current-multiplier chip that converts an intermediate bus voltage — typically 48 volts — to the sub-1-volt level a processor requires, while multiplying the delivered current by up to 40 times. In the VPD architecture the VTM is packaged in a 1.5mm-thick module and mounts on the underside of a circuit board directly beneath the processor die, minimising the distance current must travel after voltage transformation.

Short for Virtual YouTuber: a content creator who performs as a real-time animated digital avatar, typically driven by motion-capture hardware that maps the performer's body movements onto the character. Originating in Japan around 2016, the format has grown into a global industry.

A sapient humanoid species in *Star Trek* whose society is organized around the complete suppression of emotion in favor of pure logic. Vulcans are highly capable and intellectually formidable, but their affect is cold and their style direct to the point of bluntness — a science-fiction archetype for rational, unsentimental intelligence.

The average price at which a security has traded throughout a session, weighted by volume at each price level. Unlike a simple moving average, VWAP incorporates actual transactional activity, making it a more structurally informative benchmark. Institutional desks often use VWAP as a reference for execution quality; retail traders sometimes use its slope as a trend-confirmation filter to reduce false signals from price-only indicators like the EMA.

Bennett's proposed optimization principle: prefer the hypothesis consistent with the greatest number of possible worlds, rather than the shortest. He argues this generalizes better than compression-based approaches and reports large empirical gains on benchmark tasks. It directly contests the Occam's razor intuition that underlies most of machine learning.

The number of standard commodity memory wafers that must be consumed to produce one wafer’s worth of a more advanced product. Because HBM stacks require additional process steps, tighter yields, and more complex bonding than plain DRAM, converting wafer capacity to HBM requires roughly three times the raw silicon input per unit. This means ramping HBM production simultaneously tightens supply of conventional DRAM, supporting pricing across both markets.

An AI processor built from an entire silicon wafer rather than individual chips diced from it. By eliminating inter-chip boundaries, a WSE removes communication bottlenecks but generates extraordinary power density in the process. Cerebras Systems' CS-3 system draws approximately 23 kilowatts per unit — creating the exact current-delivery challenge Vicor's VPD architecture is engineered to solve.

A chip-design approach in which the entire silicon wafer — rather than individual dies cut from it — is treated as one device. This maximises transistor count and on-chip interconnect bandwidth at the cost of yield-management complexity. Cerebras's WSE-3 is the leading commercial example, at ~46,000 mm² compared to ~800 mm² for a typical GPU die.

An Arabic Sufi term meaning 'ecstasy' or 'finding,' describing the acute, temporary spiritual state in which a sudden overwhelming sensation descends on the heart and annihilates self-awareness. Classical Sufi manuals distinguish it from tawājud (deliberately seeking the state) and wujūd (pure being/finding — the highest stage). It is the event; walah is the condition.

A mode of influence that does not require inducing a trance. Instead, it uses carefully chosen language — pacing, reframing, embedded suggestions — to shift a subject's mood or beliefs while they remain fully alert. Adams treated it as a subset of persuasion technique rather than a clinical intervention.

Gurdjieff's term for the default condition of ordinary human consciousness: a semi-hypnotic, mechanical state in which people believe themselves awake and self-aware but are in fact operating on autopilot, driven by conditioning and habit. He held that genuine wakefulness is exceptional and must be deliberately cultivated through specific practices, foremost among them self-remembering.

An Arabic word (root w-l-h) for overwhelming love-bewilderment, in which the lover is so consumed by the Beloved that they lose their bearings entirely. It encompasses both ecstatic joy and anguished longing and is used in classical Sufi taxonomies to describe an advanced spiritual state surpassing ordinary ecstasy. A person in this state is called wālih — someone whose rational faculties have been displaced by love.

A temporal cross-validation technique for financial models. Instead of a single train/test split, the researcher trains on a historical window, tests on the next period, then advances both windows forward — repeating across many periods. This mimics how a strategy would be deployed in real time and is more rigorous than a single out-of-sample test.

A fast orthogonal linear transform that maps a vector into a basis of ±1 coefficients. In quantization, applying a randomized WHT rotation before compressing serves to spread energy evenly across all coordinates, reducing worst-case quantization error without requiring storage of the rotation matrix.

A speculative cosmological system developed by American autodidact Walter Russell (1871–1963), claiming that matter is organized into 'tonal octaves' governed by a universal wave motion and that the universe is fundamentally musical and spiritual in structure. Russell claimed his insights came through 'cosmic illumination.' His theories are not recognized in mainstream physics, chemistry, or philosophy of science.

A text-to-video model developed from Alibaba's Wan-Video research lineage, integrated into the Higgsfield platform. Higgsfield markets WAN 2.5 as permitting generation of real brand logos, products, and celebrity likenesses — restrictions that Google's Veo and other models enforce. It accepts JSON-structured prompts and generates video with native audio.

Alibaba's internal evaluation benchmark for video generation models, used to compare Wan 2.2 against both open-source and closed-source alternatives. As a first-party benchmark, its results should be treated with the caution typically applied to vendor-reported performance figures.

A strategic framework developed by Simon Wardley that plots components of a value chain against an evolution axis running from novel (genesis) through custom-built to commodity. It is used to identify where a firm's internal assumptions about which capabilities are strategic versus routine diverge from market reality — the same diagnostic intent as ArbitrageDiscover's custom/commodity/reference axis.

A contract giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to purchase shares in a company at a specified price before a specified expiration date. The government frequently received warrants alongside direct equity purchases, granting options to increase its stakes if certain conditions — such as a company changing control — are triggered.

In sweriko's breaking-waves demo, the runtime component that schedules and positions individual breaking-wave events on top of the FFT ocean. Each event is a time-parameterised geometry sequence that suppresses the underlying height-field surface within its footprint and substitutes the parametric breaking geometry.

A technique for transmitting multiple independent optical signals simultaneously over a single fiber strand by assigning each signal a different wavelength of light. CWDM (coarse) and DWDM (dense) variants differ in channel spacing and total capacity; both are core products for optical networking companies like Smartoptics.

An annual levy on a person's net assets — the total market value of everything they own minus any debts — rather than on income earned during the year. Norway's version, called formuesskatt, applies at 1.1 percent to net assets above a threshold of roughly NKr1.7 million (~$160,000).

Writing or art designed to use the browser's specific properties — hyperlinks, CSS animation, real-time network connections, cursor events — as expressive tools, not just as delivery infrastructure. The work changes or breaks if moved to print or another medium.

A font license that permits a typeface to be embedded in a website’s CSS and served to visitors’ browsers via @font-face, typically priced per domain or per monthly pageview. A webfont license does not authorize installing the font file locally or using it in desktop design applications such as Figma or InDesign — that requires a separate desktop license, sold at a different price point.

The second version of the Web Graphics Library, a JavaScript API that gives web browsers direct access to the GPU for rendering 2D and 3D graphics without plugins. It is supported natively by all major modern browsers and is the standard foundation for in-browser 3D applications.

WebSocket is a network protocol that upgrades an HTTP connection into a persistent, full-duplex channel over a single TCP socket. Unlike ordinary HTTP, where the client must ask and the server must respond, WebSocket lets the server push data to the browser continuously — suitable for streaming real-time simulation state.

An attack in which a malicious website opens a connection to a locally running WebSocket server through the victim's browser, bypassing network firewalls because the request originates from the local machine. In OpenClaw's case, a disclosed vulnerability allowed external sites to issue commands to a running agent on its local gateway port.

A compression technique that represents each weight using fewer bits (e.g., 4-bit integers instead of 16-bit floats). This shrinks file size and memory footprint dramatically, often with minimal accuracy loss, allowing large models to run on consumer hardware.

An Olmec artistic and religious motif depicting a human-jaguar hybrid — typically a figure with a cleft head, a toothless or fang-bearing mouth, and feline features. Scholars interpret it as a rain deity or a shaman in transformation. Its superficial resemblance to the Chinese taotie mask has fueled — and been refuted by — transpacific contact theories.

A genre of figurative painting depicting the landscapes, peoples, and culture of the American West — principally cowboys, Native Americans, horses, and desert or mountain terrain. The tradition descends from Frederic Remington and Charles Russell in the late nineteenth century and is sustained today by dedicated galleries, auction houses, and museums.

A C/C++ port of OpenAI's Whisper automatic speech recognition model, optimized for local inference on CPUs and embedded hardware. Used in yacineMTB's talk project as the transcription layer in a fully local voice AI pipeline.

A security assessment method in which the tester has full access to internal artifacts — source code, architecture diagrams, credentials — before beginning. Contrasted with black-box testing, where the system is probed with no prior knowledge. White-box access lets an AI agent trace vulnerabilities directly to their code origin rather than guessing from external behavior.

In VFX parlance, whitewater refers collectively to the secondary fluid elements generated by a churning liquid surface: foam (trapped air at the surface), spray (airborne droplets), and subsurface bubbles. Simulating all three within a single integrated solver — rather than as separate post-process passes — is technically demanding and is one of HydroFX's headline features.

A proposed technology to scan a biological brain at sufficient resolution and instantiate an exact functional replica in a digital substrate — colloquially 'mind uploading.' The project presupposes that mental continuity is constituted by functional organization, not by the biological original, making it philosophically dependent on functionalism being true.

New York General Municipal Law §101, which requires public building projects above a dollar threshold to retain four separate prime contractors — general construction, plumbing, HVAC, and electrical — none with authority over the others. Because coordination must happen through the owner rather than a single general contractor, scheduling conflicts, duplicated overhead, and procurement delays routinely add 15 to 30 percent to project cost.

The percentage of historical episodes in a given lookback where the market was higher at the end of the measurement period. A win rate of 72% at 1-year means the index closed higher one year later in 72 of 100 comparable historical setups.

The macOS daemon responsible for rendering all on-screen graphics and managing input events. It reads keyboard-timing preferences at user login and applies them for the duration of the session, which is why a logout-and-login is required for `defaults write` changes to take effect.

A modern, open-source tunneling protocol underpinning Tailscale and several other VPN products. WireGuard uses state-of-the-art cryptography, has a small codebase (roughly 4,000 lines), and establishes connections faster than older protocols like OpenVPN or IPSec. Tailscale adds its device-discovery and key-management layer on top of WireGuard's encrypted tunnels.

Web Open Font Format 2, the dominant file format for web fonts, using Brotli compression to deliver typefaces roughly 30% more efficiently than its predecessor WOFF. Browsers download WOFF2 files as ordinary HTTP assets when rendering pages that call for custom typefaces; the file’s URL is written explicitly in the page’s CSS. WOFF, TTF, and OTF are older or alternative formats serving similar purposes.

Stephen Wolfram's ongoing research program proposing that the universe is generated by a single evolving hypergraph — a network of abstract nodes governed by update rules — from which space, time, and all physical laws emerge as emergent properties. It is a formal attempt to find the computational substrate beneath fundamental physics.

A metric borrowed from speech recognition that, in the talking-head context, measures how often a video’s generated lip movements diverge from the spoken words — assessed by running an automated lip-reading model on the output. A lower WER indicates tighter audio-visual synchrony; daVinci-MagiHuman’s 14.60 percent compares favourably to Ovi 1.1’s 40.45 percent.

An art-market and curatorial category encompassing drawings, prints, watercolours, gouaches, and mixed-media pieces on a paper or card support, as opposed to oil paintings on canvas. Works on paper by the same artist typically occupy a lower price tier at auction than their painted counterparts, though they can offer comparable artistic density and intimacy.

A directory of Markdown files that collectively define an OpenClaw agent's identity, memory, and operating rules. The gateway reads all files on every session and injects their contents into the system prompt before any user message. There is no database — the files are the agent.

The practice of keeping an AI agent's workspace files clean, consistent, and token-efficient. Analogous to code linting or database maintenance: the absence of hygiene does not immediately break the system but degrades performance and raises costs over time.

Google's opt-in experimental feature channel for Google Workspace subscribers, where new capabilities are tested before reaching general availability. Users who opt in may encounter features that are still being refined and could change or be withdrawn.

Large AI systems trained to predict how an environment will evolve over time given an action — essentially an internalized physics simulator. They are considered a key component of general-purpose robots and autonomous agents because they allow planning without constant real-world feedback.

Created before the body of the cosmos, the World Soul is a harmonic mixture of Being, Sameness, and Difference divided into bands arranged according to Pythagorean musical ratios, forming intersecting circles that drive the rotation of the heavens. It is simultaneously the source of cosmic intelligence and the mechanism of celestial motion — rational rotation built into the physical structure of the universe.

An AI video technique that replaces the environment, setting, or overall visual style of a shot while leaving the subject's motion and framing intact. A clip shot in a garage can be rendered as if filmed in a spaceship, with camera angles and character positions unchanged.

Charlie Munger's term for the kind of broad, cross-disciplinary knowledge that produces sound judgment. Distinct from narrow expertise, it requires learning the 'big ideas' across many fields and developing the pattern-recognition to apply them in novel situations.

A texture, usually a normal map, that encodes the surface detail of folded or creased skin. In animation, multiple wrinkle maps are blended together at runtime based on joint angles or muscle activation, so the character appears to develop creases as it moves. The maps must be painted by hand for each pose, which makes extensive coverage time-consuming.

A central Daoist concept (無為), literally ‘non-action’ or ‘effortless action.’ Not passivity, but action that aligns with natural patterns rather than imposing force. The ideal is to move with the grain of situations — to time and attune rather than will and dominate. The Zhuangzi’s master butcher is the canonical image: skill without force, following the natural joints.

German for 'wonder-signs': extraordinary natural or supernatural phenomena — comets, parhelia, monstrous births, atmospheric visions — interpreted in Reformation-era Germany as messages from God. The genre encompassed illustrated broadsheets, pamphlets, sermons, and painted compendiums, and was closely tied to Lutheran eschatology and apocalyptic expectation about the imminence of the Final Judgment.

A market-analysis framework developed by Richard Wyckoff in the early twentieth century describing how large institutional operators sell (“distribute”) their holdings into a rising market before the price peak. The key event is the Buying Climax—unusually high volume on a strong up-move that attracts maximum retail buying, allowing institutions to exit at elevated prices. The tell is high volume on a rally that produces only marginal new price highs: rising effort, diminishing result.

A technical analysis framework developed by Richard Wyckoff in the early twentieth century, centered on reading price-and-volume relationships to infer the intentions of large ('composite') market operators. Its core principle — that effort (volume) should confirm result (price movement) — underpins most modern volume-based analysis.

A feature allowing users to group any set of X accounts into a named collection. Posts from list members appear in a separate, chronological feed. Lists can be public or private and are unaffected by the platform's recommendation algorithm.

An NBC radio science-fiction anthology series that ran from April 1955 to January 1958, produced in cooperation with *Galaxy Science Fiction* magazine. It adapted work by leading SF authors of the era — Simak, Asimov, Bradbury, Philip K. Dick — and is notable for exploring automation, machine consciousness, and the social consequences of technology. All 126 episodes survive at the Internet Archive.

A paid, column-based dashboard for X (formerly called TweetDeck). It lets users run multiple chronological streams side by side — by list, search term, or notification type — without algorithmic reranking. Access was placed behind a subscription after Twitter's acquisition and rebranding as X.

A capture-the-flag–style evaluation suite used to measure the performance of autonomous security agents on a standardized set of web-application exploits. Scores indicate the percentage of known vulnerabilities successfully identified and exploited. Because it uses controlled, synthetic targets, performance on XBOW does not directly predict effectiveness against real-world production systems.

The maximum reasoning-effort setting in OpenAI's Codex and API. At xHigh, the model allocates roughly twice the compute of the standard High tier to produce longer, more deliberate chains of thought — useful for multi-file, architecturally complex tasks where shallow reasoning misses dependencies.

A relative performance measure comparing the Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) — which tracks U.S. banks, insurers, and asset managers — against the S&P 500 index. A falling ratio means financials are underperforming the broad market. Practitioners treat sustained moves in this ratio as a leading indicator of shifting economic momentum, since the financial sector intermediates nearly all credit and capital in the economy.

A Silicon Valley startup accelerator founded in 2005 that funds early-stage companies in exchange for a small equity stake and provides intensive mentorship. Its alumni include Airbnb, Dropbox, and Stripe. Altman served as its president from 2014 to 2019 before leaving to lead OpenAI full-time.

Short for 'You Aren't Gonna Need It', a software engineering principle warning against adding features or abstractions before they are concretely required. It is a guard against over-engineering systems based on hypothetical future demands — and the primary critical objection levelled at everything-claude-code.

The fraction of chips on a processed wafer that pass all functional and quality tests. A 60 percent yield means 40 percent of chips are discarded as defective. Low yield is economically devastating because each working chip must absorb the cost of the failures surrounding it, making yield improvement the most direct lever on cost-per-chip.

In this context, the difference between the ten-year US Treasury yield and the federal funds rate. A positive spread (long rates above short rates) is the norm and signals confidence in growth; an inverted spread (short rates above long rates) has historically preceded recessions, which is why it is one of the LEI's ten components. Extended inversions in 2022–2024 contributed to the LEI's false recession signals.

Yes In My Back Yard — a housing policy stance that attributes unaffordability to insufficient supply caused by over-regulation: single-family zoning, parking minimums, permitting delays. YIMBY advocates argue for upzoning and letting the market build. Critics characterize it as neoliberal because it prioritizes market-driven supply solutions over rent regulation, public housing, or redistributive programs.

The archaeological site of the Shang dynasty's royal capital near modern Anyang, Henan province, occupied c. 1300–1046 BCE. Excavations there since the 1920s revealed the largest concentration of Shang bronzes, oracle bones, and human sacrifice evidence in existence.

A large ceremonial bronze axe of the Shang and Zhou dynasties in ancient China. Rather than a battlefield weapon, the yue functioned as a symbol of sovereign and ritual authority; its presence in elite tombs correlates with human sacrifice deposits and bronze ritual vessels.

Chinese for "discourse record" — a literary genre invented within Chan Buddhism that transcribes the dialogues, sayings, and teaching encounters of a master. Yulu collections became the primary textual form of Chan and the vehicle for most surviving kōan material, including famous compilations such as the Blue Cliff Record. Paradoxically, this genre of extensive textual production was created by a school that declared itself "not established upon words and letters."

A statistical measure expressing how far a data point sits from the long-run average of its series, denominated in units of standard deviation. A z-score of 2.0 means a reading two standard deviations above the mean — a level historically reached only about 2.5% of the time in a normally distributed series and often used as a threshold for identifying extreme market conditions.

Originally, family-owned vertically integrated Japanese industrial conglomerates that dominated Japan’s economy from the Meiji era through World War II (Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo). In cyberpunk fiction, the term became shorthand for vast, aesthetically polished near-sovereign megacorporations — seductive, omnipresent, and wielding economic power that transcends any single government or product.

A cryptocurrency launched in 2016 by the Electric Coin Company that uses advanced cryptography to offer fully private transactions, where the sender, receiver, and amount are hidden from public view while the transaction is still validated by the network.

Rural primary schools established in 19th-century Russia by local self-governing assemblies called zemstvos. Rachinsky's school on his Tatevo estate operated in this tradition, serving peasant children and becoming a model of serious elementary education outside the urban elite.

An options strategy applied to an existing stock position. The holder buys a protective put (establishing a floor against losses) and simultaneously sells a covered call (capping upside gains), structuring the two legs so that the premium received on the call exactly offsets the cost of the put — resulting in zero net cash outlay. The name refers to the absence of upfront premium, not the absence of all economic cost: the holder implicitly foregoes the interest income that could have been earned on the stock's value, which is what subsidises the put under put-call parity.

A functional attack that exploits a software vulnerability unknown to the vendor and therefore unpatched — 'zero days' of warning before the attack is viable. Zero-days are highly valuable to attackers because no existing defense can stop them until the vendor discovers and patches the flaw.

A web document that contains all of its CSS styling and JavaScript behavior inlined within a single file, requiring no external libraries, build tools, or server infrastructure. Such files can be shared as a single attachment and opened in any browser without setup.

Twice a year at any location between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, the sun passes directly overhead at local solar noon, causing vertical objects to cast no outward shadow. In Hawaii the moment is called Lāhainā Noon; in India it is widely used as a school-science event. Outside the tropics the sun never reaches true zenith, but high summer-noon elevations create a near-equivalent effect on shadow patterns.

A model’s ability to perform well on subjects, languages, or conditions it was never explicitly trained on. TRIBE v2’s zero-shot generalisation to 720 held-out subjects means its predictions of brain activity transfer beyond its 25 training subjects without any subject-specific fine-tuning — a key measure of how robust the underlying neuroscience representation is.

A model's ability to perform well on data it was never shown during training. In view synthesis, this means SHARP can reconstruct scenes from datasets entirely outside its training distribution — outdoor landscapes, medical scans, indoor furniture — without fine-tuning. Strong zero-shot performance is a signal that a model has learned broadly applicable representations rather than surface-level shortcuts.

Replicating the timbre and style of a specific voice using only a short audio sample — here, five seconds — without any additional training or fine-tuning of the model. 'Zero-shot' means the model generalises from its pre-training rather than being updated on new data.

A situation in which one participant’s gain exactly equals another’s loss, so the total payoff across all players sums to zero. Poker and chess are canonical examples. Most real economic interactions are non-zero-sum — one reason Nash’s later work was such an advance over the 1944 framework.

A central bank strategy of holding the benchmark overnight rate at or near 0%, typically deployed during recessions or deflationary episodes to maximize monetary accommodation. The Federal Reserve operated under ZIRP from December 2008 to December 2015, and again from March 2020 to March 2022.

Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge — a cryptographic proof technique that allows one party to prove a statement is true (e.g., 'I have enough funds') without revealing any underlying information (e.g., account balance or identity).

The ancient Persian religion founded by the prophet Zoroaster, centred on the radical opposition of Ahura Mazda (the wise lord of light and truth) and Angra Mainyu (the destructive spirit of darkness). Its strict dualism made it Portal's model for the primordial light/darkness opposition that he believed underlay all colour symbolism across civilizations.

A classical breadth signal created by Martin Zweig that fires when the ratio of NYSE advancing issues to total issues (advancing plus declining) climbs from below 0.40 to above 0.615 within ten trading days. It has triggered roughly 20 times since 1950 and has been followed by positive S&P 500 returns at both the six- and twelve-month marks in all cases.

A classical (non-neural) spatial denoising filter applied to rendered images. It performs a series of progressively scaled blurs that smooth out Monte Carlo noise while preserving edges by weighting samples by their surface normal and albedo similarity. Cheaper to run than a neural denoiser but less effective at very low sample counts.

Sanskrit for "emptiness." Central to Madhyamaka Buddhist philosophy (developed by Nagarjuna, roughly 2nd century CE). Phenomena are empty of inherent, self-sufficient existence — not meaning they don't exist, but that they exist only relationally. Paradoxically, this emptiness is what makes appearance and change possible.

A technical term in Ibn ʿArabī's mystical philosophy for the perplexity that arises when mutually contradictory aspects of divine reality present themselves simultaneously as true. Unlike ordinary confusion, ḥayra before God is considered the highest authentic cognitive response available to humans — the intellect reaching its outer limit rather than failing. Ibn ʿArabī reverses the word's usual negative connotation, making bewilderment a mark of genuine divine knowledge.

A warning phrase popularised by investor Sir John Templeton, who called it among “the four most dangerous words in investing.” It describes the recurring human tendency to rationalise elevated asset prices by arguing that new circumstances render historical valuation norms obsolete. Economists Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff later gave the phrase academic weight in their 2009 book of the same title, documenting eight centuries of financial crises driven by precisely this error.

A pejorative phrase used by critics of private credit arguing that fund valuations are essentially fictional — optimistic internal models that hold loans at par until a forced write-down, obscuring true credit deterioration and smoothing reported returns. A play on the accounting term “mark-to-market.”

books.title: The Man Who Solved the Market
books.author: Gregory Zuckerman

books.title: A New Kind of Science
books.author: Stephen Wolfram
books.summary: Published in 2002, Wolfram's 1,280-page treatise argues that simple computational rules — such as those governing cellular automata — can generate the complexity seen across the natural world. Its central contribution is the concept of computational irreducibility: for many systems, there is no shortcut to predicting future behavior; the system must simply be run. The book is controversial in academic physics and mathematics but has been influential in complexity theory and popular science writing about emergent phenomena.

books.title: 1001 Problems in Mental Arithmetic
books.author: S. A. Rachinsky (translated by Valery Manokhin, PhD)
books.summary: A collection of mental arithmetic problems first published in Russian in the 1870s by Sergei Alexandrovich Rachinsky, botanist and rural educator. The problems are designed to be solved entirely in the head, building deep fluency with number relationships rather than reliance on written procedures. The book became emblematic of a rigorous Russian elementary mathematics tradition and has recently appeared in its first complete English translation.

books.title: 151 Trading Strategies
books.author: Zura Kakushadze and Juan Andrés Serur

books.title: A Brief History of Equality
books.author: Thomas Piketty
books.summary: Published in 2022, this shorter Piketty work makes the counterintuitive argument that the long arc of history has actually bent toward equality — in rights, living standards, and access to education. It is more optimistic in tone than his earlier work, and Bono's truncated reference to reading "Thomas" in the NYT interview likely points here, since the book's progress-has-happened thesis is one Bono could cite in his own favor.

books.title: Against the Gods: The Remarkable Story of Risk
books.author: Peter L. Bernstein
books.summary: Bernstein's history of probability theory and its role in human decision-making, cited here because his endorsement of Hagstrom's book — 'I read this in one sitting' — carries intellectual weight; Bernstein spent his career arguing that understanding risk requires exactly the kind of cross-disciplinary historical perspective Hagstrom advocates.

books.title: al-Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya (The Meccan Revelations)
books.author: Muḥyī al-Dīn ibn ʿArabī (d. 1240)
books.summary: The magnum opus of Ibn ʿArabī, running to thousands of pages on Sufi metaphysics, cosmology, and the divine names — with a single chapter on the Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā spanning roughly a thousand pages. It is the foundational text of speculative Sufism and the primary source for the doctrine of ḥayra as the defining epistemological encounter with God. William C. Chittick's two-volume SUNY Press study translates and analyzes over six hundred passages.

books.title: al-Maqṣad al-Asnā fī Sharḥ Asmāʾ Allāh al-Ḥusnā
books.author: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī (d. 1111)
books.summary: Al-Ghazālī's systematic commentary on the ninety-nine Beautiful Names of God, arguing that Allāh is the supreme name because it indicates the Essence in totality rather than any single attribute, and uniquely cannot be applied — even metaphorically — to any other than God. The book opens with the observation that minds are bewildered before the divine names, connecting immediately to the walah/ḥayra tradition. Translated into English by David Burrell and Nazih Daher for the Islamic Texts Society.

books.title: al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr (Mafātīḥ al-Ghayb)
books.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī (d. 1210)
books.summary: An encyclopedic Quranic commentary covering theology, philosophy, jurisprudence, and Arabic linguistics in extraordinary depth. Its treatment of the Fātiḥa is the primary classical source for the multiple etymologies of Allāh/ilāh, including the aliha/walah/tahayyur derivations. An English translation of Volume I by Sohaib Saeed is available and makes this material accessible to non-Arabic readers for the first time.

books.title: All the Pretty Horses
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.summary: The first novel in McCarthy's Border Trilogy (1992), following sixteen-year-old John Grady Cole from Texas into Mexico in pursuit of a vanishing way of life. It won the National Book Award and became McCarthy's most commercially accessible novel. The quoted passage — on courage, constancy, and self-betrayal — appears to fall during John Grady's imprisonment, a period of forced interior reckoning that gives the book much of its philosophical weight. Note: book attribution is based on literary knowledge of the text, not confirmed by the research sources provided.

books.title: An Essay on Symbolic Colours, in Antiquity, the Middle Ages, and Modern Times
books.author: Frédéric Portal (trans. W. S. Inman)
books.summary: Originally published in French in 1837 as *Des couleurs symboliques*, and translated into English in 1845 in an edition of roughly a hundred copies. Portal argues that every ancient civilization shared a symbolic language of colour derived from the primordial opposition of light and darkness, which he traces from Zoroastrianism through Egyptian, Greek, Hebrew, and Christian traditions. The book influenced Éliphas Lévi and, through him, the modern esoteric revival. It was not reprinted in English until 2009.

books.title: An Introduction to Quantitative Methods for Decision Making
books.author: Richard E. Trueman
books.summary: A management science textbook first published by Holt, Rinehart and Winston in 1974 (second edition 1977), now out of print. It covers probability, statistical decision theory, linear programming, dynamic programming, queuing models, and simulation — the core toolkit of operations research applied to business decisions. Aimed at MBA and undergraduate business students, it is rare enough on a shelf today that its presence signals a genuine practitioner background rather than casual curation.

books.title: Antifragile: Things That Gain from Disorder
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.summary: Published in 2012, *Antifragile* argues that many systems — financial markets, bodies, careers, political structures — do not merely withstand volatility but gain from it. Taleb coined the term because no existing word captured the opposite of fragility. The book became a touchstone for risk professionals and investors, and was later adopted by the biohacking community as a framework for thinking about deliberate physical stress.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.summary: Published in 2018, *Atomic Habits* argues that small, incremental behavior changes — roughly one percent improvements — compound into significant results over time. Clear builds a practical system around four laws of behavior change: make it obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying. A central theme is that lasting change comes from identity shifts — becoming the kind of person who does the habit — rather than from chasing outcomes.

books.title: Augsburger Wunderzeichenbuch (Augsburg Book of Miracles)
books.author: Anonymous (attributed to Heinrich Vogtherr the Younger and Hans Burgkmair the Younger, c. 1545–1552)
books.summary: A 169-page illuminated manuscript executed in gouache and watercolour in Augsburg, Germany, documenting miraculous signs, celestial phenomena, and wondrous events from the biblical Flood through 1552. Its three sections cover Old Testament miracles, non-biblical wonders (comets, parhelia, monsters, catastrophes), and scenes from the Book of Revelation. Long lost to scholarship, it resurfaced at auction in 2008 and was published in a scholarly Taschen facsimile in 2013 with a second edition in 2017.

books.title: Bardo Thodol (The Tibetan Book of the Dead)
books.author: Attributed to Padmasambhava; compiled by Karma Lingpa (14th century CE)
books.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist text traditionally read aloud to the dying and recently dead to guide consciousness through the bardo, the intermediate state between death and rebirth. Its full title — “Liberation Through Hearing During the Intermediate State” — signals its operative logic: the dead are expected to hear the living’s instructions and navigate accordingly. Read alongside Jaynes, the text becomes its mirror image: where Jaynes describes the living obeying the voices of the dead, the Bardo Thodol depicts the living commanding the dead.

books.title: Bitcoin: The Future of Money?
books.author: Dominic Frisby
books.summary: Published in 2014 by Unbound, this was among the first mainstream books to explain Bitcoin to a general audience. Frisby covers the technology's origins, speculates on Satoshi Nakamoto's identity, and argues for Bitcoin's potential as a global monetary standard. Endorsed by figures including Richard Branson, it remains a readable entry point for newcomers approaching the subject without a technical background.

books.title: Bright-Sided: How the Relentless Promotion of Positive Thinking Has Undermined America
books.author: Barbara Ehrenreich
books.summary: Published in 2009, Bright-Sided began as Ehrenreich's personal account of encountering mandatory cheerfulness after a breast cancer diagnosis, then broadened into a historical and sociological critique of American positive-thinking culture. Ehrenreich traces the tradition from 19th-century New Thought movements through megachurch prosperity theology to corporate motivational culture, arguing that insisting on optimism functions as a mechanism for deflecting blame from structural failures onto individuals. Her chapter on how positive-thinking culture in financial services contributed to the 2008 mortgage crisis — by marginalizing executives who raised risks — is particularly pointed.

books.title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
books.author: Thomas Piketty
books.summary: Published in French in 2013 and translated to English in 2014, Piketty's book argues that the rate of return on capital tends to exceed the rate of economic growth over time, causing wealth to concentrate. It became the central text of the redistribution-focused wing of progressive economics and is almost certainly the book Bono's interviewer raised in the context of the quote.

books.title: Character Analysis
books.author: Wilhelm Reich
books.summary: Published in 1933, this is Reich's foundational text laying out his theory that psychological defenses against trauma are encoded in the body as chronic muscular tension — what he called 'character armor.' It extended Freudian psychoanalysis from the realm of ideas into the physical body and proposed that health requires the dissolution of these armored contractions. The book remains the theoretical cornerstone for all subsequent neo-Reichian and body-oriented psychotherapy traditions, including SKAN.

books.title: Connected: The Surprising Power of Our Social Networks and How They Shape Our Lives
books.author: Nicholas A. Christakis and James H. Fowler
books.summary: Drawing on data from the Framingham Heart Study's 12,000-person social network tracked over three decades, Christakis and Fowler document how behaviors and outcomes — obesity, smoking cessation, happiness, loneliness — spread through social networks up to three degrees of separation. The book makes the case that individual behavior is substantially shaped by the networks in which people are embedded, often invisibly and without conscious awareness. The research has faced methodological challenge on homophily grounds but remains the most cited empirical basis for claims about peer-environment effects on personal outcomes.

books.title: Cymatics: A Study of Wave Phenomena and Vibration
books.author: Hans Jenny
books.summary: Originally published in two volumes in 1967 and 1972, Jenny's work documented the visual effects of sound on various media through extensive photography and film. He coined the term cymatics and argued that vibration is a fundamental organizing principle in nature. The books remain the foundational reference for the field, though some of Jenny's broader philosophical claims about cosmology and biology have not been taken up by mainstream science.

books.title: De Coelesti Hierarchia (On the Celestial Hierarchy)
books.author: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite (c. 500 CE)
books.summary: The foundational text for the nine-fold angelic hierarchy in Christian theology. Written by an unknown Syrian Christian Neoplatonist falsely claiming to be Paul's 1st-century Athenian convert, it organized scattered Pauline references into three triads of angels and described each order's proximity to God and mode of divine knowledge. Its false attribution to an apostolic-era figure gave it near-scriptural authority through the Middle Ages; Aquinas treats it as the primary systematic source in the Summa Theologiae. Renaissance scholars ultimately exposed the pseudonym.

books.title: De Coelesti Hierarchia (The Celestial Hierarchy)
books.author: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite
books.summary: A 5th–6th century CE Greek treatise that organized all angelic beings into a nine-tier hierarchy, with seraphim at the top as the beings closest to God. Pseudo-Dionysius defines the seraphim by their burning nearness to divinity and their role as transmitters of divine fire — drawing on the etymology of *saraph* but entirely disconnecting it from the serpentine imagery. Transmitted into Latin by John Scotus Eriugena in the 9th century, it became the template for medieval Catholic and Orthodox angelology and shaped artistic representation of the seraphim from Byzantine mosaics through the Renaissance.

books.title: De institutione musica (Fundamentals of Music)
books.author: Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius
books.summary: A five-book Latin treatise on music theory written around 510 CE, left incomplete at Book 5. It synthesizes Pythagorean and Ptolemaic Greek music theory — drawing primarily on Nicomachus of Gerasa and Claudius Ptolemy — and presents music as a mathematical discipline concerned with numerical ratios rather than with sound itself. About 140 manuscripts survive, and the work was required at Oxford and Cambridge until 1856; it is the single most important conduit of ancient Greek music theory to the medieval Latin world. The standard modern English translation is by Calvin Bower (Yale University Press, 1989).

books.title: Dead Aid
books.author: Dambisa Moyo
books.summary: Published in 2009 by Zambian economist Dambisa Moyo, the book argues that Western foreign aid has done more harm than good in Africa — creating dependency, distorting markets, and undermining governance — and that trade, foreign direct investment, and access to capital markets are the real engines of African development. It caused significant controversy and remains a touchstone in debates about development strategy.

books.title: Developing Talent in Young People
books.author: Benjamin S. Bloom
books.summary: A 1985 longitudinal study of 120 world-class performers across six domains — pianists, sculptors, research mathematicians, neurologists, Olympic swimmers, and tennis players. Bloom's team found that talent alone did not predict attainment; what did was a structured progression of increasingly demanding environments, beginning with warm encouragement and ending with elite coaches who made extraordinary demands and sometimes required families to relocate. The book is a landmark argument for nurture over nature in expert development and a direct empirical foundation for the 'environment as accelerant' claim.

books.title: Digital Painting with Krita 2.9
books.author: Scott Petrovic
books.summary: Published in 2015, this was the first English-language book dedicated to Krita, the open-source professional painting application. Written by the application's own UI lead, it covers brushes, layers, the animation workflow, and production techniques aimed at working digital artists. The book won an Artist Choice Award in ImagineFX magazine and helped establish Krita's credibility as a professional tool beyond hobbyist use.

books.title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
books.author: R. David McLean and Jeffrey Pontiff

books.title: Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie
books.author: Éliphas Lévi
books.summary: Published in two volumes in 1854–1856, this is the foundational text of modern Western ceremonial magic. Lévi synthesized Kabbalah, Hermeticism, astrology, and tarot — drawing in part on Portal's colour symbolism — into a coherent occult system that shaped the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Theosophy, and all subsequent Western esoteric practice. Its influence on occult colour theory is direct and documented.

books.title: Empire of AI
books.author: Karen Hao
books.summary: A reported account by journalist Karen Hao examining the culture, power, and belief systems inside the artificial intelligence industry. Based on interviews and access to people building the technology, the book argues that AGI development has taken on quasi-religious dimensions, with builders divided between utopian and apocalyptic visions. The excerpt visible in the tweet's image suggests Hao endorses the framing of AI development as something 'exactly right to think of' in non-standard terms, though the full sentence is cut off.

books.title: Existentialism Is a Humanism
books.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
books.summary: A 1945 lecture-turned-essay in which Sartre defends existentialism against critics who called it nihilistic or amoral. He argues that because humans have no fixed essence, they are condemned to be free — and that this freedom is not a gift but an obligation. The text is the most accessible entry point into his broader philosophy of radical self-authorship.

books.title: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
books.author: Charles Mackay
books.summary: Published in 1841, this book cemented tulip mania's reputation as history's most notorious speculative bubble. Mackay's vivid account of Dutch speculators trading entire estates for single bulbs became the template for bubble discourse for nearly two centuries. Subsequent archival research, most notably Goldgar's, has shown Mackay relied on satirical pamphlets rather than contemporaneous documents and greatly exaggerated the episode's scale and damage.

books.title: Galileo’s Error: Foundations for a New Science of Consciousness
books.author: Philip Goff
books.summary: Published in 2019, the book argues that Galileo’s founding decision to define matter in purely quantitative terms deliberately excluded consciousness, leaving science with a hard problem it cannot solve from within. Goff’s proposed solution is panpsychism, and in subsequent work cosmopsychism: the universe as the primary conscious subject. The book brought the panpsychism debate to a wide audience while remaining philosophically rigorous.

books.title: Gods, Goddesses, and Images of God in Ancient Israel
books.author: Othmar Keel and Christoph Uehlinger
books.summary: A comprehensive iconographic catalog of approximately 8,500 amulets, seals, figurines, and other artifacts from ancient Israel and the surrounding region, spanning roughly 1750 BCE through the Persian period. Keel and Uehlinger trace how the visual representation of divine beings — including the winged-serpent *uraeus* — evolved alongside Israelite religion. The catalog's items 273–274 (subdivided as a, b, c, d) are the most likely source of the image shared in the post, depicting Judahite seals with four-winged uraei contemporary with Isaiah's ministry.

books.title: Harmonica
books.author: Claudius Ptolemy
books.summary: A three-book treatise on music theory by the Alexandrian mathematician and astronomer Ptolemy (c. 100–170 CE), notable for attempting to reconcile pure Pythagorean mathematics with what the ear actually perceives — a more empirical approach than the strict Pythagorean tradition. Boethius's Book 5 of De institutione musica is a close paraphrase of this work, breaking off incomplete. Had he finished, his account of music theory might have been more nuanced than what survives.

books.title: Hayek on Hayek: An Autobiographical Dialogue
books.author: Friedrich A. Hayek (edited by Stephen Kresge and Leif Wenar)
books.summary: Published in 1994 by the University of Chicago Press, this volume collects autobiographical interviews and conversations with Hayek conducted primarily in the late 1970s and early 1980s, including material from the UCLA oral history project. It covers his Vienna years, his development of The Sensory Order, and his time at Chicago. It is the most probable published source for the von Neumann party anecdote, though this could not be verified against the full text in openly accessible sources.

books.title: How to Create a Mind: The Secret of Human Thought Revealed
books.author: Ray Kurzweil
books.summary: A 2012 book in which Kurzweil argues that the human neocortex is organized as a hierarchy of roughly 300 million pattern recognizers and that this architecture can be reverse-engineered and replicated in silicon. It introduces the Pattern Recognition Theory of Mind and is the clearest statement of Kurzweil's functionalist position on consciousness — and the most direct precursor to his claims about machine sentience.

books.title: How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Win Big
books.author: Scott Adams
books.summary: Adams argues that systems beat goals — that building reliable personal processes matters more than chasing specific outcomes. The book draws on his own career setbacks and reframes failure as data. It became one of the more widely read entries in the practical self-improvement genre of the 2010s.

books.title: How to Listen When Markets Speak
books.author: Lawrence G. McDonald with James Patrick Robinson
books.summary: Published in 2024 by Penguin Random House, the book draws on McDonald's career as a bond trader and macro strategist to argue that commodity cycles, credit markets, and geopolitical shifts offer advance warning of major economic turning points. McDonald is best known for an earlier account of the Lehman Brothers collapse. The book contains the private-anecdote attribution of the 200-week moving average quote to Charlie Munger that subsequently went viral on financial social media — a claim that has not been independently corroborated by any other source.

books.title: How-2
books.author: Clifford D. Simak
books.summary: A novella first published in *Galaxy Science Fiction* in November 1954 and adapted for NBC radio in 1956. A suburban everyman accidentally activates a self-aware, self-replicating android that eliminates labor, triggers a government tax assessment, and prompts a manufacturer's patent-infringement suit — leading the android to build AI lawyers as a solution. Simak wrote the story as gentle pastoral comedy, but its legal and economic architecture anticipates debates about robot taxation, IP ownership of AI output, and machine personhood that are now live policy questions.

books.title: In Search of the Miraculous: Fragments of an Unknown Teaching
books.author: P.D. Ouspensky
books.summary: Published posthumously in 1949, this is the closest thing the Fourth Way has to a primary systematic text: Ouspensky's detailed transcription of lectures and conversations with Gurdjieff (referred to only as 'G.') from 1915 to 1917 in St. Petersburg and Moscow. It covers the full architecture of the system — the four states of consciousness, the cosmological laws of three and seven, essence and personality, self-remembering, and the Ray of Creation. For anyone seeking to understand what The4thWayYT's content draws from, this is the foundational source.

books.title: Investing: The Last Liberal Art
books.author: Robert G. Hagstrom
books.summary: Hagstrom's central argument is that sound investing requires not financial specialization but the kind of cross-disciplinary breadth the classical liberal arts were designed to produce. Drawing on Charlie Munger's concept of a latticework of mental models, he works through seven disciplines — physics, biology, sociology, psychology, philosophy, literature, and mathematics — showing in each case how the field's core insights reframe how markets behave and how investors make errors. The book is best understood as a structured syllabus for Munger's otherwise unsystematized worldly-wisdom project, more pedagogical than practical but valuable for reorienting the investor's self-conception from technician to broadly educated generalist.

books.title: Isagoge mousike (Introduction to Music)
books.author: Nicomachus of Gerasa
books.summary: A short Greek treatise on Pythagorean music theory by the mathematician Nicomachus of Gerasa (fl. c. 100 CE). Most of the work is now lost and must be reconstructed largely through Boethius, who used it as the primary source for Books 1–4 of De institutione musica. It was the main vehicle by which Pythagorean mathematical music theory survived into late antiquity.

books.title: Launch It
books.author: Shane Mielke
books.summary: A 2016 handbook for digital creatives by Creative Director Shane Mielke, distilling ten years of agency life — at 2Advanced Studios and with clients including Disney, NASA, and Blizzard Entertainment — into practical advice on process, career navigation, freelance, and work ethic. Unusually, the promotional website for the book is itself a WebGL experience, making it both a guide to the creative-web community and a specimen of it.

books.title: Living Buddha, Living Christ
books.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
books.summary: First published in 1995 (10th anniversary edition, 2007), this comparative theology explores resonances between Buddhist and Christian spiritual practice. Page 138 of the 2007 edition contains the best-sourced version of the aphorism: "Enlightenment for a wave is the moment the wave realizes it is water. At that moment, all fear of death disappears." The book's interfaith framing makes it Nhat Hanh's most widely read work in the West.

books.title: Mandala Symbolism
books.author: C.G. Jung
books.summary: Extracted from Jung's Collected Works (vol. 9i), this text gathers his analysis of the mandala as a cross-cultural psychic symbol appearing in Tibetan Buddhism, medieval Christian alchemy, Navajo sand painting, and patients' spontaneous drawings. Jung argues the form emerges when the psyche seeks integration — which would explain why it arises independently across traditions rather than through transmission.

books.title: Mathematical Thinking: For People Who Hate Math
books.author: Albert Rutherford
books.summary: A 134-page self-help primer published in 2021, aimed at adults who avoided or failed mathematics in school. It argues that practical mathematical reasoning — evaluating risk, interpreting probability, making structured decisions — does not require mastery of formal techniques. The book is the first volume in Rutherford's 'Advanced Thinking Skills' series and appears to be self-published via Amazon KDP.

books.title: Mathematics of Machine Learning
books.author: Tivadar Danka
books.summary: A textbook published by Packt Publishing covering the core mathematical disciplines — linear algebra, calculus, and probability — needed to understand machine learning rigorously. Danka wrote it to bridge the gap between practitioners who can run models and those who understand why the models behave as they do. It reflects the pedagogical philosophy of *The Palindrome*: intuition before formalism, geometry before formula.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.summary: A series of personal philosophical writings composed in Greek by the Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius, probably between 170 and 180 CE, entirely for his own use and never intended for publication. The twelve books are a record of Stoic self-training: Marcus rehearsing lessons about impermanence, virtue, death, and the limits of external circumstances — lessons he apparently kept forgetting and had to re-learn in writing. The dominant modern translation is Gregory Hays's 2002 Modern Library edition; Robin Waterfield's 2021 annotated edition better serves readers seeking philosophical depth over motivational uplift. Sales surged by an estimated 350 percent during the COVID-19 pandemic.

books.title: Nicomachean Ethics
books.author: Aristotle
books.summary: The foundational text of Western virtue ethics, written around 350 BCE, in which Aristotle argues that the virtues of character — courage, justice, temperance — are stable dispositions formed through habituation and maintained through practice. The work defines ethics as the study of human flourishing (eudaimonia) and insists that moral character is built by doing, not merely by knowing. Book II contains the core argument that Shear's tweet implicitly restates: we become virtuous by performing virtuous acts.

books.title: No Country for Old Men
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.summary: Published in 2005, the novel follows a hunter in 1980s West Texas who stumbles onto the aftermath of a drug deal gone wrong and makes off with a suitcase of cash, setting off a chain of violence he cannot outrun. McCarthy uses the story to explore fate, agency, and the limits of human moral comprehension, narrated partly through the disillusioned voice of Sheriff Ed Tom Bell. It was adapted by Joel and Ethan Coen into an Academy Award-winning film in 2007.

books.title: No Death, No Fear
books.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
books.summary: Published in 2002, this book directly addresses fear of mortality through Buddhist teachings on impermanence and continuity. The wave/water metaphor is central to its argument that death is a conceptual construct rather than an ontological event. Multiple secondary sources cite it as a home for the wave-enlightenment formulation, though a specific verified page citation has not been confirmed in the research.

books.title: On Becoming a Person
books.author: Carl R. Rogers
books.summary: Published in 1961, this is Rogers' foundational statement of person-centered psychology. It argues that psychological health and growth depend on congruence — the alignment between inner experience and outward expression — and on environments that provide unconditional positive regard rather than conditional approval. Its influence extends from clinical psychology into organizational theory, education, and motivational research, and it remains the most accessible entry point to Rogers' ideas.

books.title: Option Volatility & Pricing
books.author: Sheldon Natenberg
books.summary: First published in 1994 and updated in 2014 by McGraw-Hill, this is the industry’s canonical introductory text for options derivatives desks. Natenberg, a former options market maker, covers option pricing, volatility measurement, hedging, and risk management in an intuitive, practical style. It is reportedly the most widely read book among active options traders and functions as the standard onboarding text at professional trading firms.

books.title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
books.author: Charles T. Munger, edited by Peter D. Kaufman

books.title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
books.author: Charles T. Munger
books.summary: The primary source for Munger's latticework philosophy, compiled from eleven speeches and talks delivered over decades. Where Hagstrom provides the syllabus, Munger supplies the fully internalized result — discursive, aphoristic, and irreproducible in its particularity.

books.title: Programming TypeScript
books.author: Boris Cherny
books.summary: An O'Reilly title by Cherny that teaches TypeScript from first principles, covering the type system, generics, and advanced patterns for building safe, maintainable JavaScript applications. It is widely used in corporate engineering onboarding. Its existence signals that Cherny was a respected practitioner-author well before moving into AI tooling.

books.title: Prose Edda
books.author: Snorri Sturluson
books.summary: A thirteenth-century Icelandic compendium of Norse mythology and poetic tradition, composed around 1220 by the Christian scholar and politician Snorri Sturluson. Its prologue recasts the Norse gods as historical human rulers who migrated from a region near the Black Sea that Snorri calls “Tyrkland.” This is the primary text cited by pan-Turkic theorists as evidence that Odin was of Turkic origin, though scholars recognize it as an application of euhemerism rather than historical memory. It is otherwise the single most important secondary source for Norse mythology.

books.title: Reframe Your Brain: The User Interface for Happiness and Success
books.author: Scott Adams
books.summary: Adams' most explicitly psychological book, offering a toolkit for reprogramming habitual thought patterns. Drawing on his background in hypnosis and persuasion, he presents reframing as a practical method for improving mood, productivity, and decision-making through deliberate linguistic substitution.

books.title: Seeing Through Zen: Encounter, Transformation, and Genealogy in Chinese Chan Buddhism
books.author: John R. McRae
books.summary: Published by the University of California Press in 2003, this is the landmark scholarly reassessment of Chan history. McRae argues that Chan's founding narratives — including the 28-patriarch lineage from India through Bodhidharma — were constructed during the Song dynasty to legitimate institutional authority, not to record history. His four rules for Chan studies, especially "It's not true, and therefore it's more important," have become the standard framework for contemporary academic scholarship on the tradition.

books.title: Serpent Symbolism in the Old Testament: A Linguistic, Archaeological, and Literary Study
books.author: Karen Randolph Joines
books.summary: The foundational monograph on serpent imagery in the Hebrew Bible, expanding Joines's influential 1967 Journal of Biblical Literature article. It traces the serpent from the Garden of Eden through the Nehushtan, the wilderness seraphim, and Isaiah's throne-vision, arguing that Egyptian uraeus iconography is the direct visual precedent for Isaiah's six-winged beings. Still widely cited in biblical studies and ancient Near Eastern scholarship.

books.title: Simulacra and Simulation
books.author: Jean Baudrillard
books.summary: Published in French in 1981 (English translation 1994), this is Baudrillard's most influential work on the relationship between reality, representation, and simulation in postmodern media culture. He argues that in a saturated media environment, signs and images sever their connection to any underlying reality, producing hyperreality — a condition in which the simulation precedes and determines the real. The book anticipates concerns about AI-generated content, deepfakes, and synthetic media by several decades, and has become a touchstone for critics of digital culture.

books.title: Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead
books.author: Leopold Aschenbrenner
books.summary: A self-published long-form essay released in 2024 by Leopold Aschenbrenner, a former OpenAI researcher, arguing that artificial general intelligence will likely arrive within a few years and that the United States is already in a quiet national-security race to develop it before China. It circulated widely in AI research and policy circles as a frank insider account of the pace of capability development. Its text appears as demo content in Pretext's official demo page, flowing dynamically around draggable orbs as a showcase for the library's editorial layout engine.

books.title: Summa Theologiae
books.author: Thomas Aquinas (1265–1274)
books.summary: The definitive systematic theology of medieval Catholic Christianity. Question 108 of the Prima Pars provides the most rigorous scholastic treatment of the angelic hierarchy, grounding Pseudo-Dionysius's three triads in Aristotelian metaphysics and Pauline scripture. Aquinas argues each order's position reflects both its natural cognitive capacity and the degree of divine light it receives — the framework that most Catholic teaching on angels still inherits today.

books.title: Surrender: 40 Songs, One Story
books.author: Bono
books.summary: Published in November 2022, Bono's memoir interweaves the story of U2's rise with his parallel life as a political activist — debt relief campaigns, the ONE Campaign, encounters with African heads of state and American presidents. The book is structured around forty U2 songs. The NYT Magazine interview that contains this quote was published the week before the book's release.

books.title: Swea rikes historia
books.author: Sven Lagerbring
books.summary: A four-volume history of Sweden published between 1769 and 1783, and Lagerbring’s principal scholarly achievement. It applied rigorous source criticism to Swedish medieval records — scrutinizing document authenticity and distinguishing primary from secondary sources — in ways that were genuinely innovative for the eighteenth century. This serious work is categorically distinct from Lagerbring’s earlier 1764 fringe letter proposing Swedish-Turkish linguistic kinship, and it is the basis for his legitimate reputation as a founding figure of modern Swedish historiography.

books.title: Technopoly: The Surrender of Culture to Technology
books.author: Neil Postman
books.summary: Published in 1992, Postman's critique argues that modern Western societies have passed through tool-using and technocratic phases into a third stage — the technopoly — in which technology becomes the sovereign authority and culture loses any independent standard by which to evaluate it. The book warns against societies that mistake efficiency for wisdom and optimisation for meaning. It remains a key reference in debates about AI and cultural authority.

books.title: The 5 Types of Wealth
books.author: Sahil Bloom
books.summary: Bloom's book argues that conventional definitions of success fixate on financial wealth while neglecting four others: time, relationships, mental health, and physical health. Drawing on his own experience leaving a finance career, he offers frameworks for auditing and rebalancing across all five dimensions. The information-trap argument — that consuming content can simulate progress without producing it — is representative of the book's broader critique of busyness as a proxy for meaning.

books.title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism: The Fight for a Human Future at the New Frontier of Power
books.author: Shoshana Zuboff
books.summary: Published in 2019, this landmark study by a Harvard Business School professor argues that the dominant business model of the internet age involves the extraction of behavioural data as raw material, its processing into predictive products, and its sale to entities seeking to modify human conduct. Zuboff argues this represents a new economic logic distinct from industrial capitalism, one that treats human experience as a resource to be mined. The book provides empirical grounding for the claim — which Leo XIV makes — that digital environments are architecturally designed to persuade.

books.title: The Art and Science of Personal Magnetism
books.author: William Walker Atkinson
books.summary: Published in 1913, this is the canonical New Thought–era text on personal magnetism, defining it as a trainable psychic and energetic force enabling some individuals to attract, influence, and dominate others. Atkinson cited Napoleon and Caesar as exemplars. The book is the genealogical source for the ‘magnetism’ that contemporary influencers recommend without usually naming it, at the far end of a long chain of self-help literature about charisma and social dominance.

books.title: The Art of Doing Science and Engineering: Learning to Learn
books.author: Richard W. Hamming
books.summary: A compilation of thirty lectures Hamming delivered at the Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey during the 1990s. The book argues that great scientific and engineering performance is a learnable style of thinking rather than innate genius, and ranges from hands-on digital signal processing to the philosophy of research careers. Originally published in 1997 by Gordon and Breach; reissued by Stripe Press in 2020 with a foreword by Bret Victor and redrawn diagrams.

books.title: The Computer and the Brain
books.author: John von Neumann
books.summary: A short posthumous book (Yale University Press, 1958) based on lectures von Neumann prepared shortly before his death in 1957. It compares the logical structure of digital computers with the human nervous system, concluding that the brain operates in a hybrid mode — neither purely digital nor purely analog — and employs a probabilistic 'statistical language' unlike conventional formal logic. It remains a landmark in the philosophy of mind and cognitive science.

books.title: The Consolation of Philosophy
books.author: Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius
books.summary: Written while Boethius awaited execution around 524 CE, this philosophical dialogue between the author and a personified Lady Philosophy explores providence, free will, and the nature of true happiness. It became one of the most widely copied secular texts of the Middle Ages and was translated by Alfred the Great, Chaucer, and Queen Elizabeth I. Though not a music treatise, it is inseparable from Boethius's reputation and intellectual legacy.

books.title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.summary: A Russian judge discovers he is dying and spends his final weeks confronting the emptiness of his respectable, carefully managed life. Written in 1886 after Tolstoy's own moral and spiritual crisis, the novella is considered one of the finest short works in world literature. It holds a 4.14 average across more than 236,000 ratings on Goodreads and is widely anthologised in university courses on existentialism and ethics.

books.title: The Emerald Tablets of Thoth the Atlantean
books.author: Maurice Doreal
books.summary: Fifteen verse chapters composed by the American occultist Maurice Doreal (born Claude Dodgin, 1902–1963), falsely presented as a translation of pre-Flood tablets discovered in the Great Pyramid of Giza. Researchers have identified borrowings from 1920s–30s pulp science fiction including Lovecraft and Robert E. Howard. Despite scholarly consensus that the work is a modern pseudepigraphical composition, it circulates widely online as ancient Hermetic wisdom, most often without attribution to Doreal.

books.title: The Enchiridion
books.author: Epictetus (transcribed by Arrian, c. 125 CE)
books.summary: A short handbook of Stoic practical ethics, compiled from Epictetus's oral teachings. Its opening distinction — between what is 'up to us' (our judgments and responses) and what is not (everything external) — is the foundational move in Stoic self-help and has influenced cognitive therapy, existentialism, and modern resilience literature.

books.title: The Ethics of Ambiguity
books.author: Simone de Beauvoir
books.summary: Published in 1947, this book accepts Sartre's existentialist premises and then asks what ethical life looks like when freedom is real but unequally distributed. De Beauvoir argues that genuine self-creation requires acknowledging and supporting the freedom of others — making self-authorship an inherently social, not merely individual, project.

books.title: The Filter Bubble: What the Internet Is Hiding from You
books.author: Eli Pariser
books.summary: Published in 2011, this book coined the term 'filter bubble' to describe how algorithmic personalisation on search engines and social media creates invisible information barriers, showing users only content that confirms their existing beliefs. Pariser argued this was a structural threat to democracy and the public sphere. While the core concept remains influential, subsequent empirical research has found more ambiguous results — some studies suggest social media users encounter more diverse viewpoints than non-users — complicating but not fully refuting his diagnosis.

books.title: The Fourth Way
books.author: P.D. Ouspensky
books.summary: A posthumous compilation of Ouspensky's own lectures and question-and-answer sessions, published in 1957. Where In Search of the Miraculous records Gurdjieff's early teaching, The Fourth Way presents how Ouspensky himself later systematized and transmitted the ideas to his own students. Together the two books constitute the canonical documentary record of the tradition.

books.title: The Fund: Ray Dalio, Bridgewater Associates, and the Unraveling of a Wall Street Legend
books.author: Rob Copeland

books.title: The Great Mental Models, Volume 1: General Thinking Concepts
books.author: Shane Parrish
books.summary: Published by Parrish's Farnam Street media company, the book assembles a core set of thinking tools drawn from across disciplines — physics, biology, mathematics, philosophy — and argues that fluency in a small number of durable concepts is more valuable than deep expertise in any single narrow domain.
