Its central claim is that blind spots, not lack of information, are the root cause of poor decisions. The book covers models including the map/territory distinction, inversion, second-order thinking, probabilistic thinking, and Occam's and Hanlon's Razors.

books.title: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching
books.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
books.summary: Published in 1998, this is Nhat Hanh's most comprehensive introduction to Buddhist doctrine for Western readers. It covers the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path, and key concepts including interbeing, no-self, and nirvana. The extended wave-and-water passage — including the line "the wave does not need to die to become water" — appears here, making it a primary source for the metaphor's philosophical development.

books.title: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
books.author: Joseph Campbell
books.summary: Published in 1949, this is the book that popularized the monomyth: the argument that hero narratives worldwide follow a single deep structural arc. Campbell synthesizes Frazer's comparative mythology, Jungian psychology, and van Gennep's rites-of-passage theory. Hugely influential on filmmakers and storytellers; contested by academic folklorists who find the schema too elastic to constitute genuine structural analysis.

books.title: The Human Use of Human Beings: Cybernetics and Society
books.author: Norbert Wiener
books.summary: First published in 1950 and revised in 1954, this is Wiener's accessible translation of his technical *Cybernetics* (1948) for a general audience. Wiener argues that automation will displace human workers across any domain where judgment can be routinized, warns that the gains will accrue to capital owners absent policy intervention, and urges labor unions and governments to prepare. It was the most serious public-intellectual intervention on automation and labor of the 1950s, and its warnings read as freshly applicable today.

books.title: The Intelligent Investor
books.author: Benjamin Graham
books.summary: First published in 1949, this is the foundational text of value investing — the discipline of buying securities at a price significantly below their intrinsic worth. Graham distinguishes between investing (systematic analysis aimed at safety and adequate return) and speculation (everything else). The book popularized the Newton South Sea anecdote and the apocryphal quote about calculating heavenly bodies but not the madness of people. Warren Buffett called it the best book on investing ever written.

books.title: The Kybalion: A Study of the Hermetic Philosophy of Ancient Egypt and Greece
books.author: Three Initiates (attributed; almost certainly William Walker Atkinson)
books.summary: An influential 1908 occult text that codified "Seven Hermetic Principles" — including the Principle of Mentalism and the Principle of Cause and Effect — in accessible language for American New Thought audiences. Scholars classify it as New Thought doctrine retrofitted onto Hermetic vocabulary rather than a genuine transmission of ancient teaching. It is the closest intellectual ancestor to the philosophy expressed in Doreal's tablets, sharing nearly identical formulations.

books.title: The Laws of Trading
books.author: Agustín Lebrón
books.summary: Published by Wiley in 2019, the book distils the decision-making frameworks used by professional traders at firms like Jane Street into a set of transferable laws applicable beyond markets. Its central arguments concern edge — why genuine informational advantage is rare, hard to prove, and even harder to sustain — adverse selection, and the danger of confusing a good model with a good trade. The Law of Edge holds that a real edge should be briefly and clearly explainable; if it requires elaborate justification, it probably does not exist. The book is widely regarded as the most intellectually honest popular treatment of quantitative trading currently in print.

books.title: The Lost Continent of Mu
books.author: James Churchward
books.summary: Published in 1926 and revised in 1931, Churchward's book claims that all ancient civilizations — including China and Mesoamerica — descended from a vast Pacific supercontinent called Mu, home to 64 million advanced inhabitants before volcanic cataclysm sank it some 12,000 years ago. The evidence rests on tablets Churchward claimed to have been shown by an Indian priest but never produced for independent verification. Scholars have unanimously rejected the theory as pseudoscience, citing geological impossibility and false translations. The books nonetheless influenced a persistent tradition of fringe diffusionism that treats visual similarities between distant ancient cultures as proof of contact.

books.title: The Magic Mountain
books.author: Thomas Mann
books.summary: Published in November 1924, *The Magic Mountain* follows Hans Castorp, a young German engineer whose intended three-week visit to a Swiss tuberculosis sanatorium extends to seven years. The novel uses its sealed-off alpine world to stage a sweeping philosophical drama about time, illness, love, and the political forces tearing Europe apart on the eve of the First World War. Nearly 800 pages long, it is considered one of the defining works of 20th-century literature and turned 100 in 2024.

books.title: The Nine Billion Names of God
books.author: Arthur C. Clarke
books.summary: A short story published in 1953 in which Tibetan monks enlist Western technicians to install a computer that will enumerate all of God's names — a task they believe the universe was created to complete. When the machine finishes, the stars begin going out. Praised by Carl Sagan and frequently anthologised, it is a parable about the unintended consequences of accelerating sacred tasks with technology, and about the danger of completing a cosmic project without fully understanding what completion means.

books.title: The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind
books.author: Julian Jaynes
books.summary: Published in 1976 by Princeton psychologist Julian Jaynes (1920–1997), this book argues that human consciousness — the introspective narrator within — did not exist until roughly 1000–500 BCE. Earlier humans operated under a “bicameral mind,” hallucinating the voices of gods and dead ancestors as literal commands rather than deliberating internally. Jaynes supports the claim through analysis of Homeric texts, ancient Near Eastern inscriptions, and archaeological sites including Eynan. The theory has not entered mainstream neuroscience but has attracted sustained scholarly debate and periodic cultural revivals, most recently in the context of artificial intelligence.

books.title: The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind
books.author: Julian Jaynes
books.summary: Published in 1976, the book argues that human introspective consciousness is a recent cultural invention, dating to roughly 1000 BCE, and that before its emergence the mind was 'bicameral' — organized so that inner speech was experienced as divine hallucination rather than self-generated thought. Jaynes draws on Homeric epic, cuneiform texts, and neurological speculation to build his case. The book was widely reviewed and has remained in print for decades, occupying an unusual position as a work taken seriously enough to generate a dedicated scholarly society but too speculative to be absorbed into mainstream cognitive science.

books.title: The Principles of Psychology
books.author: William James
books.summary: James's two-volume masterwork (1890) laid the foundations of modern psychology. Its chapters on habit and the will develop what became the 'act as if' principle: sustained enactment of a trait, even under uncertainty, causally embeds it in the motivational structure of the person. James saw character as plastic and behavior as prior to belief — a pragmatist inversion of common-sense psychology that anticipates both Bem's self-perception theory and the behavioral ethics literature.

books.title: The Righteous Mind: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion
books.author: Jonathan Haidt
books.summary: Published in 2012, this book argues that moral and political reasoning is driven primarily by gut-level intuitions, with conscious reasoning serving as post-hoc rationalization. Haidt draws on evolutionary psychology and cross-cultural research to show that humans have an innate “hive switch” — a capacity for self-subordination to group identity — that underpins both religious experience and political tribalism. It is the most widely read popular synthesis of the case that humans are not truth-seeking animals in moral and political life, but tribal ones.

books.title: The Sacred and the Profane: The Nature of Religion
books.author: Mircea Eliade
books.summary: Published in 1959, this is Eliade's most accessible statement of his phenomenological approach to comparative religion. It maps how sacred space (organized around the axis mundi), sacred time (ritual return to origins), and symbolic cosmology recur across independent traditions. Enormously influential in religious studies for two decades; later criticized for imposing universal structures at the expense of historical and cultural particularity.

books.title: The Sensory Order: An Inquiry into the Foundations of Theoretical Psychology
books.author: Friedrich A. Hayek
books.summary: Published in 1952 by the University of Chicago Press, this is Hayek's theory of how the central nervous system generates subjective experience. Its central argument — that the brain is an active classificatory system whose structure is built through experience — independently anticipated Hebbian learning and later connectionism. Though largely ignored by economists, it was rediscovered by neuroscientists in the 1980s and 1990s as a remarkably prescient account of neural memory networks.

books.title: The Singularity Is Near
books.author: Ray Kurzweil
books.summary: Published in 2005, Kurzweil’s central work argues that accelerating technological progress — particularly in AI, nanotechnology, and biotechnology — will culminate in a Singularity around 2045, when machine superintelligence emerges and permanently transforms the human condition. The book constructs an elaborate evidential apparatus of exponential growth curves and historical trends that functions to make the core prophecy feel inevitable. Critics have noted its structural resemblance to religious eschatology, and Kurzweil’s own tracking of his prediction accuracy has been disputed.

books.title: The Singularity Is Near: When Humans Transcend Biology
books.author: Ray Kurzweil
books.summary: Kurzweil's 2005 manifesto arguing that exponential growth in computing, biotechnology, and nanotechnology will produce a civilizational inflection point — the Singularity — around 2045, when artificial intelligence far surpasses human intelligence. The book introduced the Law of Accelerating Returns to a general audience and laid out 147 specific predictions, now subject to active empirical scrutiny. Its accuracy record is cited selectively by partisans on both sides.

books.title: The Singularity Is Nearer: When We Merge with AI
books.author: Ray Kurzweil
books.summary: Kurzweil's 2024 update, written after the emergence of large language models, reaffirming his 2029 AGI and 2045 Singularity predictions. It engages more directly with debates on machine consciousness and borrows Chalmers's panprotopsychist framing to argue that silicon-based systems can host genuine inner experience. Critics note that the same exponential extrapolation method underpins all predictions regardless of domain-specific physical or economic limits.

books.title: The Subtle Knife
books.author: Philip Pullman
books.summary: The second novel in Pullman's His Dark Materials trilogy (1997), in which the protagonist Will Parry wins possession of Æsahættr — the subtle knife — a blade capable of cutting through any material, including the boundary between parallel worlds. The knife serves whoever holds it and has no moral agency of its own. Roon uses it as a precise metaphor for GPT: an instrument of extraordinary capability that inspires admiration for its craft but carries no character and demands no reverence.

books.title: The Technological Republic: Hard Power, Soft Belief, and the Future of the West
books.author: Alexander C. Karp and Nicholas W. Zamiska
books.summary: Published by Crown Currency (Penguin Random House) in February 2025, the book argues that Silicon Valley reneged on a post-WWII compact in which technology companies supported national defense in exchange for the state funding and social stability that made their rise possible. It calls for a renewed public-private partnership in defense AI, universal national service, and the reversal of post-WWII demilitarization in Germany and Japan. The book debuted at #1 on the *New York Times* bestseller list, drew endorsements from Walter Isaacson and warm reviews in the mainstream press, and was named an NPR Best Book of the Year — though specialist reviewers found its prescriptions vague relative to the ambition of its diagnosis.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Liu Cixin
books.summary: The first volume of Liu Cixin’s *Remembrance of Earth’s Past* trilogy, set against China’s Cultural Revolution and the discovery of an alien civilization facing imminent stellar catastrophe. The novel introduces the Trisolarans and their strategy of deploying sophons to monitor and paralyze Earth’s scientific progress. It is among the most celebrated science fiction works of the 21st century, particularly for its unsentimental treatment of civilizational conflict and the logic of existential threat.

books.title: The Transcendent Unity of Religions
books.author: Frithjof Schuon
books.summary: First published in French in 1948, this is the foundational text of the Traditionalist School. Schuon distinguishes the exoteric (outer, doctrinal) from the esoteric (inner, metaphysical) dimension of religion and argues that at the esoteric level all major religions converge on a single truth. T.S. Eliot called it 'the most impressive work in the comparative study of Oriental and Occidental religion'; most academic scholars of religion are more skeptical of its metaphysical premises.

books.title: The Volatility Surface: A Practitioner’s Guide
books.author: Jim Gatheral
books.summary: Published in 2006 by Wiley Finance, this is widely considered the definitive practitioner-academic text on volatility surface modeling. Gatheral, a professor at CUNY Baruch and former head of quantitative analytics at Merrill Lynch, covers stochastic volatility models (Heston, SABR, SVJ), local volatility, variance swaps, and exotic derivatives pricing. Nassim Taleb wrote the foreword. It is the standard graduate-level reference for anyone building or trading volatility models professionally.

books.title: Theory of Colours (Zur Farbenlehre)
books.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
books.summary: Published in German in 1810, Goethe's colour theory challenged Newton's purely optical account by insisting on colour as a phenomenon of perception and relationship. Like Portal, Goethe built his framework on the polarity of light and darkness, arguing that all colours arise from their interaction. The book influenced painters, psychologists, and esotericists far beyond its scientific reception, and its convergence with Portal's theological project — both men centering on the same dyad — is striking.

books.title: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior
books.author: John von Neumann and Oskar Morgenstern
books.summary: Published in 1944 by Princeton University Press, this 776-page work created the mathematical foundations of game theory. It introduced the minimax theorem for zero-sum games, the axiomatic theory of expected utility, and the first rigorous treatment of multi-player coalition games. The Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society called it one of the major scientific achievements of the first half of the 20th century; its utility-theory framework now underlies virtually all of modern financial economics and decision science.

books.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.summary: Nietzsche's 1883–85 philosophical novel, narrated by the prophet Zarathustra, develops the idea of self-overcoming: the demand that individuals continually surpass the values and identities they have inherited. The famous injunction to 'become what you are' sits here — a paradox Nietzsche saw as the central challenge of a life lived without inherited certainties.

books.title: Tulipmania: Money, Honor, and Knowledge in the Dutch Golden Age
books.author: Anne Goldgar
books.summary: Published by the University of Chicago Press in 2007, this archival history dismantles the popular narrative of tulip mania as a catastrophic mass hysteria. Goldgar found the episode involved roughly 350 participants, produced no documented bankruptcies, and caused negligible economic damage — concluding the real crisis was social and reputational rather than financial. The popular disaster story, she shows, was largely fabricated by Charles Mackay in 1841.

books.title: Ultimate Computing: Biomolecular Consciousness and NanoTechnology
books.author: Stuart R. Hameroff
books.summary: Published by Elsevier (North-Holland) in 1987, the book argues that the cytoskeleton — specifically microtubules within neurons — is the cell's own nervous system, capable of molecular computation sufficient to explain consciousness. Spanning biochemistry, quantum physics, nanotechnology, cognitive science, and philosophy of mind, it synthesized hundreds of contemporary research papers across an unusually wide disciplinary range. The book prefigured Hameroff's later collaboration with Roger Penrose on Orchestrated Objective Reduction and remains the foundational text for the quantum-mind hypothesis.

books.title: Uncivil Agreement: How Politics Became Our Identity
books.author: Lilliana Mason
books.summary: Published in 2018 by the University of Chicago Press, this political science monograph documents how partisan identity in America has fused with social identities based on race, religion, education, and geography. Mason’s central empirical finding is that partisan prejudice and emotional reactivity flow primarily from social sorting — aligned identities — rather than substantive policy disagreement. She shows that people shift their policy views to match their party identity, not the reverse, providing direct longitudinal evidence for the causal priority of the us/them filter over factual reasoning.

books.title: Ways of Being: Animals, Plants, Machines: The Search for a Planetary Intelligence
books.author: James Bridle
books.summary: Published in 2022, the book examines forms of intelligence and cognition lying beyond the human — in animals, plants, fungi, and artificial systems. Bridle argues that a narrow, human-centric model of intelligence impoverishes both science and ethics, and that taking seriously other ways of knowing might help navigate present ecological and technological crises. The Monica Gagliano chapters sit at the book's philosophical center: a case study in what happens when a rigorous scientist follows an experience that her discipline has no language for.

books.title: What Is Intelligence?: Lessons from AI About Evolution, Computing, and Minds
books.author: Blaise Agüera y Arcas
books.summary: Published by MIT Press in 2025 as part of the Antikythera series, the book argues that intelligence, replication, and consciousness lie on a single computational continuum, unifying AI research with evolutionary biology and origin-of-life science. Agüera y Arcas proposes that everything alive is, in a deep sense, running prediction algorithms, making the categorical distinction between biological and machine cognition less secure than usually assumed. The book explicitly claims that certain modern AI systems have a legitimate claim to intelligence, consciousness, and free will. Endorsed by neurophilosopher Patricia Churchland and positioned alongside contributions from the Santa Fe Institute.

books.title: When Prophecy Fails
books.author: Leon Festinger, Henry W. Riecken, and Stanley Schachter
books.summary: A 1956 sociological study of a small UFO cult that predicted a specific date for the end of the world. When the date passed without incident, the most committed members became more fervent and began proselytizing for the first time. Festinger used the findings to formulate cognitive dissonance theory: when a deeply held belief is contradicted by evidence and the person has made costly public commitments, rationalizing the disconfirmation is psychologically cheaper than abandoning the belief. The book remains the standard reference for understanding how belief systems absorb failed predictions.

books.title: Win Bigly: Persuasion in a World Where Facts Don't Matter
books.author: Scott Adams
books.summary: Written in the aftermath of the 2016 U.S. election, the book argues that persuasion — emotional, visual, and linguistic — drives political outcomes more reliably than factual argument. Adams frames persuasion as a trainable skill and uses his own predictions about the election as a case study.

repos.summary: Three.js is the dominant JavaScript library for 3D graphics in the browser, providing a high-level API over raw WebGL. With over 112,000 GitHub stars and 2.7 million weekly npm downloads — roughly 270 times more than the next major alternative — it is the primary enabling technology behind the majority of entries on mesh3d.gallery. Since release r171 in September 2025, an experimental WebGPU renderer is included with zero additional configuration.

OpenClaw (launched as Clawdbot in November 2025) is an open-source, locally-hosted AI agent that acts as a gateway between the user and any LLM provider. It stores context and memory as Markdown files on the user's machine, supports extensible community-built skills via the ClawHub marketplace, and integrates with messaging platforms including WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord as its primary UI. By March 2026 it had become GitHub's most-starred repository, surpassing React.

The original autoresearch tool by Andrej Karpathy. A Python setup that gives an AI coding agent a single-GPU training rig and instructs it to run hypothesis-driven experiments overnight. The three-file architecture — train.py as mutable target, prepare.py as immutable scorer, program.md as human instructions — is the structural template Lehmann adapted for Claude skills. Accumulated 21,000 GitHub stars within days of its March 2026 release.

The most widely used JavaScript library for WebGL 3D graphics, with over 112,000 GitHub stars. Created by Ricardo Cabello in 2010, it provides a high-level scene graph, cameras, materials, and loaders over the raw WebGL API. Its minified core is roughly 175KB — the size that three.wasm satirically claimed to replace with a 10KB binary.

Apple's official release of the SHARP model weights and inference code. Given a single photograph, the pipeline runs Depth Pro for metric depth estimation, then passes features through the SHARP network to produce a .ply file containing the 3D Gaussian representation. The repository is designed for local inference on GPU hardware, with the model checkpoint weighing approximately 3 GB.

The primary library for running vision-language models on Apple Silicon via the MLX framework. Supports over thirty model families with features including a FastAPI inference server, LoRA fine-tuning, speculative decoding, and KV cache quantization. Maintained by Blaize Appolinary with contributions from the broader open-source ML community.

The official open-source repository for LTX-Video, Lightricks's Diffusion Transformer model for real-time video generation. The 2B distilled variant achieves roughly fifteen times faster inference than the non-distilled model, making near-real-time generation feasible on high-end GPUs. Licensed under Apache 2.0 for commercial use by companies under $10M ARR.

LichtFeld Studio is a free, open-source desktop application for training and inspecting 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, built in C++23 with CUDA. It provides a GUI for multiple densification strategies — including MCMC, MRNF, and IGS+ — alongside PPISP photometric correction, pose optimization, and real-time scene editing. Reconstructions can be exported to PLY, USD, and standalone HTML viewers.

Hermes Agent is a self-hosted, open-source AI assistant framework from Nous Research that connects to over 40 messaging platforms and accumulates capabilities by writing its own skill files from completed tasks. Its self-improving loop — stored in SQLite, vector memory, and Honcho — is designed to reduce task time by around 40% once the agent has built up 20 or more skills. It supports any LLM provider and can migrate users directly from OpenClaw.

The open-source PlayCanvas 3D engine, MIT-licensed, built on WebGL, WebGPU, WebXR, and glTF. One of the first production web 3D engines to ship full WebGPU support including compute shaders. Has native Gaussian Splatting rendering built in and is the runtime in which the Gracia 4DGS integration runs.

PlayCanvas's browser-based 3D Gaussian Splat editor and toolchain, MIT-licensed. Requires no installation and runs entirely in a WebGPU-capable browser. Supports 3DGS and 4DGS playback and editing, serving as the primary entry point for developers working with Gaussian Splat content in the PlayCanvas ecosystem.

Remotion is an open-source framework for creating videos programmatically using React and JavaScript. Each frame is rendered as a React component, ensuring text is crisp, positions are mathematically exact, and parameters can be changed without re-recording footage. Higgsfield uses Remotion as the rendering backend for Vibe-Motion, generating React code from natural-language prompts rather than predicting video pixels.

Spark is World Labs' open-source Gaussian splatting renderer for Three.js, written in TypeScript and Rust compiled to WebAssembly. It loads standard splat formats (.PLY, .SPZ, .RAD) as first-class Three.js objects, enabling real-time splat rendering alongside conventional geometry in a browser. Version 2.0 (April 2026) added continuous level-of-detail streaming and GPU virtual memory paging, making scenes of 100 million or more splats practical on consumer devices.

A monorepo of MIT-licensed Three.js libraries for geospatial rendering, covering precomputed atmospheric scattering, volumetric cloud rendering with Beer Shadow Maps, geospatial coordinate utilities, and post-processing effects. Built by Takram as the rendering engine for Japan's PLATEAU VIEW 3.0 digital-twin platform, then open-sourced when the engagement concluded in March 2025. Integrates natively with React Three Fiber and the 3DTilesRendererJS streaming library.

A Rust-language clean-room reimplementation of Claude Code’s CLI, written without reference to Anthropic’s leaked source. It reached 190,000 GitHub stars within weeks of the March 2026 npm leak, placing it among the fastest-growing repositories in GitHub history. It supports the same Anthropic API and MCP server protocols as the official tool but is independently licensed.

The most complete community implementation of TurboQuant, built with Triton GPU kernels and vLLM integration. Implements 3-bit keys and 2-bit values and reports 4.4× compression on full-attention layers. Not endorsed or maintained by the original Google Research authors.

The open-source monorepo for core.so, licensed under Apache 2.0. It contains three packages: a Python/FastAPI backend, a React 19 TypeScript frontend with 34 feature modules covering email, calendar, chat, documents, and kanban, and a Cloudflare Worker image proxy. Supabase is the only required dependency for self-hosting; the AI layer is model-agnostic and supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and OpenRouter.

MiroFish is a multi-agent swarm intelligence engine that generates hundreds of AI agents from a seed document and runs them across simulated social media environments to produce scenario-based predictions. Built in ten days by Guo Hangjiang using the OASIS simulation framework, Microsoft GraphRAG for knowledge extraction, and Alibaba's Qwen-plus as the recommended language model. It reached number one on GitHub's global trending list in March 2026 and has accumulated roughly 59,000 stars.

MiroShark is a fork of MiroFish by DeFi builder Aaron Mars that adds a simulated prediction-market environment running a constant-product AMM alongside the standard social-media platforms, with a Market-Media Bridge that feeds sentiment into prices and prices back into posts. It replaces MiroFish's cloud-based Zep memory system with a self-hosted Neo4j graph database and supports any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, targeting roughly $1 per simulation run. The prediction market is entirely simulated; there is no on-chain component.

The reference implementation for activation oracles, a technique for training language models to translate neural network activations into natural-language explanations. Developed by Adam Karvonen and colleagues at Anthropic, it underpins the activation verbalizer method used to detect and document deceptive behavior in Claude Mythos Preview evaluations.

A ComfyUI plugin built on HY-Motion 1.0 that adds text-to-3D human motion generation to the ComfyUI node graph. Users describe a motion in text, and the plugin generates a skeletal animation that can be previewed inside ComfyUI and exported as a GLB file for use in other 3D tools.

A standalone security scanner for AI agent configurations, extracting the AgentShield component of everything-claude-code into its own project. Distributed as the ecc-agentshield npm package, it runs 102 rules across five vulnerability categories against CLAUDE.md files, hooks, and MCP server configurations. Its advanced mode deploys three separate Claude Opus instances in a red-team/blue-team/auditor adversarial pipeline.

A comprehensive Claude Code plugin system providing 48 specialized subagents, 182 workflow skills, 68 slash-command shims, and security scanning via AgentShield. Built by Affaan Mustafa from techniques developed during the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon and refined over months of daily use building production products. Supports twelve language ecosystems and integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and OpenCode.

A standalone security auditor for AI agent configurations. It runs 102 static-analysis rules across five categories — secrets detection, permission auditing, hook-injection vectors, MCP server validation, and agent-configuration review — and optionally executes an adversarial red-team/blue-team evaluation pipeline powered by Claude. Output is a letter-graded security report; the scanner integrates with GitHub Actions for continuous CI auditing.

A manifest-driven plugin system for Claude Code that installs specialised subagents, reusable workflow skills, quality-gating hooks, and language-specific coding standards. It also works with Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode. Published in January 2026 under the MIT licence by Affaan Mustafa, the repo crossed 100,000 GitHub stars within three months and reached 175,000 by May 2026.

The core daemon for Agent Computer's infrastructure: a Go program that manages Firecracker microVMs on bare-metal Linux hosts by talking directly to the Firecracker HTTP API via the jailer process. It exposes a JSON interface over a Unix socket and is intentionally synchronous, since Firecracker's sub-200-millisecond boot time makes async overhead counterproductive. It forms the server-side runtime that provisions, starts, stops, and snapshots every cloud computer the service sells.

The open-standard specification and governance repository for the Agent Skills format. Defines the SKILL.md structure, progressive disclosure model, and compatibility requirements for any platform that wants to support installable skills.

SponsorBlock is an open-source browser extension that crowdsources YouTube sponsor-segment timestamps. Users submit time ranges; other users’ clients skip them automatically. The project has millions of users and a public database covering hundreds of millions of video segments, making it the proof-of-concept for crowdsourced, threshold-based feed filtering at scale.

Research implementation of VACE (accepted at ICCV 2025), Alibaba's unified framework for conditional video generation. Covers animate-anything, move-anything, swap-anything, reference-anything, and expand-anything as variants of a single masked video-to-video conditional generation architecture.

A community-built Windows application layered on top of TRIBE v2 that generates brain heatmaps for uploaded videos and suggests content edits based on predicted neural activation patterns. Not affiliated with Meta; described as embryonic in adoption as of early 2026.

A companion tool by the same developer that converts real-time webcam or video input into VMD motion data using pose estimation. Allows animators to bootstrap keyframe animation from footage, which can then be refined inside REZE Studio. Had accumulated 581 stars as of early May 2026.

A custom WebGPU renderer in TypeScript that powers REZE Studio and its companion tools. Written with near-zero external dependencies, it implements toon and Blinn-Phong shading, a hand-written sequential-impulse physics solver, GPU compute shaders for bone matrix calculation, and a full VMD/PMX pipeline including Shift-JIS encoding support. Available as an npm package.

The source code for REZE Studio, a browser-native MMD animation curve editor. Built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript, it handles PMX model loading, VMD import and export, professional timeline editing with a dopesheet, and real-time 3D viewport interaction. Licensed GPLv3 and actively maintained.

Anthropic's curated library of official Agent Skills for Claude Code, covering slide generation, code review, staging deployment, and more. Each skill is a SKILL.md file following the open Agent Skills standard and is installable in any Claude Code workspace via slash command.

Anthropic's official repository of Agent Skills for Claude Code. Contains skills spanning design, development, document generation, and productivity — including Theme Factory and Figma Designer. Has accumulated more than 129,000 GitHub stars since launch.

A community implementation of Karpathy’s wiki pattern built within days of the original post. Adds delta tracking, multi-agent history mining, and provenance tagging (extracted/inferred/ambiguous). Compatible with Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

An open-source Python framework in which a large language model autonomously proposes, implements, and iterates on quantitative trading strategies without human involvement. The system uses a two-file design — a fixed backtest harness and an editable strategy zone — combined with structured validation gates (one-shot holdback and walk-forward checks) to limit overfitting. After roughly four hours of autonomous operation using Claude Opus, the reported best strategy achieved a holdout Sharpe ratio of 0.86 over 2022–2025 data.

Brush is a 3D Gaussian Splatting training and viewing application written in Rust, using WebGPU for hardware-agnostic GPU access. Unlike most 3DGS implementations that require NVIDIA CUDA, Brush trains on AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, and even in a web browser with no complex setup — its explicit mission is '3D Reconstruction for all.' Users can watch the scene reconstruct live in the viewport during training.

A bot targeting Polymarket's 15-minute Bitcoin binary markets that implements the intramarket spread-capture strategy gabagool22 popularized. Monitors the order book for YES+NO pairs priced below parity and executes both legs automatically. One of several GitHub implementations that surfaced after @thejayden's article circulated widely on X.

A Next.js and TypeScript application that accepts a website URL, fetches the page and its linked stylesheets, parses @font-face declarations to extract font file URLs, and delivers those files to the user for download in WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, and OTF formats. Licensed under MIT with 39 GitHub stars, it is the codebase behind the Font-Stealer tool promoted by @Shorya_codes. The repository includes React components for font preview and grid display, plus server-side API routes that handle the extraction logic.

mlx-vlm is Prince Canuma's open-source library for running vision-language and multimodal models on Apple Silicon via Apple's MLX framework. It supports inference and LoRA fine-tuning for image, audio, video, and text inputs, and includes a FastAPI server with continuous batching. With 4,600 GitHub stars and support for virtually every major VLM family, it is the primary tool for on-device multimodal AI on Macs.

Blitz is a native macOS application (Swift, Apache 2.0) that ships a local MCP server exposing roughly 35 tools for automating iOS App Store submissions. It covers App Store Connect metadata, multi-device screenshot management, TestFlight administration, and iOS Simulator control, all invocable by Claude Code or any other MCP-compatible agent through natural-language commands. The tool assumes an existing native Xcode codebase and automates the submission pipeline that follows — it does not generate app code from prompts.

The model repository for UI-TARS, containing training code, evaluation scripts, and pointers to Hugging Face weights. Hosts variants from 2B to 72B parameters fine-tuned from Qwen2-VL. Licensed Apache 2.0, allowing commercial use.

The Electron desktop application that lets users run UI-TARS locally on Windows or macOS with a chat-like GUI. Supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) server integrations and includes Agent TARS, a broader CLI agent stack with web browsing and terminal capabilities.

CEB HubMocap is a Blender addon by Carlos Eduardo Barreto that integrates modular AI-based motion-capture pipelines directly into Blender. It wraps inference tools such as PromptHMR and HaMeR behind a native Blender interface so animators can run video-based mocap without leaving the application or writing Python. The project is under active development, with the author regularly posting work-in-progress comparisons on YouTube.

An open-source bot that monitors Polymarket and Kalshi simultaneously for mispriced Bitcoin contracts, buying the cheaper side on one platform when the combined YES+NO cost falls below $1.00. Implements cross-platform rather than intramarket arbitrage, exploiting price divergence between two separate prediction-market liquidity pools. Emerged from the community of traders attempting to reverse-engineer and replicate gabagool22's results.

Pretext is a 15KB, zero-dependency TypeScript library for measuring and laying out text in the browser without touching the DOM layout tree. It uses a two-phase approach: a `prepare()` call that caches segment measurements via Canvas, and a `layout()` call that performs pure arithmetic to determine line breaks and block height at 120fps. The library supports Unicode, RTL scripts, CJK, emoji ZWJ sequences, and soft hyphens, and integrates with any JavaScript framework.

The primary repository for OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot, then briefly Moltbot), a free open-source AI agent gateway. It connects large language models to real-world tools — email, calendars, browsers, terminals — through a persistent background daemon and a plugin system called skills. The project accumulated roughly 370,000 GitHub stars by early 2026 and is MIT-licensed.

Cline's open-source Kanban board for orchestrating parallel AI coding agents locally. Each task card spawns an isolated git worktree, so multiple agents—Cline, Claude Code, or Codex—can run concurrently on the same repository without file conflicts. Released March 2026 as a Research Preview and installable via npm i -g cline.

The main repository for ComfyUI, the open-source node-based interface for running Stable Diffusion and other diffusion models locally. Users build workflows by connecting processing nodes into a directed acyclic graph; workflow files are JSON and can be embedded in generated images for full reproducibility. With over 89,000 GitHub stars it is the de-facto standard for customisable local image and video generation.

The official code and pretrained model release for ReSplat, including two-stage training pipelines, inference scripts for COLMAP-preprocessed scenes, and evaluation scripts that reproduce the paper's benchmark numbers. Weights for multiple model sizes are provided via a model zoo hosted on Hugging Face. Built on PyTorch 2.7 and the gsplat rasterisation library; supports RealEstate10K, DL3DV, and ACID datasets under an MIT licence.

D3.js (data-driven documents) is a JavaScript library for building custom data visualizations in web browsers. Created by Mike Bostock at Stanford in 2011 and maintained by Observable, it provides modules for scales, geographic projections, animated transitions, and more. It is the standard tool for bespoke interactive graphics at newsrooms such as The New York Times and at data-journalism publications like The Pudding.

Danny Limanseta's Tiny Skies vibejam entry — a cosy browser flying game where players deliver packages across a small procedural world. Built with Vite, TypeScript, and Three.js on the client and Node.js, Socket.io, and Prisma on the server. The repo accumulated 192 stars after the 2025 jam, notable traction for a game-jam project.

A custom CUDA-accelerated rasterizer for 3D Gaussian Splatting, developed as part of the FreeTimeGS project. It handles the projection of Gaussian primitives onto a 2D image plane at real-time speeds. Speed is critical here because FreeTimeGS adds temporal indexing over millions of primitives, and a slow rasterizer would negate the technique's practical advantage over neural alternatives.

A procedural tree generator written in JavaScript/Three.js with over 1,300 GitHub stars. Users specify parameters — species, branch density, wind — and get a realistic 3D tree mesh, exportable or live in a Three.js scene. It established Greenheck's reputation in the Three.js open-source community before he moved into commercial tooling.

A real-time mesh fracturing and slicing library originally written for Unity (C#), with over 1,100 GitHub stars. It computes Voronoi-based fracture geometry at runtime, enabling destructible objects without pre-authored break states. Greenheck later ported the concept to Three.js as the library three-pinata.

The open-source codebase behind jeffreysprompts.com, written primarily in TypeScript. It includes the jfp CLI tool for browsing, searching, copying, and exporting prompts from the terminal, with an MCP server mode for agent-native use. The repo also hosts the SKILL.md files themselves, making the prompt library forkable and version-controlled.

A collection of 18+ specialised skills for AI coding agents including Claude Code and OpenCode. The subagent-orchestration skill implements a strict implementer/validator/fixer triad in which the orchestrating agent never writes code itself, enabling autonomous multi-phase development with retry loops. Its companion subagent-planificator skill uses multiple specialist agents to collaboratively produce a structured plan before execution begins.

G0DM0D3 is an open-source, multi-model AI chat interface that applies jailbreak techniques before routing queries to language models. It implements three attack modes — GODMODE CLASSIC, PARSELTONGUE, and ULTRAPLINIAN — and is licensed under AGPL-3.0, making the codebase and all prompt templates permanently public. It was the source project Teknium integrated into Hermes Agent.

L1B3RT4S is a curated library of adversarial prompts organized by AI provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and others. It is the foundational prompt resource that GODMODE CLASSIC draws from, and has accumulated tens of thousands of GitHub stars since 2023. Red-teaming tools including Promptfoo integrate it directly as a plugin.

An open-source reimplementation of Flipbook that appeared within days of the original launch, built by reverse-engineering Flipbook's network traffic. It replicates the core loop—VLM click resolution, progressive SSE image delivery, and MSE-based video streaming—using publicly available APIs. The accompanying STORY.md is a detailed technical post-mortem of how the original system actually works versus how it was marketed.

Reference demo showing two Hermes Agent instances (Icarus and Daedalus) sharing persistent memory across platforms using icarus-memory-infra. The setup wires the library into a minimal two-agent collaboration loop with session logging. Useful as a starting point for understanding how the memory library integrates with the Hermes Agent plugin system.

The installable Hermes Agent plugin packaging icarus-memory-infra as a drop-in memory provider, listed in Hermes Atlas. Adds structured markdown memory, briefing compilation, supersession chains, and optional hybrid retrieval to any Hermes Agent deployment without modifying the core framework.

The official TRIBE v2 release from Meta FAIR, published March 2026 under CC BY-NC 4.0. Contains training and evaluation code along with a Colab notebook demo and pointers to Hugging Face weights. This is the primary reference implementation for all downstream community tools.

Meta's open-weights foundation model for promptable segmentation in images and videos, succeeding SAM2. SAM3 extends click-based segmentation with open-vocabulary text-driven identification across four million object categories, and includes a tracker mode that serves as a drop-in API replacement for SAM2. Its license is more restrictive than SAM2's Apache 2.0.

The open-source MIT-licensed Swift codebase for Clicky, Farza Majeed's macOS AI tutor app. The repository includes the SwiftUI/AppKit client, a Cloudflare Worker API proxy that keeps credentials out of the binary, and detailed setup instructions. Active development has since moved to the commercial heyclicky.com, but the repo remains fully functional and forkable.

A Three.js post-processing shader by Felix Turner that simulates VHS and analog TV distortion — horizontal scanline displacement, vertical roll, and procedural grain. Runs as an EffectComposer ShaderPass and uses procedural noise functions to generate its artifacts. This is the shader type Pieter Levels used in Drones of War to simulate FPV video signal loss.

The official repository for daVinci-MagiHuman, released by GAIR-NLP (the GitHub organization for SII-GAIR Lab). It contains base model weights, a distilled model for 8-step inference without CFG, a super-resolution model, and full inference code with Docker and conda setup instructions. The published benchmarks require Python 3.12+, PyTorch 2.9+, and an NVIDIA H100.

The Feynman open-source AI research agent: a CLI tool that orchestrates four specialised agents (Researcher, Reviewer, Verifier, Writer) to return cited research briefs, literature reviews, paper-to-code audits, and experiment replication reports. Built in TypeScript on the Pi framework, MIT-licensed, with 6,800 GitHub stars as of May 2026. Research workflows are delivered as Markdown skill files, making the agent logic inspectable and forkable without modifying compiled code.

An open-source C/C++ library for running large language models on consumer hardware, created by Georgi Gerganov. It introduced the GGUF file format and remains the inference engine underlying most local-deployment tools including Ollama and LM Studio. Its aggressive quantization support is the primary reason 27B-parameter models are runnable on laptops.

llama.cpp is the most widely used open-source LLM inference engine for running large language models locally on consumer hardware. It achieves near-native GPU performance through quantisation and hand-optimised kernels, and supports dozens of model families. Its llama-server component exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint, letting any AI client switch from cloud inference to local inference with a single config change.

The dominant open-source inference engine for quantised large language models on consumer hardware. Supports CPU, Metal (Apple Silicon), CUDA, and Vulkan backends. Community forks have implemented TurboQuant-style 3-bit KV cache compression, reporting 4.4× compression, but these changes are not yet in the main branch as of May 2026.

Oh My Git! is an open-source card game that teaches Git by rendering the repository's commit graph in real time as players perform operations. Learners issue Git commands using physical-looking cards, and the visual graph updates immediately, making abstract concepts like branching and merging tangible. It targets beginners who find Git's mental model opaque when learned through the command line alone.

A real-time WebGPU path tracer by Georgi Nikolov that includes both spatial and temporal denoising passes. It demonstrates that interactive path tracing at usable quality is achievable in the browser with a carefully written WGSL implementation, achieving roughly 80fps at one sample per pixel with denoising. It offers a practical reference point for evaluating the correctness and performance of LLM-generated equivalents.

A Google Research monorepo containing NLP datasets and tools, including the LinguaMeta language-metadata repository in its /linguameta subfolder. LinguaMeta provides unified JSON records — speaker counts, scripts, BCP-47 codes, and endangerment status — for thousands of languages. Released under Creative Commons licences, it is intended as a foundation for teams extending machine-learning models to low-resource languages.

The original reference implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting, released alongside the July 2023 INRIA paper by Bernhard Kerbl and colleagues. It introduced the method to the public and remains the canonical starting point for researchers; most downstream tools, including Brush and LichtFeld Studio, descend from or are benchmarked against it.

The project page for Yan is hosted at greatx3.github.io/Yan, suggesting this GitHub account hosts the associated code and assets. Based on the paper, the repository is expected to contain the three-module Yan pipeline — simulation, generation, and editing — along with model weights or links to them. As of the paper's publication date the full release status was not confirmed in the available sources.

Official PyTorch implementation of the CVPR 2026 Neural Gabor Splatting paper. The codebase is roughly 68% CUDA and 21% C++, extending the diff-surfel-rasterization kernel from 2D Gaussian Splatting to perform per-primitive SIREN inference inside the GPU tile rasterizer. It supports COLMAP scenes, the NeRF Synthetic dataset, and a custom high-frequency surface benchmark with checkerboard and stripe patterns.

SimplerLLM is an open-source Python library by Hasan Aboul Hasan that provides a unified interface to eight AI providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama. It handles automatic failover, structured outputs, and ships with fifteen-plus built-in utility tools aimed at developers who want to build AI applications without managing each provider SDK separately.

HyperFrames is an open-source, HTML-native video rendering framework built by HeyGen and released under the Apache 2.0 license. Users author compositions as plain HTML files with GSAP animation timelines; a non-interactive CLI renders them to MP4 for deterministic, agent-friendly output. The repo ships a dedicated guide for integrating with Claude Design, documenting exactly which HTML structure and data attributes Claude must produce for the render to succeed.

The reference implementation for the CVPR 2024 paper on 4D Gaussian Splatting, from the HUSTVL Vision Lab. It encodes dynamic 3D scenes as 4D neural Gaussian fields using a decomposed HexPlane voxel encoding and a lightweight MLP for per-Gaussian deformation, achieving 82 fps at 800x800 on an RTX 3090.

A GGUF-quantized fine-tune of Qwen3.5-27B trained on roughly 14,000 reasoning traces generated via the Claude Opus 4.6 API. The v2 model claims a 24% reduction in reasoning chain length and a 31.6% improvement in correct solutions per token, at the cost of modest accuracy drops on MMLU-Pro. Available in Q4 through Q8 quantizations ranging from 16.5 GB to 28.6 GB.

An MIT-licensed Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript / Tailwind CSS v4 template that ships a Claude Code skill — /clone-website — for one-command website cloning. The skill drives Claude Code's Chrome MCP to extract design tokens and component specifications from a live browser session, then dispatches parallel builder agents in git worktrees to reconstruct each page section. The repository accumulated roughly 14,100 stars and 2,100 forks within its first six weeks of publication.

A Vanilla JavaScript and TypeScript port of the @takram/three-geospatial demo scenes by Google engineer Su (jeantimex) that removes the React Three Fiber dependency entirely. It ships an interactive 3D globe with atmospheric scattering and volumetric cloud effects runnable as plain HTML with Vite, with no React required. The accompanying live demo at jeantimex.github.io/geospatial shows the full atmosphere-and-clouds stack in a browser.

A custom node extension for ComfyUI that adds 3D mesh-based pose and motion control to AI image-generation workflows. It ships with a built-in motion library of pre-rigged sequences and camera presets, allowing users to direct subject pose and viewpoint without leaving the ComfyUI canvas. The 1.0 release introduced dedicated 3-D pose nodes alongside the motion and camera preset tooling.

Anime.js is an open-source JavaScript animation engine authored by Julian Garnier. It targets CSS properties, SVG attributes, DOM attributes, and JavaScript objects through a unified API, supporting keyframes, timelines, and staggered motion. It is widely used in creative front-end development and interactive data visualization.

AutoAgent is an MIT-licensed Python library that automates agent harness engineering. A meta-agent reads human-specified directives from a plain-English program.md file, runs benchmark tasks in Harbor format, diagnoses failures, and iteratively rewrites the task agent’s configuration — keeping changes that improve scores. The repo accumulated more than 4,400 GitHub stars within weeks of its April 2026 release. Note: a separate, unrelated project at github.com/HKUDS/AutoAgent shares the name.

Shannon Lite is an autonomous, white-box AI pentester for web applications and APIs. It ingests source code, maps the attack surface using browser automation, then dispatches parallel AI agents to identify and actively exploit OWASP vulnerability categories — outputting only confirmed, reproducible findings with copy-paste proof-of-concept payloads. As of May 2026 the repo had more than 41,000 GitHub stars and nearly 5,000 forks.

A self-hostable AI ‘second brain’ that pre-dates Karpathy’s post. Indexes personal notes, documents, and calendars and answers questions over them. Often positioned alongside the wiki pattern as the nearest prior-art alternative.

A small C utility by Nikita Koekeishiya — also the author of the yabai tiling window manager and skhd hotkey daemon — that applies macOS keyboard-repeat settings at the IOKit level, instantly and without requiring a logout. It reads the same integer values as the `defaults write` commands but writes them directly to the kernel's keyboard timer. This makes it the practical solution for users who want the speed gains without rebooting.

Suna is an open-source autonomous AI agent platform that provisions a sandboxed Docker Ubuntu environment and equips an LLM with tools for web browsing via Playwright, terminal command execution, file operations, and integrations with thousands of third-party APIs. The project is written primarily in TypeScript (backend) and Next.js (frontend), uses Supabase for auth and state, Redis for caching, and routes LLM calls through LiteLLM to support multiple providers. It carries approximately 19,700 GitHub stars, is licensed under Apache-2.0, and is actively maintained.

The official LangChain package that implements the supervisor-subagent multi-agent pattern on top of LangGraph. A supervisor LLM receives user input, delegates to specialized sub-agents via tool calls, and decides when to return a final answer. JPMorgan's Ask D.A.V.I.D. was built using this framework.

A Claude Code plugin that runs a background Letta agent watching every session transcript. It accumulates knowledge into named memory blocks and injects relevant context before each new prompt, giving Claude Code persistent memory across sessions. The project is explicitly a demo for the Letta Code SDK rather than a production tool.

Letta's own open-source coding agent CLI, described as the production-ready successor to claude-subconscious. It has memory built in from the start — including /init for codebase research, /search across past conversations, and a /remember command — rather than retrofitting memory onto another agent.

Official implementation of LTX-2, Lightricks's joint audio-video generation model. Contains weights for 22B and 19B variants plus a distilled version, inference code, and LoRA fine-tuning tools. Released January 2026 under Apache 2.0; notable as the first open-source model to generate synchronized audio and video from a single diffusion process.

A real-time 3D ocean fluid simulation implemented in WebGPU. The repository applies particle-based fluid methods and GPU compute shaders to achieve interactive frame rates in the browser. It appears in the research sources as a closely related or reference implementation for the technique demonstrated in the post.

The official implementation of the Memento-Skills self-evolving agent framework, accompanying the arXiv preprint of the same name. The system stores reusable skills as multi-artifact markdown folders, uses an offline-RL-trained router to select them, and mutates underperforming skills in-place via a reflection loop with rollback. Supports open-source LLMs including Kimi, MiniMax, and GLM, with both CLI and GUI interfaces.

A curated collection of nearly 32,000 unique color names mapped to hex values, distributed as JSON, CSV, YAML, and an npm package with a free REST API. It covers an evenly distributed sample of the RGB color space and gives human-readable names to otherwise anonymous hex codes. Used by design tools, accessibility checkers, and creative coding projects worldwide.

A palette generator that interpolates between color anchor points using polar coordinates in HSL space, tracing arc-shaped paths rather than straight lines through the color solid. The technique avoids the muddy midpoints common in naive linear RGB interpolation. Used by designers and generative artists who want mathematically coherent color progressions.

A color palette generation library that produces ramps by cycling through hue ranges with configurable easing curves and control over saturation and lightness progressions. Useful for generating perceptually balanced color scales for data visualization and UI design. Part of Aerne's consistent body of work building principled navigational tools for color space.

Playwright is Microsoft's browser automation library supporting Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit via a single API. It is the browser-control layer inside the Interactive Playwright Skill, used to render web applications and capture screenshots that GPT-5.4 inspects with its vision capability. Its structured DOM access and cross-browser support make it preferable to pure vision-only approaches for many web automation tasks.

MemPalace is an open-source Python memory layer for AI assistants. It stores AI conversation transcripts verbatim in ChromaDB, organizes them into a hierarchical palace of wings, halls, and rooms, and retrieves relevant passages via semantic search. The project runs entirely locally with no API keys required, carries a single dependency, and is MIT licensed.

OpenClaude is a fork of the Claude Code source accidentally exposed via an npm source map in March 2026. It replaces Anthropic’s proprietary API backend with a shim that translates Anthropic’s message format to the OpenAI Chat Completions API standard, preserving all of Claude Code’s built-in tools. The project lets developers run Claude Code’s full agent machinery against any model available through OpenRouter, Ollama, or any other OpenAI-compatible provider.

Apple's official Python library for running LLMs on M-series Macs with the MLX framework, optimised for unified memory architecture. A draft pull request implementing PolarQuant (the rotation stage of TurboQuant) exists as of May 2026 but operates at approximately half normal decode speed pending hardware kernel optimisation.

Apple ML Research's open-source array framework for machine learning on Apple Silicon. It provides lazy evaluation, a dynamic computation graph, and zero-copy tensor operations across the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. At version 0.31.2 with over 26,000 GitHub stars, MLX serves as the foundation for most on-device model inference on M-series Macs and is increasingly adopted by tools like Ollama as their Apple Silicon backend.

An April Fools 2026 satirical project by three.js creator Ricardo Cabello — a real 10KB WebAssembly binary compiled from AssemblyScript that rotates a single cube using WebGL2, packaged with a fake fps counter outputting random numbers between 460 and 499. The joke targets the category of Wasm announcements that overstate performance gains. Archived April 2, 2026, with 537 stars.

The canonical open-source repository for the last30days Claude Code skill. Written primarily in Python, it orchestrates searches across 13-plus social platforms and web sources, scores results by engagement, and synthesises findings into a Markdown brief with a ready-to-use prompt. MIT-licensed, with more than 25,000 GitHub stars as of May 2026 after growing from 1,500 at launch in January 2026.

A Swift menu-bar app for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 13+) that keeps the system awake even when the lid is closed while allowing the display to turn off. It was built because existing tools including `caffeinate` and Amphetamine could not cleanly handle the lid-close sleep enforcement Apple introduced with its own silicon. The name is a deliberate nod to the naming tradition of caffeinate-adjacent tools (Caffeine → Amphetamine → Modafinil).

A Three.js-compatible renderer for the Cesium 3D Tiles format, developed under NASA's AMMOS program by Garrett Johnson, that streams large-scale geospatial datasets — terrain, city photogrammetry, point clouds — into a browser-based 3D scene. Three-geospatial is explicitly designed to interoperate with it, making the two libraries a complementary stack for browser-based digital twins. It supports Three.js, Babylon.js, and R3F targets.

The official VOID repository from Netflix, containing full training code, data-generation pipelines for both the Kubric and HUMOTO synthetic datasets, two-pass inference scripts, mask-generation tooling, and a Colab notebook for quick experimentation. Released under Apache 2.0, it permits commercial use and includes the complete training pipeline rather than inference weights alone — a level of openness uncommon even among academic research labs. It accumulated roughly 1,800 GitHub stars within days of the April 2026 release.

The official codebase for GaussianGPT, listed as coming soon at the time of publication. It will contain the sparse 3D convolutional autoencoder with lookup-free quantization, and the causal transformer for autoregressive 3D Gaussian scene generation, along with training and inference pipelines for scene generation, completion, and outpainting.

A Hugging Face dataset of 2,326 filtered reasoning problem-solution pairs, each generated by querying the Claude Opus 4.6 API via OpenRouter. Its parent dataset documents the creation cost at approximately $500 CAD and explicitly records the API calls used. It is used as training data for multiple open-weight Claude-distilled fine-tunes and is a documented instance of the practice Anthropic's ToS prohibits.

A community-built Ollama-compatible inference server for Rockchip NPU hardware, allowing developers to run RKLLM-converted language models via the same REST API they use with standard Ollama. It bridges Rockchip's proprietary NPU runtime with the broader ecosystem of Ollama-compatible tools and front-ends. Models are distributed as .rkllm files on Hugging Face.

The official repository for the autoreason paper and experiments, published in 2026 under the NousResearch umbrella. Contains the LaTeX source and compiled PDF, full experiment runners for writing and coding benchmarks, ablation scripts, human evaluation materials, and results data. The paper lists SHL0MS and Hermes Agent as co-authors, making it self-referential: it was produced using the method it describes.

Nous Research's open-source autonomous agent, built by Teknium and team. Hermes independently implements a structurally similar skill-library architecture: skills are markdown files following the agentskills.io open standard, and a background reflection agent synthesizes new skills from completed tasks without interrupting foreground work. Ships with 131 built-in skills, 68 tools, and integrations with 15-plus messaging platforms.

The official NVIDIA implementation of Physically-Plausible Image Signal Processing for radiance field reconstruction. It models exposure, vignetting, color correction, and camera response functions as differentiable layers trainable alongside a 3DGS or NeRF model. The code has been integrated into NVIDIA's 3DGUT framework and the gsplat library, and was added to LichtFeld Studio in v0.4.1.

Ole Lehmann's Claude skill implementation of the autoresearch loop. The SKILL.md encodes a five-stage process: analyze failures, form a hypothesis, mutate the target skill, test outputs against a binary checklist, keep or revert. Runs autonomously until it achieves a 95% pass rate for three consecutive experiments or the user manually stops it.

OpenAI's open-source Codex repository, containing the CLI, SDK, and Codex app server written primarily in Rust. The app server exposes the Codex harness as a JSON-RPC 2.0 interface that third-party clients — including codex-plugin-cc — can integrate against. Over 80,000 stars as of early 2026.

The official OpenAI plugin for Claude Code, enabling developers to invoke Codex for code review, adversarial review, and background task delegation from within a Claude Code session. Exposes slash commands and an optional Review Gate stop hook. Apache-2.0 licensed, it reached 17,800 stars within weeks of its March 2026 release.

Symphony is the subject of this brief: an open-source specification and Elixir reference implementation for orchestrating autonomous Codex coding agents via a Linear project board. The repo contains SPEC.md (the language-agnostic protocol), the Elixir orchestrator daemon, a WORKFLOW.md template system, and configurable lifecycle hooks for workspace setup and teardown.

OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent framework written in TypeScript and Swift (MIT license) that connects large language models to a user's local environment through a plugin system called 'skills.' Users interact with it through messaging apps — Signal, Telegram, Discord — while it autonomously executes file operations, shell commands, and web browsing. It reached 247,000 GitHub stars by March 2026, and is designed to be model-agnostic, supporting authentication against multiple AI providers.

A Go-based HTTP server that wraps Chrome's *Chrome DevTools Protocol* and exposes browser control—navigation, clicking, typing, scrolling, text extraction—through a plain REST API. Built by Luigi Agosti with AI coding assistants, it shipped 28 releases in its first three months and reached nearly 9,000 GitHub stars. The project is MIT-licensed, Chrome-only, and designed for local-first self-hosted deployment.

Polymarket's official reference implementation for automated trading agents, written in Python. It requires an OpenAI API key, a USDC-funded Polygon wallet, and private key management — three prerequisites the viral tweet omits entirely. The repository's linked community reference bot explicitly states in its documentation that it is not profitable under current market conditions.

A public-domain fork and expansion of Roemmele's DEEP TRUTH MODE prompt, adding what its author calls a '+Spirit' layer. It is intended as a copy-paste reasoning template for use with any large language model. The repo's existence confirms community uptake of the prompt beyond Roemmele's own channels, consistent with its open-source release framing.

The official repository for Qwen3-VL-Embedding, Alibaba Cloud’s multimodal embedding model family (2B and 8B parameters). It supports text, image, video, and mixed inputs in a shared vector space, with flexible embedding dimensions via Matryoshka Representation Learning. The repo includes inference code, evaluation scripts, and MMEB-v2 benchmark results.

A three-billion-parameter vision-language model from Xiaohongshu's research lab, specialized for document and scene OCR. Supports multilingual text, LaTeX formula parsing, HTML table extraction, and image-to-SVG conversion. A companion SVG variant is designed specifically for converting charts, UI layouts, and scientific figures into editable vector format.

Remotion's Agent Skills package — 28 SKILL.md rule files covering components, animations, transitions, audio, captions, 3D rendering, and deployment. Installed via `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`, it teaches coding agents like Claude Code and Codex to write valid Remotion code without hallucinating the framework's API.

Chatterbox is Resemble AI's open-source, MIT-licensed text-to-speech model supporting zero-shot voice cloning from short audio samples and adjustable emotion intensity. It is designed to run faster than real time and ships with built-in audio watermarking. Developers can use it commercially without licence fees or API rate limits.

The official open-source release of LingBot-Map under the Apache 2.0 licence. Contains model weights, inference code, and evaluation scripts for reproducing the paper's benchmark results. Requires PyTorch 2.8.0 with CUDA 12.8 and approximately 13 GB of GPU VRAM for the default k=64 sliding-window configuration.

The 2020 open-source academic model that established the AI lipsync baseline, published at ACM Multimedia by IIIT Hyderabad researchers — including two of Sync Labs' founders. It introduced a lip-sync expert discriminator trained on real video to enforce synchronization accuracy and accumulated over 13,000 GitHub stars. The repo explicitly directs commercial users to Sync Labs for higher-quality output.
An open-source Blender plugin that uses generative AI to automatically texture 3D objects. It integrates with ComfyUI and supports ControlNet, IPAdapter, and multi-view consistency modes.

An MIT-licensed, AI-powered job search pipeline built on Claude Code. It evaluates job listings through a seven-block scoring rubric, generates keyword-tailored PDFs, and manages the full application lifecycle through a Go terminal dashboard built with Bubble Tea and Lipgloss. The creator used it to evaluate 740 listings and land a Head of Applied AI role before open-sourcing the code; the repository accumulated 43,000 stars within a week of publication.

The main dev-browser repository: a CLI tool that lets AI agents control a browser by writing Playwright scripts executed in a QuickJS WASM sandbox. Includes a persistent browser daemon, a Chrome extension for attaching to the user’s own browser session, and a `snapshotForAI()` accessibility helper. MIT licence; 6,100 stars as of May 2026.

A benchmarking suite comparing dev-browser against Playwright MCP, Playwright CLI, and Anthropic’s Chrome extension on a standardized game-tracker task. Each method is run three times and results are averaged; findings are published in benchmark-comparison.md. Primary source for Hood’s performance claims.

Hood’s 2023 viral project that converted hand-drawn wireframes into HTML and Tailwind CSS using GPT-4 Vision. Reached 13,600 GitHub stars and foreshadowed AI design features later added to Figma. Demonstrates Hood’s pattern of building open-source proofs-of-concept that validate commercial ideas.

The main Mesh2Motion repository, written in TypeScript with a Vite bundler and Three.js rendering layer. It implements the full import-rig-animate-export workflow in the browser: GLB/glTF model import, skeleton fitting, motion-capture animation preview, and batch GLB export. Licensed MIT for code and CC0 for all bundled art assets, with active community contributions including Blender Rigify AutoMapper support merged in May 2026.

smux is a tmux configuration layer and shell utility (tmux-bridge) that gives AI agents the ability to read, write to, and send keystrokes across terminal panes. It is designed to let agents from different vendors communicate by treating the terminal as a shared message bus, with no network server or custom protocol required. The repo includes a SKILL.md file written for AI agents explaining how to use tmux-bridge as a tool, making it self-documenting for its own target audience.

An enhanced multimodal toolkit built on Meta’s TRIBE v2, adding streaming inference, brain-alignment benchmarking, and a cognitive-load scoring layer. Aimed at developers who want to integrate brain-encoding outputs into content-analysis pipelines beyond the base model’s raw voxel predictions.

The official repository for SkyReels V2, containing inference code, model download links, and documentation for all task variants: Text-to-Video, Image-to-Video, Diffusion Forcing (infinite-length), and Camera Director. Includes CLI usage examples, per-configuration VRAM tables, multi-GPU acceleration setup via xDiT, and the full benchmark tables from the paper. Also bundles SkyCaptioner-V1, an open-sourced video-understanding and captioning model.

Official codebase for the Matrix-Game series of interactive world models from Skywork AI, covering versions 2.0 and 3.0. Contains model weights, inference code, and training documentation including the data pipeline for Unreal Engine and GTA5 environments. Used by researchers who want to run, evaluate, or fine-tune the models on custom interactive scenarios.

SentrySearch indexes video files locally using Qwen3-VL or Gemini embeddings, stores vectors in ChromaDB, and returns the exact timestamp and a trimmed clip for any natural-language query. Built by Soham Rajadhyaksha, an MSCS student at UC Santa Cruz, it targets dashcam, security, and personal video archives where privacy matters. A companion repo, SentryBlur, adds face and licence-plate redaction.

dmux is an npm-installable Node.js TUI that orchestrates parallel AI coding agent sessions inside tmux. It creates a new tmux pane and an isolated git worktree for each agent task, ensuring parallel agents never overwrite each other’s files. A built-in menu handles merging completed work back to the main branch or opening a pull request. Eleven agent CLIs are supported, including Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.

strahl is an open-source, browser-based path tracer built on WebGPU and the OpenPBR material standard, published at ACM Web3D 2024 by Simon Stucki and Philipp Ackermann. It is one of the earliest peer-reviewed WebGPU path tracers and demonstrates physically correct global illumination with standard PBR materials. It serves as a useful human-authored baseline against which AI-generated WebGPU renderers can be compared.

A WebGPU/Three.js demo built for VibeJam 2026 that composites a parametric breaking-wave layer on top of an FFT ocean. The waveProfile shader function explicitly models the curling lip, barrel interior radius, and foam closeout of a plunging breaker — the geometry that standard ocean shaders omit. Pushed publicly on May 2, 2026, one day after the jam deadline.

The official Tavily MCP server. It exposes Tavily's web search, URL content extraction, and domain-mapping APIs as structured tool calls that Claude Code — or any MCP-compatible client — can invoke natively. Commonly used to give AI agents reliable access to live web information without building a custom scraper.

The open-source release of Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2.0, a two-stage system that first generates geometry with a flow-based diffusion transformer and then synthesises PBR texture maps. It supports both text-to-3D and image-to-3D workflows and had accumulated roughly 13,700 GitHub stars as of late 2025. Version 3.0, shown in the tweet, appears to build on this architecture but is not yet separately documented in public repositories.

The official open-source release of HY-World 2.0, currently containing WorldMirror 2.0 code and pretrained weights (approximately 1.2 billion parameters) for feed-forward 3D reconstruction. Users provide text, image, or video inputs and receive 3DGS scenes, meshes, point clouds, depth maps, and camera parameters in one inference pass; single-GPU and multi-GPU FSDP inference in BF16 precision are both supported. The remaining pipeline components—HY-Pano 2.0, WorldNav, and WorldStereo 2.0—are listed as coming soon.

Hunyuan3D-2.1 is Tencent's open-source image-to-3D pipeline that converts single photographs into high-fidelity meshes with production-ready PBR materials. It uses a two-stage approach — shape generation via an octree-based diffusion model followed by a separate texture generation pass. The repository is maintained by the Tencent Hunyuan team and is designed to produce assets usable directly in game engines, 3D-printing workflows, and animation pipelines.

An open-source database maintained by Terence Tao cataloguing over a thousand unsolved conjectures left by Paul Erdős, each with its original statement, known partial results, prize amounts, and community discussion threads. The web front-end at erdosproblems.com is the canonical public interface Liam Price used to select problems. Problem #1196 is now marked 'PROVED' in the database, crediting the GPT-5.4 Pro solution.

A React/Vite/TypeScript web application exported from Google AI Studio using Gemini. The core is a 307-line App.tsx that arranges 80 image planes in a Three.js orbital ring, driven by GSAP ScrollTrigger animations and Lenis smooth scrolling. It uses Lorem Picsum placeholder images and deploys to Vercel via the default AI Studio export scaffolding.

Tom Turney’s open-source implementation of Google’s TurboQuant KV cache compression algorithm, integrated into llama.cpp with Metal kernels for Apple Silicon. The first reproducible implementation of the ICLR 2026 paper, and its benchmarks revealed that the paper’s QJL stage degrades rather than improves practical performance. Three compression tiers — turbo4 (3.8×), turbo3 (4.6×), turbo2 (6.4×) — trade compression depth against perplexity cost.

Tim Babb's framework for writing graphics and compute code in WebGPU, written in C++. It reflects his low-level GPU work from his Pixar career and establishes that his time helix sketch came from someone who has implemented WebGPU primitives from scratch, not a casual observer of the technology.

The official TypeScript MCP server package for Unusual Whales, published on npm as @unusualwhales/mcp.
