Exposes 100+ data endpoints across 14 categories — options flow, dark pool, congressional trades, institutional 13F filings, insider transactions, and more — alongside 30 pre-built analytical prompts. MIT-licensed and compatible with Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Windsurf.

The open-source CLI and directory powering the skills.sh Agent Skills ecosystem. Provides commands to search, install, and manage skills across 54+ compatible AI coding agents. The repository underpins the community infrastructure for discovering and distributing reusable agent instruction sets.

Reference implementation of Inverse Transfer Data Augmentation for authorship style transfer. Uses GPT-3.5 to neutralize stylized text, creating synthetic parallel training pairs, then fine-tunes a BART-base model to recover the target style. Represents the closest published prior art to the Reddit post’s unslopping technique.

Official repository for Alibaba Tongyi Lab's Wan 2.2 video model family, including Wan2.2-Animate and Fun Inpainting. Provides inference scripts, preprocessing pipelines for motion and pose extraction, and Apache 2.0 weights supporting both character animation and character replacement modes.

The official repository for Wan2.1, Alibaba’s open-source video generation model released under Apache 2.0. The model comes in 1.3B and 14B parameter variants, runs on consumer GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM, and includes the VACE module for masked, ControlNet-guided video editing. It scored 86.22 on VBench, above the 84.28 recorded for OpenAI’s Sora while that model was active.

The official open-source release of Alibaba's Wan 2.2 video generation model family. The repository contains model weights, inference code, and documentation for the T2V, I2V, and TI2V variants. It is the primary distribution point for developers who want to run or fine-tune the models locally without going through Alibaba's cloud APIs.

A collection of Claude Code plugins focused on intelligent automation and multi-agent orchestration. It provides building blocks for wiring Claude to external tools and coordinating workflows across multiple agents. Relevant as a reference implementation of the same orchestration pattern the post demonstrates.

A fully local voice assistant pipeline that chains Whisper.cpp (speech-to-text), llama.cpp (language model inference), and Piper TTS (text-to-speech) — no cloud APIs required. Built by @yacineMTB to run on consumer hardware, it represents the kind of local AI application that stands to benefit most from cheap NPU-enabled SBCs. The project was explicitly designed to work on ordinary consumer hardware, making the arrival of capable $25–$100 boards directly relevant to its potential reach.

A curated paper list tracking the emerging field of 4D spatial intelligence — methods that recover dynamic 3D worlds from video. It covers Gaussian splatting pipelines, neural radiance fields with temporal modeling, and related reconstruction techniques. Useful as a map of the research landscape for anyone wanting to go deeper than a single paper.

mujoco_wasm compiles MuJoCo 2.3.1 to WebAssembly so physics simulation runs entirely inside a browser tab alongside Three.js for rendering. It is the in-browser counterpart to the server-side architecture the tweet describes — both pipelines use Three.js for visuals, but mujoco_wasm bundles physics with the client rather than streaming it from a server. The project is used for interactive robotics and reinforcement-learning demonstrations that need no server infrastructure.

A Claude Code skill that generates zero-dependency HTML presentations from a conversational brief. Claude interviews the user about aesthetics, presents three visual-direction previews drawn from twelve curated style presets, and outputs a single self-contained HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inlined. The project crossed 1,000 GitHub stars organically and has since become one of the most-distributed skills in the Claude Code community.

Serenity (@aleabitoreddit) is an X-based equity analyst whose feed concentrates on the AI hardware supply chain, with particular focus on what they call 'functional monopolies' — small or mid-cap suppliers occupying chokepoints in the photonics, advanced packaging and substrate value chains. Recurring names include Soitec ($SOI) for silicon-photonics substrates, Tower Semiconductor ($TSEM) for photonics foundry capacity, Coherent ($COHR) for transceivers, AXT ($AXTI) for indium phosphide, Lipoid Kosmetik / LPKF ($LPK) for glass-core substrates, and Japanese names such as TOWA (6315) and MSSCorp (6830) for HBM compression and CPO inspection respectively. The posting style mixes thesis posts with running performance updates and is frank about both wins and laggards.
module.credibility_note: Public posts show Serenity called Soitec at ~43 EUR in March 2026, before the rally documented in this bookmark, and has flagged related names (TSEM, AXTI, AAOI) ahead of large moves. Self-reported one-year returns of 630%+ should be treated as such — self-reported and unverified — but the timestamped Soitec call is a matter of public record.

module.blurb: Brian Roemmele is a technology researcher and writer, editor and founder of Read Multiplex. He posts about AI, the future of work, and emerging tech, often exploring themes like the 'end of work' and AI hardware. He has 422K followers on X (formerly Twitter).

Anonymous X (Twitter) account focused on semiconductor and technology equity valuation. Known for circulating corrected and reformatted data tables on chip-sector P/E, PEG, and earnings-growth metrics, often framing them with brief market-positioning commentary. Posts tend toward quantitative rather than narrative analysis.

Parmita Mishra is a user on X (formerly Twitter) with the handle @parmita. No specific domain expertise or posting topics could be determined from the available sources. Follower count is not available.

TechHalla is a tech-focused X account covering startups, AI, and digital trends. They share insights on emerging technologies and industry news. Their follower count is not notably large but they engage with a niche tech audience.

The X.com user @tszzl has a profile on the platform, but no accessible content or biographical information could be retrieved from the available sources. The profile appears to exist, but details about their domain expertise, posting topics, or follower count are not available.

Bilawal Sidhu is a former Product Manager at Google, where he worked on AR/VR and Google Maps. He now focuses on AI, spatial computing, and the future of technology, sharing insights and analysis on emerging trends. His follower count is not publicly available from the provided sources.

Independent thematic-equity research firm founded in 2023 by James van Geelen, a self-taught investor who began his career in alternative healthcare before turning to public markets in 2018. Citrini publishes via paid Substack, runs a portfolio of long/short thematic baskets called the Citrindex, and has built a following on X for early calls on AI 'picks and shovels,' GLP-1 obesity drugs, and idiosyncratic trades such as a public short of Silicon Valley Bank in late 2022, months before its collapse. The firm now reports roughly ten employees and covers themes spanning AI, robotics, defence, healthcare and government policy.
module.credibility_note: Track-record claims are largely self-reported through paywalled subscriber notes; the firm's '+131% since inception' and '+100% one-year' figures for its core portfolio cannot be audited externally. That said, several specific calls have been corroborated in the public press: the early 2023 AI hardware basket, the SVB short, and a February 2026 note on AI capex sustainability that was credited by Bloomberg with helping trigger an equity-market sell-off. Van Geelen, born around 1992, holds bachelor's degrees in biology and psychology from UCLA and is not a CFA charterholder; positions described in Citrini notes are the firm's own, and readers should assume the firm transacts in the names it covers.

module.blurb: Hasan Toor is an AI and tech educator with over 570K subscribers on YouTube and 31K followers on Instagram. He posts about the latest developments in artificial intelligence and technology, aiming to make complex topics accessible. On X, he shares insights and updates on AI tools and trends.

Aakash Gupta is a product growth expert and writer, known for his newsletter 'The Product Growth Guide'. He shares insights on product-led growth, SaaS metrics, and startup strategies. His following is notable but exact count is unavailable.

Beff (e/acc) is a prominent figure in the effective accelerationism (e/acc) movement, advocating for technological acceleration and AI progress. They post about AI, tech policy, and futurism, often engaging with other e/acc proponents. Their follower count is not publicly available due to X restrictions.

X account documenting experiments in which large language model agents are connected to live cryptocurrency trading infrastructure — including perpetual DEX APIs — and observed trading with real market data. Posts focus on emergent agent behaviour, paper-trading results, and the mechanics of running LLMs against leveraged derivatives markets.
module.credibility_note: No verifiable institutional affiliation or track record. Account is experiment-oriented rather than analytical; posts report observations without a disclosed methodology, benchmark, or statistical framework. Results should be treated as anecdote and starting point for inquiry rather than evidence of genuine alpha.

module.blurb: Jukan is an X (formerly Twitter) account focused on semiconductor industry analysis, primarily translating and synthesising Korean, Japanese, and Taiwanese trade press and research into English. The account covers TSMC foundry dynamics, memory markets (DRAM, NAND, HBM), AI chip supply chains, and geopolitical semiconductor policy with evident primary-source access and a buy-side-adjacent analytical frame. Posts frequently cite TrendForce, Nikkei, and Korean financial press. The account appears to operate from a Northeast Asian vantage point and is notable for surfacing non-anglophone semiconductor intelligence before it reaches Western financial media.
module.credibility_note: Track record of early coverage on HBF, YMTC market share, and UMC/Vanguard price dynamics. No institutional affiliation publicly declared. Content is analytical rather than promotional.

module.blurb: Marlow (@marlowxbt) is an X account that publishes short-form financial and crypto narratives, with a specialisation in Polymarket content. The account follows a recognisable story template: a cryptic reference (a Reddit username, a Discord handle) leads to a wallet search, which leads to a reveal of an improbable profit figure from the public Polymarket leaderboard. The posts are presented as investigative discoveries but draw on publicly browsable on-chain data. Multiple posts use near-identical framing, suggesting a content format designed for engagement rather than original reporting. The account does not disclose financial relationships with the wallets or bot-selling services it profiles.
module.credibility_note: Content is narrative and promotional in structure. The wallets and profit figures referenced are real and verifiable on-chain, but the framing as serendipitous discovery obscures that Polymarket's leaderboard is public and freely searchable. No institutional affiliation or research credentials declared. Survivorship bias is systematically absent from the posts. Treat as content marketing unless independently corroborated.

module.blurb: Public information about @napoleon21st is thin. The X profile is login-walled to anonymous web fetches and the handle does not appear in indexed lists of small-cap or photonics commentators, in financial press citations, or in cached search results that would normally surface a high-engagement account. The post in question reads as that of an active retail investor with concentrated positions in three specialist semiconductor and photonics small-caps (SIVE, SILC, LPK) who is comfortable using LLM 'thinking models' as a sanity-check on his own theses.
module.credibility_note: No verifiable track record was located through public web search. Treat the account as an unfamiliar retail voice rather than an established analyst or fund manager. The post itself is candid - it labels the LLM output as 'not necessarily true' - which argues against treating it as a recommendation, but readers should not infer authority where the public record does not establish it.

X (Twitter) account presenting as a professional or retail-adjacent investor sharing chart-based trading calls and market commentary. Posts typically feature StockCharts.com technical overlays and short, confident directional calls on equities and ETFs. Tone leans toward the assertive end of the retail-fintwit spectrum — brief, conviction-forward, light on sourced fundamental analysis.

Will Eastcott is a veteran graphics programmer and co-founder of PlayCanvas, a WebGL game engine. He previously worked at Criterion Software on the RenderWare engine, contributing to Dreamcast titles. He posts about real-time graphics, WebGPU, and game development. His follower count is not publicly available due to X restrictions.

Archetype Vision is a pseudonymous crypto analyst and trader focused on on-chain metrics, market structure, and altcoin cycles. They post technical chart analysis, DeFi and NFT commentary, and macro crypto threads. Their follower count is not publicly available due to restricted access.

A retail-oriented finance account on X operating under the Cluseau Investments banner, known for candid, first-person posts about portfolio construction, income investing, and the practical arithmetic of financial independence. The account mixes market commentary with personal reflection — 'what's your quit number?' style questions that blur the line between investment strategy and life philosophy. Background and institutional affiliation are not publicly disclosed.

The portfolio framing cited in this article reflects genuine familiarity with passive ETF construction and tax-efficiency strategies (notably BOXX), suggesting hands-on investing experience.

module.blurb: Calvin Froedge is a software engineer and entrepreneur known for his work on open-source projects and developer tools. He posts about programming, startups, and technology trends. His follower count is not publicly available due to restricted access.

Crémieux Recueil is the pseudonym of Jordan Lasker, an American independent researcher and data scientist known for dense, chart-heavy threads on empirical social science, economics, and statistics. Writing primarily on X and on Substack at cremieux.xyz, Lasker posts on topics ranging from IQ research and behaviour genetics to macroeconomics, finance, and historical demography. His account, which has accumulated roughly 300,000 followers on X, is regularly shared by prominent figures including Paul Graham and Noah Smith. He is a prolific cataloguer of findings from academic literature — often threading obscure studies on quantitative social science with his own commentary and visualisations — and has developed a readership that spans professional researchers, finance practitioners, and engaged generalists.
module.credibility_note: Lasker's empirical posts are generally careful to cite primary literature and acknowledge uncertainty, and his threads on topics like FOIA, market efficiency, and economic history are well-sourced. His reputation is, however, complicated by his parallel work in race-and-intelligence research, which mainstream population geneticists and psychologists have sharply criticised as methodologically flawed and politically motivated.
